articleTitle: PUK Issuance for M-PESA Agent, LNM and Bamba Chakula
markdownContent:
# **Issuing PUK to an** **M-PESA Agent**

- Dealers can initiate SIM Swaps and generate the PUKs for their M-PESA tills via DIY on Dealer Portal.
- When you receive a call from an M-PESA agent requesting for the PIN/PUK details to unlock their agent line.
- Advise the agent to contact their head office.
- The Head Office Team will log into Dealer Portal and will generate the PUK of the affected Till.
- Where Dealer Portal does not generate the PUK the logged in user will raise a PUK SR capturing the till number on the portal to M-PESA Agent Admin who will pick the SR, Vet the details and issue the PUK.

**NB**: Dealer Portal system outages will be reported via email to: [MPESAadmin@safaricom.co.ke](mailto:MPESAadmin@safaricom.co.ke) 
**Issuing PUK for Lipa Na M-PESA Merchant store till**

**NOTE: The merchant should call using the nominated number or finance contact number, which is presented on WDE, and the CEE confirms using G3 if the number is correct.** 

- PUK requests will be handled with reference to the acquirer/aggregator; see details below for the various merchants. When done CEE will issue the PUK and advise the merchant on how to unlock the SIM.

# **Safaricom Acquired**

**These are tills which the Top Organization Name is: SFC-Lipa na Mpesa Business Till Head office, SFC CBU/EBU etc.**

Caller should call from the nominated number or Finance contact number or any active users under the till or Paybill on G3.

CEE will proceed to **issue PUK** as per request from merchants/Partners after effective vetting as per the details below:

- Organization name
- Store Number
- Merchant till number.
- Operator Initials and names or
- Any contact on the organization contacts details on G3.

# **Aggregated Merchants (by Banks and Non-Banks)**

Aggregated Merchants tills have their Top Organization Name bearing the name of the Aggregator/Acquirer.

Example of Aggregators: Banks, KopoKopo, Empire Micro systems, PharmAccess, Carepay etc.

To issue PUK to these Merchants:

Via call from the Finance contact, CEE will VET the finance contact where available on M-PESA G3, by confirming:

- Names as per finance contact details on G3.
- ID number of the finance contact.
- Email address/ mobile number where available.
- Store Number  
- Till number.

**Note:** Where finance contact details are not available, the merchant will be referred to their respective aggregator/ acquirer for PUK.

**Standalone Merchants** 

- Requests for standalone organizations PUK will be done at Retail or via email to EBU CARE email teams via email to M-PESA Business: **M-PESABusiness@Safaricom.co.ke**/ [Lipanampesa@Safaricom.co.ke](mailto:Lipanampesa@Safaricom.co.ke).

**At Retail shop**

- Requests for standalone organizations will be accompanied by a written request; on official letter head, stamped or with the company seal.
- If the person presenting the letter is not the nominated or finance contact, he or she must produce nominated or finance original ID, and his /her details (names and Id number as per ID) must be in the letter. 
- If the finance contacts or nominated number is presenting the letter, he or she must produce their original ID. The CEE will confirm this from M-PESA G3 or Mpesa Business Portal or Mpesa Enterprise Portal.

**At call Centre:**

- Via an authenticated email address (email matching the one on G3) to **[M-PESABusiness@Safaricom.co.ke](mailto:M-PESABusiness@Safaricom.co.ke)**.
- Call from the nominated number, finance contact number, or any of the active users under the till or paybill in G3.

# **Issuing PUK for Bamba Chakula /WFP / M-PESA Surepay SIM cards**

- These lines are owned by M-PESA Surepay Partner and thus the Corporate PUK issuance procedure will apply.
- The customer should be referred to the organization who will contact their account manager in Safaricom to facilitate the request or issue a letter for replacement at the retail center.
- For WFP/ Bamba Chakula SIM cards the customer should be referred to WFP offices or ask beneficiaries to call/flash WFP help line 0707 722 446 for assistance. The help line is available from 9AM to 4PM daily

**N.B.** WFP always advices beneficiaries to flash that number and they will be called back in the event that they do not have airtime as the number is not toll free.

# **Definition**

This is a service that enables a customer to Check and report Numbers registered using their National Identification details.

# **How to activate/ register for the service**

Customers do not activate/register for it. The service is automatically available from the Primary Number

This is service will only be made available to a customer’s primary number. If the number is not the Primary number the service will not launch.

if a customer cannot access the service from their Primary number, Contact customer care or Visit any Safaricom Retail Shop or Care Desk for assistance.

The service only allows a customer to report a number listed on the check my numbers menu.

Once a customer reports a number(s) the number will be suspended in six(6) hours.

Customers will get a notification once the report has been processed.

# **How to change the Primary number**

Customers can change their Primary number at any of the Safaricom Retail Shops or Care desks.

**Customers may fail to see a number they thought was registered under their name because:**

The number is registered as a corporate and not with you ID

The number is no longer registered with your ID

# **Number masking.**

To protect customer’s information, check my numbers menu will mask or hide part of the numbers. To find your number Dial \*100# <My account> <what is my number> menu to confirm your number.

# **Cancelling a number reported by** **mistake.**

Customers should visit any Safaricom shop to cancel reported numbers submitted.

A reported number will be notified when it is blocked/suspended. A customer must visit any Safaricom shop in person with their National ID to report any dispute/ or reactivate their number.

# **Reporting to the police**

Should customers find numbers that don’t belong to them in the list, we encourage them to report to the police for further action.

markdownContent:
**Definition**

**KYC** – Know Your Customer is the mandatory process of identifying and verifying the identity of a customer when opening an account and periodically over time. This is to ensure that the customers are genuinely who they claim to be.

# **Tiered KYC**

ALL M-PESA customers were moved to tier 2 and monthly and yearly limits no longer apply. 

IMT Has different Limits  allowed as  below: 

**International money Transfer (IMT) Limits**

- An M-PESA recipient will receive up to a maximum of KES 500,000 daily. 
- An M-PESA recipient will receive up to a maximum of KES 1.5 million monthly.
- An M-PESA recipient will receive up to a maximum of KES 18 million KES yearly.
- The maximum permitted amount per transaction is KES 250,000.

# **M-PESA Activation**

The status of the account will differ depending on the different scenarios.

**M-PESA Account Status**

Pending active status.

Mobile Active status.

Suspended status.

Frozen account.

Capped account.

Closed account.

**Pending Account**

If the customer does not pass Vetting, refer the customer to a RC for assistance.

The Support Analyst shall track the progress of the BMC, advise the customer as per resolution and close the SR.

In addition to the verbal education, send the M-PESA activation guide via SMS from CRM SMS Templates:

- Go to M-PESA.
- Choose Activate.
- Enter your current M-PESA PIN.
- Repeat the current PIN.
- Enter ID Number.

- Chagua M-PESA.
- Chagua Wezesha.
- Weka Namba ya Kuanzia(PIN yako).
- Weka PIN mpya(PIN yako)
- Rudia PIN yako
- Weka ID.

If the customer does not still get the menu, the CEE shall advise the customer to change handset and try to activate again.

This refers to the set limits for M-PESA transactions and applies to all M-PESA users. 

# **New M-PESA**

- Maximum daily transaction limit: Ksh.500,000.
- Maximum balance an M-PESA a/c can hold: Ksh.500,000.
- Maximum limit per transaction: Ksh.250,000.

Customers will no longer need to sign the logbook at an M-PESA agent shop during withdrawal and deposit transactions.

# **M-PESA Limit Rules**

Below are the M-PESA customer minimum and maximum transfer/send limits.

The same information be found in M-PESA G2, search customer, go to customer info, click on Customer Default Rule Profile        

| Currency | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Maximum Customer Transfer Limit | KES 250,000 |
| Minimum Customer Transfer Limit | KES 1.00 |
| Maximum Customer Send Money Limit | KES 250,000 |
| Minimum Customer Send Money Limit | KES 1.00 |

| Minimum Value Customer Withdrawal at Agent | KES  50.00 |

| Minimum Value Customer Withdrawal At ATM | KES 200.00 |

| Minimum FSI Credit Request for MKCB | KES 100.00 |

| Maximum Daily IMT Receive Limit | KES 300,000 |
| Maximum Monthly IMT Receive Limit | KES 1,500,000 |
| Maximum Yearly IMT Receive Limit | KES 8,000,000.00 |
| Minimum Card Pay Bill Online Limit | KES 1.00 |
| Maximum Daily Unregistered Customer Debit Value | KES140,000.00 |

# **M-PESA Account Status**

**Mobile Active Account Status**

This is an active M-PESA account with a SIM serial number attached to it.

This is a fully registered M-PESA identity that received a Start PIN, and a customer has already activated and chose a secret PIN of their own.

The account can now send and receive e-money and perform other functionalities within the e-wallet.

**Pending Active Account Status**

If the account is registered on M-PESA but not active or activated, the status will be Pending Active.

The customer may have received start key and did not use it to activate the account.

**Customer already has a Start Key**

Search the number and check the identity status on the M-PESA G2.

If it is pending active, confirm if they have received an initial PIN within the last 24 hours and advise on the activation procedure below:

**Go to M-PESA menu.**

Select Activate or Wezesha.

Enter Initial (start PIN) PIN.

Enter new PIN.

Confirm new PIN.

Enter DOB or ID No.

Send the request to M-PESA.

A message will be received confirming the activation of the account.

# **Customer who has deleted /not received a Start Key**

If a customer claims they have not received or have deleted the initial PIN, the CEE should vet the customer and issue start key with the below vetting details.

- Search the number on G2.
- Confirm Customer’s full names.
- Confirm ID number.
- DOB or registration date as per G2.
- Go to Reset PIN and enter vetting details.
- Customer will receive a PIN.
- Advise the customer on activating. 

**Suspended Account Status**

This is the status where the account is temporarily withheld from transacting though the account can still receive money.

A suspended identity cannot initiate funds transfers and withdrawals.

Reasons for suspending an M-PESA account will include: -

- M-PESA Fraud; Done by the M-PESA Fraud Team at the Identity Level on G2.
- Multiple registrations; Done by AML at the Account Level on G2.
- Customer Request: Done by RC or Contact Center Staff at the Account Level on G2.
- Jitambulishe self-served Sim-Replacement; Suspension done for 24hrs.

**For suspended accounts due to Expired passports, please note as below:**

| ISSUE | AML GUIDANCE |
| --- | --- |
| Expired Passports (Suspended accounts) | 1.    Customer M-PESA account has a customer_suspended_tag with reason indicated as expired passport.2.    M-PESA account has funds.3.    Customer shows up at retail shop, but they do not have their new/valid passport and request to be allowed to access/withdraw the funds on the account.4.    Check on audit logs on when the customer was barred by AML. Only proceed if the suspension is still within the 1-month grace period.5.    Where the 1-month grace period has elapsed, advice customer to bring a valid document for KYC update.6.    Customer must provide the expired passport used during account creation.7.    CEE to vet thoroughly as per process. If vetting is passed, CEE to remove tag, customer withdraws his/her funds then CEE to reinstate the tag (restore the suspension)8.    Advice the customer that once the grace period elapses, they will have to bring in the valid document for KYC update. |

**NOTE:** Change of ownership using expired passports is not allowed. 

**Frozen Account Status**

An identity is changed to frozen by the fraud team due to suspicion of fraud or for investigation purposes or any other warranting reason.

Frozen identities cannot transfer or receive funds.

All unfreezing requests will be channeled to M-PESA Fraud via SR. 

# **Frozen Account Status Customer Care Operations**

**Lines Frozen at Identity status**

**New lines**

If the First Call date on Siebel is after the M-PESA registration date the CEE will raise an SR for Fraud to unfreeze and recycle the account within 48 hours.

**Existing lines**

- If the reason is available, the CEE will advise the customer as per the comments on Audit Logs.
- If the reason is missing on the audit logs the CEE to raise an M-PESA Fraud SR for action by the Safaricom Fraud Team.
- The Support Analyst upon receiving the SR shall send an Email to fraud team.
- The Support Analyst shall track the progress of the issue, advise the customer as per resolution and close the SR.

# **Lines Frozen at Account Level**

**For New lines**

- If the first call date on Siebel is after the M-PESA Registration Date:
- CEE will raise an SR.
- Support will recycle the account within 24 hours and advise customer to visit an Agent/Retail Center for registration.

**For Existing lines**

- If **the first call date on Siebel is before the M-PESA Registration Date,** CEE will confirm the reason for barring the number on audit logs and action as per the request.
- Where the reason is missing the CEE will advise the customer to present themselves to the nearest Retail Center.
- If the first call date is after the M-PESA Registration date, the CEE shall escalate via an SR to the Support team and advise the customer on 24hrs SLA.
- The Support Analyst upon receiving the SR shall recycle the account within 24 hours and advise customer to visit an Agent/Retail Center for registration and close the SR.

**Capped Account Status**

An account enters the capped state when a customer exceeds the set limit for the day or exceeds the maximum amount allowed limit of an account.

**Exceeds limit for the day: -** Customer will wait till midnight to be able to transact again.

**Exceeds the maximum limit of an account: -** Transfer funds to create space to receive other amounts. 

 **Closed Account Status**

- This is an inactive customer identity.
- A customer can request his identity to be closed by writing a letter and present it to a Retail shop requesting his M-PESA Account to be closed.
- This is also the final state of an identity once a customer is recycled.
- **PLEASE DO NOT CLOSE** customer accounts without a customer’s written authorization.

# **MPESA CUSTOMER ACCOUNT Escalations and Support**

**Jitambulishe SIMSWAP Suspended M-PESA**

- M-PESA customer who successfully replace their lines via the IVR or \*100# using Jitambulishe are suspended for 24hours on MPESA G2.
- After 24hrs are over, the account is automatically resumed.
- Suspended customers may however visit the RC or Customer Care Desk to have the service resumed before the 24hrs are over.

  **The suspension reasons are visible on:**

- Audit Logs.
- Tags under customer identity.

  **If the customer visits retail, the retail CEE will.**

- Vet to confirm ownership and check on Key comment on CRM
- Send an Email to Network fraud & MPESA Section [NetworkFraud&M-pesasection@safaricom.co.ke](mailto:NetworkFraud&M-pesasection@safaricom.co.ke) to unbar.
- Once unbarred by fraud, CEE removes Key comment and update the customer.

| Resume 24hrs After VB SIM Swap | |

## **M-PESA STATE TAGS**

Please note below whenever we come across a state tag such as below:

*"Suspended due to M-PESA Dormancy. Visit RC for ownership verification against KYC Images Portal. CEE to verify and unsuspend. If roaming, email Care Team to verify and unsuspend. In case of any challenge, engage Fraud Management Team via Analytica."*

**Action**

# **Activated Account but NO M-PESA Menu**

When a customer registers for M-PESA, or has done a sim swap, they must activate their M-PESA account to receive M-PESA menu.

The activation process syncs the serial number on Siebel to the one on M-PESA.

If a customer says they have activated M-PESA but have not received the menu:

Confirm they have followed the correct activation procedure,

Confirm the serial number on M-PESA is the same as the one on Siebel, if they are not the same, advice customer on the activation procedure and do not push the M-PESA menu,

If the serial number on MPESA and Siebel are the same, proceed to push M-PESA menu. Kindly note sending/pushing the menu before the customer activates M-PESA will make the customer have a dummy menu that they will not be able to use, and the customer will be required to do another Sim replacement.

If the menu has been pushed and not received after 20 minutes wait advice the customer to put the sim card in a different handset and re-activate M-PESA again using his chosen PIN.

articleTitle: Fixed Data Freeze- Unfreeze Capability on CRM
markdownContent:
**Definition**

Fixed Data Freeze Unfreeze Enhancement is an improvement on our CRM system that enables customers to request the suspension of their postpaid fixed data account services when a business break is necessary. This request results in the suspension of both connectivity service and billing until normal operations resume. By implementing this enhancement, we aim to enhance the customer experience and address current challenges. Previously, such requests often led to account termination and equipment recovery processes, as they were treated as churn.

**Background**

The Freeze/Unfreeze process is critical for managing postpaid fixed accounts when customers need to temporarily suspend services and billing, particularly during low-demand periods, such as hotels and schools during off-peak seasons.

A clear and seamless process ensures these requests are handled efficiently, protects revenue integrity and enables a smooth transition when customers resume their services

**Eligibility**

The business fixed data Freeze Unfreeze enhancement is primarily targeted at large and medium enterprises who are mapped to account management services. However, small enterprises who incidentally request this service in writing can also have their requests accommodated.

**Mechanics**

To request the business fixed data Freeze Unfreeze enhancement, the authorized contact of the customer should submit a request via email or letter. This request will be received by their respective account manager, who will then raise an order on the CRM system.

For SME customers, the request should be sent via email or letter to business.support@safaricom.co.ke. Future enhancements shall avail web-based self-service channel to enhance the experience.

**Communication on business fixed data Freeze Unfreeze enhancement to customers** 

The communication regarding the business fixed data Freeze Unfreeze enhancement is being conducted internally within the company. All communication regarding this enhancement will be kept internal and shared with staff members who engage with customers at the account management level. This communication will be handled as a below-the-line engagement, ensuring that it reaches the appropriate staff for implementation and interaction with customers.

**How to know request has been executed**

Customers will receive notification via their billing contact for both the Freeze and Unfreeze actions. This notification will confirm that their request has been executed, providing them with the necessary assurance that the action has been completed.

**Customer request for business fixed data Freeze Unfreeze service**

Customers can request the business fixed data Freeze Unfreeze service for a minimum period of 30 days and a maximum of 90 days. This ensures that customers have flexibility in managing their fixed data services according to their business needs, while also providing a reasonable timeframe for the suspension of services.

**SLA**

The Service Level Agreement (SLA) for freezing or unfreezing an account is set at 24 hours from the time a written request is received. Prompt submission and follow-up of customer requests will be conducted to ensure the best possible experience for customers, with the aim of eliminating customer complaints and credit note requests.

**CRM Journey**

 [Screenshot] 

See attachment for clearer image

**Business Rules**

Account Freeze/Unfreeze will require attachment of customer request before the request is raised in CRM.

This feature will apply for Enterprise Fixed data subscriber on postpaid billing.

The request will be raised via CRM order or Freeze feature at subscriber level and will suspend the service **in all systems** as well as billing in CBS while prorating current month’s bill where customer is pre-billed.

No other suspend -\_resume action will be possible for an account on Frozen Status.

It should be possible to Freeze an account on Credit/Billing/Customer Request suspend state but resuming subscriber by any of these reasons should not be possible for account on Frozen status. The subscriber would need to be unfrozen first.

Customers will be notified via billing contact for both Freeze and Unfreeze actions

I.         ***Freeze:*** *{Dear customer, you fixed data account <> has been fully suspended from billing & accessing service as requested. Thank you for choosing Safaricom.}*

II.         ***Unfreeze:*** *{Dear customer, you fixed data account <> has been reactivated for billing & service access as requested. Thank you for choosing Safaricom.}*

Reports should be availed for customers on Frozen status to allow monitoring, win-backs and termination requests.

Account Freeze will be for a maximum period of 3 months with alerts to credit control for accounts that have attained the maximum period while on Frozen status. There should however be a provision to extend the Freeze for another period of up to 6 months. Accounts on Frozen status at expiry of 6 months will be due for termination. 

Freeze period can be defined for any time frame between 1 month to 3 months. Credit control and FD-Billing will be notified at the expiry of the Freeze period so that they can recommend action to be taken either for termination or extension after engaging the customer.

Weekly alerts will be sent to Credit Control and FD Billing from 2 weeks to end date showing the remaining days to end of Freeze period.

Accounts that are still on Frozen state at time of expiry of the defined Freeze period as requested by customer will remain on Frozen status as the teams engage customer on how to treat account.

Account Unfreeze will require manual action in CRM to raise the Unfreeze request/order.

On expiry of 3 months, credit control can recommend extension of expiry period or termination of the account as appropriate.

It should be possible to raise a termination order for an account on Frozen status without the need to Unfreeze.

Account termination will follow existing business rules for account closure, recovery of equipment and treatment of deposit.

Customer will be required to settle all outstanding bills when subscription is unfrozen.

This is a BTL arrangement for customers.

The customers allowed for this process are Medium & Large Enterprises

Every 2 week, Reconciliations & assurance will be undertaken by the EBU governance team to ensure that abuse does not happen. Automation which gives DIY capabilities to the customers will eventually act as guard rails for control & will require approval.

SLA for account suspension will be 24 hours.

**Definitions**

This is a service on the M-PESA App allowing customers to buy and sell NSE-listed shares using M-PESA. 

**Eligibility**

The service is eligible to M-PESA customers aged **18+** who complete onboarding and risk acknowledgement.

**NOTE:** **ZiiDi Trader** can be **opted in**  if one is registered with

- Kenyan national ID
- Alien ID
- Diplomatic ID
- Military ID
- Passport

IDs not supported at the moment

- Refugee ID

**Note:** ZiiDi Trader does not guarantee profits or provide investment advice. 

**How to activate ZiiDi Trader**

Open M-PESA app> Select ZiiDi Trader under Financial Services> accept terms, complete verification and confirm with PIN. 

## **Share (stock)**

A share represents ownership in a company. When you buy a stock, you become a part owner. You make money if the price goes up when you sell at a higher price than you bought) or the company pays a dividend. 

**Note:** You may lose if you sell at a lower amount than you bought.  

**Owning of Shares**

The customers are the beneficial owner of the shares they buy and can view their statement on the ZiiDi Trader app. 

**Shares trading in Kenya**

Shares are traded on the Nairobi Securities Exchange (NSE) during official market hours, which are **Monday to Friday 9:30-3pm**. 

**Regulation of share trading**

The Capital Markets Authority regulates both the Nairobi Securities Exchange as well as Stockbrokers. The market. 

**Share price change**

Prices change is based on supply and demand as well as company disclosures such as dividends, acquisitions, etc. Prices are and are not set by ZiiDi Trader. 

**Share Holding**

**Holding of shares** 

Shares are held through an omnibus account with each customer’s holdings recorded separately individually. 

## **Selling Shares** 

**How to sell shares**

On the ZiiDi trader mini-App, under **Trade**\>Select the security then Tap **Sell** >Enter price & quantity of shares to sell.

Review summary → Tap **Sell Shares** → Tap **Proceed** → Tap **Sell Shares** → Confirm with M-PESA PIN >Select shares you own, enter price and quantity, and confirm. 

**NOTE:**  Selling shares is not guaranteed as selling depends on market order matching.

**Buy Order**

A buy order is the transaction initiated to buy a share.

**Placing a buy order**

After placing buy order funds are reserved while the order is active. 

## **Stock market**

A stock market is a regulated marketplace where investors buy and sell shares. 

**Stockbroker**

A stockbroker is a person or platform that executes trades for on behalf of investors.  

## **CDSC**

A CDSC account is an account held with Central Depository and Settlement Corporation (CDSC) that facilitates holdings of shares in electronic accounts, opened by shareholders and manages the process of transferring shares traded at the Stock Exchange.

**Is a CDSC account needed for ZiiDi Trading**

A CDSC account is **NOT** needed for trading as trading is done via an omnibus account. Safaricom holds a CDSC account through the broker which will be used for trading.

**Is a CDCS number a requirement**

A CDSC number is not needed because trading is done via an omnibus account. 

**Omnibus Account**

An Omnibus account is an account that consolidates investments for all the customers. 

**Consolidation of Shares via Ziidi Trader**

There will not be consolidation of shares via ZiiDi Trader with other shares bought using a CDSC account.  

## **Pricing options** 

Best Price is the most favorable price available in the stock market at the time you place an order 

**Guaranteed order execution**

Order execution is **NOT** guaranteed as trades depend on market matching, meeting willing buyer and seller at the indicated price.

## **Failed, Partial & Expired Orders** 

**Good Till Day** 

Orders are valid only for the trading day until 3:00PM on that day. 

**Order not fulfilled by 3:00PM**

If order is not fulfilled by 3PM the funds will be reversed after market close. 

**Why are funds held reserved during a buy order**

Funds are reserved during the active order period buy order duration to ensure that funds are available when the order is matched. This prevents failed transactions due to insufficient funds. 

**Duration of receiving money.**

Within 24 hours Funds are disbursed immediately after a matched sell order. 

## **Successful Trades & Portfolio** 

**Portfolio**

Portfolio is the total volume / value of shares a customer is holding. It shows shares owned and unrealized gains or losses.

**Trade confirmation** 

The customer will receive two notifications: 

1. One to acknowledge that we have received your trade request 

2. One to acknowledge processing of the Order and its outcome (whether fully or partially Fulfilled/executed) 

**NOTE:** Notifications confirm trade outcomes. 

## **Corporate Actions (Dividends Only)** 

**What is corporate action**

This is a section with all the announcement or information provided by the listed companies and have an impact on the performance of their security. Any announcement made by the board of the companies listed 

**Dividends**

Dividends are Cash payments declared by some companies. 

**How dividends work** 

Dividends are cash payments paid to shareholders based on the number of shares held as at book closure date. Dividends are paid via M-PESA Only. 

**Book closure Date** 

Book closure date is the day the company checks who owns the shares. If you have shares on that day, you qualify to get benefits like dividends. 

Credited Dividends are declared by some listed companies and paid to entitled shareholders as at a particular date. These will be paid via M-PESA if an investor holds shares held on a record date. 

**NOTE:** Dividends are **Not** guaranteed. 

## **Market Hours & Support** 

**Closing market time**

The Market is open **Monday- Friday** between **9:30am -3pm**. When markets are closed one can view portfolio and plan trades. 

**Getting help** 

Contact Safaricom Customer Care or visit a Safaricom Shop. Internal issues should be escalated to the FSS team as per internal support procedures. Customers can seek support through Safaricom Customer Care channels

The support teams can escalate issues related to allocation or misallocation of shares to the partner via the following email contact:

- [ziiditrader@safaricom.co.ke](mailto:ziiditrader@safaricom.co.ke)

## **Risks & Boundaries** 

**Lose of money**

A customer can lose money when share prices go up or down based on the company performance, supply/demand or any company announcement. 

**Investment advice** 

ZiiDi Trader does not provide investment advice but will avail some information to enable an investor to decide. 

## **Escalations:**

**NB:** ONLY 2nd Line Support Analysts will escalate issues to do with **Allocation/Misallocation of shares t**o the partner via E-mails below: 

[ziiditrader@safaricom.co.ke](mailto:ziiditrader@safaricom.co.ke)

**Definitions**

**M-PESA GO**

This is a product specifically designed for children below 18 years (10-17 years) to enable them to use specific M-PESA services       independently.

**ZIIDI**

ZIIDI is a Money Market Fund approved by the Capital Markets Authority that allows M-PESA customers to invest in Unit Trust from as low as     KSH 100 and earn daily interest.

**ZIIDI for M-PESA GO**

ZIIDI for M-PESA GO will allow customers below 18 years to save and invest as low as Ksh100 on ZIIDI daily and earn an interest.

**Registration for ZIIDI for M-PESA GO**

Parents registering their teens for the first time via the M-PESA GO miniapp, will accept a set of Terms and Conditions during the registration process.

Any registered to M-PESA GO by the parent to opt in to ZIIDI.

Any M-PESA GO account(s) linked to this parent/guardian to opt in to ‘ZIIDI’

**Opt In Channels**

For a start, M-PESA GO customers will opt in to ZIIDI on USSD.

**How to Opt Out**

Parents cannot opt out an M-PESA GO customer out of Ziidi as MPESA GO customers can only opt out of ZIIDI independently.

**Channels for Investing**

M-PESA GO customers can lock funds in their ZIIDI accounts.

**SIM Swap for Roaming Customers**

**Definition**

SIM Swap for Roaming Customers is the process of renewing a line for a customer who is abroad while retaining the customer’s number (eSIM or physical SIM).

This guide outlines the end-to-end process to ensure secure, efficient, and customer-centric service delivery.

**How it works**

The roaming customer will be required to make a written request to [diasporacare@safaricom.co.ke](mailto:diasporacare@safaricom.co.ke), [customercare@Safaricom.co.ke](mailto:customercare@Safaricom.co.ke)  or  [advantage@safaricom.co.ke](mailto:advantage@safaricom.co.ke).

**Verification of phone number**

i.         CEE must do the following checks on the number to provide relevant guide to the customer. Check if:

Registration type: Individual or Company.

Special status: Self-Whitelisted or Golden Number.

Line status: Active, Expired, Pooled, or Barred.

ii.         Customer will provide a contact number corresponding to the country they are roaming in, CEE to validate on VLR ID (HLR) the country tallies and carry out usual vetting

**Requirements for roaming customers**

      **Primary vetting (Mandatory)**

Line to be replaced (the number to be swapped)

Copy of national ID (both sides, for verification with registration details

Copy of passport biodata page

**Note**:

i.         If line is registered using passport, an ID copy may not be required. However, if passport has expired, updated registration details will be needed. Customer to share both old and new passport biodata pages.

 ii.         For customers who do not have the passport but have other travel documents such as temporary passport, East Africa passport or travel permit, check on the validity.

                 **Primary vetting (Mandatory)**

i.         Documents customer used to register.

ii.         M-PESA details, where customer is registered (**Mandatory** if line has been in use). Either:

Date (month or year) of registration

M-PESA balance

iii.          Details of 2 recent self-initiated transactions (Initiated while roaming). 

**Secondary Vetting (at least 3 of the following)**

i.         Three frequently called numbers.

ii.         Airtime balance/data bundle balance/Bundle plan/account limits.

iii.         M-PESA balance, FSI limits i.e., M-Shwari, Fuliza, KCB M-PESA.

iv.         Details of most recent interaction with Safaricom, including the issue reported 
Service Interaction, type, previous successful escalation request on the line (e.g., SIM swap, unbarring line, reversal request).

v.         PIN / PUK Certificate.

vi.         Postal / Email Address or/and credit limit (Applicable to postpaid customer only)

If the customer provides at least 2 of the 3 secondary vetting details, validate the documents given via SubReg and proceed to swap.

**NOTE:**

i.         **Company lines**

Refer to article [**SIM Swap Procedure at the Contact Center**](https://sakahub.safaricom.co.ke/app/article/33dc22ce-574e-424b-86d5-9ab27e60c346)

ii.         **Golden numbers**

(CRM/View360 access to be granted to the team)

**NOTE** 
A contact or alternative number (Safaricom or local number of the country the customer is roaming in) where customer can be reached, and preferred time for us to contact them.

**NOTE:**

i.         For the e-SIMs, CEE will request the QR code from the Manager/TL. The Manager/TL will log in to the link [https://outlook.office365.com/groups/groupsubscription?action=join&smtp=eSimPortalforRoamingCustome…](https://outlook.office365.com/mail/deeplink/groupsActions?action=join&smtp=eSimPortalforRoamingCustomers%40safaricomO365.onmicrosoft.com)  to get the QR code and will share it **only** with the agent who requested for it.

ii.         For golden numbers, Manager/TL/CEE to be allowed to validate the numbers on SubReg and proceed with the swap.

iii.          For whitelisted number, validate the number on SubReg then proceed with the swap.

**Failed vetting**

i.         Where customer fails **all** secondary vetting, CEE/ TL/ Manager will initiate a video call via WhatsApp to confirm image of customer and of the passport.

ii.         CEE/ TL/ Manager will proceed to call the customer on the alternative contact provided (within 8am to 8pm of the customer’s time zone) and will vet accordingly. Where the line provided is a Safaricom line the CEE/ TL/ Manage will confirm customer is roaming. (CEE will confirm customer’s current country from the prefix of the international contact number. This will enable one to verify the time zone customer is in).

iii.         Where the customer is not reachable, inform them to indicate the appropriate time to be called.

iv.         The customer will be advised to be ready with their passport at the time of the call.

v.         CEE/ TL/ Manager will validate the documents via SubReg. Once passed, proceed to swap the line.

vi.         The CEE/TL/ Manager will inform the customer, via email, that the SIM Swap was successful and guide him/her on how to scan the QR code and do a location update in order to latch onto the preferred roaming network.

vii.         The CEE/ Manager/ TL will advise the customer to share feedback in case of any challenge in attaching the E-SIM and advise on preferred time for call back.

**Verification of Documents**

i.         CEE/ TL/ Manager to validate the documents presented by customer against what we have on Subreg portal.

ii.         If customer presents a passport and the document we have in file is the ID, the TL will confirm if passport has the ID number of the MRZ code on the passport, if they tally, validate customer details with the ones on Subreg, if they tally and customer passes vetting proceed and swap.

iii.          Where vetting details provided are not matching with what is in the system, CEE will call and vet the customer at their preferred time.

iv.         Where no documents are found/customer has not provided the documents SubReg, escalate to AML team to further validate the documents.

v.          CEE/ TL/ Manager to confirm again that the documents have updated as per the notes given on Analytica especially where KYC update is required.

vi.         CEE/ TL/ Manager will raise another ticket for KYC to be approved after which the validation will be completed.

**NOTE:**

i.         All the vetting document to be attached on the customer’s CRM profile including the recording.

ii.   Where any anomaly is noted and relating to fraud, the CEE/ TL/ Manager will flag the line and notify the risk team for further investigations.

iii.          Where customer has lost their documents, advise them to apply and reach out once the documents are available.

iv.         Advice the customer on to how to keep the line active via Daima service or provision where customer gives consent.

**For suspended/ flagged lines**

i.         This happens in scenarios where the line is noted as suspended or flagged using key comments on CRM. (By the customer reporting potential fraud.)

ii.         Where customer requests for a swap or unsuspension of such an account, they will be advised to have their valid passport, and pages containing below.

iii.          The Manager/ TL will vet the customer using the Subreg portal. This will include validating the details customer has provided against what is captured on Subreg IMAGE portal and update the same on interaction.

**The swap procedure**

i.         The CEE/ TL/ Manager or SA (Support Analyst) receiving request will vet customer as per details provided and against the available systems. I.e., Siebel /CRM, Partner App, M-PESA etc.

ii.         CEE/ TL/ Manager or SA will confirm the sender’s email address against what is available on CRM, or previous correspondence with customer.

iii.         Where customer request is done using a different email from the registered address, CEE/ TL/ Manager or SA will take extra precaution by vetting to validate ownership.

iv.         CEE/ TL/ Manager will proceed to call customer on the alternative contact provided (within 8am to 8pm of the customer’s time zone) and will vet accordingly. Where the line provided is a Safaricom line user will confirm customer is roaming. (CEE will confirm customer’s current country from the prefix of the international contact number. This will enable one to verify the time zone customer is in).

v.         Where unreachable or unable to engage on call, CEE will request the customer for their preferred contact time.

 **Passed Vetting**

i.         Where customer passes vetting, CEE / TL / manager or SA will confirm if the line has any active call barring or active diverts to another MSISDN. Except for Voicemail, Missed Call Alert or Caller Notify.

ii.         If there is any active call barring or call diverts to another MSISDN, CEE / TL / manager or SA will seek consent to cancel them and will only proceed after the consent is given and subsequent cancellation / deactivation of the barring’s and/ or diverts.

iii.         Where **consent is granted** and vetting successful, CEE / TL / manager or SA will cancel the barring or divert using HLR.

iv.         Where **consent is not given**, CEE will advise customer on the risk and politely decline request.

v.         CEE will proceed to call the number provided by the customer for a swap to verify that the number is not in use by any other party before performing a SIM swap.

vi.         If the number is **not picked** or off air, the CEE / TL / manager or SA will proceed with the SIM swap request.

vii.         Where the number is **picked** by another party, the CEE / TL / manager or SA will establish the real ownership of the line by vetting.

viii.         Where user establishes person presenting request is impersonating, CEE / TL / manager or SA will not swap the line but will flag the line by entering key comments. CEE will enter a comprehensive description on the interaction, detailing interaction with both customers.

ix.         Where a call is received, and user is unable to establish ownership. CEE / TL / manager or SA will **suspend** the line with reason, internal request and will advise customer. This will be handled on a case-by-case basis and CEE, team leader / manager will engage AML / fraud for resolution, where need be.

x.         Where CEE / TL / manager or SA validates ownership and notes a previous fraudulent swap has been successfully completed, CEE / TL / manager or SA will confirm if line has been tampered with i.e., selfcare registration, Safaricom App and will assist accordingly to deactivate where applicable.

xi.         CEE/ TL/ Manager or SA will **proceed** to perform SIM swap once they validate ownership.

xii.         For golden numbers, Manager/TL/CEE to be allowed to validate the numbers on SubReg and proceed with the swap.

xiii.         For whitelisted number, validate the number on SubReg then proceed with the swap.

xiv.         CEE/ TL/ Manager or SA will advise customer on e-mail, on how to activate the line and M-PESA.

xv.         The CEE / TL / manager or SA will capture clear and detailed interaction and key comment where necessary.

**Best Practices:**

i.         Ensure we get the customer’s contact in the first response.

ii.         The CEE that has requested for eSim - TL/Folder team will share with the requester who will be responsible to ensure swap is closed/actioned.

iii.         Identify and capture correct vetting details as and when the customer shares them.

iv.         Capture customer MSISDN, serial number, and contact number on Genesis Cloud under the information tab as and when the customer shares them. (See the screenshot shared at the end of this document.)

v.         Ensure we reach out to the customer on call on their third correspondence as per process. The appropriate calling time will be determined by the customer’s time zone and not ours.

vi.         If on the first response the customer has shared all relevant documents but has failed some account information vetting, call the customer to complete the vetting on call. Calling will be done where the time of handling the email falls within 8AM and PM of the customer’s time zone.

# **Data minimization for Pochi la Biashara**

In an effort to keeping our Customer Data private, the Financial Services and Customer Privacy teams have partnered to deliver a solution that will restrict the customer data, that will be shared with partners:

- This change will apply to all partners (Paybill and Buy Goods). However, development will be phased and merchants will be migrated in sets
- The customer transaction journey remains the same – Nothing changes.

- A redacted version of a customer’s MSISDN - **2547XXXXX654.**

**Definition**

This is a service that enables Prepay subscribers to access airtime on credit and pay later. It is also known as Emergency Top Up (ETU).

**Eligibility**

- It is eligible to all Prepay subscribers.
- Customers on Postpay tariff are not eligible.

# **How It works**

- Prepaid customers below 14 days on the network will not be eligible for Okoa Jahazi.
- The amount requested must be equivalent to your airtime spend in the previous week. For clarity, a week runs from **Monday 0000hrs** to **Sunday 2359 hours.**
- Customers with zero accumulation in the previous week will be able to access Okoa 5, 10 and 20.
- **Okoa** and Tunukiwa usage for the week will count as part of accumulation to determine next week’s borrowing.
- Currently each loan has a repayment period of 5 days. Anytime the debt is paid the customer can borrow again regardless of the day of week.
- Blacklisted customers will be **un-blacklisted immediately** upon full loan repayment.
- Ensure customer has no outstanding loan on Mshwari, restriction is put after 60 days of not paying Mshwari loan.

# **Services that allow Okoa Jahazi**

- Voice calls and send SMS (local on-net and off-net).
- International calls
- Tunukiwa purchases.
- Out of bundle internet access.
- Send International SMS
- PRS services charges.
- Skiza subscription and renewal.
- SMS more for less subscriptions.
- MMS: to send a picture message.
- Charges for checking account balance

 **Note:**

- If the main account has a balance of **less than Ksh 1/-,** then the request to purchase data bundles via Okoa Jahazi will fail.
- You cannot Sambaza/transfer your Okoa Jahazi airtime
- One can request for ETU with as low as Ksh.0 airtime balance.
- One cannot use Okoa Credit while roaming.

**Repayment**

- The amount will be deducted from your subsequent top up(s) until fully recovered.
- Repay within a period of 120 hours(5days) from when the Credit Advance amount was credited to your account.
- Customers can view their statements using \*131#.
- Customers can now choose to repay their Loan either partially or in full

# **Late repayment penalties**

- If you have not repaid after the 5 days, the free money remaining will be used to offset the balance. Thereafter any top will be used to repay the full amount.
- Subscribers with an Okoa balance will not be able to redeem any other resources except which will be used to repay the ETU debt first.
- Subscribers cannot transfer or receive Bonga points. They will get an Error ‘sorry, a technical error has occurred. Please try again later’.

# **Modes of payment**

- Scratch cards top ups
- M-PESA top ups
- 3rd party top-up
- Sambaza
- PINless Top-up (Bamba Poa)
- Bonga

**Okoa Menu**

Customers will now be able to view the below;

**Total Okoa Debt**: A view of total Okoa debt on the menu landing page to give the customers adequate information to enable decision making.

**Okoa Statement**: Blacklisted customers will now be able to access the okoa statement for details on outstanding debt.

**Okoa Minutes**: Purchase of minutes and SMS bundles directly from \*131#ok currently 4 bundles are available as below with a Midnight and 24Hrs validity.

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 10 | 5 | 10 | | Midnight |
| 20 | 15 | 20 | | Midnight |
| 50 | 40 | 50 | | 24 hours |
| 100 | 100 | 100 | | 24 hours |

**NB** 
**NB:** When a customer purchases Okoa Minutes, on CRM this can be viewed as:

- **Okoa Combo** SMS for SMS resources awarded,
- **Okoa Minutes** for the minute’s resources awarded.

**Okoa Upsell:** Customers will now be able to enjoy the value that TUNUKIWA offers through Okoa Jahazi directly. For the first iteration we have started with tunukiwa kredo dabodabo offer as an Okoa upsell.

- The upsell is available on Okoa 20, Okoa 50 and Okoa 100, where the customer gets more kredo for Calls and SMS **valid till midnight.**
- Customers will get an option to choose if they prefer the okoa amount or choose to upgrade to the upsell offer.

**Upsell offers:**

- Okoa 20 = 34 bob kredo dabodabo
- Okoa 50 = 85 bob kredo dabodabo
- Okoa 100 = 170 bob kredo dabodabo

# **Okoa Jahazi Menu Enhancement-Lipa Okoa(M-PESA Option)**

- Lipa Okoa option has been added on the main Okoa Jahazi page where customer will be able to repay their Okoa Jahazi debt either in full or partially via M-PESA option.
- Customers will also be able to view their Okoa Jahazi statements.
- On the main Okoa page the customer will see the below options:

 [Screenshot] 

 [Screenshot] 

# **OKOA SMS**

**Definition**

Okoa SMS is a new opportunity for customers to purchase SMS bundles directly using Okoa. The proposition targets youth & mass segments by ensuring that the customers gain access to SMS bundles even when they have no airtime.

The current SMS bundles available on Okoa will be:

- Daily 20 SMS @ Ksh 5
- Daily 200 SMS @ Ksh 10
- Daily 500 SMS @ Ksh 20
- Weekly 1000SMS @Ksh 30

**Eligibility**

- It is eligible to all Prepay subscribers.
- Post-pay hybrid subscribers will be able to access this feature to offset their bills and/ or purchase additional resources.

#  **Okoa SMS features**

- Okoa SMS & Okoa Airtime for Calls & SMS will cost same as the current SMS bundles.
- OKOA SMS & Okoa Airtime for Calls & SMS debt will be charged as the cost of bundle & interest collected in the same manner.
- OKOA SMS & Okoa Airtime for Calls & SMS products & loan should be reported differently.
- Okoa SMS & Okoa Airtime for Calls & SMS will be available on ETU USSD channels ( 131, 444)
- Okoa SMS & Okoa Airtime for Calls & SMS debts will also be added to the Okoa statements under \*131\*0#
- A New denomination (30/-) have been added under Okoa SMS for the weekly 1000 SMS @30/- but not added under the denominations list.
- A blacklisted customer will not be allowed to access the features.
- Customer's Age On Network must be at least 14 days.
- After borrowing to capacity, the customer must pay their debt to borrow again.
- Debt maturity notifications and blacklist will be sent via SMS to the customer.
- We shall impose blacklist on default payment where the line will be temporarily suspended. The blacklist will be lifted automatically on payment.
- Post-pay hybrid subscribers will be able to access this feature to offset their bills and or purchase additional resources.

# **OKOA EASY TALK**

**Definition**

Easy-Talk Monthly Bundle is a 30-day Minutes + SMS combo bundle aimed at providing customers with a worry-free experience on the traditional core mobile services (calls & SMS) as well as driving affordability to our voice customers.

In addition, we have now added Okoa easy talk offer on the Okoa Jahazi menu.

**Eligibility**

The bundle is open to all Safaricom prepaid Customers.

**How It Works**

- It can be accessed through \*131#.
- On the Okoa main landing page, customers will be presented with an **Easy talk offer** that will be personalized based on usage to drive affordability & offer more value.
- These offers are geared towards delivering targeted & transparent offerings that really deliver on value based on customer usage behavior.
- Customers will have an option to select the personalized offer or Okoa airtime based on their need.
- Furthermore, a consent menu detailing the offer details will be presented to the customer to ensure transparency.

**Blacklisted Offers**

Okoa blacklisted customer will now be presented with segmented offers based on their outstanding debts. The offer price will be affordable to the customer and for customer to access the offer, they have to pay part of the outstanding debt to the extent of the offer price.

**Key Features of the blacklisted offers** 

- The special blacklist offers will only be payable via M-PESA where the loan amount to be repaid will also be added to the amount to be deducted from M-PESA to cater for the cost of offer and partial loan repayment.
- If the customer has fully repaid the debt, they will not be able to access the offers.
- The Blacklist offer will be available on \*131# and only limited to backlisted customers.
- The partial repayment will repay the oldest debt first.
- ALL other ETU Rules will remain the same.

articleTitle: Social Media & eGain Chat Evaluation Guidelines
markdownContent:
**DEFINITION**

This involves the guidelines to be used by social media teams when calling/handling customers.

**VETTING**

This is the process of acquiring information from the customer to verify ownership.

**Verify Ownership**

- For Queries/Interactions requiring vetting, the agent should vet appropriately and exhaustively as per the Saka hub guideline VMDA-0001: Contact Center Vetting Matrix. Failure to vet effectively will attract a score of NO on the vetting parameter which comes with an accompanying penalty on exhaustiveness question on resolution parameter.
- For Queries that require vetting on call the agent should use courteous words in the process of vetting i.e. (May I, Kindly, please)

Agents are expected to complete customer verification as per the vetting guidelines. Failure to accurately identify a customer exposes them to potential risk and negatively impacts the overall customer experience.

**RESOLUTION**

**Appropriate /Accurate Solution**

Applies to wrong/irrelevant solutions given & where the agent fails to vet exhaustively as per the laid down process and dismisses the customer without offering a resolution, it will be marked as an Autofail.

The agent should provide appropriate / accurate solutions to the customer. For example, if a customer contacts us on a SKIZA issue but is given a PRS related solution.

Instances of a repeat interaction - the agent should offer a different appropriate resolution to exhaustively resolve repeat issue.

Agent should undertake appropriate action - If a solution on Saka requires raising an SR but agent chooses not to, should be marked as \`NO´ and thus AUTOFAIL.

The agent should ensure customer issue is resolved - This seeks to address customers who contact us and should be assisted but the agent without giving clear explanation, chooses to raise an unnecessary ticket or sends the customer to the retail centre or M-PESA agency to get assistance.

Promising to call the customer, however no evidence of the same can be found of an outbound call.

 Closing the query without responding to the customer will be marked as a **NO** thus Auto fail.

Note: Where an agent requests customer vetting details for non-vettable queries, this will be marked as NO on resolution, as it delays customer resolution and may be perceived as a dismissive approach.

On exhaustive resolution checks to include accuracy, procedure issued, the how to, vetting, product mechanics - all the relevant information including charges to ensure customer’s issue is resolved fully as well as FCR is achieved (providing all the relevant information so that the customer does not need to re-contact us on the same issue.

Use all available resources and knowledge to give exhaustive resolution as per the guidelines and procedures set. E.g. giving correct SLAs where applicable, educating customers on how to use start key, PUK etc. For billing issues, explain and assist on all chargeable services. A score of **NO** on vetting parameter will attract an accompanying penalty on exhaustive resolution parameter.

Note: SLA of escalated issues will be shared, to the customer via DM/Inbox or Online chat and not on the X timeline or Facebook wall. 

**Importance**

- **Improves First Contact Resolution (FCR):** Resolving customer issues correctly during the first interaction eliminates the need for additional follow-ups and demonstrates efficiency.
- **Minimizes Repeat Queries:** Effective resolution prevents customers from repeatedly seeking assistance on unresolved concerns.
- **Builds Customer Trust in the Brand:** Customers are more likely to trust and remain loyal to a brand when their issues are handled professionally and resolved satisfactorily.
- **Enhances Customer Experience:** Timely and accurate resolutions contribute to a positive customer journey, increasing satisfaction and confidence in the service provided.
- **Increases Customer Retention and Loyalty:** Customers whose concerns are resolved effectively are more likely to continue using Safaricom products and services and recommend them to others.

**Available alternatives/DIY Where Applicable?**

- The agent should offer an alternative DIY procedure for resolving the issue. Where applicable, the agent is to share digital DIY solutions/USSD e.g., initiating P2P/airtime reversal via 456, getting MPESA Statements, use of MyOneApp, getting prepaid or postpaid usage statements etc.

**Timely Response**

- Response time for chats that shall apply is 5 minutes but in case an agent on another chat, the response time may go up to 10 minutes.

- Before closing the chat, the agent shall inform the customer, but in case the customer does not respond within 10 minutes, the agent may end the chat.

**INTERACTION**

**Customer Information Captured on Siebel and ORT**

- Agents are required to capture Manual interactions on Siebel or View 360 in all cases where a mobile phone number has been provided by the customer, whether the agent accesses the number on the available systems or not.

Interactions will be captured on Siebel/View 360 for all M-PESA queries that require an agent to access the G3 system (i.e. all M-PESA reversal requests, confirmation of transaction status, confirmation of contact details for example, pay bill reversal requests).

For B2B, B2C or Merchant to Customer transactions, Where the agent accesses the system, the interaction should be captured on the nominated number. However, where the nominated number is missing, the interaction will be captured on the finance contact number.  The agent should also capture interactions.

- The agent should also capture interactions for all calls/callbacks that they have done to customers.
- Other queries should be captured on ORT as defined in the work instructions.

The agent should select the correct action as guided on Saka Hub Knowledgebase.

The Type selected must correspond to the customer’s issue.

The Sub type selected must correspond to the customer’s issue.

The Comments captured should clearly outline the issue, resolution given, and the action taken.

Agent should capture all relevant details that he/she has vetted the customer on e.g. for sim swap, the SIMEX serial number, for recharge voucher the voucher serial number; PRS codes deleted and on M‑PESA reversals, M‑PESA transaction id.

Note: refer to **Saka hub article IDPA-0001: Interaction Definition and Guidelines at the Contact Centre and Retail.**

**Importance of interactions:**

**For Repeat Caller Management**: Capturing interactions appropriately helps to create a common reference point to customer issues and to manage repeat callers by instantly referring to the previous interaction.

**For Reporting Purposes**: Interactions are what generate reports used to make business decisions.

**STAFF ETIQUETTE**

**P****olite** **and respectful** **throughout the interaction**

- It is important to always be polite and respect the customer. This is demonstrated through the choice of words, tone, and manner of responding to the customer. The choice of words used when responding to the customer issue should project a warm and willing approach.

**Instances of rudeness or impolite behaviour shall be determined by:**

- Use of belittling statements/questions/words.
- The response should not be rude, dismissive, or condescending in tone. It should reflect Safaricom image positively.
-  In case of an outbound call, the agent is expected to be polite and respectful.  Instances of poor or rude behaviour on call shall be determined by poor/inappropriate/belittling choice of words, patronizing or condescending behaviour or talking down to the customer, being argumentative, outrightly dismissing or ignoring the customer. 
- Ignoring the customer completely as warranted by complete silence where a response is warranted, such as instances where the customer has posed a question.
- Ending CHAT when customer is still not satisfied with solution or needs further clarification will also amount to AUTOFAIL.

Note: A score of **“NO”** on this parameter will result in the entire assessment being scored **0.**

**Personalization**

- Agent is encouraged to use customer name/title as it appears on the username/handle if it is a proper name or title. In the absence of a name or inappropriate username/handle, the agent can disregard to safeguard brand image.

**Information present****ation**

- The grammar and punctuation marks must be used correctly, with sentences that are clear, well structured, and free from spelling or typographical errors.
- Appropriate punctuation should be applied to ensure the intended meaning is conveyed accurately.
- The response should have proper spacing between words and sentences, and suitable formatting to enhance readability.
- Overall, the response should be well presented, and easy to understand.

**Emotional connection**

- Emotional connection is demonstrated when the agent responds with empathy, so that customers feel heard, valued, and understood.
- Agents must acknowledge emotions, recognize impact, and communicate with sincerity in both difficult situations (e.g., service failures, losses, disruptions) and positive “light moments” (successes or satisfaction).
- By acknowledging challenges and celebrating wins, agents build trust and enhance Safaricom customer experience. An apology is required in cases where we have inconvenienced the customer.
- As part of building emotional connection, banter is allowed. Banter enhances engagement and should therefore be appropriate, respectful, and customer led.
- Agents may use light, friendly humour only when the customer’s tone allows (e.g., casual, positive, or playful interactions). Banter must not undermine sincerity, especially in sensitive, complaint, or escalated scenarios.

**Maintain professionalism in all customer engagements**

Professionalism in social media refers to communicating with customers in a clear, respectful, and customer-centric manner while adapting to their preferred language and communication style. Agents should provide information that is easy to understand, avoid internal jargon, and maintain a consistent professional image in every interaction to deliver a positive customer experience.

This will be achieved by the guidelines below:

- Agent should communicate in Kiswahili or English effectively and clearly.
- Where the customer has used both languages, the agent can use the dominant language to respond
- The information given to the customer must be clear and easily understood by the recipient.
- Avoid use of company jargon when responding to the customers: - for example Service Request, Siebel, escalate, HLR etc.
- Use of everyday speak/slang and mixing of Kiswahili and English will be allowed where the agent is mirroring the customer’s choice of language.
- All posts in vernacular (Luo, Kikuyu, etc.) will be responded to in Swahili to ensure the entire public is maintained in the conversation and avoiding getting our responses lost in translation.
- Posts done in other foreign languages i.e. German, French etc. will be responded to in the respective language as they are considered international languages thus possibility of responses getting lost in translation is minimal.
- A professional image must always be maintained regardless of the language used.

**SOCIAL MEDIA COMPETENCY**

To demonstrate Basic Social Media Competency the checks to include;

- Identification of emojis, emoticons and trending topics.
- Social Media lingo and abbreviations responses.
- Basic Social Media tools user issues e.g. follow backs before DM requests, blanket tweets when responding to customers.
- The CEO must be copied in where the customer had copied him while contacting us. Knowledgeable and going an extra mile;
- Avoiding Q&A and basically having a conversation; Ability to control an interaction especially difficult customers; Brand ambassador and taking ownership;
- Not being robotic, bring in the human side.
- Where the customer has posted personal data on the timeline or the wall, the agent should advise the customer to delete the personal details to avoid exposure to fraud and instead share the details via DM or inbox.

**NPS LINK**

NPS is influenced by the quality of customer interactions, as every engagement shapes the customer's perception of the brand and willingness to recommend it. Agents should therefore share the NPS feedback link with eligible customers, enabling them to provide feedback on their experience. This feedback helps the business measure customer loyalty, satisfaction, identify improvement opportunities, and drive enhancements to the overall customer experience.

Below is our guide on when to share the NPS Link.

After resolving the customer’s issue, the agent should send the NPS survey link to the customer. For example, where Escalation has been done via SR or Reversal has been initiated and customer advised on SLA. However, this does not apply for the progressive responses where the customer is still required to get back to us with more details.

 If the customer’s issue was on X timeline, the NPS survey link should be sent via DM and if on Facebook wall, the NPS survey link should be sent via Inbox.

**Note:** If NPS is shared on the X timeline or Facebook wall, this parameter will be marked as NO.

**PROGRESSIVE PENALIZATION**

Progressive Penalization is a quality management approach that applies increasing penalty weightings to repeated errors across consecutive assessments. Its purpose is to drive continuous improvement, reinforce accountability, and discourage recurring non-compliance by making repeat mistakes progressively more impactful on an agent's score**.**

- It’s a feature which allows us to apportion more weighting penalties in a KPI in consecutive assessments. For example, on assessment 1, the agent is penalized on failing to offer a DIY.
- On assessment 2, should they again fail to offer a DIY, the resulting penalty will have a higher weighting than the first assessment.
- Consequently, on assessment 3, the penalty levied will carry the highest weighting of all 3 assessments.

**In summary**, if the same error is identified in consecutive assessments, the resulting penalty will increase and have a greater effect on the score. The goal is to support sustained improvement and prevent recurring mistakes.

# **Eligibility**

a) Bingwa Sokoni service is eligible to all Dealers, M-PESA Agents, Lipa Na M-PESA merchants, Apartment Caretakers (for FTTH recommendation) and customers who register with agents as BAs

b) The number onboarding must not be registered as a corporate line.

c) BA onboarding on Bingwa should be at least 6 months active on the Safaricom network.

d) BA onboarding on Bingwa Sokoni must be provide their national or passport any order identification document that was used during line registration. This information must be validated in our subscriber profile database and must be accurate.

e) BA onboarding on Bingwa Sokoni must not be blacklisted or flagged as fraud according to our subscriber database profile.

f) BA onboarding on Bingwa Sokoni must be attached to a Bingwa Sokoni M-PESA Agent or Lipa na M-PESA Till.

g) M-PESA Agents & LNM Tills must use the till MSISDN to onboard & select option 1. LNM nominated numbers cannot onboard as Merchants but can onboard as Bingwa Ambassadors under option 2.

h) **M-PESA Agents and Till Merchants onboarding on Bingwa should be 30 days active on the Safaricom network**.

# **Commission Payment**

Bingwa sokoni agents earn a 10% commission for all GSM successful recommendations.    The reward will be accumulated and paid out as a lump sum to the Agent, Merchant or BA (the one who recommended the offers) every week on Wednesday as cash via M-PESA.

Agents and merchants should be able to nominate a number they would like payments to be processed through. This number should be a valid Safaricom MSISDN.

BAs have the onboarding MSISDN as the default payout number and need not nominate one.

# **Bingwa Sokoni Mechanics**

i.         Customer walks into an outlet (M-PESA Agent or dealer shop).

ii.         The BA/Agent or Merchant will introduce and recommend the service to the customer as well as help them to subscribe to the service (Example; Tunukiwa)

iii.         The BA/Agent or Merchant dials \*180\*5#ok and selects offer to recommend.

iv.         Agent enters Customer MSISDN.

v.         After MSISDN validation, a check is done in CVM to ensure the customer is only recommended to once per day. If customer is already recommended, BA/Agent or Merchant gets a notification.

vi.         If customer is not already recommended, USSD fetches the hot deals of the customer from CVM. The hot deals are displayed on the USSD and the BA/Agent or Merchant selects the desired offer.

vii.         After selection, the BA/Agent or Merchant selects payment method.

viii.         Recommendation record will not succeed if verification of purchase fails.

ix.         For customer to pay, customer must purchase offer within 3 hours for agent to earn commission. If offer expires after 3 hours agent will not earn commission.

x.         Commission payout is made as a lumpsum every week on Wednesday.

# **NOTE:**

- Agents and BAs can use the ‘Pay for Customer’ or ‘Customer to Pay’ payment options for the offers. LNM tills only have "customer to pay" as the only option of completing purchase.
- An offer can only be recommended once per day per MSISDN. However, different offers can be recommended to the same MSISDN per day.

# **Bingwa Sokoni Offers**

Bingwa Sokoni currently has the below offers available for recommendation

GSM Offers

Content Offers

Device Offers.

Ofa ya Boda and Bundle ya Dere Offers

# **GSM Offers**

These are recommendations for minutes, data, airtime and SMS offers.

The offers are dynamic in nature and have hourly, daily, weekly and monthly offers as well as neo(no expiry)offers.

Agent selects either sell Calls and SMS bundles or Sell Data bundles from the menu

The offers are updated from time to time as business demands.

**Mechanics**

a) The recommending Bingwa agent dials \*180\*5#

b) The agent selects sell calls and sms bundles or sell data bundles

c) The agent then enters the customer’s number

d) The agent selects customer’s preferred offer or amount customer wishes to spend

e) Agent selects payment mode.

f) If agent selects ‘customer to pay’ notification is sent to customer with the USSD string the customer should use to buy offer. If agent selects ‘pay for customer’ agent selects account to use to pay (Airtime or M-PESA)

g) Agent enters M-PESA PIN if M-PESA is selected.

h) Both agent and customer get appropriate notifications on recommendation or completed purchase.

# **NOTE NEW UPDATE ON GSM**

Effective 7th August 2026. Bingwa Sokoni bundle recommendations will be guided by the time of day as below:

**Between 11:00 PM – Next day 3:59 PM**\- KSh 20 = 1GB Bundle Valid for 1 hour (This bundle can be recommended to eligible customers during this period ONLY)

**Data Bundles Available Throughout the Day**\- These bundles can be recommended to customers at any time.

i.         All Daily Pata More Bundles

ii.         All Weekly Pata More Bundles

iii.         All Monthly Pata More Bundles

Bingwa Sokoni agents be advised to dial \*180\*5# to view the latest available bundles before making any recommendations & to ensure that only the revised bundles are recommended to customers.

Customers to always confirm available offers via \*544#, \*555# or on the One App before sending any money to the Bingwa Sokoni Agents.

# **Sell Content Offers**

**Definition:**

This is a service where partners are rewarded for recommending Safaricom content.

 **Eligibility**

The eligible bundles are:

i.         MsingiPack Access only @ Ksh 10

ii.         Baze Daily Access (Autorenew) @ Ksh 10

**Mechanics**

a) Customer walks into a partner outlet (M-PESA Agent or dealer shop)

b) Agent recommends Msingi Pack and Baze

c) Agent enters customer number (MSISDN)

d) Agent chooses the Customer to Pay option

e) Agent receives a message informing of successful recommendation or failure and reason for failure being another recommendation has been done.

f) Party B receives notification thanking him/her for visiting the agency plus a call to action on bundle purchase

g) Upon buying the bundle the customer gets confirmation message on successful purchase with an option to opt out if it’s a renewable bundle, while the agent gets a notification of successful purchase and commission earned

**NB**: Recommendation can only be done once per day per MSISDN

**Payment**

a. BAs will earn 10% of offer price cash incentives for a bundle successfully sold

b. A customer must purchase & be billed for the recommended content offer within 3 hours.

c. The commission earned will be sent to the number that was used to recommend the Bundle.

d. The reward will be accumulated and paid out as a lump sum every week as cash via Mpesa.

# **Sell Phones (Device Offers)**
