articleTitle: M-PESA Line Recycle Definition, Eligibility and Mechanics
markdownContent:
# **M-PESA RECYCLED LINE**

Automation of the M-PESA recycling process seeks to recycle on-demand M-PESA lines with previous owners' M-PESA details through CRM line Recycle VBC. 

# **Step-by-step process**

Where the CEE receives a call from a subscriber indicating that they have purchased a new line and they are not able to register on M-PESA.

# **Check the details below**

Confirm on CRM /Siebel the first call event date.

It's important to verify the full date details: i.e., Day/Month/Year

Confirm the M-PESA registration date on the M-PESA system.

If the registration date is not indicated in the M-PESA system, then confirm under the activity log when the account was created or registered.

Verify full date details: i.e., Day/Month/Year of registration of M-PESA service.  

Where both dates are matching, advice the customer that the line is duly registered and guide on how to access the M-PESA Menu.

**NB: If the M-PESA registration was done earlier than the 1st event date on CRM.**

The CEE will search number on Siebel > Select Line recycle VBC > Click on MPESA recycle to submit for recycling.

Upon recycling, a pop-up notification will be auto populated on CRM indicating the request has been successfully submitted.

The CEE will refresh the MSISDN search on CRM and on M-PESA G2 to confirm the status of the recycle process which is either a success or failure.

On CRM a record will be captured showing the recycling is completed on the ‘Recycle Description’ column of the VBC, the timestamp of the action and the user details of the agent who has performed the request.

On M-PESA G2, the customer account will be archived including any funds in the customer MMF account. The MSISDN will be populated as an unregistered number upon searching again on G2.

Where the status is successful, CEE advises the customer to proceed to the M-PESA dealer/agent outlets to register the line with their original ID.

Where the status is failed, the CEE will raise an SR with the following Fields: 

 [Screenshot] 

Enter the 1st event date as shown on the Siebel system and the M-PESA registration date on the notes of the SR and escalate via service request to

M-PESA support team to recycle the account on M-PESA system. 

Advise the customer on 24-hour SLA. 

Advise the customer that they will receive an SMS message from Safaricom informing them to visit the nearest Safaricom authorized dealer or shop with their Original ID to register the line on M-PESA. (Confirm the location of the customer if not in an area with a Safaricom retail centre outlet; advise them to visit any M-PESA outlet near them). 

# **Reasons for failure**

M-PESA recycling will fail in the following scenarios -:

- Where the customer’s account has pending tasks or reserved funds due to a pending authorized transaction.
- Where a customer’s account has funds in the Pochi La Biashara account.

Interaction is auto created on the request, indicating the status, the creator, and the date. 

Thank the customer and end the call.

articleTitle: Siebel Key Comment Guideline Definition, CEE Required Key comments & Fraud State Tags
markdownContent:
**Definition**

Key comments: They are notes captured on Siebel to quickly alert anyone accessing the account of a unique case of customer behaviour.

**CEE Required Key comments**

CEE should only capture key comment on Siebel, in case a customer reports having shared his/her details to a fraudster, to protect the customer’s account.

Key comments should not be captured for **repeat callers** and **abusive customers.** The CEE will bring into play soft skills to manage the customer on call. If the call does not yield fruit, the CEE will liaise with Team Leader on duty.

**Fraud State Tags & CRM Key Comments**

When a Line is blocked on M-PESA by fraud team for various reasons, and a ‘state tag’ is put in place on G3, a Key Comment will be created on Siebel giving guidance on the steps to be followed.

Below are the Key comments that will be captured on the lines on Siebel to guide the CEE on the action to take to resolve the customers’ issues.

| Fraud state tag suspensions- Key comment | Call Center Action | Retail Center Action | Reversal Action |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Reported on 333 refer to RC for vetting and unbarring, CEE to remove state tag once sub passes vetting | Advise customer to visit RC | Follow Key comment guideline | For all state tag blocked lines, If a customer calls for reversal, the CEEs will be required to; Refer Customer to Retail for reversal. |
| Customer to visit RC only (not franchise) for vetting and unbarring, CEE to remove state tag once customer passes vetting. | Advise customer to visit RC | Follow Key comment guideline | |
| Disputed registration by primary number on 106 or KYC, CEE to vet customer unbar line on HLR and remove state tag and advise customer on DIY option of dialing *106*5# | Advise customer on DIY option to cancel report they made. Otherwise refer to RC. | Follow Key comment guideline | |
| Customer to visit RC for vetting and unbarring: CEE to unbar line and remove state tag once customer passes vetting. | Advise customer to visit RC | Follow Key comment guideline | |

articleTitle: Fraud Actions required by both Call Center and Retail CEE
markdownContent:
**Fraud: SIM Swap: This is a till that was found doing irregular /fraudulent swaps**

**Key Comment:**

SIM Swap fraud do not unbar -sanctions is termination

**Action Required by both Call Centre / Retail CEE**

Inform Agent that the till was barred for SIM Swap fraud and it is due for termination.

Agent can visit Safaricom HQ1 with H/Office for clarifications.

**Fraud: Irregular Registration**

Spamming, SIM Box and Multiple registrations with same ID. These are tills that have been blocked for carrying out irregular registrations.

**Key Comment:**

Spamming / SIM Box / Multiple registrations do not unbar.

**Action Required by both Call Centre / Retail CEE**

CEE to advise Agent suspension period is three months from date of barring by Fraud.

If suspension period has lapsed send the till to Network fraud via NetworkFraud&M-pesasection@safaricom.co.ke for unbarring.

Inform Agent for future registrations, they will be using \*195\*4#

**Fraud: Suspicious B2C transactions e.g. Equity.**

These are B2C transactions that appear suspicious which the banks/ saccos/ financial institutions have requested we hold funds as they validate, or they have confirmed transactions fraudulent.

**Key Comment:**

Suspicious B2C transactions, refer customer to Security department of Bank xxxx or

Refer customer to organization Fraud team for validation/clearance

**Action Required by both Call Centre / Retail CEE**

Customer to be referred to the Head office of the financial institution where their Security department is based for clearance and Send an email to NetworkFraud&M-pesasection@safaricom.co.ke

**Fraud: Irregular registration / acquisition of golden numbers**

**Key Comment:**

‘Do not unbar-Refer to Fraud Team, irregular registration of a Golden number’

**Action Required by both Call Centre / Retail CEE**

Refer to Fraud Team

**Customer Fraud Reporting Process**

In some cases, particularly where investigation findings support customer remediation or reimbursement, a police-written statement is also required. As this requirement is often identified later in the process, customers are compelled to make an additional visit to the police station to obtain and submit the statement.

**Effective immediately**, customers reporting fraud-related incidents at our shops will be required to provide both the **OB number** and **a police-written statement** at the point of reporting. These documents should then be attached to the Service Request (SR) raised for the case.

State Tags are added on customers or organizations accounts for different reasons.

Different type of Fraud/AML State Tags exists as below:

**Fraud Suspend state tag**

When added will prevent outflow of funds. This restricts funds movement outbound e.g. A reversal will not be possible or when the customer attempts to send or withdraw from a fraud suspended account.

**Fraud Freeze Tag**

When added will prevent inflow and outflow of funds. This restricts funds movement inbound and outbound.

Normal escalations channels for fraud related queries remain.

**Informational Tags**

A communication tag, similar to Key Comment on CRM. The tag will be used to relay information on a customer's MSISDN or Organization short code. It does not affect transactions on M-PESA. It can be:

1. Customer Comment Tag or
2. Organization Comment Tag.

**Kindly note:**

- **DO NOT** place any State Tag at Head Office (HO) level or on aggregated Agency short code. This action prevents commission roll up task.
- **DO NOT REMOVE/MANAGE DEBTORS' TAG** **FROM MERCHANTS** ON G3. Kindly note that this tag is automated and in no way prevents initiation of a reversal transaction. When the Debtors tag is manually removed, it disrupts the flow of the task that should be working to remove or restore the tag where a merchant pays or defaults on Fuliza Biashara loan. 

Kindly do not manage the debtors' tag as it is automated. Attached is a view of the DEBTORS' Tag on M-PESA G3.

| Fraud state tag suspensions- Key comment | Call Center Action | Retail Center Action | Reversal Action |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Reported on 333 refer to RC for vetting and unbarring, CEE to remove state tag once sub passes vetting | Advise customer to visit RC | Follow Key comment guideline | For all state tag blocked lines, if a customer calls for reversal, the CEEs will be required to; Refer Customer to Retail for reversal. |
| Customer to visit RC only (not franchise) for vetting and unbarring, CEE to remove state tag once customer passes vetting. | Advise customer to visit RC | Follow Key comment guideline | |
| Disputed registration by primary number on 106 or KYC, CEE to vet customer unbar line on HLR and remove state tag and advise customer on DIY option of dialing *106*5# | Advise customer on DIY option to cancel report they made. Otherwise refer to RC. | Follow Key comment guideline | |
| Customer to visit RC for vetting and unbarring: CEE to unbar line and remove state tag once customer passes vetting. | Advise customer to visit RC | Follow Key comment guideline | |

**Suspension via a court order**

Any customer line **suspended via a court order** you advise them it can only be unsuspended by **another court order**. For further details, the customer can visit the relevant court quoted.  E.g., in this case Dagoretti Law court registry with the referenced court order number “**DAGORRETI, SCCCOMM/E490/2025”**

Do not remove tags for LEL and /or do any transactions including reversals on those numbers without consulting LEL

 **Legal State Tags**

 We have two legal state tags – Legal Suspend Tag and Legal Freeze Tag

- **Legal Suspend Tag**: when applied, it suspends the account, allowing it to receive funds but restricting any outgoing transactions.
- **Legal Freeze Tag**: when assigned, inflow and outflow of funds will not be possible.

- These tags are used to manage legal requests, including garnishee orders from Legal and LEL teams.
- **Adding/Removing**: The tag can **ONLY** be added or removed by Merchants, Operations user, Operations Manager and Legal teams.
- The tag can be viewed by all teams when applied.
- **Reversal**: For reversal requests involving a short code or MSISDN with this tag, kindly escalate via SR using the existing categories with very clear comments.

**Dormancy State Tag**

- This tag is used to manage the dormancy process for inactive short codes, specifically those dormant for more than six months as per dormancy process.
- When applied, the short code will be **fully frozen**, meaning no debit or credit transactions can occur.
- This tag is strictly applicable to short codes and should not be used on MSISDNs.
- **Adding/Removing:** The tag can be applied or removed by teams who have been assigned the permission example M-PESA Corporate, Retail CEE, Retail TL/Manager/Call Centre Analyst, Reversal Admin Team, Merchants, Operation User etc.
- The tag can be viewed by all teams when assigned to a short code.
- **Reversal**: For reversal, settlement requests etc. involving a short code with the dormancy tag, please remove the tag, process the reversal, and reinstate the tag with the original comments.
- **Reactivation**: If a customer calls to have the short code reactivated for use or to pay merchant loans/OD, note the following:

- Short codes whose details have been forwarded to UFAA will contain ‘UFAA’ in the comment section. These short codes should not be reactivated. Advise merchant to apply or a new short code.
- Short codes with dormancy tag only can be reactivated. Vet merchant and reactivate. Merchant emails must originate from then organization email on G3. For calls, merchant must call from Nominated number. 
- If other state tags exist besides the dormancy state tag, please take into account the comments from those other tags.

articleTitle: Issuance of Start Key at the Contact Center
markdownContent:
# **Unlocking M-PESA PIN**

When a customer calls to unlock their M-PESA account, CEE shall vet the customer, unlock the account if the customer has passed vetting. 

Where customer’s names on View 360 do not completely tally with the names on M-PESA, or fails the primary vetting/personal details (Full names, ID and YoB) kindly refer them to retail Centre or Care Desk for assistance.

If the customer fails vetting, the CEE shall advise the customer to confirm their vetting details and call back or visit the nearest Safaricom Shop / Care desk with their original ID for assistance or use the below available DIY channels.

For all the scenarios above, always inform the customer of the available DIY channels (below).

**NOTE:** If a customer **calls twice and fails vetting**, CEE should refer the customer to the nearest Safaricom shop / Care Desk with their original ID card.

# **USSD**

Dial *\*334#*

Select *My Account*

Select *Unlock* *M-PESA PIN*

Enter your *M-PESA ID Number*

Wait for confirmation message.

# **IVR**

Call 100/200

On the voice prompt select the option for *M-PESA Help and Reversal*

Select *Unlock M-PESA PIN*

Type you *M-PESA ID number* when asked to

Wait for confirmation message.

# **Zuri**

Open Zuri on WhatsApp or Messenger

On the voice prompt select the option for *M-PESA Help and Reversal*

Select *M-PESA PIN Unlock*

Type you *M-PESA ID number* when asked to

Wait for confirmation message.

# **My Safaricom App**

Select M-PESA menu.

Select Account

Select M-PESA Unlock

Enter ID/Passport Number

Wait for confirmation message.

# **M-PESA App**

When the customer locks their PIN while transacting on M-PESA App, they will receive a pop-up requesting them to enter their ID number to unlock.

Also, when attempting to transact, they will be presented with a screen to unlock the PIN.

**N****OTE****:** The customer must use the document ID that was used to register the M-PESA account**.**

# **Forgotten M-PESA PIN**

If a customer has forgotten their M-PESA PIN, the normal M-PESA Start Key vetting applies (check on Fraud Location, SIM swap OTA).

CEE shall check if the customer has done **a positive M-PESA authenticated transaction in the last 24 hours****,** if the customer has successfully done a PIN authenticated transaction **within the last 24 hrs**. (E.g., send Money, Pay Bill, buy airtime, Balance Check etc.) the CEE shall **refer the customer to** **Retail** for the PIN reset. The CEE should also give the Start Key Reset DIY.

If a customer who had been referred to retail calls back later having not visited retail (Reference interactions to confirm this) kindly refer the customer to retail.

CEE shall check if there is any replacement done on the customers line within 24hrs (check on orders and Interactions), if a sim replacement has been done and a customer call for a start key **before 24hrs have elapsed,** CEE should advise the customer to call after 24hrs or visit Safaricom shop for assistance. The CEE will also give the Start Key Reset DIY & inform the customer that the PIN Reset DIY after Sim swap is available after **7 days & not 24hrs.**

Where the customer calls back **after 24hrs** vet and assist as per the Call Center guidelines.

**NOTE:**  PIN Reset after SIM swap on DIY is **7 days not 24hrs**

Where the customer is calling on behalf of the owner, CEE should give the start key DIY.

After successful vetting, the start key is issued, and customer is advised on how to use it.

When customer **fails vetting**, they should confirm the vetting details then **call back or visit retail/Care desk with ID** for assistance. CEE should ensure they give the start key DIY.

If a customer **calls twice and fails vetting**, CEE should refer the customer to the nearest **Safaricom shop / Care Desk with their original ID card**.

All customer attempts to unlock the M-PESA account are captured on M-PESA audit log.

**NB:** Please educate the customer on how to set the security questions and reset PIN for them to be able to self-serve in future. Use below message as a guide;

***Jambo, dial \*334# >My Account>M-PESA PIN Manager >Set M-PESA Security Questions and answers>Enter ID/PP number>Set 3 Questions>Enter M-PESA PIN. Thankyou.***

***Jambo, to reset PIN Dial \*334#OK>My Account>M-PESA PIN Manager>M-PESA Forgot PIN>Enter ID/PP number>Answer security questions provided to get Pin. Thankyou.***

**Activation of M-PESA account with 7-digit ID**

Customers who have 7-digit IDs, The CEE shall assist the customer and advise them on how the ID appears on G2 for future reference.

CEE shall vet as per Contact Centre vetting procedure. If customer passes vetting, follow the procedure below:

Go to the Customer Info page on G2.

Click on the Unlock PIN icon that will appear as the first icon.

Then Unlock PIN pop up will appear.

Enter the Reason and vetting details.

Select Submit

The success operation pop-up will appear, select Confirm.

You will unlock the M-PESA account then educate the customer on M-PESA unlock DIY.

If the customer fails vetting, they should confirm vetting details then call back or visit retail Center / Care desk with ID for assistance and CEE shall educate the customer on DIY.

**NOTE:** If the customer is not able to reactivate the account using the 7 digits ID number, then the DOB information can be given on call for the special cases where the date of birth on M-PESA system is indicated as below:

**DDMM2014:** We shall issue the DDMMYY since the details were edited as a result of data clean up on the system by default.

**0101YY:** If the customer gets the YY (year) right, the CEE will give the DD(Date) and MM(Month) and advise on activation. If the customer does not get the YY(Year) then escalate via the SR for the customer to be enabled to activate with the 7 digits ID.

**3112YY:** If the customer gets the YY (year) right, the CEE will give the DD(Date) and MM (month) and advise the customer on activation. If the customer does not get the YY (year) then escalate via the SR for the customer to be enabled to activate with the 7 digits ID.

If the customer has provided the correct 7-digit ID number but the DOB given is wrong and does not fall under the special cases listed above, **DO NOT** give the DOB on the system but raise an SR for the customer to be enabled to activate with the 7 digits ID.

After a SIM swap, the CEE shall proactively check on the DOB and ID number then advise on activation/Raise an SR in line with the tips above.

Upon successful activation of the M-PESA account, the customer shall receive an SMS message as sampled below informing them that the M-PESA PIN has been changed successfully.

| Event | Channel | Message |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Successful Request submission | USSD | Your request has been received.Please wait for a confirmation message. |
| Successful PIN Unlock | SMS | Your account has been unlocked. You can now use your correct M-PESA PIN to transact. |
| Unsuccessful PIN Unlock – Wrong ID | SMS | Failed. Kindly enter the correct document of registration |
| Unsuccessful PIN Unlock – Maximum Unlocked times reached | SMS | Failed. You have reached the maximum of 5 times to unlock your account. Kindly call customer care 100 for assistance. |
| PIN Not locked | SMS | Your account is not locked. Kindly use your correct M-PESA PIN to transact. |
| Failed - Account does not exist | SMS | Failed. Your M-PESA account is not available. Kindly call customer care 100 for assistance. |
| Failed - Account is Suspended | SMS | Failed. Your M-PESA account is not available. Kindly call customer care 100 for assistance. |
| Failed - Account is Frozen fraud | SMS | Failed. Your M-PESA account is not available. Kindly visit Safaricom HQ1 Waiyaki way, risk department for assistance |

# **Troubleshooting Wrong M-PESA PIN**

The customer may need to double press the shift key to change letters into numbers depending on the type of phone they are using.

# **Checks on the Calling Number**

Proceed only if the calling number is a Safaricom number. 

Non-Safaricom number callers should be advised to visit the nearest Safaricom shop(RC,Franchise) or the nearest M-PESA agent. 

·       **Line Status:**

i.         **Calling for self:**  Serve only if calling number is in Active or Expiry state on **IN DATA**  

ii.         **Calling on behalf:**  Serve only if calling number is in Active state on **IN DATA.**

If not active, advice the customer to call back with an active line or ask the owner of the line to visit retail/Care desk with registration document for assistance.

articleTitle: M-PESA Statement issuing at the Retail Centre
markdownContent:
**Statement for individual Customer and Requirements**

1. A customer can get a printout of the statement or sent to their Email from any Safaricom shop or care desk.
2. The charges for a printout are **Ksh.10** **per page**, sent to the Email is **not** charged.

**Requirements**

The customer shall present any of the below documents:

**Original and valid ID as per acceptable KYC** **ie** National ID/Valid passport/ Military /Foreign Nationals Certificate (Alien ID)/Diplomatic ID

**Individual customer has lost ID, they shall present:**

Original waiting card (New version), (Issued within 2 months),

Clear copy of valid ID document (**Mandatory**)

Police abstract (Issued within 3 months).

OR

Original waiting card (Old version)

Clear copy of valid ID document (**Mandatory**)

Police abstract (Issued within 3 months)

4. CEE should only stamp statements they have printed.
5. CEE shall raise an interaction on CRM capturing the below details: Customer ID number, Duration of statement issued and POS receipt number.

**NOTE**:

All the statements issued at Safaricom Retail Centre outlets are for personal use **ONLY**.

In adherence to our Data Privacy Policy, customer statements must **NOT** be issued to third parties or to any customer accompanied by another individual. All requests for statements must be made by the account holder in person and they should not be intimidated to obtaining the statement against their will.

**Statement for next of Kin**

Requirements for a deceased customer MPESA account statement by next of kin;

1. Affidavit.
2. Letter from county administration / county government,
3. Original death certificate
4. Original ID of person making request.
5. Written request from claimant (M-PESA Next of kin statement claim form)

**NB: -** This will only apply for issuance of M-PESA statements for next of kin.

Normal M-PESA process will apply in processing of claims for the funds available.

Once all the requirements have been presented, the CEE shall:

i.  Vet the documents and validate the identification documents of the claimant

ii.   Upon authentication the CEE shall honor the respective customer’s request

iii.   Scan all documents and attach them on CRM. The attachments must be clear copies and scans of both sides where applicable. For an audit trail the attachments shall be done on the MSISDN at the account level and if the MSISDN is recycled the CEE shall attach them on the closed account.

iv.    Capture an interaction on CRM indicating the issue and the resolution give. The CEE must clearly indicate the information shared with the customer i.e. date range for statements, exact balances and accounts given

**Certified /Legal Statement**

M-PESA statements to be used in a criminal matter by police or other government/ law enforcement agencies or for civil cases should be advised on the two scenarios as below: -

**a)**  **Requests done by government bodies/ police**

1.    The police investigators handling the case will be required to obtain a court order from a court of law with;

·       An Affidavit.

·       Warrant to investigate an account.

·       Notice of motion.

2. Dully signed letter by a senior police officer that contains a brief description of the case.

4. Letter from law enforcement agencies mailed from the respective county commander’s office after it is vetted then mailed to law enforcement liaison on lawenforcementliaison@Safaricom.co.ke
5. Feedback will be mailed to the county commanders’ office of the requesting officer by Law Enforcement Liaison.

**NB:** **Court orders should be delivered to Legal Department, at Safaricom Headquarters.**

**b)**  **Requests done by lawyers / individuals who have no lawyer**

For accused person or for any other purpose connected with the police or any other law enforcement agency;

1. Drop the letter written by a lawyer requesting for the statements at the Legal Department at Safaricom headquarters (HQ1) or at the nearest retail centre for onward transmission to the Legal Department.

2. The request letter should be addressed to the head of legal and secretarial services.

3. If the statement is for a criminal case and the customer does not have a lawyer, the customer will:

1. Put it in writing.
2. Indicate the nature of the case.
3. Indicate s/he does not have a lawyer.
4. Attach a copy of his/her ID.

**NB**: We will only accept letters from Lawyers at Retail and not Court orders.

**Requests for MPESA statements for use in Police Vetting**

1. Requests received by the force to be used by the **Police Vetting Board** as per authorization received for the exercise.
2. The process is only applicable for purpose of statements to be used for this exercise.
3. The written request is logged in from the retail stores and care desks, CEE / staff will receive the request from the customer to forward their MPESA details to the vetting board.

**Request for MPESA statements for civil matters**

1. Civil cases: - Involve private disputes between persons or organizations.
2. If the statement is required for a civil matter, then the customer must fill in civil disputes statement request form indicating the purpose of use.
3. Statements issued for this purpose will be restricted to civil cases and not criminal cases. (Criminal cases are cases that involve a police investigation and/or prosecution)
4. Reference in this case therefore, provision to use the MPESA statements issued by Safaricom for use of settling private disputes.
5. CEE will confirm form is duly filled and scan a copy of customer ID, as per the retail vetting procedures, and advice customer of 6 days SLA.
6. If the statement is for personal use, retail may proceed and generate the statement as per the existing process.

**NB**: Third party collection of statement will not be allowed.

**Sub Agents Unmasked Statements Request Guide:**

The guide follows the civil statement process, and the sub agent is required to fulfill the following:

Have a valid OB

Should be the Primary Assistant created on the store on Fintech/G3 system

Their number should be the nominated number on Fintech/G3 System.

**Unmasked M-PESA Statement issuance at the Retail Centre**

i.         Team Leaders/Managers have now been empowered to issued unmasked MPESA statements for a period of up to 3 days from the date of request.

ii.         Unmasked M-PESA statements for a period of up to **three** (3) days from the date of request will be issued at the retail outlet by the Retail **Team Leader** or **Manager**

iii.         The CEE will verify that the request form has been duly completed, scan and attach a copy of the customer's ID in line with the retail vetting procedures and advise the customer of the 2-hour SLA.

iv.         The Team Leader/Manager will query the customer's MSISDN, authenticate the request via OTP, generate the requested statement, and subsequently close the SR.

v.         Where the statement request is for personal use, the retail team may proceed to generate and issue the statement in accordance with the existing statement issuance process.

**M-PESA Statements for Citizens of the future**

Citizen of the future application forms require M-PESA statements for at least **6 months** for non employed guardians/parents. 

**NOTE:**

- Retail centres do not stamp or certify M-PESA statements not printed in the retail canter.
- The current system application at the Retail Centre Outlets allows them to print customers’ M-PESA transactional data from the launch of M-PESA service in 2007.

articleTitle: Enterprise Bulk Airtime Top Up & Enterprise Wallet
markdownContent:
# **Definition**

Bulk airtime top-up is a capability targeting Enterprise clients to buy airtime in bulk then have Safaricom top-up the airtime resources to a list of lines provided by the client.

Bulk airtime top-up service allows Enterprises to provide airtime resources to their employees and or clients in bulk.

The airtime recipients are allowed to use the resources for any of the prepay offers.

# **Benefits of Enterprise Bulk airtime top up**

·       Provides value propositions to enterprise by offering more resources at a discounted rate.

·       Reduces the cash handling and workload for the multiple top-ups to hundreds and thousands of employees.

·       Creates revenue stream for digital businesses that can offer airtime top-up as a value-added service to their customers.

·       Enables businesses to reach and reward customers in emerging markets or unbanked populations.

·       It enhances customer loyalty and retention by providing a convenient and appreciated service.

**Sambaza**

**Can recipients of Enterprise Bulk Top Up Sambaza the airtime (from the Enterprise Wallet)?**

·       Yes, the airtime recipient will be able to Sambaza their awarded airtime resources.

·       They will use the process: USSD (\*485\*140#, and \*485\*140\*amount\*MSISDN#) for clients with feature devices and/or use MYSAFARICOM APP for clients with smart devices.

# **Balance Checks**

**Prepaid customers:** Dial \*144#ok; it will show the total amount of airtime, i.e. total of Prepaid top up + Enterprise Bulk top up. They can also use MySafaricom App.

**Hybrid customers:** Customer to use the MySafaricom app, voice call to 144 (charged), or the SMS balance inquiry by sending "bal" to 144.

How to sign-up for Enterprise Bulk airtime top up

·       Enterprise customers will engage their Account Managers to sign up for the service.

·       The customer can also walk into a Retail store and sign up for the service.

·       They will provide their relevant KYC documents.

·       They will provide a list of the recipients and top up amount to which the top up will be sent to.

·       The customer will make payment at the Retail M-PESA till or provide an LPO.

·       The Retail shop attendant will access POS and perform a Bulk top up with reference to the Enterprise customers Account number details provided.

**(Important: The billing account must be selected and populated with the account number instead of MSISDN)**

**How does Enterprise Bulk airtime top up work?**

The existing process and systems have been enhanced to perform wallet separation between Enterprise and Consumer top up wallet on CBS.

# **Validity for Enterprise Bulk Topup airtime**

| RECHARGE | VALIDITY IN DAYS |
| --- | --- |
| 5 -10 | 30 |
| 11 - 20 | 45 |
| 21 - 1000 | 90 |
| 1001-200000 | 120 |

Notifications sent to the Enterprise client and recipient of the bulk top up

·    **Purchase alerts**: Enterprise client will receive alerts for the amount of resources purchased. These notifications will provide details about airtime amount and expiry date for the resources.

·    **One off alert:** Upon top-up to the dependent lines provided by the enterprise, email summary is sent to the enterprise confirming the top-up amount with details of what each of the target lines received.

·    **Usage alerts**: The recipient numbers are each alerted with the amount of airtime deposited in parallel to the predefined messages related to Prepay services that have been prescribed by the line owners.

Interaction for **Enterprise Bulk Top Up** **Airtime** has been created to manage queries coming through and for ease of picking any challenges with the use the airtime in this wallet.

**Management of numbers in pool – normal/ special & deleted numbers**

If a customer calls with a Line recreation request, the CEE shall do as below to recreate the line.

**Call Center Procedure**

This process is applicable for lines registered to individuals.

·       The recreation can only be done for the previous owner of the line. A customer may request for number recreation through any of the call center touch points.

·       Company/corporate requests will present Company PIN and a written recreation request at retail center, with company letter head, stamp, or seal.

- Recreation will only be done for normal lines. Golden number recreation requests will be referred to retail centers. To confirm if Line is golden refer to article number [NRBK-0001](../../app/article/2b3006fb-978a-4ba4-b6d3-160f16b698e1)
- The CEE will check the status of the line on INDATA on CRM to ensure it is pooled and for deleted line it will create an error. Whether status is pooled or there is an error on INDATA for deleted lines, CEE will vet the customer to confirm ownership.
- Primary vetting will be done via View 360 where the customer will provide the following details:
- Full names as per View 360 (Mandatory). The CEE can also accept if the customer gives 2 correct names. e.g., the first and last name.
- ID number (Mandatory).
- If the line has no details on View 360, **BUT** are registered on **CRM & MPESA G2,** CEE should **NOT** **recreate** the line but refer the customer to the Retail shop with their identification document for assistance.
- If a customer is roaming advise them to send an email with a scanned copy of ID/passport to advantage@safaricom.co.ke or customercare@safaricom.co.ke for assistance.

 Where the customer has the **OLD** simex, CEE should do the following.

·       Check for any key comments before performing any line recreation.

·       Vet the customer to confirm the names and ID number are as registered on View 360. If the customers details are not on View 360 **BUT** are registered on CRM & MPESA G2, CEE should **NOT** recreate the line but refer the customer to the Retail shop/Care desk with their identification document for assistance.

·       **DO NOT** recreate a number with a different serial number from the one on CRM.

·       Identify a line after recreation with View 360 details to enable the customer to top up and use the line.

·       The CEE be required to query the number afresh on CRM and keep on **refreshing** **severally** in order to confirm the details have been synchronized with the ones on View 360

**NOTE:** The reason for the **several refreshes** is to ensure that the previous account has been closed and that the line has synchronized and has come to idle status on subscriber portal and INDATA. A process which is done in the backend and takes a duration **between 5 to 10 mins.**

In cases where the synchronization has taken too long the CEE should proceed to raise an SR to 2nd line support for identification to be done capturing all the vetting details (Names, ID number, Old serial Number and Alternative contact if available).

**Definition**

This process outlines compensation procedures on the PREPAID BUSINESS FIBRE (FTTB) portfolio. The compensation can either be done as a data bundle or cash back on below scenarios.

I.         New connections delays.

II.         Individual reported outage.

III.         Global reported outage

**New Connection delay compensation**

For every newly registered / acquired customer, a remedy CRQ ticket is raised to the relevant contractor for installation works to commence.

Contractor shall contact the customer within 24 hours for planning and schedule installation, based on customers’ availability and preferred timings within 48 Hrs.

System shall auto pick the remedy ticket timestamp and start a time count to ascertain timely connections and identify delayed SLA status.

Any CRQ past 48hrs SLA that is not yet connected is auto processed for 1GB bundle award via Tibco service every day.

Affected clients receive notifications upon every award.

Data Bundle award shall be given to the customer who is the primary contact registered for the Fiber account.

Automated BI reports on award status are available on Qlik sense reports.

**Individual** **LOS (Loss of Service) compensation.** 

This is applicable to compensation of individual reports of LOS, affected active customers are compensated with 5GB Wema bundles at the point of reporting downtime and Cash back if the issue is not sorted within the 24hrs SLA.

L400 SUPPORT shall engage the customer where an isolated case is noted and confirm that the customer is active in terms of payment.

If a customer visits retail, CEE shall confirm that the customer is active in terms of payment and escalate the issue to L400 SUPPORT via email to [**Business.Support@safaricom.co.ke**](mailto:Business.Support@safaricom.co.ke)**.**

The CEE shall capture the customer’s PREPAID BUSINESS FIBRE (FTTB) account, contact and summary of customers issue, and advise customer on the 2hrs SLA.

L400 SUPPORT shall raise an incident to the contractor handling the region where customer resides and advises the customer on the 24hrs SLA.

CEE shall proceed to award the customer 5GB Wema data bundle valid for 48hrs.

The bundle shall be done to the customer’s registered primary contact for the Fiber account or a number they will nominate.

The dispatch team shall contact the customer to agree on the site visit timelines based on best available time slots.

The technician shall visit the site for troubleshooting and issue resolution.

The technician shall advise customer, accordingly, confirm service is up and close ticket. SLA for resolution is within 24 Hrs.

Where LOS is not resolved within 48Hrs; customers shall be compensated with 5 GB Wema bundle valid for 24Hrs every day until closure of customer issue.

**Global reported Outages**

This involves outages affecting ports, OLTs, BNG’s and Planned maintaince.

Where loss of service is noted, L400 SUPPORT shall trouble shoot to confirm if the same is a global outage affecting many customers.

Customers contacting any touch points other than L400 SUPPORT, shall be advised on PREPAID BUSINESS FIBRE (FTTB) support channels and CEE will escalate to L400 SUPPORT  via email to [Business.Support@safaricom.co.ke](mailto:Business.Support@safaricom.co.ke).

Where issue is noted to be affecting many users or a global outage, CEE shall advise the Line 400 folder lead in Customer Operations on duty who will alert the SOC team to assist raise an incident on BMC.

SOC team shall raise an incident to the contractor who shall visit site for troubleshooting and resolution within 4 Hours SLA.

L400 SUPPORT Folder Lead will liaise with the SOC team, extract the affected customers from NMS and send notification via SMS to the affected customers if the automated notifications from OWS fail.

L400 SUPPORT folder team lead shall filter the affected active customers from NMS and award with 5GB Wema Bundles if the automated bundle award from OWS fail to be awarded.

On fault resolution, technician shall notify SOC, accordingly, confirm service is up and close ticket.

SOC shall advise L400 Support for subsequent communication of service restoration to affected customers on mail if its noted service resumption notification from OWS fail.

Retention team shall engage customers on-ground in recovery activities where a business building is adversely affected.

Service Clinics visits will kick in place for such cases, and these customers shall be managed on hyper care until issue affecting them is conclusively resolved.

**Reporting**

Daily, weekly & monthly reports for 5GB Wema bundle, compensation and discounts will be shared by the Prepaid Business Fibre (FTTB) retention team. This will be done via email reports to relevant stakeholders.

Reports will be generated to include. 

MSISDN’s registered per CI.

Date and time of service unavailability,

Restoration time.

Total GB amounts awarded for period of LOS.

Total Cash credited to customer account for period of LOS.

Total discount awarded for period of LOS (for experience recovery initiative).

**DEVICE INSURANCE (TUUNZA SIMU)**

Device insurance (“Tuunza Simu”) is an all-risk cover that protects a customer’s device (in this case customer’s smartphone) against the risks of damage and theft of their devices. This policy covers against accidental damage, theft, and mechanical breakdown caused by accidental damage of the insured device.

**CREDIT LIFE BENEFIT UNDER DEVICE INSURANCE.**

For finance devices such us Lipa Mdogo Mdogo (LMM) or Onfon’s Lipa Mos Mos **we extend a** **credit life benefit**, **which covers the financed phone amount disbursed by a financier. The customer is covered against the risk of the unfortunate death. In case this happens, the insurer pays the outstanding financed amount to the financier.**

Credit life is only applicable under the propositions that allow customers to purchase devices under credit e.g. LMM and the PayGo propositions.

**ELIGIBILITY**

This insurance product is open to all Safaricom customers and partners who purchase devices from **Masoko,** **Safaricom Lipa Mdogo Mdogo devices and** **Safaricom PayGo partner – Onfon****.**

**CLAIMS WITHIN THE COVER PERIOD**

**Theft claims** - For theft and irreparable damage, you can make only one claim within the policy year.

**Screen replacement** - A maximum of one claim for screen replacement within the duration of the cover.

**Irreparable damage** – As will be assessed and advised by the authorized repair center and, the handset may be replaced at the discretion of the insurer. This is limited to only one instance.

**Other damages** - Repairs will continue until the total repair costs reach the value of the handset.

**TYPE OF INSURANCE COVER OFFERED**

**1.Embedded Insurance -**Embedded insurance refers to integration of insurance products seamlessly into the smartphone purchase process. By embedding insurance at the point of sale, customers can get the right insurance at purchase, simplifying the insurance purchase.

**2.As an opt in insurance benefit**\-This option will be available for customers who will not have access to the embedded device insurance benefit proposition. Safaricom customers, who are interested will be able to purchase device cover from the **Tuunza mini app**, **a marketplace available on the One App.**

**PREMIUMS**

Premiums are based on the value of the device. Premium rates vary from 2% to 6%. The device is covered immediately after the purchase process is complete or once customer activates insurance on the Tuunza mini app, given all necessary information is provided accurately.

**DURATION OF THE COVER**

The cover will run for a period of 12 to 36 months, depending on the device model type, from the date of purchase.

 **EXCLUSIONS**

While our insurance plans offer comprehensive coverage, the following are the general exclusions applicable: -

Wear and tear that result in the gradual deterioration of the device.

Incidents and damage covered by the manufacturer warranty.

Accessories including memory card, Screen Protectors, Covers, earphones, battery, chargers, and adaptors are not covered for loss or damage.

Damages or losses arising from participation in illegal activities e.g., acts of Terrorism, civil War, Rebellion, civil commotions, and mutiny.

**COVERAGE DETAILS:**

- **Accidental damage:** Covers issues like screen cracks and water damage.
- **Screen insurance** is limited to one claim per policy year.
- **Comprehensive:** Includes protection against theft, and accidental damage.
- **Replacement:** In case of theft, Safaricom will replace the device with the same or a similar priced model.

articleTitle: Interaction Definition and Guidelines at the Contact Centre and Retail
markdownContent:
**Definition of Interactions**

Interactions are records logged on customer’s account on CRM Siebel whenever customers contact Safaricom, where CEE refers to previous interactions, to get a clear understanding of the customer, both on Subscriber Level and Account level, when handling customer issues.

**Retail and Call Center Interaction Levels**

- Both at the Call Center and Retail, Interactions shall be captured on the subscriber level of the customer’s CRM account indicating the reason for contacting Safaricom and the resolution given.
- They are entered for all customer engagements either at the Account Level, Customer Level or Subscriber Level on CRM depending on the magnitude of the issue customer raises,

**Subscriber level**

- If a customer issue is for a specific MSISDN, the interaction will be raised under the subscriber.
- This is the default option for Prepaid and Individual Postpaid customer accounts.

 **[Screenshot]**

 [Screenshot] 

**Account level**

- Mostly applicable to corporates with aggregated (Parent) accounts,
- If a customer raises an issue to do with the whole customer account, especially where the account holds several MSISDNs, the interaction will be raised at the Account Level.

 **[Screenshot]**

**Customer level**

- This is mostly applicable to Corporates with several aggregated accounts.
- If the issue is to do with the whole customer organizations, e.g. Barclays, US Embassy etc., then the interaction will be raised under the customer level.

**Retail and Call Center Interaction Guidelines**

- Interactions logged under the Subscriber Level get archived after a certain Period.
- CEE will need to check for them under the Account Level, if missing under the Subscriber Level. When referring to previously logged interactions to make informed and resolution.
- Once archived, they are visible under the Account Level.
- Interactions will be logged towards the end of the call preferably during CEE’s closing remarks (Call Center) and the main reason for Customer’s visit (Retail) or whenever a customer account is accessed.
- Interactions shall be logged based on the main reason for accessing the customer account, defining the below fields;

**Profile:**

CEE shall define this based on the contact center skillset they are on when handling the customer issue.

Retail consumer profile picks automatically when a retail CEE is inputting interaction on CRM

**Action:**

The CEE shall select the appropriate option from the drop-down menu;

- **Agent on Customers Behalf**, **BA on Customers Behalf or Customer on Customers Behalf:** (**Call Center**) This shall be used when a customer calling to be assisted on a different number, other than the one they are using to call or where a customer calls on behalf of another.
- A single interaction will be created on the calling number using *“either, Agent* **on Customers Behalf**, **BA on Customers Behalf or Customer on Customers Behalf***”* as the action and indicate the MSISDN with issue on the comments section. After resolution, a single but comprehensive interaction will be entered on the number with the issue.
- On the second interaction the agent should include the number that called on behalf. 

          **Repeat Caller: (Call Center**)

For every repeat contact, i.e. whether through a Call, social media, Email or SMS, on same issue that remains unresolved, regardless of whether customer contacts us the same day or later, as long as the issue remains unresolved, CEE shall select “Repeat Caller” as the action. If the customer is making a repeat contact but on behalf of another, CEE will select **“Calling on Customer Behalf”** as the action on the calling number and “Repeat Caller” as the action on the number with the issue.

- **Repeat Retail customer:** For every repeat customer on same issue that remains unresolved, CEE shall select “Repeat Retail Customer” as the action
- **Information/ Request/Operation:** This applies in cases where a customer requests information or when an agent performs a system task or operation.
- **Compliments:** CEE shall use this when a customer call to appreciate service given to them by Safaricom agents.
- **Complaint:** CEE shall use this when a customer complains on a service given to them by Safaricom agents or other Safaricom touch points.
- **Multiple Queries:** If a customer calls with more than one issue, CEE will select “Multiple Queries” as the action reason, and Type and Subtype for the main issue that the customer raised, enter comments for the same and briefly indicate the other issues raised by the customer. This is except for repeat callers and customers calling on behalf.
- **Type:** The interactions type selected shall correspond with the customer’ issue, based on the resolution given. Where customer calls on multiple queries, the CEE will select the first query as the main issue, or any other that requires vetting or an operation.
- **Sub-Type:** This field is dependent on the above, Type field, where the CEE will narrow the caller reason further to a more specific issue.
- **Comment:** The CEE shall summarize their interaction with the customer, by briefly capturing the below aspects; -

o   Where vetting is applicable, the vetting details used to vet the customer, either if the customer passed or failed vetting.

o   The issue the customer was calling about.

o   The solution, advice or information provided to the customer.

o   Where applicable, any other necessary additional information such as voucher serial, transaction ID or SR number SIM serial number and the PRS codes deleted.

o   Where the resolution involves an operation that auto-generates an interaction, the CEE shall not log another interaction, except where more information is required, such as vetting details and multiple.

  o   Where an SLA is given, the agent is expected to capture the exact SLA on the comment field. E.g given/advised on 72 hours SLA

**Partner contacting M-PESA Business line via email**

- If a partner contacts M-PESA Business, the CEE will capture an interaction on the Partners Nominated Number.
- If the nominated number is not available, this should be captured on the Notifications Number.
- If the Notifications Number is not available, then interactions will be updated on the Primary Finance Contact.

o   Ensure the interactions are captured at Subscriber Level

o   Ensure that the correct Profile and Action are captured.

o   The default Profile is EBU Care M-PESA Business and Action is Email WDE

o   Select the correct Type and Sub Type.

o   In the comments field, enter a comment to indicate the customers issue and email ID.

**Content Not to Copy Paste on the Interactions**

- Noticeboard/Call center Escalation Folder Communications.
- Indicate caller reason and resolution, and then make reference to the communication where necessary, for instances of downtime communications.
- Where escalation is done via email, e.g. SR Past SLA, you can copy- paste the email under comments for reference
- HLR Profiles after an operation.
- Indicate the caller reason and resolution that entailed the HLR operation. E.g. Customer was not able to make calls. Barings for outgoing calls (or OC) removed on HLR.
- SMS Sent to customer, without mention of the customer issue and the action taken that warranted sending the SMS.
- Indicate the caller reason and resolution given. Contacts sent via SMS are visible on CRM Activities for reference.
- Where resolution entails verbalizing a contact number, indicate the issued number on the comments.
- The whole Vetting Matrix/Template, without at least indicating what was asked and what items customer got right/wrong.
- Where vetting is done, indicate the caller reason, vetting items asked and what customer passed or failed as well as the action taken.
- Where the resolution involves an operation that auto-generates an interaction, the
- CEE shall not log another interaction, except where more information is required, such as vetting details and multiple queries.

**3rd Party Interaction**

In order to allow for accurate capturing and reporting on issues where the customers or dealer calls on behalf of the customers, enter an interaction on the caller’s number using the action “Calling on Customer Behalf” as shown below:

**Step One**: Capture an interaction on the customer/dealer/agent\`s number who is on call (caller’s number). Ensure that the correct profile and action is captured, select the correct Type and Sub-Type (see screen shot below):

**Step Two**: On the number that the call is about, in this case 072388946… capture the interaction on the specific action type as relates to the customer issue and indicate the resolution you have given (see screen shot below). Ensure the type and sub-Type are the same as what was captured in step one:

On the second interaction the agent should include the number that called on behalf. 

 **Dealer Related Interactions**

In order to allow for accurate capturing and reporting on issues where the dealer calls on behalf of the customer, please use the steps below:

**“Calling on Customer Behalf”**

**STEP 1** 
The CEE will capture an interaction on the dealer/agent\`s number who is on call.

- Ensure that the correct profile and action is captured (see screen shot below).
- Select the correct Type and Sub Type.
- In the comments field, enter a comment to indicate that the dealer/agent is calling on behalf of a different number e.g. 0722002100

**STEP 2**

On the customer\`s number, e.g. 0722002100, capture another interaction and enter the customers issue e.g. sim swap, M-PESA start key, M-PESA reversal etc.

For all staff on Dealer queues please use the CSR dealer profile only whether or not the dealer is calling on behalf of the customer or the issues where the dealer calls with their own issue and not on behalf of the Customer, please use the action reason below.

On the  second interaction the agent should include the number that called on behalf. 

Select the Type and subtype relevant to the issue.

- Action

**FTTH VIP Mechanics Home Fiber VIP Customer Support FAQs**

# **Who is a FTTH/Home VIP Customer?**

This is a FTTH Customer classified as high value based on the level of influence they have, with benefits that are expected to build brand loyalty, customer advocacy and business growth.

The categorization may be based on **Government, Business, Policies, Influencers, Expatriates, or Internal staff.**

# **What is differentiated Service?**

This is a customer service journey that aims at ensuring that VIP customers will receive distinguished customer support during service delivery and support by offering personalized, proactive relationship management and dedicated VIP account managers.

# **Who is a VIP Account Manager?**

This is an assigned staff Responsible for proactively managing the VIP with an objective of offering unmatched Customer experience by building and maintaining relationship through personalized support.

The current support email address for our customers is: ***vvipcare@safaricom.co.ke***

# **How will the Home VIP customer be identified?**

The VIP customer will be identified through vetting using the VIP classification criteria defined and once criteria is passed the customer will be onboarded as a VIP and CI classified as VIP on U2000

# **Will the Home VIP customer have a different package?** 

- **No**, the customer will be onboarded on either of the current existing FTTH packages

**Will the Home VIP Customer be served by differentiated CEE upon calling line 400?** 

- **No,** If the customer chooses to call L400 for support, CEE will assist and resolve customer issue using the existing FTTH support processes available on Saka Hub.

The CEE will be able to identify that the customer is a VIP customer using the **CI tagging on U2000**.

For any unresolved or escalated issue through email, SR, or Incident, the CEE **must also share the same escalation through an email to:** ***[vvipcare@safaricom.co.ke](mailto:vvipcare@safaricom.co.ke)*****.** The email to include: the **customer issue, name** & **contacts** and the escalation details and inform the customer that their account manager will also follow up the issue and call them back.

# **Where can I identify the FTTH VIP customers?**

- The VIP customers are currently **flagged \_VIP on U2000** in the Alias column**. (Find on attachment)**
- In addition to this the customer CI are also indicated next to the customer’s name. Plans are underway to have the customers identified on other customer management systems -- Public U2000 VIP Tag sample as below. Example with customer details on Alias **(Find on attachment)**

# **If a customer would want to be added in the list of FTTH VIP customers what should I do?**

- For such requests, you will be required to **escalate to** ***[vvipcare@safaricom.co.ke](mailto:vvipcare@safaricom.co.ke)*** **email detailing the customer contacts.** The Account managers will use the VIP Identification criteria to determine eligibility.

# **Do I need to speak to the VIP Account manager before engaging the customer?** 

- **No,** however you will be required to send a brief email communication to the account manager or to: vvipcare@safaricom.co.ke on your engagement

**What is the scope of what VIP Account managers can do and what they cannot do?**

-  In addition to their account management duties, the account manager will be empowered to offer same level of support as L400 CEE

**What is the Escalation Matrix for issues the account managers cannot handle?**

- The **same escalation matrix used at Line 400 will be used by the account managers**

**What is the SLAS for issues VIP Account managers escalate?** 

**As is current SLs will apply for support**, however the account managers will follow up to expedite the resolution

**Will VIP Account managers respond to external customers escalations via CRM or regular Email?**

The Account managers will use regular email for day-to-day customer engagement for personalized service.

Any VIP escalation received via the folder i.e. Safaricom Home should be resolved by the person handling the query and a follow-up email sent to the account managers for attention and awareness

**How will Quality Assurance be monitored and enforced?** 

- **The existing Quality Assurance metrics** will apply for line 400 CEE. The VIP account manager quality assurance will be monitored through monthly NPS surveys.

# **Definition**

Okoa Midcall is a solution which the system automatically grants a pre-defined Okoa bundle so that a customer’s active call continues uninterrupted. 

Airtime balance running out while a customer is on call is one of the reasons of many dropped calls - Okoa Midcall closes this gap.

***International calls will not be eligible for this service. This is in the roadmap and will be introduced in future iterations***. 

# **How it Works**

The solution is intended to prevent calls from disconnecting when a customer’s available airtime and voice **resources are depleted** during an ongoing call. 

The call continues only for as long as the customer’s remaining resources permit. 

# **Differences With Auto ETU**

The service differs from the existing Auto ETU overdraft solution because it awards a predefined voice bundle rather than extending the call using the prevailing pay-as-you-go tariff. 

Auto ETU lets eligible customers overdraft before a call and repay after.

# **Customer Journey**

- Customer dials a number to make a call

- IVR prompt informs the customer that their available resources are running low.  

- The customer provides consent to receive an Okoa Chap Chap Midcall voice bundle.  

- The bundle is awarded immediately the available resources are exhausted and used to continue the ongoing call.  

- At the point of switching over to Okoa resources, the customer will hear two beeps. 

- Customer continues with the call.  

- Any unused minutes remain available for subsequent calls until midnight.  

- After the call, the customer receives an SMS showing the call duration, Okoa minutes used, outstanding loan amount, service fee, remaining resources and repayment deadline. See sample notification below:

***You have received 2mins Okoa chap chap to complete this and subsequent calls valid until midnight. Loan received: Ksh1.80, Fee: Ksh0.20. Your debt of Ksh2.00 should be paid by 27-07-2026. Total unpaid Okoa Jahazi is Ksh3.10. Dial \*131# to check your Okoa minutes balance***

# **Proposed Okoa Chap Chap Midcall IVR:** 

***1.Mteja Mpendwa, Balance yako ya kuongea iko chini na simu ita disconnect hivi karibuni. Bonyeza Sufuri ku-activate Okoa Chap Chap au puuza ujumbe huu kuendelea.*** 

***2\. Dear Customer, your talk time balance is low and your call will be disconnected shortly. Press Zero to activate Okoa Chap Chap or ignore this message to continue with your call.*** 

**NB:** **Communication will be done in case of any changes on the IVR.**

If you ignore/decline the IVR prompt - No Okoa bundle will be awarded, your call will continue using your available resources & disconnect once your resources are depleted.

# **Opt-IN**

The service is available on an opt-in basis(USSD: \*131#, \*131\*0 #) .

Selected customers may also be onboarded through customer segmentation, but **they must provide consent** before a loan is awarded during a call. 

# **Proposed Opt- Out/Deactivate Journey /Unsubscribe**

- Customer dials the existing Okoa menu (USSD: \*131#, \*131\*0 #) 

- Chooses Okoa Chap Chap  

- Okoa Chap Chap Mid-call → Deactivate from the menu. 

Okoa Chap Chap-Mid-call Menu 

1. Activate  

2. Deactivate  

3. FAQs 

- Customer is removed from the mid-call-eligible list immediately. 

- Customer receives SMS confirming opt-out, with an option to opt back in any time. 

**NB:** **Previously awarded resources remain available until their stated expiry (midnight).** 

#  **Available Resources**

During the pilot, eligible customers will receive 3 voice minutes for KSh 5. The bundle configuration may be reviewed in future. 

After the pilot, different segments will have different allocations which will be shared in due course. 

**Can a customer receive more than one bundle?** 

This will depend on the customer’s available Okoa limit, eligibility rules and the configured number of awards allowed within a specified period. 

#  **Business Rules: Charges, Eligibility and Validity**

A 10% service fee applies to every Okoa Chap Chap MidCall loan. 

Awarded bundle is valid until midnight on the day it is issued with no roll over.

You may not receive the bundle if you are **not opted in**, have **no available Okoa limit**, **are blacklisted**, have **sufficient resources**, have an **outstanding restriction** or do not meet the applicable **eligibility criteria**. For these scenarios **the IVR will not be played.** 

All customer balances at the beginning of the call will be aggregated when determining if the Okoa Midcall threshold has been met. 

International calls will not be eligible for this service.

Any unused resources will be used in the subsequent calls and will have the highest priority for voice service.

**Existing okoa rules apply**

# **Definition**

This is a service that enables M-PESA and PayPal customers to link their M-PESA account with PayPal account to transfer funds between M-PESA and PayPal.

# **Eligibilty**

- M-PESA customers with an active account 
- Customers with a registered PayPal account 
- Users with access to a mobile phone and internet

# **How to get started with the M-PESA PayPal service**

- Open your M-PESA Super App (MyOne App)
- Open the PayPal Mini App and select Link Account
- Log into your PayPal Account, log in using your PayPal credentials
- Accept the confirmation for Account Linking and enter M-PESA PIN
- On Log in, two options shall be presented; Top Up and Withdraw.

# **What happens if I do not have M-PESA or PayPal Account**

Register for an M-PESA account by visiting any M-PESA agent near you with your identification

document. For PayPal visit the PayPal website and select register to create an account.

# **Services are available on M-PESA PayPal service**

- Withdraw money from PayPal to M-PESA
- Top up PayPal from your M-PESA wallet

# **Transaction processing duration**

The transactions are processed Instantly; you will receive a confirmation SMS.

# **Supported Currencies**

- PayPal balances are in foreign currency (USD) 
- Funds withdrawn to M-PESA are converted to Kenyan Shillings (KES)

# **Applicable fees and currency exchange rates**

A 3% fee applied on the daily Foreign Exchange rate for both Top Up (M-PESA to PayPal Account) and Withdrawal to M-PESA.

**NOTE:** Service fees are subject to change, for updated tariff please refer to the Safaricom website **[www.safaricom.co.ke](http://www.safaricom.co.ke)**

# **Unlinking my accounts**

A customer can unlink your M-PESA and PayPal accounts through the M-PESA Super App, log onto the App, select PayPal then select Options and Unlink Account.

# **How to unlink my M-PESA wallet from my PayPal account**

- Log in to the M-PESA app using the M-PESA pin or Chosen biometrics
- From the home screen on the navigation bar tap the **Global Payments** tab
- Select the PayPal mini app
- Tap on the unlink account tab
- You will receive a pop-up stating that you are about to unlink your PayPal account
- Selects unlink
- Enter your M-PESA pin
- You will receive a notification from Safaricom that you have successfully unlinked your M-PESA account 07xxxxxxxxto your PayPal [gggg@gmail.com](mailto:gggg@gmail.com) .To link again select Global on the M-PESA app.

# **How to send money to someone else**

For customers to send money to another customer, both your PayPal and Safaricom M-PESA accounts must be in the same name—transfers are only allowed between your own accounts.

# **Daily transaction limits**

Transactions are subject to the standard M-PESA limits; 250,000 KES per transaction and

500,000 KES per day.

- **For withdrawals:** you will be charged a 3% conversion fee of the amount withdrawn.
- **For topping up:** you will be charged a 3% conversion fee of the amount topped up. Regular M-PESA charges apply to all other transactions
- Fees are payable to Safaricom for the use of the M-PESA - PayPal service.
- For top ups normal pay bill C2B charges apply as per the current C2B M-PESA tariff. This is available on the Safaricom Official website.

# **Reversals: Can I cancel my transaction**

Unfortunately, once you've confirmed a top up or withdrawal, you won't be able to stop or reverse it.  

# **[How to look for previous transactions](https://www.paypal-mobilemoney.com/m-pesa/faq#collapse-trx8)**﻿

Go to the **[Transaction History](https://www.paypal-mobilemoney.com/m-pesa/history)** page or log in to your PayPal account. You can also view this on the M-PESA app home page.

# **[Funds NOT reflecting in my M-PESA account.](https://www.paypal-mobilemoney.com/m-pesa/faq#collapse-debug1)**

If after the estimated processing time you haven't received the funds in your account and your PayPal account has been debited; Kindly contact Safaricom through dialling line **100** for a prepaid customer or **200** for a post-paid customer.

The customer should include the PayPal transaction/reference ID, and we will get back to you as soon as possible. Your PayPal transaction ID can be found under **[Transaction History](https://www.paypal-mobilemoney.com/m-pesa/history)**

# **Unable to initiate a withdrawal transaction, keep getting an error**

If a customer has a problem initiating a Withdrawal transaction (send payment instruction) from your PayPal account, they should contact PayPal using the link below

**[https://www.paypal.com/ke/smarthelp/contact-us](https://www.paypal.com/ke/smarthelp/contact-us)**

**M-PESA PayPal service Enhancements**

# **Fuliza Support on PayPal Account Top-Ups:**

Customers can now utilize their existing Fuliza limits to complete PayPal Account top-up transactions when they have insufficient funds.

# **AML Compliance Details:**

To meet regulatory compliance requirements, we have introduced two additional information fields in both the Top-Up and Withdrawal journeys: Source of Funds and Purpose of Transfer.

# **Error and Failure Notifications:**

We have optimized the service and mapped errors to ensure users receive specific, informative failure messages when a transaction fails, replacing generic error prompts.

# **Reporting & Reconciliation Enhancements:**

We have improved reporting by including the specific PayPal Transaction ID and related details directly on the Fintech (G3) statement. This will greatly aid both technical troubleshooting and financial reconciliation.

# **Who to contact in case of challenges**

Kindly contact Safaricom by dialling 100 for a prepaid customer or 200 for a post-paid

customer. For PayPal Account related challenges, contact PayPal on **[https://www.paypal.com/ke/smarthelp/contact-us](https://www.paypal.com/ke/smarthelp/contact-us)**
