articleTitle: SMS Troubleshooting Tips for inability to send/Receive SMS
markdownContent:
# **SMS Troubleshooting Tips for inability to send/Receive SMS**

**Steps:**

**CRM IN-DATA****:**

confirm that the line is:

- Active on IN DATA, Status on subscriber portal and is not on lifecycle expiry, barred or pooled
- Has enough resources such as airtime, SMS resources to be able to send SMS,
- If expired or no resources, ask the subscriber to top up airtime to reactivate or buy SMS resources

**CRM SAWA****:**

Confirm that the line has TS21 254713\*\*\*604 for outgoing sms and TS22 25471\*\*\*9604 for incoming SMS. Presence of TS 21 and TS 22 indicates that the line is okay

 [Screenshot] 

Raise an SR if missing.

Check on SAWA that **MCEF & MNRF** are false. **MCEF and MNRF false** means that the line is okay

True indicates the presence of SMS awaiting to be delivered for either of the below reasons:

**MCEF True:** Mobile Capacity Exceeding Flag- advise sub to delete some messages from inbox

**MNRF True**: Mobile Not Reachable Flag- Purge and ask the sub to do a **location update**

 [Screenshot] 

**B****arrings**

 [Screenshot] 

The above profile indicates active for SMS

If PROV is replaced by ACT for TS20- short Message it means the sub activated SMS barrings as below:

CBOC ACT TS20-shortMessage: Outgoing SMS barring active

CBOIC ACT TS20-shortMessage: Outgoing SMS barring International active      

CBOICEXH ACT TS20-shortMessage: Outgoing SMS barring Int. while roaming active

CBIC ACT TS20-shortMessage: Incoming SMS barring active

CBICROUT ACT TS20-shortMessage Incoming SMS barring while roaming active

**NOTE:**

Capture an interaction appropriately for any activity done on customer's MSISDN.

**DIY Procedures** **(to be done by the sub on the handset):**

**Activating/Deactivating all outgoing SMS**

To activate barring of all outgoing SMS from your line dial the service code: \*33\*0000\*16#

To Deactivate barring of all outgoing SMS from your line dial the service code: #33\*0000\*16#

# **How to Bar All incoming SMS**

To activate barring of all incoming SMS to your line dial the service code: \*35\*0000\*16#

To Deactivate barring of all incoming SMS to your line dial the service code: #35\*0000\*16#

# **Barring all International SMS**

To activate this feature, dial the service code: \*331\*0000\*16#

To deactivate this feature, dial the service code: #331\*0000\*16#

# **Barring incoming SMS when roaming**

To activate barring of all incoming SMS to your line, when roaming, dial the service code: \*351\*0000\*16#

To deactivate barring of all incoming SMS to your line, when roaming, dial the service code: #351\*0000\*16#

NB: 0000 is the barring code. Sub to enter their current if already changed.

# **To deactivate barrings on HLR:**

Login to HLR> Supplementary Services> Enter the Number> Then Select Unbar Sim & Reset Code> inform customer that the Barring Password would be reset, hence, to use the default, 0000.

Educate the customer on the self-service procedure in case they need to Activate/ Deactivate again in future or send an SMS via Siebel on how to Activate / Deactivate in future.

**Service Center Number****:**

Confirm that the sub has the correct Service Center Number.

Tap on Phone Messages> Message Settings> select SIM 1 or 2 (if dual)> scroll down to SMS Center (SMSC)> +2547225000029

**RCS (Rich Communication Services )**

RCS is a messaging protocol for Google/Android users with chat features that are similar to Apple’s iMessage. Once enabled, messages are sent and received through Google's RCS backend over the internet.

**Reasons For Failure when RCS is enabled**

- When Party A has enabled RCS and sends a message to party B whos’ device is off
- The recipient or sender lacks an active internet connection.
- The recipient’s device doesn't support RCS.
- Party A sends a text to Party B who has not enabled RCS on their device.
- Issues with the Google Messages app or Carrier Services app could also affect RCS connectivity.

**Customers can disable RCS on their Android devices as below:**

1. Launch the Google Messages app.
2. Tap on your profile icon, in the top-right corner.
3. Go into Messages settings.
4. Select RCS chats.
5. Toggle Turn off RCS chat

**Active RSC Messaging display**

 [Screenshot]

 **NB:- RCS messaging does not affect M-PESA messages.**

The procedure is applicable for

- Stolen/lost handset
- Where customer requests to have his/her previously blocked handset, unblocked
- Sending IMEI data for inclusion in or deletion from the EIR i.e. black listing and un-blacklisting of handsets.

**Customer Blocking Request Received at Retail Centre**

CEE will ask the customer to present the following details:

Original Police abstract which should indicate make, model and IMEI of lost device

The original receipt if available

Copy and original ID/Passport/Diplomatic ID or waiting card if the abstract lists the ID as one of the items stolen.

- Where the customer cannot recall and has no IMEI serial of lost device, the CEE will vet the customer IMEI history using available systems. The CEE will take extra precaution to confirm with the customer history records to ensure correct device is blacklisted, where multiple devices of the same make and model are used and/or agent is not able ascertain ownership the CEE will advise customer accordingly.
- CEE will not issue IMEI where no blacklist request is made. Instead, customer will be requested to use the **web-self-care option** for the same.
- The CEE will vet using the EIR support server and customer records. The following checks must be in place for the blacklist to be done:

Full and Correct Name, Address and Contact Phone Number

Original ID as per vetting process.

Frequently dialled numbers or date of last top up is consistent with those provided by applicant

Handset make and model is as described by applicant.

Police Abstract.

Stolen lost IMEI has been used with applicant’s MSISDN.

There are SIMs periodically used in the handset as identified or not identified by the applicant

Signed application form.

Letter of authorization if submitter is not applicant

- CEE will ask the customer to fill in the application form (hard copy, in triplicate)
- Blacklist should **not** be carried out if any of the above vetting details are missing and in addition:

There are instances of duplicate IMEIs registered as duplicates in the support server.

IMEI not available either from the customer logs / history.

If grey-listing has been specifically asked for, thus where customer has requested for tracking by the police, CEE will advise them not to blacklist.

Any requests that are unusual and not as defined above must be escalated via the escalation system to the respective RCSC for the Retail Centre.

- Once the IMEI and MSISDN checks have been made, the CEE will blacklist the handset using the EIR support server.
- CEE must attach the EIR request form (fully filled signed and stamped), police abstract and the customer ID.
- CEE should raise an interaction in the escalation system indicating action taken and relate the attachment to the interaction raised.
- Customer must make their application within 1 year of the date of theft or loss of the handset. Any applications made after the 12 months have lapsed will not be considered.
- The CEE will then file the application form in the respective file as per the filing procedure

**Customer Un-Blocking Request Received at Retail Centre**

- The customers who will be requesting for un-blacklisting are individuals who found their lost devices and had requested for the same to be blacklisted, and to whom we will be returning the lost handsets.
- The CEE will verify that the customer is the owner who submitted the handset for inclusion in the EIR. Normal subscriber administration vetting will be done.
- CEE will ask the customer to fill in the unblocking application form.
- Once the identity of the customer has been verified, the CEE will un-blacklist the handset using Siebel.
- The following information must be included for un-blacklisting to be carried out:

Name (which must be the same as applicant that submitted IMEI for blacklisting)

Postal Address (where available), and Contact Phone Number.

Original valid ID and copy.

MSISDN that was in lost/stolen phone is indicated.

Signed application.

**Un-blocking should not be done if the customer does not pass the vetting criteria.**

- CEE should raise an interaction on Siebel indicating action taken and attach application form and customer ID and order relate attachment to the interaction raised.

**EIR device recovery**

- Where a recovered device is presented at the retail store, the agent will request the customer to fill in the **device recovery form** and will advise customer on the process involved in trying to contact owner.
- Agent will also advice the customer that device cannot be returned to them once surrendered and will also educate the customer on benefits of surrendering the device i.e. in cases where device is used for criminal activities.
- The CEE will enter details of the device on the customer feedback link and enter an interaction for customers linked to a MSISDN. For customers where the device is not linked to any MSISDN the log will only be maintained on the customer feedback link.
- The RCSC / CEE will query on Siebel / EIR if handset was in use by a Safaricom MSISDN. Where RCSC/ CEE is able to identify owner of the line, they will notify them to collect the device and will request customer to bring along their original ID and any available documents to verify ownership where available.
- CEE will issue the recovered device to the shop, team leader or manager for safe keeping awaiting collection. They will be required to sign the device recovery form as well while awaiting collection by customer.

**Owner of recovered device is identified and visits retail**

- CEE or RCSC will verify ownership by vetting the customer. If customer passes the vetting (this can vary i.e. provide original receipt of purchase, present serial, FDN, LTU, device history etc.

- Customer will fill the device recovery form CEE will stamp, scan the form and attach the form and customer ID on Siebel upon collection.
- An interaction will be raised and details used to verify ownership, device collection form and document ID seen indicated and attached. CEE will then log the details of the person collecting on the customer feedback link and change status to closed with comments and reference the interaction. The form will be filed as per the filing procedure.

**No number can be linked to the device/Proof of ownership is not provided**

- Logs will be maintained in the customer feedback link with comments on the same as RCSC makes attempt to establish ownership of device.

- Where proof of ownership is not provided or no claim is made for the device within 2 months, shop RCSC will liaise with the law enforcement / fraud team on best way of handling the device.
- Where CEE or RCSC is not able to find details of the device due to various reasons i.e. blacklisted by a different mobile operator or any other reason(s). CEE will liaise with the RCSC and law enforcement / fraud team for the device to be sent to the law enforcement team (fraud team) within 48 hours. RCSC will scan and attach on the link the dispatch documents and fraud team will confirm via the link receipt of the device and RCSC will change status of log to closed.
- If the handset had been reported lost and blacklisted, CEE will follow the handset un- blacklisting process.
- Handsets blacklisted due to fraud should not be un-blacklisted even after vetting has been passed. Instead, customer will be advised to liaise with the fraud team and CEE will then send an email to the law enforcement team and will give details of the occurrence, retain the device and raise an interaction until advised further.

#  **How to check for IMEI**

Customers can press \*#06# ok and the number that appears on the screen is the serial number of the handset. This should be done when still in possession of phone and this number stored safely in case it needs to be blacklisted /unblacklisted in future. Alternatively, it can be found on the inside of handset near or next to where battery is stored.

Note that IMEI details are found on EIR VBC on CRM.

We do not blacklist duplicate IMEI (IMEI used by several people)

We only blacklist unique IMEI numbers as per EIR VBC system.

We check to validate that indeed the customer reporting was using that IMEI before taking any action.

Attach the documentation as you blacklist and Unblacklist the IMEIs to customer account level on CRM and capture interactions accordingly

# **Handling Fuliza Authorised Transactions**

**CEE action:** For any authorized Fuliza transaction i.e. P2P, LNM buy goods or Paybill transaction raise, an SR to the support team and advice the customer on 12hrs SLA

**Support Team Action:** Query transaction on both M-PESA and Fuliza (CRM) systems.

| M-PESA status | Fuliza (CRM) status | Action on the transaction |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Completed | Authorized | Complete on Fuliza (CRM) |
| Authorized | Completed | Complete on M-PESA |
| Authorized | Authorized | Complete/Cancel on both M-PESA and Fuliza (CRM) systems depending on the customer/partner request |
| Authorized | Cancelled | Cancel on M-PESA |
| Cancelled/Expired | Authorized | Cancel on Fuliza (CRM) |

# **Fuliza M-PESA Repayment**

Any funds received or deposited in your M-PESA account will automatically be used to repay your outstanding Fuliza M-PESA facility.

However, repayment trigger will be affected by below scenarios:

- **HFUND** >customers who access HFUND will have Fuliza repayment suspended for 24hours to allow use of the Funds. After the 24 hours, customer must receive or deposit funds for repayment to be done.
- **SUSPENSION TAG**\>Repayment is inactive for customers who have suspension tag due to KYC, fraud, reversal. Follow guidelines on tag removal. After tag is removed, customer must deposit funds to trigger repayment.

You will not have access to your Fuliza M-PESA limit if you have any unpaid balance after day 30.

This will however be restored immediately after full payment of your Fuliza outstanding balance.

For customer who want to pay loan for recycled, recreated lines the USSD process is as below. The USSD is done from a different line.

“Dial \*334#OK, Select FULIZA, Select Pay FULIZA loan on Old Line > enter Mobile Number > enter ID No> Accept Payment”.

- Customers who have accessed HFUND loan are exempted from Fuliza repayment for a period of 24 hours. This is to allow them to use the funds.

articleTitle: Merchant Deposit at M-PESA Agent Outlet
markdownContent:
# **Overview**

Merchant Deposit at M-PESA Agent Outlet is a service that enables merchants to deposit cash directly into their business wallets through an authorized M-PESA Agent. The service provides a convenient way for merchants to fund their business wallets without visiting a bank or using alternative deposit channels.

# **Supported Merchant Products**

The service is available for the following merchant products:

- Lipa na M-PESA Buy Goods Till
- Pochi la Biashara (PLB)

# **How the Service Works**

The deposit transaction is initiated by an authorized M-PESA Agent on behalf of the merchant. Once the transaction is successfully processed, the deposited funds are credited to the merchant’s wallet.

# **Information Required for a Till Deposit**

To process a deposit into a Lipa na M-PESA Buy Goods Till, the M-PESA Agent requires:

- Till Number
- Merchant Phone Number
- Deposit Amount

# **Information Required for a Pochi la Biashara Deposit**

To process a deposit into a Pochi la Biashara wallet, the M-PESA Agent requires:

- Merchant Phone Number
- Merchant ID Number
- Deposit Amount

# **Transaction Confirmation**

**Merchant Confirmation**

Upon successful completion of a deposit, the merchant receives an SMS notification containing:

- Transaction reference number
- Deposit amount
- Updated wallet balance

**Agent Confirmation**

The M-PESA Agent also receives an SMS confirmation indicating that the transaction was successful. The Agent’s float balance is updated accordingly.

# **Wrong Deposit Reversal**

**Definition**

A Wrong Deposit Reversal is a process used to recover funds that have been deposited into the wrong merchant account.

**Reversal Process**

- For transactions made within one hour, the Agent initiates the reversal process by forwarding the transaction SMS to **2530**.
- For transactions older than one hour, the Agent should contact Customer Care through **100** or **234** for assistance.

# **Reversal Failure Scenarios**

A reversal request may not be completed in certain situations, including:

- The merchant declines consent for the reversal.
- The merchant account has insufficient funds.
- Invalid transaction details are provided.

# **Insufficient Funds Handling**

If the merchant account does not have sufficient funds to support the reversal, the Agent receives an SMS notification indicating that the reversal could not be processed. The notification advises the Agent to contact Customer Care through **100** or **234** for further support.

# **Customer Support**

For assistance with wrong deposits, reversal requests, or reversal failures, Agents can contact Customer Care through:

- Line 100
- Line 234

These support channels are available for cases that cannot be resolved through the standard SMS reversal process.

Find the escalation Matrix within the attached FAQ Document.

**FULIZA REVERSALS SYSTEM INTERACTION AND FAQs**

We shall be able to action full reversals (to reverse an amount less or equal to the Fuliza balance). This product’s support process shall plug into the existing support process for Fuliza products and 456 reversal service.

# **Below are the scenarios in the first release (full reversal)**

- Normal M-PESA reversal – where the recipient **does not have** an outstanding Fuliza debt.
- Where a customer receives an amount **less than** the outstanding Fuliza debt.
- Where a customer receives an amount **equal** to the outstanding Fuliza debt.
- Where a customer receives an amount **more than** the outstanding Fuliza debt

Initial status on CRM

Assume that at the beginning the customer who has received the funds has no Fuliza debt and has a balance of Sh 0.00 on their M-PESA wallet

***Customer A – Sender***

***Customer B – Recipient***

 [Screenshot] 

Customer M-PESA balance here is zero. (Ignore the 200 since it is a reserved balance)

 [Screenshot] 

**SCENARIO 1**

# **Recipient has no Fuliza debt**

Customer A (Sender):

- Has KSh 0.0 in M-PESA but sends KSh. 300 to Customer B using Fuliza
- Forwards SMS to 456 for reversal
- Customer B (Recipient):
- Has no Fuliza debt

**Verdict:**

- Customer A forwards SMS to 456 and the funds are reversed.
- The reversed funds are utilized to settle Fuliza debt for Customer A.

**Images**

 [Screenshot] 

**Customer’s CRM view after the transaction**

 [Screenshot] 

**The customer reverses the transaction via 456**

 [Screenshot] 

**SCENARIO 2**

# **Recipient receives an amount that is LESS THAN or EQUAL to the Fuliza debt**

- Customer A (Sender):
- Sends KSh. 200 to Customer B
- Forwards SMS to 456 for reversal
- Customer B (Recipient)
- Has KSh. 515.06 Fuliza debt
- Amount received is less than the Fuliza debt hence only part of the debt is paid
- Debt is partially paid and still has KSh. 315.06 to pay verdict:
- Customer A forwards SMS to 456 and the funds are reversed.
- KSh 200 used by Fuliza is reversed
- Customer B debt is rebooked and therefore will be expected to pay

**Images**

 [Screenshot] 

**Customers CRM view**

 [Screenshot] 

Customer B receives KSh. 200 from Customer A which settles part of the debt

 [Screenshot] 

 [Screenshot] 

# **The sender initiates reversal via 456**

Note that the transaction ID ON G2 will have 2 linked transactions

Declined due to insufficient funds since the first attempt was to reverse the full amount from Customer B M-PESA wallet

Pending/ completed/cancelled reversal arising from successful reversal from Fuliza

N/B: Any amount below KSh. 250 shall be auto completed

 [Screenshot] 

 [Screenshot] 

 [Screenshot] 

When a reversal is done successfully, the loan is rebooked via the below transaction type (this is equal to the amount that was used to settle part of the outstanding debt)

 [Screenshot] 

Customer B is reverted to the previous state of having the Fuliza debt reinstated and will thus need to pay the debt.

 [Screenshot]

**SCENARIO 3**

# **Recipient receives an amount that is MORE THAN the Fuliza debt**

**Customer A (Sender):**

- Sends KSh. 700 to Customer B
- Forwards SMS to 456 for reversal

**Customer B (Recipient):**

- Has KSh. 500 Fuliza debt
- KSh 700 Amount received is more than the Fuliza debt
- Debt is fully paid and excess KSh 200 is deposited into Customer B M-PESA account

**Verdict:**

A reversal will be possible for the amount that was used to repay Fuliza debt + the balance on G2

# **Updating transaction status on G2 to pending authorized before a reversal is completed.**

All Fuliza reversals done via 456, will be put on pending authorized before they are completed, and the CEE will now have visibility and be able to approve /reject pending OD reversals when a customer calls. Existing Mpesa reversal guidelines apply.

# **Fuliza Reversals from Accounts with Overdue loans and zero Limit:**

**Fuliza Reversal on USSD \*456#**

# **Key Rules**

- Fuliza Reversals only cover the amount that was used to repay a Fuliza loan.
- If the recipient has already used part of the money, only the amount applied to the Fuliza repayment can be reversed.
- The sender must forward the M-PESA transaction SMS to 456 within 24 hours.

- Once a reversal is initiated, the recipient will see a negative Fuliza limit.
- Since customers with overdue loans no longer have an available Fuliza limit, a virtual Fuliza limit is created to process the reversal. The original overdue Fuliza loan is then restored with its original due date.

# **Scenario 1: Wrong transfer of 1,500 sent to a customer with an OVERDUE Fuliza loan**

- The recipient's overdue Fuliza loan is Ksh 1,000.
- Ksh 1,000 clears the Fuliza loan and Ksh 500 remains in the M-PESA balance.
- The sender requests for reversal within 24 hours.
- Full reversal of Ksh 1,500 is processed.
- The original Fuliza loan of Ksh 1,000 is reinstated with its original due date.

# **Scenario 2: Wrong transfer** **of Ksh 500** **to a customer with an OVERDUE Fuliza loan****.**

- The recipient owes Ksh 1,000 on Fuliza.
- The Ksh 500 only partially repays the loan.
- The sender requests a reversal within 24 hours.
- Full reversal of Ksh 500 is processed.
- The original Fuliza loan and due date remain unchanged.

# **Scenario 3: Recipient with OVERDUE Fuliza spends part of the excess funds**

- Ksh 1,500 is sent.
- Ksh 1,000 repays Fuliza, leaving Ksh 500 in M-PESA account.
- The recipient spends the Ksh 500.
- Only the amount used for Fuliza repayment (Ksh 1,000) can be reversed.
- The original Fuliza loan of Ksh 1,000 is reinstated with the original due date.

**Sample SMS for Fuliza Balance Check on USSD 334**

Dear Stacy, your outstanding Fuliza M-PESA amount is Ksh 1000.00 due on 20/03/26. Your available Fuliza M-PESA limit is Ksh -1,000.00. Transaction Cost Ksh

**Introduction**

M-PESA Tap-to-Pay is a contactless payment solution that allows customers to make payments by tapping an NFC-enabled smartphone on a compatible NFC-enabled device or point-of-sale (POS) terminal. After tapping, the customer verifies the transaction details and enters their M-PESA PIN to complete the payment securely. Once the transaction is successful, the customer receives an M-PESA confirmation message.

# **Who Can Use Tap-to-Pay**

- Tap-to-Pay is available to customers who meet the following requirements:
- Have an active Safaricom line registered on M-PESA.
- Own an NFC-enabled smartphone.
- Have My OneApp installed on their device.
- Are making a payment at a merchant outlet that supports Tap-to-Pay.

# **Getting Started with My OneApp**

Customers who do not already have My OneApp can download it from the Google Play Store for Android devices or the Apple App Store for iPhones. After installation, they can open the application and follow the on-screen instructions to sign in and begin using the service.

# **Understanding NFC Technology**

NFC, or Near Field Communication, is a wireless technology that allows devices to exchange information over short distances. This technology enables contactless interactions, including payments, by allowing a smartphone to communicate with a nearby NFC-enabled device.

# **Checking NFC Compatibility**

Customers can verify whether their smartphones support NFC by checking their device settings.

For Android devices, users can search for “NFC” or “Contactless Payments” within the Settings menu. For iPhones, NFC is supported on iPhone 6 models and later. Users can confirm compatibility by checking their device information in Settings. For other devices, such as POS terminals, NFC support can be confirmed through the manufacturer’s specifications.

# **How Tap-to-Pay Works**

- The Tap-to-Pay process is designed to be simple and convenient:
- The cashier initiates the payment on an NFC-enabled device or POS terminal.
- The customer taps their NFC-enabled smartphone on the device.
- The customer reviews and verifies the transaction details displayed on the phone.
- The customer enters their M-PESA PIN to authorize the payment.
- The transaction is completed, and the customer receives an M-PESA confirmation message.

# **Payment Verification and Security**

Security remains a key feature of Tap-to-Pay. Customers are required to verify transaction details and enter their M-PESA PIN before any payment is completed. This additional authentication step ensures that payments are authorized only by the account owner.

Before entering their PIN, customers should carefully review:

- The merchant details.
- The transaction amount.
- Their intention and comfort with making the payment.

# **Benefits for Customers**

- Tap-to-Pay offers several advantages for customers:
- Faster and more seamless payment experiences.
- Greater convenience during transactions.
- Elimination of manual entry of payment details.
- Reduced likelihood of payment errors.
- Secure transaction approval through M-PESA PIN authentication.

# **Benefits for Merchants**

- Merchants also benefit significantly from Tap-to-Pay adoption:
- Reduced customer queues.
- Faster transaction processing times.
- Ability to serve more customers efficiently.
- Fewer payment reversals caused by incorrect payment details.

# **Troubleshooting Tap-to-Pay Issues**

- If Tap-to-Pay does not work as expected, customers should:
- Confirm that their phone supports NFC functionality.
- Ensure NFC is enabled, where required by the device.
- Tap the phone gently against the NFC-enabled device or POS terminal and try again.
- Verify that the cashier has initiated the payment correctly.

In cases where Tap-to-Pay is unsuccessful, merchants may provide alternative payment methods such as STK Push, QR code payments, or sharing Lipa na M-PESA Buy Goods or PayBill details.

# **Availability**

Tap-to-Pay is available at merchant outlets equipped with devices or POS terminals that support the Tap-to-Pay feature. Availability therefore depends on whether the merchant’s payment equipment has been enabled for the service.

# **Merchant Device Compatibility**

Merchants using certain Pesapal POS devices can support Tap-to-Pay without requiring additional setup. Existing Pesapal N950s terminals and selected N950u models are already compatible and can accept Tap-to-Pay transactions immediately.

# **The Role of Pesapal**

Pesapal is an independent payment service provider that supplies POS devices to merchants. Many businesses, including well-known brands such as Java House, Artcaffé, and thousands of other retail outlets, use Pesapal devices to process customer payments. Through compatible Pesapal terminals, merchants can offer the M-PESA Tap-to-Pay experience to their customers.

# **Conclusion**

M-PESA Tap-to-Pay provides a fast, secure, and convenient way for customers to make payments using NFC-enabled smartphones. By combining contactless technology with M-PESA PIN verification, the solution simplifies the payment process while maintaining strong security standards. For merchants, it improves operational efficiency by reducing transaction times, minimizing payment errors, and enhancing the overall customer experience.

# **Definition** 

Data minimization is an initiative that enables an M-PESA customer that is sending money to limit the information that will be visible to the recipient.

When you send money to someone else via M-PESA, instead of seeing your full name and mobile number, the recipient will only view two names and a masked mobile number.

# **Reasons for data minimization**

·       This is an initiative required under the data protection laws and it seeks to protect your identity from potential abuse e.g., unnecessary calls once you have made payments, harvesting of your number to target you for potential social engineering, among others.

·       It gives a send money customer the ability to decide whether a recipient may know their full identity.

# **How to view sender ‘s full information after receiving money**

·      The customer(recipient) will have the option to verify a sender’s identity by forwarding the **M-PESA confirmation message to 334** within 24hrs.

·       The sender will receive a prompt on their end to share their full name and mobile number.

·       If they accept, the recipient will receive an SMS with full name and mobile number of sender. 

·       If they reject the request, they will be notified of the sender’s choice.

# **Channels for viewing sender’s information after receiving money**

·       App

·       STK

·       USSD

# **How to reverse a transaction after sending money to the wrong number**

Reversing a transaction sent to a wrong number is still possible, as reversals are dependent on the unique transaction IDs.

**Note:** For reversals refer to the existing P2P reversal process.

**How to identify a masked number**

The sender’s two names and part of the number will be visible, e.g., instead of **Jane Kenya Safaricom** of 0722000000, you will see **Jane Safaricom** of 0722\*\*\*000.

**Will masking numbers increase fraudulent activities**

The measure aims to decrease fraud by limiting the number of people who may have access to your personal information.

**Handling Thank‑You or Follow‑Up Requests Under Number Masking**

A customer may use alternative contact methods or request the sender’s details, by requesting to verify the sender’s details using the process described above. Refer to ***How to view sender ‘s full information after receiving money.***

**How the change will affect business transactions**

As a business that receives money via P2P or “send money” directly from your customer, you may need to adjust your processes.

We recommend that you register for our payment products such as Pochi la Biashara or Lipa na M-PESA (Buy Goods or Pay Bill), that will enable you to keep track of transactions.

**How Number Masking Rules Are Applied to All Customers**

Number masking will be applied consistently across Safaricom’s customer base.

**Opting out of number masking**

There will be **NO** opt-out option as this is being implemented as a protective measure, and in compliance with data protection requirements.

**Communicating change to customers**

An extensive public awareness campaigns will be conducted through mass media before implementation of the minimization initiatives.

**Accessing full sender details in an M-PESA statement for legal purposes**

A customer will be required to provide a court order to access unmasked sender details.

**NOTE:**

Customers requesting for unmasked statements should be referred to retail shops with **OB number** and original ID.

Customer must have a valid reason for requesting for unmasked statement. OB should state r**eason** and **duration**.

**Masking policy on international transactions**

The masking policy will apply to all on-net P2P transactions only.

**Customer education to others who may not understand the change**

You will be required to share official communications and encourage them to reach out to Safaricom Customer Care via 234.

**Notification messages**      

The recipient will forward the masked M-PESA confirmation message to 334.

| Notification received by the sender when the recipient requests for the details | Dear Customer, you sent money to John Doe, Transaction ID ******* is requesting to view your complete Phone number. To approve, forward this message to 334. To decline, simply ignore. |
| --- | --- |
| Acknowledgment notification after a request-Recipient | Dear Customer, your request has been received and is being processed. You will get an SMS notification within 2hrs. |
| Received by the recipient when the sender approves | Your request for M-PESA Transaction ID ****** has been approved. Here are the details ********* |
| Received by the recipient when the sender declines | Apologies. Your request for M-PESA Transaction ID ***** has been declined by the sender |
| Repeat request for same transaction -request already processed | Failed. Your request of M-PESA Transaction ID *****has been declined. The request has already been initiated. |
| Repeat request for same transaction-pending | We are unable to process your request for M-PESA Transaction ID ***** because a similar request is already in progress. Please wait while we complete your initial request. |
| Notification when requester forwards an invalid transaction message | Failed. The M-PESA Transaction ID shared is invalid. Kindly check and try again. |
| Notification when there is Service Outage | Dear Customer, the Service is currently not available. Kindly try again later. |
| Notification for a transaction older than 24hrs | Dear customer, we cannot process the request because the M-PESA transaction ID provided is older than 24hrs. Please share the correct M-PESA transaction ID for assistance. |
| Requester sends a message, but the sender never responds | Apologies. Your request for this M-PESA Transaction ID ***** details has been declined. |

**Shiriki Plan for Business (renamed to Shiriki PostPay Airtime)**

Business owners and customers can choose from the subscription packages below:

**All unused plans expire at the end of the month with no rollover.**

# **To access Internet**

Advise the Sponsor to deactivate My Data Manager for them to use the Shiriki PrePay airtime. This is because My Data Manager works with Bundles and not Airtime.

**Please remind the Customer to reactivate My Data Manager should they deplete their Shiriki Airtime and revert to other bundles.**

# **Product Highlights**

**Business owners and or Customers (sponsors) shall:**

Access to highly subsidized hybrid tariff as above.

Use resources alone or share with beneficiaries.

Manage beneficiaries - add, remove, assign a limit, check balance.

Receive usage threshold notifications for your Shiriki resource.

Dial \*234\*11# for DIY Opt In/Purchase

**Business employees (beneficiaries) shall:**

Be assigned a limit on the Sponsors’ wallet (Shiriki Airtime).

Receive notifications on allocation.

# **Sponsor deposit**

Once a Sponsor dials the Opt In USSD code, they will receive an SMS with an Order number against which they will be advised to make a deposit (depending on the plan they choose-refer to above table) via M-PESA to paybill number **140140** and account number as the order number they receive on their SMS.

# **Benefit of Shiriki DIY Opt In**

We have done away with the documentation process and simplified the onboarding to just dialing the above USSD codes at the comfort and convenience of the customer.

The process is also automated as opposed to before when a customer had to wait for orders to be raised manually.

# **Step By Step Opt In Journey**

Once the customer dials \*485# and select Voice and Data Plans, then select Option -Shiriki Plan and Opt in,

the system automatically verifies the registration details and the customer is requested to enter a valid email address.

*Refer to the attachment on Customer Journey.*

# **Okoa Jahazi outstanding Debt**

If the customer has an okoa jahazi deBt, the customer will get this pop-up notification: *The number has an Okoa Jahazi.*

Please advise such potential customer to settle their Okoa Debts then attempt to Opt In again via \*234\*11# Ok, or dial \*485# and select Voice and Data Plans, then select Option -Shiriki Plan and Opt in.

# **Mechanics**

Once successfully onboarded, a sponsor can choose to add beneficiaries or choose to use alone.

The usage rates are as outlined on Table above.

Resources are prorated in the first month of subscription, depending on joining day of the month.

For the first bill, the sponsor will have a bill for the prorated period and the bill for the new month that’s beginning, and all is **due by the 16th of the month**\-Refer to the dunning milestones.

Subsequent bill payments equivalent to the value of the plan are also due by the 16th of each month.

Sponsor must allocate a limit to a beneficiary; else the beneficiary cannot access the Shiriki Plans for Business resources.

All resources shall sit on the Sponsor’s wallet. A beneficiary shall only use their allocation from the sponsor’s line.

All resources sit in the sponsor line. Beneficiaries are assigned and use their allocation while it seats on the sponsors pocket as their priority 1. If they exhaust the allocation, then priority of usage shifts to any other resources they may have.

Should the Sponsor deplete their resources, they will utilize the resources of the beneficiary since all resources sit with the Sponsor.

**All the unused resources expire at the end of the month, no rollover.**

# **Support & Changes**

Sponsors are whitelisted to access Business Support by calling 2222 or 200 or email to: *businesssupport@safaricom.co.ke* and most importantly, their Sales Manager in EBU.

Beneficiaries retain their respective support line as 100.

**Service Change (termination, upgrade, or downgrade)**

Sponsors may request service changes termination or upgrade/downgrade. This must be a **written request on email or a letter, from sponsors only.**

# **Terminations**

All terminations – Request customer to write an email to: advantage@safaricom.co.ke. This shall follow the normal post-pay termination procedure.

If a customer goes to Retail & Care Desks – a tariff migration order on CRM to change from Shiriki package to the requested post-pay one or to Uwezo.

To successfully terminate, disable Shiriki wallet on Postpaid tabs and corporate tabs on CRM configurator.

# **Upgrades**

For all upgrades – there are two options:

Raise an SR under the Category: Shiriki PostPay Airtime, select the Relevant Type and Item and attach the customer request/instruction.

Refer a customer to Retail & Care Desks – a service change order on CRM changes the Shiriki package from current to the requested one. 

# **Downgrades**

All changes from a higher package to a lower one – Request customer to write email to [advantage@safaricom.co.ke](mailto:advantage@safaricom.co.ke).

A service change order created on CRM will change from the Shiriki package currently to the requested one. This is to be done on both Postpaid and Corporate tab on CRM.

If a customer goes to Retail & Care Desks – a tariff migration order on CRM to change from Shiriki package to the requested one.

Customer support requests received through service managers shall be completed as per existing EBU In Life processes.

# **Setting limits**

Dial \*234\*11#, select “Add Beneficiary” option. Follow the prompts.

The sponsor will Add the MSISDN, Put the nick name as preferred and then input the limit to the beneficiary.

# **Add Beneficiary on CRM VBC**

**Front Facing Team Add Beneficiary on CRM VBC**

For the Front Facing Team, if the calling number is the Sponsor’s number or customer visiting the retail centre is the Sponsor (follow your vetting process at retail for verification of ownership), then the Front Facing team can add a beneficiary on the sponsors line via the SHIRIKI VBC on behalf of the customer.

Please guide the customer on the DIY procedure after assisting them.

A beneficiary can only enjoy Shiriki rates up to the allocated amounts. After exhausting the assigned limit, they shall need to top up and be charged prevailing rates on Uwezo.

A sponsor on Shiriki1 or who does not have beneficiaries has all the limit available for their use.

**Notifications**

| SCENARIO | NOTIFICATION TO SHIRIKI SPONSOR |
| --- | --- |
| Beneficiary MSISDN entered is not of the correct length | Dear Customer, you have entered an Invalid Number. Please ensure that the number starts with a zero (0) and the length of the number is 10. Thank you |
| Beneficiary MSISDN entered does not exist (Example an Competitor MSISDN) | Dear Customer, the number you have entered does not exist. Please ensure that you enter a Safaricom number. Thank you |
| Beneficiary MSISDN entered is not active (Example the MSISDN is not active on our systems) | Dear Customer, the number could not be added as a beneficiary at the moment. Please reconfirm the number with the beneficiary. Thank you. |
| Beneficiary MSISDN entered is already on Shiriki | Dear Customer, the number is already on Shiriki. Please try another number. Thank you |
| Internal Technical Error (In cases of a system outage) | Dear Customer, we are currently unable to add the beneficiary. Please try again later. Thank you. |

# **Removing beneficiaries**

Dial \*234\*11#, select “Remove Beneficiary” option, Select the beneficiary to sponsor intends to remove.

# **Pay for the resources**

The service is a post pay service recurring every 1st of the month. The sponsor will receive a monthly invoice showing amount to pay via email. Payment of monthly bills will be done to M-PESA Pay bill number 200200. The account name will be the sponsor’s mobile number. Refer to below dunning milestones.

| Shiriki PostPay Airtime Sponsor Dunning Milestone | Message Notification |
| --- | --- |
| SMS notifications 9th, 11th & 15th of Each Month | Your Shiriki subscription of Ksh*** is due for payment on {date}. To settle, make payment to M-Pesa Paybill 200200, and your mobile no as the account no. |
| Notification before barring – due date 22nd of each month | Your Line will be Suspended from making outgoing calls tomorrow. Please settle your Shiriki bill of KSH {AMOUNT} today to avoid service interruption. Use MPESA Paybill no. 200200 and your mobile no as the account no. |
| Barring outgoing services – due date 23rd of each month | No NotificationSponsor MSISDN that has not settled bills is barred for making outgoing calls |
| Suspend offer – due date + 12 (28th) | No NotificationThe Shiriki Product is removed from Sponsor Line that has not settled their bill. Note that the Shiriki Sponsor will not get their resources 1st of the next month unless they settle their bill before then. |
| Automatic Unbarring After Payment | |

**Frequency of purchase**

No. This service is a post-pay service and is renewable once per month. Resources do not roll over but expire after 30 days. New resources are provided at the beginning of every calendar month.

# **Sambaza**

This is a post-pay service that does not allow you to Sambaza airtime. The plan only allows you to share resources with your selected beneficiaries by allocating them a limit.

# **Check balance - Sponsor**

Dial \*485#, select option 2 (voice and data plans), option 4 (Select Shiriki Plan) and selecting the “Check Balance” option and select sponsor number.

# **Check balance -Beneficiary**

A Beneficiary cannot check their balance currently. The Sponsor can however check balance for beneficiaries under their Shiriki Plan.

# **Changing my subscriber number through \*234#**

A new subscriber number would be considered as a new sign up or activation.

This is a post pay service, a change in contracted party would need a termination first. Then a fresh onboarding on the new number.

# **Bonga Points**

You will be awarded Bonga Points equivalent to the value of your Shiriki subscription as per prevailing Bonga conversion rates.

**Browsing or calling without the plan as a Shiriki PostPay Sponsor**

When your subscription runs out you can top up your line with airtime.

**Browsing or calling without the plan as a Shiriki PostPay Beneficiary**

When your allocated limit runs out you can top up your line. However, you will not have access to the Shiriki preferential rates.

# **Roaming**

You will need to top up your line with normal airtime to be able to roam.

Prevailing roaming charges for calling and browsing will apply and will be deducted from the airtime value.

# **International Calls**

International Calling is supported for only Zone A (India, China, Canada and USA). Normal international calling rates apply for all other countries.

**Exhausting resources**

The resources get exhausted. This is dependent use patterns of the sponsor, and beneficiaries if any.

**Maximum or a minimum top up amount if I am on the Shiriki PostPay Airtime Plan for Business after sponsor exhausts the Shiriki resources before end of month**

You can top up any amount while on the Shiriki Plan. 

**Making Payment**

You can only make payment using M-PESA or by visiting your nearest Safaricom Shop.

 Customers can top-up their line with normal airtime and buy data bundles via \*544#.

**Shiriki VBC Details:**

 \*\*Refer to attached guide on the Shiriki VBC on CRM\*\*

**You will now be able to:**

**View Shiriki Sponsor Details** (Shiriki Plan-Product Name, Date Of Joining, Maximum Beneficiary as per the plan, Total Beneficiaries added among others details)

**View Shiriki Beneficiary Details** (Limit Allocated, Limit Usage, Limit Balance among others)

**Add a Shiriki Beneficiary** (Ability to add a beneficiary on behalf of the Sponsor-Interaction is auto created)

**Remove a Shiriki Beneficiary** (Ability to remove a beneficiary on behalf of the Sponsor- Interaction is auto created)

# **Definition**

This is a new initiative by The Hustler Fund Programme to support selected borrowers, with a strong repayment history, grow their businesses through practical training, mentorship, and expert business advice.

# **How it works**

The selected **customers will receive an SMS informing them that they could qualify for Tukuze Hub**.

The message recognizes their positive repayment record and advises them that they may receive a follow-up call from the official Hustler Fund number **+254 719 064 000** or visit: [https://www.hustlerfund.go.ke/TH](https://www.hustlerfund.go.ke/TH)

Receiving the SMS **does not mean a customer has been selected**. It simply indicates that they may be eligible to participate.

# **Charges and Participation**

Participation is entirely **Voluntary and Free of Charge**.

Interested borrowers will undergo a brief screening interview to determine their suitability for the programme/initiative.

# **NOTE**

Tukuze Hub **does not provide loans, grants, or cash payments**.

# **What It Does**

It equips entrepreneurs with Knowledge, Skills, and Confidence to identify Business Opportunities, Increase their Income, and Strengthen their enterprises.

# **Tukuze and Hustler Fund**

Participation in the Tukuze programme **does not affect** a customer's existing Hustler Fund loan or repayment obligations.

Customers who did not receive an SMS should note that the programme is being rolled out in phases.

Eligible borrowers will be contacted in future based on their borrowing and repayment history.

All customers are encouraged to continue using Hustler Fund products responsibly and maintain a good repayment record to improve their chances of qualifying for future opportunities.

# **Customer Inquiries**

For enquiries or to verify any communication about Tukuze Hub, contact Hustler Fund through the official Phone No: **+254719064000**.

# **Definition**

These are bundles that will allow customers to purchase data connectivity bundles while automatically saving on M-PESA ZIIDI.

It will enable customers enjoy mobile data & automatically grow their savings at the same time – **“*Use Safaricom data and grow your ZiiDi”***

# **Eligibility**

To be eligible, customers must be registered on M-PESA ZIIDI MMF/SHARIAH before purchasing the Akiba bundles.

**What is Ziidi?**

Ziidi MMF is a flexible and accessible investment product that allows M-PESA customers to invest in a Money Market Fund with as little as **KSH 100** and earn **competitive daily interest**.

The funds can only be invested or withdrawn via M-PESA, and all invested funds are instantly accessible through the provided channels

# **Subscription and Balances**

Customers can dial \*544#, \*444#, \*334#, \*555# and will be availed on the One App and Facebook channels soon.

Customers can purchase the bundles **as many times as they wish** with deposits to MMF automatically crediting.

Customers will check their bundle balance via the usual Safaricom data balance options of \*544\*44# and check their ZiiDi savings balance via M-PESA ZIIDI option on \*334#>Financial Services or on OneApp.

**Akiba bundles will NOT have auto-renewal option**.

**Payment**

Payment for Akiba Bundles is **only via available M-PESA balance**. Purchase via Fuliza is not supported.

Customer will pay a **one-off price** which will be **split for the data bundle** and **MMF** via M-PESA payment option.

# **Available AKIBA Bundles and Validities**

 [Screenshot] 

\*\*The Bundle offers are now **segmented and** customers will receive bundle options tailored to their respective usage profiles.

**Other Business Rules**

All Safaricom customers are eligible for this service.

For customers who have not opted in to ZIIDI will be able to opt-in for amounts less than Ksh 100 as a minimum Opt in amount.

The existing M-PESA ZiiDI T&Cs will apply to the savings. Refer: [https://www.safaricom.co.ke/main-mpesa/m-pesa-services/wealth/ziidi](https://www.safaricom.co.ke/main-mpesa/m-pesa-services/wealth/ziidi)

Customers will be able to access their savings subject to existing ZIIDI withdrawal rules and conditions  

Akiba Bundle data behaves like regular Safaricom data and can be used for tethering or hotspot, subject to normal network policy.

Akiba Bundles cannot be purchased while roaming. They will also not support roaming data usage unless otherwise specified.

# **Customer Support, CRM Interactions and Escalations (SR)**

All customer inquiries related to the product will be handled internally by Safaricom teams when customers contacts any of our CARE Touch points; *L100, L200, Safaricom Social Media Handles, E-mail,* *Zuri* and *other digital channels.*

SR & CRM Interactions will be captured under *:* **Mobile Data- Akiba Bundles**

**M-PESA Registration & Activation Information Mechanics** 

**Registration Requirements**

- Customers intending to register for M-PESA must have registered their SIM cards on the Safaricom network as per the guidelines issued by the Communications Authority of Kenya (CA).
- All prospective M-PESA customers shall appear physically at an M-PESA agent or Safaricom Retail Center Agent or care desk with their original registration documents for registration free of charge. A customer must register with their own identification details for registration as per M-PESA terms and conditions.
- M-PESA service is only available to Safaricom subscribers. Company registered lines can also be registered for M-PESA but under the names of the person issued with the line.

**Types of M-PESA Registration**

- New Line – Merged Registration
- Existing Line but without M-PESA
- Change of Ownership

**Acceptable Identification documents are:**

- Original Kenyan National ID Card
- Valid Passport (local, foreign or diplomatic)
- Military ID
- Alien ID or Foreigner Certificate
- Refugee ID

**Documents not allowed for registration are:**

- Driving licenses and police abstracts (as the sole document of identification)
- A minor (less than 18 years old) with a passport is NOT eligible to register for M-PESA

**Registration Above One M-PESA Account**

You can register a maximum of five(5) M-PESA accounts using same Document of registration.

Any extra accounts are suspended/frozen/closed by the AML team at the Account Level with the comments, ‘Multiple registrations. Excess accounts frozen/closed to leave customer 5 accounts as per the M-PESA T&Cs’ [HERE](https://www.safaricom.co.ke/media-center-landing/terms-and-conditions/m-pesa-customer-terms-conditions)

# **M-PESA REGISTRATION PROCEDURE FOR COMPANY LINES**

This is the procedure for M-PESA registration for company lines:

**Kenyans:**

1. **DO NOT EDIT** the line on Jiandikishe.
2. Instead, proceed to register the line on M-PESA. The controls put in place will check and confirm it is a company line. It will **not** enforce a match of SubReg and M-PESA and instead will go ahead to check against IPRS. (for company lines).

**Foreigner:**

1. **EDIT** details on Jiandikishe to match the passport.
2. Proceed to register the line on M-PESA.
3. **EDIT AGAIN** the line on Jiandikishe to the company details.

# **GSM-to-M-PESA Self-Registration**

The GSM-to-M-PESA journey enables Safaricom GSM customers without an existing M-PESA wallet to self-enrol using their current GSM details. This DIY (Do-It-Yourself) process leverages existing KYC information in Safaricom’s system, ensuring a seamless and secure onboarding experience

# **Target Users GSM customers with:**

- Active GSM line
- Complete KYC details in Safaricom systems
- Customers who have an active GSM registered line and want to enrol for an M-PESA wallet independently without visiting a physical outlet

# **User Journey**

- Dial \*334# and select Register for M-PESA. 
- Accept Terms & Conditions.
- Enter Identification Document No. (National ID, Passport, Refugee), Gender, Occupation, Source of Funds, Purpose of Account. 
- Receive confirmation SMS: “Congratulations! You have successfully registered on M-PESA.” 
- Customer completes activation via STK menu following standard M-PESA process. • Access services via \*334#, STK, APP (Send Money, Withdraw Cash, Buy Airtime, Loans & Savings, Lipa na M-PESA, etc.)

# **Key Features:**

Trigger Point: Customer initiates enrolment when they have no M-PESA wallet but an active GSM line.

# **System Auto-Checks**

- Validates GSM number status.
- Retrieves existing KYC details (Name, Kenyan National ID, Date of Birth, Gender).
- Confirms compliance with M-PESA standards.
- Ensures no prior M-PESA wallet exists in the SIM card.
- IPRS check Activation Customer completes activation via STK menu following standard M-PESA process.

# **Additional Key Feature**

- The SIM must be a consumer registered customer; if the line is registered as corporate, refer the customer to a Safaricom Shop.
- If IPRS verification fails, customer is directed to the nearest Safaricom Shop

articleTitle: Handling Non-Service- Related Issues (Care Center & Retail)
markdownContent:
**Handling Prank/ Abusive Caller**

**Definition**

**Prank Callers are customers who call for non-service-related issues. They may be abusive and/or ask distressful questions.**

**Action Required by CEE/TL OR MANAGER**   

The CEE/TL or Manager should not act unprofessionally.

Remind the customer that we are only able to assist them on Safaricom queries/issues or related subjects.

If the caller persists, advise the customer to desist from what they are doing and if they do not the CEE/TL or Manager    will have no choice but to disconnect the call.

If the caller persists the CEE/TL or Manager    will say: *"I shall now disconnect your call. Goodbye"*

Then disconnect the call.

The CEE/TL or Manager will capture this on the interaction.

The CEE **should not** capture key comments for Prank callers.

**Handling Non-Official Calls**

**Definition**

This is where the CEE/TL or Manager receives a call/visit/email from relative/friend/internal customer or any form of escalation for assistance.

The CEE/TL or Manager    will send an email to the Call Centre Escalation Folder [ccescalation@Safaricom.co.ke](mailto:ccescalation@Safaricom.co.ke) or respective shop folder for further assistance.

The CEE/TL or Manager    who assists the customer will capture an interaction corresponding with customer issue or raise an SR under Siebel/ CRM under the below categories corresponding with customer issue.

The analyst will use the information provided to resolve the issue. If the details captured on the SR are insufficient, the analyst will contact the customer to obtain the necessary information and then resolve the issue conclusively.

**Reports of Attacks**

**Definition**

This is where a customer calls our Helpline and reports they are being attacked.

**Action Required by CEE/TL OR MANAGER**   

While being empathic, the CEE/TL or Manager should try and get locational details which can then be shared with the Security Team.

The agent will try and find out the customer’s location and Verify the MSISDN where applicable.

Ask the customer to briefly describe/mention the road/street or name of building or landmark while listening in for background noise e.g., train hooting indicates proximity to a railway line.

Avoid asking for too much information as the customer may be in distress.

These details should be captured and escalated to the Call Center Escalation folder/ respective shop folder who will call the security number 0722007777 and provide the details.

The CEE/TL or Manager will capture this on the interaction.

**Reports of Security Problem/Emergency**

**Definition**

This is where a customer has an emergency and/or reports a security problem in an area.

**Action Required by CEE/TL OR MANAGER**   

In case a customer calls in to report they have been mugged, car jacked, involved in an accident, fire, car break down at night etc. offer to call the emergency contacts on behalf of the customer if he is unable to due to loss of phone, no airtime, unable to connect to free numbers etc.

Offer the police, fire brigade, ambulance or 911 or 999 services and explain the subscriber's situation and contact number.

Escalate via email to the TL on duty, and this will be forwarded to our Security department.

The CEE/TL or Manager will capture this on the interaction.

**Bomb Threats**

**Definition**

This is where a caller gives a bomb threat and mostly it entails:

A customer makes any threat to the wellbeing of the employee or to the company in general (e.g., You guys are crooks, and should all be locked up"= not a threat BUT "You guys are crooks and should all be blown away "= a threat)

In times of social unrest, radicals, as targets for attack, may single out certain tenants and buildings. At any time, unbalanced people may make similar attacks for a variety of personal motives.

Threats are usually aimed at the tenant rather than the building. Thus, the tenant is generally the first to know of a pending threat and, therefore, must know how to react.

**Action Required by CEE/TL OR MANAGER**   

Upon receiving a bomb threat call, stay calm, write down exact wordings of the caller and continue to interrogate the caller to acquire more details.

Use another phone (if possible) to immediately notify the security team or Manager   on duty.

The CEE/TL or Manager will capture this on the interaction.

**Security Team Action**

The security team will analyse the threat information received versus the circumstances and recommend an immediate evacuation if necessary but after clearing and cordoning off evacuation paths.

In such cases, use of non-audible means to trigger the evacuation (where possible) is advised. An alternative and further located evacuation assembly point to be identified if one in use is less than 200m from the building.

When evacuating, if possible, doors and windows in the vicinity of the suspect area should be left open to assist in reducing the blast and fragmentation effect should the bomb explode.

The security team will conduct a search of the facility in general and the areas mentioned. This is done in conjunction with the Police Bomb Squad.

The security team will look out for anything out of place, suspicious looking that may match the description given by the caller.

In case of discovering a suspicious object, the person making the discovery should jot down observations alongside a simple sketch of object and location. This will be handed over to the Police Bomb Squad.

DO NOT touch or tamper with any suspicious object found in the building. Note location and report back findings to the Security Team.

Use of two-way radios and cell phones in the vicinity of the suspect area to be minimized.

**Skirmishes**

**Definition**

Skirmishes is an episode of irregular or unpremeditated fighting, especially between small groups of people in a society.

Customers may report skirmishes in the area and seek help in getting the police, ambulance, Fire Brigade, 911/999 Services.

**Action Required by CEE/TL OR** **Manager** **/ Escalation Folder Teams**

Empathize with the customer over unfortunate situations.

Capture details of the MSISDN, location and send to the Call Centre Escalation folder in the format below:

MSISDN

Customer Name

Location

Alternative Number (where applicable)

Send the caller details above via email to the Call Center escalation folder/respective shop folder for follow up.

The resource at the Call Center Escalation Folder/respective shop folder will call the security team on 0722-007777 and provide the details.

The CEE/TL or Manager will capture this on the interaction.

**Security Contacts**

·       HQ I, Nairobi 0722003997/ 0722003998/ 0722002923

·       HQ II, Nairobi 0722004887/0722-007777

·       SCC, Nairobi 0722002300 /0722002310

·       JCC, Nairobi 0722002740/ 0722002602

·       TCC 0722002892

·       Email [securityteam@safaricom.co.ke](mailto:securityteam@safaricom.co.ke)
