articleTitle: M-PESA Airtime Purchase and Airtime Reversal
markdownContent:
**M-PESA Airtime Reversal**

**Definition**

M-PESA airtime reversal is the process of returning airtime purchased erroneously from M-PESA either for self or for other numbers.

For all airtime reversals to be done the recipient must have sufficient airtime balance equivalent to the amount they bought i.e. Partial reversals will not be possible.

**Eligibility**

- It is eligible to customers who buy airtime erroneously to their number or to other number.
- It does not apply to first top up used to activate a new line.
- If funds are partially utilized, the customer will need to top up the used amount before
- Requesting for reversal.
- Lines less than 90 days old on the network will not be able to use 456 self-reversals.
- Airtime Purchase for other number cannot be reversed through 456. 456 airtime reversal is only for purchase for self

**NOTE:** A reversal on such a line can only be done once in the 90days.

**How to reverse via care centre**

- The CEE will proceed with reversal after confirming the below terms are met.
- The reversal claim must be made within 48hrs of purchase.
- The minimum reversal amount is Ksh.5 with no limit on the maximum.
- Only one reversal per customer per month shall be allowed.
- If funds are partially utilized, the customer will need to top up the used amount before requesting for reversal.

**Airtime Bought for Self**

- CEE will Query the customer’s number on CRM
- Confirm customer’s full names.
- Confirm the available balance on customer account, from IN Data to confirm customer has airtime equivalent or more than the reversal amount requested for.
- Click on the IN-Call History button and then on the Transaction History button.
- Under Transaction History, Specify Date Range and Query Recharge History.
- M-PESA Recharge transactions will load under transaction history. Highlight the transaction to reverse (Type must be “Recharge” and Cause must be “M-PESA”
- Under the additional info tab, details of the transaction will be displayed i.e. M-PESA transaction number, recipient’s number, senders’ number (for third party requests) and amount.
- Click on Reverse Transaction tab.
- An automatic interaction is created at the subscriber level with an OM Public ID.
- Drilling down on to the airtime reversal OM Public ID gives the details and status of the reversal transaction order.
- Confirm the status is complete and airtime deducted on customers account and M-PESA credited with the same amount.
- The Sender/customer (number which bought airtime) will receive a notification SMS from M-PESA that the funds have been reversed successfully and account balance credited to the same account.

**Airtime Bought for Other**

- The CEE will confirm the following:
- Customer full name
- Transaction to be reversed.
- Airtime balance on CRM (enough to allow for full reversal)
- Initiate the reversal on CRM.
- Confirm that the airtime has been deducted on CRM (airtime balance), and the same has been credited on the M-PESA system account.

**Recipient Calling**

- Where recipient calls the CEE will proceed with reversal guidelines. No consent will be required from the sender.
- If funds are fully or partially utilized, advise the recipient to top up and call back for reversal.

**Sender Calling**

- The CEE will put the call on hold and call the recipient to seek consent before reversing.
- Where consent is given, proceed to reverse the transaction and advise the customer accordingly.
- Confirm that the airtime has been deducted on CRM (Airtime balance), and that the same has been credited on the M-PESA system.
- Where consent is not given, inform the caller of the same and advise them to handle the issue with the recipient directly.
- Where the recipient is unavailable or not picking, capture the details on the airtime reversal link for the team to try reach the recipient.
- Advise the customer we will try reaching the recipient and will get back to them accordingly.
- Do not give any guarantees that the money will be recovered. Advice on SLA of 2 hrs.
- Where the third party has returned the money back to the sender, capture the details on the airtime reversal link, for reversal team to deal. Advice on SLA of 2hrs.
- Where the reversal fails due to exceed in limit, advice customer on limits. Customer can transfer funds to create room for the reversal amount and call back.
- Where customer can perform the transaction while on call, CEE will allow customer to transact and effect the reversal.
- However, this information on account exceeding Ksh.300, 000 should only be shared with the purchaser/sender and not recipient.
- Where CEE logs into both sender and recipient’s account, an interaction will be captured in both accounts with details of the interaction with customer.

**Partial M-PESA Airtime Reversal**

Customers who have purchased airtime from M-PESA will NOT be able to make partial reversals via 456.

**Reversal requests received after 8pm**

- As per our existing guidelines, we do not call customers after 8PM, kindly give the customer either of the options below.
- Log in the reversal request in the airtime reversal link. Advice the customer on SLA of 2hrs, from 8am the next day, (i.e. to be done by 10 am). Inform the customer we are not able to get consent to effect the reversal and advice it can only be done the following day, do not give assurance that the money will be recovered.
- The customer to engage the recipient to get in touch with Safaricom through any of our alternative channels for the reversal to be done.

**NOTE:**

**Used Airtime.**

If the airtime is fully utilized by recipient, advise the sender to engage recipient for refund.

**Insufficient funds**

- Where part of the airtime bought is utilized, advise the customer to top up and send the reversal request (M-PESA SMS) to 456.
- For third party purchase, advise the customer that funds are not available to liaise with the recipient.

**Missing CDRs on Siebel**

- If the transaction is not updated on transaction history, CEE will ensure customer has enough airtime on IN Data (equivalent or more than amount purchased) and advise the customer to send the request to 456.
- Do not advise the customer to call back for the scenarios above unless the customer deleted the M-PESA SMS.
- For Pooled lines, data lines, M-Kopa, Car tracking lines, GPRS unbundled with SMS Tariff - CEE reverses the transaction without consent.

**Scenarios where an M-PESA airtime reversal will generate an error on Siebel.**

- If the customer’s M-PESA limits will be exceeded i.e. the customer account will have a balance more than 100,000 after the reversal is initiated.
- Transaction is not an M -PESA airtime transaction.
- The transaction has already been reversed.
- The airtime account balance is less than the amount being reversed.

**Handling Bamba Reversal Requests**

- DSA/Retailer will liaise with their respective dealer head office/contact person to support the reversal of any top up.
- Incase it’s a customer calling, the care centre agent will raise an SR.
- If the SR is past SLA send email to the dealer support team for the respective account managers to handle with the dealer.

Customers will now receive their deposit refunds via **M-PESA within 5 to 10 minutes** once a manual termination is completed and all refund requirements have been met.

**Introduction**

Emerald Postpay is Safaricom’s premium mobile subscription plan, designed for high-value customers who desire exclusive benefits such as priority network access, more mobile data, international roaming options, and enhanced billing flexibility. This plan replaces the older Postpay, DIY, and Revamp options and delivers superior value to both new and existing subscribers.

**Eligibility & Availability**

Emerald Postpay is available to both Prepay and Postpay customers. The onboarding process differs slightly depending on the customer segment:

**Pricing**

Emerald PostPay offers four plans:

| AMOUNT KSH | RESOURCES |
| --- | --- |
| 1000 | 400 minutes + 12GB + FREE SMS (Capped at 1000 SMS) |
| 2000 | 1000 minutes + 25GB + FREE SMS (Capped at 2000 SMS) |
| 3000 | 1500 minutes + 39GB + FREE SMS (Capped at 3000 SMS) |
| 5000 | 2500 minutes + 67GB + FREE SMS (Capped at 5000 SMS) |
| 10000 | 7500 minutes +140GB +FREE SMS (Capped at 10000 SMS) |

**How to Join:**

- Prepay Customers: Dial \*544# > Go Monthly > Join Emerald
- Postpay Customers: Dial \*200# > Option 0 or *544\**10#

**Who can Join:**

- Whitelisted Customers (Achievers segment): Automatically eligible with no deposit required.
- Non-whitelisted Customers: Can still join by paying a deposit equal to the selected plan value.
- Existing Postpay Users:

- DIY Customers were migrated to Emerald on 1st May, with their current resources expiring in 2030.
- Postpay Revamp Customers were upgraded on 1st July, with resources expiring in 2037.
- Karibu Postpay Users must terminate via \*200# and migrate to Emerald via \*544# or *544*10#.

**Note:**

To view Emerald options, customers must be on the Uwezo tariff. If currently on other tariffs like Zidisha, S-SHOOK, or Corporate Postpay Bundles, these must be terminated first before migrating.

If a customer receives an SMS to join Emerald but cannot see the option via USSD, confirm their current tariff before escalating.

**Features & Add-ons**

Emerald Postpay comes with features aimed at enhancing the mobile experience:

**Included Benefits**

- Free E-SIM at first subscription (Automated activation upon purchase)

- More Mobile Data Bundles tailored to your needs.
- International Calling & Roaming with a dedicated roaming wallet:

- Voice and SMS roaming is default.
- Data roaming is available on request.

- E-Paper Access now available free of charge (\*200# > Emerald Benefits).
- M-Ratiba is available as a payment option.
- Postpay Milestones remain applicable.
- Tethering is allowed.

**Resource Management & Restrictions**

Validity:

- All Emerald bundles expire at the end of the calendar month, regardless of the subscription date.
- No resource rollovers—unused data, minutes, or SMS do not carry forward.

**Resource Sharing**

- Sambaza & Data Sharing: Not available.
- Lipa na Data: Not supported using Emerald resources (except for migrated resources or if the user has other qualifying resources).

**Usage of 3rd Party Services**

- Mobile banking and chargeable 3rd party USSD services are not covered under Emerald bundles and are billed separately via airtime.

**Customer Migration & Plan Changes**

- Customers migrated from DIY or Revamp plans will remain on Emerald and cannot revert to previous packages.
- Migrated resources for:

- Data: Expire in 2030 (DIY) or 2037 (Revamp).
- Minutes: Expiry adjustment is underway in favor of the customer.

- Customers who had disabled auto-renewal before migration retain non-expiring migrated resources.

**Changing Plans**

- Emerald users can upgrade or downgrade plans via \*200# > Change Plan.

**Emerald Postpay Upsell Journey**

To boost Emerald subscriptions, Safaricom has introduced an upsell journey within the All-in-One bundle purchase process:

**Key Highlights**

- Available via USSD \*544#.
- Customers purchasing All-in-One bundles will receive an upsell prompt to join the equivalent Emerald Postpay plan.
- Whitelisted users will proceed without a deposit.
- Others must pay a deposit during onboarding.
- All standard Emerald Postpay and Postpay billing rules apply.

Table below shows the difference in bundle resource offering between Current

Go Monthly Postpay and Emerald Postpay

| --- | --- | --- |
| 1000 | 400 minutes + 8GB + 1000 SMS + WA | 400 minutes + 12GB + 1000 SMS |

**Billing**

The due date is 16th of the month but disconnections happen at different dates. This is as per the schedule shared on monthly basis.

- Checking Balances: Dial \*200# > My Account or *544*44#.
- Roaming Wallet: Eliminates the need for roaming deposit or email requests—users simply top up the wallet to roam.

**Why the Name “Emerald”?**

The plan is named after the Emerald gem, known for its rarity and high value—more precious than diamonds. It reflects the premium status of Emerald customers, who are seen as true gems within the Safaricom ecosystem.

# **Definition**

Ziidi MMF is a flexible and accessible investment product that allows M-PESA customers to invest in a Money Market Fund with as little as **KSH 10** and earn **competitive daily interest.**

Only M-PESA can be used to invest or withdraw money, and once deposited, money is immediately available through the channels provided.

# **How to Access Ziidi**

M-PESA customers can easily opt in and transact via the following channels:

- Ziidi Mini App on the M-PESA App/ My Oneapp
- USSD \*334# under Financial Services

# **Ziidi Interest**

Interest paid is Compound interest calculated per annum (per year) and paid daily’.

Customers will be able to access their funds **24hrs** after SIM swap.

**How to earn Interest on Ziidi**

To earn interest on funds invested in ZIIDI, the invested funds must have been held by Ziidi for a minimum of 24hrs.

# **Funds Withdrawal**

The funds can only be invested or withdrawn via M-PESA, and all invested funds are instantly accessible through the provided channels.

**How It works**

- A customer’s line should be on active status for them to access the funds.
- The investment fund is subject to 15% withholding tax from government.
- Ziidi MMF is approved and regulated by Capital Markets Authority as a Money Market Fund.
- There are no transaction fees for investing, withdrawing, or checking balances with Ziidi MMF. M-PESA transaction charges however apply for funds once they are withdrawn back to M-PESA.
- The minimum amount you can invest is Kshs. 10 and the minimum amount to withdraw is Kshs.10.
- There is no limit to maximum balance Ziidi can hold.
- The current M-PESA transaction limits will apply to all ZIIDI MMF invest and withdraw transactions. Kshs 250,000 is the per transaction limit while daily transaction limit is Ksh.500,000. Transactions to and from are not charged.
- When a customer’s line is recycled, they will need to opt in again. If there were any funds at the time of recycling, those funds will be placed in a holding account until they are either claimed by the customer or transferred to UFAA. The accrued interest will be paid out along with the principal when the funds are claimed or sent to UFAA.
- The Ziidi and MALI services will each have their own separate Mini App and USSD channels.
- Please refer to the attached PPT guide for detailed instructions on the journeys.

**NOTE:** Safaricom will run Ziidi and MALI as two separate products. Currently Mali is closed to new Opt ins, but Ziidi will allow new opt ins

# **Key Benefits of Ziidi**

- **Easy Sign-up**: Sign up easily on the Mini App or USSD via your mobile phone — no paperwork required.
- **Secure**: Your Ziidi investment is protected with your M-PESA PIN, ensuring safe transactions.
- **Real-Time Access**: Withdraw and receive funds instantly in your M-PESA account. There’s no waiting for hours or days, and no limit to the number of withdrawals you can make per day.
- **Competitive Interest**: Ziidi offers a market-competitive interest rate, calculated annually and credited to your Ziidi account every day at midnight.
- **Affordability**: Start investing with as little as Ksh. 10, with no maximum limit on the amount your Ziidi account can hold.
- **Zero Transaction Costs**: There are no transaction fees for depositing or withdrawing funds from Ziidi, and no maintenance fees are charged.
- **Easy Tracking**: Provides full visibility of your daily earnings, helping you with financial planning and tracking.

# **Required Documents for Next of Kin or Recycled Line Claim of Funds**

Next of Kin is the person whose details are nominated on ZIIDI MMF by the account owner or is the legally designated heir and in the event of incapacities such as sickness, mental instability, and death they can have access to your funds. On condition of.

For claim of funds the customer (Next of Kin) will visit the nearest Safaricom retail shop or care desks and provide the following documents:

- A duly filled ZIIDI MMF next of kin claim of funds form.
- Identification document (ID)
- Death Certificate in case of death
- Grant of Probate/Letter of Administration
- Letter from local Administration ascertaining the heir.

For claim of funds involving recycled MSISDNs, the following process will apply at any Safaricom shop in the interim.

- Customer to fill M-PESA claim of funds form
- Customer to fill ZiiDi claim of funds form (attached)

For the claim of funds to be processed and paid within seven (7) working days, the CEE must escalate the request using the **SR Category i**ndicated below. Attach the two forms mentioned above along with the necessary KYC documents and send an email with the **SR number** to [GJacobs@Safaricom.co.ke](mailto:GJacobs@Safaricom.co.ke), copying [wealthmanagementsquad@Safaricom.co.ke](mailto:wealthmanagementsquad@Safaricom.co.ke)

**Category:** M-PESA ZIIDI

**Type:** Customer Account

**Item:** Next of Kin Claim

For change of ownership of the ZIIDI MMF Account, you need to withdraw all your funds and close the account. Then follow the current MSISDN change of ownership and change of account details.

- After the MSISDN change, your Next of Kin details are captured, and they can now opt-in to ZIIDI MMF to enjoy its services.
- The new owner of the account should opt into ZIIDI MMF to enjoy its services.
- For claim of funds from a recycled SIM card, you will fill in a claims form and present your ID for processing.

**Note:** See attachments for the claims form.

# **Consequences of Attempting to Close an Account with Funds Remaining**

- You will receive a prompt that advises you to withdraw all the funds before closing your ZIIDI MMF account. If you choose to withdraw funds and close the account, the funds will be automatically transferred to your M-PESA account.
- If Ziidi balance is more than the allowed daily M-PESA limit, the investor will need to withdraw over several days until all the funds are withdrawn before opting out.
- For support and inquiry, customers should contact Safaricom Call Center or visit Safaricom Retail Center.

# **Ziidi** **Locked Funds**

Locking funds in ZIIDI MMF means setting aside a portion or all your funds to prevent unplanned spending. It also adds a layer of safety and control over your funds, helping you stay focused on your financial goals.

Key details about the locking feature:

- **Eligibility**: Only Ziidi customers can initiate the Lock Funds feature. MALI customers do not have access to this functionality.
- **Interest earned**: Locked funds will earn the same interest as unlocked funds, with no additional interest earned for locking.
- **Topping up**: You can continue adding funds to the locked portion even if there is an existing active lock.
- **Lock Period**: There is currently no set period for how long funds can be locked.
- **Unlocking**: Once unlocked, funds will be available 72 hours later.
- **Re-locking**: To initiate a new lock after unlocking, any previous unlock transactions must be completed, and the funds must be successfully disbursed or customer can cancel request.
- **No Limit**: There is no maximum limit to the amount of money you can lock.

# **Partial Unlock**

Partial unlock is a feature that allows ZIIDI Lock Funds customers to access part of their locked funds without needing to unlock all the locked funds.

**Benefits**

Customers are able to access only the funds they need from the lock funds feature without needing to unlock all the funds.

**Eligibility**

All active ZIIDI Lock Funds customers are eligible to use this feature.

**Mechanics**

- The customer will be able to unlock to up to 70% of their current lock funds balance.
- The customer is also able to cancel a pending unlock request, both partial and full unlock requests
- When a customer cancels a request, they will need to initiate a new request to unlock their funds which means the unlock count down to maturity will commence afresh. So they will not be able to piggy back on the cancelled request remaining period. For example, if the cancelled request had 2 hours pending to maturity, the new request will not unlock in 2hrs but will start afresh at 72 hrs to maturity at the point of initiating the request
- The partial unlock feature is the same as the full unlock where, locking does not debit your Ziidi wallet and neither does unlocking credit the Ziidi wallet.

# **Ziidi vs MALI**

Both Ziidi and MALI are Money Market Fund products available to M-PESA customers. However, **Ziidi will be the only product accepting new opt-ins**. MALI will continue to be operational, but no new sign-ups will be accepted for this product.

**Understanding Money Market Fund (MMF)**

- It is a type of unit trust under the Collective investment scheme umbrella. An MMF is considered a fairly low risk investment with the aim of giving a fair return.
- An MMF mainly invests the funds in interest bearing assets approved within the CIS regulations 2013, such as fixed deposits, call deposits and government papers.
- Money Market funds do not give a fixed return, but the rates vary depending on the macro environment and where the fund managers invest.

#  **Ziidi Vs Other MMF’s**

| Feature | Ziidi MMF | Other MMF’s |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Accessibility | Purely Digital onboarding for M-PESA customers via M-PESA App and USSD | Manual onboarding with some banks/Fund Managers offering digital onboarding. Bank may require you to have a bank account with them |
| Minimum Investment | Kes 10 | Kes 2000 upwards |
| Risk Diversification | Multiple fund managers | Single fund managers |
| Cash Withdrawal | Instant withdrawal into M-PESA wallet at no cost | Withdrawal takes between 24-72hours. Charges may apply |
| Fees | No fees to invest and withdraw | Some charges may apply to transfer funds |
| Locked savings | Ability to lock funds for different tenors | No locked features |

T &Cs are available on Safaricom website [Ziidi Money Market Fund By Safaricom.](https://www.safaricom.co.ke/main-mpesa/m-pesa-services/wealth/ziidi)

# **Ziidi Escalations**

 **1st Level support -** customer Facing – CEEs / Contact Centre/Retail; Try resolve the issue, if not - raise SR on CRM, Follow up with Assigned ticket owner.

**2nd Level support -** Support Analyst; Receive 1st Level support escalation, Try resolve the issue, if not all operational issues to fintech operations on email & all technical issues go to FSS Support on BMC

**3rd Level Support -** Fintech Operations - FinTech Operations [fintechoperations@Safaricom.co.ke](mailto:fintechoperations@Safaricom.co.ke) ; Close on all operational issue. Unless it is a technical issue.

**4th Level Support** – Technical Issues which goes to FSS Support Team [FSSSupportTeam@Safaricom.co.ke](mailto:FSSSupportTeam@Safaricom.co.ke) – A ticket must be raised (BMC)

# **CRM Interactions and Service Requests (SRs)**

 Interactions and SRs will be logged under **M-PESA ZIIDI** (Interaction Type and SR Category).

# **M-PESA Business Split Payments**

# **Definition**

M-PESA Business Split Payments is a solution that automatically distributes incoming customer payments from a Paybill or Till number to other business accounts in real time. Funds are shared immediately when a payment is received, eliminating the need for manual transfers and reducing delays and errors.

# **Eligibility**

The solution is available to businesses with an active M-PESA Paybill or Till number and up-to-date KYC records. Currently, only Business-to-Business (B2B) split payments are supported, while Business-to-Customer (B2C) functionality is planned for future releases. Existing Paybill or Till numbers can be used; there is no requirement to create a new shortcode.

# **Access Channels**

Split Payments can be activated and managed through:

- M-PESA Business Hub (MBH)
- USSD (\*234#)
- M-PESA Business App

# **Activation Process**

**M-PESA Business Hub (MBH)**

The Administrator activates the service by selecting **“Enable for your Business”**, choosing the relevant shortcode, accepting the Terms and Conditions, and verifying the request through a One-Time Password (OTP).

**USSD**

The Primary Operator activates the service by dialing **\*234#** and navigating to the Split Payments menu.

# **User Roles and Responsibilities**

After activation on MBH, the Business Manager or Operator is responsible for configuring and managing split rules. The Administrator's role is limited to activation and does not extend to ongoing management of split configurations. Auditors have view-only access. On USSD, split payment management is restricted to the Primary Operator linked to the Paybill or Till number.

# **Configuration Requirements**

To configure a split payment arrangement, the business requires:

- A source Paybill or Till number
- Recipient Paybill or Till number(s)
- Split percentages for each recipient account

# **Supported Split Types**

The platform currently supports percentage-based splits only. Fixed-amount splits are planned for future release.

# **Supported Transaction Combinations**

Split Payments supports all B2B transaction combinations, including:

- Paybill to Paybill
- Paybill to Till
- Till to Paybill
- Till to Till

# **Recipient Limits**

Each source Paybill or Till number can distribute funds to a maximum of three recipient shortcodes. This limit may be reviewed in future enhancements.

# **Split Percentage Rules**

Recipients can receive between **0.01% and 99.99%** of incoming payments. The combined allocation to all recipients cannot exceed **99.99%**, ensuring that at least **0.01%** remains in the originating account. As a result, splitting 100% of incoming funds is not permitted.

# **How Split Payments Work**

Once activated, Split Payments automatically apply to all incoming transactions received on the configured shortcode. Businesses cannot select individual transactions for splitting. If certain transactions should not be split, a separate Paybill or Till number should be used.

# **Managing Split Configurations**

Businesses can edit or remove split rules at any time through MBH or USSD. Changes take effect immediately, unless approval workflows have been configured on MBH. When a recipient is removed, future payments are no longer allocated to that recipient, though previously processed transactions remain unchanged. Similarly, updates to split percentages affect only future transactions.

There is currently no pause feature. To stop splitting to a recipient temporarily, the recipient must be deleted and re-added later if required.

# **Approval Workflows**

On MBH, implementation of split configurations depends on the organization's maker-checker settings. Under a **No Approval** setup, changes are applied immediately. Under **Parallel**, **Sequential**, or **Advanced** approval models, an authorized approver must review and approve the changes before they become active.

# **Charges and Fees**

There are no setup charges or subscription fees for Split Payments. However, standard M-PESA B2B transaction tariffs apply when funds are transferred to recipient accounts.

**Customer Experience**

Customers only see the total amount paid to the business on their M-PESA receipt. The internal distribution of funds among recipient businesses is not visible to customers.

# **Reversals and Failed Transactions**

Approved transaction reversals follow the standard M-PESA reversal process. When a reversal is successfully processed, all distributed amounts are returned to their respective accounts.

If a recipient shortcode is invalid or encounters an issue, the split transaction for that recipient fails. Failed transactions are displayed in the **FAILED** tab on MBH, enabling businesses to review and take corrective action.

Frozen or suspended shortcodes can still be configured as recipients, but payment distributions to those accounts will fail until the shortcode is restored to active status.

# **Visibility and Reporting**

Businesses can access complete split-payment histories through M-PESA transaction statements and reports. MBH also provides detailed audit trails through the **Approvals** and **Failed** tabs.

Auditors can view all split configurations, approvals, and failed transactions, but they cannot make changes to any configurations.

**Getting Started**

Businesses can begin using Split Payments through any of the following channels:

**M-PESA Business Hub (MBH)**

1. Log in to MBH.
2. Navigate to **Split Payments**.
3. Select **Enable for your Business**.

**USSD**

1. Dial **\*234#**.
2. Select **Split Payments**.

**Business App**

1. Log in to the M-PESA Business App.
2. Navigate to **Split Payments**.
3. Select the relevant shortcode.

# **Support**

For assistance, businesses should first review the **FAILED** tab on MBH for transaction details. Additional support is available through:

- **M-PESA Business Support:** 2222
- **Email:** MPESABusiness@safaricom.co.ke

## **Definition**

Inua Jamii is a Kenya Government-Funded Cash Transfer Program managed by The State Department for Social Protection & Senior Citizen Affairs under the Ministry of Labour and Social Protection.

*Inua Jamii* is aimed at supporting vulnerable groups by providing monthly cash transfers to improve the lives of orphans, vulnerable children, older persons, and individuals with severe disabilities.

**NOTE:**

•  Customers requiring KYC/Risk Validation were sent CVM Messages on 20th Jan 2026 directing them to visit either Retail centre or the Social Protection offices with their original ID for verification.

Customers who received messages to visit our Retail shops/Caredesk or Franchise will be assisted at the shop to update their KYC on our systems, then their details shared on Analytica under Inua Jamii suspension (see attached).

## **Enrolment**

Enrolment into the Inua Jamii program is planned & carried out periodically by The State Department for Social Protection through a process where eligible beneficiaries, including older persons aged 70 and above, orphans, and individuals with severe disabilities are taken through a verification & registration process of eligible individuals.

All enrolment issues should be channeled to the Social Protection officers located in every County across the country for any clarifications on enrolment or call 1533.

All beneficiaries who have been added to the program will receive SMS notification with the service name once funds have been sent to their wallets and can check their balance via \*222#ok (charged Ksh.1 per USSD session), then select View Balance option.

***Sample SMS: Hi ERICK, welcome to SurePay, you have been added as a Beneficiary by INUA JAMII.***

New beneficiaries must activate their Inua Jamii eCitizen Accounts using USSD code \*222# upon registration following the steps below:

i.         Dial \*222#ok (charges Ksh.1 airtime per session) >> Select Inua Jamii >> Select the language >> Select activate account >> Accept the terms and conditions >> Enter mobile money PIN.

  Then the customer will receive an SMS confirming successful account activation.

## **Inua Jamii payment transition**

The Government is transitioning Inua Jamii payments from bank accounts to MPESA agents via the E-Citizen platform to enhance service delivery.

The pilot phase began in November 2024 in Murang’a and Marsabit counties.

Starting February 2025, all beneficiaries will access their funds through MPESA agents using \*222# eliminating the need for bank withdrawals.

**Beneficiaries without Phone Numbers**

Elder persons who are already part of the program and have no phone numbers should visit a nearby M-PESA Agent with their national ID, to register for a SIM card and activate M-PESA.

## **NOTE:**

Safaricom has made an exception to allow M-PESA Agents register lines for Inua Jamii beneficiaries/caregivers above 60 years whose IDs have been validated by Safaricom.

## **Phone Number Update/Delink**

Beneficiaries can request for phone number update if they are no longer in possession of their previous number or where the number was wrongly captured in the system.

**Note:** Phone number change/delinking is only allowed once. If another change is needed, advise the beneficiary to visit social protection offices for assistance.

The error below will be presented for 2nd or subsequent change attempts: ***Phone number delinking is only allowed once. The previous number was already delinked from this ID. Current number: 254707\*\*\*231. Please advise the beneficiary to visit social protection offices for assistance***.

There are two steps involved in this action.

1.   First, Safaricom staff who is whitelisted on \*222# will do the delinking as illustrated below. Delink option is also available on CRM under Gava Wallet.

 [Screenshot] 

2.      Beneficiary will activate Inua Jamii account on the new line after delinking.

 [Screenshot] 

## **CRM VIEWS:**

An Inua Jamii (Gava Wallet) applet has been added on CRM and will be useful in:

1)     Confirming Beneficiaries transaction history.

2)     MSISDN Delinking to allow beneficiaries opt in on their preferred MSISDN.

Attached to this article is the step-by-step process of accessing and using the CRM feature.

## **Payments Allocation**

Beneficiaries and fund allocation is done by The State Department for Social Protection System and E-citizen Platform.

Phone numbers of enrolled beneficiaries will be whitelisted so that they can access funds using the eCitizen Platform USSD \*222#.

Each beneficiary identified by the government will receive an allocation that is set as per the programme the beneficiary is enrolled in – namely:

·            The Cash Transfer Program for Orphans and Vulnerable Children (CT for OVC)

·            The Older Persons Cash Transfer Program (OP-CT)

·            The Person with Severe Disability Cash Transfer Program (PwSD-CT)

## **Accessing the funds**

1.   Beneficiaries’ funds will be allocated to a universal wallet (Inua Jamii Wallet) and **NOT** to the beneficiary M-PESA Wallet.

2.   Beneficiaries can move the funds from the Inua Jamii wallet to their M-PESA Wallet.

 **[Screenshot]**

3.   The beneficiary can also access funds from the Inua Jamii wallet by withdrawing at an M-PESA Agent free of charge (no charges to withdraw from the Inua Jamii wallet).

 [Screenshot] 

 The M-PESA agents will receive normal M-PESA withdrawal commission on any Inua Jamii withdrawal.

## **Assisted Withdrawals (Coming soon)**

Once ready, M-PESA Agent assist customers to withdrawals from the virtual wallet via \*234# option.

This will be applicable to beneficiary/caregiver without their physical line but are part of the program and have an active allocation.

## **Mini Statement**

This enables beneficiaries to check their Inua Jamii wallet access history for both tracking and reconciliation of their allocation.

Below steps explains the process of accessing Inua Jamii Mini statement.

 [Screenshot] 

## **Errors**

•  If the SMS is “Service not available at the moment” advise to top up airtime

•  If error says (Request cancelled by user) means the customer did not complete the process/ended the process

•  If SMS is (The initiator information is invalid) beneficiary entered invalid PIN.

•  If the USSD(\*222#ok) error is "***Request not successful. Please visit your nearest Safaricom shop for assistance***", the customer will need to visit a Safaricom Retail centre, Franchise or Caredesk for **KYC update** (see attached step-by-step KYC update process). 

KYC update will be done at the shop to match details on our systems with details on original ID, then customer assisted to access funds before leaving the shop - Ensure customer line has airtime to access \*222#ok.

**Note**: we will update some of the SMSs to communicate the correct error.

## **Support Lines**

Beneficiaries can call 100/200 or 1533 and they will be supported.

Which categories of question are handled on 100/200 and 1533(toll free)?

       **i.**            **Questions for 100/200**

•              Balance inquiries (Beneficiary can DIY on  \*222#)

•              Withdrawal confirmation

•              Reasons for not being able to access the wallet. An example of this maybe confirming if the mobile number has been barred or maybe the PIN entered is wrong/blocked

•              Missing allocation. Confirm if customer has been allocated funds on the Surepay system. 

**ii.       Sample questions for line 1533(a toll-free number)**

•              Beneficiary management i.e. not been added on the program

## **Escalations**

Frontline teams will escalate via Inua Jamii SR on CRM

**Other escalations:**

2nd line support teams/analysts will escalate via CRM Activities as Follow-Up and assign to **D\_PSD**

**Definition**

This is the act of taking care of the customer’s needs by providing and delivering professional, helpful, high-quality service and assistance before, during and after the customer’s requirements are met.

Customer handling meets the needs and desires of any customer.

**Characteristics of good customer handling.**

**Salutation**

This is a formal greeting to a customer.

**Opening Greetings**

A CEE should use appropriate greetings whether recorded or mouthed. The greeting should be audible and clear.

They should also maintain the same tone level as the recorded greeting for a more natural effect without any delays.

The CEE must respond in a receptive manner.

In the absence of recorded greeting, the CEE must use appropriate opening, ensuring that they state their name clearly.

e) Where customer requests the agent to give 2 or 3 names, agent should give as requested.

**Example for inbound calls**

*“Jambo, thank you for contacting Safaricom, my name is\*\*\*\*\* how may I help you?”*

*“Jambo, shukrani kwa kupiga Safaricom, jina langu ni \*\*\*\* nikusaidie vipi?”*

**Example for outbound calls**

*“Good (Morning, Afternoon, Evening). This is \*\*\*\*\* calling from Safaricom.”*

*“Habari ya (asubuhi, mchana, jioni). Huyu ni \*\*\*\*\* nakupigia kutoka Safaricom.”* 

**Impact of Receptive Greeting;**

It assists you **to create rapport very quickly.**

First impacts of professionalism – Customers experience a standard greeting every time they call in.

The Customer immediately knows who he / she is talking to

It creates a sense of welcome and it demonstrates that you are open to create Rapport.

The greeting is clear and audible the first time around because of the simplistic, short words

The Customer also has a name to ask for or to refer to when he calls again, e.g. to give a compliment on excellent service received.

**Personalization**

A **CEE is encouraged to use Customer Name/Title naturally** within the call where applicable.

If the customer refuses to share their Name, or does not wish to be addressed by Name, then just continue with the call …do not insist on getting or using the Name.

In the absence of name presented on Siebel or customer not pronouncing their name the agent will politely ask for the customer’s name. ***‘****Kindly who am I Speaking to?’*

**Types of Personalization Scenarios:**

**At the Beginning of the call**

Where the customer has introduced themselves at the beginning of the call…then use the name used on introduction**\-**

     *“Magdalene, I see that your Skiza tune…”*

 *“…yes John, I am delighted to inform you that….’*

Where the customer has not introduced him/herself then confirm the name…. from CRM,

*“…am I speaking to Magdalene?”*

Where the customer has not introduced him/herself, but CRM fails to display name:

  *“...may I know whom I am talking to?*

   *“...may I know who is on the line…? “*

   *“…and whom am I speaking to?”*

If the customer refers **to themselves by their Title**

*Be sure to use professional titles where applicable. Unique titles, such as Prof, Dr, Eng., and even Mr./Mrs./ Ms./Miss are usually combined with the Surname.*

 *If CRM presents Professor Franklyn Orutwa Nyakang’o, then it would be appropriate to refer to me on the call as Professor Nyakang’o.*

**Example of how to address customers at the beginning of the call**

Dr. Mr. Mheshimiwa… the CEE will acknowledge the same during their interaction e.g. I understand Dr…or Good day Mheshimiwa (Refer to the Title as given by the customer).

Good morning Mr.…, Good afternoon Dr. ……. Good evening Mheshimiwa …….

If Customer already mouthed their Name & Title at introduction then mirror it throughout the call. ‘Use your judgement to profile the Customer and address them appropriately’

**In the middle of the call:**

… “Additionally, Mary you can delete this service on your own by dialing…”

… “Isaac, I have also noticed that your account...”

I hear you John, I understand Mary…….

**Closing**

The CEE should **thank the customer for calling and end the call immediately**.

The closing should not be rushed, and the words clearly pronounced.

The agent should not deliberately disconnect the call before the customer issue has been stated and resolved.

The CEE will also close the call where applicable with an attribute that came out during the call.

**Example of how to address customers at closing of the call**

Customer is travelling, unwell or during special holidays e.g. Christmas and Easter.

“If that is all Prof. (Name / title) I wish you a Blessed day” …. I was glad to serve you …. (Name/ Title……enjoy your holidays…. Get well soon (Name/Title).

“Thank you, Mr. Spencer, for calling Safaricom Customer Care and indeed it’s been a pleasure serving you…”

**If a customer wants to speak to a manager**

*"I regret am not in a position to connect the call directly, kindly allow me to have my manager contact you within 2 hours".*

*Nasikitika siwezi kuunganisha simu moja kwa moja, tafadhali niruhusu kumuulizia meneja awasiliane nawe katika masaa mawili*

*"I do apologize for the challenge, kindly allow me to request my manager/supervisor get back to you within 2 hours".*

*Samahani kwa changamoto hio, tafadhali niruhusu kumuulizia meneja/msimamizi awasiliane nawe katika masaa mawili.*

**Impact of personalization**

Assists in creating a great rapport.

Makes the customer feel important

Helps in taking control of the call.

**Handling Short calls**

Whenever you encounter a silent or a nonresponsive customer, prompt them to respond by saying Hallo twice separated by a natural pause (about 3 seconds).

If still no response, ask if you are still audible – can you hear me?

If still no response is forthcoming, apologize for not hearing the caller and ask them to call back from a different phone for assistance and end the call with the appropriate closing.

**Sample script;**

*“Hallo- (pause 3sec) ...hello.... (pause 3sec) ...is anyone on the call.... (pause 3sec)...can you hear me?. (pause 3sec) ...hallo...sorry i cannot hear you, if you can hear me please call us back using a different phone and we will be able to assist. Thankyou for calling Safaricom, have a good morning/afternoon/evening.”*

Also ensure you send the SMS giving the customer alternative solution to their inaudible call. The SMS is available on Siebel SMS templates under silent /nonresponsive calls.

# **Shiriki Pay**

# **Definition**

Shiriki Pay is a Safaricom service that enables individuals to securely share access to their M‑PESA funds with a trusted person, such as a spouse, child, house manager, or personal assistant, for the purpose of making payments.

# **Eligibility**

Any customer with an active M‑PESA account can use Shiriki Pay.

# **How It Works**

Shiriki Pay allows an account holder (sponsor) to grant controlled access to their M‑PESA wallet without transferring funds. The sponsor assigns a transaction limit to a beneficiary, who can then perform transactions within that limit. All transactions are deducted directly from the sponsor’s wallet, and the money remains securely in the sponsor’s account at all times.

# **How to Access Shiriki Pay**

Customers can access Shiriki Pay through the following channels:

- USSD by dialing \*334#
- Shiriki Pay Mini App within the M‑PESA app

# **Adding a Beneficiary**

To add a trusted person:

- Navigate to the “Add Beneficiary” option on USSD or the Mini App
- Enter the phone number of the beneficiary
- Set a transaction limit
- Confirm using your M‑PESA PIN

# **Managing Beneficiaries**

As a sponsor, you can:

- Add or remove beneficiaries
- Assign transaction limits
- Increase or reduce allocated limits
- View and delete beneficiaries (feature available on G3)

# **Beneficiary Capabilities**

Once added, a beneficiary can use their assigned limit to:

- Send money
- Pay bills
- Buy goods
- Pay to Pochi la Biashara

# **Making Payments as a Beneficiary**

To transact:

- Access Shiriki Pay via USSD or Mini App
- Select a payment option (Send Money, Pay Bill, Buy Goods, or Pochi la Biashara)
- Choose the wallet
- Enter recipient or business details
- Input the amount
- Confirm using PIN

# **Beneficiary and Sponsor Limits**

- A sponsor can add up to 5 beneficiaries
- A beneficiary can have up to 3 sponsors
- Maximum limit per beneficiary is KES 20,000 per month

# **Transaction Limits**

Sponsors can set either daily or monthly transaction limits for each beneficiary to control usage.

# **Wallet and Funds Management**

Funds remain in the sponsor’s wallet at all times. Transactions initiated by the beneficiary are deducted directly from the sponsor’s account. Money is not transferred to the beneficiary’s wallet.

# **Insufficient Funds Scenario**

If the sponsor’s wallet does not have enough funds to cover a transaction and related charges:

- The transaction will fail
- The beneficiary will receive an error notification

# **Removing a Beneficiary**

To remove a beneficiary:

- Go to “Remove Shiriki Pay User”
- Select the beneficiary
- Confirm removal using your PIN

# **Editing Limits**

Sponsors can view and adjust beneficiary transaction limits at any time through the platform.

# **Security**

All transactions are secured using M‑PESA PIN authentication and Safaricom’s built-in security protocols.

**Age on Network rule**: This rule has been put to weed out BAs adding themselves as beneficiaries to new customers

**Beneficiary Rule**: A limit has been put on how many sponsors one beneficiary can have.

**Fraud Check-** Fraud check at opt in for those flagged for fraud.

The system performs a background check to confirm a recent M-PESA transaction relationship between the sponsor and the intended beneficiary within the last 30 days. This supports fraud prevention and helps protect customer funds. If no relationship is found, the request is declined with the message:

*Dear Customer, your request could not be processed. The beneficiary you are adding is not eligible to be added to your Shiriki Pay.*

If the relationship is verified, the beneficiary is successfully added.

# **Usage Scope**

Shiriki Pay can be used for both personal and business purposes, making it suitable for households and small group financial management.

# **PIN Management**

If a user forgets their M‑PESA PIN, it can be reset through the standard Safaricom PIN recovery process.

# **Charges**

- A fee of KES 35 applies for each Shiriki Pay user limit setup
- Standard M‑PESA transaction charges also apply
- Customers are advised to check updated tariffs via the Safaricom app or website

# **Transaction History**

Users can check their transaction history through:

- The M‑PESA app
- USSD under “My Account”

**Multiple Wallets**

Customers can link multiple shared wallets to their Shiriki Pay account.

# **Opt-In and Authentication**

To start using Shiriki Pay:

- Navigate to the Shiriki Pay option
- Follow the on-screen opt-in or authentication prompts
- Enter details and confirm using your PIN

# **Error Handling and Support**

If an error occurs:

- Contact Safaricom customer care
- Visit the nearest Safaricom shop for assistance

# **Geographic Availability**

Shiriki Pay is only available for use within Kenya and does not support cross-border transactions.

# **Transaction Reversals**

Only the sponsor can initiate a reversal by forwarding the transaction message to 456. Currently, beneficiaries cannot initiate reversals, although this feature may be introduced in the future.

markdownContent:
**Change of** **Organization Contacts/ Notification MSISDN:**

These are requests from Buy Goods and PayBill merchants to update their notification MSISDNs or organization contact details currently captured on M-PESA G2. Updates are made directly on the M-PESA G2 platform.

**Change of Organization Contacts (Email Address/Telephone Number)**

**Requests Received at the Call Centre (L100/ L200/ L234/ L2222):**

CEEs should guide merchants **to update their** **organization email via self-service** by dialling \*234\*2# or \*234\*4#, depending on their product type.

If the self-service option fails, or the merchant also wants to update the organization telephone number, CEEs should:

i.         Share with the merchants the KYC requirements based on their business category.

ii.         Advise the merchant to submit the request by visiting a Safaricom Shop or send an email to [**M-PESABusiness@safaricom.co.ke**](mailto:M-PESABusiness@safaricom.co.ke)**.**

**Requests Received at the Safaricom Retail Centre /Franchise Shops:**

Agents should first advise merchants to update the organization email via \*234\*2# or \*234\*4#.

If the self-service option fails, or an organization phone number update is also needed:

i.         Inform the merchant of the required KYC documents according to their business type.

ii.         Review the submitted documents.

iii.         Log an interaction on CRM and raise an SR for LNM Support to action within a **24-hour SLA.**

**Requests Received via Email:**

The merchant should send an email request through their registered organization email (as captured on G2) to [M-PESABusiness@Safaricom.co.ke](mailto:M-PESABusiness@Safaricom.co.ke).

CEEs should advise the merchants/partners **to update their organization email via self-service** by dialling \*234\*2# or \*234\*4#, depending on their product type.

If the self-service option fails, or the merchant also wants to update the organization telephone number, CEEs should:

i.         Inform the merchant of the required KYC documents according to their business type.

ii.         Review the submitted documents.

iii.         Raise an SR for LNM Support, to be actioned within a **24-hour SLA.**

**Requests Received by EBU Account Management Teams / EBU Sales team:**

Account management teams will advise the merchants/partners to update their organization email through self-service option \*234\*2# or \*234\*4# as per the product.

If the self-service option fails, or the merchant also wants to update the organization telephone number, the account managers/ Dealer Support Agents will advise merchant to share KYC requirements as per Business Category. 

The account management teams will then send an email request and attach relevant documents provided to  [lnmaggregators@safaricom.co.ke](mailto:lnmaggregators@safaricom.co.ke) and [lnmverticals@safaricom.co.ke](mailto:lnmverticals@safaricom.co.ke).

The LNM Support will action within **2 hours SLA.**

**Requests Received by LNM Support Team:**

The team will pick the SR or email activity and vet the attached KYC documents as per business category.

To update the organization email, LNM support team MUST contact the current nominated number/finance contact for consent.

Where vetting is passed and consent given, LNM support team will execute changes on G2 as per request.

Where vetting is failed and the request is not fulfilled, they LNM support team will advise the merchant accordingly and capture comments on the SR.

***NOTE:*** ***The Change of Organization Contact form and KYC Requirements per business category are attached in the appendix***

***SR Category:*** *LNM BUY GOODS AND SERVICES*

***SR Type****: Change of KYC Details*

***SR Item:*** *Organization Contact*

**Change of Notification MSISDN**

Merchants may request to update their notification MSISDN for the following reasons:

i.         The current notification MSISDN is pooled or inactive, and the merchant is not receiving notifications.

ii.         The current notification MSISDN is also mapped to another Till or Paybill, resulting in incorrect notification being received by the merchant.

iii.         The merchant simply wants to update the personal number used for receiving notifications.

**Requests can be received through the following channels:**

**Requests Received via Call:** The merchant should call from the nominated number.

**Requests Received via Email:** The merchant should send the request via email from the registered organization email in G2.

**Requests Received at the Safaricom Retail Centre /Franchise Shops:** The nominated person/ finance contact will present their original ID document. ID presented must match the details as registered on M-PESA G2.

**For Aggregated Tills/Paybills (e.g., Banks, Kopokopo, Empire, Carepay, etc.):** Requests to change the notification MSISDN should be sent directly by the respective aggregator to  [lnmaggregators@safaricom.co.ke](mailto:lnmaggregators@safaricom.co.ke)

**Standard Requests:**

If the current notification MSISDN is pooled or mapped to another till/Paybill, the frontline team will raise an SR to LNM Support to change the prepack. This will be actioned **within a 24-hour SLA.**

If the proposed notification MSISDN to be updated is a personal number (not on the M-PESA Agent Tariff), the merchant must provide:

i.         A stamped or sealed written request on the company letterhead clearly stating the request to update the notification MSISDN. The letter must include the MSISDN to be added, the full names and ID number of the MSISDN owner and be signed by at least two authorized signatories (or one signatory for sole proprietorships.)

ii.         Clear National ID scanned both sides or Valid Passport of the proposed notification receiving MSISDN.

Once provided, the frontline facing teams will raise an SR to LNM Support to update the notification MSISDN. **This will be actioned within a 24-hour SLA.**

***Note******: If the customer receiving erroneous till/Paybill notifications DOES NOT own a Till or Paybill, raise an SR without vetting. Attach sample notifications received or indicate the shortcode for which the notifications are being received.***

*SR Category: LNM BUY GOODS AND SERVICES*

*SR Type: Notifications*

*SR Item: Notifications Delay/ Failure*

**Change of Organization Telephone Number/Nominated Number**

This process applies when a merchant or partner wants to update the office telephone number linked to their short code on M-PESA G2. Requests for this change shall be submitted through the following available channels:

**Requests Received via Email**

- The merchant should send an email request from their **registered organization email** to **MPESABusiness@Safaricom.co.ke**.
- If they don’t have a registered organization email, guide them on how to update or register one (refer to the process for changing organization email above).
- Once the request is received:

1. Share the **Change of Organization Contact Form** and **KYC requirements** based on the merchant’s business category. 

i.     [LPPP-0007: LIPA NA M-PESA KYC Requirements (Paybill and Merchants)](../../app/article/983ecaf3-a912-4f95-89e9-85239f76d05e#:~:text=LPPP%2D0007%3ALIPA%20NA%20M%2DPESA%20KYC%20Requirements%20\(Paybill%20and%20Merchants\))

ii.     [LPPP-0006: Short Term Paybill Definition and KYC Requirements](../../app/article/b822ef23-1d77-4c67-bd5f-b1434d88e07f#:~:text=LPPP%2D0006%3AShort%20Term%20Paybill%20Definition%20and%20KYC%20Requirements)

2. Check that all documents are complete and correct.
3. Raise a **Service Request (SR)** for LNM Support. This should be done within 24 hours.

**Requests received at the Safaricom Retail Centre:**

a)   The CEE shall inform the merchant on the required KYC documents, based on their business category.

b)   Requests shall be submitted by the following authorized persons:

The sole owner for Individual Tills, as registered on G3.

The sole proprietor/owner, as per the Certificate of Registration or Business Permit

For partnerships, at least two partners, as per the Certificate of Registration or Partnership Deed.

For limited companies, at least two directors, as per the current CR12, or one director for companies with a sole director.

For other institutions (e.g., Churches, NGOS, Societies, Government and Parastatals), the existing finance contact/ nominated number, as registered on G3.

c)   The submitter/(s) MUST present their original ID for verification.

d)   Upon submission, the CEE shall review all documents for completeness and accuracy and ensure the following before updating any changes on G3:

The request has been submitted by either the sole owner or at least two directors or two partners.

For companies with multiple directors or for partnerships with multiple partners, the individuals submitting the request at the Safaricom Shop must be the authorized signatories on the change form.

For other institutions such as churches, NGOs and governments, the request shall be submitted by the existing nominated person/ finance contact as registered on M-PESA G3.

Where the existing finance contact is unavailable and the request is submitted by the proposed nominated number/finance contact or any other organization representative, the CEE shall call the existing nominated number/finance contact to obtain consent.

The short code has no outstanding loan as per CRM, that is, (Fuliza Biashara, Taasi Asante, Taasi DTB, etc.). Where any outstanding loan exists, the CEE shall advise the merchant to clear the outstanding loan balance first to enable the change.

The previous nominated number (NN) details on the change form are as registered on M-PESA G3. Where the details do not match, advise the merchant to fil the correct previous NN details

The new NN details (name and ID) on the change form are as registered on M-PESA G3. Where the details do not match, advise the merchant to correct.

e)   Upon successful vetting and validation, the CEE shall update the below fields on M-PESA G3:

Office Phone number

Nominated Number

Finance Contact Details: Preferred Contact Number, First Name, Middle Name, Last Name, ID Number, and Email Address (as provided on the change form).

Organization Contact Details – Contact Type (Finance Contact), Contact Names, ID Number, and Email Address (as provided on the change form)

f)     The Retail Team Leader/Manager shall approve the pending task in the Task List under the short code for the changes to take effect.

g)   Once approved, the CEE shall close the previous operator's ID to allow the new Nominated Number to opt in and access LNM services.

h)   The CEE shall guide the new Nominated Number to opt in via \*234\*2# OR \*234\*4# as per assigned product.

i)      The CEE shall save the KYC Documents provided by the merchant under safcentral retail folder, \\\\safcentral\\Retail LNM KYC.

**To use the naming format - Short Code –BusinessName, (as per M-PESA G3).**

j)      The CEE shall finally log an interaction on CRM accordingly.

k)    Where vetting or validation fails due to insufficient KYC documents, unreachable existing nominated number/finance contact, mismatched details, or any other discrepancy, the CEE shall not process the request. The CEE shall log an interaction on CRM and advise the merchant accordingly.

**Requests Received at the Franchise**

- Share the **Change of Organization Contact Form** and **KYC requirements** with the merchant.
- Review the submitted documents to make sure they are complete and accurate.
- Log an interaction on CRM and raise an **SR for LNM Support** to act on it within 24 hours.

**Requests Received by EBU Account Managers or Sales Teams**

- Ask the merchant to complete and sign the **Change of Organization Contact Form** and provide the necessary **KYC documents**.
- Send the request and documents via email to:

- lnmaggregators@safaricom.co.ke or
- lipanampesasupportteam1@Safaricom.co.ke

- LNM Support team will handle the request within 24 hours.

**Requests Received by the LNM Support Team**

- Pick up the SR or email activity and check the attached KYC documents.
- If the documents pass vetting:

- Update the office telephone number on M-PESA G2.
- Record the action in the SR comments.

- If the documents fail vetting:

- Inform the merchant why the request cannot be processed.
- Record the outcome in the SR comments.

**SRs will be raised to:**

- For **Buy Goods and Services**:

- SR Category: LNM BUY GOODS AND SERVICES
- SR Type: Change of KYC Details
- SR Item: Organization Contact

- For **Paybill**:

- SR Category: LNM PAYBILL
- SR Type: Change of KYC Details
- SR Item: Change of Organization Contact

# **Lipa na M-PESA Merchant Segmentation**

This is classification of merchants depending on KYC documentations the merchant has provided. This means depending on KYC documents provided we will have different trust levels for merchants. The different trust levels will have different merchant account balance and transaction limits.

Merchants trust level will determine their daily transaction limits and maximum balance of their merchant account.

# **KYC Update**

The addtional KYC documents can be submitted at any retail shop, scanned and sent via email to M-PESABusiness@Safaricom.co.ke or to lnmkycverification@Safaricom.co.ke or the documents can be sent to their respective safaricom account managers.

Retail center analysts, EBU care CEEs will be able to ammend KYC details on M-PESA G2 and upgrade trust level of the merchant.

# **ON USSD \*100#**

Customers will now be able to initiate **Lipa na M-PESA Reversal** via \*100#.

The objective is to grow USSD self-service adoption and improve customer experience by enabling customers to initiate **eligible** Lipa na M-PESA (**Buy Goods**) transaction reversals through self-service.

# **Key Highlights**

Only transactions sent to **Safaricom-owned tills** will be eligible for reversal.

Customers can dial \*100# and navigate to the Wrong Buy Goods Reversal option, then select the transaction they wish to reverse.

Customers will receive an SMS notification once a reversal request has been initiated.

After initiation, the reversal process will commence. The till owner will be contacted through an outbound call to provide consent before the reversal is completed.

Tills must be whitelisted to support the reversal process.

More tills will be whitelisted to scale the automation for Lipa na M-PESA reversal.

**NOTE:**

Bank-owned tills and aggregated tills are not eligible for reversal.

For Paybill reversals, the current process is still in place.

  Customers calling **100** can now interact directly with ZURI Voice Bot to initiate reversal requests seamlessly. This         enhancement is aimed at improving overall customer experience by reducing turnaround time and simplifying the     reversal process for Safaricom Owned tills.

Customer dial 100 (service currently available to Zuri Voice Bot whitelisted customers).

The customer requests a reversal by stating, for example: *“I want to reverse Lipa na M-PESA”* or *“Money sent to the wrong till.”*

The system prompts the customer to provide the transaction amount for the reversal request.

Reversal initiated and the till owner is contacted via an outbound call to facilitate completion of the reversal.

**STAWISHA BIASHARA Definition and Mechanics**

# **Definition**

**Stawisha Biashara** is a permanent M-PESA agent loyalty Program that awards agents points for transacting with customers which they can later redeem for cash rewards. The cash rewards are credited into the agent tills as float.

# **Benefits**

This is a points-based loyalty program for M-PESA Agents that seeks to:

- Reward and ringfence agents for their loyalty through the Stawisha loyalty program.
- Reward agents over and above the commissions that they receive.
- Create stickiness by retaining existing agents.
- Drive availability of float
- Grow transactions.

# **Loyalty program mechanics**

- Points will be awarded for on the qualifying transactions.
- Points will be awarded based on the value transacted. There is no rounding of points. Points are awarded including decimals.
- Points awarded for a transaction that is later reversed will be deducted from the total accumulated points. This applies to:
 - Deposits
 - Withdrawal by customer
 - Buy Airtime for customers.

# **Qualifying Transactions**

- Customer deposits
- Customer withdrawals
- Buy Airtime  

# **Awarding Mechanics**

**Points will be awarded as per the below matrix:**

- Customer deposit: 1 Point for every KES 200
- Buy airtime for the customer: 1 Point for every KES 500
- Customer withdrawal: 1 Point for every KES 500 transacted

**How to check Agents’ Stawisha details:**

 Below is the new link to access agents’ Stawisha details:

 [http://172.28.223.34/fileadminv2/apps\_by\_engineering/unlimited\_data/scripts/mpesa\_stawisha\_agents.php](http://172.28.223.34/fileadminv2/apps_by_engineering/unlimited_data/scripts/mpesa_stawisha_agents.php "http://172.28.223.34/fileadminv2/apps_by_engineering/unlimited_data/scripts/mpesa_stawisha_agents.php")

# **Float Redemption Matrix**

| Stawisha Pts | Reward |
| --- | --- |
| 250,000 | KES 10,000 |
| 200,000 | KES 8,000 |
| 150,000 | KES 6,000 |
| 75,000 | KES 3,000 |
| 25,000 | KES 1,000 |
| 12,500 | KES 500 |

# **Float redemption requirements**

- All redemptions will be initiated by the agent via USSD \*234# from the till and follow prompts.
- If an agent has enough points, the deduction of points will be done from their total accumulated points.
- The float Account of the agency store will be credited.
- The agent will receive two notifications on their Primary Till:

Notification 1 will inform the agent of the successful Stawisha Points redemption and the net balance after redemption.

Notification 2 will inform the agent of the Float credit into their agency store. 

Maximum allowable points an agent can accumulate is **400,000**. To be able to accumulate more, agents should redeem the points so that accumulation can continue. And points lost once one reaches the cap cannot be awarded in future.

# **Customer Support**

For support M-PESA Agents will call line 234, 100, free of charge for further queries.

**Introduction**

Scan to Pay is an M-PESA payment feature that uses QR codes to enable fast, easy, and secure payments. Customers simply use their phone camera to scan a merchant’s QR code and authorize the transaction using their M-PESA PIN. It is available at merchant outlets and for online shopping.

# **Benefits of Scan to Pay**

- **Faster checkout** – Reduces queues and speeds up transactions.
- **Reduced errors and reversals** – No manual entry of till or paybill numbers.
- **Zero payment errors** – Merchant details are auto-populated.
- **Seamless experience** – Works with any M-PESA-enabled smartphone.
- **Secure transactions** – PIN entry stays on your device.

# **Requirements**

- A camera-enabled smartphone
- An active Safaricom line registered on M-PESA
- Mobile data switched on

**Note:** Scan to Pay services are zero-rated, meaning they do not consume your data bundles, but mobile data must be enabled

# **Safety of Transactions**

- Scan to Pay enhances security by:
- Automatically detecting your phone number (no manual entry required)
- Auto-populating merchant details to prevent errors
- Requiring M-PESA PIN authentication to complete payments

# **How It Works**

QR codes can be scanned directly from your phone camera. There are two payment journeys depending on whether you have My OneApp installed:

# **Without My OneApp (Web Journey)**

- Open your phone camera
- Point it at the QR code
- Tap the link → opens secure M-PESA web checkout (pay.safaricom.co.ke)
- Confirm merchant details
- Enter amount
- Authorize payment using M-PESA PIN. **Requires Safaricom mobile data (will not work on Wi-Fi alone)**

# **With My OneApp (App Journey)**

- Open your phone camera
- Point it at the QR code
- Tap the link → automatically opens My OneApp
- Merchant details (till number) are pre-populated
- Enter amount and confirm
- Authorize payment using M-PESA PIN

**Works on Wi-Fi or mobile data**

# **Types of QR Codes**

- **Static QR Codes** – Populate merchant details; customer enters amount
- **Dynamic QR Codes** – Populate merchant details and amount automatically.

# **Usage Limits**

Standard M-PESA limits apply:

- KSh 250,000 per transaction
- KSh 500,000 daily limit

# **Where You Can Use Scan to Pay**

- Merchant outlets
- Online shopping platforms

# **What to Do If You’re Unable to Scan to Pay**

Check the following:

- Ensure **mobile data is switched on**
- If using web journey → **turn off Wi-Fi**
- Ensure you are on the **Safaricom network**
- Turn off any **VPN**
- On dual SIM phones:
- Set Safaricom as the primary line
- Enable mobile data on the Safaricom

**Additional Notes**

- Merchant details are automatically populated – no need to type till/paybill numbers
- Merchants do not require special hardware—only an M-PESA till or paybill and QR code
