articleTitle: Retail Centre/Care Desk SIM Swap Procedure
markdownContent:
**Individual Prepaid/Postpay SIM Swap requests**

Call the number provided by the customer to verify that the number is not in use by any other party before performing a SIM swap.

If the number is picked by another party, the agent will establish the real ownership of the line by vetting both the person online and the person presenting him/herself for a sim replacement and act as per the discussion.

If the number is not picked or off air, the agent will proceed with the request.

If a customer says they lost their phone, the CEE should ensure they wipe all the APPs on CRM and advise the customer to reinstall the apps on their phone after sim replacement.

**Roaming Check:** Check on HLR/SAWA if the number is roaming before doing any SIM swap.  If the VLR shows a number **NOT** starting with 254, then customer is roaming. In this case, refer to SIM swap for lost line while roaming line. 

**NOTE:** (While using **Single View** portal for swaps, use the roaming check contained in it.

The API was enhanced and same was not applied on HLR.)

**VLR ID is shown on HLR/SAWA as below**

 [Screenshot] 

 **NOTE:** This is a mandatory check before swapping **any** line.

The agent must raise an interaction for all SIM replacements done on Siebel and attach all communication/escalation, providing notes detailing all vetting parameters used for each line swapped through the systems. The outcome of the attempt to call the line to be swapped should also be detailed in the interaction.      

An interaction should also be raised in cases where the Agent does not complete the SIM swap process stating the reason why the SIM replacement was not done.   

**Customer presents original ID**

**Primary vetting**

Original and valid ID as per acceptable KYC. Vetting is by validation of ID details vs registration details on the system.

Mandatory requirement of 2 M-PESA self-initiated transactions **OR** 2 FDNS.

Where line has not been in use on M-PESA, or calls use a combination of any 3 parameters below to vet customer.

**Secondary vetting**

**Account balances**, either M-PESA or Airtime or data bundle balance.

**Account limits** either KCB – MPESA, or M-Shwari, Fuliza or Storo bonus.

**PIN / PUK certificate**.

**Service Interaction**: Type and date of previous successful escalation / request on the line (e.g., SIM swap, over scratched, unbarring line)

**Bundle plan.**

**Customer has lost ID**

**Primary vetting**

Original waiting card (New version) (Issued within 2 months), clear copy of valid ID document (Optional) and police abstract (Issued within 3 months). Vetting is by validation of ID details vs registration details on the system.

**OR**

Original waiting card (Old version), clear copy of valid ID document (Mandatory) and police abstract (Issued within 3 months). Vetting is by validation of ID details vs registration details on the system.

**Mandatory** requirement of 3 M-PESA self-initiated transactions or 3 FDNS

Where line has not been in use on M-PESA, or calls use a combination of any 3 parameters below to vet customer.

**Secondary vetting**

- **Account balances**: either M-PESA or Airtime or data bundle balance.
- **Account limits** either KCB – MPESA, or M-Shwari, Fuliza or Storo bonus.
- **PIN / PUK** certificate.
- **Service Interaction**: Type and date of previous successful escalation / request on the line (e.g., SIM swap, over scratched, unbarring line)
- **Bundle plan**.

**Lost Military ID**

Where a military customer has lost his/her military ID, he/she should present the following documents for them to be served:

- Introduction letter from his/her Unit duly signed and stamped
- Valid military ID in lieu Card (Temporary military ID)

In case of any further queries/verification:

Agent will scan the card and emails it to Zachary Mburu ([ZMBURU@Safaricom.co.ke](mailto:ZMBURU@Safaricom.co.ke)) for verification, copying Martin Nyaga.

Agent calls Zachary to expedite the verification.

Verification process takes up to 15 minutes.

Inform the customer that details have been sent for verification and ask for their patience.

**SIM swap for Foreigner who has lost their passport**

The customer will present the following documents for assistance:

- Police abstract
- Copy of the lost passport
- Letter/document from the respective embassy. (Valid for 3 months)

The letter/document should state the name, their passport number and confirmation that their citizen has informed them of the lost passport and they’re in the process of renewal.

**SIM swap request – SIM Upgrade**

Where line is active and availed at the time of swap, apply Primary Vetting (**Mandatory -** Original Document of Registration, 2FDNS or 2 M-PESA Self-initiated Transactions).

Secondary vetting is **Not** **Mandatory** and will only be applied on need basis for validation.

Vetting is by validation of ID details vs registration details on the system, confirm line is available and active at the retail outlet.

**Secondary vetting Using any 3 parameters as below**

**Account balances**, either M-PESA or Airtime or data bundle balance.

**Account limits** either KCB – MPESA, or M-Shwari, Fuliza or Storo bonus.

**PIN / PUK** certificate.

**Service Interaction**: Type and date of previous successful escalation / request on the line (e.g., SIM swap, over scratched, unbarring line)

**Bundle plan**.

**Effecting the SIM Swap**

After vetting, if customer is registered and passes the vetting, the agent can do the replacement on Siebel/CRM

**Replacement via CRM**

Open Siebel and enter customers MSISDN.

Under Subscriber Portal, click "Modify" then "Customize”.

Select the tab "MSISDN & SIM Card”.

Enter the SIM serial under the tab "Sim Number”.

Click "Done" and submit the order.

An automated SMS shall be sent to the Customer to educate them on how to re-activate the M-PESA account.

Ensure to capture the vetting details on Siebel Interactions.

**Note:**

If the customer is not registered, the agent will vet using both the 1st and 2nd level vetting as per vetting process and CEE will register the customer on the system.

If registered on M-PESA, the CEE will assist the customer to re-activate M-PESA account.

After successfully swapping the line, kindly wipe all the apps for the customer to reinstall them afresh.

 **Individual Prepaid SIM swaps**  

The procedure is initiated by the customer and begins when s/he visits the retail centre, or requests via mail for approved scenarios.

A SIM card replacement can be requested in different scenarios i.e. when lost/stolen, damaged or when an upgrade is needed by the customer.   

The agent will vet the customer as per the Retail Vetting Procedure.    

The agent needs to verify the vetting details in the system i.e. full names and document ID.    

After vetting, if customer passes the vetting, the agent can do the replacement on the system.

**NOTE:** 

After successfully swapping the line, kindly wipe all the apps for the customer to reinstall them afresh.

**SIM Swap Requests for Companies**

**Line registered under the company, with personal M-PESA account****​** **(Prepay and Postpaid)**

For an individual line that is under the name of a company, no letter will be needed. However, M-PESA MUST be registered under the individual’s details. 

**Effecting the SIM Swap**

i.         Customer will present their original registration document

ii.         They will be vetted as per the SIM swap vetting procedures on CRM (View 360), M-PESA & Subreg

iii.         CEE will proceed to swap the line

**NOTE**: If customer requires any further action e.g. line to be unbarred or reconnected for payment, they will be advised to present the above documents from the company.

**SIM Swap Requests for Companies (Prepay and Postpaid) -**

**Company Registered line**

**Requirement details**

1.    Request must be on the company original letter head.

2.    Must state that the bearer has been authorized to do a SIM replacement on behalf of the company, indicating in the letter their full name, and ID number.

3.    CEE must contact the company contact person to verify approval for swap has been given.

4.    Party sent must have original ID and have it scanned and attached on Siebel.

5.    Preferably have the letter stamped using the company rubber stamp. In exceptional cases where company claims to have no stamp, CEE will verify from previous correspondence / account managers and company contact person.

6.    Must be signed by the company contact person.

7.    The agent must call the number to be swapped to verify before doing the replacement. Once correct vetting is done satisfactorily, System Replacement will follow.

**Effecting the SIM Swap**

1.    After confirming the customer has met all requirements above, the agent can do the replacement on Siebel/CRM).

2.    The Agent should attach a scanned copy of all the above documents on Siebel including all the vetting details in the notes before submitting.

3.    These letters should be stamped with the Retail Shop rubber stamp showing the current date, the order number, Service Interaction or Service Request number indicated clearly on the letter. This should then be filed by the staff performing the replacement.

 **Dealer OTA and E-TOP UP SIM Swap**

The dealer will contact the Dealer Management Team or Line 300 who will send an email to the Dealer Management Team to bar / replace the lost line.

Where the dealer visits a retail store requesting for line to be barred, CEE will bar the line and send an email to dealer management team / Line 300 on the same and attaches ID of person requesting for the same and log an interaction indication action taken.

Where a dealer visits any Safaricom Retail outlet for a replacement, customer will provide the following documents for a SIM replacement: -

SIM Kit (Where available)

Letter from dealer HQ requesting for a replacement and stating the full names and ID number of the person to pick up the SIM. The letter should be signed by one of the directors, stamped and the person going for the swap should present their original ID for the swap to be done.

Agent should call the Contact person to confirm the request and call the number to be swapped to verify ownership.

**Effecting the SIM Swap**

The CEE will vet and verify documents presented.

Where the customer meets the vetting requirements, the CEE will liaise with the team leader / manager to verify ownership on the E-top up system (Bamba Poa)

CEE will proceed with the swap once confirmation of ownership is done.

If the dealer has the required documents the CEE completes the swap with an E-TOP UP SIMEX and issues the Dealer with a new E-top up line and unbar the line.

If the bearer does not meet the vetting requirements, the agent should advise the dealer on the additional requirements and raise an interaction on the number stating the reason for not proceeding with the swap.

Where a dealer’s line is recycled, CEE will advise the dealer to contact their dealer manager for resolution.

**Safaricom Owned Lines**

Where shop staff request for a sim swap for shop lines i.e. test Sim cards, data lines, shop tills etc. For their store, CEE will get a written approval from the shop manager, in their absence the store team leader will approve the same via email and the same attached on Siebel.

In case where the line is registered under their names as primary contact or registered on Siebel as the customer on account level CEE will request for ID / staff badge and is required to call the number provided by the staff to verify that the number is not in use by any other party before performing a SIM swap.

If vetting is successful CEE will proceed to swap.

Where swap requested is presented for Safaricom owned lines for other departments, CEE will seek written approval from the departments Administrator / Personal Assistant to the departments HOD. The email will be attached on Siebel and swap effected.

**SIM SWAP FOR A LOST LINE WHILE ROAMING**

If inquiring for a roaming customer, advise them to ask the customer who is roaming to make a written request to

         [customercare@Safaricom.co.ke](mailto:customercare@Safaricom.co.ke) or [advantage@safaricom.co.ke](mailto:advantage@safaricom.co.ke)

If a customer physically comes to retail claiming they lost SIM card while they were roaming and VLR ID still shows foreign number **NOT** 254, customer shall present the following documents:

Passport showing the entry & exit stamps with bio page

Where passport is lost, present a temporary travel document with the entry stamp

Original ID, and where ID is lost, present copy of ID, an abstract and waiting card

**Where any of the above is not available (Passport/temporary travel document), the Manager/ TL will apply secondary vetting, this will include validating the details customer has provided against what is captured on Subreg IMAGE portal which they have access to.  The Manager/TL will then capture the same on interaction.**

**Vetting details** 

**Primary**

Two (2) frequently dialed numbers **(while line was on roaming)**. Each number should be recorded as a mobile originating (MO) and must appear in the last three months. (**Mandatory** if line has been in use)

Either 3 of these M-PESA details:

o   2 self-initiated transactions (while roaming)

o   M-PESA balance

o   FSI limits i.e., M-Shwari, Fuliza, KCB MPESA

Check the network customer was roaming on HLR.

**Secondary**

Service Interaction, type, and date of previous successful escalation request on the line (e.g., SIM swap, bill amount/bill payment, unbarring line)

Airtime balance or data bundle balance or Bundle plan or account limits i.e., Storo bonus.

PIN / PUK Certificate.

Postal / Email Address or / and credit limit – Applicable to postpaid customer only.

 **NOTE:**

In adherence to our Data Privacy Policy, third party SIM swaps or where customer is accompanied by another individual are not allowed. All requests for SIM swaps must be made by the account holder/user in person and they should not be intimidated to swap against their will.

**Related articles;**

[SIM Swap for Roaming](../app/article/e82f2b9b-a4ee-42b2-9f73-a984de3c4606) 

[E-SIM Guide](../app/article/8fc01f8c-e882-4bef-9009-aa7dc103f6c9)

**SPLIT NOTIFICATIONS – FAQS** 

**1\.** **What is Split Notifications?** It is a feature that will allow merchants to add staff numbers to receive limited transaction alerts for a Till or Paybill. Its main aim is to help frontline staff confirm payments instantly, improving service speed and customer experience.

**2\. Which channels support it?**

•               USSD (\*234#) – deployed

•               Merchant Business Hub (MBH)- coming soon

•               M-PESA Business App – coming soon

**How the Feature Works**

1. **Nominated Number Adds a Staff Recipient**

Using USSD \*234\*2# for business tills and \*234\*4# for paybills (and soon M-Pesa Business Hub + the M‑PESA Business App), the merchant will:

- Select **Split Notifications**
- Choose **Add Recipient**
- Enter the staff phone number then submit.
- Await the staff’s acceptance to complete setup

NB: Only the Primary Operator Number (Nominated number) can perform this action.

     **2. Staff Consent is Required**

The nominated staff member receives:

- An SMS with a **unique consent code**
- Instructions to dial **USSD code \*234\*12#** to accept

Once they approve and accept the terms, the configuration becomes active. From that moment, they begin receiving limited transaction confirmations (via *Jumbe*). No balances or sensitive data are shared.

**3\. Managing Recipients**

Admins can:

- Add multiple staff recipients
- View recipient status (Pending, Active, Removed)
- Remove any staff at any time
- Remove all recipients if needed

Changes take effect immediately.

**Notification Alert;**

- **Primary Operator** → Receives full MPESA notifications from MPESA.
- **Staff Recipients** → Receive limited notifications from **Jumbe.**

This distinction ensures security while enabling operational transparency.

**For Merchants (Admins)** 

**4\. Who can activate the feature?** Only the Primary Operator Nominated Number linked to the Till or Paybill.

**5\. Do I need to accept Terms & Conditions?** Yes. Acceptance is required before first-time activation. You may need to re-accept if the Terms are updated.

**6\. How do I add a recipient?** Via USSD, MBH, or the M-PESA Business App, enter the recipient’s name and phone number, authenticate, and submit. The recipient must accept/agree before activation.

**7\. Does the staff member need to approve?** Yes. They must accept via USSD using an acceptance code sent by SMS.

**8\. What happens if they don’t accept/agree?** They will not receive any notifications.

**9\. What information will staff see?** Limited transaction confirmation only. They will NOT see balances, settlement details, or full financial information.

**10\. Will I still receive full notifications?** Yes. The Primary Number continues to receive full transaction notifications from MPESA.

**11\. From which sender ID will notifications come?**

•               The Primary Number receives notifications from **MPESA**.

•               Staff Recipients receive limited notifications from **Jumbe**.

**12\. Is there a limit to the number of recipients I can add?** Currently, there is no set limit to the number of recipients you may add, subject to future system or policy updates.

**13\. Can I add non-Safaricom network numbers?** No. At this time, notifications can only be sent to Safaricom numbers. Other networks (e.g., Airtel) are not supported.

**14\. Can I remove a recipient?** Yes. You can remove any recipient at any time. Notifications stop immediately upon removal.

**15\. What if I enter the wrong number?** The recipient number must accept/agree before activation. Please ensure you have entered the correct number before submitting the request.

**For Staff Recipients** 

**16\. Why did I receive a Code acceptance message?** A merchant nominated your number to receive limited transaction alerts.

**17\. What do I need to do?** Dial the provided USSD code, enter the shortcode and acceptance code, and accept.

**18\. What information will I receive?** Limited transaction confirmation via SMS from Jumbe. No balances or full account details.

**19\. Can I decline?** Yes. If you decline, you will not receive notifications.

**Security & Technical** 

**20\. Is the feature secure?** Yes. It requires merchant authentication and explicit recipient acceptance/Agreement.

**21\. Does this change how payments are processed?** No. It only changes who receives transaction alerts.

**22\. Are Acceptance/Opt In/Agreements records stored?** Yes. All acceptances/Agreement/Opt in Records are logged for audit and compliance purposes.

# **DEFINITION**

Chat Ibambe (SMS Upsell Proposition) is an SMS version of Storo Bonus targeting our low SMS users and non-users by exciting them with a good SMS deal thus driving usage as well as growing ARPU. Enabling them to SMS more for less.

# **BUSINESS RULES**

1. Each customer will have a target to spend on SMS which will then guarantee him FREE/bonus SMS **valid till midnight** if they achieve the spending target.
2. Eligible Customers will be able to check their **T****arget**, **Daily Spending** and **Bonus Award** via \*188#>>Chat Ibambe.
3. Target will be based on customer daily average SMS spend).
4. Customers can spend on Out of Bundle SMS (sending SMS via airtime) or buy an SMS bundle to achieve their daily target.
5. 1st  Out of Bundle (OOB) charged SMS event of the day, and the customer hasn’t achieved target yet will trigger a notification to the customer, to send X more SMS that day and receive awards.
6. Awarded bonus SMS will be put in a new SMS account available on CRM IN DATA balance views as **‘Sherekea SMS** **Bonus’**
7. Customers will receive threshold notifications on their spending progress throughout the day.
8. Only utilization from main account will contribute towards spend and get.
9. Customer can check their SMS bonus balance via \*188# or SMS to 144.

# **OPT OUT**

Eligible customers will be able to opt-out via \*188# >> Chat Ibambe.

# **SMS TARGET DISTRIBUTION**

SMS target distribution will be as below:

| Daily SMS Spend | Target Spend | Award SMS | Validity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Non-users & inconsistent users | 2 /= | 30 | Midnight |
| 1 – 3 | 5/= (OOB or SMS Bundle purchase) | 100 | Midnight |
| 4- 7 | 10/= (OOB or SMS Bundle purchase) | 500 | Midnight |

# **CURRENT PROMOTION**

We are currently running a *‘Spend & Get’* proposition on whitelisted customers with zero ARPU.

When these customers send their first chargeable SMS of the day, they will receive 100 free SMS valid till midnight which introduces a paid entry point.

**BA INCENTIVES** **ELIGIBILITY**

The following categories qualify for BA registration incentives:

- Sales Support Officers (SSOs)
- M-PESA Agents
- Brand Ambassadors (BAs)

# **INCENTIVE PAYMENT CRITERIA**

The incentive paid for a successful registration is based on the customer's initial top-up value.

- Incentive payments range between KES 20 and KES 100 per qualifying registration.
- The payment amount is determined by the value of the customer's top-up after registration.
- The top-up is converted into bundles, which may include:

- Voice bundles, or
- Data bundles

- The corresponding incentive is then awarded based on the qualifying bundle value.

# **SANCTIONS AND DISQUALIFICATION CRITERIA**

To maintain the integrity of the registration process, the following violations will result in sanctions:

- Multiple registrations using the same customer details.
- Irregular or fraudulent registrations.
- Registrations conducted using an ID found on a mobile phone instead of the original document.
- Use of altered or tampered identification documents.
- Use of photocopies of identification documents instead of original IDs.

# **PENALTY**

- Any BA, SSO, or M-PESA Agent found engaging in the above malpractices will be **blacklisted for six (6) months** and will not be eligible for incentive payments during this period.

# **ESCALATION PROCESS FOR INCENTIVE QUERIES**

For cases where incentives have not been awarded and require investigation:

# **First-Line Support:**

- Raise a Service Request (SR) under:

- Sub Reg App > Incentives
- Calling line 100 with their personal numbers
- The agent/BA reaching out to the **TBL** (Territory Business Lead) or the **TDR** (Trade Development Representative)

# **Second-Line Support Escalation:**

If the issue remains unresolved after the Service Request process, the Second-Line Team should escalate the matter to: [dealerManagement2@safaricom.co.ke](mailto:dealerManagement2@safaricom.co.ke)

Please ensure that all relevant details are included in the escalation, including:

the MSISDN designated to receive the incentives,

the BA's ID number,

agent details, and

the specific period during which the BA did not receive the incentives. 

Providing complete information will help facilitate timely investigation and resolution.

articleTitle: KCB M-PESA DIY Procedure for Loan request / Repayment Mechanics & Loan Balance and Loan Limit Checks on IVR 100
markdownContent:
**DEFINITION**

The KCB M-PESA loan account is a micro-credit product which gives a customer access to loan.

**LOAN ELIGIBILITY**

Be an M-PESA subscriber for 6 months.

Save on KCB M-PESA.

Actively use other Safaricom services such as voice, data and M-PESA

Be cleared by other credit facilities in case of an acquired loan.

**MECHANICS**

Loan Request

Access the M-PESA menu.

Select Loans and Savings.

Select KCB M-PESA.

Select Loan.

Request Loan.

Enter amount.

Enter your M-PESA PIN

Loan amount will be sent to your KCB-M-PESA Account. The loan amount to be paid will be inclusive of the 8.88% interest rate and is paid within a month.

**NB:** The customer will receive confirmation message from both KCB M-PESA and M-PESA.

To access the funds, the customer needs to withdraw the cash from KCB M-PESA to M-PESA account.

**Loan limit**

A customer can access loan limits from as low as Ksh.100 and up to Ksh.250,000 and enjoy repayment period of one month.

**NB:** Customers who are not more than 6months old on M-PESA, will be assigned a KCB M-PESA loan limit of zero.

**Growing Loan limit**

Increase activity on your KCB M-PESA Account by moving money in and out of your Account.

Increase savings on your KCB M-PESA Account.

Increase usage of M-PESA services.

**Loan repayment**

The loan can be paid in full or in instalments from either KCB M-PESA account or M-PESA.

This can be done on the M-PESA tool kit/SafaricomApp or on USSD: \*334# then:

Loans and savings

Loan

Pay loan

**Loan repayment for Self**

Access the M-PESA menu.

Select Loans and Savings.

Select KCB M-PESA.

Select Loan.

Pay Loan.

Select payment from either KCB M-PESA account or M-PESA

Enter amount.

Enter your M-PESA PIN

Send

**Third party Loan repayment**

The customer can also pay KCB M-PESA loan using Paybill number **522559** for self (in case of written off loans) ,3rd party or pooled lines.

The procedure is as follows:

Select M-PESA

Select Lipa na M-PESA

Select Paybill

Enter Paybill Number: **522559**

Account No- Enter ‘’Borrower’s ID number e.g., 12345678’’

Enter amount

Enter M-PESA PIN

Send

**NB:** Loan repayment notification will be sent to both parties in case of a third-party loan repayment.

# **IVR SELF- SERVICES FOR LOAN BALANCE AND LOAN LIMIT REQUESTS**

Customers will now be able to check KCB M-PESA loan limit and balances on IVR100. 

✅ KCB M-PESA Loan Balance.

# **HOW TO OPT IN/ACTIVATE M-SHWARI**

# **First Update the M-PESA menu as** **follows**

- Go to the Safaricom Menu.
- Select M-PESA.
- Select my account.
- Select Update customer Menu and enter your M-PESA pin.

**The Menu will be updated, and customer advised via text, after which****,** **below procedure will be used to activate the M-Shwari account/opt in.**

**Go to the Safaricom menu** **on Sim Tool Kit/(STK).**

- Select M-PESA then M-Shwari.
- Select Activate or Wezesha.
- Then new M-PESA menu with M-Shwari menu will be sent to your phone. Select the M-Shwari link.
- A message will appear requesting you to read and accept the Terms & Conditions**:**

**English****: Visit:** [**www.NCBAgroup.com/m**](http://www.cbagroup.com/m)**shwari** [**www.safaricom.co.ke**](http://www.safaricom.co.ke/)**.**

- After accepting the terms, an SMS will be sent informing you that you are now activated on the M-Shwari service.

# **HOW TO DEPOSIT AND WITHDRAW FROM AN M-SHWARI ACCOUNT**

**For** **Deposit****:**

- Go to **M-PESA** menu.
- Select **Loans and Savings.**
- Select M-Shwari
- Select ***Send to M-Shwari’***
- Enter the amount you want to send.
- Enter M-PESA PIN
- Confirm the message displayed “send money to M-shwari account Kshs.2000” then press OK.

**Sample message:** Confirmed. Kshs. XXXX transferred to M-Shwari account on DD/MM/YY at 00.00pm. M-PESA Balance is Kshs. XXXX; new M-Shwari account balance is Kshs. XXXX.

**For** **Withdraw****:**

- Go to M-PESA Menu
- Select Loans and Savings
- Select M-Shwari
- Select Withdraw from M-Shwari
- Enter the amount you want to withdraw
- Enter M-PESA PIN
- Confirm the message displayed

# **HOW TO OPEN AND CHECK BALANCE ON M-SHWARI LOCK SAVINGS ACCOUNT**

**To open an account.**

- Go to M-PESA Menu.
- Loans and savings, and then M-SHWARI.
- Select Lock savings Account, Select OPEN Account.
- Select Deposit from M-PESA or M-SHWARI

- Enter amount to transfer.
- Open Lock Savings of Kshs. \*\*\* for the selected period and deposit KSH\*\*\*
 - Yes

***SMS message received:******(*** ***Dear customer, your request to open Lock Savings account received and will be processed shortly*****)****.**

**HOW TO CHECK M-SHWARI LOCK ACCOUNT BALANCE**

To check the M-Shwari Lock Balance.

- Go to M-PESA menu.
- Loans and savings, select M-SHWARI
- Select Lock Saving Account
- Select Check Balance
- Enter your M-PESA PIN to confirm.
- The customer will receive a text showing the lock account balance and the maturity date.

# **HOW TO DEPOSIT AND WITHDRAW MONEY FROM THE LOCK SAVINGS ACCOUNT**

**For** **Deposit****:**

For you to save money into your lock savings account you need to:

- Go to M-PESA, Loans and savings, and then M-SHWARI.
- Select lock savings account
- Select Top up Lock Savings Account- confirm from M-PESA or M-SHWARI
- Please enter the Top Up amount to your Lock Savings Account
- E.g. do you want to transfer Kshs. \*\*\* to lock saving account.

- Yes
- No

***SMS Message: You have transferred Kshs. 500 from your M-Shwari account to your Lock Savings account. M-Shwari balance is Kshs. Xxxxxx.xx. Your Lock savings balance is Kshs. Xxxx.***

**Withdraw****:**

- A customer can withdraw from Lock Account before maturity date, but that will take **48hrs**/2 days for funds to be available.
- Before the 2 days elapse, the customer balance notification will reflect a balance which is less the withdrawn amount.

- Confirm with your M-PESA PIN

# **HOW TO GET M-SHWARI LOCK MINI STATEMENT**

To request for the M-Shwari Lock Mini- Statement follow the procedure below.

# **HOW TO REQUEST FOR AND REPAY AN M-SHWARI LOAN**

**Loan request**

articleTitle: Okoa Lipa Mdogo Mdogo Definition, Eligibility and Mechanics
markdownContent:
# **DEFINITION**

This is a service that enables eligible Prepay subscribers to repay their outstanding Okoa Jahazi or Okoa Internet Credit Advance in instalments.

# **ELIGIBILITY**

- The service is open to **select whitelisted** Safaricom Prepay subscribers who are on Okoa.
- Customers cannot opt in to the Okoa Lipa Mdogo Mdogo service.
- Line must have been active and in use.
- Age on Network is capped at 14 days. On the 15th day the customers will be able to access Okoa.

# **MECHANICS**

- A customer gets to know the limit per week by dialing \*131# and the customer will view a list of denominations they can access.
- The highest denomination denotes the highest amount the customer qualifies for within each week.
- Each loan has a 5-day maturity period, if unpaid by day 6 then the customer will be blacklisted from Okoa Jahazi
- 50% of customer’s airtime top-up will be deducted when a customer tops up with an amount equivalent or less than their **ETU** balance.
- If a customer tops up with Ksh.1 more/above the total amount owed, the entire amount will be deducted to clear the outstanding balance.
- After repaying the loan, a notification will be sent with the outstanding balance.
- The balance of the instalment must be fully repaid within five (5) days failure to which the full outstanding credit advance will be deducted from the next top up.
- Every top up via all channels (MPESA, voucher, 3rd party, pin less) will go towards settling any outstanding okoa debts
- The customer gets notified before maturity date through SMS
- If the customer has not repaid after the 5 days, the free money remaining will be used to offset the balance. Thereafter any top will be used to repay the full amount.

articleTitle: Customer Support for P2P Reversals – Call Center
markdownContent:
**Reversal Management at Call Centre**

**Self Service Options**

**P2P Reversal Process**

Customer can request for a reversal by

·       **DIY** - Forwarding the M-PESA message to 456

·       Contacting the call centre through the available channels

·       Through the Safaricom APP

·       Sending the Transaction ID to ZURI

·       Visiting the RC for assistance

**P2P Reversals**

**Reasons for reversals**

·       Funds sent to a wrong number

·       Wrong amount sent

·       Recipient number not in use

·       Duplicated transaction

**Reasons for a failed reversal**

·       Funds utilized

·       M-PESA account is suspended/frozen.

·       Recipient has disputed the reversal

·       Maximum limit for the sender reached for the day. 

·       System Failures.

 **Sender calling**

·       CEE will query the customer number on M-PESA G3.

·       Confirm ownership of the line using the Customer Name as per M-PESA system. The CEE can accept if the customer gives 2 correct names.

·       Confirm the transaction to be reversed.

·       Confirm the transaction has been done within the last **30 days**. For all transactions older than **30 days** the CEE will advise the customer to liaise with recipient or police to resolve any dispute.

·       CEE will initiate the reversal and advise on the completion SLA.

·       Where part of the funds is used by the recipient, the CEE will do partial reversal of the available funds and advise the customer accordingly. This can only be done once.

**Recipient Calling:**

·       CEE will query the customer number on M-PESA G3.

·       Confirm ownership of the line using the Customer Name as per M-PESA system. The CEE can accept if the customer gives 2 correct names.

·       Confirm the transaction to be reversed.

·       Confirm the transaction has been done within the last 30 days. For all transactions older than 30 days the CEE will advise the customer to liaise with recipient or police to resolve any dispute.

·       CEE will thank the recipient for their honesty, initiate the reversal on G3 and advise on the completion SLA.

**NOTE:** 

o Capture interaction on third party number of the MSISDN that needs reversal. 
o On the second interaction (of the owner), also indicate the mobile number of the third party.

**3rd Party Calling**

·       CEE will query the customer number on M-PESA G3.

·       Confirm sender’s name as per M-PESA system. The CEE can accept if the customer gives 2 correct names.

·       Confirm the transaction to be reversed.

·       Confirm the transaction has been done within the last **30 days**. For all transactions older than **30 days** the CEE will advise the customer to liaise with recipient or police to resolve any dispute.

·       CEE will initiate the reversal and advise on the completion SLA. 

·       Where part of the funds is used by the recipient, the CEE will do partial reversal of the available funds and advise the customer accordingly. This can only be done once.

**NOTE**

·       After initiating the reversal, CEE will educate the customer on Hakikisha.   

     **The SLA for all P2P reversals is 2hrs. For reversals initiated from 6PM, the 2hrs SLA runs from 9 AM the next day.**

·       If the reversal was initiated before and cancelled due to a dispute**, DO NOT reinitiate it**, advise the sender as per notes and to follow up with recipient or police.

·       Where funds have been utilized, **CEE shall NOT disclose to Party A how party B has utilized the funds received.**

·       Do **NOT suspend** or **add a state tag** on customers account due to insufficient funds but advise the customer to follow up with the recipient or report to the police for assistance.

·       **M-PESA account is suspended/frozen,** unsuspend, initiate the reversal, return the suspension except for **fraud tag reasons** and civil cases where we **don’t** touch the funds. 

·       For all state tag blocked lines, if a customer calls for reversal, the CEEs will be required to; **Refer Customer to Retail for reversal.**  as per article [**ALGJ-0002**](../../app/article/e96fc051-c9c6-4944-bc07-d6bac671f9be)**\-** Fraud State Tag

**P2P Reversals Past SLA**

**Sender Calling**

Request the customer to be patient and assure them customer that we are making every effort to reach the wrong recipient to give consent for the reversal to be actioned.

An M-PESA SMS notification will be sent as soon as the reversal is finalized.

**Recipient Calling**

Request the customer to send the transaction message to 456 for immediate action. If 24hrs have elapsed from when they did the transaction, advise them to remain patient and await a call from 0722000000. **DO NOT COMPLETE THE REVERSAL.** 

**Disputed P2P Reversals**

**Recipient Calling to Dispute a pending authorized reversal**

If the recipient contacts us to dispute a pending authorized reversal and requests its cancellation, advise them to remain patient and await a call from 0722000000.

The Reversals team will handle the dispute. 

**Recipient Calling to Dispute A Completed Reversal**

·       Where the recipient is calling about a completed reversal, check notes captured by the reversal admin during completion and advise the recipient appropriately.

·       Where they do not agree advise them for follow up with sender or police.

**Recipient Calling About A Pending Authorized Reversal**

If the recipient calls and is in agreement with the reversal, advise customer to forward M-PESA mesage to 456 for immediate completion. **DO NOT COMPLETE THE REVERSAL.** 

 **Sender Calling About A Pending Authorized Reversal**

**Sender Calling**

Request the customer to be patient and assure them customer that we are making every effort to reach the wrong recipient to give consent for the reversal to be actioned.

An M-PESA SMS notification will be sent as soon as the reversal is finalized.

**Recipient Calling**

Request the customer to send the transaction message to 456 for immediate action. If 24hrs have elapsed from when they did the transaction, advise them to remain patient and await a call from 0722000000. **DO NOT COMPLETE THE REVERSAL.** 

**Sender Calling to Dispute a Cancelled Reversal**

·       Check notes captured during cancellation and advised appropriately. Where they do not agree, advise them to follow up with recipient or police.

·       For a 456 initiated reversal, advise customer to follow-up with the recipient as they are the ones that cancelled the transaction.

 **NOTE:**

**Capturing notes on reversals:** There are instances where notes are indicated as **“wr”** which is not clear. Kindly indicate clear notes for all reversals. e.g., customer made a duplicate payment, wrong number, wrong amount. Where it is wrong number or amount, kindly indicate the correct one as well  ***(where the number is available)***

**Partial reversals:** Where a customer says that they paid more than they ought to have paid/sent, kindly initiate a **partial reversal** of the correct amount i.e. subtract the correct amount from the total amount and then initiate a partial reversal of the difference, e.g. If they paid 7000 instead of 700, initiate a partial reversal of Ksh 6300.

# **Definition**

# **Definition**

This is a service that allows Safaricom customers to purchase data bundles directly within the YouTube app when their data is running low or depleted.

The service is automatically triggered when your **data is low** or **depleted** **while using YouTube****.**

The service was launched on 10th June 2026.

# **Eligibility**

The service is available to:

- Safaricom Prepay customers
- Individual PostPay customers
- Customers using the YouTube app on mobile phones.

You must have the YouTube app installed and be using Safaricom mobile data

# **How it Works**

- You receive in-app notifications when your data is almost depleted
- Once your data runs out, a pop-up appears in YouTube with bundle offers
- You can purchase data instantly within the app and continue browsing

# **Opt In/Out**

This is not an Opt-in service and hence no opt-out, however customers can:

- Ignore or decline any offers presented.
- Exit the purchase flow at any time
- Use alternative channels (\*544# or mySafaricom App) to buy data

**To** **avoid seeing up****\-****sell prompts****:**

- Ensure you have an active data bundle before using YouTube.
- Avoid browsing YouTube when your data is fully depleted

# **Free YouTube data**

Eligible customers may receive **free YouTube data** when their bundle is depleted.

The free data to be received will be a small allocation (e.g., ~30MB) to continue browsing and enable bundle purchase.

To qualify for the free data, you must:

- Have less than 5MB data balance
- Have less than KES 5 airtime balance
- Have topped up or purchased a bundle since your last free allocation.

**NOTE:**

Free data can be received only once per day (Multiple allocations in one day are not allowed, even if conditions are met).

The free data is strictly for YouTube usage only (will not be usable on other apps or for browsing).

The free data will not be explicitly advertised as “free”

# **After Exhausting the Free YouTube data**

If you continue browsing without purchasing a bundle, you will be charged out-of-bundle rates of KES 4.87 per MB

# **Available YouTube data**

Customers may see:

- Different Personalized offers based on your usage & designed to provide relevant & affordable options.
- Other data bundles available from Safaricom.

# **YouTube Offers Benefits**

- Seamless viewing with minimal interruption
- Quick and convenient in-app data purchase
- Access to personalized bundle offers
- Improved overall streaming experience. 

Interactions and SRs will be logged  under: **YouTube Upsell**

**Taasi Pochi Loan**

# **Definition**

It is a loan product offered to Pochi la Biashara merchants where they are able to access a credit facility between Ksh 1,000 to 150,000 through our partner Pezesha and Sidian Bank.

# **Customers who opted to Pezesha will have the following loan duration periods:**

 3.85% for a period of 7 days

4.71% for a period of 14 days

6.41% for a period of 30 days

# **Customers who opted to Sidian bank will have the following loan duration periods:**

 3.85% for a period of 7 days

4.71% for a period of 14 days

5.55% for a period of 21 days

6.41% for a period of 30 days

# **Benefits of Taasi Pochi Loan**

Pochi la Biashara merchants will be able to access credit for:

- Business expansion, including buying business assets.
- Stock and inventory financing.
- General funds for business operations.

**Eligibility**

- Pochi la Biashara merchants who are at least 6 months old.
- Merchants who are actively transacting on their Pochi wallet.

# **Registration/Opt In for merchant Term Loan Services**

Merchant will dial \*334\*8#, select Pochi la Biashara, go to Taasi Pochi Loans to accept Terms and Conditions and opt in. Using the My OneApp go to My finances and select Taasi Pochi.

# **Loan Approval Criteria**

A loan is approved or rejected based on:

- You must have been actively using the Pochi wallet for at least 6 months.
- Your Pochi wallet business activity: That is, how often and how much you use the Pochi wallet to receive M-PESA payments from customers.
- Your current credit listing status (rating and score) at the Credit Reference Bureau:
- It is important that you always maintain a good credit history and credit score.
- Your loan repayment behavior plays a crucial role in determining your eligibility for future loans. When you repay your loan in full and on time, it reflects positively on your creditworthiness. This, in turn, strengthens your financial profile and increases the likelihood of approval for future loans.

#  **Taasi Pochi Business Loan application process**

Once you have successfully registered/opted into the M-PESA Taasi Pochi Service:

**USSD**

- Dial \*334\*8#
- Select Taasi Pochi Loans
- Select loan period
- Select Request Loan
- Enter the amount you wish to borrow within the limit allocated

You will receive funding for your business shortly after making the Loan request. The

funds will be applied to your Pochi wallet.

#  **My One App**

- Select Pochi La Biashara
- Select Taasi Pochi
- Select loan period
- Select borrow and enter amount

You will receive funding for your business shortly after making the Loan request. The

funds will be applied to your Pochi wallet.

# **Accessing funds**

- You will access the funds from the Pochi wallet.
- Dial \*334\*8# select send money, withdraw, Lipa na Pochi or move funds to your M-PESA wallet.

**Minimum and Maximum amount**

We offer Ksh. 1000 up to Ksh. 150,000 as the loan credit limit

**Limit Increase Consideration**

Limit increase will be based on the mechanism below:

- How actively and how much you trade on your Pochi wallet.
- Your CRB credit listing and score: How well you repay and perform on all your loans affects your CRB listing and score. The better your score better your chances of a loan limit increase
- Loan Performance: How well you pay back your loans i.e., early repayments on all your loans.

# **Checking credit limit**

- Dial \*334\*8#
- Select Taasi Pochi Loans.
- Select loan period
- Select Check limit.

**Fee charged for the loan**

- The Taasi Pochi Business loan will be charged an access fee.

- The access fees will be deducted upfront before disbursement of the loan and the balance credited to the merchant Pochi la Biashara account.
- Where the loan is not paid by the due date, a roll over fee of 0% will be applied as it is zero-rated for new loans. 
- There will be a grace period of 2 days after which the loan will attract a penalty of 1% of the outstanding loan for the next 7 days.

 For example, a merchant requesting a 7-day loan of amount Ksh 10,000

- Loan amount request: 10,000/=
- Access fee: 3.85%
- Amount disbursed: 9,615/=
- Outstanding loan balance: 10,000

#  **MPESA G3 Visibility**

Search the customer’s account on M-PESA G3 using the MSISDN, review transactions and filter M-PESA Business account. G3 will inform you the lender the customer is opted to as shown below.

 [Screenshot]

# **CRM View**

To verify the loan details on CRM, select the loan contract ID to view details as shown below.

 [Screenshot] 

 [Screenshot] 

 [Screenshot] 

# **Defaulted / late loan repayment**

**Rollover fees**

Where the loan is not paid by the due date, there will be a grace period of 2 days after which the outstanding loan will attract 1% interest daily for a period of 7 days.  

Outstanding loan balance: 10,000/=

Rollover of 0

New outstanding balance:10,000 \*0% = 10,000

**Roll over fees**

Where the loan is not paid after the 2-day grace period of the due date, a roll over fee of 1% per day for the next seven days shall be applied on the outstanding balance.

**Reasons that may cause loan request to be declined**

The loan may be declined:

- If the Loan amount requested is higher than your Loan Limit. The Loan request MUST be made within your Loan Limit.
- If you have been blacklisted by the Credit Reference Bureau.
- If you have an existing Loan. You will be required to fully repay for an existing loan before requesting for another. You can only request one Loan.
- If your credit score is below the minimum allowed credit score.

**Reasons for requested amount not received**

This might be because of:

- Making a loan request as the first one is still being processed: Wait five minutes before making another loan request if the first one has not been processed.
- The M-PESA system being slow or is down. Once MPESA services are back up, the amount borrowed will be reflected in your account shortly. 

# **CREDIT REFERENCE BUREAU**

**Meaning of Negative listing at CRB**

Your loan request can be disapproved because you are negatively listed at the Credit Reference Bureau. This may be due to a previously defaulted loan that is not yet paid up for or has been fully paid for without obtaining clearance from the Credit Reference Bureau,

**Definition of CRB**

A Credit Reference Bureau is a firm that collects information from various sources and

provides consumer credit information on individual consumers for a variety of uses.

For example, it provides information on individuals' borrowing and bill paying habits.

**CRB score/rating**

This is an individual's credit score given by a CRB using the individual’s credit history which is how well you have performed on all previous loans and how well you are performing on your current loan (s). For example, are you defaulting on any loan? Do you pay all your loans on time?

**CRB Negative listing Clearance**

- You must fully repay your defaulted loan(s) to the respective financial institution(s) and apply for a clearance certificate from the CRB.
- After successfully clearing your negatively listed loans, the record may remain in your account for up to five years.
- To improve your score, you must improve your repayment behavior on all your **current and future loans, that is paying loan(s) on time.**

**Checking CRB score and Listing**

You can click on this link on your mobile phone [Creditinfo | We Facilitate Access to Finance](https://creditinfo.co.ke/) (Google Chrome Browser

recommended) to get a comprehensive report from Credit Info, which is one of the Credit Reference Bureaus. They charge Ksh. 50 for a report.

**Effects of Negative CRB listing**

Negative listing can limit you from accessing future loans from financial institutions.

After a customer has settled their outstanding loan and wishes to be cleared from CRB, they will request a CRB batch number. Kindly raise an SR as a front-line agent, thereafter, the second line support team will share the batch number with the customer by sending a request to the relevant partner,parter i.e. Pezesha or Sidian Bank, through the emails below. (please note the request will be done by the

CRB Batch number request

Pezesha- Oscar Ouma <ouma@pezesha.com

Sidian- [akngunju@sidianbank.co.ke](mailto:akngunju@sidianbank.co.ke), eiwachira@sidianbank.co.ke>

 NB: First line support should raise an SR for Batch number request and not send an email. The email to the relevant partners will only be sent by the second line support team.

**Loan repayment steps.**

**USSD**

- Dial \*334\*8#
- Select Taasi Pochi Loans
- select Pay Loan

then select

**Partial Settlement** – you can pay in installments before the Loan due date.

**Full Settlement** – you can pay the entire Loan amount at once.

The amount should reflect in your account immediately after successful repayment.

**My One APP**

- On My OneApp
- Select Pochi la Biashara
- Select Taasi Pochi Loans
- Select select repay loan
- Enter amount

**Partial Settlement** – you can opt to pay in installments before or after due date.

**Full Settlement** – you can pay the entire Loan amount at once.

The amount should reflect in your account immediately after successful repayment.

# **Taasi Pochi Loan Repayment using Bonga points**

**Loan repayment steps.**

**USSD**

- Dial \*334\*8#
- Select Taasi Pochi Loans
- select Pay Loan
- select Lipa Na Bonga
- Confirm loan repayment
- Enter M-PESA PIN

**Repayment figure not reflecting**

If the payment is not reflected within 24 hours, merchant will call Safaricom Customer Care Line 100

**Repayment not reflecting and extra fee charged**

If you were charged additional fees because the repayment made did not reflect on time, you are eligible for a waiver. Call Safaricom Customer Care Line 100 to initiate the waiver request. The waiver should reflect in less than 48 hours after it is requested.

**Early loan repayment.**

Early loan repayment is highly encouraged as this can result in you accessing a higher

loan limit faster by improving your CRB score.

 **Debt collection agency**

- The lender will use both SMS communication and direct phone calls to the nominated numbers and office contact to follow up on loan repayments and recover the debts.

articleTitle: ESCALATION MATRIX FOR NI PUSH FRAUD
markdownContent:
**Escalation Procedure**

articleTitle: POCHI LA BIASHARA REVERSALS SLA GUIDELINES
markdownContent:
**Reversal Guidelines**

Pochi La Biashara Reversal should be treated as below:

| Reversal Type | Action | SLA |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Pochi to Person | Treated as a P2P reversal | 2Hrs (Working hrs) |
| Pochi (MSME) to Pochi (MSME) | Treated as a wrong Buy Goods Till/Paybill (Safaricom Acquired) transaction | 72Hrs (Working hrs) |
| Person to Pochi | Treated as a wrong Buy Goods Till/Paybill (Safaricom Acquired) transaction | 72Hrs (Working hrs) |
| Pochi Withdrawal from M-PESA Agent | Treated as a wrong agent withdrawal Transaction | 12Hrs (Working hrs) |
| Pochi to LNM Buy Goods/Paybill | Treated as a wrong Buy Goods Till/Paybill (Safaricom Acquired) transaction | 72Hrs (Working hrs) |

**NOTE:**

Where funds have been utilized, **CEE shall NOT disclose to Party A how party B has utilized the funds received.**

Do **NOT suspend** or **add a state tag** on customers account due to insufficient funds but advise the customer to follow up with the recipient or report to the police for assistance.

**Kindly Note that Pochi partial reversals on G3 are now possible for below transactions:**

**(i) Pochi to Customer** 
**(ii) Customer Send to Pochi**  
**(iii) Pochi to Pochi**

**Micro SME Sell Airtime to Customer Reversals**

This will apply to Micro SME Sell Airtime to Customer transaction where the Pochi Merchant erroneously purchases for a wrong number.

**Guidelines**

- The reversal is done without having to call the customer for consent.
- Partial reversal will not be possible as well as reversals older than one month (30 days)
- The reversal request can come from the customer or Pochi merchant.
- The Merchant/customer will give the mobile number that receives money.
- **Purchase to self:** No commission awarded. Reverse on Siebel

- Purchase to other: **5% commission awarded must be recovered.** Ensure Pochi merchant has sufficient funds in Pochi wallet to cover the commission reversal. Proceed to reverse on Siebel. 

You do not need to raise SR unless there is a technical failure.

**CEE Action on Siebel**

- The CEE will enter the customer's mobile number and will confirm ownership of the line using Customer Names.
- The CEE will confirm transaction details i.e., amount purchased, date / time transaction was made and transaction number (where available). On the transaction History button, (Under Transaction History, CEE will specify date range and query recharge history).
- Where multiple transactions are made on the date specified, CEE will take caution to confirm with customer the exact transaction to be reversed i.e., using time, amount, and transaction id where necessary.
- CEE will confirm the available airtime balance is not less than amounts requested to be reversed i.e., not partially utilized.  Successful. If the balance is sufficient the CEE will initiate the reversal.
- The FSS Team will run a report daily of all airtime reversals done manually removing all promotional resources.

**System Failure**

Where system failure is noted in completing the transaction i.e. the airtime has been deducted in CBS, but the Pochi Merchant’s Business account has not been credited, the CEE will escalate via an SR and give details of the failure noted.

**Retail CEE**

The Retail CEE will also raise an SR to the Consumer care analyst and immediately notify the team leader on duty of any anomaly.

**Support Analyst Action**

The Support analyst will pick the SR and check if the airtime was deducted before doing a manual B2C refund to the Merchant’s MSISDN as per the **[MAAB-0001](https://sakahub.safaricom.co.ke/app/article/7cbff845-5d0d-42b2-bcd0-2565afe57856)****: Manual Adjustment Process -Support.** 

**NOTE:** The amount credited to the Pochi Merchant will be less the commission earned on the transaction.

**NOTE:** Similarly to LNM reversals, merchants (owners of Pochi) should be contacted to give consent for reversals. 

**How to contact us**

1. In case of any queries, Call Line 100, 200, or 234.
2. Visit any Safaricom retail Shop or Care Desks.

articleTitle: Credit Reference Bureau (CRB) Definition and Mechanics
markdownContent:
**Definition**

- A **Credit Reference Bureau** is a company licensed by the Central Bank of Kenya to collect and combine credit information on individuals from different sources.
- This information is provided upon the request of a bank or the individual.

**How it Works**

- Such reports help the bank decide whether you as a potential borrower will be able to repay your new loan.
- If the report shows that you have a delinquent loan - one that you are no longer making payments – the lender will consider the degree of risk in lending to you.
- It does not mean that you must be denied new credit, but lenders will be more careful when lending money to you or may apply tougher lending conditions.
- The Central Bank of Kenya has been mandated by law to license and supervise the operations of such bureaus.

**CRB Reporting**

- This is the process where information on customers who have defaulted on loans are forwarded to CRBs, recorded and shared with other financial institutions including but not limited to Banks and SACCOS.
- A default is reported to CRBs once a customer fails to repay their loans IN FULL after 90 Days have lapsed since the date when the customer took the loan.
- By this time, and despite regular notifications reminding you to repay, your loan has been overdue for >60 Days noting the 30-Day repayment period and is therefore considered “Non-Performing”.

 **Implications of being reported to CRB on a Credit    History**

- Once you are reported on CRB, other lenders including Banks and SACCOS will access information on your credit history and determine whether to give you a loan or not upon request.
- If you have a Bad Credit History, lenders will consider you as a high-risk customer and may hesitate to give you the loan given your negative repayment habits.
- The lender may choose to deny you the loan altogether given your high risk and bad credit reputation; and/or introduce tough conditions e.g. higher interest rates and/or reduced repayment period and/or reduced amounts.
- Listing with CRB does not mean that lenders are not allowed to lend the borrower any money during the 7-year period. It only means that the lender will take extra caution and negotiation will become more difficult for such a borrower. For example, a listed customer may be subjected to shorter loan terms, higher interest rates and/or the Bank may decline their loan request depending on the risk profile of the borrower and relative to the risk appetite of the lender.

**Credit Information Sharing**

- Credit Information Sharing (CIS) is a process where banks and other credit providers/lenders submit information about their borrowers to a credit reference bureau so that it can be shared with other credit providers/lenders.
- It enables the banks to know how borrowers repay their loans.
- This is also known as “Credit Reporting” or “CRB Reporting”.
- Credit reporting allows banks to better distinguish between good and bad borrowers. Someone who has failed to pay their loan at one bank will not simply be able to walk to another bank to get another loan without the banks knowing about it.
- Over time better information on potential borrowers should mean that it will be both cheaper and easier to obtain loans.

**Credit History**

- Credit history is a record of an individual's past borrowing and repayment habits, including information about late payments.
- This information is used by lenders such as banks to determine an individual's ability and track record of repaying a debt.
- The credit history is then used to establish an individual credit score.
- The willingness to repay a debt is indicated by how timely past payments have been made to other lenders.
- Lenders like to see consumer debt obligations paid regularly and on time and therefore focus particularly on missed payments.

**Credit Report**

- A Credit Report is a report generated by the Credit Reference Bureau, containing detailed information on a person’s credit history, including KYC information, credit accounts and loans, bankruptcies and late payments, and recent inquiries.
- It can be obtained by individual customers and/or prospective lenders only when they have permissible reason as defined in law, to determine one’s creditworthiness.
- The law requires credit reference bureaus to supply the customer with one free credit report per year. Any additional reports are chargeable and vary from one CRB to another.

# **Definition**

This is a web-based account of a MSISDN accessible on:  [myaccount.safaricom.co.ke](https://myaccount.safaricom.co.ke/)

The Safaricom World account gives the customer a detailed view of their MSISDN profile including account balances, usage statement (airtime & data) and M-PESA Statements. 

# **Using and Accessing Safaricom World**

Customers can use the webpage to view their MSISDN account balances, access/purchase Safaricom products and services, find a Safaricom Shop, access digital services (e.g videos, educational content, e-paper etc).

To view their Safaricom World account, a customer **needs to be connected to Safaricom Mobile connection/internet** & click on**: [myaccount.safaricom.co.ke](https://myaccount.safaricom.co.ke/)**

# **What is Safaricom World OTP?**

Customers who access ***myaccount.safaricom.co.ke/account/usage*** (usage transparency link) will receive a One Time PIN from Sender ID: **Safaricom** & a prompt to enter the OTP on the World account.

Entering the Safaricom World OTP will provide a detailed view of a MSISDN airtime and data usage.

# **Safaricom World OTP received without accessing the link**

Customers who report receiving the Safaricom World One Time PIN from Safaricom while they have not accessed the Safaricom world account/usage transparency link, should be advised to:

Check that their Mobile data connection is not tethered to another user/device (Switch off mobile hotspot).

Example: Where customer A provides mobile hotspot services to customer B & B accesses the Usage link (Safaricom World) on their device, customer A will receive the OTP.

To check & close any browser tab on their device that is running the Safaricom World account (usage transparency link).

Customers should be **cautioned NOT to share their OTPs** as this can provide visibility of their  account usage.

articleTitle: Safaricom Dealer Handling of Voucher Issues on line 300
markdownContent:
Authorized Safaricom dealers will be the owners of the recharge vouchers

- Safaricom distribution team will deliver those vouchers to dealer outlets. These dealers are the only ones who can authorize locking of recharge vouchers
- Where Safaricom retailer/agent calls to report lost recharge vouchers the CEE in the contact Centre will capture the serials on stolen-recharge-vouchers-form provided on CM Intranet. The submitted form will be sent to Dealer Management folder as an email ([DealerManagement2@Safaricom.co.ke](mailto:DealerManagement2@Safaricom.co.ke))
- Dealer Management will pick the email, use Dealer inventory on S-Hub, to verify ownership of the reported cards, after verification the \`CEE will advise the agent/retailer to contact the distributor (DSA), who will contact the dealer to lock them
- If a Safaricom dealer contacts us via line 100/200 or on social media to block stolen vouchers, the CEE will Open the stolen-recharge-vouchers-form provided on CM Intranet link 'CM Forms' that will be submitted as an Email to Dealer Management.
- Dealer Management will receive email, use Dealer inventory on S-Hub, to verify ownership of the reported cards, call the dealer to verify why he/she cannot block them via the portal.
- If the dealer confirms there are challenges/system downtime to block the cards from the portal, then Line 300 CEE will advise the dealer to read the serial numbers verbally for confirmation.
- After confirmation of ownership of the vouchers, Dealer Management will block the vouchers on VMS system, advise the dealer accordingly, then prepare a table that will indicate the serial range, the face value, locked, failed, and total.
- Dealer Management will call the dealer and advise him/her on the tally of the vouchers locked and the ones that failed and send the table and the excel attachments of the vouchers pulled from VSMAP to Safaricom dealer manager.
- The dealer manager will send an edited excel to the dealer, the edited excel will exclude used vouchers.
- In case the dealer locks the cards on the airtime refund portal, they will request the tally by sending an email to line300 escalation folder.
- In case a customer/retailer calls or uses social media to report voucher cards on Issued status (less than 100), the CEE on call or on social media will raise an SR to contact Centre support team. Support analyst will escalate the issue to distribution and fulfilment team via mail for activation. Once activated, distribution team will share email to support team who will advise the customer to use the card.
- In case an agent or dealer calls or uses social media to report multiple voucher cards (more than 100 cards) on Issued status, the CEE on call will send an email to [DealerManagement2@Safaricom.co.ke](mailto:DealerManagement2@Safaricom.co.ke), for action.
- In case a dealer sends, mail to [DealerManagement2@Safaricom.co.ke](mailto:DealerManagement2@Safaricom.co.ke) reporting vouchers on issued status Line 300 CEE will check where the vouchers are, either in Safaricom stores or with the dealer using Safaricom-Inventory on S-HUB.
- In case the vouchers are with the dealer, the CEE will send mail to the Distribution & Customer Fulfilment team Distribution&CustomerFulfilment@Safaricom.co.ke for activation, if the email will not be replied within 2hrs; the CEE will make a call for the distribution team for follow up.
- The distribution team will activate the cards and reply the email to line 300TM escalation; thus Dealer Management will respond to the reporting dealer.
- In case the vouchers will be identified in Safaricom store, and were erroneously distributed, line 300 CEE will advise the dealer/DSA who reported that they are not yet allocated to any dealer.
- The dealer will be advised to liaise with respective dealer managers; the dealer Manager will follow up with distribution team, Retailer (shopkeeper) will liaise with the Distribution Sales agent (DSA) who distributed the vouchers, so that further investigation will be done to return the cards to Safaricom store.
- In case dealer’s details will not be available on S-HUB or the dealer is
- unreachable, line 300 CEE will contact respective dealer managers to advice on the way forward.
- There are cases where Safaricom Enterprise team or colleagues doing project report locking of vouchers. Respective accounts manager will contact Line 300 and Dealer Management.
- Dealer Management can confirm ownership of the cards on Safaricom inventory and proceed in locking of the cards and share the tally to the account’s manager.
- There will be instances Safaricom distribution team, will contact line 300 team via mail to lock lost cards on transit. Line 300 CEE will confirm if the vouchers have not been allocated to any dealer. Lock the cards on VMS, tabulate and send a mail that has an attached excel with the raw data of the locked cards to the individual person who reported from distribution Team.
