articleTitle: M-Shwari Savings Deposit Account and Lock Savings Account definition and Mechanics
markdownContent:
**SAVINGS DEPOSIT ACCOUNT**

**Definition**

This is an account that allows a customer to save funds on M-Shwari.

- Customers can deposit and withdraw funds from this account as many times as possible.
- The minimum amount a customer can save is Ksh.1 while the maximum amount is determined by the KYC level.
- No charges while moving funds from MPESA to M-Shwari Savings account and vice versa.
- The transactions are controlled by normal MPESA transaction limits.

**Interest earned on Customer Savings Amount**

| Amount | Interest P.A |
| --- | --- |
| Ksh.1 – Ksh. 20,000 | 3% |
| Ksh. 20,001 – Ksh. 50,000 | 4% |
| Ksh.50,001 | 5% |

**Maximum amount allowed to withdraw M-Shwari to M-PESA**

- A customer can be able to withdraw any amount from Ksh **1.0** up- to the M-PESA maximum limit of **250,000** allowable on M-PESA.
- The withdrawals are subject to M-PESA allowable limits of holding a maximum of 500,000 in M-PESA Wallet at any given time.

**M-SHWARI LOCK SAVINGS ACCOUNT**

**Definition**

This is a Savings Account that allows M-Shwari customers to save for a defined purpose and for a specified Period ranging from 1 to 12Months.

**Account Features and Benefits**

- The M-Shwari Lock Savings account is ideal for customers looking to keep money away safely for 1 to 12 months.
- The funds saved on the M-Shwari Lock Savings Accounts will be kept in the account until the maturity date which is determined by the customer while opening the account.
- The amount will earn an interest on a flat rate of 6.63 % P.A. The interest is calculated daily and paid out on maturity.
- There are no charges levied on the M-Shwari Lock Savings account.
- One must be an M-PESA and M-Shwari customer to access the lock savings account.
- When opening the Account, the minimum amount one can deposit is Ksh.500, after which the customer can deposit any amount and has no maximum savings limit.
- The maximum lock period is 12 months.
- In case a customer breaks the lock to access the funds from the account, the funds are transferred to the M-shwari savings account after **48hrs.**
- On the maturity date at midnight the account is deactivated, and amount transferred to M-Shwari savings account, however the customer can lock the funds again by opening a new M-Shwari Lock Savings account.
- The savings in your lock savings account can be used to repay a defaulted loan. The lock savings funds will be auto debited on day 61 of any overdue loan.
- The locked tab on Siebel CRM will display 2 balances i.e. one showing total Lock savings account balance & available balance, thus the CEE will be able to tell if the customer has broken lock, the amount they requested and lock Savings balance.
- The tab also has information on the maturity date i.e. when the money will be transferred to the normal M-Shwari saving account. (The query will be done on the Lock Savings Account and not the normal M-Shwari Savings Account).
- **M-SHWARI TRANSACTIONS (SAVINGS, LOCK SAVINGS AND LOAN ACCOUNTS)**

 **Authorized Transactions**

 - For Authorized transactions, confirm if there is a reported outage and if none, raise an SR for support to deal with in 72hrs.
 - These transactions are either completed or cancelled by the FS IT team globally within 24hrs.
 - The support analyst will follow up and advise the customer once they are actioned.

 **Cancelled Transactions (M-PESA/M-Shwari Deposits)**

 - For a cancelled transaction, confirm from G2 if the customer has enough funds to facilitate the deposit from M-PESA account.
 - Advise the customer to either repeat the transaction or deposit some funds for the transaction to go through.

 **Cancelled Transactions (Withdrawal)**

 - For cancelled transaction, confirm whether the customer’s account has been locked due to an outstanding loan or any previously cancelled transaction by querying the customer’s number on **CRM M-shwari tab.**
 - In case of an overdue loan, advise the customer to clear the outstanding loan amount either from M-PESA or from M-Shwari account to be able to withdraw from M-Shwari account.
 - If customers number is on the list, advise the customer to deposit an amount equivalent to the amount on the cancelled transaction(s)to facilitate the system to recover the amount.
 - If the customer has already deposited the amount, the CEE shall escalate via SR and advise on the 72hrs SLA.
 - The Support Analyst will wait for the auto recovery. (the Bank does recoveries everyday by midday).
 - If the recovery is not done within 2 days, the Support Analyst shall raise an incident to the NCBA Bank with the narration of the transaction for manual recovery.
 - Once recovery has been made, the support analyst will advise the customer as per resolution and close the SR.

 **Cancelled/Declined Loan Request Transaction**

 - Check the status of the transaction on G2 and confirm the reason for cancellation as per the transaction log.
 - Check the status of the account to confirm whether the account qualifies getting a loan by use of the following parameters:

 **MPESA account age on network**

 - Confirm whether the customer’s M-PESA account is more than six months old and if not, advise the customer that the account should be more than six months old to get a loan.

 **Loan Restrict**

 - If it is CRB restriction, advise the customer to clear with the CRB for them to get a loan.
 - If it is the 30-day restriction, the CEE shall advise the customer that the restriction will be lifted at midnight of the date displayed and can get a loan the following day.
 - 

 **Loan not Allowed**

 - Confirm if the status is loan not allowed and advise the customer to deposit any amount to the M-Shwari Savings Account in order to request for a loan.

 **Loan not Allowed- M**

 - Confirm whether the customer’s account has been locked due to an outstanding loan or any previously cancelled transaction on CRM M-shwari tab.
 - Advise the customer to deposit the amount owed as per cancelled posted list link.
 - In case of an overdue loan, the CEE shall advise the customer to clear the overdue loan amount.
 - In case of a cancelled transaction, the cancelled withdrawal transaction process documented above shall apply.

 **Declined/Cancelled Loan Repayment Transaction**

 - For a loan repayment, the CEE shall confirm if the customer has an outstanding loan and if the customer has enough funds on M-PESA account to make the repayment.
 - If amount is not enough, advise the customer to confirm M-PESA account balance before retrying the transaction.
 - If the amount is enough, ensure the customer is using the correct procedure to make payment.
 - If the customer is unable to make a payment, escalate via SR and advise the customer on 72hrs SLA.
 - The Support Analyst upon getting the SR shall escalate via BMC to the NCBA Bank Team, track the BMC activity and once resolved shall advise the customer as per resolution and close the SR.

 **Missing Transactions(M-PESA/M-Shwari)**

 - For missing transactions, countercheck to verify the transactions were done from G2 to M-Shwari Account.
 - If the transaction is not available on G2, the CEE shall advise the customer to repeat the transaction.
 - If the transaction is available on G2 and missing on M-Shwari, the CEE shall escalate via SR for the Support team to assist and advise the customer on 72hrs SLA.
 - Once the Support Analyst receives the escalation, they will countercheck also and if still missing escalate to NCBA Bank for confirmation.
 - Once the Bank sends a response, the Analyst shall advise the customer accordingly as per the resolution on the BMC activity and close the SR.

 **M-SHWARI MINI-STATEMENT / STATEMENTS AND CHARGES**

 - For mini statements: Go to M-PESA> Loans and Savings>M-Shwari>then select Mini Statement.
 - Currently, you can get five (5) recently completed deposit account transactions.
 - Customer M-Shwari loan and savings statements are now available from the date when customer opted into the service i.e. statements above one year are now available and can be viewed on CRM on the query period, a printed copy can be obtained from a Care desk or Retail Centre.
 - For statement issuance at retail customer ID is a mandatory requirement and no third-party requests are allowed.
 - Charges are as below.

| Transaction | Charges |
| --- | --- |
| M-Shwari mini-statement | 1/= on M-PESA account |
| Account Statement from Safaricom Retail Centers and Care Desks. | 10/= per page |

 **SUPPORT ANALYST ACTION:**

 For M-Shwari Transactions (Savings, Lock Savings and Loan Accounts in Authorized, cancelled transactions (withdrawal)and missing transactions on (M-PESA/M-shwari,

 - The Support analyst will send an email to FSS for an update of status of transactions that are still authorized after 48hrs.
 - The FSS will escalate to NCBA bank and will receive an email from the bank with instructions on the action, whether to complete or cancel the transactions on the 72hrs SLA.

This is applicable to all escalations for resolution by the AML team. It includes and not limited to KYC updates, Change of ownership KYC, Subreg and M-PESA registration queries.

**AML KYC Updates**

**Escalation will be done on Analytica, user will select category - AML KYC Updates, Type as applicable and the document type.**

**a)**     **KYC Updates**

This category will be used where customers KYC status is not compliant and all change of ownership requests. Applicable where user has not been able to successfully update for below use cases:

- **Details Already captured**: Applicable when attempting to perform a KYC update but error message is “details already captured”.

- Check status on the image’s portal (Access granted to all Team leaders).
- If the ID images on the portal tally the physical ID presented and status is “Pending” or “Approved” proceed to advise customer and \\ or unbar line.
- Raise escalation and attach copy of ID / Passport.

- **Name mismatch**: Applicable when attempting to perform a KYC update but error message is “Names do not match”.

- Erroneous names only apply to cases where the name is similar but with minor errors e.g. missing letters, or differing order.

- Check and amend erroneous names on Jiandikishe then retry.
- Where retry fails, name mismatch is not minor or If name on Jiandikishe belongs to a different customer than the ID presented, raise ticket under this category and attach copy of ID.

- **Defaced IDs**: Applicable when attempting to perform a KYC update but fails to read the document because the back or front of the ID is disfigured/defaced.

- Raise ticket under this category and attach a copy of the waiting card and the defaced ID.

- **Lost ID**: Applicable when customer requests for KYC update, does not have their original ID but presents police abstract/Waiting card.

- Unbar after successful vetting.

- Check status on the image’s portal (Access granted to all Team leaders) if the ID images on the portal tally.
- Raise ticket under this category and attach a copy of the waiting card and Police abstract.

- **Deceased:** Documents required are Death certificate, affidavit, copy of ID of the deceased, copy of ID of the requesting person.

Applicable when customer is deceased, and next of kin is requesting for a KYC update.

- Unbar the line where applicable after successful vetting.
- Raise ticket under this category, and attach a copy of the death certificate, affidavit, copy of the ID of the deceased and ID of the person requesting for service.

- **Document scanned but not picking KYC:** Applicable when attempting to perform a KYC but the scanning fails to read the document i.e. where the back / front is defaced. This applies to valid foreign passports and others. 

- Unbar the line where applicable.
- Raise ticket under this category and attach a copy ID / Passport.

**b)    Change of ownership**

This is applicable for Change of Ownership queries.

- For every change of ownership process done, KYC validation will be required for new recipient after successful completion of the change, to authenticate customer KYC.

- Complete the Change of Ownership process as per applicable process.
- Update KYC as per current process.
- Where KYC validation fails,

- Confirm details of the ID on the Subscriber Failure Manager, update accordingly then retry.

- For failed KYC compliance, raise ticket under the KYC update category and attach copy of ID / Passport.

- Otherwise, raise ticket under this category and attach copy of ID/ Passport.

- **Validation service unavailable**: Applicable when attempting to register a new account on M-PESA but error message is “Validation service unavailable”.

- Raise ticket under this category and attach copy of ID / Passport.

- **M-PESA - Request approval**: Applicable when attempting to perform an update of Name or Document Number of a customer on M-PESA and error message is “The request must be approved by another operator”.

- Ensure name, document type and document number on Jiandikishe is exactly as per the ID then retry.      
- Otherwise, raise ticket under this category and attach a copy of the document - ID / Passport.

This category will be used for Sim registration queries. The use cases as below will apply.

- Amend accordingly then retry.

**Retail Agent – Step-by-Step SIM Swap Process on View360**

# **1\. Introduction**

This manual guides Retail Agents through the end-to-end SIM Swap process using the View360 portal. It ensures secure customer verification, accurate data capture, and compliance with fraud-prevention standards.

# **2\. Login & Access**

Log into the View360 portal using SSO credentials.

Confirm successful authentication and access the customer account page by searching the number requiring the service.

# **3.Customer Validation (Primary Vetting)**

**Required:**

Ask the customer for:

Original ID document

On View360, complete Primary Vetting using the following mandatory fields:

Full Names

ID Number

Year of Birth

**Outcome:**

If vetting passes → Proceed.

If vetting fails → Advise the customer to return with correct supporting documents.

# **4****. Initiate SIM Swap on View360**

Navigation

Account Overview > Quick Actions > Click SIM Swap icon

# **5\. System Pre-Checks**

The system automatically validates the line intended for swap against multiple rules.

**Checks Include:**

1\. Number is not Golden.

2\. Line is Prepaid.

3\. Account is not Regulated (NB: if failed and the decision is to proceed, attach supporting documents).

4\. Customer is not High Alert (NB: if failed and the decision is to proceed, attach supporting documents).

5\. Line is within vicinity.

6.  Line is not Roaming (NB: if failed and the decision is to proceed, attach supporting documents).

7.  Line is Active.

8.  Line is at least 24 hours old on the network.

9.  Line is not Self-Whitelisted (\**100\**100#).

10.  Line is not in Fraud Location.

11.  Line is not On.

12\. IPRS Check (verified ✔️ green tick; if verification fails, update KYC and proceed with the swap).

**Display Format:**

Results are shown in a table format:

Green tick ✔️ \= Passed.

Red **x** \= Failed.

**NB (Special Handling)**

I.         If the pre-check indicates the account is regulated and/or the customer is on High Alert: -

Consult the Manager / Team Leader on duty for further KYC validation through the Subscriber Registration Portal.

If the TL/Manager advises NOT to proceed, the swap must be declined and documented under interaction notes.

If the ID image is missing from the Subscriber Registration Portal, raise a ticket on Analytica to the fraud team for guidance.

# **6.Agent Decision**

The Retail Agent uses the pre-check outcomes to decide whether to continue with the swap.

If the decision is to proceed: -

**QR Code**

- View360 generates a QR code.
- Agent scans the QR code using the business phone

# **7.** **Phone-Based KYC & Document Capture (Journey moves to the Phone device)**

The QR code will open a portal on the device browser to collect customer data showing step by step flow.

**Step 1: Select Doc type presented by the customer**

Document number is **mandatory** if a doc type is selected.

Enter Serial number

If customer has **no document**, proceed with other supporting docs.

**Step 2:** **Capture Images**

 Where a registration document is provided, launch your phone camera and take a photo of both the front and back.

· Take a **front photo** (mandatory).

· Take a **back photo** (optional) e.g. where the document doesn’t have the back page.

**NB**

Document scanning will take place during a live session within the system.

Documents will not be saved or stored on the business phone after the upload process.

Pre-saving or uploading documents from the phone gallery will not be allowed.

Agents must scan/take a photo of the customer’s document in real time during the active SIM swap **session** before proceeding with the request.

**Step 3: Validation**

Review the documents and submit for validation, where its failed, advise the customer accordingly

 If validation **passes**, return to View360

# **8\. Secondary Vetting (View360)**

On the displayed QR code, click proceed, View360 displays Secondary verification details.

 **Secondary Vetting checks include:**

Frequently Dialled Numbers (FDN’s)

GSM details

M-PESA account details

M-PESA transactions

Post-pay account details (If any)

**Requirement:**

**✔️**At least 2 secondary checks must pass to proceed.

If secondary vetting fails- agent to probe further.

**How many secondary vetting details do i need to vet on?**

- A minimum of two categories must pass for successful vetting.
- Two correct Frequently Dialled Numbers (FDN’s) will count as one successful pass, and one additional pass must come from any of the remaining categories.

Other Categories for Vetting include:

GSM Details

M-PESA Details

M-PESA Transactions

Post pay Details

See screenshot below:

 [Screenshot] 

# **9\. Executing the SIM Swap**

If secondary vetting passes:

1. Enter or scan **new SIM’s SIMEX serial number**.
2. Add a **clear comment** explaining:

Reason for swap

Documents verified

Any escalations or approvals

3. Submit.

The system validates SIMEX:

**Valid** → OK to use

**Already used/Invalid** → Agent must scan another SIMEX

# **10\. SIM Swap Confirmation & Closure**

**Successful Swap**

Confirmation message appears.

New SIM serial is updated on the system.

**Failed Swap**

System displays the failure reason.

Agent follows the recommended corrective steps.

# **11.Interaction Capture** **(****Mandatory)**

Although View360 logs basic activity, the agent must manually record:

Customer vetting details.

SIM swap outcome (successful / unsuccessful).

Any additional notes or important observations.

# **Definition**

- This is an enhanced service enabling franchise owned outlets to offer SIM swaps on CRM to the Safaricom customers.
- The new SIM swap process via the CRM introduces a chatbot widget that back checks customer details.
- For successful SIM replacement, a customer will still need to carry their ID Cards or passport as per the usual SIM swap KYC verification process.
- If the customer has the **Original PIN** all services will be resumed immediately, but if the customer **does not** have the original PIN for the swap the customer will ONLY be able to make and receive calls, all the other services will automatically resume after 24 hours of a successful SIM swap.

# **Step by step process**

- Agent logs into CRM using AD credentials.
- Agent requests for the customer’s original ID for validation, checks CRM the line status.
- Clicks chatbot widget & selects Franchise SIM swap tab to input the MSISDN to be swapped.
- The system performs prechecks.
- Where system checks fail, the agent gets a pop-up notification advising the customer to visit the retail center for further assistance with the original Document ID.
- Where system checks pass, a QR code is generated on the chatbot widget.
- Agent scans the QR code using **the registered business line** (NB. Should be on **mobile data** and **not WIFI**)
- The code will open a welcome portal on the phone device browser with a step-by-step guide on how to collect customer data.
- Agent will be presented with the registration document page where they will be guided to take the photo of the front and back of the registration document. (Kenyan National ID will be selected by default).
- Customer KYC (Doc ID captured and uploaded for validation, both back and front).
- Enter original pin if available. (Not Mandatory).
- Customer validation undertaken.
- Depending on the score, agent is prompted to swap the line or decline due to failed vetting.
- Where the customer will be suspended on M-PESA upon swap, the agent will seek **consent** to proceed or not.
- Where theirs's consent, agent Scans / Input the new Serial number (Simex) and submits for SIM swap implementation.
- Successful swap confirmation notification is auto populated, if failed the failure reason is provided.
- Auto interaction is entered on CRM on different scenarios.

**NOTE:** **D****o not raise SRs for errors experienced when doing a SIM swap. Instead, refer customer to the nearest retail shop for further assistance.**

# **Key Shifts (What is changing?)**

| FROM | TO |
| --- | --- |
| Manual capturing of interaction. | Automated of interaction. |
| Manual ID details capture on CRM. | Scanning of an ID. |
| Manual ID validation. | System based ID validation. |
| No offering SIM swap service via CRM. | Offering SIM swap via CRM. |

articleTitle: M-PESA Business Till opt In Guideline and Charges
markdownContent:
# **M-PESA Business Till Opt In Guideline**

Confirm from G2 that the merchant has the M-PESA Business Till Product configuration:

**Check the Head Office (HO):** The migrated Tills will be attached to any of the Safaricom CBU/EBU HOs and LNM M-PESA BUSINESS TILL HEAD OFFICE. If the store is on any other HO advise the merchant that this service is currently ONLY available to merchants withdrawing to M-PESA.

**Check the Store and the Till Products:** The Store should have the Independent Merchant Product and the Till should have the Independent Merchant Store Till product. The merchant can have both the Merchant Store product and the M-PESA Business Till product. Where the merchant is withdrawing to M-PESA and they do not have the product;

Retail CEE will add the product and advise the merchant to opt in

Call Center will raise an SR for addition of product by LNM Support.

**Check if the store has a nominated number under KYC Info Tab:** This service is ONLY currently available to merchants withdrawing to M-PESA. If the store does not have a nominated number advise the merchant that this service is currently ONLY available to merchants withdrawing to M-PESA.

**Check the Revenue Configuration Tab:** This should not have any Revenue Configuration set since M-PESA Business Till will only have one account. Where the configuration profile is configured/enabled the merchant will not be able to withdraw funds.

Retail CEE will disable the configuration on M-PESA G2

Call Center will raise an SR for LNM Support to disable the configuration

**Check Operators at the Store Level:** merchants on the M-PESA Business Till will need the Primary Operator ID and PIN to be able to perform transactions.

**Where the Primary Operator is missing**; kindly advise the merchant to opt in ie. Dial \*234# and select M-PESA Business Till Menu from their nominated number or from Till MSISDN and select opt into to M-PESA Business Till service. This will automatically create the operator and will share their ID and a start key. Remember to advise the merchant to change their PIN/Start Key to be able to perform the other services.

**Where the Primary Operator is Pending Active**; Advise the merchant to dial 234# and select M-PESA Business Till Menu from their nominated number or from Till MSISDN to change their PIN number before proceeding to perform the other transactions.

**Where the Primary Operator is Active**; Advise the merchant to dial 234# and select M-PESA Business Till Menu from their nominated number or from Till MSISDN and proceed to perform other services using the Primary Operator ID and their PIN. Where the merchant does not remember their PIN or has deleted their start key go to article **A0479: M-PESA Business Till Operator ID/ Start Key/PIN Request Guideline**. Attached are the M-PESA G2 screenshots

**Advise the merchant to dial \*234\*2# from their nominated number or to dial \*234# and select the M-PESA Business Till from their Till MSISDN.** Where the merchant is unable to dial the USSD click [here](https://esaka.safaricom.net/system/templates/selfservice/safaricom/#!agent/portal/555500000001002/article/555500000010300/32273-Merchants-Unable-To-Dial-2342-From-Their-Nominated-Number) for the guideline.

# **Rates and charges**

| Business Till Transaction | Charges |
| --- | --- |
| Pay to another Buy Goods Till | 0.27 % capped at 200/- |
| Pay to a mobile number (B2C) | Existing M-PESA Send Money charges Apply |
| Pay to a utility till (Pay bill C2B) | Standard Paybill charges Apply |
| Withdraw at agent | Standard agent withdrawal charges |
| Sell Airtime to customer | Standard Agent Airtime commission rates |

Kindly note that we shall migrate merchants who are using the old buy goods till to Business till **beginning March 28th, 2022, attached find the FAQs.**

# **How to Update Email Address**

**Business Till merchants** can now update their email addresses using the **USSD \*234\*2#** DIY process.

Dial *\*234\*2#* from the nominated number.

Enter Store number.

Select *Account Services*

Choose the *Update Email* menu.

**Benefits**

This process eliminates the previous need for paperwork, allowing Business Till merchants to update their email address directly through the USSD menu.

This email address will then be used by the merchants when making requests to our various email support channels.

**NOTE:** This feature is currently available exclusively for Business Till merchants. We will extend similar functionality to organizations using Paybill, Short-Term Paybill, and Buy Goods products on \*234\*4# soon.

Updated Organization Email will be viewed on G2 portal under KYC Infor tab.

 [Screenshot] 

DIY feature enabling organization nominated numbers to update their organization email addresses, both on \*234\*2# and \*234\*4#.

| Channel | Product | Product Name on G2 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| *234*2# | Business Till | Independent Merchant Store ProductSmall Merchant ProductMedium Merchant Head Office Product |
| *234*4# | Paybill | Paybill Product |
| Buy Goods | Merchant Head Office Product | |
| Short Term Paybill | Short Term Paybill Product | |

**NOTE:** Bulk payment (B2C) shortcodes cannot utilise this feature since they do not have nominated numbers

# **Accumulation Matrix**

Bonga points are earned on **in-bundle purchases** and as well as **out of bundle** usage**.**

- In-bundle transactions start to accumulate points at **1 point** for every **KSh 20****.**

***Example:- If a customer buys a bundle (Minutes, data, SMS) worth Ksh******.******20 they will earn 1 point. If they purchase a bundle of Ksh 50 they will earn 2 points only. Etc. No proration of the award.***

- Out\-of-bundle usage earns **one (1) Bonga Point** for **every Ksh.10** of airtime spent on Safaricom network. i.e. if you spend Ksh.12 on out of bundle (call, sms, browsing charged from airtime), you earn 1 bonga point as there is no proration of the award.
- You earn one (1) Bonga point for **every Kshs.100** (Kenya Shillings One Hundred) charged on M\-PESA as transactional charge.

# **Redemption for Individual customers** 

The procedure is initiated by the customer and begins when s/he visits the retail centre.   

Where customer requests for redemption of non merchandise, CEE will advise customer on various available options to redeem i.e. via SMS, USSD, Safaricom APP or Selfcare. 

Subscribers with an Okoa balance will not be able to redeem any other resources except free money. This will be used to repay the ETU debt first. Customers should first clear the Okoa debt to allow them redeem their Bonga for other resources.   

Where the customer requests for redemption of merchandise, CEE will proceed to vet the customer as per the Retail Vetting Procedure. The agent needs to verify the vetting details in the system i.e. full names and document ID.   

After vetting, if customer is registered and passes the vetting, the CEE will confirm the available bonga balance on customers account and will give available options for redemptions i.e. full bonga, partial bonga or flexi bonga. 

CEE will check the redemption history on CRM/LMS system to validate the number of times single MSSIDN has redeemed in a single day for merchandise. 

Maximum number allowed for merchandise redemption for one MSSDN is five times, for any running promotion and customer is requesting to redeem for more than five times CEE should advise the customer on promotion terms & conditions. 

After validation the agent will assist customer generate password from their phone and will proceed to tender and issue receipt. 

An interaction must be raised on Siebel capturing details of the transaction.   

# **Redemption for company lines**

For Bonga request by companies or organizations, the Company will be required to prepare an authorization letter to be presented to a Safaricom Shop. The letter must have the following details:     

Be on the company original letter head.   

Must state that the bearer has been authorized to do a redemption on behalf of the company, indicating in the letter their full name, and ID number. Where the same is not indicated, CEE must call the contact person and also use available contacts on Siebel to verify approval for Bonga redemption.   

Party sent must have original ID and have it scanned and attached   

The letter should preferably be stamped using the company rubber stamp. In exceptional cases where company claims to have no stamp, CEE will verify from previous correspondence/account managers.   

The letter must be signed by the company contact person.   

The agent must call the contact person to verify before redemption. Once vetting is done satisfactorily, redemption will follow.     

The Agent should attach a scanned copy of all the above documents on CRM and capture a Service Interaction including all the vetting details / approvals in the notes.   

These letters should be stamped with the Retail Shop rubber stamp showing the current date, Service Interaction or Service Request number indicated clearly on the letter. The staff performing the redemption should then file this.   

# **Redemption on Safaricom lines** 

This applies to redemption of bonga points on Safaricom owned lines i.e. Safaricom owned Test lines, data lines, Retail Shop lines etc.   

Points accumulated for lines belonging to Safaricom, specific departments or shops are not redeemed at the retail shops.   

Staff lines are exempt, where staff requests to redeem merchandise from their account i.e. lines registered under the company with the staff as the primary contact and used by the staff. CEE will request the staff to present their staff ID or national ID.   

CEE upon vetting will assist customer to redeem as per their request and enter an interaction and will attach ID seen on the account.   

Where a third party is sent, third party process will apply.   

# **Changa Na Bonga and Bonga PIN** 

This service allows customers to transfer their bonga points to other Safaricom subscribers this is based on set product configuration.   

**1****.** **Pre-paid**   

Where customer visits retail in scenarios where they have not been able to set their Bonga PIN or have forgotten the same.   

CEE will vet and trouble shoot to confirm customer’s tariff and configuration to allow transfer of points and will advise customer accordingly.   

Where customer’s tariff allows transfer i.e. pre-paid lines, CEE will vet customer and request to see their original ID as per vetting procedure.   

CEE will then proceed to log into the bonga PIN system and (re)set customer Bonga PIN once customer passes the vetting process.   

CEE will then proceed to guide customer on changing the PIN on their device.   

Third party Requests for PIN will not be honoured.   

**2****.** **Post -paid**   

For post –paid individual lines, the customer will present ID and CEE will proceed to log into the bonga PIN system and reset customer Bonga PIN once customer passes the vetting process and will assist customer set their bonga PIN. CEE will raise an interaction.   

Where the system-based business rules don’t allow Changa Na Bonga i.e.  Corporate post- paid customers, manual process will apply.   

CEE will raise a Service Request on Siebel and attach the following   documents.    

I.         Original ID (Party sent must have original ID and have it scanned and attached on Siebel.)   

II.         Duly filled and signed manual adjustment form.   

III.         Customer’s written request to transfer points, should be on the company original letter head, preferably stamped and signed by the contact person.   

SA will ensure manual adjustment form is dully signed by the manager.   

SA will ensure the numbers are registered under the requesting customer on Siebel and sends an email to EBU account manager to confirm and approve request.   

Once approval is done consolidates points and will proceed to notify the customer via mail, SMS or phone call.   

SA will close SR with action taken.   

# **Manual Adjustment Procedure**

The procedure is applicable to all cases where a customer’s bonga points need to be adjusted either upwards or downwards. It also applies to cases where a customer’s airtime needs to be adjusted or topped up to the customer manually on the system.   

# **Subscriber Bonga points adjustment**

When a customer visits the shop to redeem their Bonga points, there are instances, where due to system issues, the customers’ points may need to be adjusted. Case in point as below:   

a) Customer’s points are deducted on Siebel/ LMS but the merchandise is not released from POS.   

b) Merchandise is released from POS but customer points are not deducted on Siebel/LMS    

c) Any other situation as per manager discretion and justification.   

Where any of the cases above occur, CEE will fill the manual adjustment form.   

The CEE will raise an SR and attach relevant documents.   

The SA will confirm that all the details entered on the SR are correct and will ensure manual adjustment form is signed by manager as approval.   

The request will then be forwarded to the RCM for approval after having verified validity of the adjustment. The following approval limits will apply:-   

| Category | Max Amount | Approver |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Bonga | 1-29999 | RCM |
| | 30000-49999 | RCM |
| | 50000+ | RCM |

 Once the request has been approved the SA or Team Leader will then adjust the points on Siebel for the same and close the SR with the necessary resolution details and inform the customer of the same.

articleTitle: SMS Bundle DIY procedures to Subscribe and Unsubscribe
markdownContent:
# **How to Subscribe/Buy SMS More for Less Bundle**

**Via 188**

- Dial \*188# to subscribe (opt in) and select a Bundle of your choice.
- Choose options to subscribe to either the Daily SMS/7 Days/30 Days Bundle or Buy for Other Number.
- Select your preferred Validity Category.
- Select your preferred SMS bundle.
- Confirm the selection.
- You will receive a notification confirming that you have successfully subscribed to the selected SMS Bundle. 

# **How to purchase SMS bundle via M-PESA**

- Dial \*188#Ok
- Choose options to subscribe to either the Daily SMS/7 Days/30 Days Bundle or Buy for Other Number.
- Select your preferred Validity Category.
- Select Buy Once or Auto renew.
- Select mode of payment M-PESA/Airtime
- Confirm the selection.
- You will receive a notification confirming that you have successfully subscribed to the selected SMS Bundle.

**Via 544**

- Dial \*544#
- Reply with 98 for MORE
- Select SMS bundle with EXPIRY
- Choose a bundle of your choice or buy for another number.
- Confirm the selection.
- You will receive a notification confirming that you have successfully subscribed to the selected SMS Bundle.

**Via 456/100**

- Dial \*100# or \*456#
- Select Buy
- Select SMS bundle with EXPIRY
- Choose a bundle of your choice or buy for another number.
- Confirm the selection.
- You will receive a notification confirming that you have successfully subscribed to the selected SMS Bundle.

**Via Bonga \*126#**

- Select Redeem Bonga Points
- Select Free SMS
- Select the bonga points to redeem and the SMS bundle with Expiry
- Confirm the Redemption of Bonga Points.

# **How to Unsubscribe from the Daily Auto-Renewal**

- You will get confirmation for unsubscription

**Via 544**

- Select unsubscribe.
- Choose to unsubscribe from all

If a customer calls to request for deactivation from SMS More for Less;

This is a service that allows you to send Local SMSs at a discounted rate through purchase of SMS in bundles.

**Definition**

DIY (Do-It-Yourself) Architecture Solution is a modular, customer-driven approach to product design and offering. Instead of relying on pre-selected, fixed product propositions, customers can build their own solutions using a “shopping cart” model, selecting only the components and features that best meet their needs.

**Aim of DIY Architecture Solution**

**Unified Bill** \- Refers to a single, consolidated invoice or statement that reflects all the individual items or services selected by the customer. Without a unified bill, this could result in multiple invoices or unclear cost breakdowns—causing confusion and reducing satisfaction. A Unified Bill is a crucial enabler of DIY product composition. It aligns the flexibility of customer choice with the simplicity of a single, transparent billing experience.

**Synchronised Billing Cycle** \- Refers to aligning the billing dates of all customers selected products and services—especially when these include subscriptions or recurring charges—into a single, unified billing schedule. It eliminates this friction by aligning all billable components to a single date, making the experience cleaner, more predictable, and easier to manage

**Main Product**

These are a customer normal FTTH packages such as Bronze, Silver, Gold, Diamond and Platinum. They are also known as Vanilla.

**Add-on**

An **Add-on** is an optional service you can purchase on top of your active fibre plan. It’s billed separately but works seamlessly with your existing fibre account (an integrated proposition). Popular add-ons include **DStv and Family Share**. If you purchase an add-on **mid-cycle**, it will be **aligned to your main plan’s billing cycle** so everything renews together and stays easy to manage.

**Resource add-on**

These are Add-on that are resource based (e.g. GSM service Voice/ data i.e.

Family Share) which deplete based on usage.

**Rental add-on**

These are service that’s gain access to and they expire at the end of the cycle

(e.g. DSTV, insurance, smart cameras.

**Mechanics**

**Upgrades**

You can upgrade your main FTTH plan (Bronze, Silver, Gold, Diamond, or

Platinum) at any time, even in the middle of your billing cycle.

**Downgrades**

Downgrades are not allowed mid-cycle. You won’t be able to see or select plans below your current one due to our hierarchy rules, unless your plan is suspended because of non-payment. You can downgrade at the end of your current plan’s expiry period.

**Bulk plans**

Bulk plans also follow the same hierarchy rules. This means for instance, Bronze 1 month will be lower on the hierarchy compared to Bronze 3 months and so on.

**What happens if I change my main plan mid-cycle while I have an add-on?**

When you change your main FTTH (Vanilla) plan—Bronze, Silver, Gold, Diamond, or Platinum—mid-cycle, and you currently have an add-on, here’s how it works:

Proration for main plan is based on the remaining days in your billing cycle.

However, the add-ons are automatically unsubscribed and service terminates without proration. The customer is allowed to subscribe to the add-ons afresh at the beginning of the next payment cycle.

Add-ons are **not prorated** during a mid-cycle main plan change.

The customer needs to add add-ons again at end of cycle with a one-off to sync cycle with main.

**Can I purchase an add-on separately if I don’t have a Fibre account?**

No, you cannot. A customer can only purchase an add-on if they have an active Fibre account.  

**Will a customer be allowed to upgrade the main product if they have add-ons midcycle?**

Yes. A customer can upgrade the main product if they have an add-on. A customer pays a prorated amount for the new plan and gets a refund on the unutilized days of the existing/old plan.  

However, the add-ons are automatically unsubscribed and service terminates without proration. The customer is allowed to subscribe to the add-ons afresh at the beginning of the next payment cycle.

**Add-ons opt out**

A customer can opt out of the add-ons midcycle. When this happens, proration does not take place and service is terminated

**Deleting a product in CRM**

Products may be deleted from CRM for several reasons, including but not limited to:

If customer requests to suspend product.  

When customer pays/ activates the wrong product i.e .Bulk and meant to pay 1-month etc

When customer pays for the wrong account

Bulk product not allocated e.g. payments made on paybill

When Change product fails

**MPOS/Open Business Definition/Eligibility and Mechanics**

# **Definition**

Safaricom Stock Management App (MPOS/Open Business): Safaricom has partnered with Open Business to develop a Stock Management App that digitizes businesses and adds value on LNM accounts. (MPOS stands for Mobile Point of Sale)

The Stock Management app offers merchants a simple way to track their inventory, manage their cash flow and accept business payments.

The app is currently available on any Android enabled device with at least version 4.0 and above works. iOS and Windows versions will be enabled in later versions of the app.

# **Eligibility for the Stock Management App**

Any individual who runs a business can use the stock management solution to make payments (Till to Till, Till to Paybill, Till to Mobile Number) or accept payment via LNM from the app, the customer needs a registered and active Till or Paybill.

# **Registration Process**

Customers will be required to download the M-POS Application from Google Play Store or Safaricom App store.

Customers will be presented with registration options:

With Facebook

Google account

Manually by capturing their details

A code will be sent to the number used for registration, via SMS. Where the MSISDN is invalid, the code is highlighted with red, CEE will advise the merchant to change the mobile number registered by clicking change mobile number tab on the APP.

If the verification code will not be received and the number is correct and valid, CEE will advise the merchant to resend the code by clicking Resend Verification Code tab on the App.

Requests from retail and Call Centre CEE’s will be escalated via ticket to open business support, via Zen desk after trouble shooting is done and no resolution found.

The customer will choose a subscription plan depending on the number of employees and the preferred subscription duration. (The Subscription fees plans are attached).

For cases where the merchant has selected the wrong subscription plan, M-PESA Business CEE will raise a ticket on Zendesk for downgrade/upgrade

Retail and Call Centre CEE will advise the customer to call Zendesk on 0700826587

Payment options available are:

M-PESA -after selecting subscription plan, merchant will receive an MPESA alert to authorize the payment on their device.

Pay-Pal - The merchant will be required to accept to the terms of engagement/ terms and conditions at the point of sign up for them to use the service.

# **Benefits of Open Business Point of Sale - POS.**

Stock Management and Inventory tracking

Enables the LNM from a collection account to a transaction account enabling the merchant to pay salaries, suppliers (B2C’s), payment of utilities (Paybill) and other bulk accounts (B2B).

Multiple users with the merchant granted super user controls.

It provides expense and income accounting and thus produces periodic and annual management and Profit & Loss accounts, sales reports and a simple balance sheet

# **Key Features for the Stock Management App**

**Stock Management**

A module which allows for merchants to Add, Remove, Adjust Stock & products, set Stock reorder Levels and get stock summary reports

**Mobile POS system**

A module which allows for merchants to sell products through a simple to use mobile point of sale interface by accepting payments from different payment methods such as Lipa NA MPESA, Cash, Cheque, Debit Card.

It also allows merchants to generate receipts by connecting to Bluetooth printer, as well as get daily sales reports per shop or per cashier, P& L reports and more.

**Till to Till Payments**

The app allows merchants to make Buy Goods to Buy Goods transfers in few easy steps. This is best suited for supplier payments, for stock purchases.

**Till to Paybill Payments**

The app allows merchants to make Buy Goods to Buy Goods transfers in a few easy steps, best suited when making payments to utility companies such as Kenya Power, Nairobi Water etc.

**Till to Mobile Number Payments**

Directly form the app, merchants can transfer money from their till to any registered mobile number, either one by one or in bulk. This is suitable for paying staff salaries.

# **App Functionalities**

**Selling:** This is the landing page with the products catalogue and a report on the current sale for the day.

# **Shop Management**

**Shops** – A business owner can add more than one shop on the App

**Products** – Allows adding of the product catalogue

**Inventory** – Enables the business owner to update stock quantities and selling prices

**Transactions** – Gives business owner a report on all transactions done with filters for date, cashier and shops available.

**Expenses** - Enables the business owner to add recurring expenses. By adding these, the owner will be able to make periodic disbursements especially for utilities such as stock purchase, salaries, rent etc.

# **Relationship Management**

**Cashiers** - Enables business owner to add cashier

**Customers** - Enables the business owner to capture customer details. The information captured in this tab enables the owner to manage debtors and creditors

**Suppliers** - Enables the business owner to capture suppliers’ details

Employees - Enables the business owner to capture employee details. Information captured in this tab enables the owner to make periodic bulk salary disbursements and manage the employee’s profile.

# **Setting**

**Payment Methods** - allows the owner to select the payment methods they prefer to use for accepting payments from customers.

**Business Profile** - Allows the owner to update their account details

**Printer** - allows the owner to configure the application to a printer for generating receipts.

**Receipts** – Allows business owner to customize the receipts

**Account Renewals** - Enables the customer to make payments (either as first-time subscribers or renewals) through MPESA or PayPal

**Account Status** - Gives the owner visibility on the status of the account e.g. date subscribed, expiry date

**Reports:** Exposes the owner to a wide set of reports based on transactions done via the application

**Help:** Allows owner to view support documents and create tickets on any issue that needs assistance

**Legal:** Contains legal document for the owner

**Cash Box:** Allows the owner to view cash at hand and to withdraw, deposit and reconcile account functions.

The app has 5 subscription packages listed below, based on the number of users (cashiers) needed in the business.

However, upon registering onto the app, users get a free plan which limits them to a maximum of 2 products and 2 users, after which they will be prompted to subscribe to one of the packages.

| | | | | | | | | |

To upgrade, go to main menu,

select settings sub-menu,

Customer can upgrade or downgrade at any given time, with the top up amount factored in the total amount when upgrading, and the balance upon downgrading factored in to the next subscription payment.

Device is connected to the network and with enough resources.

articleTitle: Billing and Time-based billing for Data Bundle With Expiry
markdownContent:
# **BILLING**

- Billing depends on the sessions or applications the customer has opened, the customer could be accessing [www.nation.co.ke](http://www.nation.co.ke/) and also [www.standardmedia.co.ke](http://www.standardmedia.co.ke/) at the same time using different browser tabs.
- The billing of such will be twice even if the time stamps are same on Siebel.
- The out of bundle browsing rate is Ksh. **4.30/- per MB.**
- Multiple sessions may be charged separately so if the customer has 2 sessions running concurrently for example on Facebook and YouTube, both will be charged separately.

**Buying bundles from M-PESA while having an Okoa Jahazi debt****.**

**Enough funds in M-PESA**

- Customer will be prompted of the expected Okoa Jahazi repayment in own number and can choose to either accept or cancel the data purchase transaction.
- Okoa Jahazi will be repaid and the requested bundle purchased successfully.

**Insufficient funds in M-PESA**

The M-PESA amount available will be used to repay Okoa Jahazi, and balance if any topped up as airtime.

This rule will apply only when buying data bundle for own number, using M-PESA.

# **Buying for another number**

The beneficiary will receive the exact amount of data bundle purchased for them.

The sponsor and the beneficiary will both receive the success SMS notification upon a successful purchase.

If Party A has an outstanding Okoa debt and attempts to buy bundle for another number (party B).

- The Sponsor (person purchasing for other) must clear the outstanding ETU debt first.
- A breakdown is presented showing the debt and the bundle amount.
- The customer should give consent on whether to proceed or not.
- If response is yes, both the ETU and bundle amount are deducted from MPESA account.
- The beneficiary receives the exact amount of data bundle purchased for them.
- If consent is not given, the request is cancelled.

# **Bundle Recovery:**

Customer will not be able to recover their unused bundle if the bundle expires. The customers will receive a notification before expiry informing them of the bundle amount. Any unused bundles will be lost after expiry of validity.

# **TIME BASED DATA BILLING**

- This is a method of data billing based on time spent on the internet as opposed to being charged based on volume of the data spent.
- Charges are Ksh 2/- per minute billed per second regardless of the volume of data downloaded.
- Multiple sessions may be charged separately so if the customer has 2 sessions running concurrently for example on Facebook and YouTube for 20min the customer may be charged more than Ksh40 at the end of the session.
- Upon purchase of bundles, you will need to restart the browsing session for the billing to change from Browse@ 2/- tariff (Time based data billing) to billing on data bundles.
- If you do not restart the session you continue to be billed on Time Based Data Tariff

# **Time based data billing terms and mechanics**

- This service is only applicable to Prepay subscribers.
- Active data bundles will have to be consumed first until they are exhausted or expired before you can use per minute billing.
- This Tariff is not applicable to roaming subscribers.
- Charging is per second billing for the duration over which you have an active internet connection.
- Once you disconnect from the internet you stop being charged.
- It’s important to disconnect your mobile phone or modem from the internet while you aren’t browsing to ensure you don’t continue to be charged.
- The service works even when one subscribes to My Data Manager, hence, to avoid Out-of-Bundle Billing, one must unsubscribe from the Time Based, for My Data Manager to work.
- You can purchase data bundles. But you must restart the browsing session for the billing to change from Time based to Volume based data billing

articleTitle: Huawei Router Manual Provisioning Guide and escalations of failed installation.
markdownContent:
# **Definition**

Provisioning is the configuration authenticating the router to the network, for internet access through backend integration to the FTTH infrastructure.

This can be done either through the automated design or manually, where failure occurs.

Automated provisioning is a service that ensures that all new customers will automatically be activated and receive username and password on completion of installation.

Manual provisioning will apply where due to failure Fixed Customer support intervene and manual action required to activate the customer.

Upon successful installation and activation, service will automatically activate on CBS.  

In-case of a failure, SRs are automatically created. The SRs for failed provisioning is assigned to Fixed Customer support team.

When a customer calls us, the CEE will need to confirm the following before raising an SR.

- If the router is powered ON and all the lights are normal (Normal lights should be green in color).
- If the router has LOS, if so, the customer needs to confirm if the patch code is properly connected from the ATB to the router.
- If the customer confirms cabling to be okay and the router still has LOS, the CEE shall raise an FTTH incident on BMC for the technicians to clear LOS for the SN to be discoverable. The CEE will share the Incident number via SMS and advise SLA of 24 hours.
- If the above are confirmed to be okay (no LOS and cables are properly connected), the CEE will escalate the SR in progress to HomeCustomerManagement@Safaricom.co.ke. SLA is 2 hours.
- Home Customer support will provision the link, map CI to the correct router, map the MAC address using AAA tool, close the SR to trigger product allocation and confirm service is up.

For escalation from L400 to home tech dispatch,

For a dispatch for a pending connection or unresolved issues, all tickets raised between 8 am to 6pm, will be actioned within 24 hrs and customer engaged within 2 Hrs of customer request for scheduling customer visit.

For tickets raised after 6pm, customers will be contacted by 10 am of the following day for scheduling customer visit, and resolved within 24 Hrs.

The automatic provisioning may fail due to below reasons: -

Power failure.

Loose cabling.

Lack of signal after installation (LOS)

Faulty device.

Wrong SN No. (i.e. Router serial no) while closing CRQ.

Poor power levels (i.e should be between -7 to -25dmb)

L400 CEE will trouble shoot to identify root cause i.e. Incomplete installation, loose cabling, or power failure. Etc.

Line 400 CEE will confirm with customer if they have a red light on the router. Where after trouble shooting CEE identifies issue as loose cabling or power failure, CEE will advise customer accordingly and assist resolve.

For loose cabling CEE will advise customer to confirm the connection socket (ATB – Access Terminal Box) is intact i.e. connected to the router.

Fixed Customer support will provision the link on U2000 using the details on SR, map CI to the correct router MAC address using AAA tool, close the SR to trigger product allocation and confirm service is up.

For power failure customer will be advised to call back when they have power.

Fixed Customer support will provision on U2000 using the details on autogenerated SR, map CI to the correct router MAC address using AAA tool, close SR to trigger product allocation and confirm service is up, where power resumes.

Fixed Customer support will manually allocate the product in cases where the product has not auto allocated depending on amount on IN and customers request, on Siebel CRM provisioning tab.

Fixed Customer support will send customer login credentials, advise them accordingly and confirm service is up.

CEE will advise on DIY alternatives to change the logging details either via USSD \*400#ok, default IP at the back of the router or on Safaricom App.

Where global outage is noted, Home Customer Support will advise customer on the global issue being attended to by SOC.

The central dispatch/SOC team will allocate the incident to the contractor through remedy.

Once resolved the central dispatch team will be advised by the technical team (contractor) to manually provision the customer, this will then be escalated to Home Customer Support who will provision the link, map the MAC address, close the SR to allocate product and confirm service is up.

Where faulty device is reported / identified, L400 CEE will assist customer trouble shoot to establish failure i.e., router not powering ON, faulty antennae etc.

1. CEE will raise a remedy ticket where failure is identified.
2. CEE will share the Incident number via SMS and advise SLA of 24 hours.
3. The central dispatch team will allocate the incident to the contractor through remedy.
4. Once resolved the central dispatch team will be advised by the technical team (contractor) to manually provision the customer and confirm service is up and will close the ticket.
5. The contractor will indicate the serial number on the incident and / or CRQ.

Where CEE confirms there’s no service and not related to refund, payment, power failure/level and or loose cabling ,or LOS, and such unable to resolve customer issue. L400 CEE will raise a **SR to** **Fixed Customer support** .

The **SR category I FTTH,TYPE:** **FTTH - Connection Failure, ITEM: Cannot Push Traffic, SLA 24 Hrs.**

CEE will share the SR number to the client via SMS.

**NB:** Where a customer calls for logins (SSID and Password) after the installation is done, the CEE will confirm if the router has been provisioned or not. The CEE will check if there’s an SR on CRM and if there none, they will query the CI on the Sales portal to get the CRQ which they will use to check on BMC if the ticket has been closed or not. If the ticket has not been closed, the CEE will escalate via email to HomeTechDispatch@Safaricom.co.ke requesting them to close the ticket to trigger provisioning. SLA is within 2 hours.

**Above Huawei provisioning process applies to Nokia provisioning.**

markdownContent:
# **Definition**

Retail QUEUE Management system (eQMS) is a floor management solution that captures the customer journey from their point of entry at the Safaricom shops to their point of exit from the same outlets.

# **Eligibility**

Retail QUEUE Management system (eQMS) is eligible to all customers who visit any Safaricom Retail shop.

Agent will use windows credentials to access the eQMS console System

# **Benefit of the new eQMS over the current one**

1. Users’ experience- pleasant user interface, simple clear customer journeys & system’s ease of use.
2. Near equal distribution of workload among the agents working on any shift/time
3. Real time reports on shop performance
4. Well managed breaks resulting in higher occupancy of agents to serve the customers
5. Additional capabilities - Print of Ticket & SMS option for customers

## **Access**

## Customer will receive an SMS notification (in case they have their line) and a printout of the ticket.

- The ticket will also be displayed on the screen
- They will be auto allocated to the agent on FIFO basis
- The floor marshal will assist in guiding the customers accordingly
- As an agent**,** you will use your windows credentials to access the eQMS console. Once logged in, you will be on ‘**Not Ready’** status.
- Customers will start being auto allocated to you as soon as you click on ‘**I am ready’** button at the start of your shift.
- eQMS customer console will not be logged in every morning only the initial log in will be required. After that, it auto resets every midnight and customers will find the Karibu/Welcome screen ready for use.

# **Mechanics**

- **I**f an agent does not locate the customer for them to proceed to ‘start ticket’ the ticket will go into suspended status in 60 sec and the agent will be auto-allocated the next customer
- Where a customer shows up within 30 mins, the manager will re-queue the ticket top of list to allow them to be served.
- In case the customer shows up after 30 mins, they will be required to pick a new ticket.
- If customer’s Welcome SMS is not delivered but ticket is generated, Floor Marshal will guide the customer to the next available agent once it’s their turn to be served; as displayed on the screen.
- If the ticket is processed but fails to print, while an SMS has been generated, Floor marshal apologizes to the affected customer and guides them to the next available agent once they are called.
- In the event both Ticket and Welcome SMS fails, Floor marshal will apologize to the affected customer and manually guides customers to the queue via FIFO
- As soon as Agent has finished serving a customer can take a break by engaging the ‘not ready’ button after ‘start ticket’ for the current customer you are serving so that you are not auto-allocated the next one.

## **Escalation**

1. Floor Marshal will Escalate to technical team – IT Service Centre via BMC Remedy (Report an incident for QMS); OR call 3333 IT Helpdesk citing the BMC ticket, on below scenarios.

1. Unresponsive eQMS console
2. If customer is not able to select a service
3. If the ticket is processed but fails to print, while an SMS has been generated
4. Customer’s phone number keypad fails to pop up
5. In the event both Ticket and Welcome SMS fails

2. Floor marshal will also inform agents on the floor of the failure via email citing the BMC ticket.

# **How to Check B2C product for a short code on M-PESA G2**

1. Query the organization short code on M-PESA G2 system
2. Go to Products tab and view the assigned product
3. The product name is B2C product

# **How to deposit funds into the short code to make payments**

# **RTGS transfer:**

To M-PESA holding account at NCBA and KCB banks, quoting their B2C short code preceded by 333 as the beneficiary account number. E.g. 333123456

# **Cash, EFT and Cheque**

Deposits can be made to the same M-PESA holding account using A/C number 0420448007 or 6518870012 for NCBA Bank or 1147921954 for KCB Bank. The Client should quote the B2C short code when making this deposit.

articleTitle: Lipa Karo and Lipa Kodi na M-PESA Mechanics
markdownContent:
**Lipa Karo and Lipa Kodi na M-PESA Mechanics**

# **Lipa Karo na** **M-PESA**

It is a M- PESA pay bill service for school fees collection.

Upon signing up, a school is issued with an M-PESA business number.

There are also School fees accounts that are operated by Kenya Commercial Bank and PesaPal.

Kenya Commercial Bank offers the service to several schools who bank with them.

PesaPal is a provider of school’s management information systems.

PesaPal for schools is built on a simple Web-based interface that enables any school to receive and track payments for special activities such as school trips, activity fees, fund raisers etc.

# **How It Works**

Customers will have to confirm with their school administrators whether their school or the nearest Kenya Commercial Bank, Co-operative Bank and CFC Stanbic bank branch for more information and to get the right code of the school or student a customer can:

For KCB Lipa Karo a customer needs to get in touch with their school or the nearest KCB branch.

For schools managing their own Pay Bill accounts a customer need to get in touch with the accounts or administrative office to confirm what their school business number is and how the student is identified.

For Pesapal Lipa karo a customer needs to get in touch with Pesapal or their school.

Dial \*234# and, select M-PESA Information, Select Business numbers, enter school name as the key word and follow instructions to get the business number.

Fee Payment confirmation

M-PESA will send the standard Pay Bill confirmation text (SMS) immediately after carrying out the transaction. This notification will confirm that funds have been transferred to the bank.

The bank will then send a text (SMS) to the customer, notifying them that funds have been applied to the school’s bank account.

Parents whose schools have Pesapal school management software can view their payments via web free of charge on the website [www.pesapal.com](http://www.pesapal.com/)

# **Lipa Karo na M-PESA Payments**

# **Payment via KCB Lipa Karo service**

On the mobile phone, go to the M-PESA Menu and select Pay Bill.

In the Business Number field enter 522123.

In the account number, enter school code as provided by KCB, then a K followed by student admission number without leaving a space: {School code} {K}{Student admin no.}, e.g., 123KTK123

**NOTE:** School code is for identifying the school and students will be advised by KCB or the school.

Enter required amount and input M-PESA PIN.

Confirm the transaction.

Customer will receive a confirmation message from M-PESA and another confirmation from KCB once money is credited to the school’s account.

# **Payment via school based Lipa Karo service**

On the mobile phone, go to the M-PESA menu and select Pay Bill.

In the Business Number field enter school’s Pay Bill Number. NOTE: The school the customer intends to pay to must be registered to this service.

For Account Number, enter student’s identification as advised by the school.

Enter required amount and input M-PESA PIN.

Confirm the transaction.

Customer will receive a confirmation message from M-PESA that payment has been made to the school’s Pay Bill account.

# **Payment via PesaPal Lipa Karo service**

PesaPal for Schools is an easy to use service developed to enable schools to request and manage school fees payments from parents.

With PesaPal for Schools, a school enrolls parents and students once and then the school can post payment requests to the parents automatically.

For each payment, PesaPal for Schools sends out a notification via SMS or email to parents and also automates repetitive tasks such as “account overdue” reminders freeing administrative staff to work on other tasks.

The PesaPal Business number: **220123**

# **Lipa Kodi na M-PESA Mechanics**

This is a normal Customer to Business Paybill and therefore it allows housing agents, commercial real estate businesses and landlords to collect rent via the M-PESA PayBill service from their tenants.

# **How It Works**

The housing agencies/landlord/real estate businesses must have an active Paybill Number for the service to work.

The housing agencies/landlord/real estate businesses will display or share their respective Paybill number(s) with their tenants.

The tenants will use the current M-PESA Paybill payment process to make the payments.

markdownContent:
# Automated Individual Business Till Application process

**M-PESA Business Till**

The **M-PESA Business till** is an enhancement of the existing Buy Goods Till that enables business owners to collect payments on the till and use the money collected to make other transactions directly from their till such as:

- Pay to a mobile number.
- Pay to another Buy Goods Till.
- Pay to a utility (Paybill) till.
- Withdraw funds:
 1. To owners nominated number.
 2. At M-PESA agent.
 3. To bank.
- Sell Airtime and earn commission.

**How to apply for a Business Till**

- Log in to the portal - [**Lipa Na M-PESA Application Portal (m-pesaforbusiness.co.ke)**](https://m-pesaforbusiness.co.ke/apply) and click on “Apply Now’ menu and select the product to apply for. You will then be required to select the business type to proceed with the application.

articleTitle: Definitions, Features and Mechanics of Safaricom Msurvey
markdownContent:
# **DEFINITION**

a) This is a message-based survey supported or offered by Safaricom to businesses.

b) It allows businesses to get real-time feedback and insights from their customers when they pay with Lipa Na M-PESA

c)The survey is based on the Net Promoter Score (NPS).

# **ELIGIBILITY**

It is eligible to businesses that use Lipa Na MPESA as a customer mode of payment.

# **NET PROMOTER SCORE (NPS)**

a) NPS is an index ranging from 0 to 10 that measures the willingness of customers to recommend a company’s products or services to others.

b) It is used to gauge the customer’s overall satisfaction with a company’s product or service and the customer’s loyalty to the brand.

# **BUSINESS BENEFITS**

1. Real-time customer feedback on product/service - as the merchant, you will be given access to a web portal where you can view your NPS score anytime and be able to generate simple reports.
2. You will also be able to view the customers’ verbatim.
3. Speed and accuracy of data collection – customer engagement is done immediately after purchase of goods or services hence feedback is authentic and received instantly to allow businesses to resolve issues in a timely manner.
4. Ability to reach large number of customers quickly.
5. Value for money.

# **SAFARICOM mSurvey COST**

1. Safaricom mSurvey will be offered in 7 different bundles as shown below.
2. Merchants can subscribe for any of the bundles on a monthly, quarterly or annual basis.

| BUNDLES AVAILABLE | NO. OF CUSTOMERS PER TILL | BUNDLE PRICE INCLUSIVE OF 16% VAT + 10% EXCISE DUTY (KSHS.) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Bundle 1 | 40 | 630 |
| Bundle 2 | 150 | 1890 |
| Bundle 3 | 350 | 3780 |
| Bundle 4 | 600 | 6300 |
| Bundle 5 | 1500 | 12600 |
| Bundle 6 | 3000 | 18900 |
| Bundle 7 | 5000 | 25200 |

# **HOW NPS IS CALCULATED.**

NPS is calculated by subtracting the percentage of detractors from the percentage of promoters.

# **HOW TO SIGN UP**

1. The sales representative or account relationship manager will share the client application form and contract.
2. Once filled, the client will send the documents to msurvey@safaricom.co.ke for processing.

# **HOW IT WORKS**

1. When a customer makes a payment using Lipa Na M-PESA, they receive a message to opt in where they have an option to accept or decline participating in the survey.
2. After accepting to participate, the customer will then receive an SMS on their mobile phone asking them to rate the service they have just received.
3. They will then receive another message asking them to give a reason for the rating they have just given the service.
4. **Error! Filename not specified.** 
 The customer will not be charged for the responses that they give to the survey questions (customer message responses are free).

**Note;** A customer can only receive one survey request in a month per business and can only receive 3 surveys from 3 different businesses within a calendar month.

articleTitle: Variable Routing and Forwarding definition and mechanics
markdownContent:
# Definition

VRF stands for Variable Routing and Forwarding or VPN (Virtual Private Network). VRF is a technology included in IP network routers that allows multiple instances of a routing table to exist in a router and work simultaneously.

# VRF mechanics

1. ISP’s (Internet Service Provider) create virtual private networks (VPNs) for each client MPLS **(****Multiprotocol Label Switching**) VPN and then the PE (Provider Edge) router will have multiple virtual routing tables.

2. This implies that an ISP can keep its customers separate (on virtual networks) on a common infrastructure.

3. VRF acts like a logical router, but while a logical router may include many routing tables, a VRF instance uses only a single routing table to forward traffic securely and separately through each VRF (MPLS VPN).

4. The MPLS VPNs are routed totally unaware of other MPLS VPNs being routed and thinks they are the only VPN instances on the router.

5. The beauty of this is that it enables ISPS’s to allocate duplicate IP’s to different customers without causing IP conflict.

6. If you notice a client using 'another' client’s IP, it should raise no alarm. Our MPLS address space is 172.30.x.x

**Subscriber Registration Definition and Mechanics**

#  **Definition**

Subscriber registration is the process of Safaricom subscribers who acquire new lines, registering their identification information in our system which is also merged with the Government system IPRS.

**NOTE:** Subscriber registration confirmation /customer consent for additional line requests

Service allows Safaricom customer(s) to accept or cancel registration of an additional number on their ID details.

The solution alerts users of new registration on their primary number via an SMS when being registered, either on USSD or on the subreg app.

Existing registration will apply, agent will register customer and enter customer details as applicable.

The system will then perform predetermined checks as per outlined matrix, i.e. confirm the number under the customer ID which is the most active on the network or M-PESA etc.

The number will be sent the consent notification. Where customer consents, the registrations are confirmed. And registration is cancelled, where customer declines and customer and agent notified.

Where SMS notification is not received on the primary number, the system will perform vicinity checks. Where customer primary line and agent are within 10KM’s the registration will be allowed and will declined where distance is above 10 KM’s.

Where SMS is not delivered to the primary number or if the primary number has been inactive for more than 24hrs, the registration will be allowed.

# **Subscriber Registration App and features**

Agent login credentials are only applicable to their phone number and they are accountable for it.

Enter your mobile number or email address to which the password shall be sent.

Click on the submit button and check your messages/inbox for a new password.

Retrieve the new password and proceed with login.

To validate a minor’s registration turning 18 in 2 months, he/she will have 90 days to provide their national ID, if he/she fails to do so their line will be barred.

Agent SIM card not allowed error when trying to login; this error message is displayed when an agent uses a SIM card whose IMSI is not white listed or is not a Safaricom SIM card.

Ensure the SIM card in the device is a safaricom registered SIM card

Ensure the SIM card is whitelisted to log in to the App.

Agents cannot log in to the subscriber registration app App using WIFI. The app can only be accessed using Safaricom mobile data and the GPS must be turned to log in to the App

User training will enable the user to recognize a valid birth certificate and the guardian ID details are also registered.

The app is optimized for the Huawei phone and the IMEI is white listed against the user account.

The app requires a data connection to login, however if the data connection is lost in the middle of a registration the customer details will be sent via SMS.

Registration App data usage is zero rated, but data has to be ON for the request to be submitted.

Registration for people who cannot uncover themselves (according to their religion); the customer should be referred to an agent of the same religion and gender to register them. Where possible let the customer be shown a private area and politely requested to display their face.

In case of expired passports used during registration, Safaricom will notify subscribers whose passports are about to expire to register with a renewed passport other valid document.

Agents cannot login using the same device but on different credentials. The app only allows one login at a time. One agent would need to log out for the other to login.

Solution for agent refusing to surrender device to the dealer/agent; If the agent no longer works for an agent or dealer, the dealer/agent should report the same via email to their support teams for the agent’s account to be deactivated That account will not be usable

‘No response found’ error when trying to log in is displayed when the Application does not successfully communicate with the systems hence there is no response from the server:

Try checking your connection or

Contact support when the issue persists

Delay in getting success or failure message; it takes about 5 minutes for the response message to come back.

Where the ID DOB reads 00.00. YEAR – The agent will input 01.01. YEAR

Where the ID DOB reads YEAR ONLY – The agent will input 31.12. YEAR

SIM Maximum number of lines that can be registered with same ID

A dealer can handle registration of up to 5 lines.

For >5 the customer will be referred to the nearest retail shop.

# **Subscriber Registration overview**

Safaricom retail shops.

Safaricom care desks.

Authorized franchise shops.

Authorized dealers.

Authorized M-PESA agents.

The Safaricom Jiandikishe App, applicable for both partners and Safaricom shop/care desk outlets.

The Jiandikishe web system, only applicable at Safaricom Retail outlets.

Corporate registration web portal, only applicable at Safaricom Retail outlets.
