# **DIY procedures for LNM Statements.**

**Definition**

This is a Do-It-Yourself automated process where merchant can access their stamped M-PESA statements up to 2 years on demand. The service is currently under the M-PESA Business Till Product accessible via \*234 # USSD. No registration will be required.

# **How to access Full Merchant M-PESA Statements**

Merchants can access their statements for the last **24 hours**, **3 months, 6 months**, **12 months, 2 years,** or a **specific period** using the following easy steps:

Accessing Full Merchant M-PESA Statement:

• Dial \*234# from the nominated number.

• Then select option 2 – M-PESA Business Till.

• Then enter your head office number or store number

• Select option 6 – M-PESA Statements

• Below partner statements select option 1 - Full Statement

• Select the statement period.

• Enter Email address- confirm email address.

• Enter operator id.

• Enter operator pin.

The merchant will receive a flash notification that the request for M-PESA statement has been received and is being processed.

Upon successful completion, merchant will receive an SMS confirmation that the full statement has been sent to their email. Which will also contain a **6-digit code to open the statement**.

\*The code is only valid for the statement that has been generated on email for that specific time.

**N/B:** To open your M-PESA statements use the digit code sent via SMS. The merchant is limited to 5 requests per day.

# **Full statements for a specific period (range within 30days)**

• Dial \*234# from the nominated number.

• Then select option 2 – M-PESA Business Till.

• Enter your head office number or store number.

• Select option 6 - M-PESA Statements.

• Below partner statements select option 1 – Full Statements.

• Below full statements select option 5 - Specific period statement.

• Enter the period range in the required format beginning with: “Date from – Date to” in the format: DDMMYYYY.

• Confirm the period specified by selecting option 1 – Confirm.

• Enter Email address- confirm email address.

• Enter operator id.

• Enter operator pin.

You will receive a flash notification that your request for M-PESA statement has been received and is being processed.

Upon successful completion, you will receive an SMS confirmation that your full statement has been sent to your email. Which will also contain a **6-digit code to open the statement**.

# **STATEMENT FOR MPESA PARTNERS (Buy Goods and short term Paybill)**

M-PESA Partners will use their nominated numbers and follow the registration process below:

 Dial \*234# and select Merchant Services.

- Select Merchant statement.
- Enter Paybill Number.
- Enter Document of registration Number (ID or Passport).
- Enter and confirm the Email address.
- Select the period.
- Confirm the registration details. (ID/Passport number, Email Address, Period of statement to be received, Paybill number) and select ‘Accept’ or ‘Decline’.
- Log into the email address registered to receive statement and verify the validity of your Email address.
- A confirmation text is sent to your phone, confirming a successful registration process.

**Statement Requests Via Email.**

 **Merchant Buy-goods and Pay-bill partner Requests.**

1. LNM account types include the following, and the merchants/pay-bill partner can request for one or all the account statements.

- MMF/Working Account.
- Charges Paid account.
- Merchant/utility account.
- Organization settlement account.

2. Customer can request for their statements via:

- M-PESA Business M-PESABusiness@safaricom.co.ke or Lipa na MPESA Lipanampesa@Safaricom.co.ke
- Retail shop / care desks.
- Account Managers.
- DIY where applicable.

3. Lipa na M-PESA Partners on Transacting Till (Independent, Small and Medium merchant products), can request their statements (maximum 2yrs) via \*234\*2# using their nominated number. This is done on demand, and the partner keys in the Email address to which the statement is supposed to be send. Once the statement is sent, the nominated number receives a code via text, to use to open it.
4. Statement will be generated from the available retrieval systems based on the date of transactions i.e.

- M-PESA Statements Portal ([https://mpesastatements.safaricom.net/](https://mpesastatements.safaricom.net/) ) – archived transactions i.e. From 2015 to date.
- If the statement portal is not responsive, raise a remedy ticket for FSS support team to assist.
- If the statements are too bulky, you can split the duration into a lesser duration or search period. If too bulky for shorter periods, raise a BMC ticket for FSS Support to assist.

5. EBU CARE teams will generate the statements as per customer request and will send via email within 2 Hours to the requesting email address once verified.
6. If requested on call, confirm the merchant is acquired by Safaricom. Once this is validated will proceed to export the statement as per request from merchants/Partners after effective vetting. Vetting Details are: -

- Organization name.
- Store or merchant Till number or pay-bill number.
- Organization finance details on G2.

7. Relevant teams will export the statements from M-PESA Statements Portal.
8. Requests for standalone organizations should be done by the organization finance contact/Nominated number or any active operators on G2. Where Till statement request for a standalone organization is done at retail, the finance contact will present original ID and where their details are available on M-PESA G2, they will be vetted using their ID.
9. Request for unmasked statements will be done through retail and law enforcement office (e.g., court order).
10. Aggregated merchants will contact their aggregator to issue the statements.

**Point to Note:**

**Due to data protection:**

- Statements should only be sent to the Organization’s official email address, Finance Contact email address or any of the active users as created on G2.
- Do not send to any other email address even if the request comes from the same Domain.
- Do not send to a user whose account is Dormant, except the Admin.
- Do not tell the requester what the registered official Email address is, not unless they mention it for you to confirm.
- If a dormant user requests, tell him his account on G2 is dormant and he needs to engage the admin to activate it first, then request again.
- Alternatively, he should request from the organization’s official email address as per G2.
- Advise on DIY.
- If a merchant/partner does not indicate the duration of the statement, the agent should share six months statements.
- If a merchant/partner does not indicate the account for the statement, send Utility account for Pay-bills and Merchant account for Buy-goods.

# **Definition**

2. The Service provides useful information on preparedness and management of emergencies and disasters.
3. The M-SALAMA Platform is an SMS based solution that disseminates information on Emergencies and Disasters.
4. An emergency is a serious, unexpected, and often dangerous situation requiring immediate action.
5. A disaster is a sudden event, such as an accident or a natural catastrophe, which causes great damage to property or loss of life.

# **Eligibility**

1. The Service is available to both post and prepaid subscribers on Safaricom’s network.

Everyone can be affected by emergencies or disasters. It is important to get accurate information to occurring events and be prepared in order to reduce the risks associated with disasters such as loss of life, injury or property damage.

articleTitle: Definition, Charges and KYC Requirements of Pay bill
markdownContent:
**Definition, Charges and KYC Requirements of Paybill**

# **Definition of Paybill**

Paybill is a cash collection service that allows an organization to collect money regularly from their customers through M-PESA.

Pay Bill service is for non-face-to-face C2B payments.

This is an M-PESA mode of collecting funds.

Payments are customer-initiated, and the receiving organization may have a unique identifier i.e. account number.

# **Paybill Tariff /Charges and KYC Requirements**

**Paybill Charges**

A customer can confirm Paybill charges via USSD: Dial \*234#ok, select M-PESA Information, Select Tariff Query, Select Lipa Na M-PESA, Enter Paybill number then Enter the amount and send.

The first three (3) M-PESA kadogo transactions (Kshs100 and below) are free per day. Customers will be charged from the 4th kadogo transaction onwards.

**Paybill Tariff**

M-PESA Paybill tariffs vary per organization and the services being offered by the receiving organization.

Short-term pay bills are always set on the Standard Business Bouquet Tariff. Business Bouquet Tariff - No charges to the business; customer bears all charges.

# **BUSINESS TARIFF - C2B Tariff**

**Standard Tariff**

**Mgao Tariff:** Split charges between customer and business

**Business Bouquet Tariff:** No charges to the business; customer bears all charges.

**Customer Bouquet Tariff:** No charges to the customers; business bears all charges.

**Banking Tariff**

**Fedha Bouquet Tariff:** No charges to the business; the customer bears all charges.

**Fedha Mgao Tariff:** Split charges between customer and business

**Hazina Tariff:** Split charges between customer and business

**Gaming Tariff**

**Gaming Mgao Tariff:** Split charges between customer and business

**Gaming Business Bouquet Tarif:** No charges to the business; the customer bears all charges.

**Gaming Customer Bouquet Tarif**: No charges to the customers; the business bears all charges.

**M-AKIBA Tariff:** No charges to the business; the customer bears all charges.

**Special Tariffs**

**Charity Sweepstake tariff:** No charges to the customers; business bears all charges at 8.16%.

**Lottery Tariff:** No charges to the business; customer bears all charges at 25.50%.

**Fuel Card Tariff:** Split charges between customer and business.

**KPLC Tariff:** Split charges between customer and business.

**MFS Tarif:** Split charges between customer and business.

**CSR Tariffs**

CSR Tariff 1: No charges to the business; the customer bears all charges.

CSR Tariff 2: Split charges between customer and business.

**Fintech Paybill Tariff** – M-PESA Wallet C2B Targeted Tariff:

Fintech Mgao Tariff: Split charges between customer and business.

Fintech Business Bouquet Tariff: No charges to the business; customer bears all charges.

Fintech Customer Bouquet Tariff: No charges to the customers; business bears all charges

# **Accessing Paybill Application Forms**

The Safaricom retail shops/care desks

From the Safaricom Sales Teams

The Safaricom corporate website i.e., [https://www.safaricom.co.ke/personal/m-pesa/lipa-na-m-pesa/paybill](https://www.safaricom.co.ke/personal/m-pesa/lipa-na-m-pesa/paybill)

Through email request sent to M-PESABusiness@Safaricom.co.ke

 2. This product can only be accessed from the Safaricom Home Application.

# **Contents covered and not covered by jubilee home insurance**

### **A)** **Contents covered**

#### **Home content**

1. 1. All contents in the house e.g. furniture, fixtures, fittings, clothing, cutlery, crockery, kitchen equipment, entertainment equipment, refrigerators & televisions.
 2. Customer is however only covered within the limit of your package.

#### **All risk items.**

1. Jewelry – subject to maximum of 10% of the total value of ALL RISKS sum insured
2. Laptops & computers, cameras, wrist watches, mobile phones and all other portable electronic items.

articleTitle: Retail/Care desk action points and Fraud Key Comments
markdownContent:
# **Retail/Care desk action points.**

Vet the customer as per retail vetting procedure, Resume and swap line in CRM.

Resume/Un-suspend in G2 and assist the customer to reactivate the M-PESA account.

**Remove the key comment on CRM**

# **F****raud Key Comments actions required by Retail/Care Desk CEE**

### **Fraud: SMS Spamming and possible spammer.**

**Key Comment:**

SMS Spamming - Sub to visit Retail Centre for vetting and unbarring.

# **Action Required Retail CEE**

The CEE should vet the customer as per process and confirm the following: -

Check if the line was calling/sending messages in sequence,

check if there was a swap on the customer line,

Confirm if the customer requested for the swap or was it a fraudulent swap. If swap was fraudulent, vet the customer and unbar line on HLR.

If there was no swap/ was not fraudulent have the customer explain the calls/messages and share with Network fraud via NetworkFraud&M-pesasection@safaricom.co.ke to guide.

If the customer fails vetting the normal process should follow.

# **Fraud: Mulot Spammer**

**Key Comment:** Mulot Spamming - Sub to visit Retail Centre for vetting and unbarring.

**Action Required Retail CEE**

CEE should vet customer as per process and confirm the following: -

1. Check if the line was calling/sending messages in sequence
2. Check if there was a swap on the customer line,
3. Confirm if the customer requested for the swap or was it a fraudulent swap? If swap was fraudulent, vet the customer and unbar line on HLR.
4. If there was no swap/ was not fraudulent have the customer explain the calls/messages and share with Network fraud via NetworkFraud&M-pesasection@safaricom.co.ke to guide.
5. If the calls/messages are not in sequence, get an explanation from the customer for the activity, if satisfactory vet customer as per process and unbar line.
6. If the customer fails vetting the normal process should follow.

**Fraud: Irregular Registration > 5 lines per ID.**

This is where customer has already 5 lines registered under their ID; therefore, any additional line can only be done at our Retail Shop not at an Agent.

**Key Comment:**

Irregular line registrations. Sub to visit Retail Centre for vetting and unbarring

**Action Required Retail CEE**

Vet customer let the customer confirm how many lines they have.

Block all other lines not belonging to the customer.

Remove key comment and unblock the line

**Do not inform the customer how many lines are registered on their ID. Let the customer confirm his known lines and block the others.**

### **Fraud: Irregular Registrations – Bulk**

This is a case where the Agent is doing numerous registrations.

**Key Comment:**

In case of customer line - Sub to visit Retail Centre for vetting and unbarring

For the agent. Use \*195\*4# for future registrations

**Action Required Retail CEE**

For Customer Vet customer, let the customer confirm how many lines they have.

Block all other lines not belonging to the customer.

Remove key comment and unblock the line.

For Agent, CEE to advise as per key comment.

### **Fraud: 234 Fraud – Customer**

These are the frauds where agents are called and social engineered to send funds to third parties without their knowledge.

**Key Comment:**

Suspicious Deposit Transactions - Customer to visit Retail Centre for transaction verification

**Action Required Retail CEE**

Check on the last M-PESA Agent deposit and call the depositing agent to confirm if they authorized the transaction. If so, unbar the customer line on HLR. If not, reverse the funds back to the agent.

SAAS (Software as a Service) refers to software or applications that can be delivered over the Internet and on-demand to users whenever they need it. These applications are also highly customizable, so they are tailored to each company’s unique requirements.

SAAS is when users “rent” or borrow online software instead of purchasing and Installing it on their own computers.

# **Storage as a Service (SAAS) in Cloud Computing**

1. Information Storage as a Service enables users to store data online and access it remotely over the Internet. This is executed through the web browser, or as a network drive, and the service comes in multiples of storage units.
2. The key benefits of this are to offer the customers access-anywhere data for their employees. This will support remote working and greater flexibility in terms of using multiple devices or locations.

**Service Offer**

1. The Managed Storage Service offered by Safaricom is based upon leading edge technologies and is offered on a usage basis. The utility approach removes the large capital requirements for Safaricom customers. This approach to storage enables customers to access state of the art storage management and have the benefits of Storage Area Network (SAN) management for a fraction of the costs of dedicated external storage.
2. The SAN architecture allows customers to acquire scalable disk space, while for the amount they use in 20 GB units. A comparison of typical DAS to SAN pricing shows a 33% saving with the Safaricom Storage Area Network Solution.
3. You can use cloud storage from a virtual network drive with drag and drop capability and the ability to save directly from desktop applications.

**Service Characteristics**

1. Sync & Replicate: Sync ensures offline access. Cloud storage can be used to connect PCs from different locations such as from office and from home. Sync can also be used to connect PCs from different users, or to connect two different file servers.
2. Online Backup: Files and folders, music and video can be backed up to online cloud storage. A mirror backup to mirror a local folder into cloud storage, or a snapshot backup with different versions can also be done.
3. Multiple PC File Sync: Synchronizing of files and folders onto multiple PCs, is made possible using cloud storage as a conduit and repository.

articleTitle: REPLY TO BUY on SMS shortcode 555
markdownContent:
**REPLY TO BUY on SMS shortcode 555**

**Definition**

**REPLY TO BUY** is a feature that allows Safaricom customers one step purchase through a response code reply back to the sender SMS ID. This way Safaricom customers will skip any potential 2 or 3 step journeys associated with navigating to an app/website or to a mobile wallet and cut straight to the purchase step. This journey feature makes customer experience super-convenient!

**Eligibility**

The service will be available for targeted prepaid customers

 **How the Service Works**

- Customer receives an outbound Safaricom promotional message from SMS shortcode 555 (sender ID) about an offer along with purchase response code
- Customer’s REPLY TO BUY Action: Customer replies with response code (something as simple as “1” or “yes”) back to sender ID 555 to make a purchase.
- Customer gets the offer immediately through CBS provisioning automatically by the backend system after deducting offer amount from the customer’s airtime balance. 

The image below illustrates the journey to purchase using **REPLY to BUY**.

 [Screenshot] 

**Advantages of REPLY TO BUY**

| Pointers | Current Purchase | Reply and Buy on 555 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Customer Journey Experience | Multi Steps Journey : Open endedCustomer gets offer SMSCustomer visits USSD or website/ AppCustomer browses the USSD menu or navigates website/AppCustomer selects the product and initiate’s purchaseCustomer transacts using M-PESA/ uses Credit Cards | Single Step Journey : Closed loop JourneyCustomer gets offer SMS from 555Customer replies with response code to 555 and gets an offer immediately(offer is auto provisioned via customer’s airtime deduction) |
| Response Rate | Lower response rate: Due to multi-step approach, customer ( if busy or distracted) tends to respond later and may altogether forget | Higher Response rate: Customer get instant purchase with single action |
| Cart abandonment | Higher cart abandonment: Customer has to exit SMS environment and enter into other environment like M-PESA/credit card/ App and if there are purchase failures, he may completely abandon the purchase | Lower cart abandonment: Customer stays within SMS environment to purchase, i.e., doesn’t do any transaction action – offer purchase is automated backend action with almost no failure rate |

**How to Opt Out of the service**

The customer will not be required to opt In

**Validity of the bundles**

The resources on offer will be valid for 24 hours 

**Checking balance**

To check balance, customers will dial \*444# to check balance

# **KENYA REVENUE AUTHORITY**

# **Definition**

Kenya Revenue Authority (KRA), is an agency of the Government of Kenya that is responsible for the assessment, collection and accounting for all revenues that are due to government, in accordance with the laws of Kenya

 **Eligibility**

Filing KRA tax returns in iTax has become simple and easier.

In Kenya, every registered taxpayer with a Personal Identification Number (PIN) obtained from the Kenya Revenue Authority (KRA) must file tax returns every financial year.

Those who have no business or not in gainful employment must file nil KRA tax returns.

 **PAYE mechanics**

- PAYE is a method of collecting tax from individuals *in* gainful employment. ... salary, leave pay, sick pay, payment *in* lieu of leave, *fees*, commission, bonus, gratuity. As *an* employer you are required to deduct PAYE from your employees
- One can dial the USSD code \*572# to access the menu
- KRA Business Systems are updated in real-time as soon as the taxpayer receives the KRA confirmation message (not to be confused with the Mobile Provider’s message).
- Only Traffic Revenue PRNs can be generated by dialing \*572#.
- Customs e-slips are generated online from the Simba system, and Domestic Taxes e-slips are generated online from the iTax system.
- Date: Individual Income Tax Returns should be filed on or before 30th June of the following year.

#  **Payment Information**

- Charges will occur in case you contact KRA Customer Service line on normal call charges
- Normal internet charges will occur while accessing KRA website Online
- Penalty on late filing: Whichever is higher between, 5% of the tax due or Kshs. 2,000.
- Penalty on late payment: 5% of the tax due and a late payment interest of 1% per month on the unpaid tax until the tax is paid in full
- After filing the return online via iTax, generate a payment slip and present it at any of the appointed KRA banks to pay the due tax.
- You can also pay via Mpesa. Use the KRA Pay bill number **572572**. The Account Number is the Payment Registration number quoted at the top right corner of the generated payment slip

 **Voluntary Cancellation**

If you wish to stop performing your duty as a tax agent, you will be required to inform KRA in writing at least seven days prior to termination of your services.

 **KRA Contacts & Support**

- Call on: +254 20 4 999 999 or +254 711 099 999;
- Email on callcentre@kra.go.ke or click the button under “Contact us icon “(KRA Website) to ask a question
- You can also visit any of KRA physical locations countrywide.

Lipa Kodi na M-PESA issues shall be handled as per the paybill procedures and escalated via SR using the M-PESA Services SR Category and Lipa Kodi SR type, SLA: 24hrs.

# **Registration/ Subscription Process**

1. Dial \*600#, and prompts are as follows:

- *‘’Welcome to M-SALAMA please enter your full name’’*

- *‘’Pleas select your Gender’’ F or M*

2. The user receives a SMS with a link to T&C’s at; [http://www.redcross.or.ke/landing/termsandconsitions](http://www.redcross.or.ke/landing/termsandconsitions)

3. The user will read the T&C of the service being offered. The USSD session will be terminated.

4. Redial \*600# as follows to accept the T& C’s

- *‘’Welcome to M-SALAMA please enter your full name’’*

- *‘’Pleas select your Gender’’ F or M*

- *‘’Welcome to M-SALAMA please enter your full name please accept the terms and conditions’’ Accept/Decline*

5. Once the user accepts the T&C’s they will be prompted to subscribe to the service; select 1 to subscribe to the Red cross services

- *‘’Welcome to M-SALAMA please Register for all Services’’*

6. Subscriber will receive an SMS from M-Salama as below;

- *‘’Dear Customer, you have already subscribed to 40388 M-SALAMA Kshs. 2’’*

# **Opting out/ Un – Subscription Process**

1. Dial \*600# and select the Unsubscribe.
2. Normal PRS un-subscription process

1. Dial OR \*100 # or \*200#
2. Select My- Subscription
3. Select Premium services and Games
4. Select Unsubscribe
5. Select 40388\_Msalama\_ Ksh1
6. Select Unsubscribe

If customer is unable to opt Out when they call Customer care, frontline agents should be able to unsubscribe via CRM-SDP tab.

# **Reversal Guidelines**

# Pochi La Biashara Reversal should be treated as per below

| Reversal Type | Action | SLA |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Few to Person | Treated as a P2P reversal | 2Hrs (Working hrs ) |
| Pochi (MSME) to Pochi (MSME) | Treated as a wrong Buy Goods Till/Paybill (Safaricom Acquired) transaction | 72Hrs (Working hrs ) |
| Person to Few | Treated as a wrong Buy Goods Till/Paybill (Safaricom Acquired) transaction | 72Hrs (Working hrs ) |
| Pochi Withdrawal from M-PESA Agent | Treated as a wrong agent withdrawal Transaction | 12Hrs (Working hrs ) |
| Pochi to LNM Buy Goods/Paybill | Treated as a wrong Buy Goods Till/Paybill (Safaricom Acquired) transaction | 72Hrs (Working hrs ) |

# **Micro SME Sell Airtime to Customer Reversals**

This will apply to Micro SME Sell Airtime to Customer transaction where the Pochi Merchant erroneously purchases for a wrong number.

**Guidelines**

- The reversal is done without having to call the customer for consent.
- Partial reversal will not be possible as well as reversals older than one month (30 days)
- The reversal request can come from the customer or Pochi merchant.
- The Merchant/customer will give the mobile number that receives money.

# **CEE Action on Siebel**

- The CEE will enter the customer's mobile number and will confirm ownership of the line using Customer Names.
- The CEE will confirm transaction details i.e., amount purchased, date / time transaction was made and transaction number (where available). On the transaction History button, (Under Transaction History, CEE will specify date range and query recharge history).
- Where multiple transactions are made on the date specified, CEE will take caution to confirm with customer the exact transaction to be reversed i.e., using time, amount, and transaction id where necessary.
- CEE will confirm the available airtime balance is not less than amounts requested to be reversed i.e., not partially utilized.  Successful. If the balance is sufficient the CEE will initiate the reversal.
- The FSS Team will run a report daily of all airtime reversals done manually removing all promotional resources.

# **System Failure**

Where system failure is noted in completing the transaction i.e. the airtime has been deducted in CBS, but the Pochi Merchant’s Business account has not been credited, the CEE will escalate via an SR and give details of the failure noted.

**Retail CEE**

The Retail CEE will also raise an SR to the Consumer care analyst and immediately notify the team leader on duty of any anomaly.

# **Support Analyst Action**

The Support analyst will pick the SR and check if the airtime was deducted before doing a manual B2C refund to the Merchant’s MSISDN as per the  **Manual Adjustment Process -Support.** 

**Note:** The amount credited to the Pochi Merchant will be less the commission earned on the transaction.

**NOTE:** Similarly to LNM reversals, merchants (owners of Pochi) should be contacted to give consent for reversals. 

**How to contact us**

1. In case of any queries, Call Line 100, 200, or 234.
2. Visit any Safaricom retail Shop or Care Desks.

articleTitle: SIM Swap Fraud and Action to be Taken
markdownContent:
**SIM Swap Fraud and Action to be Taken**

Collection of information on all unauthorized SIM swaps done internally (Call Center and Retail) and by M-PESA agents. This will apply for both call centre and retail CEE.

# **Red Flag to watch and Action Required**

The process will apply but not limited to.

Customers complaining about fraudulent SIM swap on their line.

Customers complaining their lines are no longer working and you confirm a swap was done that they did not request.

Customer who shared details with fraudsters and you confirm a swap has already been done by the fraudster.

# **Action required**

Check for recent Orders for any unauthorized SIM swap to confirm if the swap was done internally or by a dealer (EAIUSER)

Where the swap is by EAIUSER or no Order exists, check under Sim Swap OTA tab on CRM for a recent OTA swap.

Where there exists unauthorized SIM swap, kindly capture the below details on the [SIM swap fraud link](https://cmintranet/index.php?option=com_php&Itemid=1733); [https://cmintranet/index.php?option=com\_php&Itemid=1733](https://cmintranet/index.php?option=com_php&Itemid=1733)

Customer (Swapped) MSISDN

Select channel used to swap

Agent MSISDN used to swap/Username of the staff who swapped the line.

**NOTE**: *The link is also available under* *CM Intranet >> CC Systems >> SIM swap >> SIM swap Fraud*

# **Sub shared details to Fraudsters**

**Action Required**

Advice the customer on the need to suspend the account and if consent is given, proceed as below;

Vet the customer (name and ID)

Suspend the line on CRM using action reason SUSPEND ALL-CUSTOMER REQUEST. Enter key comment "Do not unbar, details given to fraudster".

Log in to G2 and suspend the M-PESA account under account info tab as below. In the comment box, enter "Customer gave details to Fraudsters".

If consent is not given, advice customer to visit an Agent/Retail Centre/care desk to do a Sim Swap in order to obtain a new PIN.

Educate customer on fraud and advise them not to share their details with 3rd parties.

Capture an interaction as follows: TYPE: Sim Card Issues, SUB TYPE: Details Given To fraudsters

# **Swap done by Fraudsters after sharing details**

**Action required**

Where a customer calls to report their sim, card has lost service after they shared their details with a fraudster,

Vet the customer (name and ID)

Suspend the line on CRM using action reason SUSPEND ALL-CUSTOMER REQUEST. Enter key comment "Do not unbar, details given to fraudster".

Log in to G2 and suspend the M-PESA account under account info tab as below. In the comment box, enter "Customer gave details to Fraudsters"

After you suspend the line, advice the customer to visit the nearest care-desk/ Safaricom shop for assistance, do not swap such line.

Empathize with the customer and advise the customer to do the following or reset for the customer the below, it will help prevent or minimize loss of funds.

Reset their webselfcare account via Siebel

Reset their Safaricom App via Siebel

Delete their VB Enrolment via Siebel

Reset any other application that could compromise their funds or privacy.

Advise the customer to also contact their respective banks and report the breach.

# **Golden/Special Numbers**

**Effecting the Sim Swap**

The SIM SWAP Process on CRM/Sibel is as indicated below:

Open Siebel and enter customers MSISDN

Under Subscriber Portal, click "Modify" then "Customize"

Select the tab "MSISDN & SIM Card"

Enter the SIM serial under the tab "Sim Number"

Click "Done" and submit the order.

An automated SMS shall be sent to the customer to educate them on how to re-activate the M-PESA account.

Ensure to capture the vetting details on the Siebel Interactions.

Advice on re-activation of call barring and diverts, where applicable.

Advice the customer that the new SIM card will be active on the network within 20 minutes.

Educate the customer on how to activate their M-PESA account after a SIM Swap.

**Note:** If customer fails vetting refer to Retail shop/Care desk/Dealer (with their ID) or call back with correct details.

# **Channels through which Customers Request for Sim Swap**

Via Call Prepay100, Post-pay 200

Request via SMS chat bot Applicable for Prepaid customers

Requests via Chat /Social Media touch points

Email Option

Our business partners are our agents, dealers and suppliers, on whom we rely on both operationally and in terms of our reputation, since they help to drive transformation through our products and services

**Definition**

This Service aims at giving Safaricom subscribers **an opportunity to request Kredo from Family and Friends**.

**Eligibility**

The Service is open to all Safaricom PrePay subscribers apart from PrePay subscribers who are roaming.

**How to Request The Service**

- Dial \*444# from your Safaricom line.
- Select “Niokolee” then select “Credit Request”.
- Enter the Safaricom number to request Kredo from (“the Benefactor”).
- Select the predefined Kredo amount to request e.g., Ksh 10 then submit.
- The recipient will receive a notification from 44444 asking you to “Accept” or “Decline” the request.
- Once you accept the request, the selected amount equivalent is moved from you to the requestor (and notifications sent to both parties).

**How It Works**

**Niokolee Kredo denominations**

**Number of Niokolee Requests**

1. Onecan only initiate a maximum of 2 Niokolee requests per day and any subsequent request will be automatically declined by the system.
2. Equally, one can make a maximum of 10 Niokolee requests in a month, any subsequent request will be automatically declined by the system.

**Usage**

- Niokolee resources can be used for both on-net and off-net for both calls and SMS
- One cannot buy other Minutes & airtime bundles and  resourcesfrom shared Niokolee kredo
- Niokolee Kredo is usable only while within Kenya and cannot be used when roaming
- Niokolee sharing service is only available to customers on the Safaricom network and cannot be shared to a number from another network
- One can be a requestor and a sponsor to another number and still share airtime that you have purchased. However, you cannot share the Kredo that has been shared from another sponsor.

**Priority of usage**

The priority will be Free resources, hourly resources and the shared Kredo

**Minutes Validity**

The resources will have a validity of 24 hours.

**Balance Check**

Balance check on USSD \*444# or send SMS to144 to show the balance of all the resources remaining Minutes

**Resources Roll Over**

Any unused Niokolee Talktime will not be carried over after the lapse of the validity period.

**Accumulation of Bonga points**

The beneficiary will **NOT** earn Bonga points from Niokolee Kredo

**Accumulation of Storo Bonus**

A customer will accumulate Storo bonus if enabled on their line.

**Sample messages sent to the Sponsor and the requestor**:

1. Request notification to you:

*“Dear Customer, You friend 7XXXXXXXX has requested you to sponsor them with Niokolee Kredo of Ksh. XX Reply with 1 to Accept or 2 to Decline. The request expires within 24 hours.”*

2. **Message to you after you accept the request:**

*“You have shared Niokolee Kredo of Ksh XX with 7XXXXXXXX. To check balance, send Bal to 144”.*

**Message to requestor upon successful request:**

“*You have received Niokolee Kredo of Ksh XX from 7XXXXXXXX valid until 18-04-2023. To check balance, send Bal to 144”.*

3. **Message to requestor after unsuccessful request:**

“*Your Niokolee request to 7XXXXXXXX has been declined*”

articleTitle: Paybill Validation, Definition, Key features, B2B product (bank account to buy goods/Paybill) and KYC documentation.
markdownContent:
**Paybill Validation, Definition, Key features, B2B product (bank account to buy goods/Paybill) and KYC documentation.**

# **Definition**

Paybill validation is a service that aims to cancel/auto-reverse transactions done to Paybill partner accounts that are not in the defined string/format. This service can either be internal or external.

# **Internal Paybill Validation.**

This validates the account number in the payment details received from M-PESA against the partner’s systems.

It enables transactions to be filtered before integration with the partner’s systems.

It cancels and auto-reverse the transaction to M-PESA for the ones that do not integrate.

# **External Paybill Validation Feature.**

This allows M-PESA to validate the account number provided before completing a Paybill transaction.

It also enables the M-PESA system to filter transactions that are not correct thus reducing reversal instances.

The Paybill organization provides the account number format which is then configured in M-PESA for that organization.

# **How It Works**

When customer initiates a Paybill transaction and provides the account number, the system keeps the transaction in authorized status and validates the account number format against what is configured.

If the validation is successful, the transaction is completed but if the validation fails, the transaction is cancelled, and the customer is notified to provide the correct account number via SMS.

The partners are now able to give us preferred messages to be configured in cases where the above validation has failed.

This feature helps reduce the chances of making account errors when making payments, consequently reducing the need for reversals.

# **Paybill Validation Onboarding Process For Existing Paybill Partners:**

EBU sales teams/account management teams will share the benefits of the internal/external Paybill validation feature to the Paybill partners.

The partners will send their requests to M-PESA Business:

[M-PESABusiness@Safaricom.co.ke](mailto:M-PESABusiness@Safaricom.co.ke)

[Lipanampesa@Safaricom.co.ke](mailto:Lipanampesa@Safaricom.co.ke)

Retail Center/EBU sales/account management teams will send the following details:

The account number format as expected by partner.

The Paybill short code number and organization name.

The length of the account number.

Confirmation if the account number alphanumeric.

Sample account number: if account number is alphanumeric to confirm where there is an alphabet, a number, a Symbol, or Special character.

The preferred message to be configured: the message should include the organization’s helpline and /or the name of the organization.

EBU CARE and Retail CEE will forward the completed application forms to [M-PESABSteam@Safaricom.co.ke](mailto:M-PESABSteam@Safaricom.co.ke)

The BSS team will engage Product management team to approve the message.

The BSS team will raise an incidence to FSS Support Team. The ticket will capture all the information including the organization’s customized response message.

M-PESA IT will do the configuration on M-PESA test accounts and request M-PESA BSS team to test.

The BSS team will test and inform the Paybill partner to test and give feedback.

On successful testing, FSS Support Team will change the status of the incidence to “resolved”.

SLA is 48hrs from the time a ticket is raised to FSS Support Team.

# **Paybill Validation Onboarding Process For New Paybill Accounts**

For new Paybill accounts, information should be included in the Paybill application form.

After creation on the M-PESA web, the onboarding/creation teams will send this information to the BSS team on [M-PESABSteam@Safaricom.co.ke](mailto:M-PESABSteam@Safaricom.co.ke)  who will then follow as per the existing Paybill onboarding process.

Retail teams will raise an SR and close the same after resolution of the issue.

# **B2b Product (Bank Account to Buy Goods/Paybill) And KYC Documentation.**

This service allows bank customers to access their Bank accounts without physical visits and make the following transactions.

Make direct payments to Buy Goods and Paybill account.

Transfer cash from their bank accounts to other bank accounts.

The Transactions will be authorized by using the customer’s Mobile/App/Online banking PIN/Password via USSD/App/online banking platform. For the service to work:

The bank must integrate to M-PESA G2 via API to enable them to avail this service to their customers.

The customer must be registered to the bank service i.e. Must have access to respective mobile banking platforms.

Must have downloaded their respective banking Apps or use USSD codes/online channels where applicable or use the M-Banking services accessible via Safaricom STK Menu under Safaricom menu.

**Example of these services include**: My Kash via KCB, Loop via CBA, Vooma by KCB, and Whizz by HFC.

# **Key KYC Documentations And Where To Find Them.**

CR12 documentations: Registrar of Companies - Sheria House or E-Citizen

Business Permit/Certificate of Registration: Registrar of Companies/issued by respective counties / e-citizen.

Certificate of Incorporation: Registrar of Companies - Sheria House/E-Citizen.

Resolution Letter Form: Safaricom website: [https://www.safaricom.co.ke](https://www.safaricom.co.ke/)

Cancelled Cheque or Stamped Letter from Bank: Respective Bank Institution.

Application Forms and Terms and Condition Document:

Safaricom Website: https://www.safaricom.co.ke or Retail Shop.

Partnership Deed: Registrar of Companies - Sheria House/E-Citizen.

Partnership Affidavit: Partners Advocates.

Letter from NGO Board: Board Service Charter – NGO Coordination Board.

Company or Individual KRA PIN Certificate; Online: Kenya Revenue Authority website.

Sasra Letter: Sacco Societies Regulatory Authority (Sasra).

Safaricom AML / KYC Questionnaire Safaricom website: [https://www.safaricom.co.ke](https://www.safaricom.co.ke/)

Ministry of Education License: Ministry of Education.

Trustees Deed: Ministry of Lands.

# **UWEZO TARIFF**

**DEFINITION**

A tariff is a guide on the charges the customer will incur as they use a product or service. For Prepaid services, all customers that onboard are automatically put on the UWEZO tariff.

**CHARGES ON UWEZO TARIFF**

- It is in line with the above Financial Act of 2023 revision of excise Duty from 20% to 15% that we announce the new OOB (Out of Bundle) prices in compliance to the law. The out of bundle rates will be amended to reflect the new excise duty tax. Though this was recently reviewed to 25 cents per Mb to allow access to data for all.
- Voice calls by the operator will now be priced at Ksh 4.67 per minute in peak hours and Ksh 2.50 per minute in off peak hours while sms services will be priced at Ksh 1.2 per sms.

**LOCAL CALL CHARGES**

- Safaricom's new plans with no expiry date give you 50% more airtime. Every time you purchase this plan your calls/SMS lasts longer and won’t expire.

Click [**here**](https://esaka.safaricom.net/system/templates/selfservice/safaricom/#!agent/portal/555500000001002/article/555500000007303/11229-International-calling-rates-international-direct-dialing?fromQuery=international) for the international direct dialing rates [https://roaming.safaricom.co.ke/](https://roaming.safaricom.co.ke/)

This is a mobile voice and data business tariff that provides businesses with affordable calling and internet rates.

One flat rate for your mobile voice and out of bundle browsing.

**ELIGIBILITY**

- It was previously designed for customers with small businesses though now it’s open to all.
- Both NO EXPIRY airtime and NO EXPIRY data bundles, **do not expire**.

**KEY** **FEATURES**

articleTitle: Unclaimed Financial Assets Authority (UFAA) Definition and Features
markdownContent:
# **Definition**

1. The Unclaimed Financial Assets Authority (**UFAA**) is an Authority created under the Unclaimed Financial Assets Act, No. 40 of 2011 to administer unclaimed financial assets.
2. These are financial assets (funds) held in a financial institution for a period of two years and are yet to be claimed by the owner.
3. The Government regulation (Unclaimed Financial Assets Authority) requires that organizations declare and submit unclaimed funds annually.
4. Safaricom M-PESA is a financial institution that holds customers funds in the M-PESA wallet

# **Amount** **to be Claimed**

1. Whitelisted Customers can claim from Kshs 1- Kshs 70,000
2. Customers with more than Kshs 70,000 will be required to visit the Retail shops with their IDs to claim their funds.

# **Failure to claim Funds**

1. Safaricom will notify the customer that the funds have been submitted to the Unclaimed Financial Assets Authority (UFAA).
2. The customer will be required to visit [www.ufaa.go.ke](http://www.ufaa.go.ke/) to claim their funds.
3. Once the funds have been submitted to UFAA, customers who wish to claim their funds are required to present a letter from Safaricom confirming the amount submitted. The letter can be collected from any Retail Centre.

# **Claim Closure**

1. The message content below will be sent to customers who have not claimed their funds:

*‘’We have come to the end of the claim period for M-PESA customer funds archived between (insert date) to (insert date). Please note that the claims from the \*405# USSD will be blocked as from 16th Sep 2020.’’*

2. The message content below will be received by those who dial the USSD and had not claimed the funds: *“M-PESA unclaimed funds have been submitted to the Unclaimed Financial Assets Authority and will be available from 1/11/20. Visit ufaa.go.ke or dial \*361# for more info.”*

# **LNM Unclaimed Assets**

The Merchants will be sent SMS advising them to claim the unclaimed funds.

*‘Dear Partner, Kindly email your till number to LNMunclaimedfunds@Safaricom.co.ke by (indicate date) before we submit the funds to Unclaimed Financial Assets Authority’*

# **UFAA Contacts**

1. Phone: 020 4343440, 0706866984, and 0736559152
2. Email: info@ufaa.go.ke
3. Website: [http://www.ufaa.go.ke/](http://www.ufaa.go.ke/)

# **Definition**

The change of ownership will be done via SVC (View360). It starts when the customer visits retail centers or care desks for Change of ownership requests and ends when the correct resolution or information is offered.

The instructions are applicable to Customer Experience Executives, Retail Centre Team Leaders, Retail Centre Managers, retail Business Leads and various HQ support staff.

# **Guidelines**

- This defines the process by which Safaricom customers can change or transfer the ownership and/or details of their Safaricom MSISDN at retail outlets.
- This will happen where a Safaricom account holder wishes to transfer MSISDN(s) registered to themselves to a new owner known to them.
- This does **not** include change of MSISDN for requests where the registered owner is not making the request i.e deceased accounts, recycled or deleted accounts etc.
- This is applicable for **prepaid individual accounts** does not include other accounts i.e postpaid accounts, business tariffs etc.
- Requests for change must be submitted by the registered customer and new owner must also present themselves at a retail outlet for consent. They however can make requests at **separate** authorized retail outlets.
- This request must be presented by **both parties**, physically presenting themselves at retail outlets and presenting acceptable KYC registration documents as per the subscriber registration process. The parties may present themselves at different outlets and times to submit their requests.
- The request must be initiated by the registered owner of the line. No other person will be allowed to present this request.
- Registered customer will request transfer of ownership from him/herself to the new owner and will present their original and valid document ID.

# **Action by CEE**

- The CEE will proceed to vet the customer as per the retail vetting guidelines. Account transfer will only be done once:

- **Validation of account ownership** and applicable registration documents is done.
- **Validation that customer has no loans and savings**. This includes and not limited to FSI loans and savings, Lipa Mdogo Mdogo loan, ETU (Emergency top up – Okoa Jahazi)
- **Validation of account status and or business rules**. This will be restricted where; accounts are flagged. This include accounts flagged for fraudulent or suspicious activities, flagged, null or rejected KYC status (pending and approved status will be allowed to progress with the account transfer), roaming customers, inactive status (i.e suspended, pooled or deleted) accounts not on prepaid tariffs and accounts with active loans and /or savings.

- CEE will progress to close M-Shwari on CRM where applicable as per existing process. Where customer fails vetting, the CEE will advise customer accordingly.

- CEE will progress to click on the change of ownership tab on SVC upon validation of KYC. This will trigger automated prechecks, applicable notification will be displayed.

Where business rules are not met, the request will not progress. CEE will guide customer accordingly.

- Where all business rules pass validations, CEE will engage the customer to validate the primary number. This will be used to authenticate transfer request via a one-time password (OTP). CEE will progress to trigger sending of OTP to the primary number via SVC, CEE will request customer to provide the OTP code and will enter the code on SVC for validation. 

**NOTE:**

To protect the customers from fraudulent activities, retries will be limited to set thresholds defined within the journey with an option for agent to resend OTP provided.

Customer will receive an SMS from sender as Safaricom with approval OTP. The SMS will also include a disclaimer on liability for the transfer, terms and conditions for the service as well as the privacy policy for reference.

- CEE will progress to scan registered owners ID as per the work instructions. This will include the back and front of IDs and Bio page for passports.
- Where recipient of account presents themselves at different times or location, the registered owner will provide details of the recipient i.e Full Names and ID number. CEE will capture details accurately and save.
- CEE will progress to scan recipient’s ID. This will include the back and front of IDs and Bio page for passports. CEE will validate KYC is accurately captured as per scanned document and will edit where need be.

**NOTE:**

KYC validation will be done via automated IPRS scans and authentication. Where any failure is noted, CEE will validate against KYC captured and where applicable, KYC escalation metrics will apply.

Where recipient of account presents themselves at different times or location, the CEE must validate the details of the new owner as captured by the registered owner i.e Full Names and ID number. CEE will validate KYC against ID provided and will proceed to scan new owner ID.

- CEE will progress to guide customer to consent on the request by appending their signature and ticking to consenting to the terms and conditions.

# **Steps after Approval**

Once approved, customer will receive notification on the MSISDN being transferred with the terms of reference.

Upon consent an automated trigger will commence to transfer account details (pre to pre)          

Where customer exists, the system will query customer KYC associated to document and will reuse some parameters i.e names. CEE will verify and update other KYC as required i.e DOB, gender, document expiry (where applicable) as captured on the CRM database.

Where customer is new to Safaricom, customer KYC will be validated and updated. KYC validation will be done via automated IPRS scans and authentication.

Where any failure is noted, CEE will validate against KYC captured and where applicable, KYC escalation metrics will apply.

Account transfer will be effected and applicable responses displayed on SVC. CEE will confirm account closure status, where failure is noted, CEE will trouble shoot and action as required.

# **M-PESA Activation**

Automated M-PESA account recycling will be triggered upon successful account transfer.

CEE will trigger a menu push request prior to the account closure request.

For any failures on account closure, CEE will close account via M-PESA system as per the applicable process.

- CEE will progress to raise SR for KCB M-PESA account closure where applicable as per existing process.
- CEE will progress to register M-PESA where customer consents.
- CEE will enter interaction with action taken and vetting parameters.

Where applicable and need for SIM swap arises, CEE will action as per the SIM replacement procedure.

Upon successful account transfer and image capture, KYC will be availed on the sub reg portal for verification and approval process as per AML procedures.

# **M-PESA E-Receipt Definition and Mechanism**

# **M-PESA E-Receipt on \*234#**

articleTitle: LIPA NA M-PESA Operator ID/ Start Key/PIN Request Guideline
markdownContent:
**Definition**

This guideline covers scenarios involving forgot Operator PIN, forgot Operator ID, deleted Start Key/ not received.

LIPA na M-PESA products, (Pay Bills, Buy Goods, and M-PESA Business Till), support two operator roles:

Merchant Primary Operator

Merchant Assistant Till Operator

**Merchant Primary Operator:**

During opt in via DIY, the nominated number’s name and ID shall be used to create a **Primary Operator** on the Store.

·       The Primary Operator shall receive an **Operator ID** and **Start Key** via SMS.

·       The merchant shall use the start key to set a new PIN.

Once the PIN is successfully created, the Primary Operator becomes **active** and can access all services available on the short code, based on the product.

**Merchant Assistant Till Operator****:**

The Assistant Till Operator is created by an **active Primary Operator**.

The Assistant Till Operator **MUST** be created on a Safaricom mobile number registered under an individual and is active on M-PESA.

Upon successful creation, the Assistant Till Operator receives an SMS with the **Operator ID** and **Start Key.**

## **Jambo Tourist Bundle**

**Definition**

Jambo Tourist Bundles are designed to allow travellers connect to a local network in the roaming or destination country.

Travelers can enjoy better calls, data and SMS plans compared to international roaming rates.

The resources will be used by tourists who visit Kenya and purchase a Safaricom sim card.

## **Eligibility**

The Service is open to all individuals Prepay and Post-pay Jambo tourist Safaricom customers.

## **How to purchase**

- Customer will Dial \*444# > select global connect to purchase Jambo tourist bundle.
- A customer can purchase the Jambo Tourist bundle as many times as they wish (multiple times).
- A customer can either purchase an Autorenewal or a One-off subscription for Jambo Tourist Bundle
- Customers can purchase bundle via Airtime, M-PESA or Fuliza.

## **Benefits of Jambo Tourist Bundles**

- A tourist can enjoy the below benefits compared to international roaming rates. For example.
- Tailored bundle plans with reduced roaming charges, providing economical options for data, voice, and SMS.
- Experience the convenience and flexibility of purchasing Jambo Tourist Bundles effortlessly upon arrival to the roaming country.
- Enjoy a secure network, minimizing exposure to cyber threats associated with public Wi-Fi connections while working and browsing.
- Universally compatible, Jambo Tourist Bundles cater to various gadgets like tablets or iPads.

## **How It Works**

- Foreigners will be able to purchase the Jambo tourist bundles via USSD 444 – Global Connect using Airtime and M-PESA **on their first 90 days on the network**.
- The foreigner must be registered using a Passport for them to qualify.
- Jambo resources will be used for sending International SMS & calling other international destinations will be charged out of bundle rates i.e., Normal PAYG rates.
- International Minutes can only be used to call the pre-selected 52 international destinations attached.
- The normal foreign subscriber registration process will apply, and they will be eligible for M-PESA registration and usage.
- Jambo resources can only be used while in Kenya i.e., cannot be used while roaming.
- The Jambo tourist bundles are only available as a one-off plan.
- A customer can purchase the Jambo Tourist bundle as many times as they wish (multiple times) using either Airtime or M-PESA.
- One cannot purchase Jambo Tourist bundles for another number.
- Once a customer depletes their Data bundle, they will have access to unlimited WhatsApp valid until the bundle expiry date.
- Jambo resources cannot be transferred.
- Purchase of another bundle will NOT extend the validity of the existing Jambo Tourist bundle.
- If the line goes to Expired status, the line will remain in this status for 120 days, after which the line and any unutilized resources will be automatically deleted, and the line recycled.

# **How It Works**

- Unused minutes can be rolled over by purchasing another bundle before expiry of the current bundle.

# **DEFINITION**

This involves the guidelines to be used by analysts when calling customers.

# **SALUTATION**

This is a formal greeting to a customer.

# **Opening Greetings.**

- The analyst should use appropriate opening greetings, ensuring that they state their name and organization they are calling from clearly.
- The analyst should greet the customer in a friendly, energetic, and audible manner. E.g., “Good (Morning, Afternoon, Evening). This is Winnie calling from Safaricom. Am I speaking to John Doe? (As per name on the Data /Jiandikishe).

# **Impact of opening greetings**

- It assists the Analyst create rapport and gain trust from the customer.
- Demonstrates professionalism – Customers experience a standard greeting and introduction to the survey from all the analysts.
- The Customer immediately knows who he / she is talking to.
- It creates a sense of welcome and it demonstrates that you are open to receive feedback – either positive or negative.

# **Reason(s) for Calling.**

- The analyst should clearly state the reason(s) for making the outbound call.
- The analyst should seek permission to speak to the customer. If the customer agrees, the analyst should proceed. In case the customer would not be able to speak at that time for whichever reason, the analyst should thank the customer and end the call appropriately.
- Where the customer expresses/requests to be called at a specific time (within working hours), the analyst is encouraged to call the customer and gather feedback. If outside working hours, the analyst should thank the customer for the offer and politely explain that they may not be able to call back.

# **Personalization/Use of the Customer’s name/Title.**

- The analyst is encouraged to use customer name/title naturally, within the outbound survey. If the customer refers to himself by their title e.g. Dr.,Mr. Mheshimiwa, the Analyst will acknowledge the same during their interaction e.g. I understand Dr…or Good day Mheshimiwa (make reference to names/titles as given by the customer).

# **Impact of personalization.** 

- Assists in creating a great rapport.
- Creates a sense of belonging.
- Allows us to emotionally connect with the customer.
- Makes the customer feel important.
- Is a show of professionalism.

# **Closing the call.**

- The analyst should demonstrate appreciation to the customer for their time and feedback.
- An appropriate closing may be “Thank you (customer’s name) for your time……”, “Thank you for taking this survey Mr. Kamau and for your feedback, wishing you a lovely day/afternoon/evening” and any other phrase as may be deemed professionally necessary.
- The analyst should not rush the closing and the words ought to be clearly pronounced.
- It is also advisable to wait for any forthcoming customer’s acknowledgement e.g., “…you’re welcome’, “…you too”, “...have a good evening/afternoon” etc.

# **POLITENESS AND RESPECT THROUGHOUT THE CALL**

- It is important to always be polite and respectful to the customer. This is demonstrated through choice of words, tone/pitch of voice and manner of responding to the customer.
- In case a customer is not the right candidate for the survey i.e., does not understand the product or he/she has not used it long enough to give feedback or just doesn’t understand the survey questions; do not be dismissive, argumentative, or condescending to the customer. The analyst should thank the customer for their time and end the call professionally.
- This parameter shall check for any instance of rude behavior, improper tone within the call. Any single instance shall attract a score of “NO” on this parameter will result in the entire assessment being scored 0.

# **Upbeat and enthusiasm**

- The Analyst is expected to be warm, natural, vibrant, friendly, upbeat, and enthusiastic throughout the survey. Warmth should be evident in the Analyst’s voice, tone, and pitch.
- The Analyst should help the customer feel at ease, so that they are able to give the much-needed experience feedback.

# **Listening to the customer without interruption.**

- The analyst should always allow the customer to finish giving his or her explanation and where necessary only interrupt the customer in an assertive manner if the customer is getting out of topic. This should always be done in a gentle manner and the analyst should apologize for interrupting as they take control of the call.
- Interruptions display lack of respect for the speaker. Furthermore, the listener who interrupts runs the risk of misinterpreting the message since the speaker was not allowed to fully articulate his or her thoughts.

# **Portraying Professional image**

- A professional image must always be maintained regardless of the language used. The analyst should use phrases and words that portray the Spirit of Safaricom brand.
- The analyst should be courteous and gentle to the customer. E.G. When taking the customer through the survey use words like “Kindly I would like to ask /tafadhali nielezee “as opposed to “what is/nipatie”. This is to enhance rapport and to avoid the feeling like you are interrogating the customer.
- The analyst should avoid habitual speech patterns such as Um, ehh, ati. Instead learn to use ‘Yes’, ‘OK’, ‘No’ etc. Should not mumble or speak to self, pronounce each word clearly (without slurring). In instances where yawning, sneezing, coughing, or distraction is unavoidable, kindly acknowledge and apologize to the customer.

# **Empathy/apology**

- Empathy is the ability to not only understand how the other person feels, but also to make them feel that they are being understood. It is one of the keys in building trust and relationships.
- It is emotional identification, compassion, understanding, insight and feeling. It shows that you care and understood the other person's experience thus reducing irritation. The best and recommended way to display empathy is to verbalize an apology to the customer.
- This must be done in scenarios that a customer has been inconvenienced by a system failure, service failure, network failure or any reported loss on the part of the customer e.g., loss of phone, money, relative or friend. Verbalizing of empathy should be done by the words, “I’m sorry about….”, “Please bear with us for….”, “I apologize for …” We apologize for the inconvenience caused in the situation, regardless of the cause - whether by the customer or Safaricom.
- The analyst is also supposed to empathize to the customer in case they have been inconvenienced in any situation regardless of the cause whether by the customer or Safaricom; for example, where the customer is unable to access a service due to scheduled system downtimes or network outages. (This is not limited to these examples only)
- This shows that we care as we connect/interact with our customers on the call.

# **GATHERING FEEDBACK**

**Asking the relevant questions.**

- The analyst is expected to ask questions that are related to the purpose of the specific survey objectives and questionnaire.
- Where the analyst deviates from the questionnaire and does not gather the required feedback, this will attract a score of No.

**Asking questions on the questionnaire.**

- The analyst should ask **all** the questions on the questionnaire exhaustively for the survey to meet the survey objectives. This will help in capturing all insights sought by the stakeholder.
- Where a customer provides feedback for another question/other questions when engaging on a different one, it is not necessary to ask the question again. You can capture the feedback as provided.
- Where the customer is unwilling to provide information, is passive, in a noisy place, or seems unsure of the feedback being sought, the analyst should not insist on proceeding with the survey but should thank the customer and end the call professionally.

# **CAPTURING FEEDBACK ON THE MICROSOFT FORM FOR THE SURVEY**

- The analyst MUST capture **all** feedback from the customer accurately on the Microsoft form.
- Where the customer has not given feedback on a particular question or has no feedback, this should be captured as such.
- Where there are multiple choices and the customer has more than one choice, all should be captured correctly and accurately.
- Where the customer has given detailed experiences, proposals /suggestions /wishes, this should be captured as such on the feedback space provided on the Microsoft Form.
- Capturing any feedback on questions not asked /incorrect data will attract a No score.

# **CUSTOMER SUPPORT DURING THE SURVEY**

**use of** **available/relevant systems /DIY to assist or guide the customer to resolve any other issues raised by the customer.**

- The analyst is expected to assist the customer or guide them on available DIY options on any other issue raised while on call as per procedure apart from SIM swap & Start key requests. (Refer to E-SAKA & communication shared from time to time.)
- If the customer seeks for assistance on behalf, the analyst will guide on the available DIY options or ask the owner to contact us for assistance.
- The analyst will be expected to capture an interaction on Siebel as per the guideline where he/she accesses a customer’s account on the system.
- Where an issue is escalated via email, the analyst should copy- paste the email under comments for reference.

Policy refers to a set of principles, guidelines or rules established by an organization to guide decisions and actions in a particular area.

Policy helps ensure consistency, fairness and compliance with objectives or regulations.

Find attached the policy document.

**QUALITY GUIDELINES: Staff etiquette**

# **D****efinition**

This refers to a code of conduct an employee should follow at work. At the care centre staff are expected to be.

# **Polite and Respectful.**

It is important to always remain polite and respectful to the customer.

This is demonstrated through.

Choice of words.

Tone/pitch of voice and manner of responding to the customer.

Adhere to the Customer’s preferred language.

Do not be rude, dismissive, argumentative or condescending to the customer.

The CEE should not deliberately disconnect the call, before the customer issue has been stated and resolved.

# **Instances of rudeness or impolite behaviour shall be determined based on****:**

Poor choice/inappropriate use of words demonstrating condescending/patronizing behaviour or lack of respect for the customer.

Use of Belittling Statements/Questions/Words.

Arguing with the customer.

Inappropriate manner of response as depicted by tone/pitch of voice.

Negative customer feedback within the call supported by evidence of negative service received.

Outright dismissal of a customer as demonstrated by dismissive words.

Ignoring the customer completely as warranted by complete silence where a response is warranted such as instances where customer has posed a question.

Deliberate call disconnection.

# **Silences/verbal pauses during the call**

The CEE should proactively manage dead air and engage the customer fully to avoid silent moments and pauses.

There should be no hesitations, unnecessary or unexplained silences, where unavoidable hold can be engaged.

Silence without any explanation should be limited to 5 seconds, this applies to cases where agent goes silent without notifying the customer.

When the CEE notifies the customer, they will observe 20 seconds of silence and the agent has not managed to get an answer within that time, they should engage the customer to avoid the silences and if not possible, they should engage hold appropriately.

Dead air are the long moments of silence during a call.

These can be caused for many reasons.

Maybe the agent needs to find more information, manage a slow system or wait for data that have to be processed.

Dead air might cause annoyance to our customers.

The silences can be filled by the following examples: -

# **Small talk (chit-chat)**

The CEE can build some rapport. Recommend them to ask customers about the weather or share about a familiar topic to keep the conversation while processing information or researching. However, be sure to remind them about reading the customer.

Some people do not want to hear about anything else except the resolution of their problem.

Research thoroughly about the issue.

CEEs can also ask more questions about the problem or service that the customer called for. They ask the customer about what happened, how it affected him/her, what has that person done before calling.

This can also help to get insights about the customer to give them a better experience.

# **Promotions, incentives, and up-selling opportunities**

To gain value of the waiting time, CEE can inform the customer about the promotions, incentives or up-sell products.

This is great opportunity to do so. But, again, it must be something that really matters to the customer. Otherwise, this will be just noise for the customer.

# **Briefly explain to the client what you are doing step by step.**

Agents can explain the customers what they are doing so they know that the representative is taking actions to solve their issue.

It is also helpful to repeat the information that they are submitting, this way the client can double-check if the information is correct.

# **Let the customer relax for a moment.**

Maybe the customer wants that silence. In this case, CEE should always inform the customer that they will be working on their issue and let them know they can interrupt them for any questions they might have at any time.

This way the other person can also work on something else while waiting.

# **Upbeat and enthusiastic**

The CEE is expected to be upbeat and enthusiastic.

The CEE is required to be warm, natural, vibrant, friendly, and eager to assist the customer. Smile during the conversation, though it can’t be seen.

They should speak in a manner that reflects the emotions you feel and that is consistent with what you are saying. Warmth should be evident in the agent tone and pitch.

Warmth should also be evident in your voice. If you have a hard, coarse voice, it might be difficult to express warmth in your speech.

In addition to answering calls properly and providing accurate information, CEE need to use an upbeat tone of voice over the phone.

A CEE’s positivity will keep callers happy, even when they don’t get exactly what they want. One of the best tricks to achieve this positive tone is for a CEE to smile as they speak. Even though the customer won’t be able to see it, the physical act of smiling will help a representative sound more upbeat and cheerful.

CEE should help customers feel at ease; not heighten their frustration making them open to negotiation.

# **Interrupting during the call.**

A CEE should always allow the customer to finish giving his or her explanation and where necessary only interrupt the customer in an assertive manner if the customer is getting out of topic.

This should always be done in a gentle manner while the CEE is taking control of the call.

The CEE is expected to apologize to the customer when taking control of the call if he/she interrupts.

Interruptions display lack of respect for the speaker.

Furthermore, the listener who interrupts runs the risk of misinterpreting the message since the speaker was not allowed to fully articulate his or her thoughts.

If you do not interrupt the customer this enables you to match the customer's pace and in turn, give them a positive experience.

Customers will feel more appreciated and heard if allowed to vent/express themselves without being interrupted.

# **CEE Attentiveness.**

It is important to always remain attentive throughout the call, actively listen to customers by paying attention to the customer’s issue and avoid distractions.

This is demonstrated through being Alert/Keen/Focused/Concentrate throughout the call.

The agent should use statements demonstrating they are concentrating e.g. I hear you, I understand, Ok, yes, Ndio among others.

This will help the CEE to get customers expressed and unexpressed wishes.

The CEE can paraphrase the customer’s issue for clarity.

The CEE should not deliberately request the customer to repeat their issue after it was clearly explained, repeat their names in the middle of the call among others.

# **Professional image during the conversation**

A professional image must always be maintained regardless of the language used.

The CEE should strive to use phrases and words that portray the Spirit of Safaricom Brand.

A CEE should be Courteous and gentle to the Customer. E.G. When requesting for customer’s details use words like “Kindly assist with/tafadhali nipatie “as opposed to “what is/nipatie”.

Before vetting always seek consent to vet and give customer the reason for vetting. This is to enhance rapport and to avoid the feeling like you are interrogating the customer.

The CEE should avoid habitual speech patterns such as Um, Ehh, Ati. Instead learn to use ‘Yes’, ‘OK’, ‘No’ etc.

Should not mumble or speak to self, pronounce each word clearly (without slurring).

In instances where yawning, sneezing, coughing or distraction is unavoidable, kindly acknowledge and apologize to the customer.

# **If need to empathize or apologize arose, if the agent did this sincerely.**

Empathy is the ability to not only understand how the other person feels, but also to make them feel that they are being understood.

It is one of the keys to building trust and relationships.

It is emotional identification, compassion, understanding, insight and feeling. It shows that you care and that you understood the other person's experience.

It reduces our irritation with others because we understand. The best and recommended way to display empathy is to verbalize an apology to the customer.

# **Empathy should be done in the below** **scenarios.**

The CEE is supposed to apologize to the customer in case they have been inconvenienced in any Situation regardless of the cause whether by the Customer or Safaricom, for example, where the customer is unable to access a service due to scheduled System downtimes or Network Outages. (This is not limited to these examples only).

They are supposed to show that they would have reacted on the same way.

Any reported Loss on the part of the customer e.g. Loss of a relative or friend.

If a customer has lost their phone and they have called to have the line barred or do a sim card replacement,

If a customer has sent some money to a wrong number and the reversal have been declined because the funds have been used by the recipient. (This is not limited to these examples only)

Verbalizing of empathy should be done by use of the following words;

“I’m sorry about….”

“Please bear with us for….”

“I apologize for …”

“We apologize for inconvenience caused in the situation, regardless of the cause - Whether by the Customer or Safaricom.

The CEE is supposed to show empathy by putting themselves in the customers’ shoes and share in their feelings whether good or bad.

This shows that we care, and we connect with our customers while we are interacting with them on the call.
