# **Definition**

The Gaming Bundles are specialized data packages created for gamers who want uninterrupted access to supported gaming platforms. They enable subscribers to play supported games without using their regular data bundles. Each Gaming Bundle also includes a **FREE data allocation** that can be used to browse other internet sites.

The Gaming Bundles currently support **PUBG Mobile** and **Call of Duty Mobile**, with each bundle **locked to its respective game**.

# **Purpose**

The bundles are designed to enhance the gaming experience by offering dedicated data for gameplay. This ensures seamless, reliable, and affordable access to popular gaming platforms while preserving the customer’s existing data balances.

# **Supported Platforms**

The Gaming Bundles support access to the following official gaming platforms:

- **PUBG Mobile**
- **Call of Duty Mobile**

Customers must download the respective games from the Play Store, App Store, or their official websites. Each Gaming Bundle is restricted to the specific game it is purchased for and cannot be used on other gaming platforms.

# **System Requirements**

Subscribers must ensure that their devices meet the official system requirements for PUBG Mobile or Call of Duty Mobile before downloading or installing the games.

The purchase of daily, weekly, or monthly Gaming Bundles is not tied to the subscriber’s device capability, and Safaricom is not responsible for failed installations due to unmet system requirements.

# **Bundle Offerings**

The Gaming Bundles are available in multiple packages to suit different gaming needs. Bundles are offered separately for **PUBG Mobile** and **Call of Duty Mobile**, with each bundle locked to its respective game.

| Validity | PUBG/ Call of Duty Bundle | FREE Bundle | Price (KES) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Midnight | 500MB PUBG/Call of Duty | 500MB FREE | 30 |
| Daily | 150MB PUBG/Call of Duty | 150MB FREE | 39 |
| Weekly | 500MB PUBG/Call of Duty | 500MB FREE | 99 |
| Monthly | 1.5GB PUBG/Call of Duty | 1.5GB FREE | 400 |

# **Usage Priority**

While on the respective gaming platform, consumption follows a structured priority:

- The specific **gaming bundle resources** (PUBG or Call of Duty) are used first.
- Once fully consumed, the **FREE data allocation** is applied.
- When both are exhausted, normal data rules apply, and any existing internet bundle on the line will begin to deplete.
- The priority of the regular internet data bundle follows the standard data prioritization business rules.

# **Charges**

Charges depend on the selected Gaming Bundle. Prices range from **KES 30 for the Midnight bundle to KES 400 for the Monthly package**. Each purchase provides both **game-specific data** and an equal **FREE browsing allocation**.

Regular data bundles remain unaffected unless the dedicated gaming bundle is fully used.

# **Balance Checking**

Customers can view their Gaming Bundle balance as well as their regular internet bundle balance by dialing **\*544#** or **\*555#**.

# **Eligibility**

The Gaming Bundles are available to all Safaricom mobile data customers who wish to enhance their gaming experience. The bundles are not dependent on any specific tariff or subscription plan.

# **Data Consumption and Access**

- The gaming bundle is exclusively for accessing the specific gaming platform it was purchased for (PUBG Mobile or Call of Duty Mobile).
- The FREE data allocation that accompanies each bundle can be used for general browsing on other websites.
- Customers must download and install the respective game app before gameplay.

# **Non-Transferability**

Both the gaming data bundle and the FREE browsing allocation are **not transferable or shareable**. They remain tied to the purchasing line.

**DOUBLE HAKIKISHA**

**Double Hakikisha** is a service where Whitelisted customers are presented with a second screen to re-enter the recipient’s number to **AVOID** sending money to the wrong number. Majority of the customers who send money to the wrong number via **STK** is due to a **typo** of the recipient’s phone number.

**This new journey ensures that the customer DOES NOT send money to unintended recipients.**

**Objective**

- Reduce P2P reversal requests.
- Enhance the customer experience when sending money via STK.

**What is Changing**

- Whitelisted customers will be required to confirm the recipient’s number twice before the transaction is finalized.

**Scope**

This is for Send Money transactions only.

Please continue to encourage and educate customers on the benefits of this enhanced journey.

articleTitle: END OF CALL NOTIFICATION Definition and Mechanics
markdownContent:
# **Definition**

EOC notification feature allows customers to get pop up notification after every call detailing call duration, how much they have spent and the remaining balance.

# **Pop up Notification to Indicate**

Cost of call

Duration of call

count balances from Okoa and main account

# **Type of Notification received after a Call**

At the end of every call the customer will receive a USSD flash message as below: -

“*You have spent xx: xx kshs, call Duration xx: xx minutes. Airtime Balance xx: xx Kshs; 
Okoa Balance xx: xx Kshs. To opt out Dial \*456\*4# and select End of Call Notification.”*

# **Type of Notification received once Customer Opts-in**

When the Customer Subscribes, a notification will be sent as below: -

*“Dear customer, you will be notified for free of your call cost and account balances at 
the end of every call. To opt out, dial \*456\*4\*6#” or dial \*456# and follow prompts.”*

# **Type of Notification received once Customer Opts-out**

*When the Customer Unsubscribes, a notification will be sent as below: -*

*“Dear Customer, you have successfully deactivated End of Call Notification. To activate 
dial \*456\*4#”.*

# **Activation and Deactivation of End of Call Notification**

**Activation**

Prepay as well as Post-pay customers can opt in or out as illustrated below

Dial \*456#

Select My Account

Click on End of Call Notification

Opt-In

**Deactivation**

Dial \*456#

Select My Account

Click on End of Call Notification

Opt-Out

# **Kito**

Kito is a video series sponsored by the Co-operative Bank of Kenya. It airs on Citizen TV every Friday and Saturday from 8:00 PM to 9:00 PM and is later uploaded to YouTube to grow digital viewership and engagement.

The Kito Bundle is a specially designed data pass that allows viewers to enjoy Kito content and other YouTube videos at an affordable cost.

# **Definition- Kito Bundle**

The Kito Bundle is a one-hour YouTube data bundle that provides unlimited access to Kito videos and all other content available on YouTube for 60 minutes after activation.

# **Usage**

This bundle is exclusively for YouTube and can be used to: 

Watch Kito episodes

Stream videos and music

Watch YouTube live streams

Access is limited to the YouTube platform only.

# **Cost**

The Kito Bundle is available at a one-time cost of KES 20.

# **Validity**

The bundle is valid for one hour (60 minutes) from the moment of activation, providing continuous access throughout the period.

# **Subscription Type**

The Kito Bundle is a non-recurring data pass. It is not a daily or monthly subscription, and users are not automatically charged after the hour expires.

# **Purchase Process**

Users can purchase the Kito Bundle by dialing \*544\*13# on their mobile phones and completing the prompts using airtime or M-Pesa.

# **Repeat Purchase**

The bundle can be purchased multiple times. Once the initial one-hour session ends, users may dial the purchase code again to activate another hour.

# **Post-Expiry Access**

After the one-hour validity period ends, access through the Kito Bundle stops. Users may either purchase the bundle again or continue browsing using their standard data plan if available.

**Definition: Archived Transaction**

An Archived Transaction is a transaction that has been fully completed, closed, and formally removed from active processing. It is stored in a secure, read-only state for record retention, audit, compliance, or historical reference purposes.

Archived transactions are no longer available for modification or active processing and do not exist on the G3 system.

Transactions are archived every six (6) months.

**Accessing Archived Transactions – Work Instructions**

When the front-line team receives a request for an archived transaction reversal, the CEE must raise a **Service Request (SR)**. The SR will be assigned to Second Line Support, who will then proceed with the steps outlined below.

1.       The Support analyst must raise a BMC ticket requesting support from FSS.

2.       The ticket should request for the following transaction details to enable retrieval:

o        Transaction date

o        Debit party

o        Credit party

o        Transaction amount

After FSS retrieves the transaction details, the BMC ticket will be closed with the above details which the Support Analyst will use to process the reversal. If the transaction type is not within the analyst’s authorized permission matrix, the case will be escalated to the relevant team (i.e. 3rd Line Support) for reversal processing.

articleTitle: FTTH Package FUP Counter Reset Process
markdownContent:
**Definition**

This process outlines what to do to address cases where FTTH customers remain on **Fair Usage Policy (FUP)** after a successful package renewal.

**Problem Statement**

**FTTH links remain on Fair Usage Policy (FUP) after package renewal**, resulting in degraded customer experience despite successful payment and renewal and demand at line 400.

**Scope**

This process applies to all FTTH customers whose services do not automatically reset from FUP status after a valid package renewal.

**Prerequisites**

Access to CRM system

Access to Huawei Provisioning Tool

Service Request (SR) creation rights

**Procedure**

**Step 1: Validate Payment in CRM**

Access the CRM system.

Verify that the customer’s package renewal payment is successful and correctly posted.

Confirm the active FTTH package details and renewal date.

**Step 2: Raise Service Request (SR)**

Raise an SR for each affected case under the appropriate category.

Ensure the reference INC000028884225 is included in every SR for tracking and audit purposes.

Add clear remarks indicating that the FTTH link is still on FUP after package renewal.

See below SR creation Guidelines:

Category: FTTH > Types: FUP > Item: Counter Reset

** [Screenshot] 
**

**Step 3: Provisioning Action (Bar/Unbar)** 

Access the Huawei Provisioning Tool [(](https://10.218.250.3:8542/)[https://10.218.250.3:8542/](https://10.218.250.3:8542/)[)](https://10.218.250.3:8542/)

Perform the required bar/unbar process to reset the counters.

Confirm that the FUP status is cleared, and the correct package speed is restored.

**Post-Implementation Verification**

 Recheck the customer link status to ensure FUP is removed.

Validate speed/profile restoration where applicable.

Update the SR with actions taken and resolution details.

**Closure**

Close the SR after successful verification.

Notify relevant stakeholders or customer support teams if required.

**Rollback Plan**

 If the issue persists after bar/unbar, escalate to L2/L3 support with SR reference and provisioning logs.

**Documentation and Audit**

Maintain SR records with CRM validation screenshots/logs.

Use INC000028884225 as the master incident reference for reporting and analysis.

**How the ATM Withdrawal Service Works**

To withdraw, there is a two-step process that customers will follow i.e.:

**Step 1: The Phone Process**

**On their phone,** either via STK (Sim Toolkit), USSD (\*334#), My Safaricom App or M-PESA Super App.

1. Select "withdraw cash." 
2. Choose "withdraw from ATM." 
3. Input ATM number indicated on the ATM. 

The ATM number **555555** is for withdrawals at Pesapoint, Diamond Trust Bank, KCB, Family Bank, NCBA Bank, etc. The Equity Bank ATM number is 286286. 

4. Enter M-PESA PIN. 
5. SMS provides a 6-digit authorization code which is valid for 10 minutes. 

**Step 2: The ATM Process**

**At the ATM,** customer will press the ATM's M-PESA button. 

1. Select language. 
2. Enter the 6-digit authorization code. 
3. Input their Safaricom mobile number. 
4. Enter the withdrawal amount. 
5. The ATM dispenses cash and provides a receipt. 
6. SMS confirms the transaction. 

**Important Time Constraints**

Customer should plan to be at the ATM before generating the code.

The code expires after 10 minutes. If the code expires, the customer will be required generate a new code by initiating the ATM withdrawal transaction afresh, if they wish to withdraw money again.

**Transaction Limits and Restrictions**

**ATM Withdrawal Limits**

- **Transaction Range:** Withdrawals vary from Kes 200-Kes 40,000 depending on the ATM.
- **Multiple Withdrawals:** Customers are allowed to make multiple cash withdrawals from the ATM.

**Account Balance Requirements**

- Customer to ensure M-PESA Account is active and have sufficient M-Pesa balance (including transaction fees).
- Daily transaction limits apply across all M-Pesa services.

**Common Error Causes and Solutions**

| Error Cause | Description | Solution |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Incorrect Details | Entering the wrong M-Pesa PIN, the incorrect 6-digit authorization code, or the wrong mobile number at the ATM. | Customer to re-check all details and retry the transaction carefully. |
| Insufficient Balance | Not enough available funds in your M-Pesa account to cover the withdrawal amount and the associated fees. | Customer to check M-Pesa balance before attempting a withdrawal. Adjust the withdrawal amount accordingly or transfer funds into their M-Pesa account. |
| Technical Glitches | Temporary network issues, power outages, or machine malfunctions (e.g., ATM runs out of cash or paper) can disrupt transactions. | Wait a few minutes and try again or use a different ATM (e.g., KCB, NCBA, DTB, Family Bank, Equity Bank, Co-op Bank, Pesapoint). |
| Expired Voucher | The 6-digit ATM authorization code is only valid for 10 minutes. | Customer to complete the ATM steps within the 10-minute timeframe. If it expires, to initiate a new withdrawal request from their phone to get a new code. |
| Cash not Dispensed | The M-Pesa account is debited but the ATM does not dispense cash. | Customer should note the date, time, location, and amount of the failed transaction, and contact the customer support number indicated at the ATM machine.Customer may also contact Safaricom Care where the Partner / ATM provider is unreachable or takes long to resolve the issue. |

**ATM Withdrawal Reversal**

Note: ATM Providers / Paybill partners perform their reversals after carrying out their due diligence. **Safaricom does NOT initiate ATM Withdrawal reversals.**

Where a customer requests a reversal, the CEE / RCEE will validate that the date of transaction is not older than 30 days. Where transaction is older than 30 days, CEE will give the merchant/partner contacts to the customer to engage the partner for a refund and advise them about the reversal rule.

Where transaction is not older than 30 days, the CEE / RCEE will raise a service request under:

Category: **LNM PAYBILL**

Type**: Reversal Request**

Item: \[Select the appropriate Item based on the nature of the customer’s issue\] **Missing Contact / Non-Functional Contact / Not Assisted by Partner**

**SLA: 72hrs**

**Action for Support Analyst**

Support Team will escalate the request to the ATM Provider / Paybill Partner via email and advise customer on the feedback received.

Tunukiwa is personalized and dynamic. Every day the system refreshes new offers for customers. Validity ranges from midnight, hourly, daily, weekly and monthly offers.

# **Accumulation of Bonga**

Tunukiwa earns you Bonga points whenever you purchase a Tunukiwa offer via M-PESA or Airtime. Since “Buy with Bonga” is a Bonga redemption process, it will not earn Bonga points for the customer.

Tunukiwa is a discounted offer and any amount deducted from the purchase of any of the options will not be considered in the achievement/aggregation of the Stori-Ibambe target. Tunukiwa priority of resource utilization

Bundles are used depending on the order of expiry. If the Subscriber has other bundles, the one that will be used first will be dependent on which one will expire first. Validity can only be extended by purchasing an offer of the same validity.

This is the default option presented to all customers along the purchase journey.

Initially, this was only presented to M-PESA registered customer, but since the introduction of the “Single Subscriber Registration”, this option is available to all customers.

This option will only be available to customers that are eligible for ETU. If a customer attempts to purchase Tunukiwa and their airtime is not enough, they will be awarded Okoa Jahazi to complete the request.

**Airtime + Okoa**

This applies if an ETU eligible customer chose to purchase Tunukiwa via airtime but happens to select an offer that costs more than the available airtime.

Each offer is valid for the time period specified at the time of purchase and validities will range from 24 hours, 48 hours and 7 days.

Offer validity will be specified at the time of purchase.

- Weekly
- Monthly

articleTitle: LNM DIY-(SELF -ONBOARDING) MERCHANT TILL ACTIVATION JOURNEY UPDATE
markdownContent:
To drive till activity and ensure that merchants lines are not recycled and thus **creating demand** below is an updated process following the launch of the new LNM till MSISDN activation process.

Merchant’s who do not activate their till MSISDN within 21 days of creation will receive the following updates.

**Key HIGHLIGHTS:**

**Suspend Tag Implementation:**

- If a merchant does not activate their Till MSISDN within 21 days after creation date, the organization will be tagged with a Suspend status on day 21.
- On day 30 if the merchant has still not done the activation, the Till MSISDN will be recycled, closing the till. The merchant will need to reapply for a new till.

**Suspend Tag Details**

- The Suspend tag will indicate: **"Till MSISDN has not been activated within the required 21-day period since its creation. Merchant should activate via USSD \*234\*2# for the Suspend tag to be removed."**
- Merchant whose till has a **Suspend** tag will not be able to withdraw funds or receive funds in the till.
- Merchants can still activate their Till MSISDN before day 30 (while the **Suspend** tag is still in place) via USSD \*234\*2#, of which this action will automatically remove the Suspend tag and merchant can continue with operation.

**Post-30 Days:**

- If the Till MSISDN is not activated by day 30, the MSISDN will be recycled and made available for another merchant, closing the till.
- If funds are in the store, the Suspend tag will be manually removed to allow merchants to withdraw the funds.
- Merchants wishing to continue using LNM will need to reapply for a new till.

**Affected Merchants:**

- This process applies to **Individual Buy Goods merchants onboarded via the self-onboarding portal from January 17, 2025, onwards.**
- Merchants onboarded before this date or via other channels which is not self onboarding portal will not be affected.

**Merchant Requirements for Till MSISDN Activation:**

Advise the merchant to purchase a YNC DSA SIM card for activation.

**USSD Activation Journey:**

- Dial \*234\*2# from the nominated number.
- Navigate to Account Services > Activate SIM and follow the prompts.
- Enter the YNC DSA IMSI to pair it with the assigned till MSISDN.
- Upon successful activation, the merchant will receive a notification and can start receiving till payment messages.

**Post-Activation:**

- The MSISDN will reflect in CRM within a few minutes after successful activation via the USSD DIY.

**Support Tips:**

- Ensure the merchant uses the correct SIM card (YNC DSA) for activation.
- Confirm the USSD journey is completed successfully before checking CRM.
- Emphasize the importance of activating the Till MSISDN before day 21 to avoid suspension and before day 30 to avoid closure of the till.

**Note:**  If a merchant does not activate their Till MSISDN within 21 days from the day of creation, the till will be suspended on day 21. After 30 days without activation, the MSISDN will be recycled, closing the till. The merchant will need to reapply for a new till.

Weekly

Monthly

If a Paybill/Buy goods partner has set up automatic settlement of funds to bank, they can still settle funds manually via USSD or WEB Portal at any time.  I.e.  A partner doesn’t have to wait for funds to auto settle. He can settle his funds anytime he wants.

articleTitle: Change Primary Notification Number at the Retail
markdownContent:
**Change Primary Notification Number at the Retail**

This is applicable where customer requests or where need is observed for change of primary notification number, during registration of an additional line. This can only be done at the retail outlets and care desks.

Change of notification number is viable for below reasons:

a) Irregular registration.

b) Change of number to a preferred number registered to the same customer. i.e. lost MSISDN, line used by a minor, data line etc.

c) Anomaly in the primary notification number. i.e. number not registered to the customer etc.

CEE will vet and confirm validity of customer request.

Where irregular registration is noted, CEE will suspend the lines as per the applicable procedure.

Where customer is not able to receive the consent notification or where customer requests for change in the primary number.

CEE will validate validity of request. Where request is viable, CEE will action on CRM primary number manager VBC.

Maximum allowed updates per customer are two in a period of six months.

CEE will search the ID on CRM and click on the ID hyperlink.

CEE will navigate to primary number manager VBC.

CEE will be able to view existing primary number and options to either delete or update.

CEE will scan both sides of the ID and attach as a mandatory Requirement.

CEE will select the option to update and will enter the new primary number.

The new primary number must be registered to the same customer and with the same ID.

CEE will attach the scanned ID and then submit the request. Both sides of ID i.e. back and front) in Jpeg or PDF format.

A success pop up notification will appear, and the new changes will apply.

User will select applicable reason for the update done.

CEE will capture interactions and will detail of the changes made and justification for the changes done.

**Deletion of primary notification number**

This is applicable where no alternative number is available to facilitate update of notification number.

This is viable for below reasons:

a) Change of notification number. Applicable where no alternative number is available to facilitate update i.e. where customer doesn’t not wish to use an existing MSISDN registered to them etc.

b) Anomaly in the primary notification number. i.e. number not registered to the customer etc.

c) Irregular registration.

CEE will vet and confirm validity of customer request.

Where irregular registration is noted, CEE will suspend the lines as per the applicable procedure.

CEE will scan both sides of the original ID document as a mandatory requirement.

CEE will search the ID on CRM and click on the ID hyperlink.

CEE will navigate to primary number manager VBC.

CEE will view existing primary number with an option to either delete or update the existing primary number.

CEE will select the option to delete and will attach the scanned ID. Both sides of ID i.e. back and front in JPEG or PDF format.

A success pop up notification will appear, and the new changes will apply.

User will update applicable reason for the update done.

CEE will capture interactions and will detail details of the changes made and justification for the changes done.

**Definition**

The M-PESA Prompt feature allows a merchant to send a payment request to a customer through the M-PESA Business App. The customer then receives a prompt, reviews the details, and authorizes the payment using their M-PESA PIN.

**How to request and approve payments**

To request payments from a customer the merchant will follow the below steps.

The merchant logs in to the M-PESA Business App.

Navigates to the home screen and selects M-PESA Prompt.

Enters the customer’s phone number, amount, and description.

Selects submit to send the request.

After submitting the request, the customer will receive a pop up to enter their M-PESA Pin.

The customer will approve the request by entering their M-PESA Pin.

**How We Ensure Safety of Transactions**

All transactions are secure as all communication between the app and payment services is encrypted.

**How It works**

After the customer confirms the payment.

M-PESA sends the confirmation message to both the merchant and customer.

The M-PESA Business App updates to show the transaction details.

If the customer declines the payment request cancels or doesn’t enter their PIN, the transaction is not processed. The M-PESA Business App will display a “Payment declined” or “Timed out” status.

**Duration for a payment request to be completed**

The payment will be processed instantly.

**What to do if payment doesn’t reflect**

If the payment does not reflect the merchant should.

Refresh the app or check the transaction history.

Confirm with the customer whether the payment was approved.

If still unresolved, contact support with the transaction reference.

**Details included in the payment receipt**

Transaction ID

Transaction status

Amount paid

Merchant name

Date and time

**Definition**

FWA is a Safaricom Fixed Wireless Access which connects customers who are not in fibre ready zones. This document defines the procedure to be followed when engaging and onboarding of potential 5G clients on the different customer engagement touchpoints.

**5G Onboarding and sales leads management.**

A potential customer will visit any of our outlets i.e., Safaricom shop, Franchise, Care desks or dealers’ shops. The customer can also contact customer care on available touchpoints i.e. 100, 200, via social media platform or on existing fixed support lines 400 and 2222 etc. Customer can also visit the Home Tab on Safaricom App and select 5G WI-FI.

**5G Home Onboarding**

·       A potential customer will make a request through a walk in at retail shops, Dealer shops Franchise shops and care desks. The lead will be channeled to Home channels tele sales and advise customer on engagement within 24Hrs.

·       The customer can also engage a field sales agent in the market/estate.

·       The sales agent will establish 5G availability at client’s premise and proximity to site.

·       Customer will provide KYC needed for MSISDN registration and onboarding on the sales portal.

·       Salesperson will register customer on sales portal and submit details.

·       Salesperson will select available routers populated and assign to registered customer to prompt payment.

·       Customers have the option of cash payment or a contract model based on ARPU use for all Safaricom products

·       Customers billing contact will automatically be whitelisted upon payment.

·       The customer will then collect equipment after payment and proceed to set up through DIY.

·       Sales agent will advise customer on available DIY options and on contact to support line 400.

**5G Enterprise Onboarding**

·       A potential customer will make a request through a walk in at retail shops, Dealer shops Franchise shops and care desks. The lead will be channeled to enterprise sales and advise customer on engagement within 24Hrs.

·       The customer can also engage an enterprise sales agent in the field.

·       The sales agent will establish 5G availability at client’s premise and proximity to site.

·       Customer will provide requisite KYC and fills in the application.

·       Salesperson will submit sale on SME tool.

·       SME tool will trigger customer creation SR on CRM.

·       Customer KYC verification will happen on the back end.

·       Once verified order activity will be generated and picked by order management team.

**Order Management**

·       Order manager will confirm that all customer KYC and application form is okay and get a line from Dynamic Sim Allocation system.

·       Order managers will create pre2post Tariff order. (Migrates line to Data Global Tariff. At billing we point to appropriate 5G product for accurate billing).

·       Order manager will create a sales order based on the application form and add device from configurator. If amortized, amortization shall be added as an account product on customer account, then add the amortization period.

·       Order will pick device router + deposit costs, then submit order for credit vetting activity.

·       The credit team shall approve the vetting activity.

·       Order shall generate customer payment notification request and order manager shall notify salesperson to follow up for payment.

·       Customer shall make payment on POS – cashier will receipt cash/cheque for service deposit and 5G router and order shall be complete.

·       Customer will be automatically whitelisted to access support line 2222 after payment.

·       Sales agent will advise customer on available DIY options and on contact to support line 2222.

**Activation**

·       Customer will go to Safaricom shop for line and router collection. Upon payment receipting at the shop, CEE will do SIM replacement and disable SIM Pin.

·       CEE shall trigger Fixed 5G APN provisioning (Fixed 5G bot process, IPNOC)/ TES provisioning.

·       Customer/CEE shall add and activate the product by dialling \*485# or by TES action for outdoor kits.

·       Then the line will successfully be allocated appropriate product and customer notified of successful activation via SMS.

·       Customer will receive welcome email after successful activation.

**5G For Home Routers alternative distribution channels partners:**

In addition to Safaricom shops, Franchise and Care desks, we have onboarded additional alternative distribution channels for 5G For Home Routers.

Quickmart supermarket

Hotpoint appliances

Naivas supermarket (select stores)

Jumia online

Masoko

Khetia supermarket

Kipchimatt supermarket

The 5G routers available subject to stock availability

**Activation**

Once a customer purchases the router, they will have the SIM card attached on the side of the router box.

The customer will have to detach the SIM pouch and Scan the QR code on the back of the pouch, follow the steps to register the new line, receive a One Time Password (OTP) on their Safaricom number.

Enter the OTP and accept terms and conditions to proceed with account activation. The customer can resend the OTP three times if the time expires before they input it. After three tries, the customer will need to wait for 10 minutes before they try again.

Once the account is activated, they will receive a notification on their mobile number that activation is successful

**Support**

**1st Line**

A connected customer will engage Safaricom on all available touchpoints; namely Line 100/200/234, Social media team, Retail, care desks, franchise, and dealer shops.

For Dealer touch point the customer query can be channeled to;

·       Referral to visit any of Safaricom retail shops, Care desks.

·       Call to the Fixed salesperson (Home channels/Enterprise)

·       Call to Line 400 (0722000400) or line 2222(0722002222)

·       Email to Account Manager (Enterprise/Home)

·       Email customer query to [Safaricomhome@safaricom.co.ke](mailto:Safaricomhome@safaricom.co.ke) ,for home 5G and business.support@safaricom.co.ke for Enterprise 5G.

For Safaricom internal touch points, Safaricom retail shop, Franchise, Care desks, social media and Lines 100,200,234 initial checks will be done on Siebel CRM and escalated if beyond their level of resolution. Customer queries which can be address at this level will involve.

·       Payment queries

·       Billing/Due date queries/Usage / Notification queries

·       Account information

**When a customer calls us through line400/2222, the CEE will check on the following before raising an SR.**

·       Check on payment status on CRM.

·       Check/confirm if product is allocated. If not, CEE shall escalate via email to MServiceOrders@Safaricom.co.ke for provisioning to be done.

·       Check on payment status on Allot.

·       Check if APN is provisioned, 5G APN should be 5GFixedWireless.

·       Where APN is not provisioned, the line400/2222 CEE will follow the provided provisioning guideline.

·       CEE will check if link is pushing traffic on Allot.

·       CEE will check the link parameters on GDE SOC tool [https://10.153.68.144:38443/dspcas/login?service=https%3A%2F%2F10.153.68.144%3A38443%2Fportal%2Fweb%2Frest%2Fsso%2Findex%3Fori\_url%3Dhttps%253A%252F%252F10.153.68.144%253A38443%252Fportal-web%252Fportal%252Fhomepage.html](https://10.153.68.144:38443/dspcas/login?service=https%3A%2F%2F10.153.68.144%3A38443%2Fportal%2Fweb%2Frest%2Fsso%2Findex%3Fori_url%3Dhttps%253A%252F%252F10.153.68.144%253A38443%252Fportal-web%252Fportal%252Fhomepage.html) and capture interaction on CRM.

·       Where above parameters are okay, CEE will purge the CI and advise client to reboot the CPE/router and confirm uptime.

·       For slow speeds, CEE will troubleshoot and advise the customer accordingly.

·       Where the above checks are okay, CEE shall raise an SR to Fixed Wireless Team and Enterprise Customer Support respectively to deal.

**Second line support**

·       For issue that cannot be resolved on first line the second line escalation is via SR to

·       Home Fixed Wireless team and Enterprise Customer Support with SLA of 24Hrs.

**FTTH Termination Process**

Where customer contacts other channels other than L400 i.e., L100/200, social media etc.

- CEE will send an email to L400 team through [copsftth@safaricom.co.ke](mailto:copsftth@safaricom.co.ke)  for service termination request. CEE will advise customer on SLA of 48 Hrs.
- Customers may also make calls direct to L400 and via email to safaricomhome@safaricom.co.ke or retail.
- Customers may also visit retail. CEE will send an email to L400 team through [copsftth@safaricom.co.ke](mailto:copsftth@safaricom.co.ke) .
- L400 agent will receive email, calls and emails forwarded to the queue.
- L400 will raise an Incident to the contractor on BMC for router collection.
- L400 will note reasons for termination on the Incident, i.e.

Not in a fiber ready area after relocation.

Customer request.

- Central dispatch will engage the customer within 24 Hrs and will schedule for collection of the router within 48hrs.
- Central dispatch will then send the contractor, who will receive the remedy, contact the customer within 24 Hrs, and will schedule for collection within 48 hrs based on customer availability.
- Contractor will collect the router and close the Incident.

articleTitle: M-PESA Registration Validation Errors & Escalations Retail
markdownContent:
**M-PESA Registration External Validation**

**Background Information**

- The Government of Kenya introduced mandatory registration details for new customers. Therefore, this means that Safaricom has an obligation to register and record customer KYC information in her GSM network.
- M-PESA Customer Registration process will now validate the Customer Names and ID numbers against the government database before successfully registering new M-PESA accounts.
- The details captured by an Agent during customer registration on M-PESA are only stored in G2 database and not validated against any other system.
- Customer Registration Identity External Verification is a functionality that will improve the current customer registration functionality to support the ability to validate customer KYC details as well as customer MSISDN status with external systems.
- Before M-PESA Core G2 registers a new customer, the customer’s MSISDN IN status and KYC will be validated.
- KYC validation will be done against IPRS to confirm customer KYC details as captured by the agent. This will reduce the risk of registering customers with fake IDs.
- If the MSISDN is not in active status on IN or KYC validation fails, then the registration will fail in G2.

**N.B:** The mechanics of the current customer registration journey for agents will remain the same. However, validation will happen on the back end and error messages will be sent to the registering agent in case of failed validation.

**M-PESA VALIDATION AFTER REGISTRATION**

Customers will be allowed to access the GSM services having successfully submitted required KYC documentation for registration. Where validations are still ongoing, the agent will get a notification that the M-PESA registration is pending **validation** and will be activated **within 24hrs**. The customer will not be required to go back to the agent. The M-PESA registration will be progressed once validation is completed.

The message that will be displayed on Partner App for the registering agents is:

***Dear Agent, after successful Line Registration, the customer will access all the other services*** 

***except M-PESA which will be available within 24 hours.***

 Initial PIN for newly registered M-PESA for the very first time is **0000** and customer can change to preferred PIN immediately.

**Guideline on Editing of M-PESA Customer Details**

- We shall no longer be able to change customer details on M-PESA at the call centre e.g., when one letter is missing on the name etc. Customers will instead be referred to a Retail Centre or Care desk for the details to be updated upon presentation of the required statutory documents used during the registration such as a National ID.

**Transactions on Accounts for Irregularly Registered Minors**

- Minors transacting on M-PESA should all be advised to register under

M-PESA Go. 

**Note****:** it will not be possible to send money to any line that is not registered in any mobile network.

- If you receive a call from a subscriber who is a minor and they have registered the account with someone else’s details, inform them that a reversal will be initiated and the money sent back to the sender and to seek assistance from a guardian/teacher or close relative, who will agree for the money to be sent to them to withdraw and deliver to the minor.

Also do let them know about M-PESA Go which is specifically targeting the underage, 10 to 17 years.  M-PESA GO allows them to use M-PESA Services under the supervision of their parent/guardian.  Direct them to register their line via M-PESA Go sub-website; [https://myaccount.safaricom.co.ke/mpesa-go](https://myaccount.safaricom.co.ke/mpesa-go)

- They should advise the owner of the details used during registration to visit the retail centre to have the account registered on M-PESA correctly if they intend to continue using the account.  Also inform them that it will no longer be possible to receive M-PESA or any mobile money on an unregistered line.
- Escalate the name of the agent as shown on the M-PESA system who did the irregular registration of the minor through the 'M-PESA FEEDBACK' Link on the intranet for the agent team to action immediately. In the escalation include:

The mobile number of the minor

M-PESA agent outlet name and location

The agent number (e.g., 12345)

The agent outlet mobile number

- In a case where funds have been sent and the sender is calling, advise them a reversal will be initiated, and the money will be sent back to his/her account.

**NB:** For the reversal request to be initiated change the status of the account to active on the M-PESA system and initiate a reversal.

 **Error Messages on Failed Validation**

 **Fraudulent Subscriber Registration**

- Where customer reports fraudulent use of their ID for line registration, or where during trouble shooting CEE identifies fraudulently registered line(s): -

Proceed to request the customer for their ID for vetting and validation.

Query customer ID(s) on Partner App and /or CRM / M-PESA.

Probe customer on lines registered under their name / ID; CEE will request customer to list all lines known to them.

Advise customers of cases where irregular registration is noted and will assure customer of course of action to be taken. CEE will however not share with the customer the details of the lines registered using their ID’s where not known to them.

Suspend line on CRM and capture interaction, where any line is identified as fraudulently registered.

Where line is registered on M-PESA, CEE will freeze M-PESA at the account level, after effective vetting and add notes on reason for the same. CEE will not raise an SR.

- Confirm whether there’s any loan or where the customer reports that a disputed line has taken a loan with any lending company. CEE will raise an SR on the customer’s account, to Fraud team and include the following details.

Line (MSISDN) that took the loan.

Period when loan was taken.

Loan lending organization e.g., KCB M-PESA/Fuliza/Timiza etc.

Amount taken.

- Where the customer requests for unsuspension of the line is made, CEE will engage customer to present their ID and will vet to validate ownership prior to resuming account.
- Capture key comments on CRM, where applicable.

Raise an interaction and will capture details of action taken and customer ID details.

**Social Media systems Access** 

i.         Online chats, X and Facebook queries will be responded through Social Media WDE system.

ii.         Online support CEEs will apply for social Media WDE access via Service Management suite, the requests will be approved by their respective Team leaders and systems channels support team.

iii.         WDE system will pull customer queries from X and Facebook live pages X direct messages and Facebook inbox and queue them randomly one at a time for CEEs to respond.

iv.         On successful log in the online support, the CEE will click on ready to start receiving customer queries.

v.         X passwords changes will be managed by the Safaricom PR Communications team. Any changes PR communication will communicate to the IPCC team to effect on WDE. Password changes shall be done during off peak hours. 

vi.         On instances where Social Media WDE system is unavailable, and routing of customer queries stops, the team lead in charge of the shift will raise a ticket via Service Management suite for technical team to resolve.

vii.         To access X Live Pages: The online support CEEs will use credentials usually shared by social media team leaders via shared folder. Credentials are shared to the team leaders via email by Safaricom PR COMMS team.

viii.         To access Facebook live page, the CEE will log in using their personal Facebook account and use the moderator rights granted to them by the social media team leaders.

ix.         Online support team Leaders will apply for Safaricom Facebook Administrator rights, through Service Management suite, for approval by respective Manager.

x.         As an administrator, online support Team Leader will be adding fellow Online support team leaders as administrators, give moderator rights to online support CEEs and also remove both administrators and moderators who have changed roles or resigned.

xi.         Online support CEE will be required to apply for moderator rights via Service Management Suite for approval, by respective team leader 

xii.         Once online support team Leader gives moderator rights, Online support CEEs will use their active personal Facebook account to access Safaricom Facebook page. 

xiii.         Online support CEE will log in to the Safaricom Facebook page using their personal Facebook account log in credentials, select Safaricom PLC on Facebook pages section to access the live Safaricom Facebook Page and Inbox.

xiv.         To access X-pro, online support CEE will log in using @safaricom\_care credentials already in the shared folder. 

xv.         X-pro will be used by online support team lead to reply to customer queries sent to the CEO or tagged to the CEO X handle.

xvi.         Online support folder will be provided once the user applies them on service Management suite and approved by respective team leaders.

xvii.         The Online support folder will be used for sending social media reports and Escalations to relevant teams.

**Responding to customers via WDE**

i.         The online support CEE will log in to social media WDE System using windows credentials, and then click on ready to receive customer issues.

ii.         Once the customer issue pops in, the CEE will confirm if it had previous history on WDE or had Siebel interactions, if they are not related, the CEE will continue with the current issue and advise the customer accordingly.

iii.         In case there will be a relationship, the CEE will comprehend the issue before giving out a resolution.

iv.         If the customer shares information that is incomplete/insufficient details, the CEE will advise the customer to clarify or share more details on the same. 

v.         If the customer replies, the query will be queued again and may be picked by a different CEE on shift

vi.         In case the customer issue requires vetting the CEE will either use a call or DM/Inbox depending on the nature of the issue

vii.         Where a query requires customer MSISDN or vetting, online support CEE will check whether customer number exists on WDE or ORT.

viii.         In case, there will be no contact number on WDE the CEE will advise the customer to share it via DM or inbox.

ix.         When the customer passes vetting and the CEE confirms the mobile number of the customer is corresponding to the Facebook account name or X handle, the CEE will save the number on WDE for future reference.

x.         On instances where the customer shares private information on the timeline, the CEE will advise the customer to delete the details to avoid exposure to fraud and instead share the details via DM or inbox.

xi.         All outgoing calls to customers, will be done via WDE system. Customers will be called between **7am – 8pm** unless the customer requests to be called past 8pm. If a customer requests to be called within the stipulated time and the query is received past 8pm due to backlog, the agent will request the customer to confirm if we can contact them immediately, we get their response.

xii.         If the customer called is not reachable or its past 8pm, the customer will be advised via X, Facebook post or chat, to suggest an appropriate time to be contacted. The customer response will be queued again and may be picked by a different CEE on shift.

xiii.         Once the customer passes vetting, the CEE will address the issue as per the current call center procedures and SAKA guidelines.

xiv.         On instances where a customer fails vetting, the customer will be advised to visit the nearest retail shop or care desk for assistance. 

xv.         On instances where the customer query does not require vetting, the CEE will go ahead and respond to them without vetting.

xvi.         The CEE should be able to communicate with either Kiswahili or English effectively and clearly. The choice of the language to opt for will be dictated by the customer. All posts in vernacular will be replied in Swahili. 

xvii.         Where an issue is closed on call, the CEE will send a concluding chat/X/Facebook post indicating the resolution for visibility and enter interactions on Siebel.

xviii.         Online support CEE will respond and close queries by selecting disposition code related to the customer issue then a sign off i.e. (^AL)

xix.         Online support CEE will share NPS survey link to customers via DM/inbox on issues that have conclusively been closed.

**Resolution and Escalation**

i.     Online support CEE, will ensure accurate procedures are issued, show the customer how to do it, vet where necessary, explain on product mechanics- all the relevant information including charges to ensure customer’s issue is resolved fully, as well as FCR is achieved. 

ii.     Online support CEE will educate the customer on DIY procedures.  The CEE is expected to give a digital DIY where applicable. If a digital DIY is not available, the CEE is allowed to give a USSD DIY. DIY procedures shall also apply for all 3rd party queries raised.

iii.     On instances where the online support CEE is not able to fully resolve a customer issue, the CEE will escalate to relevant teams for resolution, either via SR/email. SLA of escalated issues will be shared, to the customer via DM/Inbox or Online chat. SLA of escalated issues will be shared to the customer via DM/Inbox or Online chat.

iv.     Where a customer is following up on an escalated issue that is past SLA, the CEE will apologize to the customer and follow up with the relevant teams via email and cc online support folder and indicate the communication on Siebel as interaction.

v.     Online support folder will be managed by team Leads in three shifts. Morning lead will log in at 5am, afternoon team lead will log in at 2PM and the evening lead at 11pm. They will be expected to:  

Communicate to social media team on any issues that will arise during shift via the folder.

Send hourly report of the channel’s performance. Each report will contain, response time on each channel. If the channels are not real time (RT), they will indicate reasons for the delay.

**NB**: All reports will be shared to COPS workforce Manager

CMWmanager@Safaricom.co.ke and CC all the Online Support TLs using their folder COPS SM TLS copssmtls@Safaricom.co.ke, call   online support folder Onlinesupport@Safaricom.co.ke    call Centre Managers via

CMCallCentreManagers@Safaricom.co.ke

vi.     Escalations to be done via email include: M-PESA corporate  [mpesabusiness@safaricom.co.ke](mailto:mpesabusiness@safaricom.co.ke), Fixed Data to CMCCSDATA2@safaricom.co.ke, Line 300 Line300@Safaricom.co.ke, Line 200 Line2002@Safaricom.co.ke(invoices), Fiber sales Group Mail and FTTH  [copsftth@safaricom.co.ke](mailto:copsftth@safaricom.co.ke).

vii.     To achieve faster resolution on FTTH issues, the email escalation subject will start with SOCIAL MEDIA (in caps) then add your appropriate subject. The email should include:

Issue: A brief of the issue

FTTH A/C:

X handle/Facebook name: Indicate chat if customer contacted us via chat.

Contact: If available/provided.

SR Number: If issue is already escalated.

Any other relevant details.

viii.     Once the ftth team resolve the issue, they will send an email to the Online Support folder indicating the solution. At this point, the team lead on duty will go to the live page and respond to the customer as per the resolution while adhering to our social media guidelines

ix.     For all email escalations the CEE will Cc. Online support folder. For all email escalations on recurrent issues the CEE will Cc. COPSSMTLS on copssmtls@Safaricom.co.ke  and all fixed data escalations on recurrent issues the CEE will Cc. COPSSMTLS on copssmtls@Safaricom.co.ke 

x.     All escalations to retail shops will be done via the Feedback link. All brand related queries escalations will be done via an email to PRCOMMs team on PRComms@Safaricom.co.ke , CC online support folder and COPSSMTLS.

 **Billing queries:**

i.         All disputed billing issues shall be handled via a call. The CEE checks if we have the customer’s number on WDE, if not and where applicable, the CEE will offer a DIY to the customer to help resolve the issue and request for their number via (DM) X or Inbox (Facebook) in case they need further assistance. In the event the customer expresses dissatisfaction with the DIY, The CEE will proceed to call the customer and resolve the issue.

ii.         An acknowledgement tweet or Facebook post is to be made after the call either on the timeline, Facebook wall, DM or Facebook inbox. The only time a billing issue will be resolved otherwise is when the customer clearly indicates unwillingness to be assisted via telephone conversation, when all the available customer contacts are not going through or as otherwise advised by management.

**First Contact Resolution (FCR)**

i.         The rule of FCR shall apply on all online customer queries raised via social media. All Agents will educate the customer by offering additional information when and where necessary by use of URL links to the customer website and other alternatives both digital and USSD DIYs.

ii.         There shouldn’t be any back-and-forth on an interaction because of a wrong resolution, in-exhaustive resolution or unwillingness to assist the customer. In case of multiple messages/ client query posted in segments, the agent that receives the query with complete vetting details shall handle the client’s request. All other agents are required to close the other queries to avoid multiple responses that may confuse the customer. In cases where vetting is not required, then the agent with the most in-depth details will respond.

  **Responding to unique Customer issues**

i.               Unique customer issues are instances where the usual call center practice shall not apply. However, this is subject to change and has to be in accordance with Safaricom policies and regulations.  

ii.               Non-response are cases where the online support CEEs will be advised by online support team leader not to respond to some online comments that touch the company brand or   it is in the businesses best interest not to respond. The Social Media Team Leader will give guidance on which team will be receive the escalation.

**Interactions** 

i.     Interactions will be done on Siebel, which will correspond to the customer issue resolved and the channel used i.e. Facebook, X and Online chat.

ii.     Siebel interactions will be captured as per the below requirements:

All customer queries that require access to Siebel.

M-PESA reversals and all M-PESA queries that require an agent to access the G2 system.

 All Service Request escalations.

All issues that require follow up specifically where the customer number will be provided or will be available on WDE.

Updates and feedback done via online support folder

Repeat queries that have been escalated and not yet resolved. (Where the MSISDN is available)

Escalated issues and repeat issues from any touch point that have contacts or account numbers.

iii.     Where the query does not have the full background content, the CEE shall go to the live page to get the full context to be able to respond on WDE.

articleTitle: M-Shwari Loan Account definition and Mechanics
markdownContent:
**DEFINITION**

This refers to a Micro loan that is given to customers who enrol to M-Shwari Service. Minimum amount is Ksh.1,000 and maximum is Ksh.100, 000 based on the customer’s usage.

**ELIGIBILITY**

This service is eligible to all MPESA customer who opt into the service and qualify.

# **FEATURES OF THE M-SHWARI LOAN**

- Quick access to credit on your phone.
- Loan repayment period is 30 days.
- One-time facilitation fee of 9%, this is a fee charged on the cost of processing the loan.
- Rollover fee of 9% of the principal amount is applied if the customer does not pay within the 30-day period.
- Loan is disbursed directly to the customers M-PESA account.
- Minimum amount is 1,000/=
- Maximum amount is 100,000/= but subject to your credit limit. Your initial credit limit is computed based on your utilization on the following services:

- Safaricom Voice
- M-PESA
- Okoa Jahazi

**QUALIFICATIONS FOR AN M-SHWARI LOAN**

- Have an account with M-Shwari.
- Have a credit limit.

- After enrolling to M-Shwari, the initial credit limit is determined by your utilization on the Safaricom services i.e., Voice, Data, M-PESA and Okoa Jahazi.
- For customers whose score does not qualify them for a limit on day 1, they will be required to save for at least 60 days.
- The 60 days are necessary and enough (according to Banking guidelines) to observe the customer's savings behaviour and distinguish good or bad credit performance in order to take a robust decision on subsequent credit limits.
- Subsequent limit reviews are based on your average M-Shwari savings balance and loan performance i.e., loan uptake and repayment.

- Save with M-Shwari before borrowing. Please note based on this parameter a customer may fail to qualify for a limit.

 **NOTE:** If the above conditions are not met, the Loan Eligibility status will be **loan not allowed** but once the customer has qualified for a loan the status will change to **LOAN ALLOWED.**

**TRANSACTIONAL CHARGES FOR THE M-SHWARI LOAN AND EXCISE DUTY**

An excise duty of 1.5% (20% of 7.5% total loan fees) will be charged on the total loan amount. This will be added to the 7.5% loan fees. The customer will pay 9% (Which is 7.5% plus 1.5%)

| Interest | 7.5% |
| --- | --- |
| Excise Duty | 20% of total loan charges. Which is 20% of 7.5% interest = 1.5%. |
| | |
| Total | (7.5% + 1.5%) = 9% |

Examples of how excise duty and interest are calculated on loan:

| Loan amount | Total Charges at 9% (1.5% + 7.55%) |
| --- | --- |
| Ksh 1000 | Ksh 90 |
| Ksh 5000 | Ksh 450 |
| Ksh 10000 | Ksh 900 |

**M-SHWARI REBATES INCENTIVE (REFUND)**

- This refers to a refund made to a customer if they make a loan repayment within 10 days after reimbursement.
- The refund is 20% of the facilitation fee charged on the Loan.
- It applies to all customers who are eligible for a loan.
- Customers applying & eligible for a loan will get the below SMS message.

 ***“Dear Customer, you will receive a 20% refund of the facility fee on this loan IF you repay it within 10 days from today! Thank you for using M-Shwari.”***

- For customers who qualify, the amount will be credited to the customer's M-Shwari Savings Account **IMMEDIATELY** the customer repays their loan and receive the following message:

 ***“Congratulations! We have refunded <Amount> of the facility fee on your loan into your M-Shwari Account for repaying within 10 days.”***

- If paid on day 11, the customer **WILL NOT** qualify for the 20% refund on the facility fee.
- To confirm repayment time stamp, CEE will go to customer's M-Shwari Savings Account Statement for the specified period, the rebate amount will be visible with a narration **"*loan fee refund***".

  **Worked out Example on the Rebate Incentive.**

| REBATE ON LOAN REQUEST EXAMPLE: | |
| --- | --- |
| Loan Request Amount: | Ksh.1,000 |
| Facility Fee (9% of Loan Amount). | Ksh.90 |
| Loan Repayment.Repaid between DAY 0 and DAY 10 | Principal Amount KES 1,000Facility Fee @ 9%= Ksh 90TOTAL AMOUNT PAYABLE= Ksh.1,090.immediately after repayment customer will be refunded as follows:20% Discount on Facility Fee (Ksh.90) = Ksh.18. |
| Loan Repayment.Repaid on DAY 11 ONWARDS. | Principal Amount KES 1,000Facility Fee @ 9% = Ksh.90TOTAL AMOUNT PAYABLE= Ksh.1,090NO REFUND WILL BE DONE |

**M-SHWARI LOAN RECOVERIES BY WAY OF SET-OFF**

- Mshwari loan recoveries by way of set-off is an extensive recovery exercise conducted by NCBA Bank affecting customers who have defaulted on M-Shwari loan using savings in the customers’ accounts held on the same line or other lines registered using the same national ID.
- The affected customers will be notified through SMS that withdrawal of funds in their accounts have been restricted to facilitate funds recovery.
- Customers will be given 7 days’ notice to repay the defaulted loan before recovery is done. The amount will be held (locked) until the customer pays the loan.

The CEE will be able to know the affected lines under M-Shwari Tab on CRM

**CRM VIEWS**

The CEE will be able to identify the affected lines by checking under MShwari Tab as shown below.

Locked amount: Customer will not access the amount indicated as seen under account.

 [Screenshot] 

After 7 days, NCBA will recover the amount to repay the defaulted loans if customer does not pay. You will be able to see under statement on M-shwari Tab as shown below once recovery is done after the 7 days’ notice.

 [Screenshot] 

- Customer can still deposit and withdraw but will not be able to access the locked amount.
- Once customer pays the defaulted loan the locked amount will be availed to the customer
- Throughout the exercise the customers will be notified through SMS

# **Script Guide**

**The CEE can use below Call script** **to guide your interaction with the customer after normal vetting.**

Once customer raises query on locked funds, care representative to advise as follows:

*Dear (enter Customer name)* *we confirm that we have placed a lock on your M-Shwari Savings Account owing to a defaulted M-Shwari loan. The defaulted loan was taken from a phone number registered under your details. We also confirm that we have issued you a 7-day notice to settle the loan, otherwise we shall utilize the locked funds to repay the outstanding loan.*

# Manual M-Shwari loan repayment

- The process applies in instances where an M-Shwari customer wants to pay for a loan and this is not possible via the M-PESA Menu.
- The instances include:

- - 3rd party loan repayment i.e. paying a loan on behalf of another customer i.e. for persons abroad.
 - Loan payment on a pooled line
 - Loan repayment on a recycled line

- Customer will visit a Safaricom Shop with original ID.
- They will then enroll to M-Shwari with a new line and deposit the funds (equal to outstanding loan amount) to the M-Shwari savings account.
- Fill in a loan repayment form.
- RC CEE will then log the request on SR for the RCSA to deal.
- The analyst will then escalate the request to NCBA via remedy incident.
- NCBA will process within a TAT of 2 working days from the day the form is received from Safaricom
- SLA is 72hrs
- Where customer is able to access their M-PESA account and menu, customer will be advised to initiate loan repayment from their end.
- NCBA will action deletion of recycled accounts as per existing process by receiving bulk files from FS requesting for closure of M-Shwari accounts. 

**Handling Customer Disputes**

If customer disputes the loan, please raise service request on their contact number and proceed to inform customer as below.

***We shall forward your details to our investigations team for review of the information on your outstanding loan. Kindly note that the funds shall remain locked until the matter is resolved.***

 **Interaction Capture on CRM**

Use below to capture interaction. 

| TYPE | SUBTYPE |
| --- | --- |
| M-shwari Loan Account | Loan account statement |

**SR Escalation**

Use below to raise SR only when needed where you need to escalate.

| CATEGORY | Mpesa Mshwari |
| --- | --- |
| TYPE | Customer Loan Account |
| ITEM | Loan Payment Discrepancy |

# **KJSEA Placement Information Guide**

**How to Check Placements**

To check placement results, send the **Assessment number** as an SMS to **22263**.

# **Charges**

Each SMS query is charged **Kshs 30/-**.

# **Incorrect Assessment Numbers**

If an incorrect Assessment number is sent, **no charges will be applied**. You will receive the following message:

**“Dear Customer, no results found for assessment number E.g10204230013, or it does not exist. Please verify the assessment number. KNEC Helpline: 0800724900.”**

# **Multiple Requests**

No charges will apply if the placement message has not been received. 
However, if the placement message has already been sent, the **Kshs 30/-** charge will apply for repeated requests.

# **Results Not Received**

If you request placement information and no feedback is available, you will be informed that the results are unavailable and asked to try again later.

# **Querying Before Release**

If you query placements before they are officially released, you will receive the message:

**“Dear customer, the KJSEA 2025 placements are not available. Kindly try again later after announcement. KNEC helpline 08007224900.”**

# **Insufficient Airtime**

When there is not enough airtime to process the request, you will receive the message:

**“Dear customer, you have insufficient airtime, please top-up to receive your placement information. Query is Kshs 30/-.”**

**Definition**

Roaming is the service that enables customers visiting foreign countries have undisrupted services they were accessing while at home, by connecting them to a network in the visiting country using the same sim cards they were using on their home network.

Roaming services are categorized as:

**Inbound Roaming** **– this allows visitors subscribed to foreign networks to access the local network and services.**

**Outbound Roaming** **- this allows subscribers from the local network to access another operator's network and services in a foreign country they are visiting.**

**Roaming Services** **Offered**

1. Voice
2. SMS
3. voice mail services
4. MMS
5. Directory Services
6. Get it 411

**NB:** GPRS is available in countries that we have roaming agreements with.

**Roaming Countries/Rates**

Customers can roam in over 200 networks around the world. The list of available destinations can be found on [http://roaming.safaricom.co.ke/](http://roaming.safaricom.co.ke/)

**Roaming Activation/Deactivation**

- Post-pay customers will need to activate Roaming service before leaving the country.
- No Activation is required for Prepaid customer since the service is provisioned by default.
- Customers can also activate/deactivate roaming via the following channels:
- USSD: \*200#
- Retail: Customer will visit RC and fill a roaming activation form.
- Email: Customer will send the roaming service activation or deactivation request via email to advantage@safaricom.co.ke 
- The email must be sent from the email address that is registered under the customer’s contact management applet on CRM.
- Relationship Managers: Corporate Customers can also contact their relationship managers for Activation/Deactivation. The relationship managers will liaise with the EBU Support to action on the request and inform customer on resolution.

**USSD Activation/Deactivation Service**

**Eligibility for USSD Roaming Activation**

- This is only applicable to Individual Post-pay and Hybrid customers only.
- Post-pay customers on corporate accounts will not be able to activate roaming via USSD.
- Where the customer is not eligible for USSD activation, or where the USSD fails, customer can have the service activated by sending the request via email to advantage@safaricom.co.ke or visit any Safaricom Retail shop for assistance.

**Note:** Customer cannot activate roaming services via USSD while out of the country. Customer can only use the USSD channel to deactivate roaming while out of the country.

**Roaming Deposits**

The activation of roaming and services where deposit is NIL will be under express application and acceptance by customer & commitment to clear the bills.

Consumer customers will be activated on Express auto bar where the limit is equivalent to deposit and evaluated for upgrade every 6 months with view of upgrading & upselling other services.

New Enterprise SME will be activated on Corporate Auto bar and where the limit is equivalent to deposit under a hierarchy account and evaluated for upgrade every 6months.

Where customers qualify for upgrade, the customers will be engaged to confirm and accept the upgrade, and the segmentation will be effected accordingly.

**Roaming Tariff Advisor**

This is an automated SMS sent to roaming customers informing them of:

- The preferred network
- The charges applicable
- How to manually lock to the network.

The notifications will be once to customer and at zero costs to the customer

Content of the Notification. Two notifications will be sent.

**Welcome Notification**

Sample: Karibu USA! AT&T is our preferred network. To select this network manually, go to: Settings>Mobile Networks>Network operator. For info on roaming partners & rates visit [http://roaming.safaricom.co.ke/mobile/](http://roaming.safaricom.co.ke/mobile/) Dial +254722002200 to contact customer care. Roaming call rates will apply.

**Tariff Advisor**

Sample: You are roaming on AT&T USA. Rates applicable on this network are: Calling Kenya KSh.10/min, receiving calls Ksh.5/min, Local calls Ksh.10/min, sending SMS Ksh.10/SMS & data KSh.14/Mb. Rates may change on switch to other networks. Visit [http://roaming.safaricom.co.ke/mobile](http://roaming.safaricom.co.ke/mobile) for more details.

**Key features on Roaming Tariff Advisor**

Receipts of notification when not activated on roaming: These are network-initiated notifications that will automatically be sent to the customer as soon as they attach to any network while roaming.

When customer fails to manually lock to the preferred network: The phone automatically connects to the strongest network available and may keep switching networks from place to place depending on signal strength.

To manually lock the network settings: Go to: Settings>Mobile Networks>Network operator and select the preferred network. 

**Roaming Billing/Usage and Country Codes/Zones**

The rate to make a call while roaming depends on the country where one is roaming. Click [http://197.248.2.35/roaming/](http://197.248.2.35/roaming/) for roaming charges.

Roaming is charged on per second billing and Data usage is billed in minimum increments of 10 KB (Kilobytes). The charges are available on the website [http://roaming.safaricom.co.ke/](http://roaming.safaricom.co.ke/)

**Roaming Diverts**

Customers roaming in various countries can divert calls back home to be received back home. ***Note however*** that applicable roaming rates will apply for the diverted call for calling back to Kenya. E.g. Roamer in UK will be charged roaming rate: UK to Kenya.

**Resolution to Billing/Usage queries**

- The Roaming charges will reflect on the bill: The calling charges will reflect with the country code e.g., +195\*\*\*\*\* the SMS charges will reflect as messages sent to the SMS centre number +254722500029.
- The roaming bill will be sent via Invoice: the customer will get an invoice on arrival to Kenya a month after roaming. The roaming bills may be received up to a maximum of 3 months after roaming. 
- Use of short codes, e.g. 111, 100 and 200, is subject to availability on the foreign network. 
- Subscribers cannot be able to receive calls using promotional / free airtime, e.g., Bonga Points redeemed as minutes, Okoa Jahazi airtime advanced. 
- The Minimum account balance that subscribers need to maintain to ensure that they can receive calls while roaming on Vodacom East Africa is a minimum account balance of at least Kshs.10/-
- Customer will be barred when they reach their credit limit. In this case customer will need to make a prepayment to continue accessing roaming service.

For Roaming charges use the link [https://roaming.safaricom.co.ke/](https://roaming.safaricom.co.ke/)

Country Codes/Zones : To get country codes use the link [https://cmintranet/index.php/products-a-services/roaming/prepay-roaming?start=5](https://cmintranet/index.php/products-a-services/roaming/prepay-roaming?start=5) 

Country Zones: To get various Country Zones use the link [https://cmintranet/index.php/country-info/country-zones-kenya](https://cmintranet/index.php/country-info/country-zones-kenya)

Click [https://roaming.safaricom.co.ke/](https://roaming.safaricom.co.ke/) to view. for the reviewed roaming, international calling rates and country codes.

**Benefits of Post-pay/Prepay Roaming**

- Stay in touch on your number.
- Ease of use: With the simple keying in of numbers, you can initiate a call, top-up or conduct a balance enquiry anytime, anywhere you are.
- Wide Coverage:
- Choice: Customer can choose between activating Voice Roaming or Data Roaming and/or both. USSD channel gives you the opportunity to select either ‘Voice and SMS only’ or ‘Data, Voice and SMS’.

**Customer Service Accessibility**

A roamer may call host network's customer care to inquire about any issues they are experiencing.

Contact Safaricom Customer Care:

- Prepay dial +254 722 002 100
- Post-pay dial +254 722 002 200
- Via our social media touch points.
- X: @SafaricomPLC and @Safaricom\_Care
- Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/SafaricomPLC i.e., Safaricom Kenya Official Page
- Chat online via Self-care page.
- e-mail: customercare@safaricom.co.ke or advantage@safaricom.co.ke

How to access Roaming Rates per destination: Click [https://roaming.safaricom.co.ke/](https://roaming.safaricom.co.ke/)

**ROAMING IN THE USA**** 
Safaricom has partnered with AT&T Network to launch VoLTE service. This will give our customers an opportunity to enjoy cheaper roaming rates on AT&T network.**

AT&T is exclusively available on 4G. For one to Use Voice and send SMSs, they need to be on VoLTE (Voice over LTE or Voice over 4G)

**ROAMING IN AUSTRALIA**

Please note that all our roaming partners in Australia have phased out or terminated/2G&3G technologies. They only have 4G&5G. What does this mean to our customers?

·       Our customers must have 4G/5G capable phones. All phones that support 2G&3G only will be blacklisted or blocked by our roaming partners in Australia.

·       The customers’ phones must support VoLTE.

·       The customers’ SIM cards must be LTE capable and support VoLTE.

·       The network mode that the customers will select is **5G/4G**/3G/2G or **4G**/3G/2G and choose the networks that offers 4G&VoLTE manually.

·       The line must be provisioned for VoLTE on the HSS.

·       The customer must enable VoLTE on the phone.

In Australia, we have the following networks that support **4G or LTE and VoLTE**

·       Optus

·       TPG Telecom/Vodafone

·       Telstra: This supports 2G & 3G only. So, our customers will not be able register on this network.

**VoLTE Requirements**

- A VoLTE capable handset – can be checked on the internet.
- A VoLTE provisioned line – can be self-provisioned via USSD \*100# or \*200# / Provisioned by Safaricom (Roaming/CSDB teams)
- Turning on VoLTE on the handset – can be checked on the internet.

**NOTE**

- Data is also only available on AT&T.
- One does not need data on for VoLTE
- GPRS should not be barred on HLR. This is because, once GPRS/GPRS roaming is barred on HLR, the initial background data session required to setup the VoLTE session will not be allowed.
- USSD services are not available on VoLTE as yet, but we are working on it.
- Customers will ONLY be able to access Voice and SMS service on T-Mobile but can enjoy Voice SMS and Data services on AT&T VoLTE network.
- T-Mobile is for now only available on 2G for Voice SMS and USSD. The coverage is however limited as they are phasing it out

# **ROAMING IN TURKEY**

Turkey has banned all permanent Roamers on their networks. If any of our customers stays in Turkey for more than 90 days, without registering the IMEI with the MNOs, the IMEI gets backlisted. It will no longer be used.

Kindly note that informative SMS is usually sent by the MNOs to the devices which will be affected from permanent roaming regulation. Our customers should not ignore such messages.

**Who is a permanent Roamer?**

This is a cumulative user of roaming services by the same IMEI for 91 days.

**Conclusion**

Our Subscribers will face registration failures due to illegal IME/blacklisted IMEIs.

**What the customer can do**

The subscriber of the terminated device should get in contact with VF(Vodafone) or Turkcell Turkey local dealers and make a new activation with their Foreigner Identity Number (YKN) and register the device to be used only with this new subscription by logging in with their Foreigner Identity Number (YKN) via e-Devlet.
