# **What is split payment**

This is where a payment is made to a short code, but instead of the entire amount staying in that short code, a portion of it needs to be sent to **another short code.**

An example would be money is paid to ride hailing app short code, and then a spit is made to the driver of the ride hailing app being their share from the trip.

**How it works**

**Payment to Short code A**:

The initial payment is made to Short Code A, which has been configured for split payment.

**Splitting the Payment**:

Upon receiving the payment in Short Code A, a portion of the amount is then transferred or distributed to Short Code B. This is done **automatically** as per the preconfigured rules. The amount to be split can be defined as a percentage of the original transaction or as an absolute amount, e.g. Kshs 50 for each transaction.

**Remaining in Short code A:**

After the split, the remaining amount in Short Code A is the portion that was not sent to Short code B. This remaining amount might be used for other purposes or kept in the account for future transactions.

# **Charges**

Normal transaction charges for B2B and B2C.

# **Eligibility**

In the initial phase, it will be Paybill customers with B2B and/or B2C products. We will, however, open it up to till customers.

# **How to apply for the service**

In the pilot phase, only a few partners will be onboarded before opening it up to

the masses.

# **Access channels for the services**

USSD through \*234# and the business app.

# **Business rules**

The ensuing B2B/B2C will be charged as per the current tariffs.

The split transaction must be less than the original transaction. Thus, where split amount is defined as an absolute that is greater than the original transaction, no split occurs. For example, split amount defined as KES 50, but customer pays KES 40, no split occurs.

Reversals will be treated in the same way as they are currently. A call will

be made to party B before reversing from party B also to party C before

reversing from party C.

The whole amount will be reversed from party B to party A.

The split percentage can be specified to two decimal points.

The split amount can be specified to two decimal points.

**NB:** For this deployment we will only **pilot** with two internal teams for POC. We will use the internal testing production USSD with a whitelist of the two pay bills.

Solution will be exposed to the public after pilot testing confirms the solution works as expected.

| Feedback | Comment |
| --- | --- |
| An Email or SMS to be sent to both the Sender(splitter) and Splitee when actions are performed (Activate, delete, update) | For Pilot phase, we have the USSD pop up notifications, however, on the version two before going live, we will implement the SMS and/or Email notifications. At the moment both parties get the usual transactional M-PESA Messages. |
| | |
| Are Terms and conditions being saved? Can they be retrieved upon request? | Yes, this covered on the registered date that is logged as the acceptance of terms is mandatory before activation. On version 2 we will add the flag indicating the Yes/No actions and any other important data we can capture. |
| Outline the reversal process and document it on the terms and conditions | This has been updated on the terms and condition document attached on this mail |
| | |
| Have an access matrix for CRM. Do not allow all CCEs activate | Yes, Only Support teams will be able to Resume/reactivate service after suspension. The CEEs will only be able to Suspend and Delete all upon merchant's request. |
| | |

 **Some important Updates on the solution**

- We intend to use it for internal **pilot by Ratiba and EBU Fiber team Resellers.**
- We will only Pilot with **B2B splits between a pay bill to a pay bil**l only.
- The split rate type for piloting is **Percentage share**.
- We can split up to a **maximum of 3 recipient pay bills**. However, the total amount to be split should not exceed 99%
- We have a **new Reason type** for reporting and management purposes - **Split Business Pay Bill via API**
- **Reversals are happening** (the current journey on G2 will be used). The current Reversal process for C2B and B2B applies
- The channel to be used for management **on pilot is USSD**, the M-PESA business portal and App will be in the next iterations. We will whitelist the two short codes for piloting on USSD.
- We have an endpoint that can be used by the Operations team during Short code **recycling to delete all splits activated.**
- A merchant cannot activate or split to a short code that is not active on G2(Frozen, suspended, New, Closed)
- We have **Hakikisha to prevent splitting to wrong shortcodes** during onboarding on the USSD journey
- **CRM views developed;** CEES can view, suspend all and Delete All activated split accounts on behalf of merchants after vetting. The Resume/Activate action will only be available to Merchants Support Analysts after proper vetting. (Normal Vetting process applies).

# **Magic Voice Service**

This is a service that allows changing your voice or your background while making a mobile call to your callers on your safaricom line.

# **How Magic voice works**

Users will be able to change their voice as they initiate call to sound like a male, female or cartoon voice. Users will also be able to change their background/Ambience i.e. traffic, music, concert etc.

# **Opt in**

Dial \****07*\*\*\*\*\*\*\* or dial 24000**

Users will then be directed to magic voice IVR, where they will select the voice/background ambience of choice. They will then be connected to their caller with the changed voice/background.

# **Opt Out**

You will dial the magic voice short code 24000 and follow the prompts to unsubscribe or send STOP to 24000.

# **Mechanics**

Will my call be disconnected if the magic voice does not go through?

Yes, the call will disconnect, and caller will proceed to dial the number without the \*(Asterick)

# **Eligibility**

Service will be available to all Safaricom customers.

# **Charges**

There are two offerings for the service.

- Daily charge @ Kshs 10
- Weekly charge @ Kshs \*\*\*(To be announced)

**Will I be charged every time I initiate a call?**

No.Users will only be charged once according to their subscription package. Once daily or weekly. They will be able to use service during the validity period.

*Normal call rates will apply according to individual rates once call is connected.*

***NB: This service is an auto renew service and users will need to unsubscribe to stop daily or weekly deductions.***

# **Tuunza Mapato**

**Definition**

Tuunza Mapato is a simple and affordable insurance plan that offers small business owners’ coverage for hospitalization and funeral expenses.

**Eligibility for Tuunza Mapato**

This product is available to all Safaricom M-PESA customers.

**What Tuunza Mapato Covers**

It compensates for hospitalization and provides funeral expense support. It pays out up to 30 nights of hospital stay annually and provides funeral expense support for your beneficiaries.

**Available cover plans**

Tuunza Mapato offers four plans with different coverage levels and premium costs to suit your needs:

Msingi-Self

Msingi-Family

Bora-Self

Bora-Family

**Benefits of the cover plans**

**Msingi Cover** pays Ksh 1,000 per night for up to 30 nights of hospitalization per year and Ksh 100,000 for funeral expenses per person covered. You can choose to cover yourself or yourself + 4 family members (children or spouse)

**Bora Cover** pays Ksh 2,000 per night for up to 30 nights of hospitalization per year and Ksh 200,000 for funeral expenses per person covered. You can choose to cover yourself or yourself + 4 family members (children or spouse)

**Cost for each cover plan**

Each plan has a weekly premium:

Msing-Self: Ksh 60

Msingi-Family: Ksh 240

Bora-Self: Ksh 100

Bora-Family: Ksh 400

**Tuunza Mapato Provider**

Tuunza Mapato is offered through a partnership between Safaricom and Turaco Microinsurance Limited, combining our platform with their insurance expertise.

**Hospitals that a customer go to for inpatient service**

Customers may seek treatment at any level three (3) to level five (5) public or private hospital that is registered by the Ministry of Health for in-patient care.

**How to subscribe to Tuunza Mapato**

The customer will Dial \*334# and follow the prompts under Tuunza Mapato to subscribe. They will be required to review and accept our terms & privacy policy of the product to opt in.

**How to pay for Tuunza Mapato premium**

Payments are automatically deducted weekly from the account that the customer selected during opt-in. The first two weeks of your subscription are free.

**Coverage Details During the Free Cover Period**

During the free cover period the customer is only covered for hospitalization resulting from accidents only.

**Impact of Missed Tuunza Mapato Payments**

If a customer misses Tuunza Mapato payments the cover will not be active the following week. If the customer misses’ payments for four weeks in a row, Tuunza Mapato cover will stop, and they will not be eligible to claim the benefits.

**Cover Duration**

The cover will run for a period of 1 year from the time of purchase. At the end of the cover period, you will be required to purchase a new cover.

**Adding of a beneficiary to a cover**

A customer can add beneficiaries within the first 30 days of purchasing a cover and during the last month of the 1-year policy before renewal.

**How to Add a Beneficiary After the 30-Day Deadline**

If a customer wants to add a beneficiary to their plan after 30 days, the customer can contact Turaco on 0800 221 245 (Toll Free) for assistance with updating of their beneficiaries.

**Number of beneficiaries that can be added to a cover**

A customer can add up to 5 beneficiaries to their family cover, including spouses and children.

**Allowed age limits allowed for beneficiaries**

The allowed age limits for beneficiaries are children between 0 to 25 years and spouses between 18 to 75 years to your cover.

**Adding of next of Kin**

A customer can add their next of kin any time during the cover period for support in case of a claim.

**Changing of the cover plan**

A customer can only change a plan at the point of annual cover renewal (30 days before or after the policy renews).

**What to Expect When You Cancel or Opt-Out of Your Cover Plan**

When a customer cancels or opts-out of a cover plan, the cover plan and weekly deductions will stop, and they will not be able to make any claim.

**Reactivating a cover plan after cancelling**

A customer can reactivate a cover plan after cancelling. However, it will be subjected to a two-week waiting period.

**How to reactivate a cover plan**

Dial \*334#, select ‘View cover plan’ under the manage cover menu and follow the steps.

**Opting Back in and Changing Your Plan**

The customer won’t be able to choose another cover plan, previous cover plan will start again. They will be subjected to a two-week waiting period.

**Meaning of waiting period**

The waiting periods means that during the waiting period, the customer is covered for claims resulting from accidents only.

**How to file for a claim**

Dial \*334#, select ‘Claims’ under the Tuunza Mapato menu and follow the steps. Turaco will contact you after you submit your claim.

**Documents required to process a claim**

Proof of hospitalization or death, and any other documents as shall be advised by Turaco.

**Timeline for claim process**

Turaco shall pay all claims within 3 business days of receiving all necessary documentation and internal verification.

**How to receive the claim**

The customer will be paid directly to M-PESA after a successful claim.

**Time limit for making a claim**

There is a time limit for making a claim, all claims should be reported within a maximum of 7 (seven) days after the occurrence of the claim event.

**Queries or Support**

For any queries or support, customers can contact Turaco for free on 0800 221 245, Monday to Friday between 8 AM to 7 PM and Saturdays from 8 AM to 1 PM, except on public holidays.F

**Definition**

**KYC** – Know Your Customer is the mandatory process of identifying and verifying the identity of a customer when opening an account and periodically over time. This is to ensure that the customers are genuinely who they claim to be.

**Tiered KYC**

ALL M-PESA customers were moved to tier 2 and monthly an yearly limits no longer apply except for IMT that require different KYC documentation of various levels and its segmented based on annual transaction values as below:

- Tier 1 – 100,000 (maximum of Kshs.100,000 annual transaction values per annum).
- Tier 2 – 3 Million (maximum of Kshs.2- 3M annual transaction values per annum).
- Tier 3 - 10 Million (maximum of Ksh.10M annual transaction values per annum).

**M-PESA ACTIVATION**

The status of the account will differ depending on the different scenarios.

# **M-PESA Account Status**

- Pending active status.
- Mobile Active status.
- Suspended status.
- Frozen account.
- Capped account.
- Closed account.

**Pending Account**

If the customer does not pass Vetting, refer the customer to a RC for assistance.

The Support Analyst shall track the progress of the BMC, advise the customer as per resolution and close the SR.

In addition to the verbal education, send the M-PESA activation guide via SMS from CRM SMS Templates:

- Go to M-PESA.
- Choose Activate.
- Enter your current M-PESA PIN.
- Repeat the current PIN.
- Enter ID Number.

- Chagua M-PESA.
- Chagua Wezesha.
- Weka Namba ya Kuanzia(PIN yako).
- Weka PIN mpya(PIN yako)
- Rudia PIN yako
- Weka ID.

If the customer does not still get the menu, the CEE shall advise the customer to change handset and try to activate again.

This refers to the set limits for M-PESA transactions and applies to all M-PESA users. 

**New M-PESA**

- Maximum daily transaction limit: Ksh.500,000.
- Maximum balance an M-PESA a/c can hold: Ksh.500,000.
- Maximum limit per transaction: Ksh.250,000.

Customers will no longer need to sign the logbook at an M-PESA agent shop during withdrawal and deposit transactions.

# **M-PESA Limit Rules**

Below are the M-PESA customer minimum and maximum transfer/send limits.

# **M-PESA TRANSACTIONS**

Listed below are transactions that can be done on M-PESA

- M-PESA Deposits.
- M-PESA Withdrawals.
- M-PESA ATM Withdrawals.

**Eligibility**

M-PESA transactions are available to all M-PESA registered customers.

**M-PESA Deposits**

M-PESA deposits is a process of changing **Cash** money to **E-money,** which is done by an authorized M-PESA agent. 

**M-PESA Withdrawals**

M-PESA Withdrawals is the process of changing E-money to Cash money and can only be done from an authorized M-PESA Agent. A customer is required to visit an M-PESA agent with the original ID to do the withdrawal.

**M-PESA ATM Withdrawals**

M-PESA Withdrawals is a service that allows withdrawals from M-PESA Accounts via Selected Bank ATMs. Customers can withdraw a minimum of Ksh.200 and a maximum of KSH250,000.

Once the customer completes the withdrawal and gets a confirmation message, the agent will also get a message on their M-PESA agent transacting till. The customer will present the original ID for the agent to record and disburse funds.

**Where to perform ATM Withdrawals**

M-PESA ATM withdraw can be done form the below selected ATMs.

- Pesa Point ATM’s – Agent Code 555555
- Diamond Trust bank ATM’s – Agent code 555555
- KCB- Agent code 555555
- Family Bank-Agent code 555555
- NIC-Agent code 555555
- Fina Bank- Agent Code 555555
- Equity ATM’s – Agent code 286286
- CO-OP Bank-Agent code 472472 

**Funds deducted from M-PESA but not dispensed from the ATM**

Contact the bank you have withdrawn from via their customer care number.

The customer care contact is provided in the ATM lobby which is a chargeable line as per the prevailing calling rates.

If there is no contact, contact M-PESA customer care on 234 from your Safaricom line for assistance with the bank’s contact number. 

**How To Cancel a Transaction**

- Type any letter and **SEND** within 25 seconds to STOP the transaction.
- Pressing cancel/dismiss or close will only remove the pop-up message but will NOT stop the transaction from completing.
- Different phones have different screen message commands.
- The service will work on most handsets, however, there may be few phones that may have challenges accepting the service, in such a case customer can use a different phone.
- Hakikisha is available in countries where a Safaricom customers can roam however, you will only be able to cash in/cash out your M-PESA balance at M-PESA Agent outlets in Kenya and as provided by M-PESA Global.

# **M-PESA Transaction Statuses**

This refers to different status of a transaction after it is initiated and not completed.

- Authorized status.
- Cancelled status.
- Declined status.
- Expired status.

**Authorized Transactions**

Transaction is said to be in authorized state if the following occurs:

- A transaction that has been initiated in the M-PESA system and is pending completion.
- A transaction that occurs when the recipient/initiator of the transaction has not received the confirmation message.
- When the communication between the Safaricom SMS system and the M-PESA system is not completed.
- Funds in authorized status will be viewed when checking account balance but can only be available and active once the transaction is completed.

**Cancelled Transactions**

**Agent Deposit**

Advise them to visit the same agent to repeat the transaction afresh as currently on the system, the transaction requests sent earlier have been declined or cancelled.

**Customer to Customer**

Advise the customer to request the sender to resend the cash or should resend the cash if he/she was the sender. 

**Declined Transactions**

This is a transaction that has **NOT** gone through for any number of reasons. The reasons can be:

- When the subscriber’s account does not have enough funds.
- If the account rules have been broken, for example, the maximum daily transfer amount of Kshs.500,000 has been reached or during M-PESA system outages.
- There are no balance changes in the account statement. Funds are not transferred at all.
- Check on transaction for the system reason for declining. If the reason is because the receiving account will exceed the maximum limit, advise the customer(sender) to request the recipient to contact us for guidance.
- If the reason is that the senders account has exceeded the daily limit of Ksh.500,000 advice the customer that he can only send again after midnight.
- If the reason is insufficient funds, check on M-PESA system if there is any authorized transaction then proceed to assist as per guidelines above.
- If not advice customer that he does not have funds to send the transaction.

**Expired Transaction Status**

- These are transactions timed out on the system after remaining on authorized status for a certain period without getting completed either manually or automatically.
- For expired transactions advice the customer the money is reversed back to the sender’s account.
- For Initiated reversal it expires within 14 days, funds remain with recipient.

# **M-PESA ACCOUNT STATUS**

**Mobile Active Account Status**

This is an active M-PESA account with a SIM serial number attached to it.

This is a fully registered M-PESA identity that received a Start PIN, and a customer has already activated and chose a secret PIN of their own.

The account can now send and receive e-money and perform other functionalities within the e-wallet.

**Pending Active Account Status**

If the account is registered on M-PESA but not active or activated, the status will be Pending Active.

The customer may have received start key and did not use it to activate the account.

**Customer already has a Start Key**

Search the number and check the identity status on the M-PESA G2.

If it is pending active, confirm if they have received an initial PIN within the last 24 hours and advise on the activation procedure below:

- Go to M-PESA menu.
- Select Activate or Wezesha.
- Enter Initial (start PIN) PIN.
- Enter new PIN.
- Confirm new PIN.
- Enter DOB or ID No.
- Send the request to M-PESA.
- A message will be received confirming the activation of the account.

**Customer who has deleted /not received a Start Key**

If a customer claims they have not received or have deleted the initial PIN, the CEE should vet the customer and issue start key with the below vetting details.

- Search the number on G2.
- Confirm Customer’s full names.
- Confirm ID number.
- DOB or registration date as per G2.
- Go to Reset PIN and enter vetting details.
- Customer will receive a PIN.
- Advise the customer on activating. 

**Suspended Account Status**

This is the status where the account is temporarily withheld from transacting though the account can still receive money.

A suspended identity cannot initiate funds transfers and withdrawals.

Reasons for suspending an M-PESA account will include: -

- M-PESA Fraud; Done by the M-PESA Fraud Team at the Identity Level on G2.
- Multiple registrations; Done by AML at the Account Level on G2.
- Customer Request: Done by RC or Contact Center Staff at the Account Level on G2.
- Jitambulishe self-served Sim-Replacement; Suspension done for 24hrs.

**For suspended accounts due to Expired passports, Please note as below:**

| ISSUE | AML GUIDANCE |
| --- | --- |
| Expired Passports (Suspended accounts) | 1.    Customer M-PESA account has a customer_suspended_tag with reason indicated as expired passport.2.    M-PESA account has funds.3.    Customer shows up at retail shop, but they do not have their new/valid passport and request to be allowed to access/withdraw the funds on the account.4. Check on audit logs on when the customer was barred by AML. Only proceed if the suspension is still within the 1-month grace period.5. Where the 1-month grace period has elapsed, advice customer to bring a valid document for KYC update.6.    Customer must provide the expired passport used during account creation.7.    CEE to vet thoroughly as per process. If vetting is passed, CEE to remove tag, customer withdraws his/her funds then CEE to reinstate the tag (restore the suspension)  8 Advice the customer that once the grace period elapses, they will have to bring in the valid document for KYC update. |

**NOTE: Change of ownership using expired passports is not allowed.**

**Frozen Account Status**

An identity is changed to frozen by the fraud team due to suspicion of fraud or for investigation purposes or any other warranting reason.

Frozen identities cannot transfer or receive funds.

All unfreezing requests will be channeled to M-PESA Fraud via SR. 

**Capped Account Status**

An account enters the capped state when a customer exceeds the set limit for the day or exceeds the maximum amount allowed limit of an account.

**Exceeds limit for the day:** **\-** Customer will wait till midnight to be able to transact again.

**Exceeds the maximum limit of an account:** **\-** Transfer funds to create space to receive other amounts. 

**Closed Account Status**

- This is an inactive customer identity.
- A customer can request his identity to be closed by writing a letter and present it to a Retail shop requesting his M-PESA Account to be closed.
- This is also the final state of an identity once a customer is recycled.
- **PLEASE DO NOT CLOSE** customer accounts without a customer’s written authorization.

# **THIBITISHA SERVICE (VICINITY CHECK)**

**Definition**

This is a solution aimed at dealing with erroneous deposits and withdrawals.

The transaction (Deposit or withdrawal) will only be completed if the agent and the customer are in same location.

**Eligibility**

It is eligible to all Safaricom subscribers using M-PESA and M-PESA agents. 

**Benefits**

Address customer pain points by eliminating erroneous deposits and withdrawals.

- Improve customer NPS by eliminating losses arising from erroneous deposits.
- Optimization of Customer Operations by eliminating demand arising from erroneous withdrawals and deposits.
- KYC and Regulatory compliance by ensuring that the agent and customer are at the same location during withdrawals and deposits.
- KYC and Regulatory compliance by ensuring that the customer’s identification is verified during transaction.

**How It Works**

**Deposits**

- Thibitisha will be used to check that deposits are made to the correct customer number.
- If the customer’s handset is not physically close to the agent taking the deposit, then the deposit could be rejected.
- It will also help to ensure that the deposit was not part of a “direct deposit” that is used by customers to avoid Send Money charges.
- Response if an agent deposits to customer in different location.

**English:**

- Failed. Please ensure the customer is at your shop and you have verified their document of registration before attempting to deposit.

**Swahili:**

- Imefeli. Hakikisha mteja yuko kwa duka lako na umethibitisha maelezo kwa hati ya kitambulisho kabla ya kuweka pesa.

**Withdrawals**

**Withdrawals can fail due to the following scenarios**

- If the customer is not at the shop where they are doing the withdrawal, then the transactions will fail.
- If it is established that the agent and customer location at the time of transacting is not the same, the transaction will not take place.
- Response if a customer withdraws at a different location from agent.

**English:**

- Failed. Kindly ensure you are at the M-PESA Agent shop before attempting to withdraw.

**Swahili:**

- Imefeli. Hakikisha uko kwa duka la ajenti wa M-PESA kabla ya kujaribu kutoa pesa. 

# **HAKIKISHA SERVICE**

**Definition**

This is a service that enables M-PESA customers to confirm the name of the person/ organization / merchant that they are they are transferring money to/withdrawing from and gives them an option to cancel the transaction.

The service is also active for Super Agency Transactions (Business Deposit and Business withdrawal).

The transacting MSISDN must have the CNS Flag “Yes” on G2 for Hakikisha to work.

**Eligibility**

Hakikisha service is eligible to all M-PESA registered customers and is **NOT** eligible to M-PESA Global transactions since the Recipient records are not in M-PESA data base.

**Difference between transacting on My Safaricom App and Transacting on the current M-PESA Menu (STK Menu)**

**On my Safaricom App**

- The Hakikisha confirmation step comes before entering the M-PESA PIN.
- You may receive a notification pop up (STK Push) to enter your M-PESA PIN.
- Needs internet connection to open the App.

**On M-PESA menu (STK)**

- The Hakikisha confirmation comes after entering M-PESA PIN.
- It gives 25 seconds to cancel the transaction.
- Does not need data connection to open.

**Customer Education on Hakikisha**

When a customer calls for a reversal, assist them as per their request then proceed to cross-sell Hakikisha service by sending an educational SMS via Siebel as below.

**English SMS:**

- Jambo, M-PESA now indicates the name of the person or organization to whom you are sending money. To STOP a wrong transaction, type any letter and send. Thanks.

**Swahili SMS:**

- Jambo, M-PESA itakuonyesha jina la mtu au kampuni unayotaka kutuma pesa. Kukatisha shughuli iwapo jina sio sahihi bonyeza nambari yoyote kisha tuma. Asante.

# **Change** **of Organization Name**

This applies when a merchant/ partner changes the name of their business but wishes to retain the existing short code. In such cases, a request is made to update the business name accordingly.

Merchants/partners who opt to change their organization name, shall use the below available channels:

Send an email to [M-PESABusiness@Safaricom.co.ke](mailto:M-PESABusiness@Safaricom.co.ke) using the organization’s registered email.

Visit Safaricom Retail/ Franchise.

EBU account management teams i.e., Large Enterprise Account Managers, EBU in life team, SME/SOHO Sales Team

For requests received at the Retail centre/ franchise or via the M-PESA Business folder, an SR shall be raised to LNM Support team to action within 24hrs SLA.

***SR Category: LNM BUY GOODS AND SERVICES***

***SR Type: Account Name Change***

***SR Item: Change of Name/ Change of Ownership (as per request)***

***SR Category: LNM PAYBILL***

***SR Type: Change of KYC Details***

***SR Item: Change of Organization Name***

Relationship/ account managers shall send requests received via email to [lnmaggregators@safaricom.co.ke](mailto:lnmaggregators@safaricom.co.ke) or [lipanampesasupportteam1@Safaricom.co.ke](mailto:lipanampesasupportteam1@Safaricom.co.ke). LNM support team shall action the request within 24hrs SLA.

The LNM Support Team shall pick the SR or email activity and, upon validating the submitted change of name KYC documentation, proceed to update the details on M-PESA G2.

# **Required Documentation:**

# **Individual to Sole Proprietor:**

To change a business name from an individual to a sole proprietorship, the merchant/partner shall provide the following:

Organization short code

Organization name

Individual ID (as registered on M-PESA G2)

Valid business permit or certificate of registration

Individual KRA pin certificate

**Note:**

The name of the sole proprietor on the business permit or certificate of registration MUST match the individual business name currently registered on M-PESA G2.

If the business permit does not display the sole proprietor’s name, ID or telephone number, the merchant/ partner shall be required to fill a **Business Identification Form** for verification.

If the Certificate of Registration lists **two partners under the sole proprietorship**, **a signed letter** shall be provided requesting the name change. This letter shall be signed by both proprietors and accompanied by ID copy and KRA PIN certificate of the additional proprietor.

 **Individual to Limited Company**

To change a business name from an individual to a limited company, the merchant/partner shall provide the following:

Organization short code

Organization name

Individual ID (as registered on M-PESA G2)

Certificate of Incorporation

Current valid CR12 - within three months (90 days)

Ultimate Beneficial Ownership Certificate

**Note:**

For the change of name to be approved, the individual must be the **sole director** listed on the CR12 of the limited company.

If **additional directors** are listed on the CR12, or if the **individual is not listed** as a director on the CR12 after the transition, the name change **shall not be permitted.**

In such cases, a **change of ownership** will be recommended.

# **Sole Proprietorship to Sole Proprietorship**

This applies when a sole proprietorship is changing its business name but retaining its registration status as a sole proprietor. The merchant/partner shall provide the following:

Organization short code

Organization name

Certificate of Registration for the old business name

Certificate of Registration for the new business name

Change of Name Certificate

Individual ID of the sole proprietor 

**Note:**

If a Change of Name Certificate is not available, the merchant/partner shall provide a duly filled and signed **Novation Agreement** to establish the relationship between the two business entities.

If the Certificate of Registration for the old business name lists one proprietor, and the new business name includes an additional proprietor, **a signed written request on the company letter head** requesting the name change must be provided. The letter must **be signed by both proprietors** and accompanied by **ID copy and KRA PIN certificate of the additional proprietor.**

If the Certificate of Registration for the old business name lists **two proprietors**, and the new business name lists **only one proprietor**, a **signed written request on the company letter head** requesting the name change shall be provided. The letter must be signed by both proprietors and accompanied by their ID copies.

 **Sole Proprietorship to Limited Company**

To change business name from a sole proprietorship to a Limited company, the merchant/partner shall provide the below:

Organization short code

Organization name

A valid business permit/ certificate of registration as per the business name currently registered on G2.

Certificate of incorporation for the limited company.

Current valid CR12 - within three months (90 days).

**Note:**

For the change of name to be approved, the sole proprietor must be the **sole director** listed on the CR12 of the limited company.

If **additional directors** are listed on the CR12, or if the **sole proprietor is not listed** as a director on the CR12 after the transition, the name change **shall not be permitted.**

In such cases, a **change of ownership** will be recommended.

 **Limited Company to Limited Company / NGO to NGO**

This applies when a registered Limited Company or NGO changes its name but retains its legal structure. The merchant/partner shall provide the following:

Organization short code

Organization name

Change of name certificate

# **Change of Tariff**

This applies when merchants/ partners request for change of tariff during in-life for their buy goods till and/ or paybill accounts.

# **Tariff Change Request for Buy Goods till**

The available tariffs under the Buy Goods Till are categorized as follows:

# **Mauzo Tariff**

This is the standard default tariff assigned to Buy Goods Tills during onboarding.

# **Fuel Tariff**

Referred to as the Retail Distribution 6 tariff on M-PESA G2.

This tariff shall be assigned during onboarding or in-life, provided the merchant submits the required licenses or contractual documentation.

Merchants requesting this tariff must either submit:

A valid contract from EPRA

A supply contract from recognized fuel dealers (e.g., Shell, Total, etc.)

For a change of tariff request to Fuel Tariff during in-life, the merchant shall also provide the below:

A written request on the official company letter head, clearly stating the request. The letter must be signed by at least two authorized signatories (or one signatory for sole proprietorships).

Valid CR12 for a Limited company OR a valid business permit/ certificate of registration for a sole proprietor.

The business permit must indicate the nature of business as a fuel station or fuel distributor, where applicable.

# **Distribution Tariff**

There are two types of distribution tariff on M-PESA G2:

# **Distribution Tariff 1**

Transaction charges are incurred by the merchant.

This tariff applies to merchants offering distributor services and can be assigned either during onboarding or in-life.

To qualify, merchants must provide one of the following:

A valid business permit indicating distribution as the nature of business.

A valid distributor contracts.

An **email confirmation from the Account Manager** verifying a site visit and confirmation that the merchant is indeed a distributor.

# **Distribution Tariff 2**

Transaction charges are incurred by the customer.

This is a special tariff pre-negotiated for select merchants who distribute for Coca-Cola or East African Breweries Limited (EABL).

It shall be assigned at onboarding or in-life, provided the merchant submits the below:

A valid distribution contract with Coca-Cola or EABL confirming their distributor status.

For a change of tariff request to Distribution Tariff during in-life, the merchant shall also provide the below:

A written request on the official company letter head, clearly stating the request. The letter must be signed by at least two authorized signatories (or one signatory for sole proprietorships).

Valid CR12 for a Limited company OR a valid business permit/ certificate of registration for a sole proprietor.

The business permit must indicate the nature of business as distribution, where applicable.

# **Special/ Zero- Rated Tariff**

If a merchant requests to change their Buy Goods tariff to a special or zero-rated tariff, the Account Manager must provide a business justification.

The account manager shall initiate an internal approval process via the ISO Document Centre to be approved by:

Product Owner -Financial services

Senior Manager - Enterprise Operations

HOD – M-Pesa products and services Management

# **Tariff Change Request for Paybills**

The available tariffs under Paybill are categorized as follows:

Mgao Tariff – Transaction charges are split between the customer and the business.

Business Bouquet Tariff - No charges to the business; customer bears all charges.

Customer Bouquet Tariff - No charges to the customers; business bears all charges.

# **Required Documentation**

Paybill partners requesting a tariff change —from or to any of the available options—must submit the following:

A duly filled and signed **Addendum** (Tariff Change Form

A completed, signed, and stamped paybill tariff structure

A written request on the official company letter head, clearly stating the request. The letter must be signed by at least two authorized signatories (or one signatory for sole proprietorships).

# **Support Channels:**

The merchant/ partner shall submit their request to change tariff via the below available channels:

# **Request via Email:**

The merchant/ partner shall send an email request through their registered organization email (as captured on M-PESA System) to MPESABusiness@Safaricom.co.ke.

If the merchant does not have a registered organization email, the M-PESA Business team shall provide guidance on how to update or register one. (Refer to [OCPE-0001:LNM Change of Organization Contacts/ Notification, Nominated MSISDN](https://sakahub.safaricom.co.ke/app/article/8ebeba03-9c25-4513-9eb2-2589971e4911#:~:text=OCPE%2D0001%3A,Bookmark))

Once the request is received through a registered organization email, the CEE shall:

 Review the documents for completeness and accuracy.

Raise an SR for LNM Support, to be actioned within a 24-hour SLA.

# **Requests Received at the Safaricom Retail Centre /Franchise:**

Upon receiving the request, the CEE shall review KYC documents provided for completeness and accuracy.

The CEE shall then log an interaction on CRM and raise an SR for the LNM Support Team to action, within a 24-hour SLA.

**Requests Received by EBU Account Management Teams** **/ EBU Sales team:**

The account management teams shall send an email request and attach relevant documents provided to lnmaggregators@safaricom.co.ke or lipanampesasupportteam1@Safaricom.co.ke

The LNM Support shall action requests within 24 hours SLA.

# **Requests Received by LNM Support Team:**

The team shall pick the SR or email activity and review the attached KYC documents.

If all KYC documents provided are valid and pass vetting, the LNM Support team shall proceed to update tariff on M-PESA G2 as per merchant request and capture comments on SR.

If vetting is failed and the request is not fulfilled, the LNM support team shall advise the merchant accordingly and capture comments on the SR.

***SR Category: LNM BUY GOODS AND SERVICES***

***SR Type: Merchant Account***

***SR Item: Change of Tariff***

***SR Category: LNM PAYBILL***

***SR Type: Paybill Account***

***SR Item: Change of tariff***

# **Change of Ownership**

A change of ownership refers to the process of transferring the rights and responsibilities of an organization short code from one legal entity to another. This ensures that the registered entity on M-PESA reflects the **current legal owner**, in cases where the new entity differs from the one initially registered.

# **Instances where a Change of Ownership is required:**

When transitioning from an individual or sole proprietorship to a limited company with additional directors or a different set of directors.

When transitioning from an individual or sole proprietor to a group entity such as a church, NGO, CBO, partnership, institution, or gaming and betting company.

This shall involve closing the existing short code on M-PESA G2 and re-onboarding the newly registered entity on M-PESA G2 using the same short code and the required KYC as per the standard onboarding process.

# **Required Documentation**

**Stamped** or **Sealed** board resolution on the company letterhead stating the request to close the short code and onboard afresh the newly registered organization.

A duly completed LNM Service Application Form along with the signed Terms and Conditions.

Other onboarding KYC documents as required based on the business category of the newly registered entity 

For requests received at the Retail centre/ franchise or via the M-PESA Business folder, an SR shall be raised to LNM Onboarding team to action within 24hrs SLA.

Relationship/ account managers shall send requests received via email to [lnmrecruitment@safaricom.co.ke](mailto:lnmrecruitment@safaricom.co.ke) or [lipanampesaonboardingteam@Safaricom.co.ke](mailto:lipanampesaonboardingteam@Safaricom.co.ke). LNM Onboarding team shall action the request within 24hrs SLA.

The LNM Onboarding Team shall pick the SR or email activity and, upon validating the submitted change of ownership KYC documentation, shall coordinate with the LNM Support Team to close the existing short code. Once closed, the LNM Onboarding team shall proceed to onboard the new entity afresh on M-PESA G2.

**Note:**

The CEE or Account Manager receiving the request shall advise the merchant to download and retain statements for the existing short code as needed, prior to closure, as these records shall no longer be accessible after the change of ownership.

The bundles come in varied packages priced at different denominations, to give customers choice and options based on their need.

# **HOW TO TROUBLESHOOT M-PESA MESSAGES NOT COMING FROM M-PESA** 

If a customer contacts us saying that their M-PESA messages are not from M-PESA, the CEE should guide the customer as below.

- Search the number or name the customer is receiving from being shown as sender for M-PESA messages from their contact list and delete or edit it to read M-PESA. 
- Advise the customer that if they wish to save M-PESA in their contact list, then the name is M-PESA, and the number is also M-PESA.

This correction method should apply for any message expected to read the correct sender's name.

When prompted to save a contact sender, then save it exactly as it appears both on name and number in the contact. This will ensure you get messages displaying correct Senders as expected.

**NOTE:** Some phones like Samsung A24 prompt you to save as a contact any SMS sender, not in your contact list when you receive messages.

Some customers have ended up saving M-PESA as contact but with numbers or funny characters and funny names. M-PESA messages purportedly start coming from the funny names and numbers.

# **Reasons for My Failed SMS Delivery**

Some of the factors that may cause a sent message not to be delivered are.

- Sender does not have enough airtime or SMS bundles.
- If recipient has switched off the phone or is out of coverage.
- If recipient has incoming SMS barring's.
- If recipient’s inbox is full

# **Unable to Receive SMS**

Confirm whether problem is with SMSs from 1 person or others.

**If from one number**

- CEE will confirm sender used correct number to send the SMS.
- Advise the customer to go to the SMS settings on the phone and check on
- Number Screening
- Auto reject
- SMS/call restriction.

# **If all incoming SMS are affected**

- Check for any barring's on HLR.
- Deactivate incoming SMS barring's.
- Dial #35\*0000\*16#ok. (0000 can be replaced by any set barring password).
- Number Screening
- Try another handset to ensure handset is not faulty.

# **HLR View:**

#  **SMS MT WAITING DATA:**

- Shows there is a pending SMS.
- Advise customer to LU to cancel or complete sending the message

**MCEF:** If it shows YES, it means sim card inbox is full preventing receipt of SMS. Advice customer to delete SMS saved on the sim card.

**MNRF:** If it shows YES, it means the phone is either switched off or in a region without Safaricom network.

- CEE can purge the line on HLR and advise the customer to do LU.

**MNRG:** This affects the browser messages if sent to a sub and it happens that the phone is either switched off or in an area without GPRS coverage.

- Purge the line on HLR and advise the customer to do LU.

# **Unable to Send SMS**

Check on the following:

Confirm if customer has enough airtime balance.

Confirm with the customer that there is enough network strength or change locations.

Confirm with the customer that SMS parameters are okay

- SMS Center Number: +254722500029. For iPhone dial **\*#5005\*7672#**OK**.**
- Message type: Text/Standard.
- Message Validity period: Maximum

Deactivate any Outgoing SMS barring's on HLR and advise the customer on deactivating the barring's in future by dialing #33\*0000\*16#ok. (0000 can be replaced by any set barring password).

Try another handset to ensure handset is not faulty.

**HLR view:**

Check the HLR SMS profile to ensure SMS sending profile, TS22 is activated.

- If they do not have the profile, go to HLR under prepaid services and activate SMS.
- If there is a recurrence of the same, escalate the issue via SR.

Check HLR, if the line has any active barring's, and give customer handset SMS unbarring procedure. #33\*0000\*16#ok.

Check if subscriber has full network

- If network bars are low - Request them to change locations and see if the SMS will be sent from a different location.
- If network bars are full - Request them to do a location update and resend the SMS.

Confirm with the customer the service center number that is saved on the SIM card.

- SMS center no - +254722500029. For iPhone dial **\*#5005\*7672#**OK**.**
- Message type - Text /SMS

Confirm if SIM card is damaged: Request them to retry the SMS to same destination using a different SIM Card - If the SMS is successful, they should bring the original SIM to our Care centers to get assistance.

Confirm if handset is faulty by asking the customer to use another handset with their SIM card.

Confirm the type of handset some handsets can reject some SIM cards. 
Request them to retry the SMS using a different handset. If the SMS is successful, they should take their handset to a dealer to run some tests and establish the problem

**NOTE:**

If a customer is receiving some messages and some are missing advise the customer to change handset or if using dual sim to interchange sim slots.

If a customer receives a fraud SMS, advise the customer to.

- Forward the SMS to 333 for investigation.
- Report to police if conned.

 **Charges out of Bundle**

Troubleshoot as below:

- Confirm with communication sent by the folder or COPS Notice board if there is a global outage on SMS More for Less.
- Daily bundles cannot sendoff net messages, if message sent to off net, it would attract charges.
- Check on Siebel to see whether the SMS Bundle has expired.
- If the Bundle has NOT expired and the customer is being charged for sending local SMS or on-net for Daily SMS, please raise an SR for Technical team to deal

# **Error Messages**

**Check operator services**

- Check on barring and assist in deactivation by Dialing #33\*0000\*16#ok. (0000 can be replaced by any set barring password)
- Check on SIM Sending profile TS 22 on HLR.
- Go to HLR under prepaid services and activate SMS.

**Stop, sending previous message**

- This message is normally gotten when the previous message sending had not been completed due to a temporary software malfunction.
- Advise the customer to remove the battery and insert it afresh to enable the Sim card to delete the memory of the previous SMS sending.

**SIM Card Busy**

Gives this message when a service center number is missing. Advise the customer to check and input the number correctly.

 **Not sent try again later**

- Check barring's on HLR under **CBOC** if any **PROV** is replaced by **ACT** it indicates customer activated barring's, clear this via **‘Unbar Sim and Reset code’** under supplementary services.
- Also advise the customer on removing all barring's via #330\*0000# ok.

 **Repeated “SMS Not Sent” Notifications on iPhone Without User Action**

**Issue Summary – iPhone Devices:** 
The “SMS not sent” notifications typically arise from system-generated SMS messages sent to long codes such as *447537410217*, *447537410207*, etc. These messages are used during the activation of services like FaceTime and iMessage and usually carry activation data. They are billable as they must be successfully delivered to Apple’s servers. If users lack sufficient airtime, have blocked long/short codes, or experience other transmission failures, these messages are not sent, triggering the error notifications.

**Resolution:** 
According to online sources, Apple does not allow users to disable or customize system-level SMS error notifications. This restriction is in place for security and transparency purposes, to prevent malicious apps or SIM cards from sending messages without the user’s knowledge. However, users may try the following steps:

1. **Load airtime/credit** – This ensures the SMS messages are successfully sent (usually just once), after which the error messages should stop.
2. **Disable FaceTime and iMessage** – Navigate to *Settings* and turn off *FaceTime* and/or *iMessage* if these services are not in use.

**Additional Case – Android Devices (Legacy SIMs):** 
In some instances, “SMS not sent” messages may also stem from short codes such as *22500*, related to services like the “Phone Book Backup” (PBB) feature found in SIM Toolkits of older SIM cards.

**Resolution:** 
If the issue is linked to outdated SIM features, users are advised to **perform a SIM swap** to obtain a newer SIM card that does not have PBB enabled.

This is a step-by-step process used to keep track tills that haven’t been used for a while. The goal is to regularly check these inactive or dormant tills, understand why they’re not being used, and decide whether they should stay active or be deactivated.

This will apply to LNM short codes that are dormant for more than 6 Months.

i.         A Merchant Short code will be deemed dormant when there is no transaction done on the account for more than 6 months.

ii.         A valid transaction includes sending or receiving money, either within the organization or with customers/other merchants.

iii.         Erroneous payments received and subsequent reversals shall not be recognized as valid transactions.

iv.         Prior to a short code being declared dormant, the partner will have received communication after 1 month, 3 months, and 6 months of inactivity, reminding them to utilize their tills.

v.         Short codes that have been dormant for up to 2yrs will be handled in the [Unclaimed Funds Process.](https://sakahub.safaricom.co.ke/app/article/6699675e-ec31-4e4b-ab8a-bfa47de3f781)

**Data Extraction.**

This process involves extracting and analyzing data on inactive short codes to inform business decisions on their deactivation.

i.         Data for tills that have been dormant for more than 180 days, but less than 2 years will be extracted by the FSS Team, upon request by the Growth and Performance Marketing Team. The data shall contain below:

HO number.

Child Short code

HO Last transaction date.

Child Last transaction date.

Account status.

Contact numbers.

Office/nominated number.

Email contacts.

Account balances (for all accounts under the short code)

ii.         Once extracted, the data shall be shared with the Fintech Partners Operations Team for analysis. The following categories of short codes shall be excluded from deactivation:

Aggregators.

Government Short codes.

Internal short codes.

Special category – those with pending legal issues or those under investigation by fraud team.

iii.         The Fintech Partners Operations Team shall **share the list of dormant exempted aggregator short codes with the Customer In-Life Team**, who shall contact the aggregators and request them to engage their dormant merchants for reactivation or deactivation.

iv.         For the other agreed short codes, the Fintech Partners Operations team shall then apply the Organization Freeze state tag in bulk. This shall be done in batches, and the freeze tag message shall be as outlined below:

*“Account frozen due to Dormancy (month frozen).”*

v.         After tagging, the Fintech Partners Operations Team shall then share a report with the frontline teams on the short codes where the Organization Freeze tag has been applied.

**Till Dormancy Reactivation- Tag removal Process**

If a merchant wishes to continue using a dormant short code, they can request reactivation through the available channels.

The agent who receives the request shall log into G2, query the organization short code, and confirm whether the tag is an **Organization Freeze Tag** with the following description:

“*Account frozen due to inactivity or Dormancy (month frozen)”*

**Request received at the Call Center.**

Call must originate from the nominated number. The CEE shall then vet the merchant using the following:

Organization short code

Organization Name

Nominated number.

Full names and ID Number of nominated person/ finance contact as registered on G2.

After successful vetting the agent shall raise an SR for reactivation.

If the merchant fails vetting, refer them to Retail shop with their original registered identification document.

**Request received at the Retail Center/ Franchise**:

The agent shall vet the customer as per below:

Organization short code

Organization Name

Nominated Number/ Finance Contact

The nominated person/ finance contact shall **present their original ID document**. ID presented must match the details as registered on M-PESA G2.

After successful vetting the agent shall raise an SR for reactivation.

**Request received via M-PESA Business support (L2222 or Email)**

If a merchant calls L2222 or sends an email to [M-PESABusiness@safaricom.co.ke](mailto:M-PESABusiness@safaricom.co.ke) – the agent shall vet and reactivate the short codes.

**Request received via a call;**

Call must originate from the whitelisted nominated number. The CEE shall then vet the customer using the following:

Organization short code

Organization Name

After successful vetting, the agent shall reactivate the short code. If the merchant fails vetting, refer them to Retail shop with their original registered identification document.

**Requests received via Email:**

Email requests must originate from the organization’s registered email address as per M-PESA G2. The CEE will vet the customer using the following:

Organization short code

Organization Name

After successful vetting, the agent shall reactivate the short code. If the merchant fails vetting, refer them to Retail shop with their original registered identification document.

**NOTE**: If the organization is eligible for **UBO** (Ultimate Beneficial Ownership) submission, reactivation will only proceed **after** the customer has completed the submission.

**Handling Other Tag Types.**

Any other tag placed on the short code with a different description will be handled using the **current state tag procedures.**

# **M-PESA Nominated Number Beneficiary Service**

**Definition**

This is a service that allows M-PESA customers to designate a beneficiary who can access their funds if their account becomes inactive and Safaricom cannot reach the account holder for over 365 days.

**Eligibility Criteria for Nomination**

The account holder can nominate anyone they wish to, including themselves.

# **Benefits of This Service to the Customer and Safaricom**

Enable M-PESA customers to nominate a beneficiary during registration or afterward, to access their funds in case the account owner is inaccessible

Reduce unclaimed funds that are eventually turned over to the Unclaimed Financial Assets Authority by uniting the same with their owners or preferred beneficiaries.

Enhance Customer Trust and Satisfaction by providing a reliable and secure method for customers to ensure their funds are accessible to their beneficiaries.

Compliance with Regulatory Requirements by ensuring the nominated beneficiary process complies with all relevant legal and regulatory requirements, including data protection laws.

Operational Efficiency by streamlining the process to minimize administrative overhead and ensure a smooth experience for both customers and internal teams.

**Beneficiary Nomination Process for M-PESA Customers**

For M-PESA Customers to nominate a beneficiary, they will be required to dial \*334# and select My M-PESA Nominated Beneficiary to proceed. The customer will provide the beneficiary’s ID number among other KYC details which will be verified against our existing M-PESA database.

# **Circumstances When Safaricom May Contact a Beneficiary**

The circumstances that Safaricom may contact a Beneficiary is where the funds are marked as “archived” due to account going inactive, Safaricom will attempt to contact the account holder through their primary contact. We will contact the nominated beneficiary only where the account holder does not respond within 365 days

**How a Beneficiary Can Claim Their Funds**

For a beneficiary to claim their funds, Safaricom will verify the beneficiary’s KYC details as provided by the primary customer, before paying funds into the beneficiary’s M-PESA account.

**How M-PESA Manages Funds Based on Amounts Held**

For the current phase, only amount of KSh 100 and below will be paid into the beneficiary’s account.

For amounts above KSh 100, the usual claim of funds procedures will continue to apply, where defined legal administrative documents will be required.

**How Safaricom Keeps Beneficiary Records Updated**

Safaricom will periodically remind users to review and update their beneficiary information.

**Unclaimed Funds: No Beneficiary Nominated**

The usual claim of funds procedures will continue to apply, where defined legal administrative documents will be required.

**Unclaimed Funds and Unreachable Beneficiaries**

For unclaimed funds and unreachable beneficiaries will be handed over to the UFAA if not claimed for a period of 2 years.

**Is the nominated beneficiary direct heir to the funds held in M-PESA**

Yes, for amounts of KSh 100 or less.

**Documents Required from a Beneficiary to Claim Funds**

For KSh 100 or less, Safaricom will pay after verifying the KYC of the beneficiary as provided by the account holder.

For amounts above KSh 100, legal administrative procedures will be applied and required documentation provided.

markdownContent:
**DIY PROCEDURES FOR OKOA JAHAZI**

**How to Request**

- Dial \*131# ok and select preferred Okoa Jahazi airtime amount.
- Upon successful request, Okoa will be in effect immediately and has priority over normal airtime.
- Once successful, it cannot be cancelled.
- A customer will be charged 10% of the amount requested as below:

**Available amounts.**

| Requested Amount (Ksh) | Service Fee (Ksh.) | Airtime Received (Ksh) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1000 | 100 | 900 |
| 500 | 50 | 450 |
| 250 | 25 | 225 |
| 100 | 10 | 90 |
| 50 | 5 | 45 |
| 20 | 2 | 18 |
| 10 | 1 | 9 |
| 5 | 0.5 | 4.5 |

**Checking the Balance**

**Dial \*131#**

Select Check balance under the below options:

- Outstanding okoa jahazi debts
- Okoa jahazi account balance
- Check my okoa debt

**Dial \*144\*4#**

It will automatically send a message with current okoa jahazi loan

**Send an SMS with word balance to 144** to get all the customer’s account balance.

**DIY PROCEDURES FOR MULTIPLE OKOA JAHAZI/LIPA MDOGO MDOGO**

- This is a feature within Okoa Jahazi that allows Multiple borrowing
- The service is available to all prepay customers allowing them to Okoa multiple times.
- Customers can borrow as many times as their **Previous week usage** can allow every week.
- Each loan takes its own 5-day Service Legal Agreement (SLA).
- The customer dials \*131# and requests preferred top up
- The balance will the added to the existing loan
- Upon successful request, Okoa will be in effect immediately and has priority over normal airtime.

 **How to Request**

- Dial \*131# ok and select your preferred Okoa Jahazi airtime amount.
- If no overdue Okoa debt, the request will be successful.
- If there is an overdue Okoa debt, one is required to clear before getting any other Okoa debt.
- Upon successful request, Okoa will be in effect immediately and has priority over normal airtime.

**Checking the Balance and Okoa Limit**

**Dial \*131\*0**\# that gives:

- All outstanding Okoa Jahazi debts and the repayment date.
- Okoa Jahazi account balance.
- Okoa debt
- Okoa Chap Chap
- Okoa Limit

**NB:-**

- Check Limit Feature on CRM will be availed later.
- Blacklisted customers will not be able to view their okoa limit
- Customers with no previous weeks usage or with a limit of Ksh 50 and below will not be able to view their okoa limit

**Dial \*144\*4#**

- Account balance.
- Outstanding credit balance.
- It will automatically send a message with current okoa jahazi loan

**Send an SMS with word balance to** 144 to get all your account balances.

**Failed Okoa Jahazi Request and Resuming a Line for ETU**

**FAILED OKOA REQUEST**

**Reasons for ETU request failure:**

- Customer Blacklisted due to defaulting M-Shwari loan.
- Amount requested not being equivalent to the airtime spent in the previous week. (Customers can borrow as many times as their previous week’s usage.)
- Customer having an outstanding Okoa debt or blacklisted on ETU.

 **NB**:

If the customer has met all the conditions above and is still unable to use the ETU services, the CEE will raise a Service Request to the support team for resolution.

**ESCALATION MATRIX WHEN ALL THE CONDITIONS ARE MET BUT CUSTOMER NOT ABLE TO REQUEST ETU.**

**Sr category**

- **Category:** Top Up Issues
- **Type:** Okoa Jahazi
- **Item:** Blacklisting
- Comments: the CEE should capture the appropriate comments and advise the customer on the SLA and raise an interaction.

**RESUMING A LINE FOR ETU (OKOA JAHAZI)**

- Click on Mshwari Tab on Siebel and confirm there is no loan balance.
- Click on IN Data button.
- Confirm there is no ETU outstanding balance.
- Check if the “ETU Blacklisted” button is checked.
- Click on the Suspend/Resume ETU button to uncheck the button.
- Raise an interaction with the details of the action in the comments.

If the customer has not repaid the Mshwari loan in full or ETU, advise the customer to repay the loan/ETU in full for the ETU service to be resumed.

**Definition**

The Device Insurance Product is a service offered by Safaricom and Sanlam Insurance, providing for smartphones. It ensures protection against accidental damage, theft, and other unforeseen events such as credit life.

**Eligibility**

This insurance product is open to all M-PESA registered customers who purchase new Lipa Mdogo Mdogo smartphones on credit.

In future it will be available for smartphones purchased via other payment methods, e.g. cash.

**Risks/events covered by Device Insurance**

The Device Insurance policies typically covers:

- Accidental damage (e.g., screen damage, liquid damage)
- Theft
- Credit life.

**Benefits of Device Insurance**

**Customer Experience**: Offering embedded insurance cover on devices creates a seamless experience for customers as it easily protects their purchase without the need to navigate to external insurance providers.

**Customer Retention**: Insurance coverage can improve customer loyalty by providing added value and peace of mind. Customers may be more likely to stay with a telco that offers comprehensive protection solutions.

**Reduced Churn**: When customers are covered by insurance, they may be less likely to switch to a competitor due to device-related issues or damage.

**Cross-selling Opportunities**: Telcos can use embedded insurance to cross-sell other products or services, such as device upgrades, accessories, or extended warranties.

**Increased Revenue**: Telcos can earn additional revenue through profit share or even premiums from insurance products.

**Simplified Claims**: Integrated insurance can lead to quicker and more efficient claims processing, as the telco already has the necessary information about the customer.

**Competitive advantage**: Offering embedded insurance can set an entity apart from competitors by providing a unique and valuable service that caters to customer needs.

**Risk Management**: Providing insurance allows the telco to manage potential financial risks associated with unexpected loss.

**Cost for protecting the phone with Device Insurance**

The policy will be charged at 2.32% of the cost of the phone. This cost is embedded in the handset price.

**Device Insurance Miniapp**

This is a miniapp hosted on the M-PESA Super App that allows you to conveniently manage insurance coverage for your smartphones.

**How to access the Device Insurance miniapp**

You need to have been registered on M-PESA and have installed M-PESA APP

**Note****:** First-time download and sign-in will require mobile data, and the subsequent times when using the App, you can use Wi-Fi or Data.

Scroll down to Get Insurance or under the services tab > select Device Insurance Mini-App, and proceed to opt-in.

**Benefits of the Device Insurance miniapp**

- **Easy** – it enables you to easily opt-in, access insurance cover for your smartphone, all in one place.
- **Convenient** – it enables manage insurance coverage for your smartphone in one place.

**How to opt-in to the Device Insurance miniapp**

- Open the M-PESA Super App.
- Navigate to the Get Insurance section.
- Select the Device Insurance option.
- Follow the prompts to provide necessary details and complete the opt in process.

**Types of devices covered by Device Insurance**

There are two types of devices i.e.

- The smartphones purchased on credit through the Lipa Mdogo Mdogo solution, Mobigo and those used for the Community Health program.
- In future it will be available for smartphones purchased by cash or any other payment method.

 **Different policy statuses and their meanings**

- **Active** - means the cover is within the period set, and you can benefit from the protection and access claims within that period.
- **Expired** - means that the cover period has lapsed. You will not be able to make any claim.
- **Claimed** – means customer has exhausted the maximum number of claims allowed.

**Duration taken for my device to be covered after purchase.**

The device will be covered immediately after the purchase process is complete, given all necessary information is provided accurately.

**Currency in which the premium will be calculated.**

The currency is in Kenyan Shillings and is displayed within the app.

**Reversal of the insurance cost**

Once the cover is activated, a customer cannot request a reversal.

**Cover Duration**

The cover will run for a non-renewable period of 12 months from the date of purchase.

**Personal information security**

The customers personal information is secure as we take the security and privacy of the customers personal information seriously. We employ industry standard security measures to safeguard your data and ensure confidentiality.

**How to make a claim**

For theft claim, you will need to provide supporting documents such as a police report for theft claims.

For screen and other damage claims, you will be required take the damaged phone to the retail shop or authorized repair centre for assessment and further support.

**Number of claims that a customer can make within the cover period.**

**Theft and Loss claims** \- For theft and irreparable damage, a customer can make only one claim within the cover's duration.

**Screen replacement** - A maximum of two claims for screen replacement within the duration of the cover.

**Irreparable damage** – As will be assessed and advised by the repair centre, the handset may be replaced. This is limited to only one instance.

**Other damages** - Repairs will continue until the total repair costs reach the value of the handset.

**Claims process timeline**

- Theft and Loss claims – 72 Hours
- Screen replacement - 72 Hours.
- Irreparable damage – 72 Hours
- Other damages – 72 Hours

**Documentation required for property claims.**

- Theft/loss claims - Provide copies of the following documents at any of our retail shops or care desks near you.
- Copy of police abstract
- Copy of your ID card or Passport
- To process the claim, your stolen phone will first be blocked by Safaricom.
- Damage claims - Present the damaged phone at the nearest Safaricom shop, care desk or
- approved repair Centre.

**NOTE:** A customer may contact our customer care number to be guided to the nearest repair Centre.

**Exclusions to coverage**

While our insurance plans offer comprehensive coverage, the following are the exclusions applicable:

Wear and tear that result in the gradual deterioration of the device.

Incidents and damage covered by the manufacturer warranty.

Accessories including memory card, Screen Protectors, Covers, earphones, battery, chargers, and adaptors are not covered for loss or damage.

Damages or losses arising from participation in illegal activities e.g., acts of Terrorism, Civil War etc.

Rebellion, civil commotions, and mutiny.

**How to Contact us**

In case of any queries or more information:

• Call 100 or 200 or 234

• Call: +254 722 002100 for prepaid customers and +254 722 002200 for post-pay customers on

roaming (Chargeable)

• Twitter: @Safaricom\_Care and @SafaricomPLC

• Facebook: @SafaricomPLC

• Email: [customercare@safaricom.co.ke](mailto:customercare@safaricom.co.ke)

• Safaricom website: [www.safaricom.co.ke](http://www.safaricom.co.ke/)

# **Individual and Corporate Terminations**

Customers wishing to terminate their postpay account subscriptions will be required to present the below:  

**Individuals**  

i.         Fill in the termination form or email from registered email address on CRM.

ii.         Present original ID. 

**Corporates**

i.         A letter from the company or the approved Postpaid termination form. 

ii.         Signed and stamped/seal requesting for termination. This can be dropped at any retail center or sent via mail to the approved shop email folders, credit control CNC@safaricom.co.ke or to advantage@safaricom.co.ke.  

iii.         Instructions on how the deposit will be utilized (where applicable). 

CEE will advise the customer to clear all outstanding bills or the customer can direct the company to utilize the initial deposit to clear the bill where applicable.

The request will be presented to the CEE who will vet and ensure that all details and attachments are accurately presented and that the customer has indicated the preferred mode of receiving back the deposit.    

CEE must advice customers on deposit refund SLA’s i.e. 

i.         Within 24 hours via M-PESA after termination.

ii.         14 working days if the customer was roaming prior to the termination request. 

iii.         Within 24 working days for EFT.

CEE will advise customer on modes of refund i.e. Refunds will be in form of M-PESA, EFT or Airtime. At no time will cheques be issued.   

Where customer requests for refund via M-PESA the CEE should make sure the line receiving is M-PESA registered in their names.

For Customers wishing to receive Via Bank, the CEE should make sure the customer details on the bank are indicated on the termination order.   

The CEE will proceed to raise post to pre order on Siebel with customers request, stamp, scan and attach all relevant documents onto the system.    

The request auto completes on the CRM Siebel system. 

The hard copies of the customer request are filed as per the filing procedures.   

The request will trigger notification to credit control to process refund.

For any cases where customer reports delayed deposit refund. CEE will raise an SR for subsequent follow up by credit control teams and subsequent resolution. 

# **Individual Postpay Termination for Deceased Persons** 

Where the customer requests for termination for a deceased person, the CEE will request customer to present: -  

i.         Original Death Certificate of the deceased.  

ii.         Original ID of person requesting for termination.  

iii.         Duly filled Postpaid termination form for deceased person. 

iv.         Letter of Administration (Chief, DC, County Commissioner).  

v.         An affidavit stating their relationship with the deceased.

CEE will raise a post to pre order on Siebel; deposit available will be used to offset accrued bills if any.  

The request auto completes on the CRM Siebel system and customer is notified.

For any funds remaining after offsetting accrued bills then the Next of Kin claim of funds process will take effect.

**Definition**

This is a money transfer service for joint PayPal and M-PESA customers that enables customers to move funds between their own M-PESA accounts and PayPal accounts.

Safaricom has introduced a PayPal-M-PESA direct integration service that enables M-PESA customers to receive value for product and services into their M-PESA account i.e. withdraw, and to enable customers to make payments from their M-PESA wallets to online merchants US-Dollars (USD) by topping up their PayPal accounts without involving a third party.

**How It Works**

This service ensures that customers get adequate support due to clarity of the roles and responsibilities of the two parties involved i.e. PayPal and Safaricom.

The service enables customers to withdraw funds from their PayPal account to their M-PESA wallet with minimum risks.

**How to Access**

The PayPal M-PESA direct integration service can be accessed on M-PESA Super App through PayPal mini app  

**Service Features**

With the upcoming integration, the following changes will be noted:

a)    **Linking**

•        To use M-PESA PayPal service, M-PESA customers were required to link the same to their PayPal account from the PayPal website.

•        With the PayPal integration**, linking will be done from PayPal Mini App on M-PESA App**

b)    **Partnership**

•        This will be between Safaricom and PayPal. **Thunes will no longer be there.**

•        This helps to reduce turn around time to resolve incidences.

c)    **Channel of Access**

•        All top up and withdrawal transactions will be done directly from the Mini-App, with no need to access the PayPal website

d)    **Statements and Balances**

•        Access PayPal statement and balances directly from the Mini App

e)    **Instant Withdrawal**

•        Receive funds immediately upon making a withdrawal, with not waiting period. 

# **Account Linking (Existing PayPal Customers)**

To link your PayPal to M-PESA:

Log in to the M-PESA app using the M-PESA pin or Chosen biometrics

From the home screen on the navigation bar tap the **Global Payments** tab

Select the **PayPa**l mini app that directs you to **link account** option

Enter your email address and password

Log in

Click on the Terms and Conditions to read through

You receive a notification from Safaricom stating that.

*Dear customer you have successfully linked your M-PESA account 07xxxxxxxxxx (M-PESA number) to your PayPal account [gggggg@gmail.com](mailto:gggggg@gmail.com) (email address)* 

# **Account Linking (New Customer)**

**Product Journey for a customer without an existing PayPal account:**

Log in to the M-PESA app using the M-PESA pin or Chosen biometrics​

From the home screen on the navigation bar tap the **Global Payments** tab​

Select the **PayPa**l mini app that directs you to **link account** option​

Enter your email address and password​

Click on sign up

Set up a PayPal account by filling in your details and mobile number

Agree to link M-PESA account to PayPal account

Click on the Terms and Conditions to read through​

You receive a notification from Safaricom stating that; Dear customer you have successfully linked your M-PESA account 07xxxxxxxxxx (M-PESA number) to your PayPal account [gggggg@gmail.com](mailto:gggggg@gmail.com) (email address) 

**Topping Up PayPal**

Log in to the M-PESA app using the M-PESA pin or Chosen biometrics

From the home screen on the navigation bar tap the **Global Payments** Tab

Select the PayPal mini-app

Your available balance is displayed both in **USD** and **KSH**

Tap on the **Top-up account** tab

Enter the amount you want to top up in **KSH** and press **continue**

Enter your M-PESA pin

You will receive a pop-up that the Deposit request is successful with the transaction ID and two messages:
