articleTitle: DIY Procedures for 4G for Home and MiFi Mechanics
markdownContent:
**4G for Home WIFI Password and connection issues**

4G for home WIFI password (WI-FI KEY) is printed on the back of the Router

Changing Wi-Fi Username and Password

Make sure the machine is connected to the Router Wi-Fi

Log into this portal on the web browser, type 192.168.8.1.

Enter User: admin.

Enter password: admin.

Input preferred Username.

Input preferred password.

Login to devices with the new Wi-Fi Username and password

**Connection Issues**

Check that they have an active account by dialling (using the registered number when applying for the service) \*400\*3# and select Check account status.

Restart their router by powering off. Press the Power button- Off and On.

If it does not work and customer has an active account, they can call Line 400 from their mobile device (which was used on registration) or email us via safaricomhome@safaricom.co.ke for further help.

**Customer Package Purchase Journey**

To renew the 4G for home Internet package, simply follow the instructions below:

Using the registered number when applying for the service Dial \*400#ok the follow prompts.

Enter the “4G SIM Number” (Indicated on a label at the back of your Router)

Customer will see the 4G Home plan that they are to renew either 3 Mbps @ Kes 3,499 or 5 Mbps @Kes 4,999.

Select mode of payment M-PESA and confirm payment. Customer will be prompted to enter 4-digit MPESA PIN.

**NOTE:** Upon successful purchase, customer will receive a flash notification of successful payment, and a confirmation SMS will be sent to their Mobile number

**Mi-Fi Passwords (Default & Reset) and Mi-Fi Basic settings**

The network credentials (SSID and Password) are located on the back of the device.

If a customer forgets the WI-FI SSID, password or web management page login password, press and hold the reset button until mobile WIFI restarts.

The mobile WIFI settings are then restored to default settings.

**Mi-Fi Basic settings**

The default username & password is "admin".

The Wi-Fi/Admin password is on a label located on the back of the device or on a label located under the battery.

Launch a web browser then navigate to the MiFi Admin page.

**Note**: From the browser Address/URL field enter 192.168.1.1

**Resetting the device and Connecting Windows laptop to a Mi-Fi device**

Turn on the device.

Remove the battery cover.

Using a PIN or paperclip, press and hold the Reset button until the screen switches off.

The device will automatically restart. The default settings will now be restored. Customer can find your device.

**Connecting Windows laptop to a Mi-Fi device**

Power on the Mi-Fi hotspot by pushing the power button.

Turn on the computer.

Once the Computer is connected to Wi-Fi, the customer can browse the internet, check email, etc.

# **How to get 4G portable Wi-Fi MSISDN**

Remove SIM card, put it in a phone and dial \*100# Select Option 4 (My Account)

articleTitle: Mobile Data Slow/Poor Connection Network Queries
markdownContent:
# **Leveraging SOC tool to offer First Call Resolution (FCR)** 

In order to offer quality resolution to customers with Mobile Data queries, kindly leverage the **SOC** Tool to ensure **First Call Resolution (FCR)** for those common network issues. Especially avoid over-reliance on "Location Update (LU)" as a default fix.

Understand the SOC tool capabilities. It provides:

- Real-time monitoring dashboards
- Network alert and incident management
- Network performance metrics
- Common fault indicators (e.g., latency, packet loss, device down)

 **Common Customer Scenarios & Resolutions:**

# **Scenario 1: 3G SIM in a 4G Device**

- **Issue**: Customer has a 4G-capable device but is not getting 4G service.
- **SOC Tool Check**: Confirm SIM type (3G vs 4G).
- **Resolution**:

- Inform the customer they are using a 3G SIM.
- Recommend a **SIM replacement** at the nearest Safaricom dealer/shop

SOC tool check Note 4G ready SIM cards IMSI start with the prefix **'639021%'.**

 **Sample of a 3G SIM card that need replacement**

 [Screenshot] 

# **Scenario 2: 4G Device Locked to 3G Only**

- **Issue**: Device is not accessing 4G despite being 4G compatible.
- **SOC Tool Check**: Confirm device is locked to 3G via SOC
- **Resolution**: Guide the customer to update network settings:

**For iPhone (iOS):**

Settings > Mobile Data > Mobile Data Options > Voice and Data > Select 4G

Restart the phone.

**For Android:**

Settings > Network & Internet > Mobile Network > Preferred Network Type > Select 4G/LTE

Restart the phone.

SOC Tool check for customers locked Network capability to 3G and need to change locked status:

**Trouble shooting tips:**

**Subscriber IMSI** showing SIM is 4G ready NR\_IMSI **LIKE** **'639021%**

**Device is 4G ready -Mode:2G/3G/LTE**

**Web-browsing :** 4G traffic 0MB

 [Screenshot] 

 **Best Practices to offer FCR**

- **Avoid defaulting to LU** unless it’s validated as necessary.
- **Use SOC tool insights** before offering a resolution.
- **Capture accurate interaction notes** and **log SRs** (Service Requests) for escalations.
- **Educate the customer** on how to prevent recurrence (e.g., keeping device settings updated).

**Suggested Script Snippet to customer**

“I’ve checked your network profile using our monitoring tool. It looks like your SIM is a 3G type, which limits your access to 4G services. I recommend upgrading your SIM to enjoy better speeds. I can guide you on how to do that now.”

**or**

“Your device appears to be locked to 3G. Let me walk you through how to switch it to 4G for a better experience.”

CVM messages will also be shared to customers from 26th May 2025 as below advising customers to manually change settings or perform SIM swaps to enjoy Safaricom 4G Top speeds

*Activate 4G on your iPhone today! Go to Settings > Mobile Data > Mobile Data Options > Voice and Data > Put 4G ON. Restart your phone for best performance. Enjoy faster speeds!*

*Activate 4G on your Android today! Go to Settings > Network & Internet > Mobile Network > Preferred Network Type > Select 4G/LTE. Restart your phone for the best experience. Enjoy faster speeds!*

Pochi la Biashara is a product that allows business owners such as food vendors, small kiosk owners, boda-boda operators, secondhand clothes dealers, etc., to receive and separate business funds from personal funds on their M-PESA line.

**Competitive Interest**: ZiiDi offers a market-competitive interest rate, calculated annually and credited to your ZiiDi for Pochi account every day at midnight.

**Affordability**: Start investing with as little as KSh. 100, with no maximum limit on the amount your ZiiDi for Pochi account can hold.

**Zero Transaction Costs**: There are no transaction fees for depositing or withdrawing funds from ZiiDi for Pochi, and no maintenance fees are charged.

**Easy Tracking**: Provides full visibility of your daily earnings, helping you with financial planning and tracking.

Some Enterprise Accounts have Account Managers to help them with any business-related challenge or act as their point of contact

**M-PESA Global opt in Errors**

USSD procedure keeps timing out: USSD is designed to timeout after three minutes. Customer should send within this period.

Whenever a customer sends funds via the App and does not get an option to enter M-PESA PIN: Perform an STK push for the customer via Siebel.

If all these fails, please escalate via Service Request (SR) indicating the exact problems customer encountered for support team to deal.

**Where the SMS with MTCN has not been received**

MTCN stands for Money Transfer Control Number. It is a reference number sent to the sender and which they share with the recipient to claim money at a Western Union agent.

**Work Instructions**

Customer will contact us via line 100/200/234/online support/Retail shop.

CEE will vet the customer using the details below and the customer must pass the first two vetting details. Additional vetting can be used for M-PESA balance (option 3).

CEE will share the MTCN verbally or via SMS with the customer.

          ***Dear customer, your MTCN number is XXXXXXXXXXXXXXX Thank you.***

**Mandatory**

Customer names as registered on M-PESA G2.

Customer ID.

M-PESA balance.

**Additional Vetting**

M-Shwari Limit/ balance

Fuliza Limit/balance

**How to check MTCN on M-PESA G2**

Open the transaction on M-PESA G2.

Scroll down to Reference Data Section.

You will see the Bill Reference Number (10-digit number) which is the MTCN you will share with the customer.

**Authorized Transaction on M-PESA**

The CEE will query the number on G2 to confirm on the transaction status.

If the transaction is authorized, raise a Service Request (SR) quoting the transaction details SLA is 72hrs.

**DO NOT COMPLETE/CANCEL** the transaction.

**Transfer was successful but the funds not ready for collection**

The CEE will query the number on G2 to confirm on the transaction status.

If the transaction is completed but customer claims recipient has not received the funds, raise a Service Request (SR) quoting the transaction details SLA is 72hrs.

Support team will investigate by logging into M-PESA G2 and pick the MTCN number, confirm on Western Union outbound portal if the MTCN exists then send an Email to Western Union to verify if the MTCN exists on their side.

If Western Union confirms the MTCN exists on their side, the Support Analyst shall verify if the funds are available for pickup and advise the customer/sender on the MTCN number.

Where the MTCN doesn’t exist, the system will auto reverse the funds and the money will go back to the senders M-PESA account. Note the transaction fee is also reversed.

**Funds sent to wrong number**

The customer will call contact Centre.

The CEE will query the number on G2 to confirm on the transaction status.

CEE will raise the Service Request ticket indicating the reason for reversal, ticket SLA IS 72hrs.

The Support analyst will contact the partner to confirm the status of the funds and thereby action accordingly and advise the customer of the same.

articleTitle: Next of Kin Claim of Funds/MSISDN Requirements and Procedure
markdownContent:
**Next of Kin Claim of Funds Requirements and Procedure**

The Claimant has to visit a retail center or care desk for any of the claims below. This is applicable to customers of all denominations and the customer must present original documents.

*Take note of the attached*

*FAQs defining the claim documents, where to get them and what to look out for in such documents.*

*Retail claim of funds work instructions and procedure.*

***NB: SLA is 24 hours after submission of documents***

**M-PESA Claims**

 **M-PESA Claim of Funds – Incapacitated customers (health /mental) Documents;**

Court order, declaring the claimant as a guardian of the incapacitated person and further granting them authority to deal with the property of the incapacitated person.

Copy or original ID of the incapacitated customer

Claimants original ID (both sides).

Duly filled claim of funds form.

**M-PESA Claim of Funds- Next of Kin/Deceased Customers**

Original Death Certificate

Issued by Kenya OR other Foreign Country

Customer will present a court order, pronouncing the individual dead where the body is not retrieved for production of death certificate

Original Claimants ID (both sides)

Original next of kin succession document as guided by the table below

| Amount (Ksh.) | Next of kin succession Documents |
| --- | --- |
| 1 - 30,000 | Letter from County Administration.i.e Chief, Sub-Chief, Deputy County Commissioner, County Commissioner. NB: Letters from the Chief and Sub-chief must be accompanied with an Affidavit administered by a Commissioner for Oaths and sworn by the claimant.Letters from the Deputy County Commissioner/County commissioner must indemnify Safaricom |
| 1 - 200,000 | Letter of Public TrusteeThis can be obtained from the Attorney General’s office or DC's or Deputy County Commissioner’s office. NB:Letters granted from this office must indemnify Safaricom. (exempt Safaricom from legal liability for processing the amount). We currently only pay out to the beneficiary. The document must give instructions for funds to be paid to the claimant’s M-PESA. |
| Any Amount (from 1 - maximum allowed balance) | Confirmed Grant of Probate / Confirmed Letters of Administration.These are issued by the court |

Note: The succession documents must quote the name and ID of next of kin of and where the customer presents succession documents listing **multiple beneficiaries** for M-PESA;

Claiming amounts below Kshs 30,000/= the funds will be forwarded to the next of kin. Where there are many dependents, the person (adult) applying is the one who will receive the funds.

In Confirmed letters of administration / grant of probate where two or more administrators have been appointed, for transactions above Kshs 30,000/=, funds can only be credited to one MSISDN.

The claimants must agree on the MSISDN that should be credited. The administrators should sign a letter appointing one of them as the recipient of the funds. The person presenting request must either present a written request or affidavit signed / sworn by all administrators and include copies of their ID (The claimant will present their original ID).

Where the letters are specific to the M-PESA funds as a sole beneficiary, the same will be applied

Where the listed beneficiaries are minors, they will not be required to swear an affidavit or sign. The adult will apply and receive the funds on their behalf.

**M-SHWARI Claim - Raise an SR and attach below;**

**For amounts less than Kshs.150, 000**

Death Certificate

Claimants ID (both sides)

Letter from County commissioner.

**For amounts Kshs.150, 001 to 499,999.**

Claimants ID (both sides)

Death certificate

Letter from public trustee i.e. Attorney General’s office.

**For amounts equal to or greater than Kshs. 500,000**

Claimants ID (both sides)

Death Certificate

Letter of Administration

**KCB Claim - Raise an SR and attach below;**

**For amounts up to Kshs 100,000**

Death certificate

Claimants ID (both sides)

Letter from national government administration or Letter from public trustee

**For amounts above KS 100,000/=**

Death certificate

Claimants ID (both sides) OR a Valid passport

Letter from public trustee or Grant of letters of administration intestate / Grant of probate/Court order

**Succession of prepaid and postpaid MSISDN:**

The requirements are:

Original Death Certificate.

Original ID of claimant (both sides)

Confirmed grant of probate OR Confirmed letters of administration

NB

Public trustee is also required to go to court and to obtain Confirmed letters of administration when managing a deceased’s estate, which also includes MSISDN’s.

**Prepaid line:** CEE will receive and vet customer documents, do a pre to pre on Siebel and change customer details.

**Postpaid line:** Available deposit is used to offset existing bill, and if in excess of the bill the claimant can claim the balance. In case the claimant wishes to own the line, postpaid application process will apply, the claimant of the line owner will be required to pay a deposit.

**Information/ balances/ resources requests**

For the claimant to be given M-PESA, Mshwari, KCB, Bonga and Airtime balance Requirements:

Written request, detailing information required.

Original ID of person making request.

Original death certificate.

**NB:**

No funds / resources will be disbursed through this request, nor change of ownership effected

The CEE will give accurate details to the customer, attach all relevant documents on Siebel and advice customer of the line life cycle and how the same relate to available resources i.e. Loss of resources i.e. Bonga, data, airtime etc. due to deletion. Also, advice on reactivation i.e. through top up / Sambaza.

**Resources claim of resources: bonga points/airtime/data bundles**

If the claimant requests for a transfer of resources, the claimant will need to bring the documents below:

The Grant of Probate document **OR** Letters of Administration **OR** Letter from the Office of the Public Trustee

Original ID of Claimants

# **Succession of MSISDN from Deceased Persons**  

In cases where the owner is deceased and the next of kin, or such other person wishes to take over the line, then they will be required to present the following documents:   

Original Death Certificate of the deceased.   

Original ID of person intending to secure the line.   

Letter of Administration   

CEE will receive and vet customer documents and will proceed to do a pre to pre once authentication is done on Siebel and will assist customer to confirm available resources.    

The Agent should attach a scanned copy of all the above documents including all the vetting details in the notes before submitting. These letters should be stamped with the Retail Shop rubber stamp showing the current date, the order number, Service Interaction or Service Request number indicated clearly on the letter. This should then be filed by the staff performing the request.   

Registration will be done via the Jiandikishe App. 

- Where the customer has funds on M-PESA / M-Shwari, M-PESA work instructions will apply as per the process.

# **Customer Reporting Fraud**

Customers can report fraud cases freely via below channels:

# **Contact Safaricom** **by** **calling 100, 200 or 234**

- Where a customer calls to report fraud where there is **NO** money lost the CEE will select interaction type category **Fraud reporting only** and capture the fraud number, advise the customer it will be actioned appropriately.
- The CEE shall advise the customer in future to report any fraud related issue via 333 or via MySafaricom App.
- In case customer has lost funds, the CEE shall raise a fraud SR and ensure to capture below, under the interaction **Fraud Money Lost** comments sections:
 - The number used by the fraudster.
 - The amount of money lost by the customer.
- In case customer reports that a line has been registered under their IDs without their consent (identity Theft), the CEE shall raise a fraud SR, interactions MUST capture:
 - the number in dispute
 - any loss from loan applications indicates FSI loan organization e.g., KCB/FULIZA/MSWARI etc., date when loan was taken, and amount taken.
- The CEE shall give the customer the SLA of the SR raised and also advise the customer to **report to** **the** **nearest police station, obtain an OB number, then update** **their** **report via SMS to 333****.**
- After the call, the CEE shall send below message to the customer from CRM;

***D******e******ar Customer, For further investigation, please report the con to your nearest police station, obtain an OB number, then update your report via SMS to 333***

**SMS to 333:**

- Forward the fraudulent message to 333, capturing the number that initiated the fraudulent request.
- Once done, customer receives a notification, confirming receipt of the report.
- The fraud team pick and actions on the report.

# **On My Safaricom APP**

- Launch MySafaricom APP,
- Click on **Account,**
- Select **Report Fraud,**
- Select **Report a New Fraud**,
- Enter the requested fraud details and submit.
- Customer can track status of the report under **Current Ticket** or **View Previous Tickets** options.

# **Customer Role in Preventing Fraud**

- If a customer receives an SMS or a call from someone claiming they have sent them money by mistake, they should be advised to request sender to call Safaricom for assistance on reversal.
- Confirmation of mobile numbers: customer should use Copy Past feature or number search option to confirm, alternatively use of Hakikisha service or MySafaricom app when doing M-PESA transaction.
- Use a PIN that is not easy for other people to guess.
- Do not share your PIN with anyone, not even Safaricom staff (pin yako, siri yako)
- Do not dial codes or undertake instructions on your handset that you did not request for assistance from Safaricom Customer Care.
- Get the new SIM card which allows you to save contacts for use while transacting instead of having to write down.
- By avoiding oversharing personal details via social networks.
- Don’t respond to unsolicited texts or phone calls. This may allow fraudsters to access personal data and use it in a fraudulent way.

# **M-Shwari Definitions and Features**

# **DEFINITION**

This is a mobile-based banking service provided by NCBA through the Safaricom mobile channel to M-PESA customers to enhance the M-PESA value proposition.

- It offers a **Deposit** and **Loan products** that are convenient, reliable, and cost-effective for making micro-savings and taking micro-loans.
- M-Shwari has three accounts.

- Loan Account.
- Savings Account.
- Lock savings Account.

**ELIGIBILITY**

It is eligible to all registered M-PESA customers whether on Prepay or Post pay.

# **SERVICES THAT M-SHWARI OFFERS**

- Transfer from M-PESA to M-Shwari.
- Transfer from M-Shwari to M-PESA
- Make a loan REQUEST
- Repay loan.
- Check loan limit.
- M-Shwari balance enquiry.
- M-Shwari Lock Savings.
- M-Shwari mini statement.

# **FEATURES AND BENEFITS OF M-SHWARI SAVINGS ACCOUNT**

- M-Shwari Account uses MPESA Pin to transact.
- To get an M-Shwari account, you do not need to go to any bank branch. It’s simple, opt into the service on your M-PESA account on your Safaricom line.
- There are no ledger fees, no limit on the frequency of withdrawals, no minimum operating balance, and no charge on deposits (M-PESA to M-Shwari Account).
- No transactional charges while moving money between M-Shwari and M-PESA.
- No minimum balance needed on your M-Shwari account; no bank charges levied on the account (ledger fees).
- Saving money on M-Shwari will earn you competitive interest.
- To qualify for a loan, one needs to be an M-PESA customer for at least 6 months, put in some savings and use other Safaricom services such as voice, data and M-PESA.
- Access to credit facilities. You can borrow as little as Kshs.100 and get it instantly.
- There are no charges to balance enquiry on the Sim Tool Kit (STK).
- Convenience of mobile banking i.e., you can transact from the comfort of your location.
- Paperless (mobile centric), safe and fast service.

# **REQUIREMENTS TO HAVE AN M-SHWARI ACCOUNT**

- Be a registered Safaricom M-PESA customer.
- Have an active Safaricom M-PESA account/line.
- Hold any of the following identification documents.
 - Kenya National Identification Document (Original ID).
 - A Valid Passport Document.
 - Alien ID (resident Permit) registered by the Government of Kenya.

# **ACCOUNT** **CLOSURE**

If a customer wants to close an M-Shwari account, the CEE shall advise the customer to visit RC/Care desk with original documentation for assistance.

# **Account closure in Retail/Care desk**

- CEE will vet the customer and verify registration details against the identification document presented.
- Confirm if the account has a pending loan, and if any advice the customer to clear the loan.
- Confirm if both M-shwari savings and lock savings account have funds via CRM and if any, advice the customer to withdraw all the cash (account should have zero balance) then proceed with the account closure on CRM.

# BARRING AND UNBARRING

# Definition

- Call Barring is a service that gives customers an option to restrict incoming and outgoing Calls/SMS.
- The Service Provider restricting customers access to all or selected services in cases of outstanding bills and fraudulent activities
- Call Unbarring is a service that enables customers to remove the restrictions activated on incoming and outgoing Calls/SMS.

# Eligibility

This service is available to all Safaricom customers at no cost.

# Barring Mechanics

Where a customer calls requesting for the activation of the service, they should be advised that the service has been disabled and if they want to reactivate to visit the retail center where vetting will be done to ascertain why the customer wants to activate the barring.

# Reasons for barring

### **Customer requests**

- Lost line
- Fraudulently swapped After sharing details with Fraudsters
- Irregular registration

###  **Operator Triggered**

- Outstanding postpaid bills
- Fraud related barrings
- Expired lines
- Lipa mdogo mdogo related barring
- Subscriber irregular registration related barrings

# Impacts of Barring

- Barring impacts sim swap orders on CRM, if the line is barred the sim swap order will not be successful, the CEE must unbar the line then proceed to do the sim swap.
- The customer will not be able to use the line if its barred unless they request the line to be unbared.
- The customer will not be able to use M-PESA services to do transactions.

#  Barring of Specific callers /SMS

- Safaricom network cannot bar one specific number. However, some handsets have features that can do that.
- Alternative features like fixed dialing, No. screening, call restriction and call reject/block SMS in some handsets can also be used.
- There are also internet applications that bar one number.

A conditional monthly access fee (or minimum spend amount) of KES 50,000 (including VAT and Excise duty) that is billed to any enterprise whose total monthly bill is less than Ksh 50,000.

# **Definition**

As a regulated and licensed financial institution, we are required to identify and collect beneficial ownership information for all our business customers. This update is required to ensure compliance with recently enacted regulations and to maintain the accuracy of beneficial ownership information.

# **Who is a beneficial owner**

Beneficial owners are individuals who ultimately own or control a legal entity. This includes individuals with a certain percentage of ownership or control.

The Proceeds of Crime and Anti-Money Laundering Regulations, 2023 **(POCAMLA),** defines a beneficial owner as **a person who ultimately owns or controls a customer or the person on whose behalf a transaction is being conducted, and any person who ultimately exercises effective control over a legal person or arrangement**.

A beneficial owner of a company is a natural person who meets any of the following conditions with respect to the company:

- Holds at least ten percent (10%) of the issued shares in the company either directly or indirectly.
- Exercises at least ten percent (10%) of the voting rights in the company either directly or indirectly.
- Holds a right, directly or indirectly, to appoint or remove a director of the company; or
- Exercises significant influence or control, directly or indirectly over the company. Significant influence or control means participation in the finances and financial policies of a company without necessarily having full control over them.

# **How this information will be collected**

Information will be collected by filling out and uploading required information & documentation through a secure portal accessible only to authorized individuals registered with our company. The information can only be submitted by:

- Organization authorized users with the role of “business Administrator” within the M-PESA G2 Portal (https://org.ke.m-pesa.com) who currently manage users accessing the M-PESA portal.
- Nominated number being a person authorized to manage organization funds through USSD.

# **Type of Information Required**

Key details include full name of the shareholders, national identification details, Percentage Ownership, Nationality of Director among other details. A sample of this information and the form that will be used to collect it is appended here as part of the appendix further below as item No.12.

# **When the portal will be accessible**

Details about accessing the portal will be provided in the coming days through follow-up communications.

# **How safe is the information** **provided**

The portal is designed with robust security measures to ensure the confidentiality and integrity of the submitted information.

# **Regulations that have necessitated the collection of beneficial owners’ information**

**The Companies Act No. 17 of 2015**, Section 93A, requires every company to keep a register of its beneficial owners and submit to the Registrar of Companies a copy of its register and communicate any amendments to the Registrar. This can be achieved by logging in to the Business registry platform hosted on the e-citizen website [(eBusiness (ecitizen.go.ke)](https://brs.ecitizen.go.ke/) ).

**The Proceeds of Crime and Anti-Money Laundering Regulations, 2023 (POCAMLA Regulations),** financial institutions are required to identify and verify beneficial ownership information for their business customers, which includes legal persons and legal arrangements. This entails determining the natural person(s) who ultimately owns or controls a legal entity. These measures are put in place to prevent misuse of legal entities for illicit financial activities.

**The AML/CFT (Amendment) Act, 2023**, came into effect on September 1, 2023. It amended the Proceeds of Crime and Anti-Money Laundering Act (POCAMLA) by imposing an obligation on all reporting institutions (financial institutions included) to:

1. 1. - Identify and verify any applicant seeking to enter a business relationship with them or carry out a transaction or series of transactions with them.
 - Identify and verify a customer whether permanent or occasional, by taking reasonable measures to establish the identity of that person by requiring the applicant or customer to produce an official record reasonably capable of establishing the true identity of the applicant or customer.
 - Identity and verify the identity of natural persons who are beneficial owners of legal persons or arrangements.

# **Accessibility of the disclosed beneficial ownership information of a company** 

The beneficial ownership information disclosed by companies to the Registrar of Companies or to Safaricom will not be available to the public. A company is only allowed to use or disclose beneficial ownership information if:

- communicating with the beneficial owner concerned,
- for compliance with the Regulations (this would include making the relevant filing at the Companies Registry),
- for compliance with a court order, and
- where the beneficial owner has consented to such use or disclosure in writing.

# **Failure submit my Beneficial Ownership information.**

Failure to comply to the Companies Act shall attract a regulatory fine on the Company and each of its officers. Failure to provide beneficial ownership information to Safaricom, may result in disruption in services.

# **For any customers queries, please use the below channels:**

- - For Lipa na M-PESA customers Email: M-PESABusiness@Safaricom.co.ke , or call +254722 002222.
 - For Agents and Dealers Email: MPESAagentadmin@Safaricom.co.ke , or call line 300.
 - For Money Remittance Partners Email: IMT@Safaricom.co.ke • Engage your respective account manager/ management team.

If you have any immediate questions or concerns, please feel free to reach out to support team at M-PESABusiness@safaricom.co.ke.
