articleTitle: Dealer Outlet SIM Swap requests on Partner App
markdownContent:
**Dealer Outlet SIM Swap requests on Partner App**

# **SIM Swap on Partner App**

This is a service that enables Safaricom M-PESA Agent/Dealers to replace Safaricom customer lines using the Partner App.

The SIM Swap service was moved from \*180# to the Partner App on 12th June 2022.

# **Dealer/Agents requirements.**

- One must have access and successfully log into the Partner App.
- The service is available to Agents with M-PESA Agent role.
- If a dealer/agent does not have a smart phone, the Neon Ray Pro is available at Dealer and Agent outlets at Kshs. 4,499

# **What are the SIM Swap service and their respective customer SIM swap requirements on Partner App?**

There are 2 SIM Swap services on Partner App

- **SIM Swap with PIN;**

- Physical ID for scanning
- Original PIN for validation
- New replacement card

- **SIM Swap without PIN;**

- Physical ID for scanning
- New replacement card
- **Note**: The customer will ONLY be able to make and receive calls. All the other services will automatically resume after 24 hours.

# **Mechanics**

- Agent with M-PESA Agent role will log into the app
- Select SIM Swap
- Select SIM Swap option (With PIN or Without PIN)
- Customer details capture:

- Enter the number to be swapped

- Enter the number’s original PIN (required during SIM Swap With PIN)

- Scan ID
- Select Submit details for verification.

- IMSI and SIM Swap

- Enter IMSI (scan IMSI will be availed later)
- Select submit details for verification and replacement of the line.
- Receive notification on the Till

# **MSISDN Swap Eligibility**

- Must be on Prepay Tariff
- Age on Network must be more than 2 days
- Should be Active or not Suspended due to lifecycle on CBS (IN DATA). Expired lines

 will be resumed before swap.

- Should not be blacklisted from swaps (Belong to politically exposed customers, golden numbers /numbers whitelisted by customer or blacklisted by Safaricom Risk).
- MSISDN should not be roaming
- The Original PIN must be the same as provided in the PIN/PUK Certificate of the SIM for SIM Swap With PIN.
- ID details must be the same as is on Partner App
- IMSI must be active and available for pairing on NMS.

# **What will happen after a successful SIM Swap without PIN on Partner App?**

- Line will be suspended on HLR from using SMS, Data and GPRS with key comments on CRM indicating ““Subscriber barred-Partner App swap without PIN”,
- Line will be suspended on M-PESA G2 using a state tag. The state tag has the reason indicated on activity under Audit Logs
- As a result, the customer will **ONLY be able to make and receive calls**. All the other **services will automatically resume after 24** hours. Note; 24hrs from the time the swap was successfully completed.

# **Can a customer top up before resumption of services?**

YES.

- All direct top up procedures that require the customer to use SMS or dial USSD from the swapped number will not be available.
- Advise the customer to use the top up procedures that do not require the above eg. Sambaza from another number, Bamba Poa – direct top up, M-PESA top-up from another number, third party from another number i.e. \*140\*voucher PIN\*Number#.
- Do not advise customers to call 141 since they will incur a cost of 10/-

# **Retail and Call Centre Customer Support:**

Line will have a key comment on CRM “Subscriber barred-Partner App swap without PIN”, state tag on M-PESA G2 and SMS, GPRS & USSD barring(s) on HLR.

Where the customer **requests for resumption of service before 24 hours** the customer will be advised to visit the nearest Retail Centre/Care Desk with their ID for unbarring.

- At Retail Centre/Care Desk will vet the customer’s physical ID
- Proceed to unbar the line on CRM by first suspending using the reason Suspend All - Customer Request and then unsuspend using the reason Unsuspend All - Customer Request

- Proceed to remove the customer suspension tag on M-PESA G2

Where the **customer requests for resumption of service after 24 hours** the line will be unbarred at the call centre/care desks or retail centre.

- Vet the customer’s using ID number (call centre) /Physical ID (retail centre).
- Proceed to bar the line on CRM using the reason Suspend All - Customer Request and then unsuspend using the reason Unsuspend All - Customer Request.
- Proceed to remove the customer suspension tag on M-PESA G2.

# **CRM Key Comment - Subscriber barred-Partner App swap without PIN**

# **Confirmation of SIM Swap Order and the time of swap on CRM**

- Select SIM Swap OTA
- Select SIM Swap OTA
- Check for a Successful SIM Swap - Operation Successful
- Check swap source – SUBREGAPP\_SIMSWAP
- Check the Date Requested – Confirm if within 24 hours or after 24 hours

# **M-PESA G2 View Account has a 24 hours state tag**

State tag View on M-PESA G2 (Select **Error! Filename not specified.**to unbar remove the state tag)

G2 Audit Logs

Reason for capturing the state tag

# **HLR View (MSISDN is barred from SMS, USSD & Data)**

# **For ineligible SIM Swap requests at Agents/Dealer via Partner App**

- Agents will receive a message informing them of the reason why the swap failed at every step.
- Individual Post-pay and hybrid numbers cannot be swapped by a dealer or agent. Dealers will refer the customer to a care outlet or Retail Centre or Care Desk for assistance.
- Also note that the customer’s line will be blocked from performing a swap after 3 failed attempts using incorrect details for 24 hours. They will therefore be required to present themselves at any retail shop or care desk with ID for assistance.
- Dealers will contact their head office for assistance where they are unable to perform SIM Swaps.

# **For Customer who do not have their original SIM Card PIN OR their physical ID**

- If enrolled on Jitambulishe level II customer can Sim Swap via IVR 100/234
- Customer will visit Safaricom retail shop or Care Desk with the registered document ID.

# **Users who are unable to log into the service, will be advised as per the current Partner App user management guidelines.**

# **DEFINITION**

This is a technology that uses voice to identify customers.

- Just like the fingerprint, the voice has unique biometrics for each individual.

# **ELIGIBILITY**

- All individual Safaricom customers are eligible.
- Safaricom staff also qualify if their number is registered with their ID number on Partner App.
- Corporate customers and individual customers registered with passport numbers do not qualify.
- Alien ID holders do qualify if their registration document number is not alphanumeric.
- All Port-In customers will automatically qualify once the port in process is completed.

# **HOW IT WORKS**

- The service allows customers to access self-services easily on the IVR and reduces AHT as the full vetting process is reduced depending on threshold achieved.
- It is a more fraud proof service as voice biometrics cannot be replicated or duplicated.
- The passphrases used at activation are: -

- **English**: “*At Safaricom my voice is my password*”
- **Kiswahili** “*Sauti yangu ndio kitambulisho changu*”

# **BINGWA JITAMBULISHE**

This is a campaign where agents/dealers are rewarded kshs.10 via M-PESA for recommending Jitambulishe uptake to their customers. This will help to increase enrolments.

- To activate the service on their end, the agent will: -

- Dial \*180#
- Select Jitambulishe
- Select Commission payout number.
- Enter number (M-PESA registered) - This is done once.

- To recommend a customer, the dealer will: -
 - Dial \*180#
 - Bingwa sokoni
 - Select Partner App

- - Select recommended customer for Jitambulishe.
 - Agent will enter customer MSISDN and recommend the customer.
 - Customer receives notification to enroll.
 - Customer successfully enrolls and commission is sent to agent number.
- The commission is paid out in cash via M-PESA once a week for all successful enrolments.
- An agent can only recommend a number every 48 hours, Commission will not be paid for customers who have not enrolled after 48 hours.
- Agents will not be able to recommend the service to customers who have deleted their voice print. A notification for successful referral, already referred or already deleted voice print is sent to the agent for accountability.

# **FRAUD CHECKS**

- Customers within defined fraudster locations will not be able to access the service.
- Once they dial the IVR, Jitambulishe will not prompt them to enroll if not enrolled and those enrolled will always get a mismatched threshold upon verification.
- The system will always do a fraud check for all SIM swaps done via IVR, this will be for contact number and the number being replaced.

# **DIY Reversal for Customers**

**Definition**

It is the process for reversing funds from the Recipient’s account (Party B) back to Sender’s account.

**Eligibility**

Only the sender or recipient can request for a P2P reversal by sending the M-PESA transaction message to 456 within 24hrs.

# **How It Works**

**Reversal Via 456**

Customer (sender or recipient) will forward the M-PESA message to 456

The system checks below conditions:

The request is sent by the sender or recipient of funds.

Reversal request is within 24 hours from time of transaction.

Recipient has enough balance to initiate full/partial reversal.

Recipient MSISDN is not blacklisted from reversal.

Reversals requests are limited to a maximum of 3 times per transaction.

The requester receives a message indicating the status of the reversal request, as well as the completion SLA for initiated reversal.

*If recipient sends back this SMS to 456“Dear **Customer, you have cancelled the reversal of SGE8P4F6LW of Ksh 300 from 254748388\*\*\*. If you still wish to reverse, forward this message to 456**.” The transaction will be completed.*

- Safaricom to Safaricom (P2P) transactions are initiated through 456 and Airtime purchase for self are done/completed through 456

# **Web Initiated Reversals**

P2P reversals initiated on M-PESA G2 by an SP operator will be channelled to 456 service for processing.

For all P2P reversals the system will check status of recipient MSISDN on CBS.

Where recipient line is inactive the reversal will be autocompleted.

Where the recipient MSISDN is active the recipient will be called by IVR to seek consent. 

The recipient will be called 3 times within a 20-minute interval of each call to give consent to complete the reversal.

On all IVR calls, the recipient selects one of the presented options.

**Option 1:** To accept the reversal. This will complete the reversal.

**Option 2:** To cancel the reversal. For Ksh 750 and below, the reversal will be cancelled, and the funds availed to the recipient immediately.

For amounts above Ksh 1,000, the reversal will be routed to the P2P cancelled campaign to be handled by the Reversals Admin Team.

If there is no action after all the calls and SMSs.

Reversals below Ksh.750 will autocomplete.

**NOTE:** Transactions of amount **750** & below KSH **750** are closed end to end on 456 Journey.

Reversals above Ksh.750 will remain Pending Authorized and will be picked and actioned by the reversal Admin team.

After completion, both sender and recipient will receive SMS confirmation from M-PESA.

**Scenario 1:** Recipient Requesting for the reversal

The money is automatically reversed back to the sender

**Scenario 2:** Sender Requesting for the reversal

For active registered lines, an SMS will be sent to recipient informing them on the reversal initiated. The recipient can send back this SMS to 456 to complete the reversal.

If the recipient does not respond via SMS, an IVR call will be initiated to recipient after 2 minutes.

The SMS will not be sent for reversals initiated between 6PM and 7AM. For such cases, an IVR call will be initiated to the recipient from 7AM the following day.

For all P2P reversals the system will check status of recipient MSISDN on CBS.

Where recipient line is inactive the reversal will be autocompleted.

Where the recipient MSISDN is active the recipient will be called by IVR to seek consent. 

The recipient will be called 3 times within a 20-minute interval of each call to give consent to complete the reversal. 

**On all IVR calls, the recipient selects one of the presented options.**

**Option 1**: To accept the reversal. This will complete the reversal.

**Option 2:** To cancel the reversal. For Ksh 1,000 and below, the reversal will be cancelled, and the funds availed to the recipient immediately.

For amounts above Ksh 1,000, the reversal will be routed to the P2P cancelled campaign to be handled by the Reversals Admin Team.

If there is no action after all the calls and SMSs.

After completion, both sender and recipient will receive SMS confirmation from M-PESA.

Where some of the funds have been utilized, a partial reversal will be initiated, to help recover the remaining amount, but only if.

The balance of the recipient is above 50/-

If the amount remaining is 10% and above of the amount received.

**Initiating reversal may fail on 456 if**

Sender’s balance will exceed the M-PESA maximum balance of Ksh.500.000

Recipient has reached daily transactional limit Ksh.500,000.

The recipient account is suspended, frozen or capped.

Recipient has insufficient balance i.e. below amounts stated above for partial reversal.

A customer will only be allowed to reverse to a maximum of three times in any transaction.

**Note:** We do not action reversals of Ksh.10 and below through 456  

**Reversal Via Safaricom App**

When transacting on Safaricom App, after completing the transaction press the option for reverse to initiate the reversal.

**Reversal Via Zuri**

The customer sends the MPESA transaction ID to Zuri. You can interact with Zuri via,

Facebook Messenger: m.me/SafaricomZuri

Telegram: On Telegram, search for @SafaricomChatBot or Safaricom Zuri [http://t.me/SafaricomChatBot](http://t.me/SafaricomChatBot)

Blaze Facebook page: m.me/BlazeKenya

WhatsApp: https://wa.me/254722000100

Save number +254 722 000 100 in your contacts.

Now open a chat and type ‘**Hi**’.

Send and wait for a connection reply from Zuri

A toll-free service enhances customer engagement by providing a cost-free way for customers to reach businesses. It builds trust, improves accessibility and strengthens brand credibility by ensuring seamless communication

# **Toll-Free Number- Definition**

A Toll-Free number is a **special business number** that allows customers to call a business without incurring any charges. The cost of the call is covered by the business, making it easy for customers to inquire, seek support or make transactions. These numbers typically start with prefixes such as **0800** or **888** making them easily recognizable.

# **Target Customers for Toll-Free Service**

Toll-Free Service is ideal for:

**Enterprises & Corporates** – Banks, insurance firms, telecom providers and service-oriented companies that require high customer interaction

**Customer Support Centers** – Businesses that offer helplines, technical support or complaint resolution

**Retail & E-Commerce Businesses** – Online stores and brands that need a free communication channel for customer inquiries and orders

**Government & Public Sector Institutions** – Agencies providing public information, emergency hotlines and citizen support services

# **Why a Toll free number**

**Cost-Free Calls for Customers** – Toll-Free numbers eliminate the barrier of call charges encouraging customers to reach out more freely

**Enhanced Brand Image** – An 0800 number projects a professional, credible and accessible brand identity

**Convenient Customer Support** – It provides both potential and existing customers with a hassle-free way to contact businesses

**Increased Customer Trust & Engagement** – A Toll-Free number re-assures clients that the business values customer interaction and service excellence

# **Getting a Special (Vanity) Number**

A **Vanity Number** is a customized Toll-Free number that spells out a business name, a keyword or an acronym that aligns with your brand.

 [Screenshot] 

Benefits of **a Vanity Number** 
✔ Easy to remember, boosting brand recognition✔ Strengthens marketing and customer recall✔ Enhances accessibility and reinforces brand identity

To check availability for a specific Toll-Free or Vanity Number, please contact your **Account Manager**.

# **Key Benefits of Toll-Free Service**

✔**Enhanced Customer Experience** – Customers can contact your business for free, leading to improved satisfaction and trust✔ **Increased Call Volume & Engagement** – Eliminating call charges encourages more customer interactions✔ **Brand Credibility & Professionalism** – A Toll-Free number boosts brand perception and makes your business more accessible✔ **Better Marketing & Lead Generation** – Easy-to-remember numbers drive inbound calls, increasing sales opportunities✔ **Nationwide Reach** – Supports customer access from any location, removing geographical limitations✔ **Call Tracking & Analytics** – Helps monitor call data, improve service quality and measure marketing effectiveness.

With a Toll-Free service, enterprises can **strengthen customer relationships, expand reac****h** **and position themselves as industry leaders.**

# **POST-PAY REVAMP BILLING AND CRM VIEWS**

**Post-Pay DIY REVAMP service**

#  **Definition**

1. Post-pay DIY REVAMP is a tariff that allows customers to get highly discounted monthly plans

2. It allows airtime top up.

# **Eligibility**

It is eligible to;

- Prepay customers, individual auto bar, Hybrid and OLD karibu

- To terminate Post-pay Dial \*200# or go to the web and select Post-pay termination.

 - Settle bill via MPESA or deposit. Any remaining deposit or overpayment will be credited back to MPESA or airtime.

# **Not eligible;**

- Corporate accounts

- Zidisha customers.

- SFC tariff (Safaricom staff).

- MPESA agents/LNM Merchants tills.

If a Zidisha customer has made a payment, they can opt out of Zidisha by visiting Retail and join Post-pay or raise an **SR** for reversal to be done.

# **Terms of Purchase**

- Bundle can be purchased at any time of the month.

- Customers onboarding must buy a plan.

- Once you exhaust the bundle before end of the month, buy other neo bundles or all in one as the customer just want a bundle to cover them till end of the month.

- You **cannot** have **2 autorenewals** bundle at the same time.

- If you exhaust resources before end of the month, you will be charged an out of bundle rate of Kshs.2.30 for calls and Kshs. 2.30 for data.

- This is only applicable once the bundles run out, you can also purchase other bundles with expiry or non-expiry on \*544# or \*200#.

- **You can upgrade or downgrade your plan via \*200#(next phase, not yet implemented)**

 - ***You can also use out of bundle at your discounted Post-Pay rate.***

 - ***Post-pay DIY is Hybrid meaning you can top up airtime either via a voucher or M-PESA.***

 - ***If a customer wants to change a plan, they can opt to opt out and opt back in with a different plan for now until the change of plan is implemented.***

- You will earn Bonga points when you purchase the plans/PostPay bundle.

- PostPay bundles **cannot** be used for **Roaming.**

- Once on PostPay you will not accumulate Storo Bonus.

- You cannot transfer/Sambaza your resources. You can share data via Data sharing(***not yet implemented, next phase).***

- Data Manager service will remain active after joining PostPay. All new prepay without data manager migrating to postpay will automatically activate data Manager.

- Customers will not be able to change their credit limit. Their limit will be zero.

- Customers can pay their bills on \*200# USSD Menu

- Customers can terminate their postpay DIY by dialing \*200# option 14 by either their deposit,mpesa or partially deposit and mpesa.

- After Termination the customers will get their deposit refund within 48 hrs.

- Customers who terminate their plans will have their resources within the month of termination, the resources will expire on the 1st of the next month since the product will not renew.

- Customers onboarding using USSD have to join with a bundle unlike a customer onboarding via safaricom App or Web where they have an option to migrate without a plan. However, they can dial \*200# to buy a plan/bundle.

- Opt in to Postpay is limited to twice in a month to reduce cases of abuse where customers get free full resources then opt out and ask for deposit refund.

# **Plans**

 [Screenshot] 

 [Screenshot]

1. Customer will receive a notification when your data bundle is below 500MB, 75MB and 2MB.

2. For the Unlimited Resources there will be a **Refresh** every month with no roll over.

3. Even though the customer will see unlimited resources there is a limit at the backend.

# **Billing**

- 3rd day of the month – Balance notification SMS

- 12th day of the month- 1st reminder SMS

- 16th day of the month -2nd reminder SMS

- 16th day of the month – Bill is due

- 28th day of the month – Suspension of the product

# **More information on Revamp**

- Minutes and SMS will expire at the end of the month. Data bundle will rollover upon auto renewal ( customer needs to clear bill on time to enable auto renewal).

- The resources given on the first month WILL NOT ROLL OVER. For subsequent month only data will roll over upon auto renewal

- 2GB YT data to be used to access YouTube only shall no longer be awarded since it has been converted to normal bundle and added to the main resource.

- WA bundles to expire with the main resources

- Resources will expire at the end of the month. Only data bundles will roll over upon auto renewal before expiry ( customer needs to clear bill on time to enable auto renewal).

- The PostPay account will be set up on zero credit limit. The customer will be able to top up airtime once they have exhausted their resources

- Renewal of the resources will be done on the 1st of every month

- Customers will still accumulate Bonga points based on bundle charge.

- The minutes can be used for international calls to India, Canada, USA, China.

- For customers who exhaust their resources, they will enjoy discounted out of bundles for voice and data at Ksh 2 .3 per minute and per MB

**FOR THE NEW JOINERS**

On the 1st of November, the bundle will be renewed, and customers will be awarded full resources and charged full amount. The November bill will contain below entries

- Prorated Bundle charge of Kshs 500 October resources (Which will already be settled by the prepayment made during onboarding

- Full bundle charge of Kshs 1000 for November resources

- The bill will be due on 16th of every month, customer will be required to make payment latest by the 31st of every month to enable renewal of the bundle

- Customers will pay for the resources awarded within the same month. Example Resources renewed on 1st of November will be due for payment on 30th of November.

articleTitle: Contact Centre and Retail M-PESA opt-in Dividend Registration Query Link and M-PESA Business Portal Admin Creation
markdownContent:
# **M-PESA opt-in Dividend Registration Query Link**

- To verify if a shareholder’s registration has been received the CEE will go the CC intranet as below:
- Select ‘MPESA’
- Select ‘M-PESA Dividend Opt in’
- Select ‘Dividend registration check link’
- To check on the respective shareholder registration details.
- Select the link; Log on using your windows Username and password.
- Query using the MSISDN, starting 7XXXXXXXX (omit the beginning zero).
- Once a shareholder’s registration has been received, it should appear indicating:
- MSISDN used for registration
- Names as per M-PESA registration
- ID number submitted
- CDS account number submitted
- Date of receipt of the registration
- If the query comes out blank, it means that:
- The MSISDN used to query is not the one used to register.
- The shareholder did not complete the registration process the shareholder is not registered on M-PESA

**Note:**

The link will also be able to display registrations from last year. This will be helpful especially for shareholders who received their dividend last year and are not required to register again.

They link will help establish the registration details received last year and the shareholder can confirm if they are correct.

In case of any query, contact Investor relations on 0722004260/0722004524 or escalate to [investorrelations@safaricom.co.ke](mailto:investorrelations@safaricom.co.ke)

# **Requirements**

The MSISDN must be registered on M-PESA and on active status. The shareholder MUST register with an MSISDN that is registered under their name and ID/ Passport number.

- Shareholders are required to register the ID/ Passport number that they used when opening their CDS account. If this identification number is different from the one used to open their M-PESA account, the shareholder will be required to visit any Safaricom Shop with an original copy of your ID/Passport number and update your M-PESA records as per the ID used to open your CDSC account.

Any format of the CDS account will be accepted i.e. the entire number or just the unique number.

Entire/whole number - The CDS number can be inserted as a whole without the slashes e.g. B09B0000006945848LI, KCBC0000001642804LI, NBKC0000006276741LI, EQBC0000006276741LI

Unique number - The unique number format e.g. from the above CDS number 694584 or 1642804 or 627674 or 627674

- If the Safaricom shareholder would like to know their CDS account number, please ask them to contact their stockbroker or CDSC on 0724-256130 or 0733-222033 or 020 2229406/7/8.
- If Safaricom shareholder has a share certificate, kindly ask them to contact Image Registrars on 0724-699667 or 020-2230330/2246449/2212965 or email [info@image.co.ke](mailto:info@image.co.ke)  to fill out the manual opt in form.
- This is just a registration process where shareholders are given the opportunity submit their details. It does not guarantee that they shall receive their dividends via M-PESA. Once the M-PESA Dividend opt in period closes; validations will be carried out on the details received to verify if the shareholder qualifies to receive dividend via M-PESA or Not.
- Registrations MUST pass the validation process for the shareholder to be considered successful to receive their Safaricom dividend via M-PESA. The key considerations are:

- The person is a shareholder as at 12the September 2013 (Books Closure Date).
- The person is an individual Shareholder (No joint/group/company accounts).
- The person is a registered M-PESA user.
- The ID number MUST match on both CDSC records and M-PESA records.

- In case the shareholders request for more information, please advise them to contact Investor Relations on 0722004260/0722004524 or escalate to [investorrelations@safaricom.co.ke](mailto:investorrelations@safaricom.co.ke)

# **Admin Creation (New and change of admin requests)**

Admin creation will be done by the onboarding teams during account creation.

Where this is not done at onboarding, or the partner requires a change of the operator or an update of the KYC details of the admin; the Partner will be advised to request for the same via a written request to: -

M-PESA Business [M-PESABusiness@Safaricom.co.ke](mailto:M-PESABusiness@Safaricom.co.ke)  or Lipa na M-PESA [Lipanampesa@Safaricom.co.ke](mailto:Lipanampesa@Safaricom.co.ke)

Retail/Care Desk where the CEE will raise an SR for RCSA to follow up.

Account management teams who will share the details to ESD LNM support via email.

#  **Requirements of a written request**

Be accompanied by ID copy or scanned ID of the Admin

This will match the details captured on the letter.

If the number issued is a Safaricom MSISDN the details will be vetted using Jiandikishe and the name details must match the ID details.

Have the respective company letter head and bear the organization stamp/seal.

Be signed by 2 official signatories (1 for companies with sole signatories)

Include the respective Short Code

Include the name of the current admin for change requests.

Include the new admin details: i.e.:

- First Name
- Middle Name (Not Mandatory)
- Last Name
- Document Type (Either Passport, National ID etc,)
- Document / ID Number:
- Nationality
- Date of Birth
- Phone Number
- Email address: For organizations with domains the email should be a personal official email (ie. An active personal email with the organization’s domain name).

# **Action Required by M-PESA Corporate CEE**

- Where the documents do not pass vetting the team will advise the partner accordingly.
- Where the documents pass vetting all CEEs except the M-PESA Corporate Team will raise an SR and attach all documents.
- Call Center tickets will be channelled to ESD LNM Support.
- The CEE Will create a BMC for M-PESA IT to effect the change within 24 hours.
- LNM Support Team will update notes on the SR and proceed to close it once the admin is created.

# **Action Required by Retail CEE**

Retail tickets will be channelled to RCSA.

# **Action Required by RCSA or ESD LNM Support**

- RCSA or ESD LNM Support (respectively) will create a BMC for M-PESA IT to effect the change within 24 hours.
- RCSA and ESD LNM Support Team will update notes on the SR and proceed to close it once the admin is created**.**

# **Payments Portal B2B Payments /Transaction Process**

- Partners will be able to move funds from one business one account to another within the BE. Movement of funds will be determined by the approval levels set by the BE.
- Safaricom staff will use M-PESA G2 to execute transactions upon written request by the partner and where the team has the mandate to do so.

**Intra-Accounts Funds transfer requirements**

- This allows an organization to move funds from one M-PESA Account to another within the same Short code M-PESA Accounts.
- This will allow movement of funds to and from the following M-PESA accounts:

MMF Account to working account

Utility Account to working account

Float Account to working account

### **This will only be possible if**

- The short code is active in MPESA G2
- The accounts must belong to the same short code
- The sending account must have funds to transfer.

**Note:** Funds transfer will be locked within the current M-PESA Business limits.

# **This is currently only available on web.**

- Partners/merchants and SP users must have access to the web portal and are active users with the right permissions to be able to initiate.
- The user will login to the org system and transfer funds
- Funds will be move and the affected accounts updated correctly.
- Transaction details captured on M-PESA Business Payments Portal and G2 for reporting.

# **Inter-Accounts Funds transfer**

- This allows an organization to move funds from one short code to another.
- Partners will be able to initiate B2B transactions via USSD/Web. This will initiate a revenue settlement transaction.
- This will settle all the outstanding charges if any, and will transfer the balance to MMF account, the working account will be debited, and the receiving organization’s working account credited with the same amount.

# **Inter-Accounts Service Requirements**

- The initiating organization must be existing and active in M-PESA
- The receiving organization must be existing and active in M-PESA
- The process will require approvers which is configurable (0-n approval levels). Where n is a number configurable by the respective organization as per business needs and requirements and not more than 5 levels.
- Transaction types set and configured on the portal are:

Business buy goods: this will allow an organization to make payments to buy goods till

Business Paybill: This will allow an organization to make payments to Paybill

# **Inter-Accounts Service Models**

Partners will only be to initiate B2B transactions via the closed model.

This model only allows the whitelisted organizations to receive funds from the initiating organization.

#  **For the funds transfer to work:**

- The initiating short code (sender) must be whitelisted as a sender on the portal.
- The receiving short code must be whitelisted as a receiver in the sender’s receivers list on the portal.
- Sender/receiver whitelist will be done by LNM support within 24 hours of request.

# **Inter-Accounts Whitelist Process**

- The organization applying for B2B will indicate the list of remitting organizations that will be debited (sender), and the list of receiving organizations that will be credited (receiver) during the B2B funds transfer process.
- Subsequent whitelisting requests will be accompanied by an official letter on the company letterhead, detailing the whitelist organization, signed by at least 2 authorized signatories (where applicable).
- The requests will be channelled via SR to the LNM support team and relevant documents attached.
- Whitelisting will be done within 24 Hours and partner advised via email/SMS.
- LNM support teams will close SR with relevant notes.

articleTitle: Contact Centre Service Request Information and Escalation Process
markdownContent:
**CEE Action Required**

# **Upon receiving a customer query: -**

CEE will trouble-shoot conclusively making use of all available systems that are at their disposal to resolve the customer issue at hand.

Reference all communication that has been shared through Noticeboard or Call Centre Escalation Folder and refer to E-saka to get details if it happens that they do not have information at their fingertips. Proper troubleshooting is important to conclusively address the issue.

# **First escalation point**

For issues that cannot be resolved on call, the CEE is required to raise an SR capturing all necessary information.

Advise the customer that the issue has been escalated for further troubleshooting and action.

Give the customer anticipated timeline (SLA) for resolution so that customers’ expectations are well managed.

At this point do not send an email unless from your interaction with the customer you note that the customer is not willing to wait at all. This should be an exception rather than the norm.

**Repeat caller**

If a customer calls back and issue not yet fully addressed reference notes that have been added to the SR under resolution , notes , activities and attachments on Service requests (SRs) and advise the customer to be patient based on the information that has been added to the SR ticket .

In the event the issue has been closed, explain to the customer what the solution given is based on what is seen on the SR closing notes.

Where customer issue is not fully resolved but SR is closed, the CEE will raise a new SR.

# **Support Analyst Action required**

Once the Ticket is raised by the CEE it is assigned to the Support analyst for action and closure.

The Analyst will action the SR by offering the applicable resolution to the customer and close the SR with clear notes on resolution offered

For Escalated issues that require approval from 3rd Line Support Analyst the 2nd Line support analyst will escalate the issue to them for approval and then await approval once done they analyst will contact customer, resolve issue and close SR. Example for a recycled line the 2nd line support analyst will raise the issue with NMS for line recreation then once done and shared back to the analyst for resolution and closure.

# **The Table below shows sample of SR Category, Type. Item and SLA**

| Categories | Type | Item | SLA |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SIM Card Issues | SIM Swap | First Call Activation Failed | 6 |
| SIM Swap Order Failed | 6 | | |
| Unable to Raise SIM Swap Order | 6 | | |
| Pooled on Subscriber Portal | 6 | | |
| Number on Pool | Number on Pool | 24 | |
| Number Missing On HLR | 24 | | |
| Golden Number On Pool | 24 | | |
| Pooled on Subscriber Portal | 24 | | |
| Number Not in Siebel | Registered on Jiandikishe | 6 | |
| Suspended Line | Suspend/Resume Greyed Out | 6 | |
| Resume Order Failure | 6 | | |

| Global System Failure | 6 | | |
| SIM Bar | SIM Bar Order Failed | 6 | |
| Unable To Raise Bar Order | 6 | | |
| Bar GPRS Only | 6 | | |

# **Quality Service Requests**

**Characteristics of a Quality Service Requests (SR)**

Issue is outside your scope of responsibility.

Correct SR Category/Type/Item

Validate and capture customer issue while including all relevant information that will help in resolution.

Capture details as expected e.g. vetting details and contact number etc.

**Non-Quality Service Requests**

**Characteristics of a Non-Quality Service Requests (SR)**

Ticket raised and the issue could be handled on call to offer FCR.

Any ticket where information captured is insufficient to resolve the issue and the Support analyst handling the ticket needs to call the customer or seek more details to resolve the issue e.g. no voucher serial numbers, IMEI, vetting details, Contact number etc.

Escalation done when there is communication with instructions not to escalate. E.g. email from Notice Board or Call Center Escalation Folder.

Duplicate tickets.

Ticket raised and either wrong category, item or type selected.

# **Trends of Non-Quality Service Requests**

SRs raised for issues within CEE’s scope of responsibility- that should be resolved using the available systems as well as products and service knowledge. This leads to unnecessary escalation thus will attract an Auto-fail score.

Selecting wrong Category, Type as well as item or any of the same e.g. Lipa Na M-PESA issue escalated as a Pay bill reversal issue.

Failure to provide adequate and relevant information for ease of reference. The Support analyst depends solely on SR notes and thus the escalated issue should be explained clearly on SR notes without necessitating the support analyst/ person dealing with SR to call the customer for more details. The CEE should provide enough and correct information to facilitate resolution.

Capturing wrong transaction ID for reversal cases.

Failure to provide contact /alternative number for follow up where necessary

Failure to provide details of the Recharge Voucher and SIMEX/IMEI serial numbers. All the digits of the serial numbers of recharge number and replacement SIMEX should be included

Failure to provide required Vetting details/capturing wrong vetting details/Customer Information as required. This applies for cases where the CEE raises an SR for issues that requires vetting e.g. PIN/PUK, SIM SWAP etc.

Raising duplicate SRs. This applies to cases where the CEE raises a ticket while there is an existing SR on the same issue.

Billing issue; failure to clearly indicate the CDRs that are missing: from what time against what is available on the system. One should capture all related data with reference to billing system.

Basic troubleshooting not done. A ticket should have troubleshooting information. e.g. customer gets an error when trying to send SMS.

Actual problem not identified. Notes captured should be understood.

Unnecessary SR: The CEE Raising an SR because they are unable to manage the customer/ want to end the call, rushing to advise the customer that they will escalate the issue without confirming the actual issue as well as possible resolve etc. e.g. due to data billing issue etc. The idea is to explain clearly the issue to the customer especially for billing cases with the support from system.

Raising SRs for repeat queries without confirming why the first option/s given failed to work.

Raising SR for cancelled transactions e.g. cancelled MPESA reversals and for cases that the previous SR/closed indicate the next step that the customer should take.e.g. Visit retail shop, change handset etc.

Raising an SR when there is a global system issue and there is an email guiding on how to handle the customer.e.g. Apologize to the customer waiting the issue to be resolved.

Raising SRs for issues that are outside Safaricom and the procedure/process does not require one to do the same. This also applies to raising the SRs that will result to the support analyst/person dealing with an SR to advise the customer on the same as what you could have advised the customer/customer failed to agree etc.

# **Exceptions for Non-Quality SR**

The above is a guide and does not cover all the areas that can result to an SR considered non-quality.

The CEE is expected to use all the systems at their disposal and consult where necessary before raising any SR.

If experiencing system outage, the CEE may escalate the issue and clearly indicate the reason on SR notes

# **SR Past SLA**

**Prerequisites**

When an SR is past SLA it means it has gone beyond the Stipulated Service Level Agreement time.

Where an issue goes Past the defined SLA, a follow-up escalation is done via email to the responsible email folder and copy the owner (analyst assigned the SR) where applicable.

Ensure to capture the below details when sending an email escalation:

Subject: Past SLA: Capture in Brief what the issue is

Customer Number:

SR Number:

Contact Number:

Order Number where applicable:

# **Reported Issue and Action Required by CEE**

Similar issues or multiple reported issues

When many similar issues following each other on first contact point indicating there could be an outage or issue cropping up that needs to be investigated and arrested before it becomes a crisis in the contact Centre.

Any issues that are on escalations link and are past SLA

**Action:** This should be sent via email to the Call Centre Escalation Folder for further investigation

# **Data Reversals Past SLA**

**Action**

If issue is on the data reversal link send to Call Centre Escalation Folder

If issue is on SR, send to COPS Support Center Escalation

All Prepaid and M-PESA issues that are Past SLA on SR

Action: Email SR Owner and COPS Support Center Escalation

All Post-paid issues that are Past SLA on SRs

Email SR Owner and COPS CCSPostpaid@safaricom.co.ke

**Fibre to the home (FTTH) that are Past SLA on SRs**

**Action:** Email SR Owner and CopsFtth@safaricom.co.ke

Fibre to the building (FTTB) that are past SLA on SRs

Action: Email **Business.support@Safaricom.co.ke** and COPSCCSData

Network issues that are Past SLA on SRs

**Action****:** Email SR Owner and CM support High Priority Folder

Initiated reversals that are not completed within stipulated SLA

**Action**

Do an outbound to Recipient to get consent and Proceed to action based on consent given by recipient.

Send an email to SR owner and COPS Support Center Escalation for those that are on SRs

Email Call Centre Reversals where there is no SR on the same.

Backend Errors that are Past SLA on SR

**Action****:** Email CC CRM Escalation

Mobile Number Portability (MNP) issues Past SLA already on SRs

**Action****:** Email MNP CM escalations

Fraud related issues that are Past SLA on SR

**Action****:** Email SR owner and Line 300 TM Escalations

Customer Retention issues that are Past SLA

**Action****:** Email SR owner and Customer Retention

**Exceptions**

Do not send or copy the emails to COPS Call Centre CEE CMCallCentreCEE@Safaricom.co.ke.

For SRs past SLA raised at the retail shops, send to the respective Retail Shop’s folder and copy the analyst assigned the SR

# **SIM Swap on Partner App Intercept – Non-KYC Compliant Customers**

Following the ongoing Communication Authority’s SIM registration exercise and the fast approaching deadline, we will be intercepting every SIM swap request made by a customer who are yet to update their SIM registration details on Partner App.

This will ensure that we update their registration details before proceeding with the SIM Swap.

# **FAQS**

# **What is SIM swap intercept?**

This is a SIM swap service intercept via a pop-up message on the Partner App that will prompt M-PESA Agents/Dealers to update the SIM registration details for customers who are yet to submit their registration details.

# **What is the content of the SIM swap intercept pop-up message?**

“Dear Agent, the submitted line 2547\*\*\* is not duly registered. Please click on continue to update customer details before proceeding with Sim Swap.”

# **How does it work?**

Every time an M-PESA Agent/Dealer attempts to perform a SIM swap on the Partner App of a customer who is yet to submit their registration detail; they will receive a pop-up message advising them to update the SIM registration details of the customer before proceeding to SIM Swap.

1. 1. The pop-up message will appear every time an M-PESA Agent/Dealer attempts to perform a SIM Swap of a KYC non-compliant customer.
 2. The M-PESA Agent/Dealer will not be able continue with the SIM swap journey before updating the customer’s SIM registration details
 3. The current SIM swap journey will continue once the customer details are updated

# **Who will be targeted?**

All customers who are yet to update their SIM registration details and are seeking SIM Swap services at M-PESA Agent/Dealer outlets.

# **How can a customer check their SIM registration status?**

To check SIM REGISTRATION DETAILS compliance, customers will dial\*106# and select option 1 “Check Registration Status”

# **What are the available channels a customer can access to update their SIM registration details?**

- Web – [https://safaricom.com/account/kyc-upload](https://safaricom.com/account/kyc-upload)
- My Safaricom App - [https://safaricomapp.page.link/updatesimdetails](https://safaricomapp.page.link/updatesimdetails)

- Safaricom shops / Safaricom care outlets / Safaricom

articleTitle: KCB M-PESA Issues, Escalations and Resolutions
markdownContent:
# **KCB M-PESA KYC STATUS**

The status will be displayed on CRM/Siebel under MPESA VAS >KCB-M-PESA tab> KYC Level.

The status varies as shown below:

- **Not Verified:** - New customer records waiting KYC processing, no action required by customer.
- **Customer Profile incomplete:** - Customer records being processed, no action by customer.
- **Success:** - Customer records successfully processed by opt-in service; no action required by customer.
- **Customer KYC check failed:** - Customer KYC processing failed. Customer gets a message advising them to visit a retail Centre. The retail CEE will amend customer details as in ID in M-PESA G2.
- **Customer IPRS Check incomplete:** - Customer records is still in IPRS processing stage, no action required by the customer.

# **LOAN REJECTED**

- When a customer complains of inability to get KCB-M-PESA loan, CEE can confirm the customers CRB status under KCB-M-PESA customer details.
- If the status indicates **1** means **CRB passed** and customer is not listed on CRB. However, if the customer is still unable to get loan, The CEE can advise the customer to try again or use USSD:\*334#
- If the status indicates **0** means **CRB status failed** means sub is listed on CRB in such cases, the customer should contact KCB bank or CRB for further assistance.
- If the loan request persists, under the above circumstances, the CEE should raise an SR explaining the exact error experienced as below

- **Sr category**: KCB M-PESA
- **Type**: Customer loan account
- **Item**: Loan Request

# **KCB M-PESA STATEMENT VIEW**

Customer statement can be viewed for a maximum period of 1 Year from the date of query on CRM.

The CEE can view the following on the statement:

- Activity Time Stamp i.e. date and time.
- Transaction Reference (KCB transaction reference number).
- Activity Type i.e., transactions that affect the account balance (financial or non-financial).
- Balance before Activity.
- Transaction Amount.
- Balance after Activity.

# **Benefits**

The CEE can view M-PESA to KCB MPESA account transactions and KCB MPESA Account to M-PESA transactions.

All transactions to and from M-PESA to KCB M-PESA pass through the savings account i.e. when opening a fixed deposit account from M-PESA; the amount to be fixed will first go through KCB-M-PESA savings account before being transferred to the fixed deposit account.

# **KCB M-PESA LOAN ACCOUNT DETAILS**

The loan account tab has the loan contract ID and loan virtual contract ID, this will be used when there’s an issue that requires an escalation to the bank.

- KCB loan repayment period is one month, referred to as loan term in this tab.
- KCB – M-PESA Savings account details. This tab has visibility of the customer accounts: savings, fixed deposit and target savings accounts.
- The savings maturity date is displayed.
- Where the customer has several accounts, the CEE will be able to navigate to the tabs on the right to view details of customer savings.

# **LOCKED /FORGOTTEN KCB M-PESA ACCOUNT PIN**

- KCB M-PESA was moved to STK. Therefore, the KCB M-PESA PIN is the same as the M-PESA PIN.
- If the customer is not able to find KCB MPESA on the MPESA tool kit, confirm if customer is using BIG or SMALL SIM:

- Where customer is using the BIG SIM advice the customer to access KCB M-PESA through the STK and use the M-PESA PIN.
- If M-PESA PIN is locked, kindly vet the customer as per the M-PESA PIN guidelines and unlock.
- Where customer is using Small SIM; advise customer to upgrade to BIG SIM card; educate the customer on benefits of upgrading to Big SIM and the available outlets for the same.
- Where the customer is not willing to upgrade, advise customer to contact KCB bank.

# **KCB M-PESA (Recycled Account)**

- In the event of an erroneously recycled KCB M-PESA account, vet using the normal process then proceed to check KCB M-PESA accounts balance.
- If the customer has any amount above 1Ksh advise the customer to withdraw all funds from KCB M-PESA Savings account, KCB M-PESA target and fixed accounts before raising an SR for Recycling. Where a customer has a balance of below 1ksh, vet using the normal process then proceed to raise an SR.
- KCB M-PESA target account transactions (**deposit or withdrawals are done once after 24hrs).**
- If 24hrs have not expired from the last transaction advise customer to withdraw after it expires and call back for further assistance.
- In the event that customer tries to withdraw, and it fails (this can be verified from M-PESA audit logs) the CEE needs to indicate on the SR that customer has tried to withdraw without success, because in some cases, funds could belong to the previous owner.

# **KCB-MPESA Failed opt In Issue**

- For customers who want to activate KCB M-PESA on their new acquired line and had **previously** activated KCB M-PESA on their old line which has been recycled line, the CEE should escalate via SR as a Failed opt in and advise the customer on SLA.
- The Support Analyst will engage with KCB Team to fully recycle to allow customer to successfully opt in since previous line was recycled but not fully.

**Nominated number**

If a new customer deposits funds to KCB M-PESA account and is recovered to repay previous customer’s loan, customer should be advised to provide an active KCB M-PESA line also referred to as (nominated number) to allow refund before recycling is done. If the customer has No other active account except the existing one the CEE should indicate on SR.

- **Name mismatch**

KCB M-PESA account may have different names with Partner App details but same ID number. An SR should be raised with the following categories to enable the support team to raise an incidence to the third line support via BMC:

- category: KCB M-PESA.
- Type: Account Amendment.
- Item: Change of Account details.

Once received, the support analyst will escalate to the link and Cops analyst team pull the file and escalate via incidence to the bank for recycling.

- **Change of ownership**

In cases where the change of ownership was done and KCB M-PESA not recycled. The customer should visit retail center for assistance.

# **KCB M-PESA CUSTOMER CARE:**

- KCB customer care team: +254711087000 (chargeable).
- Facebook: KCB Bank Group.
- Twitter: @Kcbgroup.
- SMS: 22522.
- Chat: Available on their website https://ke.kcbbankgroup.com.
- [KCB M-PESA product information is as is in this link: https://www.safaricom.co.ke/personal/m-pesa/do-more-with-m-pesa/kcb-m-pesa](https://www.safaricom.co.ke/personal/m-pesa/do-more-with-m-pesa/kcb-m-pesa).

# Definition

This is a service that allows Customers to use their accumulated No Expiry bundles to make payments at **Safaricom** Lipa Na M-PESA merchant till Both Paybill and Buy goods merchants. It is **NOT** open to all merchants.

- The eligible data bundles are; Post-pay DIY Karibu bundles, Go Monthly Postpay and Neo (Milele) bundles.

# Conversion Rate

 The conversion rate is Ksh 0.06 per Mb (6 cents per Mb). Below is a summarized conversion table:

| Ksh | MBs @ 0.060 |
| --- | --- |
| 50 | 833 |
| 100 | 1,667 |
| 300 | 5,000 |
| 500 | 8,333 |
| 1,000 | 16,667 |
| 1,500 | 25,000 |
| 2,000 | 33,333 |
| 2,500 | 41,667 |
| 3,000 | 50,000 |
| 5,000 | 83,333 |
| 10,000 | 166,667 |

# How To Lipa Na Data:

| Customers will dial *544#>My Data Deals>Redeem your Data>Buy Goods/Paybill. Customers will also be able to access bundles calculator and check eligible bundle balances on the same menu. Only Whitelisted Customers (Those with high data bundle volumes) can access the service via direct string *544*34#. Eligible services include.Payment for Fiber-200200Payment of Postpaid bills-200200Purchase of devices from any R/CPayment for telematic services- Internet of Things (IoT)Conversion of the data to roaming data.Postpaid productsSambaza |
| --- |

# To check the amount of money they can get from their data bundles

**C****ustomers will dial** \*544#>My Data Deals>Redeem Your Data>Bundles calculator. Customers can also access the bundles calculator via Safaricom App/Web under Redeem Your Data option

# To view balances of the eligible data bundles

**C****ustomers will dial** \*544#>My Data Deals> Redeem Your Data >View Bundles. Customers can also access the View bundles option via Safaricom App/Web under Lipa na Data.

# Priority

**W****hile redeeming the different bundle accounts for Lipa Na Data is as per below:**

- Neo Data Bundles
- Go Monthly Postpay Data
- Karibu Postpay DIY data bundles

# Reversal

In case a customer pays to the wrong till, fails to get a notification thus payment not honored by merchant, they will call 200/100 or visit Safaricom shop requesting for reversal of the bundles.

# CEE Actions for Reversal Requests

When a customer calls or visits a Safaricom shop requesting for Lipa na data reversal, the CEE will confirm the relevant transaction details on the CRM Lipa Na Data VBC. If the transaction was successful, the CEE will raise an SR and advise customer on SLA.

If the transaction status is ‘Failed’ on the VBC The CEE will check whether data bundle was auto reversed and if yes advise customer. If no the Cee will raise an Sr and advise customer.

# **Retail/Call Center Support Analysts Reversal Actions**

Upon receiving Lipa Na Data SR, the analyst will verify details as captured by CEE. There are two possible scenarios that the analyst needs to verify:

Data bundle has been deducted on CRM but no corresponding transaction on G2. We have implemented auto-reversal for such scenarios thus Analyst will confirm if the bundle was auto reversed. If auto reversal failed, analyst will refund the bundle manually via BSS (Via Manual adjustment) and advise customer.

The transaction was completed successfully but customer requests for reversal for reasons such as wrong till, lack of notification etc. In this case the analyst will follow the below procedure:

- Confirm the transaction was successful on the CRM Lipa Na Data VBC
- Query the M-PESA Txn id on G2 and confirm that e-cash was transferred from Lipa Na Data B2B paybill **9188333** to merchant’s account
- Call Merchant to seek reversal consent
- If consent is given then analyst will reverse the cash via G2
- Analyst will then manually adjust the data bundle onto customer’s account via BSS (consider the data bundle units used on BSS and convert accordingly-MBs to Bytes)
- Reversal disputes to be treated as per existing rules & procedure
- Lack of funds on Merchant till to be treated as per existing reversal procedure

**Definition**

 Ziidi Shariah is a Shariah-compliant investment product that adheres to Islamic law.

**Eligibility to Invest in Ziidi Shariah**

ZiiDi Shariah is open to all M-PESA registered customers seeking ethical and Shariah compliant investment opportunities, regardless of religious background. However, it is designed specifically for those who wish to align their investments with Islamic principles.

**Key Highlights**

- The product is regulated by the Capital Market Authority.
- The fund manager is Gulf Capital Investment Bank
- It will be available through a mini app known as ZiiDi Sharia or \*334#

**NOTE:**

Since ZiiDi and ZiiDi Shariah have different fund managers, the profit earnings may be different.

Earnings are referred to as PROFIT **NOT** interest.

**How ZiiDi Shariah-Compliant Investments Differ from Conventional Products**

A Shariah-compliant investment product adheres to Islamic principles, which prohibit interest (riba), excessive uncertainty (gharar), and investments in haram (forbidden) industries like alcohol, gambling, or pork. Instead, it focuses on profit-sharing, asset backed investments, and ethical financing.

**How Shariah-Compliant Investments Differ from Conventional Products**

ZiiDi Shariah is a Shariah-compliant investment product that adheres to Islamic law (Shariah).

It is guided by principles outlined in the Quran and Hadith (sayings and actions of the Prophet Muhammad) and is designed to ensure that its practices are ethical and adhere to specific rules. ZiiDi is regulated by the Capital Markers Authority.

**Ensuring Shariah Compliance in This Product**

ZiiDi Shariah is structured to avoid interest (riba), uncertainty (gharar), and prohibited industries.

It is certified by a Shariah supervisory board, which ensures compliance with Islamic principles.

**Fund manager for ZiiDi Shariah**

The fund manager for Ziidi Shariah is Gulf Capital Investment Bank.

**Transparency on Fees and Interest Charges**

All fees are transparent and comply with Shariah principles. There are no interest charges, as they are replaced with profit-sharing or service fee.

**Investment Process**

**Is This Investment Only for Muslims**

No, ZiiDi Shariah is available to all M-PESA registered customers interested in ethical and Shariah-compliant investments.

**Minimum investment requirements**

The minimum investment amount is Kes.100, and the minimum amount to withdraw is Kshs.10. There is no limit to maximum balance ZiiDi Shariah can hold.

**Getting Started with Your Investment**

ZiiDi Shariah can be accessed via:

ZiiDi SHARIAH MMF Mini-App on the M-PESA super app

USSD under \*334# > Financial Services > ZiiDi > ZiiDi Shariah

**Flexibility in Withdrawing Your Funds**

A customer can withdraw their funds and receive immediately, **except** for locked funds which will be availed after **72 hours** of successful withdrawal.

**Charges and Limits**

There are no transaction fees for investing, withdrawing, or checking balances on ZiiDi Shariah MMF.

The current M-PESA transaction limits of KSh 250,000 per transaction and daily transaction limit of Ksh.500,000. will apply to all ZiiDi Shariah invest and withdraw transactions.

**Distribution of Profits**

Profits are calculated annually, compounded, and paid out daily at midnight based on funds invested during that period. (Please note the reference to ‘PROFIT’ **NOT** ‘INTEREST’ when handling a Shariah compliant product).

**Tracking of investment**

A customer will receive periodic statements detailing your investment performance, profits, and any fees deducted.

**Fees associated with this ZiiDi Shariah**

Fees may include management fees, administrative costs, and profit-sharing ratios. All fees are disclosed upfront and comply with Shariah principles.

**Lock Funds**

**What It Means to Lock Funds in ZiiDi Shariah**

Locking money in ZiiDi Shariah gives a customer a layer of security and control over your money and keeps you concentrated on your financial objectives.

It also means putting away some or all of your money to avoid unforeseen expenses. As of right now, locked money won't receive any more interest than unlocked funds do.

**Duration of Locking Funds**

There is no specific time limit for locking your funds. One can lock their funds for as long as they like using the ZiiDi Shariah Mini App on the M-PESA Super App or via USSD by dialling \*334#. Additionally, one can top up thier locked funds without the need to unlock them first.

**Funds Availability after Un-locking**

A customer can only unlock all their locked funds, not just a portion of them, and your money will be accessible 72 hours after it is unlocked.

After unlocking, all prior unlock transactions must be finished and funds must be successfully disbursed before a new lock funds request may be started.

**Do Locked Funds Move from My ZiiDi Shariah Wallet**

No, ZiiDi Shariah has only has one wallet where funds can be locked, and these funds remain static. For partial locks, the Mini App will display three balances: the overall ZiiDi Shariah balance, the available balance (for use), and the locked balance.

**Is there a transaction limit for locking or unlocking funds**

No, there is no limit to the amount that can be locked or unlocked. However, the amount you wish to lock or unlock must be equal to or less than the available balance in your ZiiDi Shariah wallet. Additionally, there are no fees associated with locking or unlocking your invested funds.

**Will Locked Funds Earn Higher Returns in ZiiDi Shariah**

No, the interest earned will be the same for the locked and unlocked funds.

**Risks and Returns**

**Potential Returns on This Investment**

Profits are based on the performance of the underlying assets and are shared between the investor and the fund manager according to the agreed profit-sharing ratio.

**Are There Any Investment Risks**

Like all investments, there are risks, including the potential loss of capital. However, the product is designed to minimize risk through ethical and asset-backed investments.

**Is there a guarantee in my investment**

No, investments are not guaranteed. Profits depend on the performance of the underlying assets.

**Customer Support**

**Who to contact for more details**

For assistance, dial 100 (Prepaid) or 200 (Postpaid) to contact our customer support team or visit our website.

**Can I Visit a Physical Branch**

Our services are primarily digital, but you can visit the nearest Safaricom Shop for in\[1\]person support.

**Claim of Funds by Next of Kin**

Next of Kin is the person whose details are nominated on ZiiDi Shariah by the account owner or is the legally designated heir and in the event of incapacities such as sickness, mental instability, and death they can have access to your funds. On condition of.

The customer (Next of Kin) will visit the nearest Safaricom retail shop or care desks and provide the following documents:

A duly filled ZiiDi Shariah MMF next of kin claim of funds form.

Identification document (ID) • Death Certificate in case of death

Grant of Probate/Letter of Administration

Letter from local Administration ascertaining the heir

**Ethical Considerations**

**How This Product Upholds Ethical Investing**

 ZiiDi Shariah avoids industries and practices that are harmful or unethical, such as alcohol, gambling, and exploitative lending, in line with Shariah principles.

**Does this product support social responsibility**

 Yes, ZiiDi Shariah promotes ethical and socially responsible investments, contributing to sustainable development and community welfare.

**FWA ON PARTNER APP**

**Definition**

Fixed Wireless Access is an Internet Solution designed to offer connectivity to premises (Home or Business).

**How to activate a customers FWA router** 
A customer will be required to provide an active Safaricom number accompanied by their national/Maisha ID. To activate a router, the agent will:

Log in to the Partner app.

Tap on Fixed Wireless Activation

Click on ‘New Activation’

Select the plan (4G/5G)

Follow the prompts and submit.

After activation, the customer will receive a successful activation message on their phone number. The agent will also receive a pop-up success message on the app.

**How to view the activations done on the Partner App** 
To view the FWA activations done, the agent will tap on the FWA activations tab where they will see the details of the routers activated.

**How to purchase the Router Bundles**

A customer will be prompted to pay via M-PESA after selecting their preferred bundles on the Partner App. 
The customer can also opt to buy bundles via the USSD code \*400#

**Details displayed on the FWA reports page**

Name of the customer

The 4G/5G Package Plan

The router number (Router MSISDN)

The status of the activation (Invalid/Success)

**Difference between routers ‘With SIM Card’ and those ‘Without SIM Card’**

Routers with sim cards come with a sim inserted in the device while a router without a sim card, will require a DSA serial to be attached during the activation process.

**How to access ‘Fixed Wireless Access’ tab.** 
To be able to see the FWA tab, one needs to have one of the below roles:

Dealer Shop Agent

Direct Sales Agent

Franchise

Van Team Lead

**If one has the above roles and still can’t see the FWA tab,** they should reach out to their respective TDR and share the below details: -

Name

Log in number.

Role on the app

Dealer name

If currently not on Partner App, one will need to be onboarded on the app as per the existing guidelines. Kindly reach out to your respective TDR and request to be onboarded. Ensure you have your original National/Maisha ID.

**How to resolve faulty router issues** 
When a customer presents a faulty router the agent will troubleshoot and then based on the findings, advise the customer accordingly.

**Troubleshooting guide:**

Troubleshooting will involve checking if the SIM card is in the device SIM slot and that it is inserted correctly.

The agent will also ensure the SIM card is the one that came paired to the device or the one that was mapped to the device during purchase/activation.

The agent will ensure the SIM card is not damaged and is in active status.

The agent will confirm the CI number has an active bundle.

The agent will ensure the router is not damaged. If the router is still not working, the agent will proceed to swap the router as per the existing guidelines.

**Router Swap Guide**

For faulty routers, the customer will be referred to the retail shops for router swap to be done. 

Routers will be swapped with the un-kitted router type.

The customer will then remove the sim card from the faulty router and insert it in the new router.

This will ensure smooth transition and a quick turn around time.

Once the SIM card is inserted the agent will switch the router on and request the customer to reset their WI-FI name and password.

Should you receive any queries on the above frozen accounts, please advise the merchants accordingly. For re-activation requests, please **raise SR** as per below categories.

**NOTE:** Any reversals touching on these codes you can un-tag, initiate and tag back again. Merchant calling for till to be activated should call from the nominated number

# **Partner Support - Dealer Commissions**

**MPESA Commission Issues**

- M-PESA Agents earn commission from transactions done through the till. These transactions include customer deposits, customer withdrawals, Bamba airtime transaction and M-PESA customer registrations.
- The Commissions accumulates in the till commission account after every transaction and rolls up to the head office for payment at the end of the month.
- Commission tariff attached.

**Failed commission roll up**

- Escalation for failed commission roll up received on line 300 should be sent on email to M-PESA finance team for resolution. Email address [m-pesafinance@Safaricom.co.ke](mailto:m-pesafinance@Safaricom.co.ke)  **SLA 24hrs.**

 **M-PESA Commission claw back**

- Commission claw back is done when agent engages in irregular /fraudulent transactions to earn more commission. These irregular activities include split deposits & arbitrage transactions.
- Split deposits – this is where M-PESA Agent split deposit amount into several transactions to earn more commissions
- Arbitrage deposit transactions – this is where M-PESA agent circulates funds from M-PESA to bank through customer deposits and mobile banking transactions to earn more commissions.
- To appeal commission claw back or request for claw back statements M-PESA agent head office should raise a service request on dealer portal.
- To raise the request M-PESA head office will login to dealer portal and select below category

- Service request category: fraud escalations
- Request type: arbitrage
- Request Item: select the relevant request item from dealer portal dropdown that will appear

- The SLA for Arbitrage service request is 14days.
- Follow-up on Arbitrage request past SLA through line 300, the SR raised by the M-PESA agent head office should be sent to fraud team via email to [M-pesafraud@safaricom.co.ke](mailto:M-pesafraud@safaricom.co.ke)

# **Simex Commission (SIM Swap commissions)**

- Dealers and M-PESA head office purchase SIMEX (replacement SIM cards) through ordering on dealer portal. SIMEX are normally used to replace lost or damaged customer and agent SIM cards.
- Sim swap Commissions are earned once the SIMEX has been used to replace a customer/agent line.
- Commission statements for sim swaps done in a given period of time are normally available and downloaded on dealer portal.
- To access the statements agent will login to dealer portal and select reports.
- Then select Daily sim swap commissions.
- Specify the period by selecting the end date.
- then click on pull to view and download the report.
- Agent unable to access Sim swap commissions statements– escalation should be sent via email to dealer portal technical support team.

# **Sim Swap Commission Invoicing**

- Sim swap commission invoicing is done on I-SUPPLIER
- I-SUPPLIER link [https://shub.safaricom.co.ke/](https://shub.safaricom.co.ke/)
- Dealer will login on I-SUPPLIER and select invoices section.
- Click on create invoices then click on “GO” button.
- On the page that will appear; under organization field, enter the word Safaricom and click on “GO”
- All the simex commission PO available for payment will populate.
- Select the one to be paid the click on next.
- Enter invoice number, invoice description, and attach a copy of the invoice.
- Click on next button and submit. A confirmation message will then be received.

**Delayed Sim swap Commission Payment**

Safaricom partner support staff should confirm the communicated invoicing & payment dates from Dealer Management – e.g., 10th and 25th of every month. The dealer/ agent needs to have invoiced on the date specified by Dealer Management during the invoicing cycle.

- Safaricom partner support staff should confirm with the agent calling that invoicing was done.
- Then escalate delayed payment to Finance team, Accounts Payable via email on [AccountsPayable2@Safaricom.co.ke](mailto:AccountsPayable2@Safaricom.co.ke)

# **Airtime,Line & Simswap Commissions for Dealers & Retailers**

M﻿\-PESA agents are paid 5% commission from selling airtime over the counter i.e., through M-PESA from their Float account

A dealer is a Safaricom Authorized Distributor whereas a retailer is a reseller who is normally supplied with products from Safaricom by the dealer.

articleTitle: Upholding Integrity – Addressing Fraud in Retail Operations
markdownContent:
**Upholding Integrity – Addressing Fraud in Retail Operations**

Year to date, we have identified multiple instances of fraudulent activities within our retail operations. These include:

**Unauthorized use of SIM replacement (SIMEX) cards** by retail staff, acquired from external dealers for personal financial gain.

**Failure to adhere to established processes and guidelines**, leading to conflicts of interest and financial risk to the company.

Retail staff have been found purchasing and selling unauthorized SIM replacement cards sourced from dealer shops and brand ambassadors. This practice not only violates company policies but also constitutes fraud.

Some employees have either acted negligently or have been complicit in these activities, posing a significant risk to our business and impacting profitability.

**Consequences of Fraudulent Activities**

As part of our commitment to ethical business practices, employees found engaging in fraud face serious consequences, including:

**Disciplinary Action**

- Immediate disciplinary measures, including suspension or termination.
- **YTD, 32 employees have been terminated following HR investigations.**

**Criminal Charges**

- Fraudulent activities can result in criminal prosecution, fines, or imprisonment.
- **YTD, 8 former employees have been apprehended and are facing court proceedings.**

**Civil Penalties**

- Individuals may be held personally liable for financial losses incurred by the company or its clients.

**Maintaining Integrity & Reporting Misconduct**

Safaricom remains committed to upholding the highest standards of integrity. We urge all employees to remain vigilant and report any fraudulent activities. Adhering to company policies and procedures is crucial. If unsure, escalate concerns to your direct manager or:

- **Corporate Security Team:**

- Emmanuel Ndibo (Head of Ethics and Compliance)
- Eric Mugo (Chapter Lead, Fraud Operations)

- **Anonymous Reporting Channels:**

- Ethics Hotline: [**safaricom@ethics-line.com**](mailto:safaricom@ethics-line.com), **0800720009**
- Internal Ethics Helpline: [**integrity@Safaricom.co.ke**](mailto:integrity@Safaricom.co.ke)

By acting with integrity and accountability, we protect our business, customers, and reputation. Let’s continue to foster a culture of trust and ethical conduct.

**Do the right thing.**

**Sending Blasts On CRQs**

Sending blast for CRQs is the process of notifying clients on some emergency or planned work that has been scheduled.

**For emergency CRQ**

1. The Fixed network solutions team will send request to the FTTH folder team for specified customers to be notified. An emergency CRQ will be carried out within a short period of time after customers are notified.
2. CEE will confirm the mentioned ports are existing on U2000 or Nokia AMS system.
3. The CEE will use the OWS system to send to send notification as per email from Fixed Network Solutions Team
4. Whenever OWS system is unavailable Line 400 CEE will extract customers contacts from U2000 or Nokia AMS system and send SMS blast using L400 SMS tool to the clients who will be affected, clearly specifying the exact day and period that clients will be disconnected.
5. Line 400 team will respond back to the fixed network solutions team on email, confirming SMS notifications were sent to the intended customers and attach a list of clients’ contact numbers.
6. At the start of the CRQ, Line 400 folder team will award 5GB Wema bundles to clients who have active subscriptions if OWS system fails to award bundles.
7. OWS systems will update clients via SMS after the CRQ is complete to confirm restoration of services.

**For Planned CRQ**

1. The Fixed network solutions team will send request to the FTTH folder team for specified customers to be notified. Customers are notified 48 hours before the start of a CRQ.
2. CEE will confirm the mentioned ports are existing on U2000 or Nokia AMS system.
3. The CEE will use the OWS system to send to send notification as per email from Fixed Network Solutions Team
4. Whenever OWS system is unavailable Line 400 CEE will extract customers contacts from U2000 or Nokia AMS system and send SMS blast using L400 SMS tool to the clients who will be affected, clearly specifying the exact day and period that clients will be disconnected.
5. Line 400 team will respond back to the fixed network solutions team on email, confirming SMS notifications were sent to the intended customers and attach a list of clients’ contact numbers.
6. At the start of the CRQ, Line 400 folder team will award 5GB Wema bundles to clients who have active subscriptions if OWS system fails to award.
7. OWS system will update clients after the CRQ is complete to confirm restoration of services.

6. L400 CEE will receive customer request and will confirm account payment status on CRM Siebel.
7. Where account status is noted as rental suspend, CEE will advise customer accordingly and request customer to make applicable payment. Where account status on Siebel CRM is normal, CEE will confirm link is up and connected on U2000 system.
8. Where loss of service is noted; CEE will confirm if the same is an isolated case or a global outage / affecting many customers. Where an isolated case is noted, CEE will raise a work order to the respective contractor or incidence on BMC if work order portal is having an issue.
9. CEE will use the format when an incident is raised on BMC, CI -i.e., 11100000 | Reporting Contact number | alternative number | customer names | Estate | OLT | Kindly plan to attend and clear LOS.
10. L400 CEE will apply the 5GB data bundle compensation process.
11. Central dispatch will engage the customer within 2 Hrs, and will schedule for resolution within 24 Hrs.
12. Contractor will visit site for troubleshooting and resolution and will advise customer, confirm service up time close ticket.
13. Where issue is noted as affecting multiple users Multiple LOS/ global outage, CEE will advise the folder lead on duty. The folder lead will alert the SOC team to assist raise an incident if OWS Tool did not pick.
14. Folder lead in liaison with the SOC team, will send notification via SMS and award 5GB Wema bundles to the affected customers where OWS will not have sent the notifications and awarded bundles. The home retention team for will track the downtimes for further compensation to be done.
15. SOC team will raise an incident to the contractor who will visit site for troubleshooting and resolution. Contractor will update SOC, accordingly, confirm service up time and close ticket.
16. SOC team will receive a resolution and will alert stakeholders. i.e., COPS L400 team, all customer engagement touch points, home retention and home tech dispatch via email and/ or call as suitable.
17. Folder lead will send notification on resolution via SMS to the affected customer where OWS fails to send such notifications.
18. Where a customer calls after LOS has been resolved and the issue requires manual reprovisioning, the CEE will raise SR to Fixed Customer Support to provision under: Category: FTTH, TYPE: Manual Provisioning ITEM: LOS Cleared
