articleTitle: Individual Advantage and Corporate Advantage Tariff and Mechanics
markdownContent:
# **INDIVIDUAL** **ADVANTAGE TARIFF.**

This is a tariff for individual customers.

The registration can only be done at a Safaricom Shop.

It is categorized into.

- Advantage Hybrid Tariff.
- Advantage Tariff.

They are further categorized into different accounts depending on billing process.

For individual account they are under **Standard Account.**

# **REQUIREMENTS FOR ONBOARDING.**

Fill the individual advantage forms and attach.

- Copy of ID/ Passport/ Alien ID or Certificate.
- Copy of PIN Certificate.

- Two referees (individuals).
- Deposit (depending on nature of contract or equivalent to the credit limit being set min Ksh.2000).
- Email addresses, Postal Address and Physical address.
- Bank Details:

Name of the bank

Branch

Account number

# **BILLING**

- Different accounts can be billed differently depending on credit limits.
- Some accounts have active credit limits while others have no active credit limits.
- A customer can choose to have the account with **No Active Credit Limit** or have **Active Credit Limit.**
- With **No Active Credit Limit** The accounts do not have a limit and the system does not bar the line.
- With Active Credit Limits, the accounts have a credit limit and system automatically bars the line once it hits the limit set. They include.

Individual Autobar

Express Autobar.

# **Individual Autobar service.**

- This is a service where a certain amount is set as the limit on the usage for a customer’s line.
- Once the customer hits the limit, the line is automatically barred from making outgoing calls/SMS/data.
- This enables the customer to control their usage.
- The customer will indicate the desired/projected monthly usage, and this will be used as a benchmark for the credit limit.
- The customer needs to make full payment in full for the billed and unbilled amount to allow more usage.

# **Express Autobar.**

- This is a service where the customers set limit on the usage is equivalent to the deposit made.
- The customer will make a deposit that will be used as the credit limit.
- Once the customer hits the limit the line is automatically barred, and the customer can make any payment to allow more usage.

# **Billing cycle for Individual Autobar and Express Autobar.**

- Bill run on the 1st of every month
- Balance SMS notification – 2nd of every month to alert customers on the previous month bill.
- 1st, 2nd & final email reminder letter – sent out 2nd week of every month
- 1st SMS reminder – Sent out on 15th of every month – to remind customers that 16th is the due date of the outstanding bill for previous month
- 2nd SMS reminder - Sent out on 22nd of every month – to reminder customers the due date was on 16th
- Deactivation notice – Sent out on 4th week of every month - for customers with more than three outstanding bills.
- 3rd SMS reminder – Sent out on 29th of every month
- 27th / 28th of the month – **Soft bar** the customers who have not paid their bills for the previous month
- 4th / 5th of the following month – **Full bar** the customers who have not paid their bill for the previous month

**NB**: These dates are subject to change, especially when they fall on weekend/public holidays. However, such changes are normally communicated to stakeholders internally.

# **Customer support on the Autobar Service.**

- Sending Threshold SMS reminders: SMS reminders are generated and sent upon specified thresholds i.e.-when you have spent 75% and 90% of your current limit.
- Customer Care service for 24 hours on Line 200.
- Account payment slip for current bills and E-bill service for previous invoices 
 Safaricom Shops and Care Desks.
- To know the limit the customer can call 200, check on the Safaricom App or send a request to advantage@safaricom.co.ke.

# **How to Increase or decrease Credit Limit for Autobar and/or Hybrid Accounts.**

**Express Auto bar and Hybrid Accounts:**

- For postpay DIY and karibu postpay. Customer needs to increase limit via \*200# and selects change limit. For postpay DIY, the limit should be equal or more than the plan cost. To change plan for postpay DIY, customer dials \*200# and selects buy or change plan to activate the plan of their choice
- To downgrade, the customer dials \*200# and selects change limit. They can only downgrade to a minimum of ksh 1000. To downgrade to a limit lower than ksh 1000, customer writes an email request to advantage@safaricom.co.ke
- **To increase** for the other customers, they need to visit the shop to do an additional deposit and have the credit limit increased.

#  **Individual Auto bar Accounts:**

- The customer to submit a written request for the adjustment.
- The customer needs to have been on the Postpaid service for at least three months before the limit can be increased, this is subject to credit control's approval.
- Customer does a written request and tops up the deposit with an amount directly proportional to the requested credit limit.
- **To decrease, the Customer** does a written request and brings to the Retail Shops or sends on email to advantage@safaricom.co.ke , indicating the desired Limit amount.

**NB:**

 **1.(a)If the customer insists, they are not able to follow the due process due to unavoidable circumstances.**

- CEE to confirm if customer has a hybrid account. If they do, advise them to top up in the meantime then follow the credit limit increase process.
- If customer has no hybrid account, CEE to Send an email to Line200 TM Escalations Line2002@Safaricom.co.ke and copy CC Postpay TLs CCPostpayTLs@Safaricom.co.ke for the TL to do follow up with credit team for guidance.
-  CEE to inform customer that their request has been forwarded for consideration and they will be called back with a response.
- If it is past 8PM on a Weekend, CEEs on Line 200 folder can still call the Post-pay TL who was on duty to handle the issue.
- All parties will enter interactions clearly indicating action taken and response given. Include any emails as attachments where needed.

 **(b)For Corporate Accounts under Z Account insisting they are not in a position to follow the due process due to unavoidable circumstances.**

- Confirm if they have a hybrid account, if yes advise them to top up in the meantime, then follow the credit limit increase process.
- If it does not have a hybrid account and is an individual account, follow the procedure in (a) above.
- If it’s a corporate account under a company, follow the procedure in (a) above.

**A repeat caller on credit limit increase request**

CEE to Send mail to Line200 TM Escalations Line2002@Safaricom.co.ke and copy CC Post-pay TLs CCPostpayTLs@Safaricom.co.ke for the TL to do follow up with credit team for them to guide on the issue.

If it is past 8PM on a Weekend, CEEs on Line 200 folder can still call the Post-pay TL who was on duty to handle the issue.

All parties will enter interactions clearly indicating action taken and response given. Include any emails as attachments where needed.

# **CORPORATE ADVANTAGE TARIFF.**

This is a tariff for corporate customers.

The registration can only be done at a Safaricom Shop.

It is categorized into.

- Corporate Advantage Hybrid Tariff.
- Corporate Advantage Tariff.

They are further categorized into different accounts depending on billing process.

For corporate account they are under **Aggregated Account.**

# **REQUIREMENTS** **FOR ONBOARDING.**

- Fill in the Corporate Advantage Forms.
- Copy of Certificate of Registration.
- Copy of PIN Certificate (New generation Cert Combined: PIN and VAT Certificate).
- Bank Statements (where applicable).
- Bank Details.

Name of the bank.

Branch

Account number.

- Letter of Undertaking for Government.
- VAT Exemption Certificate (where applicable).
- Bank Statements (where applicable).
- Application form should be signed by the contact person and should bear the company rubber stamp.
- Two referees who must be companies that offer the company credit facilities or are suppliers. Referees must not be sister companies or individuals or their creditors.
- Deposit (depending on nature of contract or equivalent to the credit limit being set **min Ksh.2000).**

# **BILLING.**

- Different accounts can be billed differently depending on credit limits.
- Some accounts have active credit limits while others have no active credit limits.
- An organization can choose to have the account with **No Active Credit Limit** or have **Active Credit Limit.**
- **Corporate Auto bar** is the account that have **Active Credit Limits** under **Corporate Tariff**.
- The accounts have a credit limit and system automatically bars the line once it hits the limit set.
- With **No Active Credit Limit** The accounts does not have a limit and the system does not bar the line. They include.

VIP Corporate.

Corporate.

Government.

Small businesses.

E1

# **Billing cycle for Corporates and Corporate Auto bar Accounts.**

Monthly bill run as per bill cycle done on 1st of the month.

Bill includes Access fee for the following month

Due dates for bill payments is16th of every month.

On the 17th, an SMS is sent to the contact person for confirming receipt of bills.

On the 26th, we make a telephone call for follow up on the outstanding amount (Automatically output report of all customers not paid up) customer is advised via SMS on the outstanding bill that is due.

20 Days after due Date we'll send reminder SMS for outstanding accounts to the contact person.

25 days after due date and subscribers under corporate accounts with unpaid invoices are temporarily suspended (outgoing calls barred). Collection plan kicks in for all accounts with balances above collection plan entry level

Interest is charged on unpaid amount for the previous bill run i.e., collection plan interest fee should be 2% of outstanding amount over 10days after due dates.

26 days after due date1st reminder letter is automatically generated which are dispatched either by emails mail merge as an attachment for customers with email address or Posting mail merge for the customers without email address.

Emails-to-fax mail merge (email-to-Safaricom fax-to-customer fax) SMAP will send the relevant messages on the e-mail server. The e-mail server will take the appropriate action.

30 days after due date, bar Incoming Calls takes effect (Note, collection plan affects subscribers who have not settled invoices for the previous months only.)

2nd reminder letter – 35 days after due date (With similar delivery procedures as

3rd and final reminder letter – 45 days after due date.

# **Billing cycle for VIP Corporate Accounts.**

Monthly bill run as per bill cycle currently 1st of the month.

Bill includes Access fee for the following month (cycle forward fee-billed but unearned amounts) and any prorate for the current month in case connection took place within previous bill cycle and usage for the month.

Due date is 16 Days after Bill Run.

Any suspension is based on management's decision, and it is a manual process

# **Billing cycle for small business and Government accounts.**

Monthly bill run as per bill cycle is done on 1st of the month.

Bills includes Access fee for the following month.

Due dates for bills payment is16th of every month.

On the 17th, an SMS is sent to the contact person for confirming receipt of bills.

On 24th, a 2nd SMS reminder is sent and an email in a defined format is sent to customers with email addresses.

15 Days after due date telephone call to customers for follow up on the outstanding amount is done (Automatically output report of all customers not paid up).

Collection plan kicks in for all accounts with balances above collection plan entry level on 6th of the following month. Subscribers under corporate accounts with unpaid invoices are temporarily suspended (outgoing calls barred).

Interest is charged on unpaid amount for the previous bill run i.e. collection plan interest fee should be 2% of outstanding over 10days after due dates.

1st reminder letter is sent on the 11th. They are automatically generated letters which are dispatched either by emails mail merge as an attachment for customers with email address or Posting mail merge for the customers without email address.

Emails-to-fax mail merge (email-to-Safaricom fax-to-customer fax) SMAP will send the relevant messages on the e-mail server. The e-mail server will take the appropriate action

On 13th, Incoming Calls are also barred (Note, collection plan affects subscribers who have not settled invoices due for previous months).

2nd reminder letter – 35 days after due date (With similar delivery procedures as

3rd and final reminder letter – 40 days after due date.

Use of the bundle resources will not be available to users who are roaming. Prevailing out of bundle charges is applicable for Roaming usage.

The bundled SMS, data and minutes on the Corporate Prepaid plans will not be used to access premium rated services.

# **Definition:**

Corporate Value Packs(CVP) are a range of data bundles that give an Enterprise customer ﬂexibility to purchase data based on their requirements.

# **Eligibility:**

All customers (new & existing) will automatically enjoy the **New** CVP Data plans.

For the existing customers, the auto-renewal on the **1st of January 2025** & going forward will be on the **new** CVP data plans.

**New Changes:**

The CVP 80GB bundle and the CVP 100GB bundle have been assimilated to one. i.e to: CVP Data 100GB priced at 5,000/=

The onboarding, service activation and billing process does not change.

# **Who is it targeted at****:**

The 100GB bundle is tailored for high-data usage and ensures that your teams within the organizations remain connected and productive. The bundle is especially ideal for secondary devices such as MiFis, dongles or tablets.

# **Onboarding:**

To purchase the CVP plans, the Enterprise customer will ﬁll in the CVP Application form and submit it to their relationship manager for internal activation of the service.

The service will be active in 2 working days.

# **Onboarding Requirements:**

# A potential Enterprise customer needs to provide:

· The list of mobile numbers and the corresponding CVP data plans to be added.

· Normal KYC requirements accompanying the application form.

**Validity:**

The CVP Data resources(plans) will expire at the end of each month with **NO Roll Over of unused resources**.

The product will auto renew every 1st of the month and all numbers on the CVP Data plans will be loaded full resources for the month unless customer has requested for termination in writing or instructions from credit control to terminate have been issued due to unpaid bills.

**Upgrade/Downgrade and Change of Plan**

CVP data bundle users will be able to upgrade and downgrade their bundles by making a formal request in writing to their relationship Manager.

The prorate charge will apply.

**Deposits and Credit Limit**

Payment of deposits by enterprises joining the plans will be subject to Credit Control approval. Deposit exempt customers will not pay deposit.

The customer can opt to either have a credit limit/allowance or not have one.

**Billing** **& Bill payment**

The Enterprise customer will be billed at the end of the month for all employee numbers under their account.

The bill will be sent to the registered email address by the 5th of each month.

The previous months bills is due for payment by the 16th of the next month.

Customers who do not pay their bills by then will be disconnected until full payment is done.

All charges payable are inclusive of VAT and excise tax but remain subject to other applicable levies and taxes at the then prevailing rates including applicable variations to VAT and excise tax.

Customers can pay via EFT/bank transfer or Mpesa.

**Priority of usage for CVP data when having other data bundles**

Priority in usage will be given in the following order:

Priority 1- Bundle with the shortest validity e.g daily, weekly etc.

Priority 2- 30-day Postpay bundle e.g CVP Data.

Priority 3- Bundle bought earlier e.g a bundle bought on 29/11/2024 will be consumed first before another bundle bought on 05/12/2024.

**Will the Enterprise customer earn Bonga Points?**

The end user that gets the CVP Data bundle will be awarded Bonga Points equivalent to the value of the bundle upon bundle purchase and as per prevailing Bonga conversion rates.

Note: To earn the Bonga points, the customer must have enrolled prior via \*126#.

**Usage notiﬁcations**

End users will receive an SMS prior to exhaustion of their resources.

**Balance check**

To check balance, customers will dial: \*200#, select ʻ ʻMy Accountʼ then CVP Data Bundles balanceʼ option.

By dialing \*200#, selecting ʻMy Accountʼ then CVP Data Bundles balanceʼ option.

**Other Features:**

You cannot sambaza CVP bundles.

You cannot roam with CVP data bundles.

**Call Hunting Definition and Mechanics**

# **Definition**

Call hunting is a value-added service layered to either toll free or fixed voice services i.e. SIP/E1

Call hunting is a service designed to allow corporate customers who have multiple phone lines to provide/advertise a single number (the Presentation Number) behind which will be a group of lines (Ring-To-Numbers).

The Presentation Number will automatically transfer all incoming calls to an available line.

# **Applying for Calling Hunting service**

Formal application for call hunting lines or features for existing pilot lines is required and request is done at Retail.

a technical scoping is done by a presales or solutions architect together with the sales professional to qualify what the customer needs and validate their current investments i.e. equipment they already have e.g. PABX, Desk phones, building being fibre ready and how they would want the calls to flow (hunted).

Below is a summary of what is needed for a customer to onboard:

Application Form (Corporate Voice)

Technical qualification template

KYC (for new customer)

Order to cash team will raise an order that configures on CBS (call hunting).

**NOTE:**

·       Existing pilot lines will be migrated free for first time migration.

·       The normal Post-pay application and credit approval procedure will apply.

·       All other Post-pay and Prepay business rules apply.

# **Presentation Number in Call Hunting**

This is the number provided and advertised by a corporate through which calls are transferred to other numbers (Ring-to-Numbers).

# **Replacement of Presentation Number**

Presentation Number in Call Hunting cannot be replaced. This is because the class of services is not available for SIM Replacement.

# **Presentation Number Sim Card**

**For a new acquisition:** the Presentation Number (PN) will not be a physical SIM but an MSISDN configured on the Safaricom IN.

**For existing numbers****:** an exchange solution will be offered in which Safaricom will offer 2 lines in exchange of physical SIM cards (One will be configured as PN in IN so the physical SIM will be destroyed. The other will be offered as physical SIM to the corporate to have it put in their PABX system to allow outgoing calls. It can either be Post-pay or Prepay).

# **Declined services for Presentation Number**

The Call Hunting Presentation Number will not be able to originate calls or SMS to another number.

The Call Hunting Presentation Number will not be able to receive SMS, or access Premium Rate Services/VAS

# **Ring-to-Numbers**

These are multiple lines that a corporate may use to channel calls received by the Presentation Number while using the call hunting service.

# **Ring-to-Numbers of other Networks**

Call Hunting Ring-to-Numbers will be corporate post-paid Safaricom numbers only.

# **Busy Ring-to-Number**

When a ring-to number is busy when call hunting:

The system will be able to search for Ring-To-Number (RTN) status and ignore busy numbers.

The IN will be configured to allow a 20 second duration (seconds) for the Presentation Number (PN) to ring a specific Ring-to Number (RTN) before searching for the next available RTN in line.

The IN will be configured to manage either the Ring-To-Numbers into a priority list or allow for random hunting. The customers will be offered flexibility and option to choose.

Several Ring-to-Number (RTN) numbers will be able to be set to ring simultaneously or sequentially. The customers will be offered flexibility and the option to choose.

Voicemail, Call Waiting, and Hold features on both RTN and PN numbers will be barred.

The last number on the list will have an additional call forward to the Executive Voicemail service activated.

# **Maximum allowed Ring to Numbers per Presentation Number**

A maximum of 30 distinct and completely different Ring-to-Numbers are allowed per Presentation Number. However, application can be done if more is required.

# **Benefits of Call Hunting**

Corporate customers need not advertise numerous numbers for their organization. Only the Presentation Number will be advertised

Multiple Ring-To-Numbers can be set in the order the customer would like them to ring and can be added to as need arises.

Corporate customers can determine how many times each Ring-To-Numbers should ring before looking for the next available number.

Subscribers who ring the Presentation Number will be charged for the outbound call based on existing tariffs.

Safaricom would act as an exchange so that if the Presentation Number is dialed, the exchange will automatically hunt for a free number in the same group and the incoming call will land on an available number.

articleTitle: M-PESA API Definitions, Types and Mechanics
markdownContent:
# **Definition, Eligibility and Onboarding Requests**

# **Definition**

This is a new interface on G2 covering both disbursements (Business to Customers – B2C) and service payments (Customer to Business – C2B and Business to Business – B2B)

M-PESA released new API (Application Programming Interface) to enable developers to access M-PESA services.

API stands for Application Programming Interface.

It is a set of programming tools used to build applications. APIs generally consist of a set of routines, protocols, and other tools generally used to get or update data. API‟s enables two systems to communicate with each other through access and integration of systems.

# **Safaricom API "Daraja:**

Safaricom API Portal dubbed “Daraja” is a self-service platform that provides developers access to our API suite. With Daraja, Safaricom endeavours to aid customers in their road to discovery through interesting and encouraging platforms that enable them to reach their potential. Daraja is open to both individuals and companies who are interested in accessing M-PESA APIs.

# **A sandbox environment**

This is a testing environment that will allow developers to create their test applications. Sandbox products are used to test APIs in the sandbox environment and is different from production products which are coupled to the M-PESA short code

# **Eligibility**

Daraja is open to both individuals and companies who are interested in accessing M-PESA APIs.

# **Target Audience**

**Integrators & developers:** They directly consume the API's

**Business owners:** They reconcile of all value that come into their businesses.

# **Onboarding/Integration requests**

Customers must have an LNM short code and advised as per the onboarding process in case they do not have a Paybill/buy goods short code.

Developer and partners can access Daraja by login to https://developer.safaricom.co.ke/, create an account, load the APP details, perform tests and load the app on production/integration

New developers will logon to the portal and create an account by registering their details to gain access to the sandbox environment;

Existing developers will log in to the portal using their login credentials.

# **Types of APIs (Application Programming Interface)**

C2B- Customer to Business Payments (Confirmation and Validation)

B2C- Business to Customer payments

B2B- Business to Business payments

Transaction query - Checking of transaction status and details

Account Balance- Checking of a Paybill organization’s account balance

Lipa Na M-PESA Online Payment API-for customer payments through applications that allows transaction completion through M-PESA PIN

Lipa Na M-PESA Online Query API - Checking of transaction query for the Lipa Na M-PESA Online.

# **Account Registration**

Requirements to register an account

The developer will require to provide the following details to create an account:

Developers Name

Primary contacts – email, company and phone

Country

Username

Email address.

Mobile contacts

# **Achievement for Safaricom API "Daraja**

Reduced turnaround time to complete integration from 60 days to 4 days. (from the time of request, onboarding and integration of API's)

Access to a central access point where developers/integrators can log into and explore (self-discovery) from the portal.

Improved customer experience Efficiency in the collection of payment.

# **Confirming Created Account**

Once the developer has successfully created their account on Daraja, he will receive an email confirmation from Safaricom Developer Portal team confirming that the account has been created.

A secure link will be provided for login and reset password.

Changing the e-mail address assigned to the Developer Portal account.

The developer cannot change the email address that was used to create the account.

Changing the password assigned to the Developer Portal account.

On first time login, the developer will be required to change password.

The developer will click on the user link which will redirect to the portal login page.

When a developer has forgotten the password, he will be able to reset from the portal using the “forgot password” option.

An email with a link to reset the password will be sent to the developer’s email address.

# **Sandbox Environment**

**Requirements to test in the Sandbox** **environment.**

The developer will require the following to enable him to test his application:

Test organization

Test MSISDN

Test data

Test scenarios

End points to the test environment

**Note:**

The Developer will get access to test an APP after creating an account on the Developer Portal.

Upon successful login to the Developer Portal, the developer can access the step-by-step guide on how to test an APP by clicking on the “Get Started” link.

# **Requirements to move from the Sandbox environment to Production**

To migrate to production, developers will require the following:

To upload the filled in test cases; and accept terms and conditions.

Production organization (M-PESA short codes on Production)

End points to Production

# **Perform API integration and sandbox tests**

On the sandbox environment developers will be able to:

Create their test applications.

Select the preferred API products for which you will want to use.

The developer will carry out tests for his APP and provide a status.

# **API Benefits**

**Integrators & Developers**

Simpler onboarding process

Less complex programming language

Documentation is available.

Available online support channels

A sandbox environment for testing

**Business Owners**

Improved customer experience. There is efficiency in the collection of payments.

Easier reconciliation of payments.

# **Payments Web Portal User Creation and Change Process**

This covers BE (Business Entity) Admin creation, change and update of missing KYC details.

Safaricom will only manage the BE admin and the respective Primary Operator will create the other users/roles within the BE/organization.

Web Access

All requests for M-PESA Business Payments Portal access via web must be accompanied by a request from an admin.

Safaricom will only create the BE (Business Entity) admin and the respective Primary Operator will create the other users/roles within the BE (Business Entity) /organization.

As part of the creation process, administrator user with admin role will be created by the Safaricom IT service desk. The creation teams will raise a BMC ticket to IT service desk for creation of the admin user.

The admins will be created on M-PESA Business Payments Portal to manage BE (Business Entity) accounts and to create and manage other users.

All the Operator KYC details must be captured on the portal and the requests must be accompanied by physical/scanned documents.

**Roles**

The portal will have a combination of 2 role type i.e. Static roles provided by Safaricom and static Permissions that an admin will use to create business friendly roles.

The BE (Business Entity) Admin role is static and thus is pre-defined by Safaricom. As a result, the admin will be able to create users:

Using a set of predefined static roles

Using self-created roles using a pre-defined set of static permissions.

The admin will only be able to create/edit/close other users. The other users will only be able to execute activities as per the current issued defined role/permissions.

# **Payments Portal Web Roles and Permissions**

These are permissions that will enable individuals/users to access, transact and interact with the portal via the various access channels.

**Permissions**

Are system defined privileges that will be assigned to a role to enable that role to perform certain operations.

**Roles**

One or a group of permissions that will enable a user to perform tasks i.e. Manage account, transact etc. on the portal. An organization will use the predefined roles, or a will use the permissions to create their own roles.

**User**

This an executor of a task as defined by the assigned role via USSD/Web/API. System users will be assigned roles to enable them to perform one or various tasks.

# **Business Admin Role**

This is a pre-defined role and cannot be modified. The BE admin will be able to:

Create other users within the BE

Assign and create/edit roles

Edit other users within the BE

Close other users within the BE

Unlock other users within the BE

Reset passwords for the other users within the BE

Change the KYC details of the other users within the BE

# **Other pre-defined roles**

Nominated number user – this is the nominated number which will access services via USSD.

Business Manager Role

B2B Manager Role

Business Operator Role

Auditor Role

# **Permissions**

Are system defined privileges that will be assigned to a role to enable that role to perform certain operations.

**B2B Product (Bank Account to Buy Goods/Paybill), KYC Documentation & B2B Reversals**

This service allows bank customers to access their Bank accounts without physical visits and:

Make direct payments to Buy Goods and Paybill.

Transfer cash from their bank accounts to other bank accounts.

The Transactions will be authorized by using the customer’s Mobile/App/Online banking PIN/Password via **USSD/App/online banking platform. For the service to work:**

The bank must integrate to M-PESA G2 via API to enable them to avail this service to their customers.

The customer must be registered to the bank service i.e. Must have access to respective mobile banking platforms.

Must have downloaded their respective banking Apps. or use USSD codes/online channels where applicable or use the M-Banking services accessible via Safaricom STK Menu under Safaricom+

**Example** of these services include: My Kash via KCB, Loop via CBA, Vuma by KCB, Whizz by HFC.

# **Key KYC Documentations and Where to find them**

CR12 documentations: Registrar of Companies - Sheria House or E-Citizen.

Business Permit/Certificate of Registration: Registrar of Companies/issued by respective counties /e-citizen.C

Certificate of Incorporation: Registrar of Companies -Sheria House/E-Citizen.

Resolution Letter Form: Safaricom website: [https://www.safaricom.co.ke](https://www.safaricom.co.ke/)

Application Forms and Terms and Condition Document: Safaricom Website: [https://www.safaricom.co.ke](https://www.safaricom.co.ke/)

Partnership Deed: Registrar of Companies - Sheria House/E-Citizen.

Partnership Affidavit: Partners Advocates.

Letter from NGO Board: Board Service Charter – NGO Coordination Board.

Company or Individual KRA PIN Certificate; Online: Kenya Revenue Authority website.

Sasra Letter: Sacco Societies Regulatory Authority (Sasra).

Safaricom AML / KYC Questionnaire Safaricom website: [https://www.safaricom.co.ke](https://www.safaricom.co.ke/)

Ministry of Education License: Ministry of Education.

Trustees Deed: Ministry of Lands.

# **B2B Reversals**

M-PESA Corporate and Partner Support Teams resolve B2B reversal request on e-mail or call receipt and should strive to provide first call resolution. Where unable to reverse, either due to inability to get reversal consent or due to insufficient funds, a service request will be raised as follows.

Kindly check the Wrong Store or Beneficiary Store on M-PESA Web prior to raising a Service Request. The Store type will determine the Category selected when raising the SR.

For B2B Reversals at M-PESA Agent Tills, raise the Service Request under:

Category: MPESA Services

Type: B2B Reversal Transaction

Item: At Agent Till

SLA: 72 hrs

- For B2B Reversals LIPA NA M-PESA Stores, raise the Service Request under:

Category: LNM B2B

Type: B2B Reversal Transaction

Item: At LNM Short Code

SLA: 72 hrs

# B2B Reversal Validity

There is no validity for B2B reversals as this are organizations.

When a request is done and the transaction has archived, an SR is raised for reversals team to follow up .

SR owner should raise  a BMC ticket for FSS team to provide transaction details, then follow up with the recipient.

Once consent is given, SR owner should liaise with Fintech operations to do journal entry.

Wh﻿en raising the service request, capture clear information about the customer issues raised and indicate all relevant information required by the support analyst to resolve customer issue and close the SR. Refer to Article A0251: Service Request (SR) definition and Features

articleTitle: Lipa na M-PESA Application - Bank Details
markdownContent:
# **LNM Bank Account**

**Optional Bank Account Requirement for Shortcode Applications**

Organizations and consumers applying for new LNM shortcodes are no longer required to submit bank account details as part of the application process. This change addresses challenges many organizations face in acquiring cancelled cheques or bank letters from their financial institutions, which often leads to delays or missed opportunities.

**Eligibility**

Any organization or customer applying for a new LNM shortcode can now apply without the need to provide bank account details during application.

**Withdrawing Funds Without Bank Account Details**

No, organizations that do not provide bank account details during the application process will be unable to transfer funds to their bank accounts. They will be required to update these details to withdraw funds to bank.

**Updating or Changing Bank Account Details for an Organization**

For Organizations with access to the M-PESA Business Portal:

The Business Administrator or Manager logs into the portal.

Navigate to the ‘Business Support’ menu and select the ‘New Bank Details’ option.

Choose the relevant shortcode and download the bank update form. If an organization already has an existing bank account linked to the shortcode, the ‘Change of Bank Details Form’ will be provided. If no bank account is currently linked, the ‘Update Bank Details Form’ will be presented instead.

Complete the form, ensuring it is signed and stamped by authorized signatories.

Upload the completed form along with the required KYC documentation (refer to Pg-2 of the form).

Submit the form for Safaricom verification and approval. The processing SLA is 72 hours.

For Organizations Without Access to the M-PESA Business Portal:

Print and complete the relevant form.

Submit the signed and stamped form to any Safaricom shop for verification, after which the details will be captured in the Service Management Suite tool. Alternatively, the completed documents can be emailed to [M-PESABusiness@Safaricom.co.ke](mailto:M-PESABusiness@Safaricom.co.ke) , where a Service Request (SR) will be raised for merchant support action.

**Requesting Deletion of an Existing Bank Account by an Organization**

No, once a bank account is linked to a shortcode, it cannot be deleted. However, if the account needs to be changed, organizations must follow the existing application process for updating bank details.

**Additional Documentation for Updating or Changing Bank Account Details**

Yes, additional documentation may be required. Please refer to Pg-2 of the attached forms for a detailed guide on the required KYC documentation, based on the organization's business category.

**NOTE:** Regulated entities such us International Money Transfer, Financial Institutions and Betting firms must provide bank details during applications.

**FIEH-0010: FTTH CBS Adjustments**

**FTTH CBS Discount with illustrations**

**Reasons for increments**

·       Customer charged connection fee erroneously.

·       Bulk payments by new customers activates the highest package.

·       Lack of proration after product is removed from the customer account.

·       Failed payment integration on CRM

·       POS Bulk payments (1 package at a time)

·       Winback offers for dormant customers.

·       Payment made to wrong account

·       Managers/Retention discretion as compensation for bad experience.

·       4G for Home browsing out of bundle.

·       4G for Home lines that have PRS

·       6+1 bulk reward offers

·       Deleted products

**Payment made to wrong account**

The CEE will delete the product on the wrong account and raise SR with details indicating wrong CI and the correct CI, amount prorated on IN data and MPESA transaction code.

The CEE will then raise a decrement activity and inform the customer of SLA.

The line 400 Team Leader will approve the decrement activity and the funds will be decremented from the wrong CI.

The CEE on the folder team will pick the SR and confirm that the funds have been decremented from the wrong account and confirm the MPESA transaction code has not been reversed on 150501.

The CEE on the folder team will raise a manual adjustment SR on the correct account indicating the amount to increment that was decremented from the wrong CI.

The line 400 Team Leader will approve the increment activity and the funds will be incremented on the correct CI.

The folder CEE will confirm that the account has been credited, customer will be contacted, and both SRs will be closed.

Captures customer key information, profile, products, and interactions.

Synchronize customer data on different channels and thus view a customer from all channel interaction points.

Omnichannel – customer to have same experience regardless of the channel used.

Click on **Manage Postpay**.

Validate ownership using your M-PESA or Service PIN.

**Via EMAIL**

Customer will send the request on email to ***[advantage@safaricom.co.ke](mailto:advantage@safaricom.co.ke)***, indicating the account number and invoice date required.

# **SAFARICOM POSTPAY BILL PAYMENT/PAYMENT POINTS.**

There are several ways and points to pay for the PostPay bills and these are:

Via M-PESA

Safaricom retail centers- Cash or Cheque.

Over the counter at Standard Chartered Bank (SCB) and National Commercial Bank of Africa (NCBA). While paying at the bank, give the complete account number.

Over the counter and ATM Co-op bank.

Pesa point ATM payment.

Direct debit and credit card payment.

Directly from bank via Paybill 200200.

Customer can pay for another number by dialing \*430# (pilot)/\*200# and select Pay for another number.

**Postpay Payment Via M-PESA.**

**Via My Safaricom APP**

Launch My Safaricom APP.

Click on **Manage Postpay**.

Click on **Pay Bill**.

Confirm whether for **My Account** or **Other Number**.

Confirm whether paying **Full Amount** Outstanding or choose to **Enter Amount** preferred.

Confirm payment details and **Click Pay**.

Enter **M-PESA PIN** to compete the transaction.

**Via STK and M-PESA APP**

Go to M-PESA account and select Lipa na M-PESA.

Enter business no. as 200200.

Enter the account number (use either your account no. or Phone number).

Enter the amount.

Enter MPESA PIN.

Confirm details and select ok.

**Note**

For account number, enter either the **Account Number or Phone Number,** ensuring you use the number **including the zero** E.g., 0721123456 and the **account number must be complete** including the hyphen (-). E.g., 1-6897587909.

# **Bank Payment for Postpay Bills.**

Customers can make payment for their PostPay bills at the following banks.

Co-operative Bank.

# **Debit and Credit Card Payment**

Credit/Debit card payments are done to clear outstanding bills only. In case a customer wants to clear a current bill, the request must be made in writing for the card to be run.

To use direct debit and credit card as a means of payment.

Customer needs to fill the attached debit/credit card subscription application form.

Attach a copy of the ID and a copy of the **FRONT SIDE** of the debit/credit card.

Send it via email to ***[creditcardsupdates@Safaricom.co.ke](mailto:creditcardsupdates@Safaricom.co.ke)*** only. (The customer will scan and send the details by themselves).

The debit/credit cards are run by the 5th of every month.

Where the cards fail to run, the customer will receive a text message: "Dear Customer. Your Safaricom credit card payment of Ksh. XXXXXX has been declined by the bank. Please contact your Card Centre for more details. Safaricom".

Where the card has expired, the customer will receive a text message in the below format and they will be expected to fill in a new form and share the details as per the card subscription process. 
**"Your credit** card details registered for paying your Safaricom bill have expired. Please update your Card details with us. Safaricom."

**Definition**

MALI is an investment product that allows M-PESA customers to invest in Unit Trusts, for as low as KSH 100 and earn daily interest.

**Benefits**

The wealth management tool will give a return of 10% interest annually and the government charges 15% withholding tax on investment income.

Customers deposits into the MALI Paybill account will be free. All management and professional fees are charged to the fund, not the customer.

**NOTE:** This service is still on pilot to Safaricom Staff and selected Customers. We shall update once launched and availed to all customers.

**How To Register**

·       To register, customers must have been registered on M-PESA for over 3 months.

·       Customer must accept the Terms and Conditions.

·       One must not have done a sim replacement in the last 3 days (72hrs).

·       Must have an active M-PESA account, i.e., the customer must be registered on M-PESA with active status.

·       Number should not be in a prison site.

**How to Opt In**

·       Dial \*334#

·       Select Financial services.

·       Select MALI

·       Select Accept the T&Cs

·       Enter your M-PESA PIN

·       You will receive a message for your successful opt-in.

**How to Opt Out**

·       Dial \*334#

·       Select Financial services.

·       Select MALI

·       Select My Account

·       Select Close Account

·       Enter M-PESA PIN and follow the prompts to opt-out.

**How It Works**

·       The customer must have opted in an investment product they intended to invest in

·       Customer’s M-PESA account must not be in frozen/suspended status.

·       Customer must have sufficient M-PESA balance to successful pay for the investment product.

·       The minimum investment amount is kshs.100/-

·       The maximum investment amount per single transaction will be in line with the current M-PESA transaction limit rules. \[Maximum hold on the M-PESA wallet is Ksh 500,000 and maximum single transfer amount of Ksh 250,000.

·       The customer must have enrolled and invested in an investment product they intended withdraw from.

·       Withdrawal will be at the prevailing daily yield as at the C.O.B i.e., 1800 hours.

·       Withdrawals done between 0000 hours and 1800 hours the previous days’ yield will be available. Example Tuesday withdrawal at 0700 Hours will be awarded Monday’s yield.

·       Withdrawals done between 1801 hours and 2359 Hours that day’s yield will be available. Example, Tuesday withdrawal at 1900 Hours will be awarded that day’s yield.

·       Customers will withdraw on demand and access funds instantly.

·       All transactions to and from the M-PESA wallet will be as per the current M-PESA limits rules \[Maximum hold on the M-PESA wallet is Ksh.500,000 and maximum single transfer amount of Ksh.250,000)

·       SIM Swap must not have been done in the last 24 hours (For both new and registered customers)

·       The minimum amount you can withdraw is Kshs.10 and the minimum amount to Invest is Kshs.100

·       The current M-PESA transaction limits will apply to all MALI Transactions. The daily transaction limit is Ksh.500,000 and per transaction is Ksh.250,000.

·       The customer must have enrolled and/or invested in an investment product they intended opt out from

·       For customer to opt out, balance check on the product category will be confirmed to ensure withdrawal of funds before termination of products.

·       Customer must accept/confirm withdrawal of funds from an investment product before opting out.

·       All transactions to and from the M-PESA wallet will be as per the current M-PESA limits rules, \[Maximum hold on the M-PESA wallet is Ksh 500,000 and maximum single transfer amount of Ksh 250,000

·       Investments earn a daily interest rate, which is added to the principal amount. Any interest earned is subject to withholding taxes, before the customer can be paid.

·       The wealth management tool will give a return of 10% interest annually and the government charges 15% withholding tax on investment income.

·       The interest rate is 10% per annum and the government charges 15% withholding tax on investment income.

**NOTE:** 

Interest paid is Compound interest calculated per annum (per year) and paid daily’.

Customers will be able to access their funds **24hrs** after sim swap.

Mali is regulated under the capital markets and below is the investment structure.

**Investment structure**

·       Lines with existing MALI Investment product will be recycled as per the current MSISDN lifecycle management process and the list shared with the Partner (Genghis Capital) for delinking of the MSISDN from the Investment product fund on their end.

·       Unit trust funds for all clients are always reinvested collectively and therefore a unit trust client’s investment account cannot be debited (or have idle funds) unless the clients issue instructions to do so for payment/redemption purposes.

You can access this service via M-PESA App and USSD

6. **How to access the SurePay HELB Mini App in the M-PESA Super APP**

- Be registered M-PESA customers with a smartphone.

- Download the M-PESA Super APP from the Google App Plays store or Apple App Store or Huawei App Gallery.

- Have mobile data on your device for the first time download and sign in. This ensures secure login during the first-time download.

Note: ***Subsequent sign-in attempts can be made over a WIFI connection.***

- Accept the terms and conditions of the M-PESA Super App.

- Enter a valid M-PESA PIN for authentication.

- Allow M-PESA to access your biometrics (Face recognition / Fingerprint).

- Once successfully logged in to the M-PESA Super App, navigate to the services tab and search/scroll to the SurePay HELB App icon.

7. **Who can access SurePay HELB Mini-App**

M-PESA registered individuals who have access to or own a smartphone and have installed the

M-PESA Super APP

To withdraw your upkeep

**M-PESA App**

- Select the SurePay HELB mini app on the services tab.

- Enter Amount

- Confirm the details.

- Enter your M-PESA PIN

**USSD**

- Select Withdraw Funds

- Enter the Amount

- Enter your valid/registered mobile number (*the mobile number should be registered with your ID number)*

- Once successfully registered, you can now proceed to log in to the SurePay HELB Mini-App

- For existing beneficiaries(students), enter your mobile number and press on continue.

- You will receive a 4-digit verification code sent to the email address and mobile phone shared which you will use to verify your phone number on the SurePay HELB mini-App.

- Enter the 4-digit verification code on the SurePay HELB mini-app App and select Verify.

- You will be prompted to set a customized secret PIN that will be used as your login PIN for the SurePay HELB mini- App.

- Once the PIN is successfully set, you will be directed to the SurePay HELB App home page.

- Note: It is advisable to set a different memorable SurePay HELB Mini app PIN from your M-PESA *PIN #PIN yako, siri yako*.

Contact HELB to assist.

The FULIZA amount will be settled first, and the balance will be available for your use.

NO. You must be the validly registered owner of the mobile number and ID used when registering for the HELB.

Contact HELB to change your details.

**Short Term Definition and KYC Requirements**

# **Short Term Paybill Definition**

This is a C2B Paybill with a defined short duration.

This is a cash collection service that allows your organisation to collect money on a regular basis through M-PESA for a 
limited period of up to 6 months. The solution also allows you access to a channel to manage your funds and get real time 
reports for transactions made on your account at no extra cost.

The defined duration is 1/3/6 months. Extension of the duration will only be done where a partner provides a written justification.

# **KYC Requirements for Short Term**

# **Medical fund**

Duly filled and signed short term pay bill Application form and Terms and conditions stating purpose and duration. (Provided by Safaricom).

Copy of ID/Passport/Alien /Military card of the applicant.

Certified supporting documents from the Hospital / Doctor treating the patient which should confirm the need for the collection e.g. reference to an operation/required treatment (on the institution’s letter head, stamped and signed by authorized personnel).

**If applying on behalf of the beneficiary.**

**If a minor**: the parents/guardian of the child should apply, and a copy of the child’s birth certificate or Birth Notification should be attached to the rest of the documents as listed above.

**If the person is incapacitated:** certified copies of IDs for the applicant will be required.

Letter from the bank /cancelled cheque stating the bank details 6. Registered Safaricom line for settlement of funds (number to be indicated in the application

# **Education Fund**

Duly filled and signed Short term pay bill Application form and Terms and conditions stating purpose and duration. (Provided by Safaricom).

Copy of ID /Passport/Alien /Military card of the applicant.

Certified Admission letter and fee structure (Either stamped or on institution letter head).

If applying on behalf of the beneficiary.

If a minor: the parents/guardian of the child should apply and attach a copy of the child’s birth certificate.

Registered Safaricom line for settlement of funds (number to be indicated in the application form).

Letter from Bank or cancelled cheque confirming bank details

# **Funeral Fund**

Duly filled and signed Short term pay bill Application form and Terms and conditions stating purpose and duration. (Provided by Safaricom).

Applicants copy of ID/ Passport/Alien /Military card.

Copy of burial permit or copy of death notification.

Registered Safaricom line for settlement of funds (number to be indicated in the application form).

Letter from the bank /cancelled cheque stating the bank details.

# **Wedding Fund**

Duly filled and signed Short term pay bill Application form and Terms and conditions stating purpose and duration. (Provided by Safaricom).

Applicants copy of ID/ Passport/Alien /Military card.

Copy of wedding permit and wedding notification.

Registered Safaricom line for settlement of funds (number to be indicated in the application form).

Letter from the bank /cancelled cheque stating the bank details.

# **Charity/ Catastrophe/NGO/ Religious /Fund Raising**

A covering letter from the committee stating the purpose of the Paybill and the Bank A/C details should be stated in the letter. At least two Committee officials to sign the letter.

Letter from the bank /cancelled cheque stating the bank details.

Registered Safaricom line for settlement of funds (number to be indicated in the application form)

Duly filled and signed Changa na M-PESA Application form and Terms & Conditions.

Signed Letter Justifying the need of the account.

Letter from the bank /cancelled cheque stating the bank details.

Party Certificate of Registration. (This applies to candidates under a party only).

Individual KRA pin.

Signed Tariff Guide.

Party KRA pin for candidates applying under a registered political party.

**NOTE**: **For more information please use the attached document M-PESA Short Term Paybill Handbook.**

**Definition**

# **Make Your Sherehe Bundle**

Sherehe(Daily Allocation) bundle is a data bundle product that provides a worry-free browsing experience by allowing customers to make a one-off payment and conveniently receive data bundles daily for a period of time.

We therefore help the customer to manage internet connectivity through daily allocation of their selected bundle for the selected duration.

Customers get a choice of 3 days, 7 Days, 14 Days, and 30 Days daily allocation for the purchased data bundle.

The Make Your Sherehe Bundle revamped journey gives customers two options:

**Input spend amount in Ksh**

Customers will be allowed to input any amount (in Ksh) and then be presented with different daily allocation bundle variations for that amount. The variations will be for 3 days bundle, 7 days, 14 days and 30 days.

**Input Preferred bundle (in MBs) to be allocated daily:**

Customers will also have the option of entering any amount of MBs they'd want to receive daily and then will be given the different variations available. e.g. if you want to receive 500MBs daily, you will be given amount to pay for 3 days allocation, 7 days, 14 days and 30 days. 

These will give customers the flexibility to choose any amount in terms of the cash they want to spend or MBs they want to receive in terms of daily allocation.

#  **Business Rules**

All customers will be eligible to purchase Sherehe Bundles.

Sherehe Bundles will be available on USSD – 544 and Digital channels -App & Web.

The bundles validity options shall be as below:

3 days

7 days

14 days

30 days

Unutilized resources shall expire at midnight when the customer shall receive next day’s daily allocation resources till the validity of the current product.

Available payment options will be airtime & M-PESA.

Allow for auto-renewal option.

Sherehe bundle resources cannot be shared/transfered to other customers

Reversal of Sherehe bundle can only be done on the first day bought/first allocation if the bundles are not partially used

Customers shall be able to purchase multiple Sherehe Bundles

All other Mobile Data standard business rules will apply.

The following response messages will be sent out during the registration process via the short code 534. These Messages will appear during the USSD interaction when the shareholder is opting in.

- Full names of the primary operator/operator
- Operator ID of the primary operator/operator
- National ID number of the primary operator/operator

 On the agent phone select ‘Change PIN’,

- If the Agent M-PESA account has been activated with start key but has M-PESA menu
- Advice the Agent to activate the menu by using their M-PESA secret PIN
- Agent to follow the steps provided on their M-PESA menu to receive the
- M- PESA menu.

# **Unlocking M-PESA Agent Assistant PIN**

Vet the operator with the details below.

Operator ID

Agent Number

Full names of the operator on the MPESA system

ID number of the operator

Last two transaction at the agency (operator can verify this from the transaction book.

If all the details provided are correct, unlock the account on the system.

Enter the vetted details on the comments field.

If the operator fails vetting, advice the operator to have the head office administrator requests for unlocking.

articleTitle: PRS Deactivation Escalation Procedure and Management procedure on CRM
markdownContent:
# **My SMS Deactivation****.**

- Query the MSISDN on Siebel:
- Access the SDP tab to confirm the active My SMS Services on the line. On Demand PRS will not appear on SDP, and a tag has been added to all on demand codes that do not require any un- subscription in Siebel and in the [PRS link](https://cmintranet/index.php/component/content/article/495?start=2).
- Advise the customer on the active My Subscriptions Services and confirm if he/she would like all SMS Services deactivated. The SDP product will be indicated to quickly identify the SDP product on the customer’s account as attached below. If the customer would like to deactivate all the SMS Services, press the control key on the keyboard and highlight all the active SMS Services product ID and delete all the SMS Service.
- If the customer would like to remain with a specific SMS Services subscription, go ahead and delete all the other subscriptions the customer does not wish to keep except the requested SMS Services.
- Capture an interaction with the action e.g. “*all My subscriptions deactivated as per customer request*” or “*all My subscriptions deactivated as requested except 12345 as per customer request*”.
- Educate the customer on the self-service procedure in case they need to deactivate a code in future using the \*100# (Prepay) or \*200# (Postpay).
- Send an SMS via Siebel on how to deactivate My Subscriptions in future.
- For the cases where both the customer and the CEE cannot deactivate using both the USSD and Siebel SDP, raise an SR for further investigation/action. Ensure that the error being experienced is captured to enable further analysis.
- Do not raise an SR for On-Demand un-subscription, the customer just needs to stop triggering the code by not sending any messages to the code. Confirm if the code is an on-demand subscription on the link.

- **Item**: PRS Provider
- **Type**: PRS
- **Category**: Value Added Services

**Comments**: Capture the appropriate comments

Advise the customer on the SLA and raise an interaction.

# **Games Support (Gameloft, Nazara & Huawei).**

All games subscriptions are visible on CRM. No need to log on to other partner support functions. This will be visible under the SDP tab as Nazara.

# **4-Digit PRS Services Deactivation**

- Advise the customer to send ‘STOP Keyword" to deactivate the short code or as per the procedure provided by the PRS provider.
- If the customer had tried to deactivate a 4 digit My SMS Services via SMS and failed, raise an SR for further investigation/action.

# **Subscription Issues on GET IT 411**

# **Bingwa Sokoni Reversal Scenarios**

**Scenario 1. Where Resources not awarded. Where agents say No Resources have been awarded.**

- Analyst will follow up for resources to be awarded and where award is not possible, it will be reversed guided by BusinessAutomation&OrderManagement@Safaricom.co.ke

**Scenario 2. Where Resources were awarded to the correct MSISDN and not utilized.**

- CEEs will verify that indeed agent float was deducted, and customer was awarded the relevant bundle from relevant systems, G2, Siebel & Bonga Link.

# What is the Hustler Rating and what does it mean?

The Hustler Rating measures your financial behavior on the Hustler Fund, based on borrowing frequency, repayment timeliness, and savings consistency. 

Ratings range from A1 (Excellent) to C3 (need for improvement).

# How can customers check their Hustler Rating?

3\. Select My Hustler Rating 
4\. Receive Prompt SMS showing their Rating

# Why is the Hustler Rating important?

A higher rating increases your loan limit and qualifies you for other products within Hustler Fund, giving you more financial flexibility.

# What happens if my rating is low?

A low rating may reduce your access to higher loan limits and limit financial product options. Improving your rating opens up more possibilities for you.

# How Can I improve my rating?

You can improve your rating by repaying loans on time, borrowing responsibly, and maintaining consistent saving habits with Hustler Fund. Positive financial behavior over time will help boost your rating.
