Reversals will be done due to processing failures, transaction, customer manually paying to the M-PESA GlobalPay short code, or Due to a Merchant’s goods return policy e.g. Goods/Services were not received, or a customer decides to cancel the purchase before goods are delivered.

**Auto reversals**

Auto reversals will be processed when a merchant voids the transaction. There is no waiting period for this as the transaction is reversed immediately.

Auto reversal will also be in place to resolve Processing failures for transactions that are complete on M-PESA, yet processing failed on 3rd party systems.

Refunds will be processed when the merchant refunds the customer for returned goods,

Processing Refund payments for returned goods will be automated.

**Manual reversals**

A manual reversal processed by Tutuka when a debited transaction is still in a pending state (preauthorized state) since the merchant has not settled. There is a waiting period of 7 days before a pending transaction can be reversed.

Tutuka will provide daily transaction reports detailing all transactions recorded by Tutuka. These statements will be used for reconciliation of failed transactions.

Manual reversals will also be performed, in by the Support team if failed auto reversals are identified.

Any exceptions must be escalated to Tutuka within a 30 (thirty) day period from the date when the exception arose.

## **Refunds**

The FS Operations team, on the other will process any manual refunds identified in bulk. SFC M-PESA refund & Fraud refund processes apply

Reconciliation will be done by finance treasury team upon receipt of the automated daily statements and reports.

Partial reversals – less charges, one time.

## **SIM Swaps**

Customer will not be able to access any card details within 24 hrs after a SIM swap.

However, if the details had been saved on a merchant site, the transactions will go through.

This Functionality is to ensure a customer is not allowed to create a new CVV within 24 hours of a sim swap thus preventing the card from being used in case it has fallen into the wrong hands.

## **How To Raise a Payment Dispute on** **M-PESA A****pp**

GlobalPay customers can now raise a dispute by selecting the transaction in question, eliminating the need to manually enter transaction details. This ensures that the details are automatically picked appropriately and without errors.

Customers can still enter the details manually if they want to.

As before, the customer must first contact the merchant and then file a claim after 7 days if no assistance is provided.

Customers must take a screenshot of and attach evidence of their interactions with the merchant.

Disputes will only be filed through the GlobalPay Mini-App on the M-PESA App. The form on the Safaricom website will no longer be available.

## **How to raise a Global Pay dispute**

Log in to your M-PESA App.

From the Grow Tab select M-PESA GlobalPay

Select the 3 dots just above your card.

Select Raise a Dispute option and fill in the required details. Once submitted, you will be contacted by a customer support agent within 24 hours to commence the dispute resolution process.

## **Handling payment dispute at the Call Center and RC.**

The CEE/RCEE will verify that the customers M-PESA account was debited, and a refund has not been done. If the customer’s complaint has not been resolved, The CEE/RCEE will send the customer an SMS notification with the link for accessing & submitting the dispute form.

Upon submission, the completed dispute form will be submitted via email to [M-PESACard@safaricom.co.ke](mailto:M-PESACard@safaricom.co.ke)

The Support Analyst will review the escalation and contact the customer incase additional information required. If the issue cannot be resolved internally and requires to be escalated as a dispute, the support analyst will raise and SR and assign it to themselves. The customer will be notified of the 45 days SLA and the SR closed.

If the dispute is because of a transaction authorization error, Safaricom will resolve the dispute within **72 hours.** However, if the dispute is between the customer and the participating Retailer, the maximum resolution time is **forty-five (45)** working days.

The SR owner will keep tabs of the dispute progress and advise the customer of the outcome as shared by Tutuka.

The Support Analyst will submit the dispute form to Tutuka via email [support@paymentology.com](mailto:support@paymentology.com) , depending on the dispute categories as explained on the escalation process below.

To initiate the dispute process, the customer might be required to provide supporting documents to clarify the dispute. These documents will enable all parties (Safaricom, Tutuka & Visa) to understand the issue being disputed by the cardholder.

## **Escalation of Payment Disputes**

All disputes must first be followed up with the respective Merchant.

If the customer does not receive any response within 7 days from the time the transaction was done, then they will follow up on the same with Safaricom.

Should the customer fail to reach an amicable agreement with the participating retailer, you may contact Customer Care or visit our retail shops or access the dispute resolution form that is published on the Safaricom website to lodge a dispute.

**NOTE:** The customer is expected to follow the cancellation and refund policies of the merchant before raising any dispute.

**How to handle double** **deduction****s on** **my virtual card**

Where double deductions occur, the merchant usually refunds a payment within 72 HRS. However, if you do not receive any refund within 72 hours, you should follow up with the Merchant directly via the link/email they have provided on their website.

If no assistance is received after 7 days, you can then raise a dispute to Safaricom via the Dispute Form for further assistance.

**How to handle** **a** **pending Reversal**

All follow-ups for pending reversals should be followed up with the respective Merchant from where the payment was made. You can fill up the escalation form that the merchant has provided in their online platform.

Please note, escalations done via the merchants have a shorter SLA (Service Level Agreement), compared to raising it through Safaricom which will take **45 days.** 

## **Applicable supporting documents include**

| Supporting Documents |
| --- |
| A legible copy of the actual sales receipt that was generated at the completion of the transaction. electronic proof of the transaction |
| A written cardholder complaint (letter or form) with specific information about the disputed transaction email message sent by the cardholder |
| Progressive cardholder documentation |
| Any other documentation that may be appropriate to support a particular chargeback, second presentment. |

## **Dispute Categories**

A dispute is a transaction that a cardholder/customer does not agree with or disputes and therefore requests that part of or the entire transaction should be reversed or refunded. Dispute conditions occur in 4 categories and have been assigned VISA chargeback reason codes as below.

| VISA Category | VISA Subcategory | Examples | Escalation Requirements |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Category 10: Fraud | 10.4 Other Fraud—Card Absent environment | This includes transactions where,stolen payment card credentials were used, andtransactions flagged by the Visa Fraud Monitoring Program. | Dispute form + Email/letter from the customer.Supporting documents transaction receipt/Police abstract |
| Category 11: Authorization | 11.3 No Authorization | Disputes in this category include.transactions processed without an authorization, e.g. on 3Ds.Declined authorization,Expired card orWhere a Card Recovery Bulletin was ignored. | Email/letter from the customer with transaction details. |
| Category 12: Processing Errors | 12.5 Incorrect Amount 12.6 Duplicate Processing | Processing error disputes include.Late presentments.incorrect transaction codes,Incorrect currency,Incorrect account numbers,duplicate processing/ duplicate payments involving payment by other means, andTransactions containing invalid data. | Email/letter from the customer with transaction details.(Transaction receipts/Evidence to show the Non-M-PESA transaction) |
| Category 13: Customer Disputes | 13.1 Merchandise/ Service not received.13.2 Cancelled Recurring Transaction 13.3 Not as Described or Defective Merchandise or Services13.6 Credit Not Processed 13.7 Cancelled Merchandise or Services | This category tends to deal with issues that can crop up between the customer and the merchant, such as:the merchant fails to deliver the product /goods are not shipped by the delivery date given/ the merchant bills the cardholder before shipping the transaction/due to Poor communication between the merchant and cardholder about shipping and delivery times.a merchant processes a recurring billing transaction after the cardholder’s subscription or payment card account has been cancelled,merchandise is damaged/defective/does not match the product description,refund credit or cancelled/voided transaction receipt has not been processed by the merchant after the cardholder has been notified that a refund will be given. | Dispute form + Email/letter from the customer.Supporting documents transaction |

Applicable Card-Not-Present Visa Disputes & Reason Codes for the categories above are summarized below.

## **Chargebacks**

Chargebacks refer to the reversal of the cash value (in whole or in part) of a transaction by the card issuer.

Chargebacks are handled according to rules set by Visa. Chargebacks cannot be submitted within 7 days of the date of settlement. This is to give the merchant an opportunity to send through a refund.

VISA chargeback reason codes have specific requirements/ supporting documents that need to accompany the chargeback submission.

If a chargeback is submitted the Merchant can either accept the dispute & pay disputed amount or reject the dispute by providing compelling evidence.

If a chargeback is successful (no second presentment is sent) the money is loaded back on to the card. When the automated adjustment task runs, the load adjustment call will be sent for the wallet or account to be loaded with the funds.

Tutuka support will communicate to the client support when a chargeback is loaded back on the card so that they can advise the cardholder of the outcome.

Chargeback transactions can be accessed through the settlement report as per the settlement processes referenced in section 3 and 4 above.

A second presentment (sometimes called a re-presentment) is the merchant’s opportunity to disagree with the chargeback request. After a chargeback has been submitted, the merchant/acquirer has 30 days in which they may submit their second presentments.

In case a second presentment is sent through, further investigation will be done in collaboration with Safaricom 3rd line teams to avoid an arbitration chargeback request.

In a case where there is a delay in the delivery of goods, the cardholder needs to wait 30 calendar days before a chargeback can be submitted. However, if this is not the case, the cardholder can proceed with the chargeback submission.

Chargeback time frames differ according to the chargeback reason code used. A chargeback or fraud chargeback cannot be submitted if the transaction is older than a certain number of days from the date of settlement.

| Reason code | Timeframe of when to expect feedback from a submitted chargeback | Chargeback cannot be submitted if the transaction is older than | Applicable scenarios |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Consumer disputes | 30 days | 120 days old | Merchandise/ Services Not Received,Cancelled recurring, Not as Described orDefective Merchandise/ Services, CounterfeitMerchandise, Misrepresentation, Credit NotProcessed, Cancelled Merchandise/Services,Original Credit Transaction Not Accepted, Non-Receipt of Cash or Load Transaction Value |
| Processing Errors | 30 days | 120 days old depending on the chargeback description. | Late presentment, Incorrect Transactioncode, Incorrect Currency, Incorrect AccountNumber, Incorrect Amount, Duplicate Processing/Paid by Other Means, Invalid Date |
| Authorization | 30 days | 75 days old depending on the chargeback description. | Declined authorization, No authorization, Expired card |
| Arbitration chargeback | 30 days | 30 days from the second presentment date | Second presentment |
| Fraud | 30 days | 120 days old | Fraud |

**C****hargeback Re-Presentments**

Visa’s rules allow merchants to fight chargebacks by re-presenting the transaction; this is chargeback re-presentment.

Visa specifies compelling evidence which must be included with the re-presentment to prove that the chargeback should not have been granted.

If the issuer accepts the merchant’s evidence, they will reverse the chargeback. If the parties involved in the chargeback do not accept the outcome at this point, Visa will decide the matter in arbitration.

**Compelling Evidence Requirement for merchants Rejecting Visa Disputes**

Compelling evidence in a chargeback representation will consist of proof that the cardholder knowingly participated in the transaction and received the intended benefit.

Merchants have the right to submit compelling evidence for the 10.4 (Other Fraud—Card Absent Environment) and 13.1 (Merchandise/Services Not Received) reason codes.

Acceptable evidence that can be submitted for either reason code, when appropriate includes.

Photographs, emails, or other evidence that the cardholder has received or is using the goods or services they purchased.

In situations where purchased goods were to be picked from the merchant’s location: a signature, copy of identification, or other identifying information provided by the cardholder at the time of pickup.

If the purchased goods were shipped to the cardholder: documentation from the carrier confirming that the merchandise was delivered to the cardholder at the correct time and address. 
For digital goods: network or server data that proves the cardholder downloaded the product or logged in to use it. This can include the cardholder’s IP address and geolocation, information about the device used, confirmation that the cardholder has a verified customer profile on the merchant’s site, proof that the cardholder accessed digital goods or services through that profile after the transaction date, and transaction data showing that the cardholder has made previous, undisputed transactions with the merchant.

When purchased goods are shipped to a business address: proof that the cardholder was employed at that address at the time of delivery.

For transportation-related transactions, including Travel & Expense: proof that the ticket was received at the cardholder’s billing address, proof that the ticket or boarding passed was scanned, evidence that the cardholder earned or redeemed frequent flier miles related to the transaction, or evidence of subsequent related transactions such as seat upgrades or on-board meals.

For the 10.4 reason code only, the following compelling evidence may also apply:

- A signed order form for a mail or phone order transaction.
- For airline transactions: documentation of the cardholder’s name on both the purchased itinerary and the departed flight manifest.

## **Fraud Chargeback Escalations**

Fraud chargebacks apply when a card holder says that they DO NOT recognize transactions and have no knowledge of the transactions and were not in the vicinity where the said transactions were performed, i.e. they DID NOT attempt the transaction at all.

The customer will contact Safaricom via the different channels, call, social media or through a retail shop to report the fraud.

The CEE/RCEE will proceed to block the card & M-PESA account to prevent additional loss of funds.

The CEE will send the customer an SMS notification with the link for accessing and submitting the dispute form and advise the customer that the chargeback process can only begin after the form is filled and emailed back with all the required documentation. These will comprise.

- dispute form completed and signed by the cardholder which will have detailed descriptions of the cardholder’s complaint.
- A copy of the Customer’s ID and a Police Abstract
- OB number & Police station & assigned investigative officer (IO)
- Any proof which will prove the cardholder’s dispute is valid.

The Support analyst will then send the documentation to [support@tutuka.com](mailto:support@tutuka.com) & copy M-PESA Fraud.

Tutuka support does relevant investigation and submits the fraud chargeback to Visa.

## **Submitting Disputes to TUTUKA**

Upon receipt of a filled dispute form from the customer, the Support analyst will verify that all the supporting documents have been provided then send an email to Tutuka support team capturing the SR number on the subject for tracking purposes. The email Escalation to Tutuka should comprise of

The title – this will give a brief description of what the issue is.

Customer’s card/reference number

Amount disputed.

Date of the transaction

Merchant/store name

Description of what happened.

A dispute form attached.

This email will generate a ticket on Tutuka’s side that will be used for tracking purposes. Any other follow up on the same issue will retain the same ticket number.

Once the dispute request has been submitted to Tutuka, the Support Analyst should attach the respective email to the SR for future reference & follow up, & notify the customer of the SLA, before proceeding to close the SR.

The SLA for the resolution is 45 working days.

Upon receipt of the escalation Tutuka’s support team will check that all the relevant documentation has been received and confirm receipt of the query via an automated ticketing system. Tutuka will also let the client support team know if any documents or information is missing.

Tutuka support will then investigate by checking if the transaction has settled or been banked by the merchant. If the transaction has settled with the merchant, Tutuka support will then submit the chargeback to Visa.

Tutuka support will then respond back to the support team to confirm if the chargeback has been submitted or not.

## **Card Details Management**

The PAN will comprise of a six-digit BIN 498705 and ten randomly generated digits within a pre-defined range. The PAN will be connected to the customers M-PESA wallet upon successful activation.

The validity period of the M-PESA card will be 6 Months. The cards will be automatically cancelled after expiry. The customer will be required to activate a new card. The activation process applies.

A customer will also have the option to cancel M-PESA GlobalPay or opt out from the service via a DIY service and may reapply if need be.

Just like the M-PESA PIN, Card details are confidential and should always be kept secure by the customer.

Any pending refund or reversal involving an expired card will be processed to the customer’s MSISDN, provided it is still active.

FS Business Operations team will be responsible for ensuring the card numbers are available on the system & ordering new ones from VISA when required.

**Cancellation/Opting out.**

M-PESA customers will be able to Opt out via M-PESA App

**How to O****pt Out** **on** **M-PESA A****pp**

Log in to your M-PESA App

From the Grow Tab select M-PESA GlobalPay

Select M-PESA GlobalPay

Enter PIN

Select the 3 dots just above your card.

Select Opt-out and confirm.

Enter PIN

One will receive an SMS notification with of successful opt-out.

Cancelling/Opting out will permanently detach the card credentials and may be used if a customer’s card details have been compromised or fraudulently used.

## **Card Cancellation**

Log in to your M-PESA App.

From Grow Tab select M-PESA GlobalPay

Select the 3 dots right above your GlobalPay Card.

Select Cancel Card.

Enter M-PESA PIN.

You will receive a notification indicating successful card Cancellation.

Customers who intend to continue using the M-PESA GlobalPay service after the service has been cancelled will be advised to activate the service again, to be issued with new credentials. Renewal, just like activation will be a DIY process. A customer who has opted out of the service, will be required to accept T&Cs again, during reactivation.

The customer will also have the option to contact Safaricom call centre or visit a retail shop to cancel an M-PESA card the CEE/RCEE will be required to vet the customer using the existing vetting processes. If vetting is successful, the CEE/RCEE will then proceed to Cancel the card from CRM.

The customer will receive an SMS notification confirming the action.

A card suspended for over 6 Months will be cancelled automatically. M-PESA recycling process will apply.

Fraud detection teams and FS operations will be able to cancel my M-PESA cards in bulk in line with existing fraud management & MSISDN recycling process.

**Individual M-PESA GlobalPay Cancellation:**

M-PESA Customers will also have the option to request for cancellation through retail centre’s / care desks. These cancellation requests may be in the form of Change of ownership, individual Accounts Closure request, or cancellation requests by Next of Kin.

RCEE will advise customer to provide the required vetting documents in line with the existing vetting procedures. Upon successful vetting and validation of required documents, The RCEE will raise an SR as per customer request and attach relevant documents on CRM as per existing processes.

The Support Analyst will recycle the M-PESA MSISDN as well as cancel the card on the M-PESA GlobalPay VBC on CRM.

Any pending refund or reversal involving a cancelled card will be manually processed to the customer’s alternative MSISDN in line with the existing refund process. Manual cancellation makes the card to lose all M-PESA financial capabilities (loads, deducts, refunds etc.)

**Safaricom Initiated M-PESA GlobalPay cancellations:**

## **MSISDN Recycling**

Bulk MSISDN recycling will be managed as per the Existing MSISDN recycling process where the list of MSISDNS that have the M-PESA GlobalPay service will be cancelled in bulk.

Automation of the recycling process is currently underway.

During the MSISDN recycling process, the list of numbers that have already been recycled on M-PESA G2 will be sent to the backend Virtual Visa Card Service, where the numbers are queued and taken through the currently implemented Opt Out function to clear any associated virtual card if any and remove them from the virtual card database.

## **Fraud Related Cancellations**

M-PESA fraud detection teams, in line with the existing fraud management process will be able to cancel M-PESA cards as a single entry or in Bulk.

articleTitle: M-PESA GlobalPay Virtual Visa Card Features
markdownContent:
The M-PESA GlobalPay Virtual Visa Card offers a range of specific features designed to enhance convenience and security for users.

## **CVV (Card Verification Value)**

Is a security feature that enables merchant sites to ensure you are the real owner of the card to reduce fraudulent activities on your card.

A CVV is generated by the customer during the payment process, to verify the payment.

All CVV generated will only be valid for 30 minutes. This will prevent anyone who has your card details from using your card because they may have to generate another CVV.

## **Expired CVV Number**

One cannot use an expired CVV number that is generated at the point of activation. Every time you want to make a payment, a CVV number will be generated, and it will only be valid for only 30 minutes.

## **CVV** **Generation o****n M-PESA App**

Log in to your M-PESA App.

For the Grow Tab select M-PESA GlobalPay

Select show card details.

Enter M-PESA PIN

Your card details will be displayed on the screen in the Card Format. (PAN, Expiry & CVV)

**Private Card Details, Expiry Date** **&** **CVV**

The Private Card Details, Expiry Date, and CVV are confidential numbers that should not be shared with anyone, including Safaricom Staff.

**F****lash SMS**

Flash SMS is a type of SMS that appears directly on your main screen and is not automatically stored in the message inbox. The M-PESA GlobalPay service utilizes Flash SMS messaging to further secure the VISA Credentials.

**Additional functionalities**

## **Monthly Budget**

A set budget functionality is a visual aid and not an enforced aid. Meaning the functionality notifies the customer that the limit has been passed but it is not there to prevent the customer from actuating the transaction.

This feature enables the customer to define a desired monthly spend & be notified when at 80 percent & 100 percent of the defined amount.

Transactions are not blocked once the budget is exceeded.

## **Cost Estimator**

This feature enables the customer to convert the cost of an item from applicable exchange rate to KES.

The 10 most common currencies have been availed and this will vary depending on the customer’s frequent currency used. The application also allows the user to convert any other currency in use around the world.

## **Statements/Mini Statements**

The customer will be able to access Mini- statements from the M-PESA GlobalPay Menu.

The Mini- statement will comprise of the last 5 transactions and will be sent to the customer via a flash SMS notification.

The transaction details will also reflect on the full M-PESA statement as pay bill online transactions.

The Support teams will be able to view M-PESA GlobalPay transactions from the customer’s profile on CRM. CRM statements will comprise of

M-PESA Transaction ID

Original Amount

Source Currency

Forex (Fx) Rate Applied

Amount In KES

Transaction Date

Transaction Status

Operation Name (Deduct/Load Adjustment)

Merchant Name

Narrative

Reversal MPESA ID

Description

M-PESA customer statement request process applies.

Customer should be able to view the mini statement even if the Card is suspended or cancelled.

The customer will not be able to access the Mini statement if the wrong PIN is entered M-PESA PIN to view Mini-Statements

The Merchant Name to be truncated to a Max of 12 Characters for a proper screen fit on USSD

## **Insufficient** **fund****s** **SMS notifications**

Customers will receive SMS notifications of insufficient funds when a merchant is trying to bill them for a monthly-based service as merchants are allowed to store the card details of the customer for future billing dependent on the services they provide.

**NOTE:** This is for subscription-based services, as they can bill the customer every monthly cycle without the customer having to go back to the website.

**Handling of Insufficient** **fund****s** **SMS notifications**

When the customer receives insufficient funds messages, there is a high probability that there is a merchant that is trying to bill him/her for monthly-based service and at that point the customer does not have the necessary funds.

The customer needs to either credit the account to allow the transaction to go through or remove the card details from the merchant site if they do not want the services or goods, it is advisable that the customer removes the card details from the merchant site.

**How to** **Suspend** **/****Unsuspend** **&** **Card** **Cancellation on** **M-PESA A****pp**

## **Suspend**

Log in to your M-PESA App.

Select Grow Tab

select M-PESA GlobalPay

Select Suspend Card.

Provide reason for suspending card.

Enter M-PESA PIN.

Receive a message of successful card suspension. 

## **Unsuspend**

Log in to your M-PESA APP.

From Grow Tab select M-PESA GlobalPay

Select your Unsuspend Card.

Enter M-PESA PIN.

You will receive a notification indicating the successful unsuspension of the card from M-PESA GlobalPay

## **Card Cancellation**

Log in to your M-PESA App.

From Grow Tab select M-PESA GlobalPay

Select the 3 dots right above your GlobalPay Card.

Select Cancel Card.

Enter M-PESA PIN.

You will receive a notification indicating successful card Cancellation.

The customer will also have the option to contact Safaricom call centre or visit a retail shop to suspend / unsuspend, especially if the phone has been misplaced, lost, or is stolen.

The CEE/RCEE will be required to vet the customer using the existing vetting processes. If vetting is successful, the CEE/RCEE will then proceed to suspend the card from CRM.

Upon unsuspension, the customer will access the same card number.

The customer will receive an SMS notification confirming the action.

Suspending will not be possible if the customer enters a wrong pin, and if the card is already suspended.

Fraud detection teams and FS operations will be able to suspend/unsuspend in bulk in line with existing fraud management & MSISDN recycling processes. The customer should not be able to unsuspend if the card is suspended by Safaricom e.g. For fraud-via M-PESA API on CRM.

**How to get Mini Statement on** **M-PESA A****pp**

Log in to your M-PESA App.

From the Grow Tab select M-PESA GlobalPay

All your recent transactions are visible on the homepage.

**Manage Card – Monthly Budget** **on** **M-PESA A****pp**

Log in to your M-PESA App.

From the Grow Tab select M-PESA GlobalPay

Under the Spending tools option, select Set Budget.

Enter your monthly budget amount and select Set Budget.

Enter M-PESA PIN.

You will receive a notification on the screen - Monthly budget successfully created.

On the M-PESA GlobalPay page, you will be able to view the amount used so far, from your set monthly budget.

**Check****ing** **Monthly Budget Usage Status** **on** **M-PESA A****pp**

Log in to your M-PESA App.

From the Grow Tab select M-PESA GlobalPay

On the M-PESA GlobalPay page, you will be able to view the amount used so far, from your set monthly budget.

Message Received – Dear customer, your usage as at DD/MM/YYY is Ksh xx, xxx. Your current limit is Ksh xx, xxx.

## **Repeat** **Transactions on M-PESA App**

A repeat payment permits a merchant to debit your M-PESA wallet for regularly occurring payments e.g., subscription services such as NETFLIX.

Repeat payments need customer authorization as shown below.

## **Enabling Repeat Payments**

Log in to your M-PESA App.

From the Grow Tab select M-PESA GlobalPay

Select Enable Repeat Payments (just beneath your GlobalPay card).

Select Enable.

Enter M-PESA PIN.

You will receive a notification confirming the successful enablement of repeat payments.

## **Disabling Repeat Payments**

Log in to your M-PESA App.

From the Grow Tab select M-PESA GlobalPay

Select Disable repeat payments.

Enter M-PESA PIN.

You will receive an SMS notification with a confirmation of repeat payments disabled.

**PIN** **requirements** **for** **repeat payments.**

Once a customer inputs their card into a merchant website for any subscription services and enables repeat payments, the payments will not require them to enter their M-PESA PIN in the next billing cycle, as funds will automatically be deducted from the M-PESA account.

Customers are advised to ensure that they keep their card number, validity period, and CVV details as securely and privately to avoid anyone else from using their card details for subscription services, as they would end up being deducted.

M-PESA GlobalPay Customers will be required to opt in to repeat payments & accept T&Cs to enable repeat/subscription payments to be successful.

To opt in the customers via the Safaricom app Select Grow >then Select Repeat Payments.

Opting into the repeat payment service will allow all repeat/subscription payments. The functionality does not support selective services.

To activate a subscription on a merchant’s site, the customer will browse through an online subscription service to review available offers/options.

The customer will then select the desired subscription and provide additional information such as the mailing or physical address before being prompted to select the desired mode of payment.

The customer will then select VISA as the payment option.

The customer will then be prompted to enter the M-PESA GlobalPay credentials (Card number, CVV, & Expiry date)

The M-PESA GlobalPay details will be validated by the merchant site before being stored, for recurring payments/subscription renewals.

Once a payment is processed, the customer’s M-PESA account will be debited, and the funds credited to the M-PESA GlobalPay pay bill.

The customer will receive two notifications to confirm a successful transaction, One from M-PESA, and the second one from M-PESA GlobalPay.

A customer who has not opted into subscription payments service on the M-PESA GlobalPay, will be notified to opt in once a merchant site attempts to deduct a payment.

There is no restriction to the number of retries, triggers, or reminder notifications sent by the merchants’ site for declined transactions.

The customer has the option to disable repeat payment transactions at any time, by selecting disable from the repeat payments’ menu. The customer can also opt out of the subscription from the merchants’ site or remove card details from the merchant site.

The customer is also provided with a link, on repeat payments menu, to access more information on repeat transactions, as well as the T&Cs

## **PIN Management**

If the customer locks the M-PESA PIN, he/she will be required to access the existing DIY PIN unlock channels e.g. via USSD, App or Voice Biometrics respectively.

Customer will also have the option to call Safaricom call centre or visit a Safaricom Shop. The RCEE/CEE will vet the customer as per the set guidelines and unlock or reset the M-PESA PIN from the M-PESA system.

The customers will be able to change the M-PESA PIN to secure their transactions through the STK and web Self-care as per the current process.

## **Viewing Card details**

To View Card Details, the customer will login to M-PESA App select Global Pay> then select see card details and will be prompted to enter the M-PESA PIN.

The Card details will be provided through a Flash SMS, and will include the 16-digit Pan & the expiry date of the M-PESA Card

The support teams will not have access to view customer Card details & security credentials. The Customer Details available on CRM comprise of:

Customer MSISDN:

Opt in Status:

Opt in Date:

Customer Name:

Last Action Dates:

Opt Out date:

ID Number:

Card Status:

ID Type:

## **Generating CVV**

To View the CVV, the customer will select Generate CVV option from the M-PESA APP>GlobalPay>Select card details>select CVV will be prompted to enter the M-PESA PIN

The CVV will be provided through a Flash SMS and will have a validity period of 30 Minutes.

The customer Management teams will **NOT** have visibility of the M-PESA Card details/credentials and customers should also be advised to ensure the credentials are secured for security.

M-PESA GlobalPay card details & CVV on the APP will be hidden by default. To view the card details the customer will be prompted to enter the PIN.

## **How to O****pt Out** **on** **M-PESA A****pp**

Log in to your M-PESA App

From the Grow Tab select M-PESA GlobalPay

Select M-PESA GlobalPay

Enter PIN

Select the 3 dots just above your card.

Select Opt-out and confirm.

Enter PIN

You will receive an SMS notification with of successful opt-out.

## **How To Get Assistance**

For any queries, call 100 for prepaid customers & 200 for postpaid customers.

For M-PESA-related queries please dial 234 for assistance.

Visit our Retail Centres /Care desks.

Access our social media handles; Twitter–@Safaricom\_Care and @SafaricomPLC, Facebook - www.facebook.com/SafaricomPLC.

## **Customer Support Process**

Issues arising during activation will be resolved in-line with existing M-PESA customer support processes.

If unsuccessful, the customer will receive the following message: *“**Failed. Your activation request for My M-PESA Card has been declined, please contact customer care”.***

Anticipated Failure scenarios during activation and proposed actions are as below.

| Failure Scenario | Proposed action |
| --- | --- |
| Wrong M-PESA PIN | M-PESA PIN unlock & Reset process applies |
| Card already activated against a document ID | One card per document ID |
| System failures | Existing support processes for USSD, STK push and M-PESA G2 apply |
| Frozen/Suspended M-PESA Account | M-PESA Support process Applies |

## **Transacting using M-PESA GlobalPay**

A customer will browse through an ecommerce site to review available offers/options.

The customer will then select the items of interest before proceeding to check out.

Before selecting a payment option, the customer will be required to provide additional information such as the mailing & shipping address, where applicable before being prompted to select the desired mode of payment.

The customer will the select VISA as the payment option and will be prompted to enter the M-PESA GlobalPay credentials (Card number, CVV, & Expiry date)

Once the M-PESA GlobalPay details have been validated by the merchant site, the customer will be able to proceed to check out.

Once a payment is processed, the customer’s M-PESA account will be debited, and the funds credited to the M-PESA GlobalPay paybill.

The customer will receive two notifications to confirm a successful transaction, One from M-PESA, and the second one from M-PESA GlobalPay. The transaction confirmation message from M-PESA will indicate the surcharge.

M-PESA GlobalPay Transactions will only be possible on international merchant sites. Transactions to Local sites will be blocked and an error message given to redirect the customer to use M-PESA Express/LNM Online checkout.

Customers attempting to transact on 3DS merchant sites may be prompted to enter a Onetime Password (OTP) sent to their MSISDN

Anticipated Failure scenarios during transaction processing and proposed actions are as below.

| Failure Scenario | Proposed action |
| --- | --- |
| Wrong M-PESA PIN | M-PESA PIN unlock & Reset process applies |
| Insufficient funds | Fuliza is to be introduced/part of the scope |
| Invalid Card Credentials | The customer will be notified when the card details are invalid or expired |
| System failures/time-out | Existing escalation processes for USSD, STK push and M-PESA G2 apply |
| Limit Rules | Minimum 105, other M-PESA limits apply |
| Frozen/Suspended M-PESA Account | M-PESA Support process Applies |
| Authorized transactions | Default action for authorized transactions on M-PESA will be cancelling/ Do Not Honour” met authorization criteria. |
| VISA Authorization e.g. Restricted Zones | Visa transaction Controls & authorization rules apply |
| Repeat payment Opt in required. | Customer must opt in to allow subscription/repeat payments |

# **DEFINITION**

This is a service that allows customers to transfer internet data bundles from one mobile number to another.

# **ELIGIBILITY**

This service is accessible to both Individual Post Pay and Prepay subscribers.

# **HOW IT WORKS**

- Sambaza Internet allows subscribers to transfer data bundles. **One can now transfer a maximum of 5GB a day.**
- A minimum of 5MB data bundle balance is required to remain on account before Sambaza Internet request is successful. And the minimum that a customer can transfer is 5MB internet data bundles.
- Customers can Sambaza Internet up to 10 times daily.

**NB:** If the customer has reached limit in Sambaza, Customer can use the line with bundles as hotspot and be able to use with other devices **/**Computer.

# **Bundles that one can Sambaza:**

- Monthly bundles with expiry (Go monthly Bundles).
- Non expiry bundles.
- Post-pay bundles.

# **Bundles that one cannot Sambaza**

- Daily Bundles
- Giga bundles.
- Promotional bundles.
- Okoa bundles.
- Deal of the day/month bundles
- All Tunukiwa/DIY Bundles
- Bonus/Free Bundles

# **SELF SERVICE OPTIONS**

**Via USSD:**

- Dial \*544#
- Sambaza internet
- Enter bundle to Sambaza.
- Enter phone number to Sambaza.
- Select bundle of choice-with expiry or No expiry

Wait for a confirmation message.

**USSD Direct Strings**

- Monthly Bundle- dial **\*544\*92#**
- Go Monthly Post Pay Data- dial **\*544\*94#**
- Post-pay Data- dial **\*544\*93#**
- Milele Data bundle- dial **\*544\*91#**

**Via MySafaricom APP:**

articleTitle: M-Shwari Credit Score and Batch numbers
markdownContent:
- Credit Score is a measure of credit risk established from one’s credit history and calculated from a credit report using a standardized formula.
- A positive credit score is characterized by payment of M-Shwari loans on time (less than 30 days), frequent and increasing savings on M-Shwari Deposit accounts and where a customer has not defaulted on any Safaricom product.
- On the other hand, a negative credit score is characterized by late payments and/or defaults on M-Shwari loans.
- A Good Credit History is one where an individual has a positive credit score.
- The Customer would be considered as a low risk and M-Shwari would be comfortable to lend to such individuals at favorable terms including enhanced credit limits.
- A Bad Credit History is one where an individual has a negative credit score and may be considered undesirable to lend to such a person.
- This may also result to reduction and/or cancellation of existing credit limit that the customer currently enjoys.

# M-Shwari loan after CRB listing

- By the time the customer is listed with CRB, their loan limits will have been cancelled hence the client cannot get another loan M-Shwari immediately.
- The record of the defaulted loan will form part of their negative credit history and will result in a lower score should they be considered for a new limit which will solely be determined by their savings behavior.
- The new limit will range from 100 – 500.The client will also have to wait for a period that could range from 2 months to 4 months prior to a limit increase.
- The length of time will depend on the customer’s last limit review date and the disbursement date of the defaulted loan.
- During the wait period the customers must be active on their M-Shwari Savings account and exhibit positive behavior on Safaricom services.
- The borrower also must clear their status with the CRBs and must settle all arrears or overdue loans, or installments listed with CRB (including M-Shwari).

# Delisting from CRB list

- Once you repay a nonperforming loan (NPL) as listed with CRB, the record will be updated with a "Closed" status however, a bureau is required to retain information on non-performing loans until the end of **seven years** after it is repaid in full.
- Listing with CRB does not mean that lenders are not allowed to lend the borrower any money during the 7-year period. It only means that the lender will take extra caution and negotiation will become more difficult for such a borrower. For example, a listed customer may be subjected to shorter loan terms, higher interest rates and/or the Bank may decline their loan request depending on the risk profile of the borrower and relative to the risk appetite of the lender.
- As such, the record is categorized as “closed with default history” CRB CLEARANCE PROCESS.
- For M-Shwari loans, once a defaulter finally settles their loan, can they get a clearance certificate?

# Process of being cleared by the CRBs

- The borrower must settle ALL the listed overdue and/or arrears amount submitted by any bank IN FULL for him/her to be cleared by CRB.
- After settling an M-Shwari loan (assuming all other listed loans have been settled), the borrower can then proceed to either or all the three licensed CRBs (ref below address) as follows:

- If M-Shwari loan was repaid between 1st and 8th day of the calendar month – visit CRB on or after the 15th Day of the same month and
- Request for a Credit Report.
- If M-Shwari loan is repaid between 9th and last day of the calendar month- visit CRB on or after 48 working days’ hours and request for a Credit Report.
- If customer is not willing to wait as above, visit any of the CRB offices and obtain a Clearance Certificate at prescribed fee (currently Kes.2, 200/-) with a TAT of 48 hours.
- The CRB will have to confirm that the customer has cleared the subject loan by calling and/or querying NCBA via email hence may take some time.

# Getting Batch numbers

### Getting M-Shwari batch number

- To clear with the respective CRBs they will require a batch number which will be issued once the customer clears the outstanding balance.
- Use URL [M-shwari blacklist checker](https://cxintranet.safaricom.net/cm2/E_MshwariBlacklists_query.php) for reference to get the **batch number** if a customer requests.
- If the batch number is missing 48 hours after loan clearance kindly raise an SR.
- To clear with the respective CRBs they will require a batch number which will be issued once the customer clears the outstanding balance.

# Getting a Fuliza batch number

- To clear with the respective CRBs customer will require a batch number which will be issued once the customer clears the outstanding balance.
- If a customer calls to request for a **Batch number**, kindly Use URL [Fuliza blacklist checker](https://cxintranet.safaricom.net/cm2/E_MshwariBlacklists_query.php) for reference.
- If the batch number is missing 48 hours after loan clearance kindly raise an SR for Support team to follow up.

# Getting a KCB M-PESA batch number

- To clear with the respective CRBs customer will require a batch number which will be issued by KCB Bank once the customer clears the outstanding balance.
- If a customer calls to request for a **Batch number**, kindly use URL [KCB M-PESA blacklist checker](https://cxintranet.safaricom.net/cm2/E_MshwariBlacklists_query.php) for reference.
- If the batch number is missing 48 hours after loan clearance kindly advise the customer to contact KCB bank for assistance.

# **How to subscribe**

-  Dial \*444#.
-  Select More.
-  Select Flex.

-  Choose to buy once or autorenewal
-  Confirm purchase.
-  Customers will receive an SMS notification for a successful purchase.
-  Auto renewal will be at midnight if the customer has adequate airtime.

# **To unsubscribe from flex**

- Dial \*444# OK
- Select More
- Select Flex
- Select "98" for MORE
- Select “Stop Autorenewal”
- Select the Flex Bundle you want to Unsubscribe from.
- You will get a successful unsubscribed notification

# **Checking flex balance**

**VIA 444 USSD**

- Dial \*444#
- Select More.

articleTitle: OKOA DATA BEI YAKO (FLEX) and OKOA DATA PAYMENT.
markdownContent:
# **Definition**

This is a service that allows Safaricom Prepay subscribers who meet the eligibility criteria to borrow data loans for as low as ksh 1.

# **Eligibility**

All Safaricom prepay customers.

# **How to access Okoa Bei Yako Data Bundle**

A customer will access the Okoa Bei Yako Bundle by dialing \*544# or \*131# and selecting Okoa Bundles.

**Amount a customer can get on Okoa Bei Yako**

A customer will get an option to enter the amount of money they want to spend.

**How to I pay for the Okoa Bei Yako Data bundle**

On top-up, Okoa bundle loan will be deducted until the debt is fully paid.

**What is the service charge for Okoa Bei Yako Bundle**

The customer will be charged an advance fee of 10% for band 2 and above. Please note Band 1 will not be charged an advance fee.

 [Screenshot] 

# **Business Rules:**

- Customers will be able to request for Okoa bei Yako data bundle for any amount from as low as Ksh 1.
- A customer can get the service as many times as per their score.
- Once they key in the amount, the resources they qualify for will be displayed and customer will decide whether to proceed as is or change the amount.
- The MBs displayed will be based on the amount and rate used.
- The Bundles will be valid for 24hours.
- The resources will have 24hr validity.
- For every amount entered service charge should be collected and the rest of the amount cater for the cost of the bundle
- All other business rules for Okoa will remain as is, ie. customer will have to be eligible for Okoa service.

# **Okoa Data Payment**

**Definition**

This is a service that allows Safaricom Prepay subscribers who meet the eligibility criteria to purchase data bundles using Okoa as a payment option.

**Eligibility**

All Safaricom prepay customers who are not blacklisted from the Okoa service are eligible for the service.

**How to I access Okoa as a payment option on data bundles**

- Prepay customers purchasing data bundles will be presented with Okoa as a payment option on the USSD menu.
- Customers selecting airtime as a payment option with insufficient airtime will be given an option of completing the purchase using Okoa.

**Bundles available using Okoa**

For now, this will be available on daily and weekly bundles, but We plan to introduce Okoa payment for all data bundles purchases.

**Validity of the data bundle resources bought using Okoa**

Daily and Weekly Bundles purchased using Okoa as a payment option will maintain their validity i.e. Customer purchasing a weekly bundle valid for 7days will receive their data bundle resources valid for 7days.

**How many times can I purchase data bundles using Okoa**

As many times as, your Okoa credit score.

**How to repay for the Okoa debt for data bundle purchase**

- On top-up, Okoa bundle loan will be deducted until the debt is fully paid.
- Business rules for Okoa repayment will prevail i.e., customers will be given 5 days to repay their Okoa debt the recovery options will kick in after the 5days period are over.

**Service charge for data payment done using Okoa**

- The customer will be charged an advance fee of 10% for each request, Customer requesting for ksh 10 to complete their purchase will pay service charge of ksh 1 (10%), hence making total repayment of ksh 11.
- The summary will be displayed on the journey before customer accepts to purchase data using Okoa.

**Can I use Okoa data payment when buying for other?**

- The Okoa data payment will be available for purchase of daily bundles and weekly for self as well as buy for other.
- Customer will use the service when selecting “buy once” option.

# **M-Shwari Listing**

- As per our M-Shwari terms and conditions, CRB listing implies sharing/ reporting, positive and negative data relating to loan performance to credit reference bureaus.
- Positive reporting means sharing data on loan accounts that are performing in terms.
- Negative/ adverse listing implies reporting default data to the CRBs. Default data on a customer adversely listed on CRB stays on file.
- During the registration session, all the M-Shwari customers were requested to on reading the M-Shwari terms and conditions to ‘accept’ Terms and conditions.

# **FULIZA Listing**

- As per our Fuliza Terms and conditions, CRB listing implies sharing/ reporting, positive and negative data relating to loan performance to credit reference bureaus.
- Positive reporting means sharing data on loan accounts that are performing as per the terms.
- Negative/ adverse listing implies reporting default data to the CRBs. Default data on a customer adversely listed on CRB stays on file.
- Customers who fail to pay their outstanding Fuliza balance after 120 days are listed with CRB.

# **KCB M-PESA listing on CRB**

If a customer has an outstanding loan on day 91, the account gets **listed on CRB** with a Non-Performing Loan (NPL) status.

**NCBA Listing**

- Adverse listing is done on customers with outstanding loans above day 120 from the date of reimbursement.
- The customer is reported to the Credit Reference Bureaus after 120 days of non-remittance of payments and the record stays on file for up to seven years.
- NCBA updates CRBs daily within 24 hours after the payment has been made.
- Upon sending the instructions to the CRBs, NCBA communicates via SMS to customers with the CRB batches containing the instructions for the updates.
- CRBs have committed to process the updates 24 hours after the update has been sent by NCBA.
- Customers will be required to pay through the normal M-Shwari channel/process on their handsets as per T&Cs.
- The data sharing arrangement with 3rd parties for collection purposes is covered in the current M-Shwari Terms and Conditions.

# **Debt Collectors Agencies**

NCBA has engaged the services of 4 external debt collection agencies to help with recovery of outstanding M-Shwari debts:

- Gilchery Skip-Trace Limited.
- Metropol Corporation CRB Limited.
- Quest Holdings Limited.
- CCI Kenya.
- Boresha
- Master Quick Col
- Collection Africa
- Finley International

The service agreement requires the agencies to reach out to M-Shwari defaulters via SMS, email, outbound calls, and negotiate repayment of the outstanding monies.

**NB:** Attached find a list of numbers that will be used to contact customers.

The following SMS will be sent from M-Shwari to all affected customers.

‘’Please note that we have forwarded your M-Shwari loan data to GILCHERY SKIP-***TRACE LIMITED for collection. Please pay your loan today to avoid any inconvenience’’***

# **M-Shwari Credit History**

- Once the repayment period (30 Days) lapses, that nonpayment record will become a part of the customer’s credit history and is made available to be used during the formulation of the customer’s credit score.
- A loan default is when you have not made your loan payments to M-Shwari as per pre agreed timelines (30 Days).
- Once a default is posted to a consumer's credit record or credit history and the loan remains outstanding for Over 90 Days, it is reported to CRBs and the record stays on file for up to seven years.
- Owing to the long period of time, it is important for all M-Shwari customers to avoid defaulting on a loan whenever it is possible.
- One of the best ways to reduce the possible repercussions of a default is to work some type of payment plan with our M-Shwari Debt Collection Agents once you receive a call from them.
- You should however strive to meet the payment plan as agreed if any.

How to improve Credit History after being **reported**

- The first step is to pay off all overdue loans that have been reported with CRB‟s (if any).
- Then begin rebuilding your credit history and ensure all loans taken from all lending institutions are repaid on time.

Information Update on the Credit Report once paid in full

- Credit Reference Bureaus store information from lenders and public records in compliance with the CRB Regulations.
- When you use credit, a record of your payment history is reported to credit reporting agencies.
- This information is the chief source of your credit report and score, which both define you’re paying habits.
- Your credit report is your information collateral to lenders.

# **M-Shwari Loan Repayment after Listing Notification**

Once a customer offsets a pending M-Shwari loan they will receive the message below that is sent daily to active lines.

*“**Thank you for paying your loan. Your CRB record was sent on dd/mm/yy. Metropol ref MCRBXXXXXX and Transunion Batch Number XXXXXX. Visit CRB for clearance after 48 hrs.”***

The message is sent the following morning after the update is sent to CRB.

Updates are usually sent 24hrs after the loan is paid on weekdays and the following Monday if a loan is paid on weekends.

articleTitle: Closed User Group (CUG) Definitions and Mechanics
markdownContent:
**Closed User Group (CUG) Definitions and Mechanics**

# **Definition**

Closed User Groups are groups of mobile subscribers who can make and receive calls from members within the group at preferential rates and with additional benefits only applicable to the group.

CUG allows employees, within the pre-defined user group, to make and receive unlimited calls.

A monthly subscription fee applies for each member that joins the defined CUG.

# **Eligible Customers**

The service is offered to corporates accounts, they have the discretion of deciding whom to include. However, prior notification will be required before members can be added or even excluded.

# **Features**

A subscriber can only belong to one CUG however a corporate is entitled to more than one CUG.

There will be a minimum of 5 subscribers per CUG but no maximum cap.

# **Rates**

| Size of CUG | Monthly Fee Per Line (Kes. Inc Tax) |
| --- | --- |
| 5-20 Lines | Ksh 650 |
| 21-50 Lines | Ksh 550 |
| 51-100 Lines | Ksh 450 |
| 101-350 Lines | Ksh 350 |
| 350+ Lines | Ksh 300 |

# **Benefits**

Cost Savings for the business due to discounted rates - the charges for this service are competitively priced therefore organizations are likely to make great savings.

Ensures smooth & cost-effective communication within & across departments.

Improves employees' productivity through collaboration.

Increased operational efficiency & Cost control – companies can choose plans that fit their budget.

Tailor-made – customized packages for businesses and bulk discount.

# **Sample Use Cases**

Institutional CUG e.g. Healthcare- Enhances communication among healthcare professionals, improving patient care and operational efficiency.

# **DIY For Accessing Closed User Group**

To apply for closed user group contact Safaricom Business via email on [Corporatesales@safaricom.co.ke](mailto:Corporatesales@safaricom.co.ke)  and documents required are Certificate of incorporation/Business Permit, Original ID of the Directors and KRA PIN.

**Reverse Call Definition and Mechanics**

# **Definition**

This is a feature that will enable subscribers complete their calls by allowing the ‘called party’ to Pay for the initiated call.

# **Eligibility**

All customers are eligible to make a reverse call. I.e. prepay, hybrid and post-pay subscribers

Subscribers will use reverse call if they are calling other subscribers within the network. One will not be able to request a reverse call for Off Net, Roaming & International calls.

Reverse call should work for:

Prepay subscribers calling another Prepay / Post pay / Hybrid subscribers,

Post-pay subscribers calling prepay/ Hybrid/post pay subscribers.

# **Mechanics of Reverse Call**

To originate a reverse call, the calling party needs to dial a special prefix (#) together with the called number e.g. #0722123456

IVR will play an announcement to the called party alerting them that it is a reverse call and they will be charged for the call. The called party will then be given the option whether to accept or decline the call.

# **Accepted Reverse call**

Once the called party accepts, the call will be connected, and amount deducted from the called party. The calling party will not incur any charges.

# **Declined Reverse call**

The call will be disconnected and both parties will not be charged.

# **Called party does not have enough airtime/minute**

The reverse call will not go through if the ‘Called’ subscriber has insufficient airtime.

# **Reverse Call Notification**

Once the recipient answers the call, IVR will play an announcement to the called party alerting them that it is a reverse call and they will be charged for the call. The called party will then be given the option whether to accept or decline the call.

Customers will be billed Ksh 0.50 on the 3rd reverse call request of the day but will not incur any other costs while using the service for the rest of the day.

**After the 1st reverse call request of the day**

“You have 1 Free Reverse call left for today. Kindly top your line with airtime or dial \*131# for okoa jahazi’’

**After the 2nd Reverse call request of the day**

‘’You will be charged 50 Cents on your 3rd reverse call request. Please note you will not incur any other cost of use this service for the rest the day’’

# **Bonga Accumulation**

Only the called party will earn Bonga points as they are the ones paying for the call.

# **Business Rules**

Charging of party B account should be from customers main account (for prepay subscribers) or from credit limit (for post pay / Hybrid subscribers), other resources will also be used except the below resources as they are highly subsidized.

Tunukiwa Hourly Minutes

Tunukiwa Talktime

Talkmore Minutes

All in one Minutes

Talkmore Minutes Daily

Tunukiwa Minutes

Tunukiwa Hourly Talktime

Daily Dabo Kredo

Storo Bons Airtime

Tunukiwa Daily Talktime

The reverse call will not go through if the ‘Called’ subscriber has insufficient airtime. (In this scenario, the calling party will get the following message ‘Dear customer your reverse call request was unsuccessful, kindly Top up airtime or Dial \*131# for Okoa Jahazi.

If the Recipient /called party doesn’t Accept by pressing 1, Decline by pressing 2 or presses any Other Key, the reverse call will Disconnect.

If the recipient/called party presses the wrong prefix, the reverse call will not go through until the recipient selects or dials the correct prefix.

# **Benefits**

Increase the number of completed calls.

Always keep our customers connected.

articleTitle: Fraud Location, M-PESA and SIM Swap Fraud
markdownContent:
# **Fraud Location: Prison** **Site**

If a CEE receives a call with requests for any of the services below:

- Request for a SIM swap
- Request for a start key

The CEE will Check the location of the caller's mobile number on SAWA system or on WDE and the line being swapped on the 'fraudster location/subscriber locate tool' on the SAWA system.

If the line is in a prison site and is requesting for any of the above services, CEE will bar the line and advise the caller accordingly.

All other services can be offered upon vetting as per Contact Center/Retail Center procedures.

The provision of fraud location details on WDE does not change the call guideline processes and therefore a customer should not be denied service if they are within a fraud site but their request does not require fraud location vetting.

If Found in Prison site

- **First verify the tariff, if it indicates ‘M-PESA agent tariff’, ‘SYJ tariff’, ‘dealer tariff’, do not suspend the line.**
- **If the tariff is not as above, display the fraudster's account on Siebel and suspend both incoming and outgoing calls**
- **Check on M-PESA system to confirm whether fraudster has any balance of the defrauded amount and initiate reversal back to the victim's account.**

 Blank Fraudster Trace

- **For any SIM location that gives this error, kindly refer customer to Retail Shop for further assistance.**

**M-PESA Fraud**

# **Fraudulent Deposits**

- The M-PESA agents continue to suffer losses as a result of social engineering scams which are perpetrated by suspected fraudsters through deposit fraud.
- The risk team put in place measures that monitor the transactions with an aim to identify suspicious trends to determine if they are fraudulent.
- Upon analysis the affected accounts are barred on HLR/SAWA and key comment put on Siebel.
- An email will be auto generated to the call center escalation folder with the list of affected MSISDN.

# **Action Required by Call Center CEE**

- The key comment ‘’Suspicious deposit transaction’’ should be captured on Siebel by the agent handling the call then should escalate to the folder for verification.
- In case the customer whose line received the deposit is suspended and customer calls to inquire about their line status, CEE will advise the customer that they are confirming the issue with the line and getting back to them.
- Check on interactions if there is any action already taken by the folder CEE and advise the customer.
- If the interactions show the line remains barred for fraudulent deposits, advise the customer accordingly.
- If no interaction has been captured, ask the customer for an alternative contact and send the details to ccescalation@Safaricom.co.ke.

# **Action Required by Retail CEE**

- Retail CEE should call the agent and verify; the transaction will be captured on CRM for the affected MSISDNs.
- Check if the line has the key comment.
- Access the last deposit transaction on G2 and call the agent to confirm that the deposit was valid, and they received the cash.
- If they confirm that transaction was valid, proceed to unbar the line.
- If they confirm that transaction was not valid, reverse the money back to the agent and leave the MSISDN barred.
- Capture an interaction showing the action taken.

# **Action for Care centre escalation folder**

- Agent will receive an email from isecurereports@Safaricom.co.ke containing a list of the affected lines.
- Access the customer account and check last agent deposit transaction on G2 and call the agent to confirm that the deposit was valid, and they received the cash.
- If they confirm that transaction was valid, proceed to unbar the line.
- If they confirm that transaction was not valid, reverse the money back to the agent and leave the MSISDN barred.
- Capture an interaction showing the action taken.

# **SIM Swap Fraud**

Fraudsters start by gathering data about a customer via social engineering (sending fake texts, phone calls to trick customers into divulging personal information) then proceed to sim swap their numbers.

Reporting Sim Swap Fraud by CEE

Collection of information on all unauthorized SIM swaps is done internally (Call Center, Retail and by M-PESA agents.

# **Requirement that Trigger collection of information;**

- Customers complaining about fraudulent SIM swap on their line.
- Customers complaining their lines are no longer working and you confirm a swap was done that they did not request.
- Customer who shared details with fraudsters and you confirm a swap has already been done by the fraudster.

**Action Required by CEE**

- Check for recent Orders for any unauthorized SIM swap to confirm if the swap was done internally or by a dealer (EAIUSER)
- Where the swap is by EAIUSER or no Order exists, check under Sim Swap OTA tab on CRM for a recent OTA swap. On CRM click on SIM swap OTA tab to view details.
- Where there exists unauthorized SIM swap the CEE will be required to capture the details on the SIM swap fraud link;

[https://cmintranet/index.php?option=com\_php&Itemid=1733](https://cmintranet/index.php?option=com_php&Itemid=1733)

- Customer (Swapped) MSISDN
- Select channel used to swap
- Agent MSISDN used to swap/Username of the staff who swapped the line.

**N/B:** The link is also available under CM Intranet >> CC Systems >> SIM swap >> SIM swap Fraud.

# **Handling Sim swap Fraud cases by CEE**

**Call Center Action Points**

- Where a customer calls to report that they have been called by fraudsters and have given out their details, advice the customer on the need to suspend the account and if consent is given, proceed as below;
- Vet the customer (name and ID)
- Suspend the line on CRM using action reason ‘’suspend all-customer request’’. Enter key comment **"Do not unbar, details given to fraudster".**
- Log in to G2 and suspend the M-PESA account under account info tab as below. In the comment box, enter "**Customer gave details to Fraudsters"**.
- Where a customer calls to report they were called by fraudsters and shared details but on advising to suspend line they decline or they don’t give consent to suspend line, advise customer to visit an Agent/Retail Centre/care desk to do a sim swap in order to obtain a new PIN.
- Educate customer on fraud and advise them not to share their details with 3rd parties.
- After suspending the line, advice the customer to visit the nearest care-desk/ Safaricom shop for assistance, so do not swap such line.
- Empathize with the customer and advise the customer to do the following or reset for the customer the below.

Reset their webselfcare account.

Reset their Safaricom App.

Delete their VB Enrollment.

Reset any other application that could compromise their funds or privacy.

Advise the customer to also contact their respective banks and report the breach.

- This will help the customer prevent or minimize loss of funds.

**Note****:** At this point the fraudster has all the details and may also call to ask for swap and may pass vetting.

# **Retail/Care desk action points**

- Vet the customer as per retail vetting procedure, Resume and swap line in CRM.
- Resume/Un-suspend in G2 and assist the customer to reactivate the M-PESA account.
- Remove the key comment on CRM.
- Empathize with the customer and advise the customer to do the following or reset for the customer the below.

- Reset their webselfcare account.
- Reset their Safaricom App.
- Reset any other application that could compromise their funds or privacy.
- Advise the customer to also contact their respective banks and report the breach.

This will help the customer prevent or minimize loss of funds

markdownContent:
This process is applicable where a customer is outside the country and is requesting for M-PESA Account re-activation after line recreation.

# **Requirements**

- The Line will be recreated as per the current line recreation process for customers residing outside Kenya.

These documents will be emailed to Safaricom Customer Care customercare@Safaricom.co.ke or advantage@safaricom.co.ke

# **Acceptable M-PESA registration documents for Roaming Customers**

- Copy of ID used to register for M-PESA - certified by Notary Public or by the Kenyan Embassy
- Copy of passport page with the stamp of entry into foreign country - certified by Notary Public or by the Kenyan Embassy

**NB:** Notary Public is a counsel/lawyer/public officer who attests or certifies writings (such as a deed) to make them authentic and takes affidavits, depositions, and protests of negotiable paper.

# **DEFINITION**

This is the total length of time a CEE places a customer on hold to check for further information, refer to a colleague, seek approvals etc.

# **Seek Consent**

- Ask the customer if they can hold a moment and wait for consent before putting him/her on hold.
- Ensure that the Customer is aware that you would like to put him / her on hold.

**NB:** **Wait for the customer to confirm by either YES or NO.**

# **Reason for engaging hold**

- Explain the reason for engaging hold and use language that is courteous and respectful.
- Use the Hold button, Not Mute, to place the Customer on hold.

**Hold management**

- Always get back to the customer within the stipulated duration. (60 seconds for all skillsets **except** Data which is 120seconds).
- It shall be considered the number of hold instances in the call and should not exceed a maximum of 3 instances.
- Where there is only one hold instance the duration of 60 seconds shall apply.
- For multiple instances (up to 3 instances) a maximum cumulative duration of 120 seconds shall apply (all skillsets).
- Where a call warrants more than 2 minutes of hold – typical for data calls – it will help to verbalize the same and get consent before the same is applied.
- Necessity will be judged by the Query type and Related systems.
- Where the CEE has still not resolved the customer issue despite up to 3 holds, it is expected that the issue be escalated via SR as this is an indication that there is no immediate solution to the query; or that it requires further offline investigation by the CEE.
- Where a CEE is experiencing any system challenges, it is expected that this shall be visible to all via the individual system outage tool for necessary reference during assessment.

**Thank the customer for hold**

- Always thank the customer for holding and for their patience and explain your progress or what the outcome was for him being on hold.
- Where the customer has put the CEE on hold while he himself has been released from hold by the CEE, the CEE should prompt the Customer twice then end the call by saying “am sorry I cannot hear you, if you can hear me kindly call us back, you will be assisted.”
- At this point end the call using the standard call closing phrase.

# **Call Intercept – Non-KYC Compliant Customers**

# **Defination**

This is a voice message that will play on every outgoing call initiated by a non-compliant SIM registration details customer advising them to update their SIM registration details before connecting the call.

# **Content of the sim registration details of Call intercept message**

*“**Dear Customer, your sim card details are not updated. Kindly visit your nearest mpesa agent or Safaricom shop with your original id to update your details or go to* [*www.safaricom.com*](http://www.safaricom.com/) *to update online.”*

# **How does it work**

1. Whenever a non-compliant customer makes a call, they will be intercepted by the voice message advising them to urgently update their SIM registration details.
2. Call Intercept will;
 1. Play and proceed to connect the call without disconnecting it.
 2. Play before the dialing tone/Skiza tune.
 3. Play during every call initiated by a customer who has sufficient airtime and has not updated their SIM registration details
3. The Call intercept voice message will not play if the customer has insufficient airtime to connect the call.
4. They will hear the current insufficient message notification and then Okoa, redeem Bonga or purchase airtime from M-PESA and once they have sufficient airtime the voice message will play before proceeding to connect the call.

# **Who will be targeted**

This exercise will target customers who are yet to update their SIM registration details.

For as long as the customer is yet to update their SIM registration details, they will continue to hear the voice message every time they initiate an outgoing call.

# **Automated APN Provisioning**

The Fixed Data COE, in collaboration with the OSS team, has automated the process using USSD \*485#, where upon activation of FWA services (4G and 5G), the respective APN will be triggered.

This is a change geared towards eliminating customer pain during the onboarding process.

For LE and Public customers' requests that require activations to be done via backend, APN provisioning via BOT will continue as always to support this need.

# **Step-By-Step Process Link Activation**

**Customer Presents Payment SMS:**

\- Customer shows an SMS notification requesting a service and deposit payment of a sales order to a Customer Experience Executive (CEE).

**2\. CEE Receipts Sales Order:**

\- Customer Experience Executive (CEE) processes the sales order on the Point of Sale (POS) system.

**3\. SIM Replacement and Configuration:**

\- CEE replaces the customer's SIM card and disables the SIM PIN to prepare the SIM for use.

**4\. Provide Physical SIM:**

\- CEE gives the customer the new physical SIM card.

\- Insert the SIM card into the appropriate powered Customer Premises Equipment (CPE).

 **5\. Guide Activation:**

\- Instruct the customer to dial \*485# on their registered contact to activate the SIM.

\- This step allocates the correct product, configures the Access Point Name (APN), and registers the customer contact for in-life management.

All 5G for Business Activations will be on **5GforBusiness APN.** Failure to select this will lead to failure of APN provisioning and customer will not access service.

To ensure optimal customer experience, make sure:

- **5G customers** are activated on the 5G APN: 5GforBusiness
- **4G customers** are activated on the 4G APN. FixedLTE1

If the correct APN is not selected, APN provisioning will fail, and customers will be unable to access the service.

FWA APN Activation Paths

1. **The USSD \*485#** - this is the default activation path for all FWA activations. Dial \*485# and proceed to activate the 5G SIM card on a customer’s registered contact. No customer should leave the Safaricom shop or receive a new 5G SIM card as ready for use until the APN activation is correctly set. Verify that the customer’s APN is properly set to 5GforBusiness for 5G activations and the appropriate APN for 4G activations before a customer uses the service.
2. **The Email to OSS Bot:** For Large Enterprise and Public customers' requests OR any subsequent reprovisioning of APN, for example after a sim swap, APN provisioning will continue to be done via Email to the BOT.

The email body MUST mention the appropriate APN to be activated: 5GforBusiness

If the correct APN is not activated or the APN activation is not done, provisioning will fail, and customers will be NOT access the 5G service. Ensure the correct APN is used to avoid these issues and provide seamless service.

# **Definition.**

Fiber optics transmit data in the form of light particles -- or photons -- that pulse through a fiber optic cable.

Fiber to the building (FTTB) is a type of fiber-optic cable installation where the fiber cable goes to a point on a shared property and the other cabling provides the connection to single homes, offices or other spaces. FTTB applications often use active or passive optical networks to distribute signals over a shared fiber-optic cable to individual households or offices.

- **A passive** optical network (PON) is a cabling system that uses optical fibers and optical splitters to deliver services to multiple access points. A PON system consists of optical line termination (OLT) at the communication provider’s end and a number of optical network units (ONUs) at the user’s end.

- **The Active** Optical Network arrangement is a point-to-point structure (PTP), meaning that each user has his own dedicated fiber optical line terminated on an optical concentrator. In an active optical system, environmentally electrical switching equipment are deployed, such as a router or a switch aggregator, to manage signal distribution and route data to proper places.
