# **How to troubleshoot** **FTTH** **issues related to Gaming Issues**

- The CEE will confirm the router parameters and will advise the customer to login to the console and map the servers locally/closer home (South Africa) to reduce high latencies on gaming sites.
- The L400 CEE will run a ping test on random sites to check whether it is an issue to do with the gaming sites only or other sites in general.
- The CEE will then proceed to check if the OLT has 2 VLANS & shift accordingly or run a software upgrade on the router to S204, in case this fails the CEE will the escalate to Fixed technical support and copy Home Customer Support via email with an SLA of 2 hours.

        [Screenshot]

**FTTB SLOW SPEEDS**

If a customer call complaining that they can connect but at very slow speeds, ask the following questions before you proceed:

- Has he tried accessing different websites using different browsers?
- Are other users on the network experiencing the same?
- Is the customer connecting via Wi-Fi or via cabled LAN (sometimes Wi-Fi is subject to intermittent speeds due to obstacle interference, distance from access point, wave reflection and or refraction and these affect the wireless transmission with the LAN?

Once you verify that the slow speeds issue is not restricted to the customer’s LAN, use the following steps to verify the problem:

# **Checking Link Utilization**

Every link has its allocated bandwidth and if all the bandwidth is exhausted, this will result to packet loss/slow speeds. Check if customer is maxing on his link using Allot. If the customer is maxing, advise him/her to manage internet usage by checking the number of user’s vis-a-vis the total bandwidth. Also, some protocols are known to utilize more bandwidth than others; advice the customer on the most active protocols so that he/she can control their usage.

- Log on to Allot link [https://10.15.6.65/smp/pages/login.jsf](https://10.15.6.65/smp/pages/login.jsf) and Launch NetXplorer and then graph.
- Right click on ‘Network’, and then scroll to ‘Real time monitoring’ and then click on ‘pipes’,
- Under ‘show data for last’, define the length of time that you want to graph for in terms of number of days, hours, or minutes.
- Under data resolution, select the time intervals to appear after graphing. This should depend on the length of time that you’re graphing.
- Then click on the ‘Limits’ tab, you can check either Subscriber or internal host tab.
- You can query either using the **Ip 197.248.170137 or the CI 95084018.** Of the importance here is the customer’s allocated bandwidth.
- Check on the link utilization and advise the customer; accordingly.
- If the link is maxing, (i.e., utilizing the entire allocated bandwidth), this normally affects internet speeds negatively and brings about high packet loss.
- Advise the customer to consider upgrading his bandwidth or manage his link usage.
- If the link is maxing, you can go to the next step and advise the client on the protocols that are using most of his link bandwidth. To do this, follow the below steps:

If all the above scenarios are ok ie. Link parameters are ok, no packet loss, no latencies and link is not maxing, ask the customer to carry out a speed test through [www.speedtest.net](http://www.speedtest.net/) in order to confirm whether whatever he’s getting from his side is what is allocated in terms of bandwidth/speeds.

**NOTE: When carrying out a speed test, ask the customer to connect only one machine directly onto the router/IDU to get more accurate results.**

**If the issue persists, raise a service request for the 2nd Level Support to action.**

- Categories: Fiber Active | Fiber GPON
- Type: Slow Speeds
- Sub Types: Slow Speeds

# **Checking Latencies and Packet Loss**

- Log on to ‘Tacacs /putty’ using your credentials.
- Login to the respective PE and trace the link.

We will use Client’s circuit ID: 95048582 | Switch serving client: Gospel | Bundle- Ether100.8739|Gateway 197.248.161.17 link as an example.

- Use the ping command **“ping vrf carrier 4.2.2.2 source 197.248.161.17”** or **“ping vrf carrier 4.2.2.2 source Bundle-Ether100.8739”** to verify whether the link has any packet loss or high latencies.
- Ping different sites to confirm the average packet loss/latency.
- By default, ping test success rate should be 100% (o% packet loss). If this is not the case, try ping different sites to get an average success rate.

 [Screenshot] 

From the above results shows that the customer has no packet loss, and the latencies are within acceptable range.

If the link has high latencies and packet loss, raise a service request for the 2nd Level Support to deal.

- Categories: Fiber Active |Fiber GPON
- Type: High Latencies
- Sub Types: High Latencies

- Login to Rundeck using [http://172.29.227.112:4440/user/login](http://172.29.227.112:4440/user/login) and re-provision the link.

 [Screenshot]

- Categories: Fiber Active | Fiber GPON

- Sub Types: Slow Speeds

# **Definition**

This is a credit facility that will be offered to M-PESA Agent head offices.

M-PESA Agents will be able to borrow between Kshs **50,000 to 10,000,000** for their M-PESA Agency.

# **Benefits of M-PESA Agent Business Loan**

- Keeping agency businesses open and afloat.
- Quick and easy access to affordable credit to complete transactions.
- Growth of agency networks.
- Seamless transaction for customers.

# **Eligibility:**

- This service is available for **M-PESA Agent Head offices**.
- All M-PESA agent head offices will be able to access the loan based on the credit scoring to determine qualification.

- Store must have been active for a minimum of 6 months.
- Agents will use their Head office till numbers to access the service.
- An agent can only apply for one loan or one till per store at a time.
- Only active tills are eligible.
- The store should not be suspended or blacklisted.

# **Loan Features**

- The loan will be accessed through USSD \*234\*3# and the business app.
- Offered in loan duration of 4 days.
- Loan limit is based on their store activity. The more you transact the higher the chances of increasing the Loan Limit.
- Loan limit will be adjusted downwards or upwards based on your repayment history.
- If you have an existing Loan, you will be required to fully repay for an existing loan before requesting for another i.e. One loan at a time
- You can opt out of the product if you do not have any outstanding loan.

# **Product Pricing**

- **Loan Duration:** Loans will have a 4-day duration.
- **Access Fee**: One off access fee-based loan charges at the time of taking the loan Currently 0.083% for a period of 4 days.
- **Roll Over Fee:** 0.083% for a period of 4 days.
- **Penalty Fee:** There will be no penalty fee applied.

# **Customer Journey**

**To register for the M-PESA Agent Business Loan Service?**

- Dial \*234#
- Select M-PESA Agent Services
- Business Loans
- Select M-PESA Bloom
- Select Join
- Accept terms and conditions to opt in
- Enter Operator ID
- Enter Operator PIN

**To check my Loan Limit**

- Dial \*234#
- Select M-PESA Agent Services
- Business Loans
- Select M-PESA Bloom
- Check Limit
- Enter Operator ID
- Enter Operator PIN

How to determine Loan Limit; by monitoring your monthly commission, we will be able to establish how much you qualify for.

**To increase Loan Limit;**

- Borrow and pay your loan timely.
- The higher the M-PESA Agent Head Office commission the higher the chances of increasing the Loan Limit.
- To earn higher commissions the M-PESA Agent MUST transact actively, that is, they should increase their deposits and withdrawals at their M-PESA Agent tills.

**How to request for a Loan after registration**

- Dial \*234#
- Select M-PESA Agent Services
- Business Loans
- Select M-PESA Bloom
- Select Request Loan
- Enter Loan Amount
- Enter Operator ID
- Enter Operator PIN
- You will receive the funds shortly after making the Loan request.
- The funds will be applied to your M-PESA Agent Head Office float account for redistribution.

**To access the funds**

- Once the funds have credited to the M-PESA Agent Head Office,
- Log onto M-PESA System or use the M-PESA Agent Management Till to do the distribution.

**Reasons why loan can be declined****.**

- If the Loan amount requested is higher than your Loan Limit. The Loan request MUST be made **within** your **Loan Limit.**
- If you have been **blacklisted** by Safaricom for fraudulent activity or defaulting previous loans.
- If you have an **existing Loan**. You will be required to fully repay for existing loan before requesting for another. You can only request one Loan at a time.

**How to make a repayment for the Loan**

**The agents have an option to either pay the loan for themselves or pay from a different head office till (Pay for other).**

1. **Pay for self****.**

- Dial \*234#
- Select M-PESA Agent Services
- Business Loans
- Select M-PESA Bloom
- Select Pay
- Select pay for self:
 - **Partial Settlement** – you can pay in instalments before the Loan due date.
 - **Full Settlement** – you can pay the entire Loan amount at once.
- Enter Operator ID
- Enter Operator PIN
- Payment can be done from your M-PESA Agency head office Float account.
- Failure to pay back on time.
- A roll over fee of **0.083%** will be applied once
- The M-PESA Head Office working account will be suspended until the loan is repaid fully.

**Pay for other**

- Dial \*234#
- Select M-PESA Agent Services
- Business Loans
- Select M-PESA Bloom
- Select Pay
- Select pay for other.
- Enter store number.
- Enter nominated number

 - **Partial Settlement** – you can pay in instalments before the Loan due date.

 - **Full Settlement** – you can pay the entire Loan amount at once.
- Enter Operator ID
- Enter Operator PIN

# **Reasons for not receiving requested loan amount.**

This might be because of:

- Making a loan request as the first one is still being processed.To avoid this, the agent should wait five minutes before making another loan request if the first one has not been processed.
- Agent store account status. Account should be in **active status**.
- Primary operator status.**Primary operator must be active.**
- The M-PESA system being slow or is down. Once MPESA services are back up, the amount borrowed will reflect in your account shortly.

**Repaying loan after due date**

Your credit limit will be adjust based on your repayment history and suspended on default.

**How to contact in case of any queries**

- Telephone: contact Safaricom on: **Agent 2134**
- E-mail: M-PESAagentadmin@safaricom.co.ke

| Not Paid by end of the 31st day from the day of borrowing | -Permanent Blacklist | |
| 3rd time Offender | Not Paid by end of the 9th day from the day of borrowing | -Permanent Blacklist |

# **How to Map/Un map** **Notification****s on CBS Tool**

The L400 folder CEE will map or un map contacts numbers that receive payment notifications. This is done upon request. We can map up to 3 contacts on CBS and they don’t have to be registered under the same customer.

# **How to** **Map/Un** **map** **as per** **request on call:**

- The L400 CEE will confirm the calling number is the same as the one on sales portal. If the calling number is different, CEE will advise that the registered person to call back.
- The L400 CEE will authenticate client’s phone number, raise an SR. CEE will send ticket details on SMS to the client indicating the ticket number and SLA of 24 hours. Line 400 CEE will assign the SR to FTTH Folder team for changes to be done.
- Line 400 folder team will counter check client’s information, map or un map details as per customer’s request using CBS system. Folder CEE will close the SR, contact client, and advise on the updated changes.

# **How to Map/Un map as per request on email:**

- The L400 CEE will confirm the email address used by the client is the same as the one on sales portal. If the email address is different, CEE will advise customer to use the registered email address.
- FTTH folder team will authenticate client’s email address, raise an SR, attach customer’s email on the SR. CEE will respond to the email indicating the ticket number and SLA of 24 hours.
- Line 400 folder team will counter check client’s information, map or un map details as per customer’s request using CBS system. Folder CEE will close the SR, contact client, and advise on the updated changes.

**Failed FTTH/FWA (Fixed Wireless Access) CRM Posting**

# **Definition.**

- Failed CRM posting is where a customer makes payment for FTTH account renewal, funds are debited from the customer M-pesa account but fails to interface on CRM for product/service renewal.
- Where a customer calls to complaint of service renewal failure, Line400 CEE will ask the caller to provide the payment details to confirm if payment was successful on M-PESA 150501.
- CEE will then proceed to raise a manual adjustment SR for increment to be done on CRM. SR notes should have the customer names, CI, M-pesa transaction ID, amount paid and the contact.
- SR categories are**, FTTH, Failed CRM Posting, Increment.**
- The SR should have an Activity for TL’s approval.
- The activity/SR will be approved by the TL after which the funds will be credited to the customer account, auto product renewal will then take place and the folder CEE will confirm service uptime before closing the SR.

# **Post Payment Link Reset.**

- Once the client pays after the disconnection, an SMS notification will be sent to the customer by CBS informing of successful payment.
- Customer will be automatically reconnected.
- Where payment has been made and the service is still not resumed, the customer will confirm the router is powered on and the network devices connected well.
- L400 team will confirm if product has been renewed/activated on CRM, log into U2000/NCE to check if HSI (High Speed Internet) is enabled, confirm if the customer CI is correct and click on the reset button to assist reset the customers link as shown below.
- Where CI on NCE is different from the one on Sales Portal, the CEE will raise an SR to Fixed Customer Support to configure the correct CI with it’s PPoE password, Map the MAC address on AAA and confirm service uptime before closing the SR.

- Automated bills are only applicable post pay payments under the Safaricom Staff payment plan.

# **Fixed Data Products Overview**

Fixed data is refers to fixed-line connectivity for customers. This can be seen as **a connection to an end customer, by means of a cable, through which a user can make phone calls or connect to the Internet**. Fixed lines are clearly separate from the mobile phone network, by which end users are connected to the network via wireless transmission technologies. In safaricom fixed business, we have the following 4 groups of products within fixed data.

# **Internet For Business (IFB)**

- This is provided as either Fiber to the building (FTTB) or through Fixed LTE.
- On Fixed LTE, a customer has a choice from the following packages: Bronze- 4G(90GB), Silver-4G(120 GB), Gold-4G(200GB) and Diamond-4G(400GB).
- On IFB Fiber, a customer has a choice from the following packages: IFB3(3mbps@2,999/=), IFB5(5mbps@4,100/=), IFB7(5mbps@5,799/=), IFB9(9mbps@9,999/=) and IFB15(15mbps@15,699/=).
- Target group is SMEs Or Large Enterprises using bandwidths below 15 mpbs in a particular site / branch.
- Billing is done on Anniversary Date (Not prorated) i.e., from 01/mm/yyyy to 30/mm/yyyy.

For IFB Fiber FAQs visit articles [New IFB Fiber Packages](https://safaricom.egain.cloud/system/templates/selfservice/safaricom_wss/help/agent/locale/en-us/portal/999900000000000/content/Prod-11746/A0561-Fixed-Wireless?query=%20A0561).

For IFB Fixed LTE FAQs, visit articles [New 4G Products Brief A0561](https://safaricom.egain.cloud/system/templates/selfservice/safaricom_wss/help/agent/locale/en-us/portal/999900000000000/content/Prod-11746/A0561-Fixed-Wireless?query=%20A0561) and [New 4G Products FAQs A0562](https://safaricom.egain.cloud/system/templates/selfservice/safaricom_wss/help/agent/locale/en-us/portal/999900000000000/content/Prod-11747/A0562-FAQs-Fixed-Access-Wireless?query=a0562).

See below for more details on IFB propositions.

# **Internet For Large Enterprises (LE)**

·       This is provided via Fiber (Standalone), Fixed LTE, Microwave or VSAT.

·       The bandwidth for this product is usually >15 Mbps

·       Target Group is for customers with multiple sites, complex networks and/or high number of users.

·       Billing is done on a calendar month basis (is thus prorated)

In cases where the customer is in a fiber ready building and have a need for bandwidth above 15mbps, they will be sold internet and not IFB.

# **WAN. (Wide Area Network)**

The products from Safaricom in this category are WAN, MPLS, P2P, SDWAN, etc)

·       This is provided offered via Fiber (Standalone), Fixed LTE Over MPLS, Microwave or VSAT.

·       The bandwidth can range from 3 Mbps upwards (No limit)

·       Target group is companies that need a LAN (Local Area Network)

·       Billing is done on a calendar month basis (is thus prorated)

# **Safaricom Home**

This refers to Fiber To The Home (FTTH), 4G For Home and 5G For Home connectivity.

More about [FTTH products and how it works can be found here.](https://safaricom.egain.cloud/system/templates/selfservice/safaricom_wss/help/agent/locale/en-us/portal/999900000000000/content/Prod-3086/A0456-Definition-and-Mechanics-of-Fibre-To-The-Home-Service-FTTH)

More about the [4G For Home packages can be found here.](https://safaricom.egain.cloud/system/templates/selfservice/safaricom_wss/help/agent/locale/en-us/portal/999900000000000/content/Prod-11746/A0561-Fixed-Wireless?query=%20A0561)

Each of 3 product groups have a unique price list covering the relevant bandwidths and each has unique products on CRM/CBS. A customer with a WAN can also have IFB and/or Internet on any site depending on the need assessment.

# **Definition.**

This is applicable where customer reports slow speeds or frequent disconnection issues.

**Where customer contacts other channels other than L400 i.e. retail, L100/200, social media etc.**

- CEE will confirm account payment status on CRM Siebel.
- Where account status is noted as rental suspend, CEE will advise customer to make payment.
- Where account is noted as normal or on rental suspend and CEE confirms they have made payments, CEE will send a request via email copsftth@safaricom.co.ke to L400 team for customer connectivity issue under slow speeds.
- Retail CEE will send email to copsftth@safaricom.co.ke for action by the FTTH team.

**Customers may also make calls direct to L400 and via email to safaricomhome@safaricom.co.ke.**

- L400 CEE will confirm that the customer has an active subscription/Product on CRM.
- L400 CEE will recheck allot status and confirm its not on disconnection portal and if its on disconnection portal and product is active, the CEE will proceed to unbar the CI on the Huawei provisioning tool.
- L400 CEE will confirm service uptime and advice customer accordingly.
- L400 CEE will proceed to log into U2000/NCE and confirm that the customers status is connected.
- L400 CEE will proceed to check on the connected devices on U2000/NCE under More and select Query ONT Learning MAC address > Click on Query advise the customer accordingly as shown below.

        [Screenshot] 

**Where the customer is disputing the connected devices, advise them to change the WI-FI password, reset the link and let them monitor.**

       **[Screenshot]**

- L400 CEE will proceed to check on the customers router power levels under Advanced > ONU Optical Module Info and confirm its within the range (acceptable range is -7 to -25 dbm).
- If the router power levels are above or below the set threshold above, then the L400 CEE should proceed to raise an incident on remedy to the respective partner /technician to assist optimize the power levels and advise client on the 24 Hr SLA. CEE will then send the incident number to the customer via SMS.
- If the power levels issue is global and affects all customers on the said port and not isolated to the calling customer, then L400 CEE will notify the folder lead who in turn notifies NOC to assist raise an incident for the respective partner to resolve the power levels affecting the entire port.

# **Definition**

EBU incidence escalation process applies when an issue is reported or noted on the various EBU service incidence, or where a customer has a general customer complaint/ compliment.

It outlines the various ways on how to escalate and resolve customer issues.

# **Customer categorization**

EBU customers are categorized into two categories.

1. Premium Customers
2. Standard Customers

# **Customer Support and Escalation matrix**

This outlines the process of customer support and escalation to the various support levels to ensure fault troubleshooting followed by resolution, recovery, service restoration confirmation and Incident / service request closure. 

Customer Support is classified in 3 levels:

- 1st line Support
- 2nd line support
- 3rd Line Support

# **How to Resolve Customers Issues**

Customers issues can be addressed and resolved using various strategies as below.

# **Proactive strategy**

- This is the process of actively and continuously observing systems, networks, applications, or other critical infrastructure to identify and address potential issues before they impact performance or availability.
- Its aim is to detect early warning signs, unusual patterns, or anomalies, enabling preemptive actions to prevent problems, minimize downtime, and overall reliability and performance at the customers site or network infrastructure via systems or tools.

# **Reactive strategy**

This is the process of responding to customer requests and issues after they have been reported. 

- When a customer contacts us to report an incident on their services, the CEE shall use the below systems to check the nature of the fault experienced by the customer e.g. Payment, router, connection, network, domain slow speed issues etc. and issue resolution or escalate to 2nd line support team where applicable. 

| System | Intent |
| --- | --- |
| NCE | Used to check the status of the device |
| Allot | For checking slow speeds, payments and barrings |
| CRM | For capturing interactions and checking account details |
| WHMCS | Used to address domain inquiries |
| Solarwinds | Used to monitor link performance, diagnose and triggers notifications/alerts to customers in cases of issues/outages |
| OWS limited to FTTH customers | Used to register alarms every 8 mins, then sends WEMA bundles within 15 mins and notifies the customer once the link is restored. |

- The CEE shall raise any global issue to the support teams who will then escalate to SOC (for correlation of any running incident) REF: Global Incident process.
- In addition, the CEE shall raise an SR for issue that require an on-site visit to the customer’s location based on the severity of the situation and will send a field contractor as per the customer’s region.
- The CEE will raise an interaction on CRM detailing the customer details and the issue the customer was experiencing and the resolution offered.
- Incases an issue reoccurs within 7 days; The CEE shall not raise another SR but will open the last SR raised and reassign the SR to the previous CEE for troubleshooting and resolution.

**2nd Line Support**

- The ticket raised from the 1st line support team will be assigned to the 2nd line support ECS.
- The 2nd line support ECS who is assigned the SR will go through the notes on the SR to understand what the issue is.
- The 2nd line ECS will then troubleshoot and conduct an analysis which will assist in identifying and fixing the fault. If the issue is resolved, the SR shall be closed, and customer updated.
- The 2nd line support teams or Service Owners will be responsible for escalating to 3rd line support teams or vendors based on the escalation procedures for existing contracts and where a support contract does not exist, escalation should be done to the immediate manager or vendor.
- In cases where the issue has not been resolved, the 2nd line ECS will escalate to the relevant 3rd line support team via BMC and communication shared with the customer.
- The 2nd line support will remain the owner of the SR and will follow through the escalation with the 3rd line support, the ticket shall remain open and shall be updated on a regular basis for easier tracking until the issue is fully resolved.
- Once the issue is resolved, the 2nd line ECS will call and confirm with the customer on service availability, provide a detailed incident report with the root cause analysis and resolution of service where applicable and close the respective ticket.

# **3rd Line Support**

- 3rd line support consists of service owners, vendors or partners who handle incidents escalated by the 2nd line ECS team.
- They perform in-depth analysis, troubleshooting and service restoration on the backend.
- They will liaise with the 2nd line ECS team giving progressive updates until the is fully resolved.
- Once the issue is fully resolved they will provide the 2nd line ECs team with a detailed root call analysis and resolution.

# **Global incident**

It refers to widespread disruption or failure of services and systems. It occurs in various contexts, such as Internet services, Cloud computing platforms, telecommunications, networks, or power grids and impacts many customers simultaneously.

# **Categorization of Global Incident.**

Categorization matrix provides the priority of handling global incidents.

| Business Service Priority | Description |
| --- | --- |
| P0 | Crisis |
| P1 | Critical |
| P2 | High |
| P3 | Medium |
| P4 | Low |

# **Compensation.**

This process refers to the benefits or reparations provided to a customer when a product or service fails to meet expectations or when an issue arises. It includes refunds, discounts, replacement of products, free services, credit notes etc. to address the inconveniences caused and maintain customer satisfaction and loyalty.

# **Reasons for Issuing a credit note.**

Compensation process should be identified and itemized as per incident procedures. The credit note can be issued due to the following reasons:

- Overcharge on an account because of Tariff difference hence a customer is issued a credit note.
- Customers' authority to utilize deposit paid as account payment.
- Taxes (VAT & Excise Duty) charged, and the customer has presented the documentation for exemption.
- Rebate on other charges as approved by the Finance Business Partner to EBU, Chief Finance Officer or HOD, Credit & Customer Billing Department.
- Errors /Omissions

**Credit notes approval matrix.**

Account Manager - Credit > Tribe Lead- EBU > Chief Enterprise Business Officer > Senior Manager – Credit > HOD – Credit and collections.

# **Communication.**

This process outlines the procedure for communicating emergency, planned, and service outage notifications, as well as education messages in accordance with the agreed upon SLA, with updates provided hourly.

This will ensure that the customer has the information and will not go looking for information elsewhere or where to escalate the issue.

**Types of notifications**

1. **Emergency Notifications:**

This is communication done immediately to the customers in cases of an emergency.

2. **Planned Work Notifications**

This is communication that is done to customers and are given a 48-hour notice prior to the planned work.

3. **Service Outage Notifications**

This is an Email notification sent to Enterprise Services Support by the Digital SOC /Incident Management team detailing the Incident, affected sites/nodes, number of Enterprise Customers affected and expected resolution timelines.

Enterprise Customers will receive a notification from the ESS team 2 Hours after restoration (to cater for recurrence/stability).

4. **Customer Education Notification**

This is communication sent out to the Enterprise Customers for education purposes about the EBU products and services (Customer education material) by the ESS team.

**Note:** The ESS team will draft a template which must be approved by Legal and Marketing.

# **Customer Support**

EBU Customers will report their incidences via the available touch points:

- Email: [Businesssupport@safaricom.co.ke](mailto:Businesssupport@safaricom.co.ke)
- Calling customer care on 2222 or 0722002222,
- Via the Social media platforms
- Via the Account/Service managers (who can call 2222 or send an email on behalf of the customer).

articleTitle: Timiza DIY Procedures for loan & deposits
markdownContent:
# **HOW TO ACCESS TIMIZA**

- Dialing \*848# or
- Downloading Timiza App.

# **OPTING IN**

- To opt in the customer will;
- Dial USSD code\*848# on the mobile phone.
- Accept terms & conditions and enter the national ID no.
- A confirmation message will display indicating request is being processed.
- Account is opened and customer receives an SMS with an initial log in pin for mobile login and activation phone app.
- Re-dial the USSD code \*848# and input the initial pin sent to them.
- Choose a security question.
- Create a new pin.
- Re-enter new pin.
- Confirm Pin change.
- Customer will get a message “**Log in using your log in pin & start transacting on Timiza”.**

# **TO DEPOSIT FUNDS**

**Via USSD**

- Dial \*848#
- Enter Timiza Pin.
- Select Deposit from M-PESA.
- Enter amount to deposit.
- Enter MPESA pin.
- A message showing a successful submission is displayed.
- M-PESA message to confirm transaction is received.

**Via Timiza App**

- Open Timiza App

- Press on Timiza Balance
- Choose Deposit.
- Enter amount to Deposit.
- Enter MPESA pin to confirm
- A confirmation message will be sent.

# **TO WITHDRAW FUNDS**

**Via USSD**

- Dial \*848#
- Enter Timiza Pin.
- Select Withdraw to MPESA.
- Enter withdrawal amount.
- Select to accept to withdraw.
- Enter Timiza pin.
- Pop up is displayed with amount withdrawn,
- M-PESA confirmation message is received.
- Timiza confirmation message is displayed

**Via Timiza App**

- Open Timiza App
- Press on Timiza Balance
- Choose Deposit.
- Enter amount to Deposit.
- Enter MPESA pin to confirm
- A confirmation message will be sent.

# **HOW TO REQUEST FOR A LOAN.**

Customer can use either the USSD or the Timiza App to request.

**Via USSD**

- Dial \*848#
- Enter Timiza Pin.
- Select Loans.
- Select Request Loan.
- Enter Amount.
- Choose Accept.
- Confirmation message received for loan disbursed to Timiza account and not directly to mpesa

**Via Timiza App**

- Download the Timiza App from play store.
- Register on the App.
- Log in using Timiza pin.
- Check the loan limit which will be displayed on the app home page.
- Select my loans
- Choose request loan.
- Input the amount to borrow.
- Press ‘Continue’.
- Timiza will confirm if the loan is successful.

# **HOW TO REPAY LOAN**

A customer can pay a loan via:

- MPESA STK menu.
- Timiza App.
- Via USSD

**Via STK (MPESA menu)**

- Go to M-PESA menu.
- Select Lipa na M-PESA.
- Select Paybill.
- Enter Paybill number 300067.
- Enter Account number (customers number 07...).
- Enter Amount.
- Enter M-PESA pin.

After transacting Hakikisha pops up “*you’re about to pay xxx to BARCLAYS TIMIZA.”* After confirming transaction, the customer will receive an SMS from both M-PESA and TIMIZA confirming loan repayment.

**Via Timiza App**

- Open the Timiza App
- Enter Timiza Pin
- Tap on the loan
- Select Repay Loan
- Select from Timiza wallet or M-PESA
- Enter the amount or Select Pay Full Amount.
- Select make payment and wait to enter MPESA Pin if using M-PESA option

Confirmation message will be sent with transaction details.

**Via USSD (\*848#)**

- Dial \*848#
- Enter Timiza Pin
- Select Loan
- Select pay Loan
- Choose amount, full or partial.
- Select payment Option, MPESA or Timiza account.
- Wait for MPESA pop up to enter MPESA Pin.
- Confirmation message will be sent with transaction details.

articleTitle: Timiza Service Definition, Loan Eligibility and Mechanics
markdownContent:
# **DEFINITION**

It’s a partnership between Safaricom and ABSA Bank giving financial self-service service that allows a customer to easily open an account, borrow and transact on the go from customer’s mobile phone.

# **ELIGIBILITY**

- It is eligible to registered active M-PESA customers**.**
- It’s not a must for a customer to have an ABSA account to opt in to Timiza
- Timiza is operated entirely from the mobile phone and cannot be accessed through an ABSA Bank branch.
- It is a separate bank account and is NOT linked to customer’s Absa bank account or any other bank account.
- A customer can access Timiza by dialing \*848# or Installing Timiza app on phone

# **Requirements for A Timiza Account**

- Be a registered Safaricom Subscriber, be a registered M-PESA customer and have an active Safaricom M-PESA account.
- Hold a Kenyan National Identification Document (ID)
- Kindly note that passports are **not** allowed.

# **SERVICES AVAILABLE ON TIMIZA.**

- Send money to another Timiza registered customer/send cash via ATM
- Deposit from M-PESA and Withdrawals
- Loan.
- Save money on the Timiza account.
- Airtime top up, to own number or other number.
- Paybill services (making payments to a Paybill).
- Insurance.
- My account which has:

- check balance

- Change pin
- Update email
- Retry registration

# **TIMIZA DEPOSIT ACCOUNT**

- It is an account that a customer can save money.

# **Definition;**

Manual adjustment refers to a process of adjusting resources, airtime or Bonga points from a customer’s line due to various reasons.

# **Reasons for Manual Adjustment;**

**Erroneous deduction of airtime from customers’ accounts for below scenarios.**

- Erroneous overcharge on SMS/ Calls
- PRS messages that are sent and charged on new lines.
- Skiza tunes that continue to be billed even after the customer has unsubscribed.
- Charge on the 191 calls that disconnect before being assisted.

**Resources purchased from Airtime, Bonga Points or M-PESA but not awarded for below scenarios.**

- Failed awarding of resources purchased via airtime.
- Airtime purchased via M-PESA but not credited.
- Resources purchased via Bonga points but not awarded.

**Resources refund request from customer, in cases where available systems fail to automatically credit/debit the customer’s account. Scenarios include.**

- Reversal of Data Bundle or Calls and SMS Airtime bought using prepaid Airtime.
- Postpaid deposit refund after Post2Pre migration for amount Ksh 100/= and below.
- M-PESA Airtime reversal initiated by CEE but fails to debit customer’s airtime account.
- Reversal of Bonga everywhere (Lipa na Bonga) payments for declined, cancelled or erroneous transactions.

Bonga points consolidation for corporate accounts.

Goodwill allocation of airtime to a customer account upon authorization by the Manager

# **How to perform Manual Adjustment.**

- For manual adjustment to be done an SR shall be sent by the CEE indicating the issue the customer is facing.
- Support Analyst shall then confirm and validate the complaint as indicated on the SR using systems available, CRM, MPESA G2 and BSS.
- On assessment of the Service Request, it shall indicate whether the manual adjustment shall be undertaken on either;

- Airtime account adjustment
- Bonga Points account adjustment for Individual lines
- Bonga Points account adjustment for Corporate lines.
- For each successful Bonga or Airtime adjustment, there will be an automatic Interaction created on CRM.

# **Airtime Account adjustment**

- Support analyst shall first calculate to know the amount to be adjusted manually.
- Support analyst shall expire the resources purchased and acquired from the transaction done and if any Bonga points were awarded in this case shall be clawed back.
- Support Analyst shall initiate a refund process of the airtime on CRM by clicking on TASKS on SR level and selecting Manual Adjustment Tab, then under Adjustment Type, select Airtime, fill in all the information correctly and submit.
- If the amount is less than Ksh 5000 it will be auto approved and the amount adjusted to the customer’s account.
- For amount above Ksh.5000, the activity shall be automatically allocated to support manager’s queue.
- Support Manager shall pick the activity, validate the request and approve or cancel.
- If the request is cancelled on CRM, the support manager shall indicate the reasons for this.
- Support analyst shall check periodically of the status. If cancelled, the analyst shall adjust the request to the specifications required of the request and re-submit for approval.
- For refund to M-PESA, Support analyst shall refund an equivalent amount of airtime using M-PESA Organization 316764 system.
- Under transaction services, analyst shall select *business payment to customer*, then shall specify that payment is made to MSISDN, indicate amount to be paid, give a brief description as to the reason for refund and submit for disbursement.
- Analyst shall then notify a colleague to verify the request of refund and complete. Once the transaction is completed the customer’s account is credited.
- The Analyst shall then advise the customer of the refund and close the Service Request.

# **Bonga Points account adjustment for Individual Lines**

- Bonga points adjustment for individual lines shall be done for reversal of either Lipa Na Bonga transactions or Bonga point resource purchases.
- For Lipa Na Bonga transactions the Analyst shall confirm if the transaction was completed, cancelled or Declined on M-PESA G2.
- For completed Lipa Na Bonga transactions the Analyst will seek consent from the Merchant to reverse.
- If Merchant declines, no reversal will be done. Analyst will communicate to the customer and Close the SR
- Where consent is given the Analyst will reverse the transaction on CRM *under Bonga Everywhere* tab and this will automatically;

Reverse the transaction on G2.

Reverse Bonga points to the customers Bonga account.

Populate an automatic interaction on CRM.

- The Analyst shall confirm the above has happened, advise the customer and close the SR.
- If reversal under *Bonga Everywhere* tab fails to deduct Bonga points from the customer’s account, the Analyst shall initiate the Manual Adjustment process.

- For cancelled or declined transactions the Analyst shall confirm the points deducted and initiate the Manual Adjustment process.
- For Bonga Points resource Purchases, Support Analyst shall expire the resources purchased and initiate the Manual Adjustment process.
- Support Analyst shall initiate a Manual Adjustment process of the Bonga on CRM by clicking on TASKS on SR level and selecting Manual Adjustment Tab, then under Adjustment Type, select Bonga, fill in all the information correctly and submit.
- If the amount is less than 15000 Bonga points it will be auto approved and the amount adjusted to the customer’s account.
- For amount above 15000 Bonga points, the activity shall be automatically allocated to support manager’s queue.
- Support Manager shall pick the activity, validate the request and approve or cancel.
- If the request is cancelled on CRM, the support manager shall indicate the reasons for this.
- Support analyst shall check periodically of the status. If cancelled, the analyst shall adjust the request to the specifications required of the request and re-submit for approval.
- Once approval process is completed by the Manager the amount of Bonga points shall be automatically credited into customer’s account.
- The Analyst shall then advise the customer of the adjustment and the Service Request shall be closed.

# **Bonga Point Adjustment for Corporate Lines.**

- Support Analyst shall receive the request to consolidate Bonga points via a service request.
- The Analyst shall confirm that the customer’s written request is attached on the Service Request and the email is from the customer’s registered email address on CRM OR there is a duly signed Bonga Consolidation form from the Company’s contact person.
- Support Analyst shall initiate a Manual Adjustment process of the Bonga points on *CBS LMS* tab on CRM by deducting points from the donor’s account/s.
- To credit the recipient’s number, the Analyst/Agent shall raise SR on the receiving MSISDN then perform a Manual Adjustment by clicking on TASKS on SR level and selecting Manual Adjustment Tab, then under Adjustment Type, select Bonga, fill in all the information correctly and submit. Support Analyst/Agent shall attach all the necessary documents on the SR, duly  
 signed Bonga Consolidation form from the Company’s contact person.
- If the amount is less than 15000 Bonga points it will be auto approved and the amount adjusted to the recipient’s account.
- For amount above 15000 Bonga points, the activity shall be automatically allocated to support manager’s queue.
- Support Manager shall pick the activity, validate the request and approve or cancel.
- If the request is cancelled on CRM, the support manager shall indicate the reasons for this.
- Support analyst shall check periodically of the status. If cancelled, the analyst shall adjust the request to the specifications required of the request and re-submit for approval.
- Once approval process is completed by the Manager the amount of Bonga points shall be automatically adjusted on recipient’s account.
- The Analyst shall then advise the customer and close the SR.

**Prepaid Business Fiber**

This is a business connectivity service available to customers on prepay payment model. No deposits required. Customers make payments when they need connectivity. Customer is available for renewal if the break between subscriptions does not exceed 90 days.

**Where can I get Prepaid Business Fiber**

Any business in select safaricom fiber ready buildings who do not require formal invoices and receipts for their business operations. This service is best suited for customer who require basic internet access. Those who require additional services, like Static IPs, will need to subscribe to our post-pay services.

# Eligibility

All new and existing customers who have branches/businesses in the qualifying fiber ready buildings.

# Signing up for Prepaid Business Fiber

New customers will be required to provide copy of National Identity card for the new service.

Existing customers will only be required to give a copy of their National ID for the new service.

# Billing for Prepaid Business Fiber

You will be paying for service before you use. Billing will be on anniversary date basis, a monthly cycle. You shall determine when your month starts and ends by the day you make a payment. For instance, if you make a payment on 15th your month shall start then and end on the 15th day of the next month. During these monthly cycles, the next expiry, your anniversary date, shall always be on a date one month from the date of last payment.

# How to pay for Prepaid Business Fiber

Customers will make payments through M-PESA. Other payments methods may be introduced in the life of the solution, customers will be notified when these are available.

# Prepaid Business Fiber not paid

You will be suspended on your anniversary date if no payment has been done for renewal on the 30th day of service. You can pay on anniversary or prepay before the date of expiry. If you do not make any payment, your link will remain suspended.

Your connection shall remain suspended for up to 90 days after the date of the last payment. Thereafter, you shall be required to apply for the service afresh should you need to use the service again.

# How to upgrade or downgrade packages on Prepaid Business Fiber

You can downgrade and upgrade the service via USSD \*485#. This will be available when making payments on anniversary or at renewal date.

# Support

In case of challenges, a customer shall have access to reach Safaricom Business support teams through email to business.support@safaricom.co.ke or make a call to Line 2222.

articleTitle: Retail Center Support & Escalations for M-PESA CUSTOMER ACCOUNT
markdownContent:
# **Migration to a Higher Tier**

Customer will visit a Safaricom Retail Shop and fill in a registration form. They will be required to carry the following:

- - A copy of their identification document as per M-PESA G2 system.
 - A copy of the KRA PIN Certificate. 

- Newly registering M-PESA customers and existing M-PESA customers will check the Tier 2 request box on the registration form.
- To complete the registration customer will provide a clear copy of the identification document to migrate to tier 2.

## 

# **Frozen Account Status Retail Operations**

**Lines Frozen at Account Level.**

**For New lines: -**

- CEE will advise the customer to fill in the registration form and will scan their ID
- Then will raise an SR.
- Support will recycle and register the line within 24 hours.

**For Existing lines: -**

- CEE will confirm the reason for barring the number on audit logs and action as per the request.
- Where the reason is missing the CEE will confirm if the customer has multiple M-PESA account.
- **For multiple** account **the CEE** will advise the customer as per the M-PESA terms and conditions that a customer can only have two accounts,
- Issue them with the M-PESA freeze-unfreeze form them to fill and pick the preferred 2 account and unfreeze the preferred account and will freeze the other account at the account level.

## 

# **M-PESA Customer Suspended/Frozen Account Status Guideline**

- Safaricom Retail and Call Center Teams will no longer be changing the M-PESA **Accounts Identity Status** on M-PESA G2.
- If a customer calls for any freezing/suspending request these will actioned at the **Account Level** after effective vetting.
- Any M-PESA Account frozen/ suspended at Identity level will be as a result of suspicious activities pending/undergoing investigations by Safaricom Fraud.
- Safaricom AML will freeze accounts at the Account Level for multiple M-PESA registrations.

markdownContent:
# **Definition**

This is an enhancement that will enable customers buy NEO Voice bundles for Calls and SMS (Without Expiry) directly at Top Up without requiring them to do an extra step.

# **Eligibility**

All prepaid and hybrid customer who can top up their accounts using Voucher top up of all Denominations.

Only recharge via vouchers will be eligible.

## 

# **Key Features**

- The resources awarded will be based Calls & SMS without expiry. E.g. 20 Ksh voucher will give 30Ksh. Calls & SMS Bonus, which is **50% Extra.**

***‘Dear customer, your top-up has been deducted to pay your Okoa Jahazi debt. Please try again with a lower amount. Dial \*144# to check your current balance’***

- The bundles have no expiry, and the usage priority & rate will be the same as bundles without expiry on 544.
- EXTRA Talk time of 50% for Calls and SMS will be awarded on every Top-Up Voucher recharge via \*444\*Scratch card pin# only.
- Existing NEO Voice business rules will apply for EXTRA Talk time purchased through this new recharge journey.

## 

# **Purchase** **Mechanics**

- Customer are required to enter the voucher PIN i.e. \*444\*Voucher PIN#.
- EXTRA Talk time of 50% for Calls and SMS will be awarded on every Top-Up Voucher recharge via \*444\*Scratch card pin# only.
- Customers will be able to purchase Neo Voice bundles directly using Recharge vouchers via a simplified customer Journey i.e. **\*444\*Scratch card pin#.** This will commence **0000 hours 14th JUNE 2020**.

articleTitle: M-TIBA Service Definition, Requirements and Mechanics
markdownContent:
# **Definition**

1. M-TIBA is a mobile health wallet. This is a service on your mobile phone that allows you to set funds aside for healthcare. Funds stored in M-TIBA can only be used to pay for services and medication at specific healthcare facilities which carry the M-TIBA logo.
2. People can top-up and receive funds specifically intended for healthcare in the wallet and spend this money at designated healthcare providers.
3. M-TIBA is an initiative of Safaricom, Pharm Access Foundation and Care Pay.

# **Eligibility**

Anyone who is a Safaricom customer above the age of 18 years is eligible to register on M-TIBA.

# **Required Documents for registration**

1. Must have a duly registered Safaricom SIM card that is enabled for M-PESA usage and be a holder of a valid national identity card or a valid passport.
2. Additionally, you will need to accept M-TIBA Terms and Conditions on registration.

# **Healthcare facilities participating in M-TIBA**

1. M-TIBA works with a large network of healthcare providers.
2. Inquire for M-TIBA agent for a list of healthcare facilities participating in M-TIBA in the area or call our Toll-Free line on 0800 721253 or visit www.mtiba.co.ke to see a list of healthcare facilities**.**
3. Participating healthcare facilities will carry the M-TIBA logo for easier recognition.

# **Healthcare Services Provided**

1. M-TIBA funds can be used to pay for outpatient healthcare services and medication.
2. The indicative cost of consultation at healthcare facilities participating in M-TIBA in Nairobi is between 200 Ksh and 400 Ksh per person per visit. This excludes the costs of drugs and/or tests that may be prescribed by the doctor. Prices may vary depending on the healthcare facility selected.
3. The range of outpatient services paid for depends on the services chosen M-TIBA facility can provide and on the amount of funds stored in M-TIBA account.
4. Users are encouraged to save as much as possible to be able to pay for healthcare services in full.

# **Regions covered by M-TIBA facilities**

The full list of Regions covered by the M-Tiba facilities is as indicated on the provided link here :[http://m-tiba.co.ke/facility](http://m-tiba.co.ke/facility)

# **Difference between M-TIBA and M-PESA**

1. M-TIBA enables users to set funds aside specifically for healthcare use while M-PESA is a mobile money transfer service.
2. There is no deposit limit on M-TIBA while deposits in M-PESA have a limit.
3. Funds in M-TIBA are dedicated for healthcare use while use of M-PESA deposits is open.
4. Healthcare providers contracted by M-TIBA are checked for quality, availability and cost of services and are committed to better healthcare.

# **Funds Security /Personal Data Security**

1. Funds stored in M-TIBA will stay safe.
2. M-TIBA is secured with a PIN which should be known only to the customer. Do not share the PIN with anyone.
3. The funds stored in M-TIBA are managed by UAP. UAP is a licensed Insurance company and a medical scheme fund manager regulated by the Insurance Regulatory Authority of Kenya.
4. All information/data in our system is secure and protected using the highest standards.

# **Charges to send money to relative or friend through M-TIBA**

1. M-TIBA does not charge any fees for this service.
2. The only applicable charges are the standard M-PESA charge for transferring money to other M-PESA users. The official M-PESA charges are available here: [http://www.safaricom.co.ke/personal/m-pesa/get-started-with-m-pesa/m-pesa-tariffs](http://www.safaricom.co.ke/personal/m-pesa/get-started-with-m-pesa/m-pesa-tariffs)

# **Registration/Sign up** **Process**

1. Simply dial \*253# to register
2. An M-TIBA agent can assist to register
3. Registration can be done from any of the facilities that carry the M-TIBA logo
4. Registration can also be done by calling the Toll-Free line 0800 721253.

N/B: A Customer can only register one M-TIBA Account.

# **Amending Personal details**

1. Make sure details provided are correct details during registration.
2. If noted that certain details are wrong, please call the M-TIBA Toll Free line on 0800 721253 or email customercare@mtiba.co.ke.

# **Funds Transfer Process from M-PESA to M-TIBA**

## One can transfer money into their wallet and other people’s wallet using the procedures below:

# **Transferring for self**

1. Step 1 - Go to M-PESA menu
2. Step 2 - Select Lipa Na M-PESA
3. Step 3 - Select PayBill option
4. Step 4 - Enter business number: 300066
5. Step 5 - Enter “M-Tiba” as the Number
6. Step 6 - Enter amount you wish to transfer to your M-TIBA
7. Step 7 – Click OK to confirm details
8. Step 8 - Receive a confirmation SMS from M-PESA
9. Step 9 - Receive a confirmation SMS from M-TIBA

# **Transferring for others**

1. Go to M-PESA menu
2. Choose Pay with M-PESA
3. Choose Pay Bill and enter number 500066
4. Enter the phone number of your relative or friend as Account Number, e.g. 0712345678
5. Enter your M-PESA pin to complete payment.

**N/B:** All transactions from M-PESA to M-TIBA are free of charge.

# **Checking M-TIBA balance**

1. Dial \*253#
2. Enter M-TIBA PIN (or press 1 if you have forgotten your PIN)
3. Select option 2: "My MTIBA"
4. Available products will be displayed along with the available balances

# **Accessing M-TIBA wallet**

1. Dial \*253#
2. Enter M-TIBA PIN (enter 1 in case you have forgotten to reset)
3. Reply with:
4. Get treatment (enter clinic number to get treatment)
5. My M-TIBA Benefits (shows balance)
6. Find Clinic (location dependent)
7. Settings (has the following)

Reply with:

1. 1.Change PIN
2. 2.Add Dependent
3. 3.Next of Kin
4. 4.Leave program
5. 5.SMS Opt Out

# **Changing/Resetting M-TIBA PIN**

1. Step 1 - Dial \*253#
2. Step 2 – Enter M-TIBA PIN
3. Step 3 - Select option 9 “Settings”
4. Step 4 – Select Option 1: “Change PIN”
5. Step 5 - Enter Current PIN
6. Step 6 - Enter New PIN
7. Step 7 – Confirm New PIN

The Customer will receive an SMS notification confirming PIN change “Your PIN has been changed”.

# **Required Process while at the M-Tiba Provider facilities**

1. Dial \*253#
2. Select Option 1: to login in as a member
3. Enter MTIBA password (PIN number as was received from Registration SMS)
4. Select Option 1: to authorize provider to bill the wallet
5. My Wallets: Choose MTIBA wallet
6. Enter Provider till Number
7. Choose which dependant is being treated
8. Receive a transaction number by SMS
9. Get Treated
10. Your National ID will be asked by the clinic for confirmation during billing.

# **Authorizing treatment using M-TIBA**

1. Dial \*253#
2. Enter your M-TIBA PIN (or press 1 if you have forgotten your PIN)
3. Press 1 to Register a get treatment
4. Select recent clinic (1, 2, 3) or enter Till Number of clinic you’re visiting (e.g. 465004)
5. Press 1 to Authorize
6. You will receive an SMS message with a transaction number.

N/B: A customer can authorize his/her billing from where they are, provided they are able to communicate with them about the “provider number” (till number) to which the funds have to be transferred.

# **Bingwa sokoni on zuri**

To grow self-service uptake on our channels; via increased usage on **ZURI on WhatsApp** and **VB** users, we are glad to introduce an **Enhancement** on **Bingwa** **Sokoni.**

Partners can now recommend customers to enroll to:

Jitambulishe

ZURI on WhatsApp

and earn **KShs.15 commission** for every successful enrolment in Jitambulishe or ZURI on WhatsApp**.**

# **How it works:**

The customer walks into a partner outlet (M-PESA Agent or dealer shop)

The agent recommends Jitambulishe **or** ZURI enrollment via **\*180\*5#,** dial ok.

Agent selects sell Jitambulishe or chat with ZURI and enter customer’s number.

Both the Agent and notification success message; customer’s notification advises them to call 456/click on ZURI link to enroll.

Agents earn KSh.15 via M-PESA weekly once the customer enrolls within 48hrs.

If the customer doesn’t enroll within 48hrs, the recommendation expires, calling for another recommendation

# **Key Features:**

M-PESA Agent |Dealer needs to register commission Payout number before they can recommend customer to enroll Jitambulishe/ZURI enrolment.

The commission is paid to the agent commission payout number once a week for all successful enrolments.

Recommended customer to enroll within 48 hours otherwise the agent will not be paid the customer.

Only customers who are not enrolled can be recommended for enrollment to Jitambulishe/Zuri

Customers can only be recommended once within 48 hours. This helps minimize the possibility of customers receiving multiple SMS.

Customers who delete their voiceprint on IVR will not be eligible to be recommended again.

Customers who will not be enrolled after 48 hours are eligible to be recommended by another agent and if successfully enrolled after, the new agent will get the commission.

# **Sell zuri/ jitambulishe on bingwa sokoni campaign faq’s**

What is Sell Zuri /Jimbulishe on Bingwa sokoni ? This a Zuri acquisition campaign whereby an M-PESA agent or dealer is rewarded with an incentive of 15/- for recommending customers to self-serve via Zuri on WhatsApp. The campaign aims at increasing awareness and uptake of self-service menus within Zuri.

How much will the MPESA agents and dealers get in the sell Zuri/Jitambulishe on Bingwa sokoni campaign? Upon successful referrals and Customers authenticate their numbers and self\[1\]serve, the agents/dealer will get 15/-

Who is eligible for sell Zuri/Jitambulishe on bingwa sokoni campaign? All M-Pesa agents and dealers who have activated the Bingwa Sokoni service.

# **User  Journey to sell Zuri/Jitambulishe on Bingwa sokoni**

The dealer/Agent dials \*180# and selects Bingwa sokoni >Sell Jitambulishe/Zuri. Selling Jitambulishe

The dealer/Agent selects sell jitambulishe option and they enter the customer’s number and submits. Customer receives a link via SMS informing them that they have recommended by agent to enroll to jitambulishe by dialing 456. Customer dials 456 and follows the prompts to enroll to jitambulishe. Selling Zuri

The dealer/Agent selects sell Zuri option and they enter the customer’s number and submits.

Customer receives a link via SMS which they click on and directs them to zuri on whatsapp.

Customer initiates a conversation i.e. by typing ‘hi’.

The customer will need to select specific menus i.e. Manage Subscriptions, Usage & M-PESA statement, Airtime top up, buy bundles, Safaricom Home & Bill manager, Check Balance etc. provide his / her mobile number & enter the One Time Pin (OTP) sent via text of STK Push to be authenticated. (based on the journey)

The Agent/Dealer educates the customer and ends the conversation.

The agent earns the 15/- incentive Upon successful enrolment to Jitambulishe or successful authentication on Zuri.

The agent or dealer will be awarded only when the customer is authenticated via mobile number.

The agent/dealer will not be able to refer to a customer who is already using zuri, upon keying in the customer MSISDN, they will get message” sorry customer is already active on Zuri/Jitambulishe”

An agent can recommend the same MSISDN Once in 48hrs.

Zuri does not have an opt out option. If your delete your voice in jitambulishe, you cannot get referred again.

Bingwa sokoni payments are done every Sunday. Billing period is Sunday to Saturday(7days) The reward will be accumulated and paid out as a lump sum to the partner of assistant (the one who recommended the service) every week as cash via M-PESA.

If they do not receive the weekly payments, Normal escalation for Bingwa Sokoni escalations will be followed.

# **Definition Shiriki Prepay Airtime**

This It is a **Prepay Plan** that Business Owners and or Customers (referred to as Sponsors) can share communication resources depending on their changing requirements for calling, browsing and SMS. For Business owners and customer.

# **Buying Shiriki Prepay Airtime**

By Dialing \*234\*11# and select the plan as per their communication needs.

# **More about Shiriki Prepay Airtime Sponsor and Beneficiary.**

A **sponsor** is the customer/business owner that buys the plans.

All Airtime resources sit on the sponsors wallet.

A sponsor can **share the airtime** with others-Referred to as **Beneficiaries**.

Sponsors can share their Airtime with up to **14 beneficiaries.** (Please note this is not Sambaza)

Beneficiaries enjoy the discounted rates based on the Sponsors Plan.

A beneficiary can only be attached to only one Sponsor.

Sponsors can also choose to use the Airtime alone without sharing.

A beneficiary shall only use their allocation from the sponsor’s line. If they (beneficiary) exhaust the allocation, then priority of usage shifts to any other resources they may have.

Should the Sponsor deplete their resources, they will utilize the resources of the beneficiary since all resources sit with the Sponsor.

The Sponsor will also be able to remove beneficiaries and check their balance.

# **Charges and plans**

There are 6 plans as below.

Access to highly subsidized as below.

| Package Name | No. of Users (Including sponsor) | Voice per Min(KES) | International Calling Zone A**(KES) | Data per MB (KES) | SMS(KES) | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Shiriki Ksh 1,500 | 15 | 2 | 3 | 0.12 | 0.03 | |
| Shiriki Ksh 3,000 | 1.25 | 3 | 0.11 | 0.03 | | |
| Shiriki Ksh 4,500 | 1.25 | 3 | 0.09 | 0.02 | | |
| Shiriki Ksh 6,300 | 1.25 | 3 | 0.09 | 0.02 | | |
| Shiriki Ksh 9,000 | 1.25 | 3 | 0.09 | 0.02 | | |
| Shiriki Ksh 13,500 | 1.25 | 3 | 0.09 | 0.02 | | |
| | | | | | | |

# **Validity of the plans**

The plans are valid for 30days from the Date Of Purchase.

All the unused resources expire at the end the 30days validity. There is no rollover.

# **Resources Allocation**

The Sponsor gets the full Airtime Resources as per the plan bought. Please note that there is **no Proration of Resources.**

# **Purchase modes and Frequency of plans purchase**

A Sponsor can buy the plans via:

**Buy Once:** M-PESA, Airtime or Fuliza.

**Auto Renew:** Airtime Only

PostPay Customers are not eligible to purchase the plans. They will get a clear notification should they try to purchase the plans.

**To access** **Internet**

Advise the Sponsor to deactivate My Data Manager for them to use the Shiriki PrePay airtime. This is because My Data Manager works with Bundles and not Airtime. Please remind the Customer to reactivate My Data Manager should they deplete their Shiriki Airtime and revert to other bundles.

# **Okoa Jahazi outstanding Debt**

Customers will be able to buy  the service if they have an okoa debt.

- For sponsors/customers purchasing the plans for the first time, they will get a notification to first pay their OKOA loan after which they can purchase.
- For subsequent purchases, when the sponsor buys the plans, they will get a prompt to pay the outstanding Okoa on the same purchase journey-Refer to the attached customer journey.

# **Support**

Sponsors can call business support by calling 2222 or 200 or email to businesssupport@safaricom.co.ke and most importantly, their Sales Manager in EBU.

Beneficiaries retain their respective support line as 100.

# **Service Change (termination, upgrade, or downgrade)**

Should a sponsor require a different plan, all they need to do is purchase it by dialing \*234\*11#.

**Kindly note**:

Sponsor can only purchase another similar plan when they have exhausted their current Shiriki Prepay Airtime.

Any attempt to purchase a higher or lower plan before exhausting their resources, the Sponsor gets the below notification:

*You can only buy a higher or lower Shiriki PrePay Plan after the current one expires on dd/mm/yyyy. To buy the current Ksh 1,500 Shiriki Prepay Airtime:*

*Proceed (Progress with the existing purchase journey)*

*Cancel- Send this message. Your request has been cancelled. For more information on Shiriki Prepay Airtime, Dial \***234**\*11# & Select ‘How It Works*

 Should a customer require to buy a higher or lower plan, they will have to wait for the 30days expire period to elapse.

Any attempt to purchase a higher or lower plan before expiry of the current plan, the Sponsor gets the below notification:

*Your current Shiriki Prepay Airtime is Ksh 00,000. You can only buy another Shiriki Plan when your Shiriki Prepay Airtime is 0. Dial \***234**\*11# to check balance.*

# **Setting Limit via USSD**

Dial \*234\*11#, Select ‘**Add Beneficiary**, Enter the **Beneficiary Number**, **Nick Name** and **Limit.**

A beneficiary can only enjoy Shiriki rates up to the allocated amounts. After exhausting the assigned limit, they (Beneficiary) shall need to top up and be charged prevailing rates on Uwezo.

# **Front Facing Team Add Beneficiary on CRM VBC**

For the Front Facing Team, if the calling number is the sponsors number or customer visiting the retail centre is the sponsor (follow your vetting process at retail for verification of ownership), then the Front Facing team can add a benefiary on the sponsors line via the SHIRIKI VBC on behalf of the customer. Please guide the customer on the DIY procedure after assiting them.

**Notifications**

| Beneficiary MSISDN entered is not of the correct length | Dear Customer, You have entered an Invalid Number. Please ensure that the number starts with a zero(0) and the length of the number is 10. Thank you |
| Beneficiary MSISDN entered does not exist (Example an Competitor MSISDN) | Dear Customer, the number you have entered does not exist. Please ensure that you enter a Safaricom number. Thank you |
| Beneficiary MSISDN entered is not active (Example the MSISDN is not active on our systems) | Dear Customer, the number could not be added as a beneficiary at the moment. Please reconfirm the number with the beneficiary. Thank you. |
| Beneficiary MSISDN entered is already on Shiriki | Dear Customer, the number is already on Shiriki. Please try another number. Thank you |
| Internal Technical Error (In cases of a system outage) | Dear Customer, we are currently unable to add the beneficiary. Please try again later. Thank you. |

# **Removing a Beneficiary on behalf of the Sponsor**

CEE can After confirming ownership of the Sponsors Line, use the Shiriki VBC on Siebel. *Refer to the attachment on the Shiriki Sponsor VBC.*

**Note** 

A Sponsor/Beneficiary  can top Up Airtime should they exhaust their plan/limit

**A sponsor/Beneficiary cannot use the Shiriki Airtime for PRS’s and other Premium Rate Services**

This is because the Shiriki Airtime is highly discounted, and the Premium Rate Services are priced higher. Advise the sponsor/Beneficiary to Top Up should they wish to utilize those services.

# **How to remove beneficiaries- Sponsor**

By Dial \*234\*11#, then select “**Remove Beneficiary**” option and Select the Beneficiary they intend to Remove.

# **Stop Auto-Renew**

Sponsor will dial \*234\*11# and Select Stop Auto-Renew.

# **Sambaza**

The plan does not allow Sambaza airtime. The plan only allows sharing resources with selected beneficiaries by allocating them a limit.

# **checking my balance as a Shiriki sponsor**

By dialing USSD code \*234\*11# and selecting the “Check Balance” option and select sponsor number.

# **checking my balance as a Shiriki beneficiary**

The Beneficiary is currently not able to check their balance via USSD.

The Sponsor can however check balance for beneficiaries under their Shiriki Plan.

# **Usage Prioritization for Shiriki PrePay plans**

Shorter validity Airtime are used first. Example, if a sponsor has a 24hour Airtime validity, that will be used before the 30day Shiriki Prepay Airtime.

# **Roaming**

The resources cannot be used while roaming 

# **International Calls with the Shiriki Prepay Airtime**

The International Calling is supported for only Zone A (India, China, Canada and USA). Normal international calling rates apply for all other countries.

**Buying data bundles via \*544# if I am on the Shiriki Prepay Airtime Plan**

Customers can top-up their line with normal airtime and other buy data bundles via \*544#.

# **Definition**

# 4G/5G self service router activation is a three-step process to enjoy Safaricom Home Wi-Fi service on 4G or 5G router. To enjoy the service, you will be required to

Buy 4G/5G router and set it up.

Scan QR code to register SIM card and activate account.

Purchase bundles/package to enjoy Wi-Fi service.

# **Availability**

You can visit any Safaricom retail shop, authorised Safaricom dealer, Masoko.com or selected outlets to purchase a router.

# **Charges**

The 4G and 5G routers available subject to stock availability are:

| Description | Model Number | Cost Ksh |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 4G Router | Huawei LTE Indoor CPE B320-923 | 2,999 |
| 5G Router | Huawei H155-382 Indoor 5G CPE | 10,999 |
| 5G Router | Nokia Gateway 2 5G19-01W-A | 11,999 |

# **Activation**

Once you get the router, the SIM card will be attached on the side of the router box.

Detach the SIM pouch and Scan the QR code on the back of the pouch.

Follow the instructions to register the new line.

You will receive a One Time Password (OTP) on your Safaricom number. Enter the OTP and accept terms and conditions to proceed with account activation. You can resend the OTP three times if the time expires before you input it. After three tries, you will need to wait for 10 minutes before you try again.

Once account is activated, you will receive a notification on your mobile number that activation is successful.

# **How to scan QR code**

- Open your camera app: Most modern smartphones have built-in QR code scanners. Simply open your camera app.
- Point your camera at the QR code: Make sure the QR code is clearly visible and centred in the camera's viewfinder.
- Wait for the scanner to recognize the code: Your phone's camera app should automatically detect the QR code and display a notification or prompt.
- Tap the notification or prompt: This will usually open the link or content associated with the QR code.
- If your phone doesn't have a built-in QR code scanner, you can download a dedicated QR code reader app from your app store.

# **Activation**

The activation process typically takes just a few minutes. Just follow the prompts on the guided process and the activation should complete. Should this not happen please contact us for assistance at the nearest Safaricom or Safaricom Dealer shop of call 100, 200 or 400.

# **Error during line registration and account activation**

If you encounter an error, make a note of the error message and restart the activation process. If the problem continues, consult the troubleshooting section in the user manual or visit the nearest Safaricom or Safaricom Dealer shop or contact us on 100, 200 or 400 for assistance.

# **Router Setup**

To activate your router, you will need to disable the SIM card pin on a different phone using the instructions below.

- Remove the SIM from the pouch and insert into a phone.
- *Access settings*: Open your phone's settings app
- *Find security lock or lock screen*: Look for a section named "Security," "Lock Screen," or something similar.
- *Locate SIM card options*: Within the security settings, you should find options related to SIM cards.
- *Disable SIM card lock*: Look for a setting called "SIM card lock," "SIM PIN," or something similar. Toggle this setting to "Off" or disable it.
- *Enter PIN (if required)*: You might need to enter your current SIM card PIN to confirm the change.

Once done insert the SIM card into the designated slot on your router.

- Locate the SIM card slot on your router. It's usually on the side or bottom.
- Carefully insert your SIM card into the slot, ensuring it's properly aligned.

Connect the router to a power source and follow the user manual provided in the box.

i.        Plug the power adapter into the router and then into a power outlet.

ii.        The router's power light should illuminate.

Connect to the Wi-Fi using the username and password provided at the bottom of your router.  Once you’re connected to the router’s Wi-Fi network, you can enjoy the service. 

# **If the SIM card is not recognised**

If your SIM card isn’t recognized, try removing and reinserting it. Ensure it’s properly seated in the slot. If the issue persists, contact customer support on 400.

# **Can’t connect to the Wi-Fi network after activation.**

Ensure your device is connected to the correct Wi-Fi network and that you’ve entered the correct password. If you still can’t connect, restart the router and your device, and try again. If issues persist, contact us on 400

# **Can I activate my router without an internet connection**

Yes, the activation process can typically be completed without an existing internet connection, as the router uses the SIM card to connect to the network. Follow the prompts as guided once you successfully scan the QR code.

# **Can I use any SIM card with my router**

This router is designed to work with specific SIM cards from our network. Using a different provider's SIM card will not work.

**Does the router come with any free resources 
**Yes, you will receive free 30GB upon successful account activation for your 4G router.

# **Packages**

Purchase 4G Wi-Fi bundles on MySafaricom app or dial \*400\*3# and select Buy plan

| Price Ksh | Bundle volume | Validity |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 499 | 7.5GB | 7 Days |
| 999 | 25GB | 30 Days |
| 1,999 | 60GB | 30 Days |
| 2,999 | 140GB | 30 Days |
| 4,100 | 180GB | 30 Days |
| 6,299 | 250GB | 30 Days |
| 12,499 | 500GB | 30 Days |

Purchase 5G Wi-Fi bundles on mySafaricom app or dial \*400\*4# and select Buy plan

| Price Ksh | Bundle volume | Validity |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 3499 | 400GB | 30 Days |
| 5999 | 25GB | 30 Days |
| 9999 | 1500GB | Days |

# **Can I use my 4G/5G bundles anywhere?**

4G Wi-Fi bundles will only be usable in places where there is good 4G coverage and will work only on the 4G Router.

5G Wi-Fi bundles will only be usable in places where there is good 5G/4G coverage and will work only on the 5G Router.

# **How to get account number**

The account number is the mobile number of the SIM in the router. The mobile number will be printed on the back of the SIM pouch.

# **How to check if account is active**

For 4G router:

Simply dial \*400\*3# and select Check Account Status

For 5G router:

Simply dial \*400\*4\*2 and select Check Account Status

# **4G Wi-Fi Bundle Renewal**

To renew the 4G Wi-Fi Internet package, you can Visit MySafaricom App and select 4G Wi-Fi or follow the instructions below:

Dial \*400# and select "4G Wi-Fi"

Select "Buy 4G Plans"

Select the "Account number"

Select 4G plan to renew

Select your preferred mode of payment i.e. M-PESA or Postpay/Credit Limit

If you select M-PESA, you will be prompted to enter your 4-digit M-PESA PIN.

Upon successful purchase, you will receive a flash notification of successful payment and a confirmation SMS will be sent to your Mobile number.

Alternatively, you can load airtime directly to the SIM number, Dial \*141\* recharge code\*Router SIM card number#

You can buy a new 4G Wi-Fi bundle once you exhaust your current allocation.

# **5G Wi-Fi Bundle Renewal**

To renew the 4G Wi-Fi Internet package, you can Visit MySafaricom App and select 4G Wi-Fi or follow the instructions below:

Dial \*400# and select "5G Wi-Fi"

Select "Buy 5G Plans"

Select the "Account number"

Select 5G plan to renew

Select your preferred mode of payment i.e. M-PESA or Postpay/Credit Limit

If you select M-PESA, you will be prompted to enter your 4-digit M-PESA PIN.

Upon successful purchase, you will receive a flash notification of successful payment and a confirmation SMS will be sent to your Mobile number.

Alternatively, you can load airtime directly to the SIM number, Dial \*141\* recharge code\*Router SIM card number#

You can buy a new 5G Wi-Fi bundle once you exhaust your current allocation.

# **Can I use the SIM card in the router on my phone**

No, the router SIM will only work on your designated router.

# **Does the 4G/5G Home Wi-Fi require a password**

Yes, username and password (WI-FI KEY) is printed on the back/bottom of the Router.

# **How to reset router**

Locate the reset button on the router (usually a small pinhole) and press it for about 10 seconds using a paperclip or similar object. This will reset the router to factory settings.

After resetting, try the activation process again.

Resetting the router will erase all customized settings, including Wi-Fi names and passwords. You will need to reconfigure the router after the reset.

# **What should I do if I lose my SIM card**

If you lose your SIM card, contact customer support immediately to report it. They will help you deactivate the lost SIM. You can then get a replacement of the SIM card at the nearest Safaricom or Safaricom Dealer Shop.

# **Support**

For assistance, please call 400 from the number that you used to pay for the service.

Alternatively, you can send an email to [safaricomhome@safaricom.co.ke](mailto:safaricomhome@safaricom.co.ke).

You can also reach us on social media:

1\. Twitter: @Safaricom\_Care

2\. Facebook: Safaricom PLC
