# **Definition**

M-PESA Float is the amount of money that an M-PESA agent is required to have in their till to perform M-PESA transactions.

# **How It Works**

Agents are required to maintain a monthly average float balance of Ksh.20,000 on the minimum failure to which, their tills are suspended for a minimum period of one week.

Agents will need to top-up their float to facilitate resumption, which is done after the

Suspension period is over.

Agents whose till float balance are not topped up by the time the suspension period is over, shall not be resumed, until they add their float.

# **Float** **M****anagement Movement**

Float movement refers to the in and out moving of float to other branches by the head offices.

MPESA agents enquiring about float movement in and out of their branches to contact their head office contact person.

The head offices are trained on float management and are equipped with a website and handset to facilitate this activity.

For cases where the agent has waited for more than 6 hours for the head office to move their float, advise the agent to send an SMS message to the number **0714628628** to request for the float movement.

The details below are required: -

M-PESA agent outlet name and location

The agent number (e.g., 12345)

The agent outlet mobile number

Advise the agent that the SLA is 2hrs.

**NOTE:**  No other issues e.g., reversals, start key requests etc. should be sent via the cchannel **0714628628**

# **Float movement procedure**

Moving money from Working Account to Float Account (Can only be done by the primary assistant)

Primary Assistant will go to

M-PESA Menu

Chose Move Money

Choose from Working to Float

Enter the amount.

Enter your agent ID and secret PIN.

Moving money from Float Account to Working Account

M-PESA Menu

Choose Move Money

Choose from Float to Working

Enter the amount.

Enter your agent ID and secret PIN.

# **Business withdrawal**

Business withdrawal is initiated by the business customer (MPESA Agent) when withdrawing float to get cash from a Super-agent.

Go to M-PESA Menu

Go to Business services.

choose business withdrawal.

Enter the super Agent’s agent number (this is the super agent’s till

number)

Enter amount.

Enter agent ID and secret PIN.

Both the Agent and the Super-Agent will get a confirmation SMS

# **The Amount of Float an M-PESA Agent can hold.**

Below are the rule bands of how much float an M-PESA Agent can hold.

| Bands | Maximum Hold Amount |
| --- | --- |
| Rule Band A | 150,000 |
| Rule Band B | Ksh. 250,000 |
| Rule Band C | Ksh. 500,000 |
| Rule Band D | Ksh. 1 million |
| Rule Band E | Ksh. 1.5 million |
| Rule Band F | Ksh. 2.5 million |
| Rule Band G | Ksh. 5 million |

# **How To Identify on G2**

To view the agent band, Click Rule profile hyperlink (blue in colour)  

 [Screenshot] 

The screen below will appear, and the band maximum balance will be indicated on the right.

# **Change of account rule band**

The request to amend the rule band is made through the admin who raises a SR via the Dealer Portal and is effected by our team with an SLA 24Hrs.

Account rule band off a till affects the maximum float balance a till can hold.

To change rule band M-PESA head office should raise a service request on dealer portal.

articleTitle: M-PESA Start Key Process and DIY Procedures
markdownContent:
**M-PESA Start Key Process and DIY Procedures**

# **Definition**

M-PESA start key is a four-digit code used to access M-PESA services. One must input the codes before accessing M-PESA services.

M-PESA start key is a four-digit code issued to a customer to enable them to set a new and valid M-PESA pin.

# **Eligibility**

This is a service available for only registered Safaricom customers who have active M-PESA accounts.

# **Activating New M-PESA Account**

Upon M-PESA registration, customer is sent a start key via SMS to activate M-PESA account, by following below steps.

Go to M-PESA menu.

Select Activate or Wezesha.

Enter new M-PESA start key

Choose a new PIN (advise customer to a strong PIN they can easily remember, **avoid 0000 or 1234** **or Year of Birth)**

Confirm new PIN

Enter DOB or ID Number. (Same as registration document used).

Confirm by clicking ok.

# **Unlocking** **M-PESA PIN**

**DIY USSD Mechanics (Self Unlock)**

Dial **\*234# ok or** **\*334# or \*456# or \*100# ok**,

Select M-PESA PIN Manager

Select M-PESA PIN unlock

Enter your ID number

Press OK to unlock

**NOTE:** Customers can only use the option once per day. Customers have 2 chances to enter correct ID, on the 3rd wrong ID entry the customer will be locked out of the service for the day. This blacklisting will reset at midnight.

# **DIY IVR Self-Service Mechanics**

This is applicable to customers enrolled to Level 2 on Jitambulishe.

Dial the IVR (**100 or 234**)

Select the language of choice

Select the option for “M-PESA Services”

Select unlock pin option,

The procedure of unlocking M-PESA PIN on IVR

Unlock PIN

Put ID number

The M-PESA PIN will be unlocked and SMS sent

# **Forgot M-PESA Pin**

**For new line**

In case a customer registers for a new line but forgets to activate M-PESA account

Go to M-PESA menu

Select Activate / Wezesha

Enter Start key PIN (PIN issued by IVR or agent)

Enter new PIN (which can be the same PIN they had before)

Confirm new PIN

Enter DOB or ID No. \[Same as ID used for registration\].

Send the request to M-PESA by clicking on the Ok button.

**IVR process**

Dial the IVR (**100 or 234**)

Select the language of choice

Select the option for “M-PESA Services

Select forgot PIN option

Enter ID

Confirm whether you “Recently replaced your sim” and then select the “Forgot PIN” option.

Verify ownership by verbalizing the Jitambulishe pass phrase

Verification status is confirmed and instructions on how to use the Start-Key played back

If verification is successful, the Start-Key is sent via SMS… if voice verification fails after 3 attempts, customer is routed to an agent.

# **Changing M-PESA Pin After Sim Replacement**

Go to Safaricom menu

Select My account.

Select Change pin.

Enter Old pin (Existing pin).

Choose a New Pin or Repeat old pin.

Confirm chosen pin.

markdownContent:
# **M-PESA Agent Unable to Send and Receive**

This could be a network limitation problem or handset problem.

For network, this will get resolved once the network problem in the specific area is resolved by our engineers.

Escalate the issue via Siebel Service request using the categories below:

**Category**\-Network. 
**TYPE**\-SMS. 
**ITEM**\- Sending/receiving (select the desired category as per the case being escalated).

Short description- enters the location of the agent The date they start experiencing the problem Handset type and error message (if any)

Assign the service request to the MPESA support team to action. The SLA for network issue is **48 Hours.**

**Handset problem**

Advice the agent/customer to follow the steps below to resolve the problem.

**Step 1:**

Request the agent/customer to do an SMS balance inquiry to ensure that it's not a network problem.

If it is not, proceed to step 2.

**Step 2:**

The problem usually is that all M-PESA messages had been screened and to find them the agent needed to

Go to messages>select>

Scroll to screened messages>

Select and you will find all those messages.

To deactivate this feature.

Go to messages> select >

scroll to message settings> select >

scroll to No. screening option> select >

choose M-PESA > go to options >select >

Choose the delete number option.

**Step 3**

If it's a repeat call and the above procedures did not work.

Troubleshooting the issue with the steps below:

# **Network Check.**

Check if subscriber has enough network,

Low network bars request them to change locations

See if the SMS will be sent from a different location.

Full network bars, request them to do a location update and resend the SMS messages.

The handset may be out of the network range or the network is temporarily overloaded.

# **SMS Unbarring Procedure.**

If the line has no barring’s on Siebel

Give customer handset SMS unbarring procedure. #33\*0000\*16#ok.

**SMS set up Number. (+254722500029)**

Ask the agent to confirm the service centre that is saved their SIM card by reading it to you first.

For incorrect centre number, request them to write down the correct number

Store it in the message settings.

**Faulty Handset**

Confirm the type of handset for example, Sonny ericsson-T100 rejects some SIM cards.

Request them to retry sending the SMS using a different handset.

If the SMS is successful, they should take their handset to a dealer to run some tests and establish the problem.

# **HLR profile**

New SIM card, recreated or swapped, check with HLR SMS profile

Ensure SMS sending profile, TS 22 is installed.

If they do not have the profile, please activate it for the agent.

# **Damaged SIM Card**

Request them to retry sending the SMS to the same destination using a different SIM Card.

If the SMS is successful, they should bring the original SIM to our retail centres to test and establish if SIM is damaged.

They will be advised on whether to get a SIM swap.

Sim card Replacement

Search correct M-PESA Agent

articleTitle: M-PESA PIN AND SERVICE PIN ADOPTED FOR ALL BONGA TRANSACTIONS
markdownContent:
As we continue to seek to give customers a simplified experience on Bonga transactions, a lot of customers had queries around having two different pins when carrying out Transfer Bonga points & Lipa na Bonga points Service. We have now **dropped** the **Bonga pin** and **adopted** the **M-PESA Pin** and **Service pin** **across all Bonga transactions requiring a pin.**

Customers who are registered on M-PESA will use their **M-PESA Pin,** while customers not registered will use the **Service Pin.**

# **Key Features**

Customer will be asked to input their M-PESA Pin or Service Pin when carrying out Transfer Bonga Points & Lipa na Bonga Points.

Customer will be able to Set or Change Service Pin under the \*126# Menu

Customers who were using Service Pin will not be affected. However, Those that were using **Bonga pin** will be **prompted** to change to Service Pin or M-PESA Pin.

# **Objective:**

To give customers a simplified experience when carrying out Bonga transactions by having M-PESA /Service Pin to be used across all Bonga Transactions.

NB:- Attached please find the customer journey, use existing interactions and SR's on Bonga pin for escalations.

This is the role that enables MPESA till to do float movement from working to float account and vice versa

Management role also enables sub agent to receive float deposit and withdraw float through banks and other super-agent

- SLA for the request is 24hrs

- Enter till number and click on search.

markdownContent:
# **Dealer Support Change of Account Rule Band**

**CHANGE OF ACCOUNT RULE BAND**

- Account rule band of a till affects the maximum float balance a till can hold
- To change rule band M-PESA head office should raise a service request on dealer portal.
 - Service request category: mpesa services
 - Request type: mpesa account rule band changes
 - Item: rule band change
- Service request SLA is 24hrs
- For request past SLA the CEE should assist to change the rule band.

- Login to the M-PESA WEB and search for the specific store number indicated in the above service request.

- Enter the SR number under reason and submit.

**AGGREGATOR REQUEST**

This request is done when MPESA head office want to give the till to an independent person. The till change distribution model (commission distribution model) is changed from Centrally owned to aggregated. Once aggregated the till will be distributing commissions in the ratio 80:20 80% of commissions will be paid to the subagent and 20% to the Agency Head office.

 - Sub agent National ID

- click on add then the select Agency independent store product

markdownContent:
# **Dealer Support Suspension and Unsuspension of Lost Tills**

**DEALER SUPPORT SUSPENSION AND UNSUSPENSION OF LOST TILLS**

**SUSPENSION OF A LOST/STOLEN TILL**

- Request to suspend a lost till is raised through any of the following channels. 

1. Agent head office/sub agent calling customer care or visiting Safaricom shop. On receiving the request partner support staff should confirm the agent number, outlet short code and outlet name then freeze the Float account and suspend working account (if the working account has funds)
2. The request can also be reported by the head office through raising a service request on dealer portal.
3. - - - Service request category; MPESA services.
 - Request type: MPESA agent account
 - Request Item: Suspension of lost tills
 - Problem Description: indicate reason for suspension and include agent number, short code, and outlet name.
 - SLA for the suspension is 24hrs.

**Procedure for suspending lost or stolen till on M-PESA System**

login to MPESA and search to the outlet using the short code provided.

1. Under float account status click on edit and change the status for active to Frozen
2. Enter the reason for freezing then submit the request.
3. Out status will change to frozen. 

**UNSUSPENSION OF A LOST/STOLEN TILL**

- Request to unsuspend lost/stolen till should be raised on dealer portal by agency head office. On logging in to dealer portal the head office should select below categories
 - Service request Category: MPESA services
 - Request type: MPESA agent account
 - Request Item: Unsuspension of lost tills
 - Problem Description: indicate reason for unsuspension and include agent number, short code, and outlet name.
- The SLA for the service Request is 24 hours.
- Procedure for unsuspending lost or stolen till on M-PESA System; the Safaricom partner support staff will login to MPESA and search to the outlet using the short code
- Check on the Audit logs for the reason for suspension. This is available within the previous 6 months. If unavailable from the Audit logs, the Safaricom partner support staff will then raise a ticket via BM Ticket for archived audit logs, **SLA=48** hours. Once provided, then the Safaricom partner support staff will unsuspend if reason is clear or escalate to the team responsible for suspending the till to get a go-ahead or not.
- Under float account status click on edit and change the status for Frozen to active
- Enter the reason for Unfreezing (include the SR number) then submit the request.
- Account status will change to active.

articleTitle: Router configuration and troubleshooting WIMAX issues
markdownContent:
# **Router configuration**

If a customer calls requesting to be assisted to configure their router, or in the process of troubleshooting you suspect that the router could have lost configs, ask them the model of the router and the follow the below steps to configure:

1. Verify the type of router the customer is using, commonly used routers especially by home users, cyber and SME are Linksys, D-Link, TP-Link and Level one router.
2. Default log in for the above routers is 192.168.1.1 or 192.168.0.1(for a D-link)
3. User name and password is **admin**.
4. Once you log into the router interface assign the static ip; **key entries** are:

Internet ip: put the customer public ip e.g. 41.139.204.98

Subnet mask: 255.255.255.252

Default gateway: this is derived from customer public ip e.g. 41.139.204.97 (one digit less on the last octet of the public ip)

Preferred DNS server: 41.203.208.18

Alternate DNS server 41.203.208.19

Ensure DHCP server is enabled

For simulation of the router use the following links:

Linksys: [http://ui.linksys.com/files/WRT54GL/4.30.0/Setup.htm](http://ui.linksys.com/files/WRT54GL/4.30.0/Setup.htm)

Dlink: [http://support.dlink.com/emulators/wbr2310/wireless.htm](http://support.dlink.com/emulators/wbr2310/wireless.htm)

TP-Link: [http://www.tp](http://www.tp-link.com/support/simulator.asp)[\-link.com/support/simulator.asp](http://www.tp-link.com/support/simulator.asp)

Level one router: [http://download.level1.com/level1/qig/WBR](http://download.level1.com/level1/qig/WBR-6011_QIG_English.pdf)[\-6011\_QIG\_English.pdf](http://download.level1.com/level1/qig/WBR-6011_QIG_English.pdf)

- For high-end routers, ask the customer whether we manage their router; if yes, escalate to business support with all the necessary details and if no, ask the customer to request their IT department to assist. You may however give the ip address details to the customer.

**N.B:** To check FIBER/WIMAX connection speeds, on a browser open the address Http://www.speedtest.safaricombusiness.co.ke or Http://www.speedtest.net and begin test.

# **How to check the link parameters on Alvaristar**

Take China Wuyi ye Lihang as an example client on Bazaar Base station.

1. Logging to Alvaristar with individual loggings
2. Drill down to equipment manager tab by double clicking on it to view the BS listed
3. Double click on the desired BS in this case Baazar to open the BS and drill down to the clients by clicking on subscriber units.
4. Select the desired client in this case (China Wuyi ye Lihang) and double click to open and show the client parameters. On the main page, scroll down to air interface summary section to check the link parameters.

**Note:**

1. Of importance to note are the uplink and Downlink current rate signals; anything other than QAM is poor signal. As per the below, QAM-64 3/4 is the best signal while BPSK 1/2 is the weakest signal.
2. Also important under link parameters is the uplink /downlink SNR(Signal to Noise Ratio); Anything less than 20 is poor

5. Click on the Refresh button severally at the bottom of the page as you observer the changes if any on the uplink and downlink current rate signals as well as the uplink and downlink SNRs.
6. If client parameters indicate QPSK or BPSK on any of the current rate signals and or less than 20 on any of the SNRs, a ticket should be raised for faulting under ‘Wimax-Poor RF signal’.
7. Poor parameters on Wimax link will affect the performance on that Link and customer may complain of slow speeds, timeouts etc. Solution to poor parameters is realignment of the ODU to ensure proper signal reception. This is done by contractors who have to visit the site, hence the need to capture the issue in SR.
8. Click on the Refresh button severally at the bottom of the page as you observer the changes if any on the uplink and downlink current rate signals as well as the uplink and downlink SNRs.

# **Slow speeds on WIMAX connection**

Check signal parameters on Alvaristar; if they are poor capture the issue on SR.

If parameters are ok, Ping the BS serving the customer, if there are packet drops alert NOC via mail and copy business support and CMFIXED DATA TEAM.

If BS is OK, Ping the customer gateway on BS from the switch, if there are packet drops, capture the issue in SR.

If gateway is ok, check on bandwidth utilization on Allot, if customer is maxing on the link, advise on the same. Advise the customer to consider upgrading to a higher bandwidth capacity on manage the usage.

If customer is not maxing, ask the customer to ping the internal gateway (router), if latencies are high advice customer to check on LAN connection. If the latencies are low and customer is still experiencing slow speeds, ask the customer to by-pass the LAN and connect the computer directly at the IDU and conduct speed test from speedtest.safaricombusiness.co.ke.

If you have done the above checks and everything is positive but customer is still experiencing slow speeds, then capture issue in SR indicating all the troubleshooting done.

# **Resolution for high WIMAX latencies**

Ask the customer to do a ping test to his internal gateway (router) and note the average latencies in ms.

If latencies are high advice the customer to check the LAN.

If the latencies are low from step one above, ask the customer to ping his default gateway i.e. IP at the Base station and note the latencies.

If the latencies are high at this point ping also an internet page such as google.com and note the latencies too and capture the issue in SR for second level support to deal.

**Note:** High latencies affect the connection speeds and are derived by carrying out a ping test or a trace route from the affected link.

# **WIMAX link not picking MAC Address on Alvaristar**

On AlvariSTAR double click to open the CPE of the link in question.

Go to bridging, if you cannot pick a mac address ask the customer;

1. To unplug and plug in the ETH cable on the IDU.
2. Connect the other end of the ETH cable to a computer and see if you will pick mac address of the computer.
3. If you are still unable to pick mac after procedure (b) ask sub to use new cable.

If the customer has used a new cable and still you cannot pick mac address, capture the issue in SR because the IDU could be faulty.

# **Customer unable to reach DNS address**

The Safaricom DNS addresses are 41.203.208.18 and 41.203.208.19

Request the customer to connect their computer on to the router directly.

1. Ask the customer to ping the internal gateway (router).
2. If the customer is getting reply from the internal gateway, ask the customer to ping any of the DNS addresses.
3. If the DNS are not replying, ask the customer to go to Command prompt (CMD) on their computer and do ipconfig/all to check that the correct DNSs have been configured on the router.
4. If still customer is unable to reach DNS guide the customer on making a direct connection to IDU and test.
5. If after doing all the above tests the DNS is still unreachable capture the issue on SR for second level supports to deal.

# **Steps on how to configure a WiMAX router**

After setting up a router on LAN, Logging to the admin page for the router using the default root 192.168.1.1 or 192.168.0.1 from your address bar on the browser.

Take a cisco Linksys router as an example 
NB: settings required for configurations are usually provided for by the Internet service provider. In this case Safaricom has assigned the following to the client China Wuyi ye Lihang

- IP: 41.139.211.170
- Gateway: 41.139.211.169 
 Other required details that are standard for all other safaricom wimax client include:
- Subnet mask: 255.255.255.252
- DNS 1: 41.203.208.18
- DNS 2: 41.203.208.19

The customer will:

1. Double click on the internet explorer browser icon to launch or any other browser of choice and enter the default root address of the router on the address bar and hit enter to load the admin page.
2. Use the default credential as below: 
 Username: admin 
 Password: admin
3. Once logged in go to the set up and drill to basic set up.
4. Under basic set up, click on the drop down menu as below and select Static IP.
5. Once static IP is selected, the entries to be filled will appear.Enter details.
6. Save the setting at the bottom of the page by clicking on the tab as indicated. The router will restart or give you options to restart, proceed to restart for the changes to take effect, there after cone can connect by attaching a cable from any of the LAN ports indicated on the router.

# **How to reset a WiMAX link**

Take China Wuyi ye Lihang as an example client on Bazaar Base station:

Logging to Alvaristar with individual loggings.

Drill down to equipment manager tab by double clicking on it to view the BS listed.

Double click on the desired BS in this case Baazar to open the BS and drill down to the clients by clicking on subscriber units.

Select the desired client in this case (China Wuyi ye Lihang) and double click to open and show the client parameters.

Drill down to Unit control and click on reset, to reset the clients wimax link. The client will lose connectivity for a few seconds before the link picking up afresh.

# **How to by-pass router connection**

By-passing a router connection simply means connecting directly to the IDU (in case of a wimax connection) a single PC.

Take client: China Wuyi ye Lihang as an example using windows 7 OS, with the below settings:

- IP: 41.139.211.170
- Gateway: 41.139.211.169
- Subnet mask: 255.255.255.252
- DNS 1: 41.203.208.18
- DNS 2: 41.203.208.19

The customer will:

1. Take the Ethernet cable running from the IDU to the router and terminate it to any of the LAN ports on the desired PC for connection.
2. Click Start->Control Panel-> Network and Internet->View network status and tasks or Network and Sharing Center, click on change adapter settings.
3. Select the connection, right click it and select Properties.
4. Select Internet Protocol Version 4(TCP/IPv4), double click it or click Properties.
5. Select Use the IP address, type IP address, subnet mask and default gateway IP address into it.
6. Select the DNS server addresses, type the DNS server addresses into it.
7. Click OK to save and apply your settings.
8. You may be required to restart the PC for the changes to take effect and enable you to connect.

# Service definition

Express parking with M-PESA is a service by Safaricom in partnership with KAPS that allows a customer to drive in and out of a mall without having to validate parking. Hence, minimizing contact with the entry booth, parking ticket and payment booth.

# How it works

When driving into a mall, the entry barrier automatically allows the vehicle access. Once the customer is done, they simply drive out; the exit barrier automatically opens. Their parking bill is automatically deducted with a notification sent to their phone.

# Benefits of using the service

1. Simple Do It Yourself online registration process.
2. No contact with the parking booth at entry or exit of the mall.
3. Prepaid wallet that offers easy payment flow.

# Express parking locations

Express parking is currently available at the 4 sites below:

1. JKIA
2. Gateway Mall
3. Village Market
4. Rupa Mall in Eldoret

articleTitle: A0072 : Express Parking With M-PESA Payment procedure and funds account

5. On entry to mall, the **entry barrier** will automatically give access to vehicle with parking sticker.
6. On exit, the barrier will automatically open and funds deducted from the parking wallet.
7. Once parking payment has been deducted and notification message is sent to your phone.

Express parking funds account

- Customers can query their parking account statement via KAPS app on Google playstore or Apple store.

articleTitle: Definition and Mechanics of Safaricom Kleek Service
markdownContent:

# **DEFINITION**

LinkedIn is a networking tool that helps one to build and engage with his professionals; hence able to access knowledge, insights, and opportunities.

# **ELIGIBILITY**

- LinkedIn is eligible to everyone; both Safaricom and Non Safaricom Customers
- It is a platform for anyone who is looking to advance their career.
- This can include people from various professional backgrounds, such as small business owners, students, and job seekers.
- LinkedIn members can use LinkedIn to tap into a network of professionals, companies, and groups within and beyond their industry.

# **HOW IT WORKS**

- LinkedIn is the world's largest professional network on the internet.
- Customers can use LinkedIn to find the right job or internship, connect and strengthen professional relationships, and learn the skills they need to succeed in their career.
- The customers can access LinkedIn from a desktop, LinkedIn mobile app, mobile web experience, or the LinkedIn Lite Android mobile app.
- A complete LinkedIn profile can help a person to connect with opportunities by showcasing his unique professional story through experience, skills, and education.
- A customer can also use LinkedIn to organize offline events, join groups, write articles, post photos and videos, and more.
- The customer can use LinkedIn to research companies and reach out to the hiring community
- The customer can find and join LinkedIn groups by searching for desired groups from the Groups available, he may Like page or the Search field at the top of the homepage.

# **BILLING**

While accessing LinkedIn, one is charged on normal data connection charges.

**ACTIVATION**

**Website**

- Go to https://www.linkedin.com/reg/join.
- The customer will type first name, last name, email address and a password he will use.
- Click Join Now. And follow the prompts

**Google Play Store**

On the search icon, type LinkedIn then Install

**TERMINATION**

To terminate LinkedIn Account one can follow below steps.

- Log into LinkedIn account.
- Select the tab under the profile picture in the top toolbar.
- Choose “Settings and Privacy” from the dropdown menu.
- In the “Account” tab, select “Closing Your LinkedIn Account”
- Select the reason for closing your account and hit “next”
- Select “Close Account”

# **CUSTOMER GUIDE ON LINKEDIN**

If LinkedIn feature is not working as expected,

- Click the Me icon in the top right of homepage, select ***Sign Out***, and then click ***Sign In***.

- Remember, passwords are case sensitive and should be at least 6 characters long.
- Once signed in, the customer should check to see if he still has the same problem.

- Clear cache and cookies. Then sign into the account to see if that fixes the problem.
- Try a different Internet browser. For example, if you're normally using Internet Explorer, try using Firefox or Chrome instead, and sign into the account.
- If the issue doesn't occur with a different browser, you can keep using that browser.
- Check and disable the browser's pop-up blocker. Sometimes, this keeps the customer from seeing or doing things on LinkedIn site.
- If dropdown menus are not visible, the customer may need to update his JavaScript settings
- If none of these solutions work, the CEE will check on the customer’s internet, try purging the line and advise the customer on restarting the handset.

# **Subscription Mechanics**

1. Using the Safaricom registered line the customer will dial 813 and select their preferred option as indicated below to subscribe and listen to their preferred music

1. Navigation menu – Press 0
2. Previous menu – Press #
3. Top Charts - Press 1
4. Local Music– Press 2
5. International Music – Press 3
6. Gospel - Press 4
7. Artist Playlists - Press 5
8. Download – Press 6
9. Dedication - Press 7
10. Help menu – Press 9

2. Calling 813 is a one-off charge at Kshs 3.

# **Song Download Mechanics**

1. Using the Safaricom registered line the customer will dial 813
2. Press 6 to download music of their choice
3. They will receive an SMS with a link to download the selected song.
4. Calling 813 is chargeable at Kshs. 3. (Deduction is done on available airtime)
5. Customer will need to have active Internet to download (Prevailing Data rate apply).

# **Favorite song selection mechanics**

1. The system intelligence will take the customer straight to the ‘My Favorite Playlist’ provided a ‘My Favorite Playlist’ is created.
2. Alternatively, a customer can create via IVR

1. A customer will dial 813
2. Press 5 Artist Playlists anytime and go to their favorite list.
3. Calling 813 is chargeable at Kshs. 3. (Deduction is done on available airtime)

# **Preferred Song selection Mechanics**

- Safaricom Kleek allows a customer to search and select the song artist wise.

1. A customer will dial 813
2. Press 0 Navigation Menu
3. Press 5 Artist Playlists
4. Then Select for Preferred Artist e.g. for Diamond by pressing the correct number on their mobile phone.
5. Calling 813 is chargeable at Kshs. 3. (Deduction is done on available airtime).

# **Song Dedication Mechanics**

1. A customer will dial 813
2. Press 7 to dedicate a song or record their message and enter Mobile number of the recipient.
3. Recipient will dial 8137 (Free) to listen to the dedicated song or message
4. Calling 813 is chargeable at Kshs. 3. (Deduction is done on available airtime).
5. Recipient (whom the song is dedicated to) will not be charged by dialing Toll Free number 8137.

# **Unsubscription Mechanics**

### a) Via IVR DIY

1. A customer will dial 813
2. Press 0 Navigation Menu
3. Press 9 Help Menu then follow IVR prompts to Unsubscribe
4. Calling 813 is a one-off charge at Kshs. 3.

# **Nairobi Expressway M-PESA Payments**

**This service is on pilot**

**Motorist Customer Journey**

**How will the solution work**

**At the entrance**

Customer drives to the expressway entrance and picks the token.

Token will capture

Date and time of entrance.

The location

Type of car

The customer then drives to his/her desired exit

**At the Exit**

1\. The customer will present the token to the toll attendant at the exit point and inform attendant that they will make payment via M-PESA and provide their M-PESA registered phone number.

The attendant will inform the customer of the amount to be paid and will request for customer’s M-PESA registered phone number.

2\. The customer gets a prompt with details of amount to be paid and authorizes the transaction by entering his/her M-PESA pin.

3\. The attendant will get a notification of successful payment and will then lift the barrier and provide customer with receipt of payment

4\. The customer then drives through

**Customer FAQs**

**What is required to enable M-PESA payment on the expressway**

•Customer will need to have an active M-PESA registered number with sufficient funds for the payment.

**How will I make payments using my M-PESA at the expressway?**

•Inform the toll attendant that you intend to make payment via M-PESA and provide your M-PESA registered number.

•The Toll attendant will key in the amount to be paid onto the point-of-sale device;

•You will then receive a pop up on your phone asking you to authorize payment to Moja Expressway Co. Limited by entering your M-PESA PIN for the transaction to be processed.

**What notification will I get as a confirmation that the fees have been remitted?**

•M-PESA will send the standard Pay Bill confirmation SMS immediately after carrying out the transaction. This notification will confirm that funds have been transferred to the expressway paybill.

**Can I pay for use of expressway using Fuliza**

•Yes, you can make payment using Fuliza

**How do I request for reversal of a wrongly paid transaction?**

•Contact the Moja expressway directly on 0111039777 and request for the reversal. Moja Expressway ltd will check the transaction and advice you how soon the M-PESA paybill reversal will be done.

**How do I get assistance?**

For all customer care queries, kindly call Safaricom customer care 100 or 200

**Toll Attendant FAQs**

**How do I get my password**

•You will receive SMS with your POS password. Make sure the phone number provided is registered under your name

**What do I need to log in to the POS?**

•Your staff id and password received via SMS

**How do I change my password?**

•Click on forgot password on POS,

•enter your staff id

•Enter OTP received via SMS on POS

•Enter new password

**What does the customer need to provide for M-PESA Payments?**

•Customer will need to provide their M-PESA registered mobile number

**How do receive payment from customer?**

•Select amount

•Enter customer MPESA phone number

•Click on initiate payment

**What scenarios will lead to failed transaction?**

1.Customer does not respond to payment prompt

2.Customer enters incorrect M-PESA PIN

3.Customer has insufficient funds to complete the transaction

4.Customers phone is unreachable/ off

**How do I open the barrier?**

•Scan the QR code presented on the POS screen after payment on the toll QR code reader

**How do I get assistance for POS queries?**

•For all customer care queries, kindly call 0709920000

articleTitle: Introduction, Eligibility, Feature and Benefits of New Karibu Postpay
markdownContent:
# **Introduction**

Karibu Postpay is a simplified way of joining PostPay. The PostPay tariff on sign up allows you to set a preferred monthly credit limit with a minimum allowable limit of 1,000.

# **Eligibility**

Karibu PostPay is open to all PrePay customers with an exception of corporate accounts which includes Zidisha customers.

Customers who initially had a PostPay profile Karibu PostPay, Advantage hybrid, Advantage Plus and Platinum can now buy PostPay Bundles by dialing \*200#.

Staff are currently not eligible.

Blaze customers will also be able to join without unsubscribing from the blaze tariff.

# **Features**

a) Exciting bundles that offer Minutes, SMS and Data.

b) The plans will be offered on the sign-up journey, they will also be accessible on \*544# and \*200#.

c) Out of bundle charges for Voice is Kshs. 2.30 and Kshs.1.30 for Data. Only applicable once the bundles run’s out or buy other bundles on \*544#.

d) Once on PostPay customers will not accumulate Storo Bonus.

e) Customers can buy the bundle only once in a month as there is no provision for multiple subscriptions.

f) You cannot use the bundles for roaming services.

g) Customers who have less, or No monthly limits can always increase their limits by paying deposit.

h) Customers will earn Bonga points when they purchase the plans.

i) Subscribers cannot transfer/ sambaza their resources.

j) Upon activating My Data manager, the service will remain active on joining Karibu PostPay.

k) PostPay customers will be able to purchase PostPay Bundles via \*200# ok option 0.

l) If you sign up in the middle of the month both the **Amount and the Resources** will be prorated (partly awarded depending on the remaining days of the month)

m) A notification will be sent to the customer once the line is barred and upon reconnection.

n) To stop auto renew simply dial \*544#, \*200# and select stop auto renew. Once the bundle runs out normal data and voice rates will apply.

o) Normal calling rates of 4.3/- per minute will apply when one onboards without a plan using App or Web.

p) Their profile will remain as Hybrid meaning they can use airtime.

q) All other features for Hybrid remain including CRM views, Termination, milestone.

r) A customer who terminates the post pay service will have to wait for 1 hour to be able to onboard back.

**Benefits**

a) You can increase and decrease your limit.

b) The minutes can be used to make international calls to China, India, Canada and the USA.

C) It is easy to join and Exit via APP, Web and USSD \*544#.

d) The unlimited resources are subject to fair use policy.

e) All plans shall have no expiry.

f) The bundles will auto renew until the customer unsubscribes from the subscription.

g) Plan will be immediately subscribed.

h) The resources will Not Expire at the end of month after which on the 1st of the next month you will receive their full resources and non-expiry bundles.

i) For the Unlimited Resources there will be a Refresh at the end of every month hence the Expiry date on CRM even though the resources will Not Expire.

j) Priority will be for resources that expire. You can change your plan simply by selecting the option buy plan select your preferred you will be unsubscribed from your current plan and you’re preferred.

k) Customers will be able to make On-net call/SMS, off net calls/SMS. They will also be able to browse using the data that they have purchased.

l) You can use your credit limit to buy a plan.

m) Note: You cannot use M-pesa to buy a plan.

n) You will receive threshold notifications when your data is about to run out, the messages will be sent when you have 500MB, 75MB and 2MB.

o) If you have already hit your credit limit, you will have to make a payment via MPESA (200200) to your account and then proceed to buy a different bundle of your choice. You can also use out of bundle at your preferred PostPay rate.

# **Definition**

‘***Buy one get one free’*** offer (BOGOF) on the 555 Menu under the Gen Z folder is an offer that aims to give subscribers more data bundles with every purchase of 1.5GB bundle every day from **6:00 am to 12noon**.

# **Eligibility**

The BOGOF offer is only available to Safaricom subscribers aged between 12 – 24 years and on **S-HOOK Tariff**

This BOGOF offer will not be available to subscribers who are roaming.

# **Mechanics**

Customer will purchase the BOGOF bundle by dialling on \*555# and selecting GEN Z OFFERS.

Subscribers can buy the offer as many times as they wish.   The BOGOF Data Bundles will not be transferable (no *Sambaza*)

# **Validity**

The resources awarded shall be valid for 3 hours from time of purchase.

Any unused data bundles after the 3 hours validity period will expire and will not be carried over.

A customer can extend the validity of the BOGOF bundle for 3hours by purchasing a similar offer within the eligible timelines.

# **Priority of usage**

The priority will after the hourly bundle and before the daily bundles

# **Will the BOGOF bundle be reversible?**

No. This bundle being an hourly offer will not be reversible.

articleTitle: Opting in and Termination Mechanics of New Karibu Postpay
markdownContent:
# **How to Opt In:**

### **a)Via USSD \*544#**

- Dial \*544#.
- Select Join PostPay.
- You will be presented with 2 options either join via Web or continue with USSD.
- You will be presented with a pre-defined credit limit. Customers with no credit limit will be prompted to enter their preferred limit and make payment. (Via M-pesa).
- You will be prompted to enter your email address.
- Select a plan.
- Accept terms and condition.

**NB:** You will receive a notification your line has been moved to PostPay.

A customer on another postpay package should first unsubscribe to join the service. They will need to dial \*200# Ok., Select option 0, Buy postpay bundles. For Hybrid customers, they will dial \*200# Ok then they will see change plan option 0 which means they have changed from Hybrid to postpay DIY though the experience remains the same.

### **b) Via USSD \*100# or \*456#**

- Dial \*100# and \*456# and select My Account/Join PostPay
- Select Join PostPay
- Customers will be presented with 2 options either join via Web or continue with USSD.
- You will be presented with a predefined credit limit where no deposit is required. Customers with no credit limit will be prompted to enter their preferred limit and make payment (deposit is required) via MPESA.
- You will be prompted to enter your email address for billing purposes.
- Select a PostPay bundle plan.
- Accept terms and conditions.

# **Customer request for FTTH at the call Centre**

Once you receive the customer request, enquire if the customer had requested to get internet connection via \*400# or Zuri chatbot.

In case the customer had sent the request using above channels, and the ticket is within SLA (24hrs), advise the customer to be patient as the Safaricom Fiber Sales team will get in touch.

In case you confirm that the customer had not attempted the DIY (\*400#/ZURI) capture the customer details via FTTH sales lead link on CMIntranet (cc systems>Fiber to the Home>FTTH sales Lead) [https://cxintranet.safaricom.net/cm2/S\_FTTHSales\_Index.php](https://cxintranet.safaricom.net/cm2/S_FTTHSales_Index.php)and also educate the customer on the DIY options. Do not send emails to the folder.

After submitting the above details, advise the customer that the request will be actioned within 24hrs.

The above customer details submitted, will be received on **fibersalesgroup@safaricom.co.ke** email folder for the Fiber sales team with a link to action.

For Fiber ready areas, the sales agent will call the customer and advice on packages available and the payment procedures.

For non-Fiber ready areas, the sales agent will send an SMS to the customer, advising that the area is not fiber ready thus to use other Safaricom internet options available.

Safaricom Home Fiber sales team will receive the request and respond to the customers then update comments by clicking on pending status via [**https://cmintranet/index.php?option=com\_php&task=display&tmpl=component&Itemid=1840**](https://cmintranet/index.php?option=com_php&task=display&tmpl=component&Itemid=1840)

Incase customer contacts the call Centre following up on FTTH connection requests, you will view ticket status and responses from Fiber sales team via [**https://cmintranet/index.php?option=com\_php&task=display&tmpl=component&Itemid=1840**](https://cmintranet/index.php?option=com_php&task=display&tmpl=component&Itemid=1840) .

Pending status will mean the Fiber sales team has not actioned on the request. Actioned status means that the customer has been contacted and comments have been indicated on the closed ticket for visibility.

In case the customer contacts the call Centre that he/she has not been contacted and the request is past SLA, and you confirm that the request is pending from the link, send an email to Fiber sales team **fibersalesgroup@safaricom.co.ke** and advice the customer that the issue will be responded to within 2hrs.

# **Installation and activation of FTTH**

To get connected, the CEE will advise the customer to send an email to safaricomhome@Safaricom.co.ke or dial \*400#.

On filing the application form and making payment, activation set up will be completed within 24hours after receipt of payment.

On connection, a customer will get a Wi-Fi router at no additional costs that will enable Internet access via both wireless & LAN.

# **Safaricom Home Fiber Password Change**

Safaricom Home Fiber customers may call to change their WIFI passwords from the default ones they have after onboarding, or their WIFI passwords have been compromised.

In case a customer calls 100/200/ or contact us via social media, pick the request and share it via email to copsftth@safaricom.co.ke for line line400 support team to action.

For requests received at the call center on line 400, the customer must call from the registered MSISDN on the sales portal or in case the request is done via email, it has to be the email captured on Sales portal.

# **Definition**

**A service request (SR)** is a request from a CEE that initiates a service action to 2nd line support for further analysis and resolution where they are unable to resolve on call or service is beyond their scope of responsibility.

**A Service Request (SR) Number** is assigned to every problem reported through the Service Desk. This is the number that is used to track customers’ request

**A service-level agreement (SLA):** is a commitment between a [service provider](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Service_provider) and a [client](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Customer). Aspects of the service: quality, availability, responsibilities are agreed between the service provider and the end user.

# **Service Request (SR) CRM Sections**

**Service Request Category:**

A general description of the types of services provided under the service and/or the characteristics that define the service category

**A service request type**

Is a category of related services that share schemas. It defines the schema attributes that are common across a set of similar managed resources. The SR type selected shall correspond with the customer’ issue raised.

**Service Request Item:**

A unit, especially one that is part of a list, collection, or set. This field is dependent on the above, Type field, where the CEE will narrow the caller reason further to a more specific issue.

**Comments Section:**

The CEE shall Capture clear information about the customer issues raised and indicate all relevant information required by the support analyst to resolve customer issue and close the SR.

# **What to consider when raising an SR**

- The CEE will raise a Service Request for issues outside their Scope of Responsibility.
- The CEE should select Correct Category, Type and Item for proper routing and appropriate resolution.
- The CEE should capture the SR notes with relevant information to aid the Support analyst resolve the issue without having to call the customer again, hence avoiding back and forth with customer. The ticket should have enough information to resolve the issue e.g. include the voucher serial numbers, IMEI, vetting details, Contact number etc.
- Where a request comes via call from E1 line, the CEE will request for an Email contact and capture the same on the SR
- Where a request is received via Email, the CEE will copy and paste the email on the SR Comments Section with below details;
 - The Email address that sent the Email

Ticketing system validates the payment instructions.

M-PESA completes payment request

Ticketing system receives successful payment response.

Ticketing system receives payment confirmation and teller is advised on successful transaction.

articleTitle: Onboarding Process for Short Term and Long Term PAYBILL
markdownContent:
**Onboarding Process for Short Term and Long Term PAYBILL**

# **SHORT TERM PAYBILL**

Application is made via:

The Lipa Na M-PESA Self Onboarding Portal this is accessible from:

# **Portal Link:**

Open the link [https://selfservice.m-pesaforbusiness.co.ke/LNM/](https://selfservice.m-pesaforbusiness.co.ke/LNM/)

Click **Apply Now** and follow the prompts to fill in the required details.

Click on **My Applications** to track the progress of your applications.

# **MySafaricom APP:**

Launch MySafaricom APP and click M-PESA

Click Lipa Na M-PESA Portal

Click **Apply Now** and follow the prompts to fill in the required details.

Click on **My Applications** to track the progress of your applications.

# **Sending the request on email to:**

[short-termpaybill@safaricom.co.ke](mailto:short-termpaybill@safaricom.co.ke)  or

[M-PESABusiness@Safaricom.co.ke](mailto:M-PESABusiness@Safaricom.co.ke)

# **Visit any Safaricom Shops**

Application forms are available on the Safaricom Corporate website, at the retail centers and by sending an email to [M-PESABusiness@Safaricom.co.ke](mailto:M-PESABusiness@Safaricom.co.ke)  or [short-termpaybill@safaricom.co.ke](mailto:short-termpaybill@safaricom.co.ke)

Upon successful application by applicants, CHANGA na M-PESA accounts will be created by LNM Support and or Retail teams and customer notified.

Account Set up will take a maximum of 48 hrs.

Account holders will also be able to receive statements via e-mail requests through the e-mail address short-termpaybill@safaricom.co.ke or M-PESABusiness@Safaricom.co.ke. Sla is 2hrs.

The account holders who want to access the funds before the stipulated period of activation, can make withdrawal to bank requests via email to short-termpaybill@safaricom.co.ke or [M-PESABusiness@Safaricom.co.ke](mailto:M-PESABusiness@Safaricom.co.ke)  The SLA is 24hrs.

This is a Paybill used for a short duration of 1/3/6 months after which it is deactivated after the set period has expired.

When creating short term pay bill set up of the effective and expiry dates is done on MPESA G2. (Effective date is the date of setting up the short term pay bill and expiry date is the date the account needs to be closed)

For extension of the duration the merchant/partner will provide written justification for the purpose of the extension up to a maximum of 6 months.

The category also includes the short term political short term Paybill requests.

Account renewals will be done only once

Account will be closed after the stipulated period of activation and funds withdrawn to the bank /M-PESA account indicated by the account holder as indicated in the application form.

# **LONG TERM PAYBILL**

Partners must provide the KYC documents that meet the KYC requirements and fill the application, a tariff guide form. CEE will advise the customer to either present to documents to:

Retail / care desks

Email scanned copies to either lnmrecruitment@Safaricom.co.ke or M-PESA Business M-PESABusiness@Safaricom.co.ke.

Where applicable hand them to EBU sales / account management teams who will capture the same on the SME tool.

Deliver KYC documents to Safaricom Limited, Safaricom House HQ2, Waiyaki Way for receipt by the M-PESA Merchant Support Team.

The customer will be advised to wait for a response from the LNM Support Team within 48 hours.

# **Audited Financial Statement**

Audited financial statements will not be requested for during onboarding. They will be requested based on transacted value.

The transacted value (turnover) threshold will be Ksh. 1,000,000 per month.

AML Team, through transaction monitoring, will ensure the report is shared with onboarding team for accounts that hit 1M on transactions per month for sales teams to follow up on submission of the following documentation depending on the category:

Registered companies over 1 year ago: Latest financial statements or annual returns

Sole proprietorship: Latest personal Returns

All other categories but not limited to SACCOs, NGOs, Political Pay Bills, Churches and Religious Organizations: Latest financial statements/or annual returns.

Where company director is a sole, resolution letters should be signed by one director and stamped/sealed. M-PESA settlement will be allowed.

Where CR12 document has other companies as majority shareholders, the organization is expected to provide CR12 for those companies and copy of identification documentation (IDs /passports and KRA PINs for Kenyan directors).

Where organizations want to trade with other business names not as per Certificate of Registration, Trade Name Certificate should be provided.

Where additional tills are required for Limited Liability Companies, existing till CR12 documentation provided should be less than 2 years old. Otherwise updated CR12 current to 3 months should be provided.

Upon change of ownership of company’s directors, organization’s will be expected to provide updated CR12 documentation, New directors copy of their identification documentations and their KRA pin certificates.

Where Sole Proprietor business permit does not indicate details as per owner identification documentation, Certificate of Business Registration to be provided proving relation of the applicant to the business.

Safaricom salesperson onboarding must sign the application form confirming existence of premise prior to uploading the form for processing.

Tariff Guide must be signed by partners for all Pay bill products.

For access to M-PESA Portal, M-PESA Business Administrator form must be filled for Paybill products, Bulk payment products and Buy goods -Bank settlement.

articleTitle: M-PESA Chama Requirements/Registration and Application Process
markdownContent:
**M-PESA Chama Requirements/Registration and Application Process**

M-PESA CHAMA ACCOUNT is a short term Paybill service that eases the collection of chama contributions from members.

This is a service being offered to groups/chamas to allow them to collect funds quickly, conveniently and securely from members.

The M-PESA Chama account can hold a minimum of 0 and up to Ksh 100,000,000M.

The service is currently available to Safaricom subscribers only.

**For Pin reset:** One can visit the nearest BOA-Kenya branch and request for the PIN to be resent.

Customer will receive an SMS from the bank confirming the transaction and the amount of money transferred, then another SMS from M-PESA confirming the amount credited into the M-PESA account and the updated balance.

Security of M-Chama transactions: security measures have been put up to protect transactions from unauthorized access. Customers are advised not to disclose their M-Chama PIN to anyone else.

Chama needs to have an account with BOA-Kenya to be registered for the service. Non-account holders may open a Chama Account at any BOA-Kenya branches countrywide.

The group representative can register the rest of the members and provide access for members to log into the portal to access the chama statement.

# **Chama Paybill Requirements**

Duly filled and signed application form &Terms and conditions (Attached)

Signed Tariff Guide (Attached)

Copy of certificate of registration from Registrar of societies

Certified list of officials from the registrar of societies.

Stamped Minutes signed by at least two nominated officials within 30 days stating:

Authority to open a Paybill account or transact business on behalf of the company 
Appointed persons having signatory authority and provide copies of their identification documents

Bank details

Nominated Safaricom Number to initiate fund withdrawal on behalf of the company (not mandatory)

Copy of Identification Documents of signatory officials i.e. Copy of the National ID/ Military Service Number (Passport/Alien Certificate for Foreign Nationals).

Cancelled cheque of letter from Bank confirming Bank details

# **Register/sign on to M-Chama services**

To sign on to M-Chama, a Chama will need to register at the nearest Bank of Africa branch.

Once registered, every member of the Chama will receive a PIN by SMS on their phone

The new customer will be required to dial \*987# to display a menu of the services available.

To enjoy the M-PESA Pay Bill services, one must be a registered M-PESA customer.

By dialling \*987# and being able to access the M-Chama menu confirms that you are registered.

 **Services Available on M-CHAMA and Accessibility**

The following services are available under M-Chama:

Deposit Cash to your Chama account.

Withdraw cash from your Chama account.

Request for Cash from your Chama account.

Approve Cash Requests.

Check Balance.

Change PIN.

# **Funds accessibility**

The money collected is transferred by the group representative to the bank account provided in the application form.

The group or a group representative will initiate the request for the funds to be transferred to the bank account by logging into a portal access and making the request or sending an email to [Chama@safaricom.co.ke](mailto:Chama@safaricom.co.ke)

# **Accessing funds/Usage and other Services on M-CHAMA**

**To approve Cash Requests**

Dial \*987# to access the mobile platform.

Select M-Chama.

Select your Chama.

Press 1 to select Approve Cash Requests.

Select cash request to approve.

Confirm approval.

# **To request for Cash from your Chama**

Dial \*987# to access the mobile platform.

Select M-Chama.

Select your Chama.

Press 2 to select request cash from Chama.

Enter cash amount.

Select 1 to submit your request.

# **To deposit Cash to your Chama**

Go to Safaricom M-PESA menu.

Select Pay Bills from the menu.

Enter the Bank of Africa business number 972900. followed by your

M-Chama account number.

Enter the amount you wish to transfer.

Enter your M-PESA PIN.

# **To withdraw cash from your Chama**

Dial \*987# to access the mobile platform.

Select M-Chama.

Select your Chama.

Press 2 to select request cash from Chama.

Enter cash amount.

Select 1 to submit your request.

# **To check Balance**

Dial \*987# to access the mobile platform.

Select M-Chama.

Select your Chama.

Press 3 to select Check Balance.

# **To change PIN**

Dial \*987# to access the mobile platform

Select M-Chama.

Select your Chama.

Press 3 to select Change PIN.

Enter current M-Chama PIN.

Enter New M-Chama PIN.

Re-enter New M-Chama PIN.

# **Contact Support**

For more information on M-chama contact contact Bank Of Africa Telephone: 254 703 058 120 / 020 327 5000 SMS: customers can send an enquiry to 20030(chargeable)

Email: [yoursay@boakenya.com](mailto:yoursay@boakenya.com)

**Virtual Meeting Definition and Mechanics**

# **Definition**

Virtual Meetings are the hosting of a meeting in a virtual environment and not face-to-face.

Virtual meetings, sometimes referred to as virtual conferencing, is the hosting of a meeting in a virtual environment and not face-to-face.

# **Objective**

Conferencing services/audio conferencing solutions will help the organization improve business processes and communications while significantly reducing the cost of conducting meetings.

Safaricom offers a total solution including a full portfolio of infrastructure products, high quality bandwidth over various channels and an excellent conferencing management platform.

The product line offers a diverse range of options, from desktop applications to boardroom deployments. Safaricom also operate public rooms for hire at an hourly rate at selected retail centres.

# **Benefits**

Offers real-time conferencing.

Links clients and partners in different geographic locations while making participants feel like they are in the same room.

Cuts down on travel thus reducing costs and increasing flexibility and efficiency.

Shortens product development cycles and time-to-market.

Communication with partners or employees in remote locations is made easier.

Expands services to a wider customer base.

Simple user-friendly platform.

To increase their clients’ trust for the enterprises.

To provide better and more convenient service to their clients.

The Toll-Free service conveys an image that the firm is professional, established and serious about being of service to its customers.

# Fraud

This is an intentionally deceptive action designed to provide the perpetrator with an unlawful gain or to deny a right to a victim.

## 

# M-PESA fraud definition

M-PESA fraud is any dishonesty or deceit involving the M-PESA service which leads to the loss of funds for an M-PESA customer or an Agent.

## 

# Fraudsters Ploys and Strategies

- Pin Disclosure: Fraud types keep changing from time to time but one thing that is constant is the disclosure of PINs by a customer which makes them an easy target for fraudsters.
- Currently most of the M-PESA frauds revolve around irregular swapping of customer lines and withdrawal/transfer of funds.
- There are also customers conned by fraudsters into sending them funds in exchange for goods/services that will never be offered.
- Use of old M-PESA messages. A customer will receive a message showing that they have received Kshs.5xxx from 07xxxxxxx. Then the person calls them requesting to send the money back after he/she sent to a wrong number.
- Fraudsters Impersonating SAF/MPESA staff.
- Receiving extortion messages.
- Agent asking SIM/M-PESA PINS from customers.
- Fake currency
- Agent conned to crediting account.

**Call Conference Definition and Mechanics.**

# **Definition**

- This is the ability to add up to five other persons into a conference call.
- This service allows an A-party to invite several subscribers into a single conversation.
- It is handset dependent. It is accessible by both Prepay and Post-pay customers.

# **Cost**

- The charge is on the initiator of the call.
- They are charged like they are making a separate call to each of the numbers dialled and according to their tariff.

# **Maximum callers allowed in a Conference call**

- Call conferencing will handle a maximum five calls. In case the caller initiates the call to more than 5 people e.g. 6, the extra number(s) will non-discriminatively be dropped.
- But Feature is handset dependent. The network’s maximum is 5 but some handsets might allow fewer calls while other might allow more than that.

# **Call Conference Mechanics**

- Party A initiates a call to Party B, then places the call on hold and calls next number (one needs to activate call wait/hold)
- The procedure is repeated for all numbers needed in the conversation.
- After calling all the numbers the A-party then presses the conference call button on their handset and all parties will be able to communicate.
- Feature is handset dependent. The network’s maximum is 5 but some handsets might allow fewer calls while other might allow more than that.
- All parties to the call can invite other numbers into the call, i.e. once the A-party invites a B-party, the B-party may also originate a call to a C-party who will be able to join the same conference call.
- If the A-party puts a B-party on hold, where the B-party had also invited other numbers into the conference call, those numbers will not go on hold but will be able to continue talking without the A-party.
- Calls can be to Safaricom, Airtel, landlines and international numbers.
- The A-party will be able to conference call while roaming. This is however dependent on the roamed network having a multiparty module on its mobile switching center (MSC)

# **Customer unable to use Call Conference Service**

- Confirm if the customer is using the correct procedure, if not, advise on correct procedure.
- Ensure the customer handset supports the service, if not; advice customer that service is handset dependent.
- Confirm if the customer has enough airtime. If not, advise the customer, if yes verify on HLR whether Call wait/hold is activated, if not, activate the service for customer on HLR under Supplementary Services.
- If the customer meets all this condition and is still unable to use the conference facility, raise an SR (SLA 14hrs) 

**Category:** Value Added Services

**Type:** Call Conference

**Item:** Activate

The Hustler fund is a digital financial inclusion initiative designed to improve financial access to responsible finance for personal, micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs) in Kenya. articleTitle: Call Wait or Hold Definition and Mechanics
markdownContent:
**Call Wait or Hold Definition and Mechanics**

# **Definition**

- Call wait is the ability to get notification of an incoming call while on another call.
- Call hold is the ability to put one caller or an outgoing call on hold in order to handle another call or take a call that is waiting. Call hold is a phone feature that is active while on call.

# **Cost**

Call wait/call hold service is free of charge

# **Call Wait or Hold Activation and Deactivation**

Activation mechanics

Via USSD: A customer dials \*43#ok

# **Deactivation Mechanics**

Via USSD: A customer dials #43#ok

Status check activation, deactivation

A customer can do a Status Service check via: \*#43#ok

# **Call wait and Call Hold Customer Services.**

# **Handling customer Complaints Call Wait or Call Hold**

When customer calls and wants activation, the CEE will assist on activation via HLR/SAWA and offer alternative ways to activate and deactivate via USSD process.

In case the CEE is unable to assist the customer and offer FCR, the CEE will escalate via Service Request (SR) SLA 14hrs.

# **For Call Wait Escalations, use below SR Categories:**

Category: Value Added Services

Type: Call Wait

Item: select appropriate

# **Activating Call Wait or Call Hold Via HLR/SAWA:**

CEE activates for customer on HLR: ‘Supplementary Services’,

Under the “Activate Call Wait & Hold” dropdown.

**Caller Notify Definition and Mechanics**

# **Definition**

Caller Notify Service is a Divert to 0722188188 used only for Not Reachable Reason.

When this divert is used, the caller and called number both get notified as soon as the subscriber is reachable /back on the network to receive a call.

# **Caller Notify Service Mechanics**

Message to caller from the called number is “You attempted to call me, but I was unreachable. I am now back on the network. Please call me. Thank you.”

Message from the calling number to the called number is “I tried to Call you at 10.33am. Please call back “

# **Caller Notify Activation and Deactivation.**

# **Activation mechanics** **Via USSD****:**

To activate Caller, notify service, advice customer to dial \*\*62\*0722188188#ok

# **Deactivation mechanics** 

**Via USSD**

Caller Notify is on USSD menu \*100# and \*200# under Products and Services with Deactivate and manage Blacklist options.

Mobile /USSD based subscriptions cannot be deleted via Siebel. Advise the customer to dial \*100# for Prepay and \*200# on Post-pay and follow the prompts

Dial \*100# or \*200#

Select Products and Services

Select 98 for more

Select Caller Notify

Select Manage blacklist

Select action to perform either

Add to blacklist

Remove from blacklist

List numbers in blacklist

Enter the number to blacklist/remove from blacklist

Confirmation flash message is received

# **DIY Blacklisting numbers on Caller Notify**

If there are specific numbers a customer does not want to be informed when they become available. They can blacklist those customers numbers using the Caller Notify Self Service menus.

**Dial \*100# or \*200#**

Select Products and Services

Select 98 for more

Select Caller Notify

Select Manage blacklist

Select action to perform either

Add to blacklist

Remove from blacklist

List numbers in blacklist

Enter the number to blacklist/remove from blacklist.

Confirmation flash message is received.

# **Customer Care Service for Caller Notify**

Activation Caller Notify Via Sibel/CRM:

A CEE can activate for the customer: On Siebel Subscriber Portal>Supplementary services>Select the product to add and submit request

**NOTE:** Note that you can only subscribe a customer to one call forwarding product at a time.

Deactivation of Caller Notify Via Siebel/CRM:

Query the number on Siebel

Under Subscriber Portal>supplementary services>Uncheck the product to delete and submit the request. The order will complete, and the product removed from the subscriber.

articleTitle: Fraud Key Comments and Action Required
markdownContent:
Key Comments are notes captured on Siebel to quickly alert anyone accessing the account of a unique case of customer behaviour.

CEE should only capture key comment in Siebel, in case a customer reports having shared his/her details to a fraudster, to protect the customer’s account.

**NOTE:** Key comments should not be captured for repeat callers and abusive customers. The CEE will bring into play soft skills to manage the customer on call. If the call does not yield fruit, the CEE will liaise with Team Leader on duty.

# **Key Comments (Customer Triggered)**

- **SMS Spamming** – Sub to visit Retail Centre for vetting and unbarring.
- **Mulot Spamming** – Sub to visit Retail Centre for vetting and unbarring.
- **Irregular line registrations.** Sub to visit Retail Centre for vetting and unbarring

**Call Centre CEE Required Action**

- Customers whose accounts have the above Key comment should be referred to Retail for further assistance.
- Do not inform the customer how many lines are registered on their ID. Let the customer confirm his known lines.
- Where a customer has already 5 lines registered under their ID; any additional line can only be done at our Retail Shop not at an Agent.

**Retail Centre CEE Required Action**

The CEE should vet the customer as per process and confirm the following: -

- Check if the line was calling/sending messages in sequence if so, check if there was a swap on the customer line, and if so confirm if the customer requested for the swap or was it a fraudulent swap. If swap was fraudulent, vet the customer and unbar line on HLR.
- If there was no swap/ was not fraudulent have the customer explain the calls/messages and share with Network fraud via NetworkFraud&M-pesasection@safaricom.co.ke to guide.
- If the calls/messages are not in sequence, get an explanation from the customer for the activity. If satisfactory, vet customer as per process and unbar line.
- If the customer fails vetting the normal process should follow.
- Vet customer let the customer confirm how many lines they have. Block all other lines not belonging to the customer.
- Remove key comment and unblock the line.

# **Key Comments (M-PESA Agent Triggered)**

**Fraud: Sim Swap**: SIM Swap fraud do not unbar – sanctions is termination

**Fraud: Irregular Registrations – Bulk**

In case of customer line: Sub to visit Retail Centre for vetting and unbarring.

For the agent; Use \*195\*4# for future registrations.

- **Spamming / SIM Box / Multiple registrations do not unbar**.
- **Fraud: Suspicious B2C transactions e.g. Equity:**

Suspicious B2C transactions, refer customer to Security department of Bank xxxx

Refer customer to organization Fraud team for validation/clearance

- **Fraud: 234 Fraud – Customer****:** Suspicious Deposit Transactions – Customer to visit Retail Centre for transaction verification.

**Call Centre CEE Required Action**

- Inform Agent that the till was barred for SIM Swap fraud and it is due for termination.
- Agent can visit Safaricom HQ1 with H/Office for clarifications.
- For Customer on Irregular bulk registration: Advise customer to visit the nearest Retail Center / Care Desk.
- For Agent on Irregular bulk registration: CEE to advise as per key comment
- For Multiple Registration fraud CEE to advise Agent suspension period is three months from date of barring by Fraud.
- If 3 Months suspension period has lapsed raise SR with the till details for Support Analyst to send the till to Network fraud for unbarring and inform Agent for future registrations, they will be using \*195\*4#.
- Suspicious B2C transactions e.g. Equity: Customer to be referred to the Head office of the financial institution where their Security department is based for clearance and Send an email to NetworkFraud&M-pesasection@safaricom.co.ke.
- Fraud: 234 Fraud – Customer: Advise Agent to visit the nearest Retail Center / Care Desk

**Retail Centre CEE Required Action**

- Inform Agent that the till was barred for SIM Swap fraud and it is due for termination.
- Agent can visit Safaricom HQ1 with H/Office for clarifications.
- For Customer on Irregular bulk registration: Vet customer and let the customer confirm how many lines they have. Block all other lines not belonging to the customer.
- Remove key comment and unblock the line.
- For Agent on Irregular bulk registration: CEE to advise as per key comment.
- For Multiple Registration fraud CEE to advise Agent suspension period is three months from date of barring by Fraud.
- If 3 Months suspension period has lapsed raise SR with the till details for Support Analyst to send the till to Network fraud for unbarring and inform Agent for future registrations, they will be using \*195\*4#.
- Suspicious B2C transactions e.g. Equity: Customer to be referred to the Head office of the financial institution where their Security department is based for clearance and Send an email to NetworkFraud&M-pesasection@safaricom.co.ke.

**Fraud: 234 Fraud – Customer:** **Check on the last M-PESA Agent deposit and call the depositing agent to confirm if they authorized the transaction. If so, unbar the customer line on HLR. If not, reverse the funds back to the agent**.

# **Key Comments; Refer to Fraud Team**

**Irregular registration / acquisition of golden numbers:** ‘**Do not unbar-Refer to Fraud Team, irregular registration of a Golden number’**

**Call Centre CEE Required Action**

Customers whose accounts have the above Key comments should be referred to Fraud Team for further assistance.

**Retail Centre CEE Required Action**

Customers whose accounts have the above Key comments should be referred to Fraud Team for further assistance.

articleTitle: Please Call Me/Flashback Definition and Mechanics
markdownContent:
**Please Call Me/Flashback Definition and Mechanics**

# **Definition**

Flash Back Message/ Please Call Me is a free service that allows all subscribers to send an SMS message to another subscriber, requesting them to call them back.

# **Cost**

Customers can send 5 free messages allocated for the day and there after send 5 additional messages charged at 50 cents each once they deplete the free messages.

Upon sending the first 5 free Please Call Me requests, subscribers will be notified that they have left 5 chargeable Please Call Me for the day at 50 cents each.

# **Flash Back Message Mechanics**

The service is accessed by dialing \*130\*number# ok

# **Unable to send the 6TH Flashback Messages**

Customer needs to have minimum balance of 50 cents to send the Please Call Me request.

# **Maximum Allowed Flashback Messages Per day**

A customer can send to a maximum of 10 Please Call Me messages daily.

# **Flashback Messages Roll over**

The Flashback Messages Cannot Roll over.

One day’s free Please Call Me sum is 5 and are valid for 24 hours (12:00am – 11.59pm). The next day you get a new set of only 5 free Please Call Me and the 5 chargeable Please Call Me.

 **DIY Checking Please Call Me Message Balance**

- Customer dials \*130\*number# ok,
- A flash message appears on the screen showing the number of flash backs remaining for the day. E.g. you have 4 free flashback messages left to send
