# **Safaricom PRS appointment process****.**

1. Upon receipt of the mandatory requirements, the applicant will be called to sign a Non-Disclosure agreement (NDA) before further engagement
2. Once the Applicant has signed and returned the NDA, they are to send their business proposal via email to prspsupport@safaricom.co.ke
3. Safaricom is to review the business proposal and schedule for a meeting on the same.
4. Upon approval of business proposal, the applicant shall fill in the technical evaluation forms for approval.
5. Upon approval of the technical evaluation, the applicant shall be issued with a certificate to allow for connection onto the Safaricom SMSC
6. Applicant to sign appointment contract and return to Safaricom legal team
7. Filling in of supplier details form
8. Payment of connection to the Safaricom SMSC should be done before access is granted.
9. Connection fee is Ksh.75,000/- plus 16% VAT
10. Upon appointments as a Safaricom PRS Provider, connection to the following is allowed point to point connection, mapping of PRS VLAN id to the connection

# **Technical requirements**

1. Manage at own cost the point to pint link with Safaricom
2. Offer minimum capacity of 40 SMS’s per second
3. Safaricom approved 3rd party content software and hardware specifications
4. Technical and Customer Support center team available 24 hours

# **Financial requirement**

1. Initial setup fee of Ksh.75,000/- inclusive of 16% VAT
2. Monthly short code fee of Ksh.10,000/-
3. One off golden number (easy to remember numbers) fee of Ksh.200,000/-

# **Revenue share/payment methodology****.**

1. The premium rate service attracts a charge above the normal SMS/call charge rate.
2. The revenue generated is therefore split between the network operator and the PRS provider
3. In cases the PRS provider is running a campaign on behalf of a 3rd party, they too get revenue share based on the agreement with the PRS provider.
4. The revenue share varied from service to service and is exclusive of government taxes and VAT.

**Other requirements****.**

These shall be communicated from time to time. Please send mail to prspsupport@safaricom.co.ke for any clarifications

**NB:**

1. Safaricom Reserves the right to accept or reject any application
2. There are three aspects to PRS; Voice based, SMS based and USSD based.
 - Voice based usually comes with 0900 numbers as a prefix obtained from CCK.
 - SMS based are usually short codes; in our case we issue 4-digit codes to the PRS
 - USSD based are usually 3-digit service codes

# **LTE | 5G NOT CONNECTING.**

- The CEE will confirm what error the client is getting when they try to connect to the internet.
- The CEE will check on the account status on INDATA if normal or suspended. If suspended check on account balance and advice the customer appropriate.
- The CEE will also check on HRL if the line is suspended or barred on BAGPRS.
- The CEE will confirm if payment is done also check if on INDATA the product is normal.
- If on check on HLR the link is barred on BAGPRS the CEE will share an email for the CI to be unbared to CMCCSPostpaid@Safaricom.co.ke
- While still on HLR, scroll down to confirm if APN is provisioned.
- The CEE will login to SOC Tool GDE and search for Quality Complaint Handling and query the MSISDN. 

Note the following details will be populated.

Subscriber Information

Automatic Fault Diagnosis

Service Experience Overview

Detailed Records and GIS

- The CEE will analysis the above details and note the Fault Diagnosis and the Demarcation Result and Handling Suggestion and advice the customer appropriate.
- If all parameters above are confirmed okay for Indoor Units and the client is still unable to connect, purge the number and advise the customer to reboot the router. If the problem persists, refer the customer to visit any nearest retail shop for assistance.
- The CEE will advise the customer for indoor routers to remove the sim card from the router and insert into a different handset, this is to confirm if the Sim card is prompting for a PIN, if so, client should >Enter pin>go to phone settings and disable PIN request.
- The CEE will request the customer to return the Sim card properly to the router and reboot. Should the above fail to work/resolve the problem, advise the customer to visit any nearest retail shop for assistance.

Note: If the customer can’t remember the sim PIN, advise them to visit retail for a sim swap. If the sim card is not prompting for a PIN, advise the customer to properly insert the Sim card and reboot the router.

For Indoor unit, ask the customer to remove the sim card and read the sim card Serial Number to counter check with what you have on the system. If the SN is different advice the customer to visit the shop for assistance.

The CEE will ask the client to check if the outdoor cable from the ODU is properly connected to the IDU (Indoor Unit). If not, advise the client to properly connect the cable. If properly and the issue persist, raise a service request to 2nd Level Support

If all parameters above are confirmed okay and the client is still unable to connect, purge the number and advise the customer to reboot the router. Remember ODU takes time to pick than IDU after reboot.

# **SLOW SPEEDS**

- If the customer calls and complain of the Speed. The CEE will first confirm the account status and the customer package on INDATA. Either 5mbps, 3mbps or LTE Fixed Wireless or 5G etc.)

- If on 5mbps or 5G and status is okay proceed with other checks.

- If on 3mbps, confirm if the customer is browsing with the full speeds or is on FUP (throttled speeds). If on FUP, advise accordingly.

- If on LTE Fixed Wireless Bronze, Silver, Gold or Diamond and the bundle are exhausted advice accordingly for the client to either repurchase via \*485# or wait for monthly allocation.

- The CEE will check if the APN is provisioned, if not, provision.

- The CEE will login and check on Allot on the utilization by graphing the link.

- The CEE will advise as per the Allot output. If the customer link is maxing the CEE will advise the customer to consider upgrading his/her bandwidth or manage his/her utilization.

- The CEE will advise the customer on the protocols that are using most of his/ her link bandwidth.

- If the Link parameters are confirmed okay, not maxing, and the CEE will purge the MSISDN and advise the customer to reboot the router. If the issue persists, raise a service request to 2nd Level Support.

The customer will then contact the partner for reversal request as per the current process.

- Where both contacts are available as above, the customer will get the SMS below;

***“Dear Customer, kindly contact (organization name) on 254703070707 or 254732170170 for reversal request of transaction NF326QBXXX. Thank You.”***

Where either of the contacts above are available, the customer will get the SMS below depending on the contact;

***“Dear Customer, kindly contact (organization name) on 254703070707 for reversal request of transaction NF326QBLVM. Thank You.”***

Where the contact of the LNM paybill partner is missing contact, the customer will get the SMS below;

***“Dear Customer, kindly contact 100 or 200 to get contacts for (Organization name) for reversal request of transactions NF326QXXX. Thank you.”***

articleTitle: Internet of Things definition and Mechanics
markdownContent:
# **Definition**

IoT or Internet of Things is network of communication-enabled assets with application servers with view to monitor or control the assets.

The assets have sensors that collect information about the assets i.e. speed, humidity, operating conditions and sends them to the application server via communication gadgets using SIM cards.

#  

# **Importance of IoT to businesses**

With digitization as part of their competitive and survival strategy, businesses are employing IoT to connect to and collect data from their trade assets which powers data driven business models.

Such businesses enjoy the following benefits:

- Operational and cost efficiency through automation and process optimization through reduction of manual errors in their business processes i.e. smart metering.

- Drive innovation leveraging analytics from consumption patterns and real time.

# **Target customers for IOT**

Safaricom IoT SIM Management solution can be used across various vertical industries where cellular IoT technology has been adopted.

The service is offered to any registered business within any of the listed industries using IoT solutions.

| Vertical Industry | Use Case |
| --- | --- |
| Automotive | Vehicle trackingFleet ManagementTelematics Based Insurance |
| Health | Remote patient monitoring |
| Utilities | Smart GridSmart Power MeteringSmart Water MeteringOil & Gas Metering |
| Financial Services | Agency bankingMobile Point of Sales |
| Retail Sector | Asset Management & Tracking |
| Public Sector | Smart City initiatives i.e. Surveillance, Smart Parking |
| Transport & Logistics | Cargo Tracking |

# **Safaricom Shared IoT APN**

- Safaricom shared IoT internet APN is a cost effective and secure device-to Internet communication using public internet infrastructure.
- This is secured using access control lists restrictions to prevent devices visiting unallowed IP addresses by white listing only allowed IoT server IP addresses on the internet firewall.
- Network Address Translation implementation means a direct connection to device from the Internet is not possible to enhance IoT service security.

# **Private internet APN**

This connectivity option allows secure connection of IoT devices to the IoT server hosted within the enterprise private I.T. network through internet IPSec VPN, keeping sensitive information tunneled from the SIM cards to the infrastructure via the named private internet APN.

# **Private corporate APN**

- This option allows connection of IoT devices directly and securely to the IoT server hosted within the enterprise private I.T. network using leased corporate lines i.e. MPLS links and other fixed connectivity options.
- Data from the IoT devices and SIM cards is tunnelled to the corporate infrastructure via named corporate APN.

# **Safaricom Global IoT SIM Card**

- This is special SIM card, designed and optimized for IoT/M2M services.
- It enables IoT devices to securely and seamlessly connect to customers IoT servers across multiple operator networks.
- The SIM cards are conveniently be managed by Safaricom IoT Connectivity platform.
- Safaricom Global IoT SIM card is designed and optimized for IoT/M2M communication, thus does not support typical human communication services.
- It is not possible to swap normal SIM cards for Safaricom Global IoT SIM cards over the air; thus, migration involves physical swapping of the SIM cards. Safaricom supports this migration by allowing customers to hold stock of the Global IoT SIM cards, the swapping the SIM cards at their convenience.

Its unique features include:

- Support only Data and SMS services
- Voice and USSD services are not supported
- IoT SIM cards are ruggedized to withstand extreme conditions i.e. withstand vibration and temperatures

# **Definition and features of Safaricom IoT Platform**

- Safaricom IoT SIM Management platform is a set of tools and features that provide reliable, secure and managed IoT device to server communication with tools that give complete visibility and control over an entire IoT connectivity infrastructure.
- This web-based portal offers IoT service providers or business within house IoT solutions a single and centralized interface to monitor and control IoT SIM cards.
- Users can monitor real time connection status, view resource usage per SIM, troubleshoot network and device faults as well as perform basic IoT SIM card inventory.

The solution has the following components:

Safaricom Global IoT SIM Card

IoT Optimized Network

IoT SIM Management Platform

# **The value of Safaricom IoT SIM Management Platform**

An efficient way to manage IoT SIM cards fitted in remote assets is a headache to many enterprises, and the problem is compounded as the solution scales to thousands of connected assets.

Safaricom IoT SIM Management Portal grants enterprises enhanced visibility and control over the IoT infrastructure. It has the following inbuilt functionalities:

Widgets that visualizes IoT device connectivity

Customizable reporting capabilities

Tools to configure and troubleshoot IoT SIM connectivity issues

Customizable event triggers that monitor and control resource usage

The IoT SIM Management Portal is an intuitive enterprise for IoT connectivity. Do It Yourself portal that can be used in:

- Accurate IoT SIM card and device inventory
- Data and SMS Resource audit and usage control
- Single and first point of contact to trouble shoot service issues

# **Supported connectivity options for IoT**

Safaricom IoT SIM Management solution enables IoT devices to securely connect to the servers. The following connectivity options are supported:

IP connectivity via 2G, 3G and 4G packet network

SMS service

IP connectivity is secured through Safaricom IoT APN, private internet APN or private corporate VPN depending on the customer requirements.

# **IoT support channels**

Customer shall provide mobile numbers that shall be allowed to contact Safaricom Business Support during onboarding.

The following support channels are available to on boarded customers:

- Normal Business Support channels or telephone: 0722002222
- Email: business.support@safaricom.co.ke
- Dedicated Platinum Engineer

articleTitle: KCB M-PESA Account Opening for Fixed & Target Accounts
markdownContent:
# **DEFINITION**

This is a service that allows the KCB M-pesa customer to save money for a specific period and earn interest for the money deposited.

**ELIGIBILITY**

This service is open to all KCB M-pesa registered customers

**DIY ACCOUNT OPENING MECHANICS FOR FIXED SAVINGS ACCOUNT**

- Access M-PESA menu
- Select Loans and Savings
- Select KCB M-PESA
- Select Fixed Savings Account
- Select Fixed deposit
- Open Account
- Select the source of funds; M-PESA/KCB M-PESA
- Enter amount (amount needs to be more than KES 500)
- Enter period (1, 3, 6 or 12 months)
- Enter M-PESA PIN and confirm the transaction
- The Customer will receive an M-PESA confirmation.

# **Key features on Fixed Savings account.**

- The customer will not be able to top-up to the amount locked.
- Locked periods: 1, 3, 6, and 12 months.
- Minimum amount to be locked KSh. 500, there is no maximum limit.
- The balance in the account will earn an interest and will also be used to improve loan limits.
- Minimum period for locking: 1 month.
- Interest on savings rate is at 6.3 % p.a.
- Upon early /premature redemption the customer forfeits all interest accrued.
- The customer can have only one fixed savings account at a time.
- The customer gets cash back immediately to KCB M-PESA account on prompting cash back.

# **DIY ACCOUNT OPENING MECHANICS FOR TARGET ACCOUNT**

- Go to M-PESA menu
- Select Loans and Savings
- Select KCB M-PESA
- Select Fixed Savings
- Select Target Savings Account
- Select Open Account
- Select source of funds; M-PESA/KCB M-PESA
- Enter Target amount you intend to save for the period (amount needs to be more than KES 1000)
- Enter period (1, 3, 6 or 12 months)
- Enter initial deposit amount (not less than KES 50)
- Enter M-PESA PIN and confirm transaction.
- The customer will receive an M-PESA confirmation message.

# **Key features Target Account**

- Target Periods: 1,3,6 and 12 months.
- Minimum contribution amount: KSh. 50, there is no Maximum limit.
- Minimum target period: 1 month.
- Interest is earned daily and paid on maturity or upon breaking lock.
- Customers get cash back immediately to KCB M-PESA account on requesting withdrawal.
- Customers enjoy attractive Interest rates of 6.3% p.a. on savings.

# **Benefits of Target Account**

- Customer tops up continuously until he achieves the target.
- The customer can choose from target periods of 1, 3, 6 and 12 months with a minimum contribution of KES 50.
- The interest earned is cumulative.
- Early withdrawal of funds from Target Savings is allowed; subject to withdrawal of the entire amount saved. Total interest on savings will be earned to the day of the withdrawal.
- The customer get cash back immediately to his KCB M-PESA account on prompting cash back.
- Minimum target period is 1 month.
- The customer enjoys attractive Interest rates of 6.3% p.a. on savings.
- The customers are allowed up to 4 withdrawals within target lock period to maintain interest.

**TRANSACTIONS STATUS ENQUIRIES (SAVINGS, FIXED,TARGET AND LOAN ACCOUNTS)**

When a customer contacts Contact Centre with an KCB M-PESA transaction query, the CEE shall apply Contact Center Vetting Process to confirm the status of the transaction on both CRM under KCB M-PESA Tab and M-PESA G2.

# **Authorized Transactions.**

- If the transaction is authorized and there is no outage, raise an SR to Support team and advise customer on **72hrs SLA**. The sr details are as follows:
- **Sr category**: KCB M-PESA
- **Type**: Savings Withdrawal Transaction
- **Item**: Authorised Transaction
- The Support Analyst shall liaise with FS Team for action. These transactions are either completed or cancelled by the FS IT team globally within 24hrs.
- Once actioned the Support Analyst will advise the customers as per the resolution and close the SR.

**Declined/ Cancelled Transactions (M-PESA/ KCB M-PESA Deposits)**.

- For declined/cancelled transaction and there is no outage reported, confirm from M-PESA if the customer has sufficient funds to facilitate the deposit to KCB M-PESA Savings account.
- Where funds are sufficient, advise the customer to repeat the transaction. If the funds are insufficient, advise the customer to deposit funds into MPESA account and try again.
- If it still fails, the CEE will advise the customer to use ussd \*334#

**Savings Withdrawal Declined/Cancelled**

- If the transaction is declined/cancelled and no outage reported; confirm whether the customer has sufficient funds on KCB M-PESA savings account to facilitate withdrawal.
- If the balance is sufficient, confirm whether the customer’s account has been blacklisted due to an outstanding loan or any previously cancelled transaction by querying the customer’s number on [KCB](https://cmintranet/index.php?option=com_php&Itemid=1236) M-PESA blacklist check on CC Systems.
- If there is an outstanding loan, advise the customer to clear the outstanding loan amount either from M-PESA or from KCB M-PESA Savings account to be able to withdraw from KCB M-PESA Savings account.
- In case of a cancelled withdrawal due to an outstanding KCB M-PESA loan, advise the customer to deposit an amount equivalent to the amount on the cancelled transaction(s) and contact KCB to facilitate the system to recover the amount.

**Missing Transactions (M-PESA/KCB M-PESA)**

- If there is no outage reported, countercheck to verify the transactions were done from M-PESA G2 to KCB M-PESA account.
- If the transaction is not available on M-PESA G2, advise the customer to repeat the transaction.
- If the transaction is available on M-PESA G2 and missing on KCB M-PESA, the CEE shall escalate via SR for the Support team to assist and advise the customer on **72hrs SLA**. The sr details are as follows:

- **Sr category**: KCB M-PESA
- **Type**: Savings Withdrawal Transaction
- **Item**: Missing Transaction 
- The Support Analyst will countercheck on the cancelled transaction and if still missing, raise a BMC to KCB Bank to update the transaction(s).
- Once the Bank sends a response, the analyst shall advise the customer as per the resolution on the BMC activity and close the SR.

**Cancelled/Declined Loan Request Transaction.**

Confirm if there is any global issue reported. If no global issue reported, check the status of the account to confirm whether the account qualifies for a loan. This can be checked using the below parameters:

**M-PESA Account age on Network.**

- Confirm whether the customer’s M-PESA account is more than six months old.
- If not, advise the customer that the account should be more than six months old to get a loan.

**Loan Restrict.**

- Query the number on KCB M-PESA Tab on CRM and confirm the customer’s loan limit. Where the loan limit is 0, advise the customer that they do not qualify for a loan. 
- Where the customer has a loan limit, confirm the amount they are trying to borrow.
- If the loan requested exceeds the maximum loan limit advise the customer on both the DIY option to check limit and available limit that can be accessed.
- Confirm the customers CRB Status under KCB M-PESA tab on CRM and advise the customer as per the Status (Status 0 and 1) and advise the customer to contact KCB customer care to confirm if they are blacklisted by the bank or CRB for further assistance.
- Where the customer gets an error of KCB M-PESA account not recognized, raise SR and advise the customer on **72hrs SLA**. The SR details are as follows:
- **Sr category**: KCB M-PESA
- **Type**: Savings Withdrawal Transaction
- **Item**: Declined/cancelled Transaction

- The support analyst will raise a BMC remedy to the bank and await resolution, advise the customer on the resolution, and close the SR.

**Declined/Cancelled Loan Repayment Transaction.**

- If no global issue reported, confirm if the customer has an outstanding loan and if any, advise customer on the DIY option of checking the loan balance.
- Where the customer has an outstanding loan, confirm if the customer has sufficient funds on M-PESA and KCB M-PESA account to make the payment.
- If amount is not sufficient, advise the customer to replenish their M-PESA and KCB M-PESA account balance before retrying the transaction and if the amount is sufficient and the customer is unable to make a payment, advise the customer to contact KCB for assistance.
- Where the customer has not been assisted by the Bank, escalate via SR and advise the customer on 72hrs SLA. The SR details are as follows:
 - **Sr category**: KCB M-PESA
 - **Type**: Customer loan account
 - **Item**: Loan Repayment

- The support analyst shall raise a BMC ticket and await resolution from the bank, advise the customer as per resolution and close the SR

articleTitle: Process of Refund to a Non-Fibre Ready Area.
markdownContent:
# **Process of** **Refund** **to a** **Non-Fibre Ready Area**

Newly created customers will receive refunds of payments done after confirmation that client’s premises is not fibre ready. Line 400 folder team will receive request to refund payments either on email or on service request ticket.

# **Refund Request Via** **Email**

- Home tech dispatch team will send email to the folder team confirming that client is not within fibre ready area and a refund to be processed.
- The L400 CEE will confirm the mode of payment that client used. For payments done at a retail shop, CEE will raise an SR, send an email to the specific retail shop and request reversal to be done to an M\-PESA account as specified by the customer.
- For payments done via M\-PESA, the CEE will confirm the transaction details using M\-PESA G2 system and check if payment reflected on CRM. The L400 CEE will then raise an SR and attach the email request sent from dispatch team. Any payment done within 48 hours will be reversed on CRM.
- The CEE will contact the customer and advise on reason why the reversal was done, close the SR and advise on alternative option of getting a 4G router.
- When raising an activity, the CEE should break larger amount exceeding KES 5000 into multiples of KES 5000 and ensure they capture the associated MPESA transaction to avoid a wrong transaction being reversed and reason for reversal as captured on Remedy and CI Sr.

# **Refund Request Via** **SR**

- The L400 CEE will confirm the transaction details using M\-PESA G2 system and check if payment reflected on CRM.
- Any payment done within 48 hours will be reversed on CRM. For payments done in the last 48 hours, a decrement request will be done on the ticket for funds to be debited from the FTTH account and reversal will be completed using 150501 reversal portals.
- The CEE will contact the ccustomers and advise on reason why the reversal was done and close the SR.CEE will advise on alternative option of getting a 4G router.
- For payments done via airtime purchase, CEE will raise an SR for airtime reversal and assign Support team with an SLA of within 24 hours. CEE will contact client and advise on reason why the reversal was done, close the SR and advise on alternative option of getting a 4G router.

articleTitle: Definition, Types of My SMS Service/PRS, Promotional SMS and GET IT 411
markdownContent:
# **My SMS/ Premium Rate Services**

- My SMS or PRS texts are messages about services, NEWS or entertainment sent to Safaricom customers upon their request or as push messages from businesses.
- Safaricom has partnerships with licensed Premium Rate Service (PRS)/My SMS providers whose core business is to run services and promotions on short codes leased to them by Safaricom.
- There is no limit to the number of My SMS Services one can subscribe to.

# **Types of My SMS Services**

# **Chargeable services**

- **Voice based**: This comes with 0900 prefix obtained from Communication Authority of Kenya (CA).
- **Short Message Service (SMS) based**: They come from 5-digit codes sender ID.
- **Unstructured Supplementary Service Data (USSD) based**: These are usually 3-digit service codes e.g. \*620#

**NB**: Charges vary depending on the service provider and channel.

# **On demand services**

- On Demand services are those that customers use to request for information and are billed only upon the request.
- No messages are sent to the customer unless the customer repeats the request again.
- The Customer is charged a one-off fee. Examples include KCPE, KCSE results query, news feedback etc.

**N.B**. The services are NOT displayed on the SDP tab in CRM, but the billing can be viewed on IN Transaction History.

# **Bulk****/Promotional Messages**

- Promotional Messages are used by organizations such as banks, corporates, enterprises, SMEs and Political Parties to communicate to their subscribers from time to time.
- The messages range from ATM notifications, bank transactions OTP (One Time Password) messages to promotional and general information.
- The messages are sent from sender names e.g. Safaricom, KCB, Java etc. at no cost to the recipient and are free of charge to the recipient customer(s).

**Note:**

- Information on promotional messages is now available on CRM SDP**(SDP Promotional sms)** or on USSD menu under Marketing Messages. Agents can now blacklist promotional messages on behalf of customers and also view what has previously been blacklisted
- Corporates get customer contacts for Promotional SMS in two main ways:
 1. When customers transact through their M-PESA accounts, tills or Paybills.
 2. By directly asking their customers to share their numbers for communication where you wish to receive any information relevant to their product or service.

# **Promotional SMS Blacklisting on CRM**

- Query the MSISDN on Siebel:
- Access the SDP tab and select on *SDP Promotional SMS.*
- Ask the customer to ***SPELL*** the name of the promotional SMS they want to blacklist.
- Enter the sender ID customer has given under ***Blacklist Sender Name***
- Press enters and you shall see a pop message on CRM confirming the sender name has been blacklisted.
- Confirm with the customer receipt of SMS from their end confirming the blacklist.
- Capture an interaction with the action e.g. “*Promotional SMS SENDER ID Naivas has been blacklisted as per customer request*” Educate the customer on the self-service procedure in case they need to deactivate/reactivate code in future using the \*100# (Prepay) or \*200# (Postpay) or \*456\*9\*5# ok
- Send an SMS via Siebel on how to Blacklist promotional SMS in future.

NB; If a customer wants all promotional SMS to be blacklisted CEE should type the word ***ALL*** as the Sender ID. Please educate the customer that they shall not get any promotional messages when they blacklist all.

# **Promotional SMS REACTIVATION on CRM**

- Query the MSISDN on Siebel:
- Access the SDP tab and select on *SDP Promotional SMS.*
- Ask the customer to ***SPELL*** the name of the promotional SMS they want to Activate
- Press enters and you shall see a pop message on CRM confirming the sender name has been Activated.
- Confirm with the customer receipt of SMS from their end confirming the reactivation.

NB;CEE can also search a sender name on SDP Promotional SMS Tab on CRM to confirm if it is Transactional or promotional. Any sender ID which is promotional,CEE should raise SR for 2nd line to escalate to partners.

# **GET IT 411**

**Definition**

- - This is an SMS service where a customer can receive information of different channels/services that are provided at a premium.
 - Customers can receive information automatically by sending any of the corresponding key words for different push channels.
 - This is delivered via SMS in the form of alerts or updates.
 - Customer can subscribe to more than one channel.

# **GET IT 411 charges**

Charges are Ksh.3 for SMSs received from 21411.

# **MDUNDO MIX**

**Definition.**

MDUNDO MIXES is an internet Music streaming and download platform offering the best in entertainment of unlimited and exclusive DJ mixtapes, on any device, anywhere, anytime, in the English language and other languages.

**Subscription.**

Customers will subscribe from mdundo.com.

**Charges.**

The customers will be charged ksh 5 daily for the mdundo mix content.

**How to unsubscribe**

Upon subscription customers will receive a link upon which they will be directed to the mdundo web link(Mdundo.com) to unsubscribe.

Customers can also unsubscribe from mdundo.com.

articleTitle: DIY Procedures & Service Management for M-PESA Customer Account
markdownContent:
# **How to Deposit** **at an Agent**

- This is a process of changing Cash to E-money.
- It is done by an authorized MPESA agent.
- At the M-PESA agency the customer will:

Have the phone they intend to deposit at the shop.

Present the cash and original ID to the agent.

Give out the mobile number for the agent to deposit.

After the deposit the customer will receive the confirmation message with the transaction details.

The amount will reflect on the customer's M-PESA account.

# **How to Withdraw at an Agent**

- Customer should ensure they are at the agency where they intend to withdraw, if far the transaction will decline.
- This is done by the customer from their phone via: -

STK (MPESA Menu).

My Safaricom App.

# **STK (MPESA MENU)**

- Go to Sim Took kit/Safaricom tool kit on the phone.
- Choose MPESA.
- From the options select Withdraw cash.
- Choose from Agent.
- Enter agent number.
- Enter the amount to Withdraw.
- Insert MPESA PIN.
- Confirm with Hakikisha.
- A confirmation message will be sent with the transaction details.

# **MY SAFARICOM APP**

- Open the Safaricom App on your phone.
- Go to MPESA
- From the options choose to Withdraw.
- Select from agent.
- Enter agent number and amount and press Next.
- Confirm with Hakikisha.
- Enter MPESA Pin.
- A confirmation message will be sent with the transaction details.

**NB:**

- Once the customer completes the withdrawal and gets a confirmation message, the agent will also get a message on their MPESA agent transacting till.
- The customer will present the original ID for the agent to record and disburse funds.

# **How To Withdrawal at an ATM**

**On the** **phone: -**

- Go to M-PESA menu.
- Select Withdraw Cash.
- Select from ATM.
- Enter the Agent Number as displayed on the Bank ATM.
- Enter your M-PESA PIN.
- You will receive an SMS notification from M-PESA with a 6-digit authorization code. The code expires after 10 minutes, and you will be expected to initiate the transaction afresh if you need to withdraw money again.

**On the ATM:**

- Select the M-PESA button on the Bank ATM.
- Select your preferred language.
- Enter the 6-digit ATM authorization code on the ATM keyboard.
- Enter your Safaricom mobile number.
- Enter the amount you wish to withdraw.
- Press continue button to proceed with the transaction.
- ATM will dispense your cash and issue you with a receipt.
- You will also receive an SMS from M-PESA confirming the transaction.

# **How To Send M-PESA Tuma Popote**

**Via USSD**

- Dial \*334#.
- Select Send Money.
- Select Send to another network.
- Enter Recipient Number.
- Enter Amount.
- Enter MPESA Pin.
- Confirm the transaction details via Hakikisha.
- Accept/Cancel the transaction by confirming on the menu.

**Via SAFARICOM APP**

- Open Safaricom App.
- Select the option with send money.
- Choose to send to other networks.
- Enter mobile number.
- Enter the amount.
- Enter MPESA Pin.

**NB:**

- Money sent via M-PESA Tuma Popote will be credited directly to the recipient’s mobile money wallet where it can be accessed.
- The minimum you can send is Ksh.101.
- Customers sending funds from the Sim Tool kit will be charged the current send money on net tariff, which will apply.
- This applies to lines registered on Mobile Money services only.
- If a customer tries to send to an unregistered customer, the transaction will fail with the following error: *‘’Dear customer, the number you are sending to is not registered for mobile money.*
- If a customer tries to send to a line that is not registered on any network, the transaction will fail.

# **DIY HAKIKISHA SERVICE**

**Opting In**

- Customers will automatically opt into the free service.
- If a customer opts out, they can opt back in by:

Dial \*234#.

Select MY M-PESA information.

Select HAKIKISHA.

Select opt-in.

**Opting Out**

- Dial \*234#,
- Select MY M-PESA information.
- Select HAKIKISHA
- Select opt out.

**Note:** Other customers will also not be able to confirm your name when you opt out of the service.

**If the customer does not receive the notification pop out (STK Push) to enter the M-PESA PIN.**

- There are cases where my SIM card will not be updated. Please find solutions as below: -

| Scenario | Solution |
| --- | --- |
| If you have an Old SIM Card | You will be required to swap your SIM Card at the nearest retail center/M-PESA Agent outlet |
| Poor network signal or Unreachable | Ensure that your phone is on and in a place with good network signal |

# **DIY CHECK M-PESA TARIFF CHARGES**

**Querying M-PESA Tariff on the Phone**

- Dial \*234# when the phone is on standby mode.
- Select My MPESA Information
- Tariff Query
- Options that will appear, and the customer can select their desired option.

Withdrawal

Send money

ATM withdrawal

Deposit

Lipa Na M-PESA

Once they select the option; the system will ask them to enter ‘*the M-PESA amount’* they want to query the charges. (for the first 4 options).

The system will respond with a message indicating the amount and the respective M-PESA charge. See sample message below.

*‘**To send 1000, you will be charged ksh13 if recipient is registered or Ksh66 if the recipient is registered on another network. Thank you for using M-PESA service.’***

**NB:** The M-PESA USSD (\*234#) service has been updated with the revised M-PESA tariff charges.

# **Definition**

SD-WAN is a service that enables businesses to quickly and securely transmit data between multiple business premises independent of the internet also known as Software Defined Wide Area Network

It is a service that is eligible to all existing and new customers from across both SME and Large enterprise segments of the market.

# **Eligibility**

It’s a Postpaid service.

Application can be done by filling out an application form provided by a sales executive.

New customers will be required to provide the relevant KYC documentation which includes the following:

- Certified Copy of Certificate of Incorporation
- Certified Copy of Company PIN Certificate
- Dully filled in & signed SDWAN Application Form
- Certificate of Registration
- Letter from an Authorised person in the agency/Ministry/Parastatal for Government - agencies, ministries, parastatals
- Contract document for Government - agencies, ministries, parastatals

# **Key Features**

- SD-WAN utilizes a centralized management function to route traffic safely and intelligently through the WAN.
- It provides the flexibility to support hybrid WAN connectivity combining private (MPLS) with Internet connected sites.
- It supports both a hub-and-spoke and branch to branch Dynamic Multi-Path Optimization and VPN features.
- It securely connects users to any application, both in the data center and in the cloud, across all WAN transport services, including broadband Internet service.
- It has Dynamic Multi-Path Optimization which ensures that different WAN circuits have their performance and capacity optimally and automatically used to provide assured application performance.
- Dynamic Multi-Path Optimization includes three critical capabilities for assuring application performance.
- Continuous monitoring of link performance including packet loss, latency and jitter.
- It has a capacity that provides real-time information to protect against brownouts and blackouts.
- Cloud-hosted Gateways provide security and ease of management benefits between enterprise sites directly to cloud destinations such as SaaS and IaaS.

# **SD-WAN Service Onboarding**

- Each customer onboarded shall be given access to call support line 2222 on their specified contact MSISDN.
- Once done the request will be forwarded to FD Billing Delivery Team for billing via service request on CRM and a completed BPM activity from TES PM.
- Once receipted and the service is activated the executive will close the service request and notify TES PM and the account manager of the same.

# **Suspend & Resume SD WAN Services**

- Suspension and resuming may arise from debt management by credit control or customer request.
- Fixed data credit and collection milestones will apply for service denial due to debt or arrears on connectivity and SDWAN service.
- Credit and collection team will instruct ECS support to suspend service on the SD-WAN portal for SDWAN service.
- Upon service suspension, ECS shall enter an Interaction on CRM with an appropriate comment.
- Credit collection team will suspend billing on CBS if a customer does not make payment before next bill run.
- Credit collection team shall instruct unsuspension of an SDWAN customer upon payment of the arrears.
- In case of erroneous service reactivation, person liable for this is the person who performed the reactivation action.
- The SDWAN service cannot run without the link service uptime unless it is on 3rd Party internet where only SDWAN Portal services will be enforced.

# **Customer Contact Support for SD-WAN**

- The agent receiving the query will probe the customer, determine possible diagnosis and resolve the issue raised.
- The agent will confirm the account status on INDATA if normal or suspended. If suspended confirm the account balance and share with the customer.
- The agent will check on HLR and confirm if the APN is provisioned ie apn|SDWAN
- The agent will login to SOC Tool GDE and search for Quality Complaint Handling and query the MSISDN. From the result the CEE will analysis the Fault Diagnosis plus the Demarcation Result and Handling Suggestion and advice the customer appropriate.
- The agent will purge the line ask the customer to reboot.
- In a scenario the issue cannot be resolved, the same shall be escalated to a second 2nd level via service request ticket.

articleTitle: Skiza Artists, Onboarding and Artist Portal Account
markdownContent:
# **Skiza artists**

**Definition**

articleTitle: DIY Procedures for Skiza Tune and Skiza for Business
markdownContent:
# **Downloading Skiza**

1. **Via USSD**

- Dial \*811# OK, select your preferred Category and follow the prompts.
- Dial \*100# OK, Select My subscription then Skiza, select the Category of your choice and follow the prompts.
- Dial \*456# OK, Select buy then Skiza, select your preferred Category and follow the prompts.
- Dial \*200# OK, Select Products and services then Skiza, select your preferred Category and follow the prompts.

*(USSD service is Free of charge)*

2. **Via IVR:** by dialing 811 and follow instructions - (Charged at Kshs. 3 per minute)
3. **Via Web:** Download directly from www.skiza.safaricom.com (data charges apply).
4. **Via Zuri:** chat bot, write Skiza and follow prompts.

# **Recording Business Tune**

Send an SMS with their preferred message or enquiry to the short code 22229. At a cost of Kshs. 10.

Submit their already done 30 second jingle for review using the email businesstunes@bluewatergroup.co.ke.

Query the progress of their request by sending unique name e.g. SAF14 to the short code 22229.

The Business tune will be renewed at KES.5.00 daily which translates to KES.150 monthly.

# **Business tune activation**

Recording a New tune

If Client wish tune to be recorded, they send an SMS with their preferred message or enquiry to the short code 22229. Each SMS costs Ksh. 10.

They will be required to either submit your already done 30 second jingle for review using the email **businesstunes@bluewatergroup.co.ke.**

Subscribers can query the progress of their request by sending unique name e.g. SAF14 to the short code 22229.

The Business tune will be renewed at KES.5.00 daily which translates to KES.150 monthly.

# **Business tune deactivation**

- Simply Dial \*811# and select Manage Active Tunes option 5
- If client unsubscribe from the service, any remaining paid days will be lost.
- No refund for any unused elements of your ring back tune service will be available.

# **To Note while Roaming:**

Your Business Tune Ring Back will not be heard while you are roaming.

# **Business Tune Changing of Content:**

If you would like another Business tune customized, send an SMS with your preferred message or enquiry to the short code 22229. Your request will be processed. Each SMS costs Kshs. 10.

# **Skiza Gifting:**

- Send SMS to 811(Kshs 1 per sms) in the following format; GIFT Skiza (RBT) code <a space> recipient number (without initial zero). For example,>GIFT 7010001 722123456.
- The charge is1/- per tune. Skiza copying process as indicated below:

# **Skiza Copying Procedures:**

1. **Via IVR:**

- Call the customer with the desired tune, press ‘11’ when the

called party’s phone is still playing the Skiza tune.

- You will receive a notification message confirm tune successfully copied.

2. **Via the web:**

- Open the web link [www.skiza.safaricom.com](http://www.skiza.safaricom.com/)

- Click My tunes in the website menu area.
- Click Skiza Copy in the navigation area.
- Click Copy Skiza, then Copy Skiza window is displayed.
- Enter the phone number of the subscriber from whom you want to copy the RBT or click Address Book and select the phone number from the list in the text box, Phone number. Click Confirm.
- Click Search. The RBTs satisfying the query condition is displayed.
 - Select Skiza type. The types are Skiza, My Skiza, and Music box. Select one or more Skiza or music boxes by checking the check box, Select corresponding to the RBT. Click Copy. The system displays a success or failure message after this operation.

**For non RBT subscriber, you can copy the RBTs in the following steps:**

- Click My Skiza in the menu area.
- Click Skiza Copy in the navigation area.
- Click Copy Skiza. The Copy Skiza window is displayed.
- Enter Your Phone Number and Copy Party Phone Number.
- Click Obtain the Verification Code.

3. **Via SMS:**

- Send SMS with the word SKIZA (a space) CODE to 811 E.g. SKIZA 7010001 ( Ksh. 1 per SMS)
- Every SKIZA tune has a specific code representing it.
- To get the code, Send SMS with the word SEARCH/TAFUTA followed by name of Song/artist to 811. For example, > SEARCH NIBEBE YESU or TAFUTA ROSE MUHANDO send text to 811. (Ksh.1 per SMS)

# **Checking Skiza Library**

Customers allowed to have a maximum of 80 Skiza tunes. They can check the tunes by:

1. **SMS**

- Send an SMS with the word GET or PATA to 811
- Customer gets a response with a list of tunes subscribed to.
- The SMS is charged at Ksh.1 per SMS.

2. **Web**

- Customer can use [www.skiza.safaricom.com](http://www.skiza.safaricom.com/).
- Select My tunes, gets all the subscribed tunes.

***NB:*** *Data charges apply*

3. **USSD**

- Dial \*811# ok, select Manage Active Tunes option 5
- Dial \*100# ok, select My subscriptions, select Skiza tunes and follow prompts.
- Dial \*200# ok, select My subscriptions, then Skiza tunes and follow prompts
- Dial \*456# ok, select Stop, then Skiza and follow prompts.

4. **Zuri Chat box**

- On the chat Box write Skiza
- Select View Skiza tune and follow prompts
- Safaricom app.
- Select Services
- Select skiza tunes
- Then select your preferred category and follow prompts

5. **MySafaricom APP**

- Launch MySafaricom APP
- Select Account
- Select My Subscriptions
- View your Skiza Subscriptions

# **Setting Skiza tunes to Specific Callers**

By sending a text message to 811 in the following format;

SET (a space) RBT code (a space) caller phone number (without initial zero).

*For example,> Set 7010001 722799218*

**Note**: To restore it back for all callers, SMS the word DEFAULT to 811. (Ksh 1 per SMS). All Skiza tunes are set default to all callers once downloaded.

# **Deleting Skiza tunes**

1. **Via USSD****:**

- Dial \*811# OK, Select Manage Active Tunes option 5 and follow the prompts.
- Dial \*100# OK, Select My subscription then Skiza, select Delete all my tunes
- Dial \*200# OK, Select Products and services then Skiza, select your preferred Category and follow the prompts. *(USSD service is Free of charge)*

2. **Via IVR****:**

- Dial 811
- Select delete skiza tune and follow prompts
- Calling 811 costs Kshs.3

3. **SMS****:**

- Send the word DELETE <space> (RBT Code) to 811
- The customer will receive confirmation sms on deleted skiza tunes
- The SMS is charged at Ksh.1 per SMS)

4. **Web:**

- Use www.skiza.safaricom.com
- Select Skiza tunes
- Highlight all skiza or one by one and delete

*Data charges apply*

5. **Via Zuri Chat box**

- On the chat box write Skiza
- Select Delete all and follow prompts

6. **Via My Safaricom app**

- Launch MySafaricom APP
- Select Account
- Select My Subscriptions
- Select Skiza
- **Unsubscribe** from the unwanted Tune (One by one or All Tunes)

# **TROUBLESHOOTING ON EMAIL ISSUES**

- Customer is unable to create Email Account on cPanel. The CEE will probe further to understand the error the customer is getting and give the appropriate advice.
- Unable to Receive Emails | Send Emails

- The CEE will confirm whether the client can access internet. If they are not able to, they should check their connection or contact current ISP for assistance.
- If they have installed or configured a firewall? They should try receiving with the firewall temporarily turned off. If this works OK, then consult or contact the firewall vendors.
- The CEE will confirm the status and the ISP hosting the domain from [http://whois.com](http://whois.com/) or [https://ping.eu/ping](https://ping.eu/ping) . If the domain is hosted by a different domain hosting provider and the only problem is receiving, ask the customer to contact the host.
- If the domain is hosted by Safaricom and the status is expired, the CEE will advise the customer to do the renewal and share the invoice number from WHMCS. Upon payment the domain will automatically renewed.
- If the customer is using an email client (e.g., Outlook), confirm the outgoing mail server; this should be given by the ISP providing the internet. For customers using Safaricom fixed data but hosted by another ISP, the outgoing mail server is smtp01.safaricombusiness.co.ke
- If the customer’s organization is using an internal exchange server, ask him to have their IT personnel to check if the server configuration is ok.
- The CEE will confirm if the domain is resolving by login on tacacs and ping the domain name. If it is resolving, it will show the host server. This out indicates that the domain is being hosted by safaricom. If you realize that the domain is being hosted somewhere else, and the client is having issues with sending and receiving mails/ website access,the CEE will advise them to contact their host.

- The customer is unable to access cPanel host. The CEE will request the customer for his/her internet ip to check if the domain is blacklisted. If the domain is blacklisted the CEE will whitelist the internet ip on WHMCS; if the domain is hosted by Safaricom; if not, ask the customer to follow up with their ISP host.

- The CEE will also check if the domain blacklisted on the MX toolbox. If the domain is blacklisted by any site advise the customer to follow-up with respective site on MX toolbox.

- The CEE will add and update the MX record on cPanel. It’s important to check if the records entered are correctly or present in RAT 1& 2 and SMTP 1 & 2 and what priorities are given to each record, the lower the priority, the higher the preference, i.e. also note that priority settings is done under zone editor in cPanel.
- The CEE will check if the RAT |SMTP routes are correctly pointed on Iron Port. The CEE will login to Iron port and update or add both the RAT|SMTP.
- The CEE will check on the mail routing, for domains using cPanel to route mails, ensure that the routing is local, and for domains using mail server, ensure that the routing is remote. 

**NB:** For domains using mail server, the records on RAT/SMTP should be a public IP instead of host.

- The CEE will guide the customer on how to reset the DNS, Add records and update MX, A, CNAME records on the cPanel.

**NB:** Resetting your zone file will erase any modifications you have made to your zone records. The system will attempt to preserve TXT records. However, its recommend that the CEE take note of any records save.

- The CEE will confirm if the Domain is suspended for spamming on WHMCS and share an email to the customer explaining on the steps to take. Once the measures are taken, the customer will share a detailed cleanup report with screenshots so that we can unblock the account/accounts. The CEE will raise a service request with the attached report to the 2nd Level support. Select the appropriate Service request.

# **DOMAIN CHANGE OF EMAIL ADDRESS**

- The CEE will guide the customer on how to change the email address from the customer’s web portal and on cPanel.
- In cases the customer is unable to change the account email due to any system issue, the CEE will request the customer to send a written request to business.support@safaricom.co.ke from the current registered email requesting the same with the below details

Name as registered on WHMCS.

ID/Passport as registered on WHMCS.

Domain name under the customer account.

New email address to change to.

- The CEE will log the request via Service request to ECS team to action.
- ECS team will confirm the request by calling the customer and action the request.
- All requests to change the account details must originate from the registered email on cPanel.

articleTitle: Definition, Eligibility and Mechanic of EXI SURVEY
markdownContent:
# **Definition**

The Enablement Experience Index (EXI) helps us know if Customer Facing Teams (CFT) /Frontline teams have the right tools, systems, processes, training and support to serve the customers delightfully. The survey is run by the CXX team in conjunction with the Research and consumer Insights team.

# **Eligibility**

EXI is measured by asking the Customer Facing Teams (CFTs) to rate their experience supporting customers with Consumer, Enterprise and M-pesa products and services.

# **EXI Mechanic****s**

### **a) EXI objectives**

1. To have a tangible way of measuring CFT Enablement to deliver Customer Experience Excellence (CXX).
2. To measure current Enablement Levels for Customer facing Teams.
3. Enriching the Enablement space.
4. To identify opportunity areas for enhancement of frontline Service delivery.
5. To provide insights that improve NPS as offered at frontline touch points.

### **b) Benefits of EXI survey**

1. The EXI survey helps us improve Customer Facing Teams experience when serving customers by giving them access to the best Systems, Processes, people and tools.
2. One can pause survey at any time, by clicking on “Pause Survey” at the bottom of the survey page.
3. Once you are ready to resume the survey, go back to the EXI Survey link and click ‘Resume Survey’ and proceed with the survey.
4. This feature will allow you to save any unfinished survey and complete it later.
5. Responses are held with Utmost confidentiality and anonymity.
6. Strict measures are taken to ensure the platform is secure and the responses held in confidence by the CXX Products team and Research &Consumer Insights team only!
7. Feedback I taken with utmost trust to ensure you feel free to share it.
8. On average the survey may take you between 10 -15 minutes to complete.
9. The EXI survey results shall be collected, analyzed and feedback shared through Departmental leads.
10. In case you will need further information on this, kindly send an email to ExiSurvey@safaricom.co.ke.

articleTitle: International Direct Dialing Troubleshooting and Resolution Guides
markdownContent:
# **International Direct Dialing Troubleshooting and Resolution Guides**

When customer call with International Calling difficulties, CEE will;

- Verify from the call center folder whether there is any reported case of network downgrade
- Obtain Correct MSISDN experiencing the challenge
- Check Siebel account status and balance for successful connection to international destination
- Confirm customer has enough airtime to last at least one minute.
- Confirm customer is using correct dialing procedure and telephone number (International 000 or country code, area code or mobile network code {minus prefix 0} then recipients’ mobile number)
- Ensure no barring in HLR. (Dial #330\*0000#ok. 0000 can be replaced with any set barring password)
- Location updater i.e. switching off handset, removing SIM and putting it back will assist to establish new connections. (Customer can also try call from a different handset to determine extent of problem)
- If customer is still not able to make the call, escalate the issue via and SR and advise customer on the 24Hrs SLA.
- Advise customer on our network hotline SMS number of 5555 of reporting any network issue (Free of charge).

Click [https://roaming.safaricom.co.ke/](https://roaming.safaricom.co.ke/)﻿ to view. for the reviewed international calling rates and roaming rates.

# **CREDIT FINANCING**

Safaricom has been running a service that allows M-PESA agents to take up short term float credit to fund their weekend float operations dubbed Bloom.

# **Safaricom Bloom finance**

- As part of the company’s continuous improvement and support of its partners to ensure adequate float availability in the market especially during the weekends, holidays, and those special days when banks are inaccessible,
- To give agents access to funds throughout, the company has come up with Agent finance where an agent can opt in and borrow at any time of the month.
- The financing is at a fee of 0.075% of the amount borrowed.
- The agents can only borrow up to the set credit limit which is based on scoring based on 3 months average commission for the entire agency net of withholding tax. The Limit is also affected by total Fund base approved by Safaricom Finance.
- To qualify for financing agents monthly commission should also be Kshs90000 and above.
- To opt in M-PESA agent head office should dial \*234\*3\*7# using the head office till.
- The agents are expected to repay back the credit float by end of the four days.
- If the head office does not pay by the end of the fourth day the financing will roll over and attract roll over fee of 0.075% of total amount borrowed.
- The M-PESA head office shall be blacklisted from bloom service should the agent fail to repay the loan by the 8th.
- Find below blacklist matrix

**Agent unable to borrow or repay Bloom.**

- On receiving escalation on line 300 where a head office is unable to borrow, the partner support staff shall login on M-PESA to confirm whether the organization has been blacklisted.
- This is done by confirming from head office float account statement whether the last repayment was done on time 

# **Stanbic Mjeki Loan**

- This is a product by Stanbic bank which provides Safaricom dealers and M-PESA Agent with short term loans to increase M-PESA float and restock Airtime and devices for dealers
- This Loan is payable in 7days for M-PESA float and 30days for devices
- To opt in agent/ dealer will visit Stanbic and provide below requirements:
 - Certificate of Incorporation.
 - Memorandum of Association.
 - Articles of Association.
 - KRA PIN Certificate of the Company/ Certificate of exemption.
 - Copies of National ID or valid Passport copies and photos of the signatories
 - List of directors/and signatories of the company. (KYC of any director owning more than 25% should be provided)
 - Latest filed annual returns or CR12 for Entities that are more than 18 months since formation
 - Evidence of physical location of the directors. (Can be indicated in the board resolution included in the contract.
- On receiving the above application, Stanbic will then send communication to Safaricom M-PESA agent support or dealer management requesting for the following details (MIS verification): 6 months turnover and commission data, date of inception, outlets, and directors of the company.
- Once application has been completed successfully Mjeki loan for float is credited to M-PESA head office working account. Airtime, devices and Simex financing is credited on dealer portal.
- Float financing is at a fee of 0.245% per week. For device Mjeki loan the charge is 1.05% per month
- Mjeki loan is unsecured. In the event of default Safaricom will suspend the head office and remit commissions to the bank.
- Loan repayment can be done through: Business to Business (B2B) settlement on M-PESA, RTGS, internal transfers and cash deposit.

# **KCB Kopa float**

This is a long-term credit facility by KCB bank which provides Mpesa Agent with long term loan facility to increase their M-PESA float

Below are the product features and requirements for Kopa Float.

**Features**

- Maximum Unsecured loan amount of Kes.10M
- Loan qualifying amount 12 times of 6 months average residual commissions
- Interest Rate 13%
- Negotiation Fees 3%
- Loan Tenor 60 months

**Requirements**

- Copy of mpesa contract
- Mis Verification from Safaricom (6 months turnover and commission data, date of inception, outlets, and directors of the company)
- Commissions must have passed through the KCB bank account for the Agent
- Letter of Undertaking to channel proceeds to KCB account.
- Business Registration documents
- Audited Books of accounts for amounts above Kes.5M.
- Board Resolution to borrow
- Bank account statement
- Mpesa Commission Statement

# **Family bank float financing**

Safaricom have partnered with Family Bank to avail Stock Financing to M-PESA Agents and Dealers.

- This a short-term loan to increase M-PESA float. The loan duration is 7days.
- The loan facility is charged at 0.249% per week
- Loan Limit is 1.5 x 6 months average Commissions earned.
- The facility has Zero Processing fees.
- Maximum limit is KES 20 million.

**Family bank Dealer Stock Finance**

- The loan duration is 30 days
- The loan facility is charged at 1.084% per month
- Loan Limit is 70% of 6 months average airtime and device sales
- The facility has Zero Processing fees
- Maximum limit is KES 20 million

# **Okoa float**

- This is a float financing service by onfon media company which provides M-PESA agent head office and M-PESA subagents with short term loans to increase M-PESA float.
- To access the service M-PESA agent/subagent will dial \*898# and provide M-PESA till details required. Agent will then be advised on the requirements
- Document required includes:
 - M-PESA commission statement for the last 6months
 - Certificate of incorporation or equivalent
 - National ID copies for directors or sub agents
 - KRA pin certificate
- Documents should be sent via email to info@okoafloat.com. Once approved by Onfon media the Agent/ subagent will be required to sign an electronic contract with the terms and conditions.
- Okoa float is a solution for short term float need, repayment period is within 3days
- Float borrowing limit depends on profile rating, which is determined by average M-PESA commissions, ability to pay back on time based on previous borrowing and frequency of float borrowing.
- The credit facility charges a fee of 0.3% per day
- To repay agent should do a business withdrawal to Onfon media super agency till number 456623
- If an agent/subagent defaults, the loan will continue to roll over after every 3days until fully paid
- NB: Agency head office will not be liable for default by sub agents under them

# **Safaricom Device financing**

- This is credit financing given to Safaricom dealers and M-PESA agent head offices to enable them stock devices.
- The credit facility is offered once every month. Repayment period is one month.
- The facility is offered at zero interest rate, has no access fee.
- Agents should opt in for the credit facility via email clearly indicating the smartphones they wish to purchase and their value each month.
- The credit limit is based on previous month commissions
- Agents will not qualify for the facility if:
 - - Are under suspension
 - Have a history of late payment for the credit advanced.
 - Agents with Bank Guarantee Debt over 15 days

**Device financing Blacklist**

- Late payment by 3 days; the agent will not be issued with Device financing for 1Month.
- Late payment after 5 days of the repayment week; the agent will not be issued with credit for 2 Months.
- If the repayment falls on the end of the month or agent fails to pay until the end of the month, Finance Team will recover the unpaid funds from the agents’ commissions

articleTitle: M-PESA Ali Express and M-PESA Business App
markdownContent:
**M-PESA Ali Express Definition and Eligibility**

AliExpress is an online retail service based in China that is owned by Alipay that offer products to international online buyers.

# **AliExpress payment via M-PESA**

This is a partnership between Safaricom and Alipay to integrate M-PESA as a payment method on AliExpress e-commerce.

# **Eligibility**

The M-PESA payment method is available to all M-PESA registered users who have an AliExpress account via the AliExpress APP.

# **Service Accessibility and Cost Charge**

To access AliExpress M-PESA service the customer will need to download AliExpress app on Google play store and Apple app store.

# **Cost/Charges**

Standard Lipa Na M-PESA Business Bouquet Paybill charges will apply.

Order Cancellation status: Payment being verified.

A customer can still cancel an order. They don’t need to contact the seller for this action.

# **Reporting a Dispute**

To report a dispute visit AliExpress report centre, [https://report.aliexpress.com](https://report.aliexpress.com)

# **AliExpress customer support**

To access customer service, kindly visit [https://helppage.aliexpress.com/buyercenter/index.htm](https://helppage.aliexpress.com/buyercenter/index.htm)

# **M****\-****PESA BUSINESS APP Definition & Eligibility**

# **Definition**

M-PESA Business App is a simple channel that will allow merchants to transact easily, and better visualize their income.

# **Eligibility**

The app targets M-PESA Business Till merchants. These merchants:

Must have a single store, with a merchant product.

# **Must be active on M-PESA.**

# **APP Accessibility**

Merchants will download the M-PESA Business App on their nominated numbers, from Google Play store or iOS app store.

Merchants who have the M-PESA Business Till and have an android smart phone will receive an SMS with a link to pre-register for the app.

Once the app is published on Google Play store, these merchants will be prompted to download it and sign in to experience its features.

**Note:** Log in on Merchants app

A merchant’s credentials (Operator ID and Store number) are only applicable to their (nominated) phone number hence merchant cannot log into their account from a different merchant’s app.

**CHANGE OF DOMAIN OWNERSHIP**

# **Requests by current owner.**

Customer will be allowed to transfer domain account from person to person.

The transfer request must originate from the current account owner.

The written request will be sent via email registered on cPanel and sent to business support Business.support@Safaricom.co.ke**.**

The request must contain the following:

Current Owner Details (Mandatory)

Full Names

Document ID

Email Address

# **Domain details**

Domain Name

Email Address used to register the Domain on cPanel.

# **New Owner Details (Mandatory)**

Full Names

Document ID

Email Address

- The receiving CEE will vet the request via the details on WHMCS and CPanel, the requester details must match details as per details captured at registration.
- The new owner will first create an account on the domain web portal.
- Where customer does not pass the vetting, will be advised accordingly.
- Where the request is received via retail, the CEE will advise the customer to send an email with the above-mentioned details to Business.support@Safaricom.co.ke
- Where customer calls call center on other channels other than L2222, CEE will advise customer on requirements and advice customer to email the Business.support@Safaricom.co.ke and give a 2 Hour SLA.
- The CEE will then log the request on Service request and attach the email request for action by ECS team or follow create a new client transfer product - service on WHMCS guide to transfer the domain on WHMCS and advise the customer.

# **Transfer / change of ownership requests by third party.**

# **Adrian Routers (4G for Home Routers)**

# **How to insert the simcard to the device**

Please insert the SIM card in the simcard slot indicated at the bottom of the device

# **Powering the device**

Connect your device to an available AC power outlet using the included power adapter. The device SYS LED indicator will change from orange to green light to indicate the device has completed the startup procedure.

# **Logging in to the device**

First set up the device using a Web Browser from a local PC connected to device LAN port. Ensure that the connected PC has acquired IP address via DHCP from the device. After IP connectivity is established between the PC and CPE device, launch a Web browser and specify http://192.168.0.1 in the address bar. A window will pop up requesting a password. **Note the default password is “admin\_4Gfwa”.** Input the user login password and then click the “**LOGIN**” button. After successful log on, the default home page of the WEB GUI interface will appear.

# **Confirming the Firmware or Software version**

Log in to the device using [http://192.168.0.1](http://192.168.0.1/) on your browser. Under system status select system information. Confirm that the device is running on version V2.10B3822. If that’s the software version, the device is OK and if not, then the device needs a software upgrade.

# **Upgrading the software version**

For the upgrade to be done ensure you have **Downloaded the firmware and saved it on your laptop)**

Log in to the device using [http://192.168.0.1](http://192.168.0.1/) on your browser. Under general settings you’ll be prompted to input a password. Use **admin\_4Gfwa** as the password. Select system maintenance. On the opened window choose **Maintenance (**on the horizontal tabs**).** On the opened window go to firmware upgrade **choose file**. Navigate to where you saved the **file**, **select** then **open (The firmware will appear next to the choose file button).** Confirm the file selected is **V2.1.0B3822\_R4110.** Select the reset to factory default **check box.** The lastly select **APPLY**

The 4G router will transition to **Transmitting file** then **Burning file** then **Rebooting.** Once upgrade is complete, the device will reboot and take you back to the log in page.

If you get an **‘operation fail’** error **during firmware upgrade**, go back to system maintenance > maintenance > then select load default under load factory default option, the device will reboot > then log in afresh and repeat the above steps.

# **Changing Wi-Fi and Password**

Log in to the device using [http://192.168.0.1](http://192.168.0.1/) on your browser. Under Wi-Fi configuration. Select Wi-Fi 2.4GHz. Click the ‘**enable’** check box on the wi-fi radio status. Update your network name and password to your preferred for 2.4GHz. Select ‘WPA2-PSK’ in security mode. Click ‘**apply’** to save the setting.

The device will reset to the log in page. Log in and repeat the above process to make changes for the **5GHz**. Once complete, allow the device to reboot automatically. Alternatively power the device off and on using the power button at the back.

# **Confirming network signal**

The 4G CPE router should only be sold to customers in areas with adequate 4G coverage. Download the APP ‘Network **cell info lite’** from Google play store on your phone. The 4G signal strength should be below -100 with the best being around -40. That means that the pointer should be in the green section between -100 and -50 for good LTE signal.

# **Delayed Powering on**

Remove the simcard from the device and check if there’s any change. The device failed to boot successfully. Reset using the RTS burton at the back of device then retry. If the SYS light is blinking orange check the sim PIN. Disable sim pin if not disabled yet.

# **If the LTE lights are not coming on, but the SYS light is solid green**

The device needs an upgrade. In case it still behaves the same after upgrade then reset the device by holding the RST burton at the back for about 10 seconds. Also, it may mean that the LTE coverage is poor. Check the signal strength using the **CELL INFO LTE** app.

# **If Wi-Fi is not visible on the devices after successfully setting up the device**

This means that that the LTE lights 1234 are all on but 2.4GHz and 5GHz is off. Log in to the device using [http://192.168.0.1](http://192.168.0.1/) on your browser. Go to Wi-Fi configuration and enable radio to enable Wi-Fi.

# **Device is connected properly but the speeds the customer is getting is poor.**

Call line 400 on the whitelisted number for the support team to assist check on the line configurations.

# **If the customer loses service after some time, when the device is reboot it resumes service but goes off again**

This happens when Wi-Fi is connected but no internet. Check the APN if both IPV4 and IPV6 learns the GW.

# **If the device malfunctions**

Device does not power on or powers on but does not initiate all the indicators. Replace the router if issue does not resolve after device upgrade. The customer is to return the device to the dealer who in turn takes it to the retail shop near them for the replacement process to be done.

# **Error operation fail when upgrading the device**

This occurs when the device is upgraded after attempted connection but fails. Load the device default and upgrade again.

**NB: Find attached troubleshooting details for Adrian 4G FOR Home router.**

# **Safaricom Dividends via M-PESA and Payment Partnership- BRITAM**

# **Definition**

Dividend refers to a reward, cash or otherwise, that a company gives to its shareholders.

Dividends can be issued in various forms, such as cash payment, stocks or any other form.

Dividend is usually a part of the profit that the company shares with its shareholders.

# **M-PESA Dividend Opt-in Registration process**

The Safaricom shareholders will be given an option to receive their dividend payments via M-PESA service.

Shareholders who received their dividend via M-PESA the previous year will **NOT** have to register again.

The qualifying dividend limit is Ksh. 70,000.

# **Registration Process**

To register, the customers will enter the USSD short code \*534# when their phones are on standby mode. The shareholder is given up to 5 trials to register. The steps are below.

Select Safaricom

select Register.

Accept the Terms and Conditions

Enter your ID/Passport number

Enter your CDS account number

# **Response Messages during registration**

Below are the Messages sent on registration

***Successful response message after registration****:* ‘’Thank you for registering. Your request has been received.’’

***Decline the Terms and Conditions***: ‘’You cannot proceed with the Opt-In process without accepting the terms and conditions. Thank you’’

***Missing details (ID number, CDS number)***: ‘’Incomplete information. Try again.’’

***System outage***: ‘’Sorry we are not able to process your request now. Please try again later.’’

***Opt-in message for Safaricom shareholders***: ‘Register now to receive your Safaricom dividends via M-PESA by dialling \*534#. If you received last year’s dividend via M-PESA, do not register again”

An SMS communication will be sent out to Safaricom shareholders who registered during the Opt in informing them of whether their registration was successful or not. In addition; it will notify them whether they will receive their dividend via M-PESA. The SMS communication will be as below: -

***Successful registration response message****:* “Dear Safaricom Shareholder, your M-PESA Opt-in request was successful. You will receive your dividend payment via M-PESA

***Unsuccessful registration response message******:*** “Dear Safaricom Shareholder, your M-PESA Opt-in request was unsuccessful. Your dividend payment via Cheque/EFT will be dispatched.

**NOTE:** Those registrations that are not successful will be paid out via Cheque or EFT (Electronic Funds Transfer; into the shareholder’s bank account).

# **Checking Registration Status**

Shareholders can check the details they have submitted to verify if they have submitted the correct details by: -

Dialling \*534# then

Select Safaricom

Select Check Registration

A record of the ID/Passport number and CDS account number that have been submitted will be generated on the screen.

# **M-PESA Dividend Payment Partnership- BRITAM Registration Process.**

To register, the customers will dial the USSD short code \*534# when their phones are on standby mode. The steps are below.

Select the respective company.in this case British American Company.

Accept the Terms and Conditions by visiting the dividends issuer’s website for the respective Terms and Conditions. In this case BRITAM website (www.britam.co.ke)

Enter your ID number.

Enter your CDSC account number.

An SMS message will be sent to the customer for successful and unsuccessful registration.

Successful response message after registration: ‘’Thank you for registering. Your request has been received.’’

Unsuccessful response message after registration due to wrong or invalid details (ID number, CDSC number): ‘’Dear customer, sorry we are not able to process your request now. Call 0724699667 for more information.’’
