# **Bonga Expiry**

**Definition**

This is a permanent implementation where Bonga points accrued will now have a validity period to enable customers redeem their points.

**Eligibility**

The service will apply to all Safaricom customers who have Bonga points services and have not redeemed their Bonga points for the last 3 years.

**Reason to expire Bonga points.**

This is a business decision aimed at encouraging Bonga redemption. Customers will dial \*126# and select Check total points to expire to know when the Bonga points will expire.

**Mechanics.**

- One cannot extend or reinstate expired Bonga Points.
- The expiry date was moved from 1st January 2023 to a later date that will be communicated.
- One cannot reverse a Lipa na Bonga transaction once the points have expired.

# **Partner Support - Float Movement/Issues**

**FLOAT ISSUES/MOVEMENT**

Float is the E-Money that agents operate with the tills.

**Float Movement**

- M-PESA agent business operates with float (e-money) and cash. Customer withdrawal will increase agent till float and in return the agent will give out cash reducing cash at hand. On the other hand, deposit to customers will reduce float in the till and increase cash at hand.
- To add float, agent needs to deposit funds through banks or other super agents (business deposit). Float deposit can be done either to the head office or to the specific till that needs additional float. When deposited through the head office; head office operator will move the funds from HO working account to float account then distribute to the tills that need float within the agency hierarchy.
- For a till to do float deposit and float withdrawal through super-agent, it should have store management role.
- When float is deposited directly from super-agent/bank to the till the till assistant will need to move funds from working to float account.
- Float movement from float to working can only be done by primary till operator.
- Business withdrawals can only be done by an operator with primary till operator role.
- 5,000 While Maximum float deposit/withdrawal transaction amount is Ksh. 400,000.
- Float deposit is also available on mobile banking from the following banks: KCB,
- M-PESA Agents should go through respective banks to be whitelisted to buy float through mobile banking.
- Super-agent tariff
 - Default tariff – charges Kshs100 for amount below Ksh 100,000 and 0.1% for transaction amount above Ksh 100,000
 - Super-agent tariff1 – charges Kshs50 for amount below Ksh 100,000 and 0.05% for transaction amount above Ksh 100,000
 - Super-agent tariff 2 – zero rated  

**Low float suspension and unsuspension.**

- MPESA agent tills should operate above Ksh 20,000 monthly average float level.
- Tills operating below the above recommended float level are normally sanctioned through suspension. Penalty period 1 week.
 - On receiving request to unsuspend, Safaricom partner support staff should confirm the till had been suspended for low float – check on Audit log and corresponding email from M-PESA Agent Admin team (via email [mpesaagentadmin@safaricom.co.ke](mailto:mpesaagentadmin@safaricom.co.ke) ) indicating the till was suspended due to low float.
 - Confirm that the suspension period has elapsed, and the agent has added float to above Ksh 20,000 before unsuspending.

**Float report request**

The is a report of float performance of tills for a given agency. Request for float report should be sent via email to [mpesaagentadmin@safaricom.co.ke](mailto:mpesaagentadmin@safaricom.co.ke)

**Float movement for suspended till.**

- Request for float movement for a suspended till should be raised on dealer portal.
 - Service Request category for float movement: MPESA services,
 - Request Type: float management
 - Request item: float movement for Frozen/suspended till
- SLA for the request is 24hrs
- On receiving the request on call, confirm a service request has been raised. Then search for the store on MPESA system. Check audit logs to confirm reason for suspension.
- Then go to initiate transaction and select HO float management. Enter the head office short code as the store to transfer float to. Enter the amount and reason for float movement the submit to initiate transaction. 

**Delayed float deposit through Safaricom holding account.**

M-PESA agency head office should report delayed float deposit via email or call line 300.

- On receiving the call, the partner support staff should escalate the issue to M-PESA Finance team and capture the following details:
 - Amount deposited,
 - Deposit slip or M-PESA transaction ID
 - date and time,
 - short code to receive the deposit,
 - name of the organization and
 - contact details (email & mobile contact).

- MPESA Finance email [m-pesafinance@Safaricom.co.ke](mailto:m-pesafinance@Safaricom.co.ke)

articleTitle: Partner Support - TILL SIM REPLACEMENT/ TILL SIM SWAP
markdownContent:
# **Partner Support - TILL SIM REPLACEMENT/ TILL SIM SWAP**

**SIMCARD ISSUES/TILL REPLACEMENT/ TILL PUK**

**Till self-swap**

This functionality on dealer portal allows M-PESA head office to do sim card replacement for M-PESA tills within their hierarchy. Reason for till swap includes lost till/stolen till, damaged Sim card, inactive sub agent tills, upgrade to new generation SIM

- Dealer will login to dealer portal. Dealer portal link [https://dealerportal.safaricom.net/dealers](https://dealerportal.safaricom.net/dealers)
- Then select till swaps and click on till swap request.

**This will open the Till Swap Request page.**

Step 1: Enter your phone number.

- This is the number that was used to register you on Dealer Portal.
- Read and understand Safaricom Data Privacy Statement as indicated on the privacy policy hyperlink.
- Select the “box” I have read and understood the privacy policy and select NEXT.
- The system will send a One Time Password (OTP) to be number entered via SMS.

Step 2 – Enter OTP

- Enter the OTP received on the number that you entered and select Verify &Proceed
- Or Select the Resend it link if they do not receive the OTP via SMS.

Step 3 – Request for Till Swap through

- Selecting/typing the Store Number of the till that you would like to swap. All your stores will be populated automatically.
- Selecting/typing the Till Number of the Till that you would like to swap. All the Till numbers of the selected store will be populated automatically.

- Navigate to till number and select the specific till to be replaced.
- The store name, till number and till MSISDN will populate automatically.
- Dealer /MPESA HO will then be required to enter the IMSI number for the new replacement sim card.
- Select reason for sim swap and then click on submit.
- Sim swap will then be completed automatically.

**Till sim swap via service request.**

- This option is used to raise sim replacement request for M-PESA till when till self-swap (above) is not working. Agent tills that cannot be swapped via self-swap includes lines that have not been in use for more than 1month, blacklisted tills and outlets missing on dealer portal.
- On dealer portal service request categories agent should select M-PESA services, agent account then Sim swap with no approval.
- Agent will then be required to enter, till agent number, till mobile number, outlet name and new replacement SIM card serial number.
- Once submitted the system will generate a service request which will be received by Safaricom M-PESA support team on CRM.
- The service request SLA is 24hrs.
- Agent calling line 300 should provide the service request number.
- Safaricom partner support staff should confirm the status of the request and assist complete sim swap on Siebel if the request is past SLA and close the SR.

**Till reactivation after sim swap**

- To reactivate M-PESA Till after sim swap, agent should use previous primary assistant pin as the start key and create a new pin.
- If the previous primary assistant pin has been forgotten M-PESA head office admin should Login to M-PESA system and reset start key for the till.
- Once activated the till should receive M-PESA menu update.

**Till Puk Request**

- To get till PUK number.M-PESA agent head office should use TILL PUK option on dealer portal.
- Login into dealer portal and select TILL PUK
- Click on till PUK request and select the specific agent.
- Store name, agent number and till MSISDN will populate automatically.
- Click on submit for the system to fetch and populate PUK number for the till.

For tills missing on dealer portal M-PESA head office should raise a service request on dealer portal for PUK. SLA 24hrs

- To raise PUK service request agent head office should login to dealer portal and select service request.
- Service request category; MPESA service
- Select Request type: M-PESA agent account.
- And request item TILL PUK.

# **MECHANICS**

Customers can access KCB MPESA through the following channels:

- Access through the M-PESA menu
- Through USSD**: \*334#**
- Safaricom App.

Then:

- Select Loans and Savings.
- Select KCB M-PESA and Activate.

# **DIY PROCEDURE FOR KCB-MPESA DEPOSIT/WITHDRAW/ QUERY BALANCE**

Money in and out of the KCB M-PESA Account is ONLY available through M-PESA channel.

**KCB-MPESA Deposit**

To deposit from M-PESA,

- Access the KCB M-PESA menu.
- Select Deposit from M-PESA.
- The M-PESA account will be deducted, and the KCB M-PESA Account credited with the amount.

**KCB-MPESA Withdraw**

To withdraw to M-PESA

1. Access the KCB M-PESA menu.
2. Select Withdraw to M-PESA.
3. The KCB M-PESA Account will be deducted, and the M-PESA Account credited with the amount.

**KCB-MPESA Query balance.**

The customer will not be charged for checking KCB-MPESA balance.

The procedure is as follows:

- Access M-PESA menu
- Loans and savings
- KCB M-PESA.
- Select My Account.
- Select check balance and confirm with M-PESA PIN.
- Customer receives an SMS notification with the balances for the account requested for.

# Product definition

SurePay product is an e-voucher service that allows restricted use of funds on M-PESA. An organization will be able to restrict use of funds on M-PESA by specified beneficiaries, at specified retail outlets to ensure any funds allocated serves the intended purpose.

For an easier understanding, think of a case of a paper Carrefour Supermarket shopping voucher. This can be redeemed only at a Carrefour branch. SurePay is the electronic version of this with some added features.

# How SurePay works/voucher redemption

- Organization allocates funds to the beneficiary.
- Beneficiary receives notification of funds allocation and instructions on how to redeem them.
- Beneficiary visits an approved service provider and receives the service.
- Service provider initiates payment request.
- Beneficiary receives notification to confirm transactions via PIN
- Redeemed funds paid directly to service provider via M-PESA account.

# Benefits of using M-PESA SurePay

- Available on both web and mobile.
- M-PESA SurePay interface can be used for both restricted funds and cash disbursement services.
- Cheaper as it will eliminate the need for organizations using physical vouchers which cost to print and distribute.
- Secure as it provides a safe cash disbursement avenue as money is sent directly from the organization to the service provider.
- It allows organizations to set own rules e.g. users need for documentation upload before disbursement etc.
- It ensures the person who qualifies for the service is the only one who can benefit as payment requests are confirmed by PIN by the beneficiary.
- It ensures the beneficiary visits the service provider and receives service in order to benefit from the program.
- Cash allocation can be locked to a specific financial period.
- It allows partner organizations to adopt a modern and new mobile based technology for disbursement of funds and other services.
- It has clear reports based on set up data that will be useful to analyze progress on different programs and customer behaviors. This will also eliminate the issue of manual data reconciliation by the participating service providers
- The M-PESA SurePay will facilitate a full payment eco-system that will generate additional transactional revenue from all our LIPA NA M-PESA payment avenues including pay bill and buy goods hence increasing revenue generation.
- M-PESA SurePay will be integrated with other systems the corporates use.

# SurePay web system administrator

Safaricom will grant system access to one user that your organization will nominate as an administrator. The administrator will be tasked with creating other users (Operators and Managers) whose roles will be to manage fund disbursements.

# Beneficiary Identification

- The beneficiary refers to an employee nominated by the company to use the service.
- The sponsoring organizations normally identify the group of people they want to assist, engage them directly and collect their details together with the service providers they want to work with. Safaricom does not participate in this process.
- Beneficiaries are identified by their Safaricom mobile numbers while service provider must have a Pay bill or Buy Goods till.
- A process is ongoing to allow use of non-Safaricom mobile numbers.

# Beneficiary PIN number

- When their details are uploaded on the platform by the organization, they receive an SMS with a PIN. As per the customer journey below, they beneficiaries will need to enter the PIN when redeeming vouchers.
- This PIN can be changed by dialing \*432\*2# and selecting Change PIN.
- In case of a beneficiary forgotten PIN, the organization can reset it from the Bulk center on the webpage.

# Funds safety in SurePay account

The beneficiaries cannot withdraw the funds in the account. Just like one cannot cash the paper shopping voucher, the SurePay voucher cannot be cashed.

It can only be used for payment for services rendered and can only be used at authorized shops.

# Beneficiary Support

Beneficiaries should call the sponsoring organization for all escalations. E.g. those sponsored by CITAM should call CITAM admin who collected their KYC for queries that may include SurePay PIN reset, voucher balance, queries on where to redeem etc.

**The difference between SurePay and B2C (Bulk Payment)**

SurePay is closed loop meaning voucher can only be used at shop authorized by the organization while B2C is open loop, meaning funds are sent directly into M-PESA account of the beneficiary and they can use it in whichever way they want without any restriction.

articleTitle: Airtime Reversal at the Retail Shop
markdownContent:
# **Reversal Terms**

The CEE will proceed with reversal after confirming the below terms are met.

The reversal claim must be made **within** **48hrs** of purchase.

The minimum reversal amount is Ksh.5 with no limit on the maximum.

Only one reversal per customer per month shall be allowed.

If funds are partially utilized, the customer will need to top up the used amount before requesting for reversal.

#  **Airtime Bought for Self**

CEE will Query the customer’s number on CRM.

Confirm customer’s full names.

Confirm the available balance on customer account, from IN Data to confirm customer has airtime equivalent or more than the reversal amount requested for.

Click on the IN-Call History button and then on the Transaction History button.

Under Transaction History, Specify Date Range and Query Recharge History.

M-PESA Recharge transactions will load under transaction history. Highlight the transaction to reverse (Type must be “Recharge” and Cause must be “M-PESA”

Under the additional info tab, details of the transaction will be displayed i.e.

- M-PESA transaction number,
- Recipient’s number,
- senders’ number (for third party requests)
- Amount.

Click on Reverse Transaction tab.

An automatic interaction is created at the subscriber level with an OM Public ID.

Drilling down on to the airtime reversal OM Public ID gives the details and status of the reversal transaction order.

Confirm the status is complete and airtime deducted on customers account and M-PESA credited with the same amount.

The Sender/customer (number which bought airtime) will receive a notification SMS from M-PESA that the funds have been reversed successfully and account balance credited to the same account.

# **Airtime Bought for Other**

The CEE will confirm the following:

Customer full name

Transaction to be reversed.

Airtime balance on CRM (enough to allow for full reversal)

Initiate the reversal on CRM.

Confirm that the airtime has been deducted on CRM (airtime balance), and the same has been credited on the M-PESA system account.

**Recipient Requesting**

CEE will proceed with reversal guidelines. No consent will be required from the sender.

If funds are fully or partially utilized, advise the recipient to top up and call back for reversal.

**Sender Requesting**

The CEE will call the recipient to seek consent before reversing.

Where consent is given, proceed to reverse the transaction and advise the customer accordingly.

Confirm that the airtime has been deducted on CRM (Airtime balance), and that the same has been credited on the M-PESA system.

Where consent is not given, inform the requester of the same and advise them to handle the issue with the recipient directly.

Where the recipient is unavailable or not picking, capture the details on the airtime reversal link for the team to try reach the recipient**.** [https://cxintranet.safaricom.net/cm2/A\_MpesaAirtimeReversal\_Insert.php](https://cxintranet.safaricom.net/cm2/A_MpesaAirtimeReversal_Insert.php)

Advise the customer we will try reaching the recipient and will get back to them accordingly.

Do not give any guarantees that the money will be recovered. Advice on SLA of 2 hrs.

Where the third party has returned the money back to the sender, capture the details on the airtime reversal link, for reversal team to deal. Advice on SLA of 2hrs.

Where the reversal fails due to exceed in limit, advise customer on limits, customer can transfer funds to create room for the reversal amount. Allow customer to transact and effect the reversal.

However, this information on account exceeding Ksh.300, 000 should only be shared with the purchaser/sender and not recipient.

Where CEE logs into both sender and recipient’s account, an interaction will be captured in both accounts with details of the interaction with customer.

**Note:**

**Used Airtime**

If the airtime is fully utilized by recipient, advise the sender to engage recipient for refund.

**Insufficient funds**

Where part of the airtime bought is utilized, advise the customer to top up and send the reversal request (M-PESA SMS) to 456

For third party purchase, advise the customer that funds are not available to liaise with the recipient.

# **Missing CDRs on Siebel**

If the transaction is not updated on transaction history, CEE will ensure customer has enough airtime on IN Data (equivalent or more than amount purchased) and advise the customer to send the request to 456.

**NOTE:** For Pooled lines, data lines, M-Kopa, Car tracking lines, GPRS unbundled with SMS Tariff - CEE reverses the transaction without consent.

# **Scenarios Where an M-PESA Airtime Reversal Will Generate an Error on Siebel**

If the customer’s M-PESA limits will be exceeded i.e., the customer account will have a balance more than 300,000 after the reversal is initiated.

Transaction is not an M -PESA airtime transaction.

The transaction has already been reversed.

The airtime account balance is less than the amount being reversed.

articleTitle: M-PESA Business DIY Procedures for Services
markdownContent:
**M-PESA Business DIY Procedures for Services.**

# **Portal Login Process by Partners /Merchants**

Once created all users will receive the following via the indicated contacts **via SMS and Email**

The username

One-time temporary log in password

Organization Code

Portal URL

OTP – external users

The one-time temporary password will expire after 24 hours days

The user will be prompted to change the password on first time login.

The user will also be prompted to select a security question and enter their preferred answer.

Every log in will be authenticated via an OTP sent to the user’s MSISDN captured during creation.

# **Access Channels**

**USSD**

This is accessible via \*234\*4. Partners will dial the USSD from a nominated number.

# **Web Channel**

The web user interface will be displayed upon successful login by the users.

This is accessible via: [https://sp.mpesaforbusiness.safaricom.co.ke](https://sp.mpesaforbusiness.safaricom.co.ke/) for Safaricom staff and [https://org.mpesaforbusiness.safaricom.co.ke](https://org.mpesaforbusiness.safaricom.co.ke/) for partners

The web portal is accessible via handset and or a computer.

Portal web users will be able to access the service via USSD and or web as defined during creation.

**API Channel**

This is accessible via API integration to M-PESA broker solution.

**This will enable partners**

To receive automated instant M-PESA notifications. Example: Check Balance, transaction details.

To initiate transactions via API.

Partners will be allowed to integrate into the portal as per the current M-PESA Business API integration process.

Inter-Accounts Transaction Procedure

# **Web Procedure:**

This will be done on the web.

Partners/merchants must have access to the web portal and are active users with the right permissions to be able to initiate B2B transactions.

The operator will login to the org system to initiate the transaction and a business manager is required to approve the transaction per the approval levels.

# **USSD Procedure**

For the merchant/partner to be able to initiate the transaction via USSD a Nominated number must be attached to store or Head office.

Partners/merchants will dial the current service USSD Code to make the payment.

All transaction initiated via USSD will require a PIN. This is currently set as the nominated number’s M-PESA PIN.

Payments Portal B2C Funds Transfer Process

Partners will be able to initiate B2C transactions via USSD/Web. Movement of funds will be determined by the approval levels set by the BE.

Safaricom staff will use M-PESA G2 to execute transactions upon written request by the partner and where the team has the mandate to do so.

# **B2C MODELS**

Partners will only be to initiate B2C transactions via the open model. This model only allows an organization to disburse funds to MSISDNS.

This model will allow send funds to MSISDNS via B2C M-PESA model.

The service is available for MSIDSN:

Both M-PESA registered and non-M-PESA registered MSISDNS

Both Safaricom and another network MSISDNS

# **B2C Service Requirements**

The organization must be existing and active in M-PESA

B2C account must active in M-PESA the system

The process will only start if the account balance is enough for completion of payment of all the listed accounts.

# **Web Procedure:**

This will be done on the web.

Partners/merchants must have access to the web portal and are active users with the right permissions to be able to initiate B2C transactions.

The operator will login to the org system to initiate the transaction and a business manager is required to approve the transaction per the approval levels.

This will allow partners to initiate singular and bulk transactions

# **USSD Procedure**

This will allow partners to initiate singular transactions

For the merchant/partner to be able to initiate the transaction via USSD a Nominated number must be attached to store or Head office.

Partners/merchants will dial the current service USSD Code to make the payment.

All transaction initiated via USSD will require a PIN. This is currently set as the nominated number’s M-PESA PIN.

# **Portal Payment Process:**

The system will check the registration status of the receiving MSISDNs on G2 and automatically select an appropriate transaction type.

Transaction types set and configured on the portal are:

Business payments to customers with withdrawal charges

Business Payments to customers

For the transaction to be initiated:

The accounts must have enough funds i.e. short code on G2 must have enough funds.

The transaction cost plus the amount to transfer must be equal or less than account balance. If this is not met the transaction will cancel the transaction will fail

The organization will be responsible for ensuring that the utility account has enough float.

Funding will be done as per the current LNM Short codes funding procedures.

The Current M-PESA transaction limits apply.

The portal will send the request to M-PESA G2 via API. This will:

Initiate a balance query on the respective Short Code’s utility account on M-PESA G2

Where the balance is sufficient in the Utility account the B2C payment will be processed as per request.

Where the balance is insufficient a balance query will be done on the MFF account.

If the balance is sufficient in the MFF account; funds will move from MFF to Utility and the B2C payment will be processed as per request.

The funds are insufficient in the MFF account the B2C payment will fail.

**NOTE:** The API MFF balance query will only be possible for short codes will the Special Rule band on M-PESA G2.

Where the organization Short Code does not have the Special Rule Band and the organization has M-PESA web access; They will be advised to move the cash manually from MMF to Utility account and the team will escalate these as indicated below.

Call Center CEE will escalate via SR to LNM Support to change the Rule Band

M-PESA Corporate will change the Short Code’s Rule Band

Retail Center/Care Desk CEE will escalate via SR to the RCSA to effect the change.

SR’s SLA is 24 hours.

Where the organization does not have web access change of Rule Band will be escalated as above.

# **Service Mechanics on AliExpress App**

To use M-PESA simply

Download the AliExpress App on Google play store and Apple app store.

Sign in to AliExpress App

Select a product to purchase

Select M-PESA as a payment method

Enter M-PESA Pin on the prompt

# **Merchant KYC Requirement to sign in**

Till Number/Store Number.

Operator ID and operator PIN.

M-PESA Business App Features

Merchants can:

View their store balance.

View money-in/money-out charts.

Perform quick actions from the home screen.

# **Contact Safaricom Support.**

Transactions performed on the App

Withdraw to owner

Withdraw to bank

Withdraw at Agent.

Send to Paybill

Buy goods.

Pay customer.

Payments Portal Self Reversal Process

Partners will be able to reverse transactions erroneously received from other organizations and or individuals via USSD and web.

# **Requirements**

The organization must be existing and active in MPESA G2

The organization must be the credited party. The transaction to be reversed must be credited to the affected organization account (store or head office)

The transaction to be reversed must be 134 days old.

The organization account balance must be equal to or higher than reversal amount

The transaction must not have been reversed (in either authorized or complete status)

The reversal will only be initiated via USSD or via web by a user with the appropriate rights.

Reversal will only be done by the credited short code.

# **USSD process**

For the merchant/partner to be able to initiate a reversal via USSD a Nominated number must be attached to store or Head office.

Partners/merchants will dial the current merchant USSD \*234\*4# ok, select My Account Services and follow the prompts to initiate the reversal.

This will send the prompt to G2 to initiate and compete the reversal.

Web process

This will be done on the web.

Partners/merchants must have access to the web portal and are active users with the right permissions to be able to withdraw funds.

The merchant business operator will login to the web and follow the prompts to initiate and will follow up with a manager to approve the reversal.

Safaricom will only complete the initiated reversals upon written request from BE.

The debit party and the credit party will receive a notification for successful reversal

The transaction details will be captured on G2 and the payments portal for reporting.

The current M-PESA reversals dispute process will apply for all disputes.

# **Karibu Gift**

# **Definition**

This service aims at giving Safaricom subscribers who are on the old Karibu postpay an opportunity to share their accumulated minute with family and friends.

# **Eligibility**

- This Service is only available to Individuals who are still on the old Karibu postpay at the moment.
- Only the whitelisted customers will dial \*444\*4#
- The maximum one can share is 500 minutes and a minimum of 50 mins.

# **How It Works**

- Customers will dial \*444\*4# to select Karibu Gift
- Selects the minutes they want to share, enter the MSISDN the confirms to complete transfer of the resources
- The sponsor cannot input their sponsor number as a beneficiary
- The Sponsor can Gift as many times with no limitation as long they have the resources
- A customer cannot share resources that have been shared from another sponsor.
- Karibu Gift is only available to customers on the Safaricom network
- Currently the service is only available via the USSD \*444\*4#.

**NB:** Reversals **are not possible** once the resources have been transferred.

# **Checking Karibu Gift balance**

To check balance, customers will send the word BAL to 144

# **How the resources can be used**

The customer can use the resources to make both off-net calls and on-net calls.

# **Priority of usage**

Resources with a shorter validity period will take precedence over Karibu Gift

# **Resources rollover**

The resources do not roll over.

# **Accumulation of Bonga Points**

The beneficiary will not earn Bonga points.

# **Accumulation of Storo Bonus**

The beneficiary will not earn Storo bonus.

# **Validity**

The validity of the various resources will be displayed, and the customer selects their preferred option.

It is a service plan that gives customers the convenience to spend on Safaricom network and pay end month. However currently there is no provision available for new subscriptions.

Individual Prepay customers. Blazers can Opt-Out by dialing \*555# before joining Postpay.

- Subscribers who opt out of this service will not be able to subscribe back.

articleTitle: Handling claims for funds in Recycled Accounts (Archived fund requests)
markdownContent:
**Handling claims for funds in Recycled Accounts (Archived fund requests)**

# **REQUIREMENTS**

# **Customers residing within the country**

M-PESA Customers residing within Kenya will present the following documents at any Safaricom Shop/Care desk for assistance.

Original Document ID

Duly filled M-PESA claim form

# **Customers residing outside the country / in foreign countries**

M-PESA customers residing in foreign countries the below documents will be send via email to the respective shop’s email address or Customer Care customercare@Safaricom.co.ke along with the refund/ reversal claim request.

Copy of ID used to register for M-PESA - certified by Notary Public or at the Kenyan Embassy

- Copy of passport page with the stamp of entry into foreign country - certified by Notary Public or at the Kenyan Embassy
- Copy of passport’s Bio page with the stamp of entry into the residing foreign country - certified by Notary Public or at the Kenyan Embassy
- Copy of passport page with the stamp of exit from Kenya - certified by Notary Public or at the Kenyan Embassy
- Duly filled M-PESA claim form or a signed customer written letter requesting for the claim indicating all the details that must be filled in the M-PESA Claim form - certified by Notary Public or at the Kenyan Embassy.

NB: Notary Public is a counsel/lawyer/public officer who attests or certifies writings (such as a deed) to make them authentic and takes affidavits, depositions, and protests of negotiable paper

# **RETAIL PROCEDURE:**

**This procedure is applicable for:**

**Claim from Recycled lines as a result of MSISDN lifecycle** \- This will be applicable where the customer making the claim is the previous owner of the line:

Customer will be vetted based on the recycled CRM and M-PESA account information.

- The CEE will search for the customer’s number under recycled MSISDN tab on M-PESA system.
- The CEE check to confirm closure of all other FSI accounts. Where the accounts are active the CEE will proceed as per the respective FSI account closure processes.

**Claim from M-PESA accounts as a result of Incomplete MSISDN lifecycle recycling and erroneous registrations** – This will be applicable where the customer making the claim is the current owner of the line but M-PESA has details of another customer.

The customer will be vetted primarily on CRM and a comparison done on M-PESA.

The CEE will check the first call activation date on CRM and compare with the registration/dates that the funds were credited on M-PESA.

**Where the funds were credited after the first call event date and**;

The account is already recycled only claim of funds will be processed.

The account is active on M-PESA the customer will be given the option of reversing the funds before recycling the line or recycling the line and processing the funds from the archived account.

The account has funds credited before and after the first call date on CRM.

The customer will be advised the funds received after will be reversed and the rest recycled with the line for claim by the previous owner.

CEE will validate the reversal with the sender on intended recipient where applicable Where the customer indicates that they do not want the funds reversed the account will be recycled and an SR raised for manual movement of the funds from the archived account by the M-PESA BSS Team.

**Where the funds were credited before the line was activated on IN,** that means that the funds belong to the previous owner and thus no claim of funds will be processed. However, the M-PESA Account will be recycled as per the M-PESA recycling account to enable the new owner register for M-PESA.

The CEE check to confirm closure of all other FSI accounts. Where the accounts are active the CEE will proceed as per the respective FSI account closure processes.

# **To process the claim.**

The CEE will vet the presented the document ID against the details on the M-PESA/CRM systems. In addition, the CEE will.

Review the nominated number M-PESA transactions to confirm if the line has suspicious activity e.g., previous credits from archived funds or credits are from only one M-PESA agent/customer.

Any suspicious requests for claim of archived funds will be forwarded to Fraud Team for validations with reasons of suspicious activity before processing.

The CEE will confirm the availability of funds and advise the customer to fill in and sign the M-PESA claim of funds form.

The stamped duly filled M-PESA claim of funds form and the ID will be scanned on both sides (clear copies) attached on the MSISDN as an attachment on CRM at the account level.

- For an audit trail the attachments will be done on the the MSISDN at the account level and if the MSISDN is recycled the CEE will attach them on the closed account.
- The CEE will enter an interaction on CRM indicating the issue and the resolution offered.

- The CEE will pay out the claim as per the details attached on the claim form.

- The CEE will recycle the M-PESA Account where the account is active before processing the payout.
- The CEE will enter the Interaction ID, Claimant’s number, Number where the funds are being processed from and the amount on the comments box.

Once done the CEE will engage a Team Leader to complete the task on M-PESA.

The TL will vet the documents;

Confirm suspicious activities on the recipient account/notes on the donor etc. Any suspicious activities will be reported to M-PESA Fraud for investigations.

Enter the Interaction ID, Claimant’s number, Number where the funds are being processed from and the amount on the Reasons box for Audit purposes.

The CEE will raise an SR in the absence of a TL attaching the document ID and the duly filled stamped form for an Analyst to complete the task.

The Support Analyst will pick the SR vet the documents,

- Confirm suspicious activities on the recipient account/notes on the donor etc. Any suspicious activities will be reported to M-PESA Fraud for investigations
- Complete the task, advise the customer and close the SR.
- The Support Analyst will enter the Interaction ID, Claimant’s number, Number where the funds are being processed from and the amount on the Reasons box for Audit purposes.

Note:

- Claim of funds of all the other FSI accounts will be done as per the respective FSI account process.
- Where funds have been submitted to UFAA the customer will be advised as per the current UFAA claim of funds process.

**M-Akiba Service Information & Mechanics**

**M-Akiba Service Information & Mechanics (A0338)**

**Definition & Eligibility**

The M-Akiba Bond is a special Infrastructure Retail Bond that has been issued by the Government of Kenya to raise money to fund its' infrastructural projects. This is in line with vision 2030 to instigate a saving culture. The Government is looking at borrowing 5 billion Kenya shillings through the Special Infrastructure Bond. The interest rate for this bond is 10% per year and it is fixed payable twice in a year for the next three years.

**Eligibility**

You need to be a Kenyan Citizen living in Kenya.

You need to have a mobile phone (a simple phone will be okay)

You need to have registered your mobile number with Airtel or M-PESA Mobile Money

You need to open an M-Akiba CDS Account (this is Free)

**Benefits and Difference of M-Akiba**

M-Akiba Bond is a low-risk savings/ investment

It is affordable.

It is a sure source of income from the interest earned after every six months.

Agreed upon returns in form of interest paid – semi annually.

There is no taxation on the bond.

Liquidity as one can sell when need arises.

A way of saving money for the future

Convenient and confidential

You can transact Anywhere, anytime within the republic of Kenya

No need for a bank account, you use mobile money

When the bond matures the investor is paid back the face value of the bond.

**Difference** **in the M-Akiba Retail Bond**

In the past years, the Government has been issuing Treasury Bonds and Infrastructure bonds with a minimum investment amount Kshs.50,000.00 making it difficult for most Kenyans to afford the bonds.

The Government has now issued a special bond (M-akiba) with a minimum investment of Kshs.3,000. This bond is affordable to most Kenyans compared to the initial ones that had a minimum investment of Kshs.50,000

**Investing in M-Akiba Bond**

An investor buys the bond at a certain price called the face value/ par value and earn an interest at a certain rate called coupon rate calculated on the face value of the bond.

An investor can sell the bond to other investors at the face value before maturity. Selling the bond at a discount means he sells it for less than the face value while at a premium means selling it more than the face value. There are two ways one can benefit from the bonds.

One is by earning the interest that is paid out semi annually.

By selling the bond at a premium and getting the capital gain.

The minimum an investor can buy a bond is Kshs.3,000 worth. Thereafter, one can buy in the multiples of Kshs.500.00 per day.

If you choose to use the mobile money payment channel, daily allowable limits of Kshs.140, 000 per investor per day shall apply. However, if you use Pesalink, maximum amount will be 999,999 per day.

You can wait for the next day to do purchase transactions after exceeding the minimum allowed per day. You can repeat this daily until you reach the amount you wish to invest for as so long as the bond is still available for sale.

**NOTE:** There are no restrictions as to how much an investor shall buy in the secondary market.

Owing to the Mobile money charges and statutory levies it is advisable to sell the bond after day 60 from the bond value date (17th July 2017) after this date, you will be able to get your full initial investment; however, to enjoy the maximum return from the M-Akiba bond, it is highly recommended to hold the bond to maturity.

# **FTTH Refund for failed installations**

# **Reversal Requests guidelines**

This is applicable for reversal process for customers who request and make payment for service, but their request is not done to completion for various reasons including technical reasons.

This will be due to either technical or non-technical reasons.

# Technical

- Outside coverage
- Out of design / Scope
- Capacity issue I.e. (Splitter full)
- Additional material required. Applicable where it will require more than the guidelines given for poles, cables etc., thus additional higher budget that cannot be accommodated.  

# Non-technical

- Client cancelling installation request and requesting refund i.e., due to delayed installation.
- Denial of access during installation to client’s premise.
- Client unavailability.
- Route challenges.
- Unoccupied houses.
- Wrong package paid for at onboarding stage. 

The sales team will engage a potential customer and where payment is done,

(A CRQ is generated against the customer account and installation process will commence).

The central dispatch team will engage customer and schedule for installation.

They will then send the contractor technician to visit customer to access customer premise for installation to be done.  

(Where the installation is viable, they will proceed with installation and activation and will confirm service uptime).

# Reversal Requests – During onboarding due to technical reasons and non-technical reasons.

Where the installation is not viable, contractor will advise the dispatch team to update the CRQ on remedy with the specific reasons. They will capture details:

**Out of design** – Include GPS co-ordinates for the customer location to allow for verification by sales agent. This will be done within the 48Hrs.

**Capacity Issues** – Indicate reasons clearly on the CRQ the exact issue e.g. Signal issues, FAT full, etc. This should be done within the 48Hrs.

**Additional Material** – indicate the exact reason and additional material required on the CRQ, this should be done within the 48Hr

- Where the contractor identifies request as not feasible as per the above scenarios, the contractor will attach the notes of the status/outcome on the CRQ.
- (Technician will advise the customer accordingly on the reasons why installation cannot be done and that a refund will be done within 24hours).
- Central dispatch will then proceed to close the CRQ which will then result in generation of an SR to line 400 on CRM.
- Once closed all such tickets will not progress automatically but will raise an SR assigned to Call Centre L400 team on CRM and reversals done within 24Hrs of   SR creation.
- For installations that cannot be done within 48 hours but require more time to close including splitter issues, the customer will be advised on the time required to resolve (7 days) and these tickets will not be closed.
- (Customer will progressively be advised on the status of the installation process including timelines by the home dispatch team under home customer management.).
- The channels team will compile daily all failed installation tickets from the bi-hourly sales report and share it on mail to the L400 team for proactive refunds and closure of the SRs. 

- # M-PESA payments Reversal Process

Where payment is done via M-PESA, within 48Hrs of payment receipt. L400 will reverse transaction on CRM- Siebel. CEE will initiate M-PESA reversal against the M-PESA TID payment for the customer on CRM by clicking on the tab reverse FTTH transaction.

CEE will capture an interaction on customer account on CRM stating the reason for reversal.

L400 CEE will proceed to delete the FTTH connection Fee product on Siebel under CRM provisioning Tab.

L400 CEE will advise customer accordingly on the reasons for the refund and close SR.

Where payment is done via M-PESA and 48Hrs have elapsed since payment receipt, L400 CEE will create reversal activity on the SR.

CEE will create an activity to the L400 team leader for approval of the reversal as a manual adjustment decrement.

Upon approval L400 CEE will initiate a reversal on M-PESA G2 system for Paybill 150501 stating the reason for the reversal.

Marker checker will apply, L400 CEE or call center reversal team will complete the reversal request on M-PESA G2.

CEE will advise customer accordingly and close SR.

SLA is within 24 Hours of initiation of refund request. 

# POS payments.

For failed installation ticket reversals for payments done via POS at retail outlets, the CEE will validate the reasons for the refund by the comments on the SR.

The Shop /Line 400 CEE will proceed to decrement the amount on CRM/Siebel and there after login to SharePoint to commence the refund process with finance team using the link below [***https://safaricomo365.sharepoint.com/sites/ISODocumentCenter***](https://safaricomo365.sharepoint.com/sites/ISODocumentCenter)

The CEE will attach the approved decrement SR showing that the decrement has been done, attach proof of payment i.e receipt, reason for reversal and the customer mobile or account number for the refund to be made to and assigned to credit control team in finance.

The CEE will advise the customer that the reversal will be done within 24Hrs to the mobile number shared by the customer or preferred bank account.

 The CEE will proceed to delete the FTTH connection Fee product on Siebel under CRM provisioning Tab.

 The CEE will proceed to close the SR thereafter and advise the customer.

 Experience team under channels will share daily via email by 10 am a report of all failed installation tickets that require refunds to the Regional Account Manager, Team leaders, Zone leads and L400 team for customer communication on the reasons for failed installation.

 The sales agent will contact the customer, advise and apologize that connection will not be possible due to specified reasons on the ticket and that funds will be reversed within 24 hours.

 (At this point they may cross sell 4G for Home if customer is in a 4G covered area).

 (Sales team shall maintain a database of all cancelled sales and use this as a guide for future roll out / capacity expansion based on demand).

 A list of all reversed sales outside coverage /design will be shared with the channels - retention team to engage salesperson and agency involved for penalty on lack of integrity.

# Credit limit and bonga adjustments  

- Manual adjustment process will apply for airtime and bonga reversals
- For payments made via post pay credit limits and require adjustments, L400 team will engage credit control for subsequent adjustments of the customer’s monthly bill for failed installation tickets.
- Reporting and Tracking.

Weekly refund reports will be compiled and shared by the experience team under channels detailing all failed installation tickets against the refunds done.

Scenarios where tickets have been closed requesting for refund, yet the customer does not want the funds back but willing to wait until when the issues affecting installation have been sorted, then this should be done in writing and an email send by the customer to [safaricomhome@safaricom,co.ke](mailto:safaricomhome@safaricom,co.ke).

Daily SR status report for failed connections will be generated by the L400 folder team showing the SR status.

# Deletion of customer data on Sales portal

Upon successful refunds of failed installation tickets, deletion of customer details will be done monthly in accordance with the churn process.
