- The 50 mb will be restricted to the Boomplay content and any browsing outside the web portal will be charged from the customers bundle or airtime.
- The data bundles do not expire however subscription is charged as per the duration I.e. daily, weekly or monthly
- A customer will receive a prompt when you reach 10mb,2MB threshold As well as depletion.
- If a customer opts not to renew your subscription but continue to access Boomplay content, they will be charged at the normal data rates.
- A customer can access content via Wi-Fi after successful subscription or when the content bundle is depleted.
- The content bundle cannot be transferred or tethered for use on other devices.
- A customer will earn Bonga points for every purchase of Boomplay content bundles

# **Definition**

# **FTTH Service Renewal.**

- Before the renewal date, the customer will be sent an SMS notification from CBS informing them on renewal to be able to continue enjoying the service.
- This is sequential i.e. 7days, 5days and 1 day before the expiry of the current subscription.
- If there is no sufficient amount in the CI wallet for renewal, CBS will send a SMS advising the client that the service has not been renewed and advising them on how to pay.
- Renewal will be done automatically upon payment of applicable package as per available payment options.

# **Where failure is noted to allocate/renew service:-**

Where customer contacts other channels other than L400 i.e. L100/200, social media etc. CEE will confirm account payment status on CRM Siebel.

- Where account status is noted as rental suspend, CEE will advise customer to make payment, where applicable.
- Where account is noted as on rental suspend and customer confirms they have made payments, CEE will send an email to copsftth@safaricom.co.ke to go to the L400 support team/Folder support to assist.
- In cases where the customer makes a follow up and issue has breached the email SLA the CEE will send arequest via email to L400 copsftth@safaricom.co.ke and will advise customer on FTTH support channels i.e., via call or email. SLA 2 hours. 

- Customers may also make calls to L400 or via email.
- Customers may also visit retail outlets.
- L400 / retail CEE will receive customer request and will confirm account payment status on CRM Siebel.
- Where account status is noted as rental suspend, and no payment is reflected, CEE will advise customer accordingly and request customer to make applicable payment.
- Where customer confirms to have made payment, CEE will check on Siebel CRM on IN Data tab.
- Where amount is reflected on the IN tab, CEE will check if the provisioning tab is active.
- Where the provisioning tab is active / activated, CEE will advise the client to use USSD \*400#ok to activate the product. Where USSD fails, the CEE will delete the expired product and allocate the correct FTTH product on provisioning tab as per the customer request and amount available on IN DATA on
- Siebel CRM. [Screenshot] 

- Where the provisioning tab is inactive, CEE will identify the customer and do first call activation to activate the provisioning tab functionality then proceed to delete/activate the product on provisioning tab.
- Retail CEE will send an email to copsftth@safaricom.co.ke for assistance where they are having challenges assisting the customer.

articleTitle: NETWORK ISSUES and STANDARD RESPONSES SENT VIA SMS TO 5555
markdownContent:
# **NETWORK ISSUES and STANDARD RESPONSES SENT VIA SMS TO 5555**

- When a customer reports a Network Issue on the Network Tool (5555) it will be picked by Line 300 CEE.
- Line 300 CEE can access the network complaints from the Network 5555 SMS tool on CM Intranet Link provided.
- Here the agent will be able to sort and close the SMS and offer the appropriate response to the customer.
- For complaints that will need the CEE to raise a Service Request, kindly confirm all details from customers on call and use the information to raise a quality ticket.
- The customer will receive a text with the ticket number and be advised on the SLA (24 hrs. from the time received).
- When closing that SMS on the SMS 5555 tool, the CEE need not resend another message to the customer and will instead close the ticket without sending a text to the customer and include the following text for reporting purposes;
- For other Network 5555 complaints, they will not need the CEE to call back and only a response is necessary.
- For uniformity purposes, use the template provided to reply to all Network related issues.
- It will provide general guidelines on how to respond to case scenarios that are usually received on the Network tool.
- This information is necessary since it will be used to generate periodical reports.
- Do not discard any SMS, close all SMS and provide the appropriate reply text.

# **Reported global or specific region network issue from NOC.**

NOC (Network Operation Centre) reports a global or specific region network issue through Call Centre Escalation Folder/Line 300 Folder. The fault could be data or voice or both.

- The affected Customers who had reported their network issues to the Network Tool (5555) will receive a blanket SMS informing them that the issue is faulting, and we are working to resolve it.
- Once the issue is resolved, the customers who had reported their network issues to the Network Tool (5555) will get a blanket message informing them that the issue was resolved and thus to do location update.
- If the customer sends the following words; **Network, Network Problem, Network Issue, or Network error;** and does not fall on the affected sites as per site details and NOC reports: they will be asked to give a brief explanation of their issue.
- In case, a Customer sends non-network issues to 5555; They will be referred to the correct contact center touchpoint for assistance.

# **Troubleshooting tips for the Line 300 CEEs where there no reported issue****.**

The CEE will check previous interactions on Siebel (CRM) if the issue had been resolved.

In case a Customer sends network issue on an area whose fault was closed as per NOC report, the CEE will check customer profile on HLR (SAWA). **i.e. Barring’s, Call diverts, MNRF True, etc.**

If the profile of the number is okay, then the serving site (BTS) is checked.

If the serving site (BTS) is on NOC report and the fault is closed, the Customer number will be probed further.

If the serving site (BTS) is on NOC report and the fault is ongoing, the customer will get a response that there is network issue in their area, and we are working to resolve it.

The CEE will send a message to the customer and paste it also on Siebel interaction.

The interactions will include supporting evidence from the NOC report on the faulting area.

The Number is queried on CEM or CDRS on Siebel (CDRs are only checked when CEM does not display data regarding a number).

Airtime and data plans on IN data (Siebel) will also be checked.

If the line is okay, then the Customer will be sent the response that the network issue in their area was resolved.

The Customer will be advised to do Location Update (LU) and re-try accessing the voice or data services.

The message sent to the customer will be pasted on Siebel interaction.

The interactions will have supporting evidence from the NOC report of the closed issue.

In some cases, the Line 300 CEE will request for Location if the customer’s current site is unavailable on google maps. This will also apply, if the customer will request for a booster construction, and did not specify their location.

If the details provided and the customer is not in an affected area, but there is a planned booster construction, the customer will be advised on the planned site, same details will be included on Siebel interactions

# **Exceptions for Siebel interaction for bulk responses;**

The customers were asked to explain their issue.

Issue is under faulting and being reporting in large numbers.

Issues sent are not network related and therefore are referred to other touchpoints.

Line manager requested the tool to be cleared since the issues had been resolved.

**Standard Responses In Network 5555 SMS**

- For issues that have been escalated via SRs;
- Use Area Code \*Network Code\*\*
- Sub called back; issue raised on Sr Number.
- e.g. ER\*NC\*\*Sub called back; issue raised on **SR 1-26DXGX8N.**

For issues that are not related to Network or Safaricom products;

Close; Submit SMS>No Reason; Non-Service Related.

For other issues that will need a CEE to submit an SMS to the customer, here are the standard responses;

| Issue | English Response | Kiswahili Response |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Non Safaricom related issues | Dear customer, we have received your issue. 5555 is only for network queries. Thank you. | Jambo, tumepokea swala lako. Nambari ya 5555 hutumiwa kwa maswala ya network pekee. Asante |
| Safaricom but not network related | Dear customer, kindly SMS your query to 234 or 100 for assistance. Thank you. | Jambo, tafadhali tuma arafa fupi / SMS kwa nambari ya 100 au 200 kwa usaidizi zaidi.Asante |
| Global reported issues | Dear Customer, the network issue in your area is under investigation. We kindly request for your patience. Thank you. | Jambo, tatizo la network eneo lako linafanyiwa uchunguzi. Twakusihi uwe na subra tunapoishughulikia Asante |
| Resolved cases | Dear Customer, the network issue in your area is now resolved. Thank you for your patience. | Jambo, tatizo la network eneo lako lishatatuliwa. Asante kwa subra yako. |
| Specific noted voice problem on CEM | Dear Customer, the network issue in your area is now resolved, kindly switch your phone off and on and let us know if the issue recurs. Thank you. | Jambo, tatizo la network eneo lako lishatatuliwa. Zima simu kisha uiwashe na utujuze kama shida itatokea tena. Asante |
| No airtime | Dear Customer, the network issue in your area is now resolved kindly top up to enjoy our services. Thank you. | Jambo, tatizo la network eneo lako lishatatuliwa. Weka mjazo (credit) kwa simu ili uweze kufurahia huduma zetu. Asante |
| Unable to connect to the internet | Dear Customer, Kindly switch your phone off and back on to test internet services. Thank you. | Jambo, tafadhali zima na uiwashe simu ili ufanye majaribio ya huduma za intaneti. Asante |
| Poor 3G Network | Dear Customer, Kindly switch your phone off and on then choose 2G Network via settings for internet services. Thank you | Jambo, tafadhali zima simu yako kisha uchague 2G Network kupitia Setting ili upate huduma za intaneti. Asante |
| SMS waiting data | Dear customer, you do not have a problem with network, kindly delete SMS in your inbox as it is full. Thank you. | Jambo, huna shida na network. Futa arafa fupi / SMS kwani zimejaa kwa kisanduku chako cha simu. Asante |
| Safaricom guarantee | Dear Customer, Safaricom Guarantee service compensates for dropped calls. To opt out, dial *100*3*1#ok or *200*3*1#ok. Thanks. | Jambo, Safaricom Guaranteeinakupa dakika za bure za mazungumzo kwa kukatiza mawasiliano. Ili ujiondoe, bofya *100*3#ok au *200*3#ok. Asante |
| Issue on SR | Jambo, kindly note that the network issue in your area has been forwarded as per request ID number 1-A6CMP5R and will give you feedback in 48hrs. Thank you. | Jambo, fahamu kuwa tatizo lako la network kwa eneo lako limetumwa kwa idara husika kwa tikiti ya 1-A6CMP5R. Utapata majibu kwa saa 48. Asante |
| Request for BTS /4g installation | Dear customer, your request has been received, thank you for staying connected to Safaricom. | Jambo, ombi lako tumelipokea. Asante kwa kushikamana na Safaricom. Shukrani. |

articleTitle: KCB M-PESA Statements CRM View and Guide
markdownContent:
**KCB M-PESA Statement View & KCB Error Code Messages**

# **KCB M-PESA Statements CRM View and Guide**

Customer statement can be viewed for a maximum period of 1 Year from the date of query.

# **Benefit**

The statement has details as below:-

# **Activity Description**

• M-PESA to account-deposit to KCB M-PESA

• Account to M-PESA-withdrawal from KCB M-PESA.

Note: All transactions to and from M-PESA to KCB M-PESA pass through the savings account .i. e when opening a fixed deposit account from M-PESA

the amount to be fixed will first from M-PESA to savings account and from where it is the moved to the fixed deposit account .

- Activity Time Stamp i.e. date and time.
- Transaction Reference (KCB transaction reference number)
- Activity Type i.e. transactions that affect the account balance (financial or non-financial)
- Balance before Activity
- Transaction Amount
- Balance after Activity

# **KCB M-PESA– Loan Account Details**

The loan account tab has the loan contract ID and loan virtual contract ID, this will be used when there’s an issue that requires an escalation to the bank.

KCB loan repayment period is one month, referred to as loan term in this tab.

# **KCB – M-PESA– Savings account details**

This tab has visibility of the customer accounts: savings , fixed deposit and target savings accounts.

# **Benefit**

- The savings maturity date is displayed.
- Where the customer has several accounts, the CEE will be able to navigate to the tabs on the right to view details of customer savings.

**FTTH Upgrades and downgrades.**

Upgrades and downgrades are possible at any time within the subscription month.

However, for upgrade requests, proration will be done, and client will be requested to top up the difference depending on the package they are upgrading to.

Customer can upgrade or downgrade via; 

- DIY i.e., on the Safaricom APP,
- By dialing \*400#ok and following the prompts,
- Via a manual process by contacting Safaricom touch points. 

In case of failed DIY attempt or upon customer request, customer will contact Safaricom on the available touch points.

Where customer contacts other channels other than L400 i.e. L100/200, social media etc.

- CEE will advise customer on applicable DIY options.
- CEE will advise customer to ensure they have enough funds to fulfil the request.
- For cases where the CEE is not able to resolve the issue on call they will raise the customers issue via Email to copsftth@safaricom.co.ke , and advise customer on available FTTH support channels. The SLA is 2Hrs.

Where request is received at retail or L400 by customers and on email from internal staff.

- L400 / retail CEE will confirm there’s sufficient amount on CRM/ Siebel.

Where customer has insufficient amount, L400 / retail CEE will advise customer to top up amount.

- CEE will advise on available payment options and DIY, where preferred customer will be advised to call back after topping up their account should DIY fail. 

Where customer has sufficient funds, L400 CEE will upgrade / downgrade as per customers request on CRM Siebel and will advise them accordingly.

- CEE will manually delete the product and allocate the correct package on CRM.
- Customer will be advised on available DIY options i.e. USSD \*400# or My Safaricom App for upgrade, downgrades and management of their subscriptions.

# Signing up

- To sign into YouTube, enter your Google Account email and password.
- After signing up for YouTube, sign into your Google account. Google service will automatically sign you into YouTube.
- Deleting your Google Account will delete your YouTube data, including all videos, comments, and subscriptions.

## 

# **Mechanics to buy All in One + FREE YouTube Bundle**

A customer can get the All in One + FREE YouTube Bundle by simply:

- Dialing \*544#ok select Data bundle with Expiry, then select: All in One Bundle + FREE YouTube and follow prompts
- A customer can also buy All in One Monthly Bundles through \*100#ok or \*456#ok select option Buy then choose data bundles and follow prompts.
- Post-pay customers can dial \*200#ok then select option buy data bundles and follow prompts

N/B: A customer can buy for another number and the number will get the full resources.

**Bundle Purchase Payment options**

A customer can buy the All in One + FREE YouTube bundle using M-PESA or Airtime.

## 

# You tube bundle with NO Expiry purchase journey

- Customer dials \*544#, selects Data Bundle (NO EXPIRY DATE)
- Customer selects option 1: Buy for My Number.
- Customer Enters Amount they wish to spend and follow prompts

## 

# Cost and Payment Options

- The 80MB YouTube bundle costs Kshs. 10. While the 200Mb YouTube bundle costs Kshs. 20.
- A customer can pay for the service using **Airtime or M-PESA.**

## 

# Bundles Features

- The customer can only use the YouTube data bundle to watch videos on YouTube.
- The YouTube bundles will be valid for 24 hours after which they will expire.

# Large Enterprise/SME/SoHo) Calling

- For every Enterprise customer’s call/visit into Retail, the CEE will check the customer’s number, against the {technical & billing contacts on CRM}.
- Sensitize the customer on the proactive SMS alerts being sent out to customers {invoice, disconnection, dunning milestones, Planned maintenance, Re-connection and Loss of Service alerts}.
- Reference the initial application form that is attached on CRM. Should there be a need to amend, CEE will seek customer consent to use/ edit /add the technical numbers that is on CRM and VET with the following documents:

Certificate of Incorporation number. (where applicable).

Certificate of registration or Business permit.

Last amount paid and the mode of payment.

- Also check if there was a previous interaction with the same caller about the similar {dunning, re-connection, preventive maintenance & LOS alerts} enquiries, confirming it’s the same person as per registration documents.
- Verify the existing customer contacts on CRM for the customer to validate as per the above process.

# Checking/changing Technical Email/Phone contact:

- If the contacts are correct, CEE will inform the customer of the same, and ask the customer if the notifications {dunning, re-connection, preventive maintenance & LOS alerts} are received successfully (where applicable).
- Where the contacts are different/have since changed, CEE will proceed to vet the customer with the following documents:

- Certificate of Incorporation number.
- Certificate of registration or Business permit
- Last amount paid and the mode of payment.

- If the customer passes the vetting, the CEE will edit/add the technical MSISDN & email addresses on CI level for customers with multiple accounts and on Parent account level for customers with one account.

- Where a customer has multiple technical contacts, the CEE shall confirm if the person requesting is the one on the registration documents as the authority to assign/ edit/add technical contact can only be done by the person on the registration documents.
- Raise an interaction indicating action and comprehensive vetting details.

Billing Email/Phone contact: ***(New– Procedure allows CEE to change the billing MSISDN on the call after vetting)***

- Verify the existing customer contacts on CRM; for the customer to validate (as per process) and sensitize the customer on the proactive SMS alerts being sent out to customers {dunning, disconnection, re-connection alerts}.
- If the billing contacts are correct, CEE will inform the customer of the same, and ask the customer if the notifications {dunning, disconnection, re-connection} alerts are received successfully (where applicable).
- Where the customer does not receive the said notifications, CEE will escalate the issue via SR to the 2nd line support team, clearly indicating the customer problem.
- Where the billing MSISDN is different/has since changed, CEE will proceed to vet the customer with the following documents:

- Certificate of Incorporation number.
- Certificate of registration or Business permit
- Last amount paid and the mode of payment.

- If the customer passes the vetting, the CEE will edit/add the update billing MSISDN on CI level for customers with multiple accounts and on Parent account level for customers with one account.
- Where the billing email address is different / has since changed, CEE will advise the customer to make a formal request as follows:

# At the Retail Shop.

The Customer shall provide a written request with below requirements: -

- Be on the company original letter head.
- Have the letter stamped using the company rubber stamp/ seal. In exceptional cases where company claims to have no stamp, CEE will verify from previous correspondence / account managers and company contact person.
- Letter must state that the bearer has been authorized to request for change of billing email contacts on behalf of the company, indicating in the letter their full name, and ID number.
- The letter must also indicate the email to be changed.
- Letter must be signed by the company contact person.
- The sent party must have the original valid ID.

# L2222 Support.

- The business’ contact person shall send a Written request via email with below requirements: -

- Originate from the organization’s email address.
- A company letter requesting the changes, signed and stamped should suffice as well.
- The email must indicate the email to be changed and a brief explanation.
- Verify from previous correspondence / account managers and company contact person.

- If the above are correct, the CEE will edit the billing Email address as per request.

- Inform the customer of the effected changes and notify the business contact person of the change effected.
- Raise an interaction indicating action and attach comprehensive vetting details for future reference.

articleTitle: Claiming Archived Funds before UFAA Submission
markdownContent:
# **Claiming Archived Funds before UFAA Submission**

Safaricom, under the M-PESA Service is required by law to declare any funds it has held in the M-PESA system that have been dormant in the archived account and not claimed within a period of two (2) years by the Owners (as defined by the Act) or as when instructed by the Unclaimed Financial Assets Authority (UFAA).

Between 8th June and 16th Sep 2020 Safaricom submited all unclaimed funds held in accounts that were **recycled between 1st July 2017** and **30th June 2018.**

Every year Financial Services (FS) will run a drive to encourage customers to claim their funds before submission to UFAA.

M-PESA customers who have funds (balances below 70,000) in their M-PESA accounts are contacted via SMS and encouraged to dial USSD \*334#  \*405# to withdraw their funds before submission to UFAA.

This USSD is only available during this period

Customers with more than Kshs 70,000 are advised to visit the Retail shops with their IDs to claim their funds.

**N/B**: For customers who call/visit the shop for claims from G2 accounts that were archived between 1St July 2017 to 30th June 2018, kindly advise them that the funds will be available for collection from UFAA as from 1/11/20.

articleTitle: Self Service Procedures under Corporate Advantage PLUS
markdownContent:
# **Moving from One Postpay Tariff to Another**

A customer can move from one PostPay tariff to another.

**Requirements;**

- Corporate requests should be written on a company letter head and signed by the contact person or an authority in the organization.
- A written request from the customer submitted at the Retail Centre.
- Corporates wishing to migrate their subscribers to advantage plus tariff will follow normal application procedure for this tariff.

# 

# **Additional Lines/Services to A Corporate Account**

- Additional Services include; Roaming, Data, etc.
- The corporate will submit a written request on a company Letter head with a stamp and signed by the Contact person or an authorized representative of the Corporate.
- The request is submitted to a retail shop or emailed to advantage@safaricom.co.ke.

# **Account Transfers**

- Customers transferring from an existing postpaid account to a new account will need to fill in fresh application forms.
- Customers transferring from an existing postpaid account to another will need to bring letters from both the account they are moving from and the account they are moving to, detailing the movement.

# 

# **Corporate Advantage Plus Service Termination at the Retail Centre**

- Customers wishing to terminate the service will notify Safaricom in writing of their intention to terminate their contract by filling a Contract Termination Form.
- The letter must be on company letter head with an official sign and stamp.
- The letter should be addressed to the credit manager and dropped at RC or e-mail Scanned copy of the signed letter to credit control.
- Upon deactivation, the customer tariff will revert to their original plan.

The SLA 24 hours receipt of the request

# **Definition**

This is a promotion that will see all 4G devices bought from the open market receiving free resources after attaching to Safaricom network for the first time.

# **Open Market devices**

These are the devices bought in the open market other than Safaricom shops.

# **Eligibility**

The Free data will be awarded to all 4G devices sold in the open market by our dealers and other retailers etc.

# **How it works**

Customers purchasing devices from the open market will be awarded with Free data when they do the below actions;

- Insert a Safaricom sim cards on the new device
- Purchase any data bundle pack for any amount
- Receive the FREE 1GB data award. This bundle is open to access any internet content.
- Receive the FREE 150MB daily data for 30 days. The **Free 150MB Daily allocation bundle** for Open Market Device Bundling will be locked to access **Youtube only**.

Customer will receive two types of bundles:

- 1GB one off bundle valid for 24hrs. This bundle is open to access any internet content.
- 150MB daily allocation bundle for 30days valid till midnight. The **Free 150MB Daily allocation bundle** for Open Market Device Bundling will be locked to access **Youtube only**.

# **Mechanics**

- Any unutilized bundle will expire at midnight as customer receives the allocation for the next day, resources will **NOT** roll over.
- After 30days the offer will be removed from customer’s profile.
- The free data will not be transferable or shareable.
- The free bundles will not be used to extend any other data resource that customer has.
- If customer has other resources with less validity, i.e., hourly should be utilized first before the Free resource.
- Once customer receives the FREE data the IMEI is blacklisted and cannot receive another FREE data.
- For devices that have duplicate IMEIs, the subsequent IMEI attaching on our network will not be awarded the Free data.
- To check balance customer will dial \*544# select Balance and Tips option to see all the data balances.
- The FREE data is not locked, customer can browse / access any content.
- Any unused data will expire after 24hours for the one off or at midnight for the daily allocation data.
- Customer will be required to buy a data bundle in order to receive the FREE 1GB and the subsequent Free 150MB daily allocation bundle.
- Customer cannot be awarded twice if they have redeemed the FREE data already in another simcard.

# **Creating a PayPal Account**

Customer Signs up for a PayPal account at paypal.com/ke and follow the steps to complete registration.

While signing up customer can skip linking a card.

To finish setting up PayPal account, simply click on the PayPal logo at the top left or click on the link in the email from PayPal to confirm the email address.

# **Service Registration**

Log in with PayPal login details (email and password).

Enter M-PESA account phone number.

After submitting account details, Thunes, on behalf of M-PESA, will send a 4-digit verification code to the mobile number associated with the M-PESA account.

Enter the code to confirm and complete the account linkage, this will enable customer next time they can log in directly with their PayPal email and password and get started.

# **Topping up PayPal Account**

After completing the registration, click "Top Up".

Enter the amount to top up in USD and click "Calculate" to get the equivalent amount converted in KES. This is the KES amount to be transferred from M-PESA account. The exchange rate used will be displayed on the same page.

Go to M-PESA menu and select "Lipa na M-PESA" then the "Pay Bill" option.

Enter Business Number 800088.

Enter phone number as the Account Number.

Enter M-PESA PIN and click "Send".

Use newly topped up balance to easily and more securely shop online or send payments with PayPal.

Customers can also top up from My Safaricom App.

# **Withdrawing money from PayPal to M-PESA account**

After completing the registration, click "Withdraw".

Available balance will be displayed. Customer will only be able to withdraw money up to the available USD balance shown in their PayPal account. If customer held a balance in their PayPal account in a different currency, they should log in to PayPal account at paypal.com/ke and convert the money into USD.

Enter the amount they would like to withdraw from their PayPal account in USD.

Customer will be redirected to a page showing the amount to be received in KES, the exchange rate used for the currency conversion, and the estimated transaction processing time.

Confirm and complete the withdrawal of funds.

# **Sending funds to different person****.**

Both PayPal and M-PESA accounts must be held in the same name and customer can move money between the accounts.

The service does not support money transfers between different people.

# **How to set up a USD dollar account****.**

**Personal account:**

Log in to your PayPal account.

Click PayPal balance.

Click Manage currencies.

Select the currency: USD dollar.

Click Add Currency

**Business account:**

Log in to the PayPal account.

Click Currencies under the PayPal account balance.

Open the Select new currency dropdown.

Select the currency you want.

Click Add Currency.

# **Linking PayPal Account to both Card and M-PESA**

It is possible, customer to follow the direction on the website.

Contact PayPal in case you need further help as below.

**Email**

Go to www.paypal.com and log in to the account.

Click Help & Contact near the bottom of the page.

Click Message Center.

Click Compose.

Choose the topic and sub-topic that best match your reason for contacting us.

Type the message.

Click Send.

# **Customer care Access**

Phone

Call as a guest: 1-402-517-4519, Monday through Friday 9AM to 5.30PM local South African time.

Call as an existing customer.

Go to www.paypal.com and log in to the account.

Click Help & Contact at the bottom of any PayPal page.

Click Call customer support to see the One-Time Passcode (6 digits).

The One-Time Passcode is a random number generated by our system that helps verify your identity and get faster support.

The One-Time Passcode is valid for one hour. If it expires, you will need to go to the Call customer support page again to find a new One-Time Passcode.

Customer can also call: 1-402-517-4519.

articleTitle: Social media services Definitions, Mechanics and Features
markdownContent:
# **FACEBOOK**

#  

# **Definition**

Facebook is a popular free social networking website that allows registered users to create profiles, upload photos and video, send messages and keep in touch with friends, family and colleagues.

#  

# **Facebook Sign- up Mechanics**

- If using the phone go to m.**facebook**.com/if using Computer go to **facebook**.com.
- Click Create New Account.
- Enter your name, email or mobile phone number, password, date of birth and gender. Click Sign Up.
- To finish creating your account, you need to confirm your email or mobile phone number.

**N/B:** Keep in mind that the Facebook mobile site is the version that works with most mobile browsers.

#  

# **Safaricom Facebook account**

The Safaricom Facebook account is www.facebook.com/SafaricomPLC i.e. Safaricom Kenya Official Page. Simply 'Like' the page to see the Safaricom Facebook updates.

#  

# **Free Facebook mode**

**Definition**

- This Service offers Safaricom subscribers a chance to experience basic Facebook services for free, without using their airtime or data bundle (“Facebook Free Mode”). Facebook Free Mode is a lightweight version of Facebook where you can post, comment, and like for free.
- It also offers subscribers an opportunity to experience in data mode, using their airtime or data bundles (“Facebook Data Mode”). To view photos or videos, switch to Data Mode (full Facebook) by clicking the “See Photos” button on the top right on FB.

**Eligibility**

All Safaricom users can enjoy Facebook for free by default.

# **SMS charges on Facebook**

**Facebook** doesn't **charge** you for using **Facebook** texts. However, your mobile provider's standard rates for sending and receiving text messages (**SMS**) still apply.

#  

# **Key Features**

- New Facebook customers will have FREE Facebook access for 15days. To enroll to Facebook, they can visit www.facebook.com.
- Returning Facebook customers who have not used for more than 15days will be given FREE access to Facebook for 3days.
- Free mode will be capped at 20MB free mode consumption per day.
- An existing customer can switch modes between paid and Free.
- Free mode for a new/returning customer means the full Facebook experience excluding videos while Free mode for an existing customer includes text, like, comment.
- If an existing customer on the toggle/picture/video/external link will take them to an interstitial page which will provide notice for the customers to buy bundles.
- The service is not available for FB App on IOS but IOS users can access using the browser.
- Customers can now purchase bundles without Expiry on Facebook
- Free mode is capped at 20MB free mode consumption.

#  

# **TWITTER**

**Definition**

- **Twitter** is a free social networking microblogging service that allows registered members to broadcast short posts called tweets. Twitter members can broadcast tweets and follow other users' tweets by using multiple platforms and devices.
- Tweets can be up to 140 characters long and can include links to relevant websites and resources. Twitter users follow other users. If you follow someone you can see their tweets in your twitter 'timeline'.
- **Twitter widgets:** allows one to embed a Twitter timeline widget that showcases all their Twitter posts right on their website. People can browse their web pages and get a sneak peek into their Twitter chatter without having to leave their site.

#  

# **Mechanics to tweet**

- Type your Tweet (up to 280 characters) into the compose box at the top of your Home timeline or click the Tweet button in the navigation bar.
- You can include up to 4 photos, a GIF, or a video in your Tweet.
- Click the Tweet button to post the Tweet to your profile.

**Twitter Lingo**

**@mentions on twitter**

- A mention is a Tweet that contains another person's username anywhere in the body of the Tweet.
- A mention is a Tweet that contains another person's username anywhere in the body of the Tweet. Visiting another account's profile page on Twitter will not display Tweets that mention them. However, you can search Twitter for Tweets mentioning their username.

**#Hashtags**

A hashtag is a keyword or a phrase, immediately preceded by the pound sign (#), used to describe a topic or concept on Twitter.

**Direct messages "DM" on twitter**

Direct messages are personal messages sent from one Twitter account to another; they do not appear in public for anyone else to read. You can only send a direct message to a person who follows you.

**N/B:** An @reply is a public message sent regardless of follow-ship. Anyone can view it (if your Tweets are public). A direct message can only be sent by someone you follow and can only be seen by the sender and intended recipient.

**A twitter Handle**

- A Twitter handle is the username that appears at the end of your unique Twitter URL.
- Twitter handles appear after the @ sign in your profile URL and it must be unique to your account.
- A Twitter name, on the other hand, is simply there to help people find the company they're looking for.

**YOUTUBE**

- **YouTube** provides a simple way for people to store videos online and share them with others.
- **YouTube** videos cover any topic anyone cares to upload a video about.
- These videos are easy to share via other forms of social media, email and websites and can also be embedded in other websites.

#  

# **Mambo ni YouTube offer**

**Definition**

- This is a new Safaricom product that Offers FREE 2GB YouTube Bundle to all Safaricom customers who buy any All in One Bundles of KES 1,000 and above.
- **The All in One Bundle** is a monthly plan that gives our customers a combination of Minutes, Data and SMS in one convenient bundle. The All in One plan is available from Ksh 1,000 and comes with options that take care of your needs, whether you need to Talk More or to Browse More. Simply dial \*544# and select “All in One Bundle + FREE YouTube” to buy your bundle.

**Bundle features**

- A Customer can start using the FREE YouTube bundle to watch YouTube content immediately after purchase up to 5GB. The customer will not to wait until their current bundle is depleted.
- All bundles come with the FREE WhatsApp in addition to the FREE 2GB YouTube bundle valid for 30 days.

**YouTube Upsell**

**Definition**

It is a daily YouTube bundle that customers are offered after they purchase a normal bundle.

**Eligibility**

The product can be accessed by any Safaricom customer.

#

- The customer will dial the USSD \*544# and after purchasing a normal bundle will be asked if they would like to purchase a YouTube bundle.

#  

# **GOOGLE SERVICES**

**Definition**

- **Google Play Services** is a background service that runs on Android, which in turn helps in integrating Google's advanced functionalities with other applications. It is also used to update Google apps. It ensures that even older versions of Android enjoy the latest features provided by Google
- A [**Google Account**](https://support.google.com/accounts/answer/27441?hl=en&ref_topic=3382296) is a username and password that can be used to log in to consumer Google applications like Docs, Sites, Maps, and Photos, but a Google account doesn't necessarily end with @gmail.com. Think of it this way: All Gmail.com accounts are Google accounts, but not all Google accounts are Gmail.com accounts.
- A [**Gmail account**](https://support.google.com/mail/answer/56256?hl=en)﻿ is a free Google account with an email address that ends in @gmail.com.

This service is only offered to Users in Kenya with:

Back up and sync is a storage service that automatically saves your photos and videos to your Google Account. These photos and videos will be accessible from any device where you are logged in to your account.

articleTitle: Handset DIY’s for phone settings and Maneuvering
markdownContent:
# **Handset DIY**

# **M\-PESA Service and Nokia C3 Handset**

For customers who get the error message ‘wrong M-PESA PIN’ on entering their correct M-PESA PIN number when transacting on M-PESA service using the Nokia C3 handset or another Qwerty handset e.g. Nokia X2

**NOTE:**  advise the customers as follows: -

When transacting on M-PESA service on this handset; before entering their M-PESA PIN.

Advise them to press and hold the arrow button/ also known as the function key which is located on the bottom right-hand side of the handset’s keypad

This will change the format from ‘alphabets’ to ‘numbers’

Thereafter, they can enter their M-PESA PIN number and continue to transact on the service.

# **Confirming Original handsets**

Use the following procedure

- Dial \*#06# to establish the mobile handset’s IMEI (Serial)
- Copy the 15-digit number displayed on the screen.
- Type the 15-digit number (IMEI) and send it via SMS to 1555.

# **For Samsung customers not able to query IMEI using \*#06#,**

Guide to turn off auto blocker by following below steps.

Disable Auto Blocker:

Go to Settings.

Select Security and Privacy.

Select Auto Blocker.

Then turn it Off.

Then retry the procedure \*#06# again.

Remind to turn auto blocker on again for security reasons after checking the IMEI.

**Handset not registering network**

# **When handset is not registering network:**

Confirm network settings are either automatic or manually selected as Safaricom.

Restart your phone and try again.

Take the handset to the technician for repair if it does not work. 

# **Handset is not requesting for PIN upon switching ON**

You will have to change your phone settings to activate PIN code request.

General procedure is as; Go to Menu-settings-security settings-Pin code request-On

# **Different TIME and/or DATE in Nokia Handset**

Select Time Zone GMT 3 in the Date and Time Setting

This message is especially in Nokia’s; own number sending is off so customer needs to switch it on.

Alternatively, long press the # key and change phone line in use.

**Stopping data services on an Android Phone or Tablet procedure**

For the earlier versions of Android Operating System e.g. Android OS, v2.3.6 (Gingerbread) go to:

Menu>settings>Wireless and networks>mobile network>Data enabled>Uncheck the box.

For the latest versions of Android Operating System e.g. Android OS, v4.1.2 (JellyBean), upgradable to v4.4.2 (KitKat) go to: Go to Settings>More>Mobile Networks>Mobile Data/Data Enabled>Uncheck the box.

# **Cancel all diverts in phone**

To cancel all diverts on your phone dial; 
##004#ok or #004#ok 
OR ##002#ok or #002#ok.

Cancel all voice mail diverts in phone.

To cancel all diverts, Dial ##002# OK or ##004# OK.

# **Applications using data bundles in my Android phone**

Open "My data usage" link: <<[https://tinyurl.com/safaricom-data-usage](https://tinyurl.com/safaricom-data-usage)\>>

Or follow the below steps:

Go to Settings

Tap on Data Usage

Check on The List of Applications showing data usage.

**Enabling data roaming in an android phone**

Tap on APP

Tap on setting.

Tap more setting.

Tap mobile networks.

Tap on Data Roaming and change to ON or OF

# **Restricting data usage in Windows Phone.**

For windows phones you can use an application called data sense.

Most phones already have it but if you don’t have it you can download it from

The windows market. (**This applies only for phones running windows Phone 8 and above)**.

Go to the app and select settings at the bottom of the screen.

On the next page you can turn on restrict background data to lower data usage When the phone is not in active use.

You can also set browser data savings which will result on the data being Compressed reducing the volume.

You can also set the limit so that the handset will notify you when the set Amount is reached.

Swiping across on the first page of data sense reveals usage summary per Application.

# **Ending "background data" on a phone**

**Different Phone Models have different steps to restricting background data. See**

Below samples for guidance:

**Samsung Phones:** From Main Menu, Go to Settings>connections>data Usage>mobile data usage>for each application in the list, switch off allow Background data usage

**OPPO:** From Main Menu, Go to Settings>Accounts and Sync>switch off

**Huawei:** From Main Menu, Settings > Wireless & Networks > Data Usage > select Particular Application and switch off background data.

**Techno:** From Main Menu, Setting > Network & Internet > Data Usage > Mobile Data Usage > select Particular Application and switch off its data Connection

**iPhone:** From Main Menu, Settings > Mobile Data > select Particular Application and switch off its data connection.

**Nokia Phone** and **other common androids:** From Main Menu, Go to Settings>network and internet> Data usage> mobile data usage> Select Restrict background data check box for every app.

# **Applications running in an Android phone**

The customer can change the settings to limit/restrict background data

For most android Phones you will find this under Settings> data usage then go to menu and tick/check restrict background data

For older devices running 2.3 and below go to settings > accounts and Sync and uncheck background data.

These devices do not have data usage summary so the user may need to Download one from play store.

# **Creating WI-FI Hotspot on phone**

**Android Phone**

Go to Settings on your Samsung Phone.

From the **Home** screen, press The **Menu** button, then tap **Settings**.

Select Settings> More>Tethering & Portable Hotspot

Turn on Portable Wi-Fi hotspot.

Click on Set up Wi-Fi hotspot and change.

Set Network SSID:(This is the name displayed when you search the Wi-Fi)

Set Password: This is the password to give you access to the Wi-Fi network. Then Save.

**Windows phone**

Click on Menu>Settings and Enable Internet Sharing

Click Set Up and change the Broadcast Mode and Password and save

# **Tethering via Bluetooth in an Android Phone**

**Older versions**

Tap on settings.

Tap on Tethering and Wi-Fi Hotspot

Check Bluetooth Sharing

Enable Bluetooth on your computer.

Go to control panel and select device and printers.

select device to add to the computer. 

**Newer versions.**

Touch the "Settings" application.

Touch "Wireless & Networks" and select "Tethering & Portable Hotspot."

Tap the "Bluetooth Tethering" check box to enable.

Bluetooth Internet sharing on your Android device

Pair the other Bluetooth device to your Android device.

# **Setting internets manually on an Android Phone e.g. Huawei Ideos****.**

Note that there is an over- ride feature on the network that automatically autocorrects settings when customer’s access internet hence most will not need to Input settings manually or call for the same but in-case they do, give them the manual Settings.

Go to settings>Wireless& network settings>Mobile Networks>Access point Names>New APN

Name: Safaricom

APN: Safaricom

Username: saf

Password: data

Tap on the menu button and save settings.

**Trouble shooting guide.**

Check if the MSISDN has Airtime/ Bundle

Were they able to browse before.

Does the MSISDN’s have barring on HLR? Check barring on the MSIDN-

Follow the barring procedure Can the customer access some sites: Example via a browser or other application (Facebook, Twitter etc?)

What error message does the customer get

Confirm the settings the customer has if they are as below, if not give the Customer the settings and ask them to try again.

Should the customer call back after putting the settings and still unable to

Browse, raise an SR with the below details below:

Phone type and if its 2G/3G/4G

# **Error message when attempting to browse**

Were they able to browse before?

If they were able to browse before

# **For the other versions of Android Operating System, the procedure is**

Go to Settings>More>Mobile Network>Access Point Names>New APN.

Name: Safaricom 
APN: Safaricom

Username: saf 
Password: data 
Tap on the menu button and save settings.

# **Turning on/off 4G network on mobile phone**

You can activate or deactivate 4G in your Phone or tablet's menu settings.

Examples as below.

iPhone: Settings> Mobile/Cellular> Voice & Data

Android: Settings> More Networks> Mobile Networks> Network mode>

Change to LTE/4G

# **Managing handsets locked on 3G network**

Safaricom offers both 2G, 3G 4G network. While 3G is used mainly to access High Speed Data, voice services can be offered on both 2G, 3G and 4G

Customers who unknowingly select 3G Only mode on their phones will restrict their phone to the 3G networks.

The downside of this is that they may experience degraded voice quality in the event that 3G coverage is degraded or unavailable.

This mainly affects**,** Android, IOS (Apple) Blackberry and Windows

# **Switching between 3G and 2G networks on Android:**

Go to Settings> Wireless & Networks> Mobile Networks> Select Network Mode> Select > WCDMA (preferred) GSM or GSM/WCDMA Auto Mode

Go to settings>More>Mobile networks>Network Mode. Select either GSM/WCDMA (auto mode) or WCDMA only**.**

GSM only is for EDGE and GPRS usage and locks the device to Edge and WCDMA only is for 3G and HSDPA usage and locks the device to 3G.

**Blackberry:**

Go to Manage Connection>Mobile Network Option>Network Mode. Set either 3G or 2G

Go to Manage Connection>Networks and Connections>Mobile Network option> Network Mode. Set either 3G or 2G

# **i-Phone Operating System (IOS)**

  Menu >Tap on Settings icon> Tap on General>Tap on Network or Mobile Data or Cellular>Choose Network mode> Tap the indicator next to Enable 3G/Slide to turn it on or off.

**Note:** If you turn on 3G, your phone automatically switches between the two networks modes provided you're within range of a 3G network.

**Windows:**

Menu > Settings > Mobile Network > Select Highest Connection Speed: E or 3G.

**Cold Boot****.**

**Definition:** A Cold Boot or Boot simply restarts your device.

**Mechanics,** Doing a Hard Reboot/Cold Boot

Android Phones with no removable batteries

Press and hold the Power and Volume Down buttons simultaneously until

You see the screen shuts down and you see the reboot animation.

# **IOS Devices.**

iPhone except the iPhone 7 and 7 Plus

Press and hold both the Sleep/Wake and Home buttons simultaneously for atleast 10 seconds, until you see the Apple logo. You can let go of both button after the Apple logo appears.

**iPhone 7 and 7 Plus**

Press and hold both the Sleep/Wake and Volume Down buttons.

simultaneously for at least 10 seconds until the Apple logo appears.

Rebooting an iPhone 8 or iPhone 8 Plus takes three steps.

Press and quickly release the Volume Up button.

Press and quickly release the Volume Down button.

Press and hold the Side button (aka power) until you see the Appll4 logo.

**Note:** Apple now refers to the Sleep/Wake (power) button as the Side button as of the iPhone 8, iPhone 8 Plus, and iPhone X.

A reboot simply restarts your phone.

A reset wipes all data to clear bugs

#  **Accessing Safaricom Web Portal from Phone**

If your mobile is WAP enabled, you can access Safaricom Web Portal by clicking on the Internet icon your handset and typing wap.safaricom.com.

You can also add wap.safaricom.com as a bookmark on your handset for easy access whenever you want to browse and download content.

You will automatically be registered and logged in to the system.

# **GET IT 411 channel/service active list on** **phone**

Send an SMS with the word ‘LIST’ to 411 or 21411 for free.

**NETWORK ERRORS & MESSAGES**

**Network error messages:**

**English:** Sorry, your call cannot be connected at the moment please try later. 
**Swahili:** Nasikitika, hatuwezi kukamilisha nambari ya simu kwa sasa, jaribu tena baadaye 
The network may be having problems connecting especially during high traffic, escalate via service request.

**English:** Sorry, we cannot complete the call as dialed, please check the number and try again.

**Swahili**: nasikitika hatuwezi kukamilisha nambari uliopiga, tafadhali angali namba halafu upige tena.

First confirm if number is accurately dialed

Recipient might have diverted their calls to an invalid number.

Advise customer to send SMS recipient and advise him/her to cancel.

# **Wrong divert**

**English:** Sorry, the number you have dialed is not in service.

**Swahili:** Nasikitika nambari uliopiga haitumiki 
Dialled number is non- existing or a deleted number.

**English:** Sorry, the number you have dialed is temporarily out of service. 
**Swahili:** Nasikitika simu haifanyi kazi kwa sasa

Destination or number being called is unavailable and Sim has Incoming call barrings.

Recipient number could have been barred due to various reasons. E.g. Stolen / lost Sim, nonpayment of bill

**English:** Sorry, the service requested is not available from this line. Please dial 100 for assistance. 
**Swahili:** Nasikitika, huduma unayoitaka haipatikani Kwa simu yako. Tafadhali piga100 upate msaada 
Dialling number is barred from originating calls; deactivate call barrings of outgoing calls

**English:** Sorry, we cannot complete the call at the moment, please try again.

Recipient number is diverted to another but does not have enough credit to allow the divert

**English:** Sorry, the mobile subscriber cannot be reached. 
**Swahili:** Nasikitika, mteja wa nambari uliopiga hapatikani kwa sasa 
Recipient’s phone is off or out of coverage

**English:** Sorry, the call is terminated due to low transmission signal level.

Radio link loss, retry calling later

**English:** "the number dialed is not in service please call 991 for assistance "Number has been diverted to a wrong landline number (Note Diverts to landline may give u numerous unique messages such as the caller cannot accept your call

English: Sorry the party you called cannot accept your call at the moment This means the person you are calling is already on another phone or call and so s/he is not in a position to accept your call

**English:** SOS calls on you are within the range of network, but you are not allowed to use it. However, in an emergency you may be able to

If call 112 or 999 if emergency calls cannot be made, then the customer is not in a GSM covered area or phone is not registering network. Check that the network bar is displayed or move to a coverage area

**English:** No access 
This means the handset’s antenna is fault

**English:** Number unobtainable. 
Confirm the dialed number; prefix 0 in 0722 might be missing

**English:** "System unavailable". 
Switch mobile off for a minute the switch it back on.

**English:** Service not available 
Customer is trying to Activate some GSM services that are not available on the network

**English:** Number currently in use

**A network problem**. Contact Safaricom or SMS 5555 (network hotline for free)

When topping-up instead of pressing # one presses calling key or Ok or Yes Issue: Quality reception when calling

Avoid placing your fingers on the top of the phone, where the aerial is. The phone will have to use full strength to establish a quality transmission

**Issue:** Check your subscription 
Customer tried to activate a GSM service. Customer is then requested to check their subscription regarding the related service rights of use/access

# **Definition**

- Data Amnesty is a data bundle given back to customers who have data billing disputes to appreciate them for their loyalty and to encourage them to continue using our data services.
- It aims at making the customer feel valued and appreciated for their loyalty to Safaricom and win back their trust.

## 

# **Eligibility**

- It is eligible to all Prepaid and Postpaid Safaricom customers using mobile data services locally.
- Data billing issues arising from roaming usage are NOT considered for amnesty.

## 

# **Key Features**

- Data Amnesty bundle has a validity period of 7 days.
- It cannot be rolled over with the purchase of another bundle.
- Amnesty bundle can only be given once in 60 days per MSISDN.
- Customer can only be given a maximum of 50% of the data bundle in dispute.

articleTitle: Data Amnesty awarding procedure from the Contact Centre
markdownContent:
# **Data Amnesty awarding procedure from the Contact Centre**

- CEE will receive a call from a customer complaining that their bundle has been lost or depleted too fast.
- The CEE will acknowledge the concern and empathetically explain the usage to the customer using CRM-CDRs together with other available systems to confirm Data Usage.
- If the CDRs are missing - The existing process of handling cases of missing CDR will apply – where it is escalated via SR for Support to get back to the customer when the CDRs are availed. SLA is 24hrs.
- Where the CDRs are available and the usage explanation given, confirm if the customer understands and agrees with it.
- The CEE will then proceed to educate the customer to use the following ways to help manage and control their data bundles.

Advise the customer to activate Data manager by dialing \*100#ok> Select Balances& Data manager> Select Data Manager and Activate

Restrict their phone’s background data.

- Dial \*544#ok to Check balance then follow the data transparency link [https://bit.ly/2Q1ChQx](https://bit.ly/2Q1ChQx)﻿ provided to view their data statement.
- If customer is satisfied with explanation given, **DO NOT AWARD AMNESTY**, end the call as per the call closing procedure.
- Where the customer is not satisfied with their billing explanation (is still disputing), 
 CEE will Check under Data Amnesty History to confirm that they have not been awarded a data amnesty in the last 60 days.
- Verbalize that ***due to their loyalty and to enable them to continue using our data services***, you are offering a free data bundle. **Do NOT use the term data** **amnesty** when awarding the free data bundles.

- Offer a minimum of 20MBs
- Awarded a maximum of 50% (half) the disputed bundle.
- Advise the customer that the bundle is valid for 7 days and cannot be rolled over.

Proceed to award the amnesty bundle as below:

- Go to Siebel
- Search Subscriber.
- Go to IN Call History.
- Click Transaction History.
- Select the Data Bundle Purchases.
- Click on Data Amnesty Tab under Account Resources.
- Select the Amnesty to Award.
- Select the Data Bundle to award and click save. 

- The CEE will then confirm the Amnesty data bundle (Sawazisha bundle) balance on Siebel via IN DATA Tab or Check balance via transaction History.
- Advise the customer that they will receive an SMS notification that they have been awarded \*\*\*MBs Sawazisha bundle valid for 7 days.
- CEE will also advise the customer on how to check the bundle balance, by sending an SMS with the word BAL to 144 to check on the balance of the Sawazisha bundles awarded.
- An automated interaction is created when the customer is awarded amnesty bundles.
- If the bundle fails to award amnesty, enter it on the Amnesty Link to be effected within an hour. End the call as per procedure.

# Defination

The M-PESA menu push solution enables customers to receive the full M-PESA menu after Sim Swap. This means that the customer shall not be required to reactivate their M-PESA account manually. This will grow self-service channels and reduce demand,

The customer shall not be required to interact with the solution on their handset as it is an automated menu delivery.

If the customer’s phone is off or the customer is in a place without sufficient network, then the service shall retry delivering the menu in an interval of 2 hours for 3 consecutive days after which the retries will stop.

This service is currently available on Gemalto Sim cards only

# Objectives

Demand Reduction in all customer touchpoints.

Give customers a better experience by ensuring automatic M-PESA menu delivery after sim swap

Ensure that M-PESA remains the Mobile Money ecosystem of choice.

Reduced cost to serve across customer touchpoints

Provide M-PESA customers with a service that meets their needs.

# When

The enhancement will take effect **from** **11th December** **2021** and shall be available to **Gemalto sim cards** as a start.

The customer performs a sim swap action and automatically receives the full M-PESA menu

Customers who fail to receive the menu, shall receive instructions on how to activate after sim swap

If the customer is out of network or the handset is off, the service shall retry menu delivery every 2 hours for 72 hours.

Customer must have performed a successful Sim Swap.

articleTitle: Escalations Of Network Issues Via Line 300
markdownContent:
**Escalations Of Network Issues Via Line 300**

Line 300 CEE will identify when there is a global network outage that has not been captured in the NOC report or there is no communication to respective folders.

The CEE will pick samples of MSISDN from the Network Tool and checks on CEM or Siebel CDRs if Customers are able to access voice or data services. The CEE will check if the customer has airtime or a data plan on IN data. The profile of the sample numbers is checked on HLR.

If the network issue is reported and needs the CEE to call back, normal calling procedure applies. The CEE will always be required to remain courteous and friendly and professional.

Line 300 CEE will raise an SR that captures the sample numbers, BTS’s serving those Customers and an incident raised on the SR that was raised. NOC team tracks the incident raised.

When an SR and Incidents are raised, the CEE sends an email to CM support High Priority Folder, will copy NOC-Performance Management, Line 300 Folder, Support team that handles network SRs, Line 300 Team Leader and Line 300 respective shift manager.

After an SR and an Incident are raised, the CEE will send a blanket SMS to the affected customers who had reported to the Network Tool (5555) informing them the issue is faulting and working to resolve it.

The mail to CM support High Priority Folder is pasted on the Siebel interactions. If the cases were very many then interactions are not put on Siebel.

The CM support High Priority Folder probe the network issue under SR and Incident. If the issue is not resolved, the team does a further escalation to the RAN-optimization of the affected region with the network issue.

When the network issue raised under SR is resolved, an email is sent to Line 300 confirming the issue was resolved.

The Customers from the area or region that had a network issue and had reported it to Network Tool (5555) are sent a blanket SMS informing them the issue is resolved and to do LU before re-trying.

The email is pasted on the interactions. If the cases were very many then interactions are not put on Siebel.

# **Creating a Twitter account**

- Step 1: Sign up on Twitter. Enter Twitter.com and click on the sign-up option.
- Step 2: Optimize your new Twitter account. Twitter will ask you to add a profile picture, write a bio and follow people.

# **Getting started with Twitter**

- Step 1: Set Up Your Profile: Choose your profile name (aka handle) e.g. @Wix, Upload Images, select a Color Palette, Complete Your Bio and Add Your Website.
- Step 2: Follow Some People.
- Step 3: Understand the Twitter Lingo e.g. #Hashtags, Retweets, @Mentions
- Step 3: Decide What Content to Tweet About.
- Step 4: Join Trending Hashtags.
- Step 5: Maintain Your Channel.

# **Sending a new tweet to someone**

- Type your tweet in the box in the top left corner of the page.
- To send someone an @reply, enter the person's Twitter name at the beginning of the tweet in the format @username.
- To send someone a mention, type his or her Twitter name anywhere within the tweet.

# **Sending Post /updates to Twitter**

To send/Post updates on your twitter account, follow the steps below:

- Check that little box at the top of your Twitter home page which reads “What are you doing?”
- Type in a tweet in this box and then press “Update.” But, remember, you have to express yourself in only 140 characters!

# **Following someone**

- Following someone means you've chosen to subscribe to their Twitter updates.
- When you follow someone, every time they post a new message, it will appear on your Twitter home page

# **Finding People to follow**

When you create an account, you can search for people by name or username, import friends from other networks, or invite friends via email. You can also follow some of the people twitter suggested.

# **Retweets**

This is re-posting of a Tweet. Twitter's Retweet feature helps you and others quickly share that Tweet with all your followers. You can Retweet your own Tweets or Tweets from someone else. Sometimes people type "RT" at the beginning of a Tweet to indicate that they are re-posting someone else's content.

# **Turning off Retweets**

- Turn off Retweets for a specific account if you don't like what they share.
- Select Turn off Retweets from an account profile page to stop seeing Tweets they've Retweeted (tap the gear icon on iOS or click or tap the overflow icon on web and Android).

# **Twitter Limit**

- Direct Messages (daily): The limit is 1,000 messages sent per day.
- Tweets: 2,400 per day. Retweets are counted as Tweets.
- Changes to account email: 4 per hour.
- Following (daily): The technical follow limit is 400 per day.

# **Adding Location on My Tweets**

- Log in to your Twitter account
- Click settings
- Click Security & privacy settings
- Select ‘Enable’ Add a location to my Tweets and follow the prompts

# **Twitter Reads**

- Followers read Tweets.
- If Tweets are public, anyone who runs a search for a keyword in your Tweet may be able to see that message. Tweets are public by default.
- if you're hesitant to have people you may not know read your updates, protect your Tweets to approve followers and keep your updates out of search.

# **"Trending"**

- In Twitter, a word, phrase, or topic that is mentioned at a greater rate than others are said to be a "trending topic" or simply a "trend". Trending topics become popular either through a concerted effort by users or because of an event that prompts people to talk about a specific topic.
- Trending on twitter means that it's the most topic being talked about/being mentioned a lot by the users on the twitter. Mostly it begins with the #tag

# **Suspended twitter A/c**

- In order to maintain a safe environment for users on Twitter, Twitter may suspend accounts that violate the Twitter Rules.
- Common reasons for suspension may include: Abusive Tweets or behaviour: They suspend an account if it has been reported as violating the Rules surrounding abuse.
- When an account is in read-only mode, others will still be able to see and engage with the account. The duration of this enforcement action can range from 12 hours to 7 days, depending on the nature of the violation.

# **Deleting A photo/Tweet on Twitter**

**Photo**

You can delete a photo by deleting the Tweet that contains it.

**Tweet**

- In the top menu, tap your profile icon.
- Tap Profile.
- Locate the Tweet you want to delete.
- Tap the icon located at the top of the Tweet.
- Tap Delete Tweet.
- Tap Delete to confirm.

# **Sending a Link on Twitter**

- Visit the website that you want to send as a link on Twitter and "Copy" the URL.
- Browse to the URL shortening service of your choice e.g. bit.ly or tinyurl.
- Paste the copied URL into the "Convert" or "Go" box so as to shorten the URL.
- Log in to your twitter account & click on the "Tweet" box to compose your message and paste the shortened URL into the "Tweet" box.
- Click "Tweet" to send your link on Twitter.

# **Adding a Twitter Account to Blogspot**

- Sign into your Twitter account and click on the icon with your name in the top right corner of the screen. Choose "Settings" from the menu.
- Go to the "Profile" tab of the "Settings" menu.
- Click on the link below the "Website" field that reads "You can also add Twitter to your site here."
- Click on the "Widgets" option and then "My Website" on the "Select Your Widget" screen.
- Click on the blue "Profile Widget" option. Use the available tabs to change the appearance and size of your widget. The "Preference" tab lets you decide how many tweets will appear on your widget and whether all tweets will be shared immediately. Use the "Appearance" tab to set the colors for your widget and the "Dimensions" tab to set the size.
- Click on the "Finish & Grab Code" button at the bottom of the screen. Click on the "Add to Blogger" button, which is located just under the full code for the widget. You are redirected to the Blogger website.
- Sign into your Blogger account, if prompted. Click the blue "Add Widget" button to include the Twitter account on your Blogspot page.

# **Submitting a complaint**

Review the Terms of Service section to find out what constitutes a violation, and how to go about fixing a related problem.

Twitter's Terms of Service is posted on the website, and the Twitter Rules are posted in the Help Center.

# **Safaricom Twitter handle**

The Safaricom Twitter handles are @ @SafaricomPLC and @Safaricom\_Care

articleTitle: CHANGE OF PRIMARY NUMBER FOR ROAMING CUSTOMERS
markdownContent:
# **CHANGE OF PRIMARY NUMBER FOR ROAMING CUSTOMERS**

If a customer is roaming and not able to update their KYC details via the link since the OTP is being sent to a different number, the customer shall send the required documents via email to advantage@safaricom.co.ke or customercare@safaricom.co.ke.

Once received, the Email CEE shall vet the customer and update the correct primary number as provided by the customer.

The customer will be required to provide: -

- Customers full names.
- MSISDN to be updated as primary number.
- Alternative Contact Number (for the Roaming Country as the customer).
- Copy of ID.
- Valid passport. Pages containing below will be scanned;

1. Bio details (page with customer’s particulars).
2. Page with immigration stamp exiting Kenya.
3. Page with immigration stamp of entry country.

# **Checks**

- The Email CEE shall confirm if the primary number provided is roaming.
- The Email CEE shall make an outbound call on the alternative number provided and Vet the customer.
- The alternative number should be an international number with the roaming country code as the customer or a Safaricom number to be confirmed as roaming in the same country as the customer.
- If it’s a Safaricom number, the customer must give consent to be called as roaming charges apply while receiving the call.

articleTitle: Unclaimed M-PESA Funds / UFAA UFAA Contacts
markdownContent:
# **Unclaimed M-PESA Funds / UFAA**

Safaricom, under the M-PESA Service is required by law to declare any funds it has held in the M-PESA system that have been dormant in the archived account and not claimed within a period of two (2) years by the Owners (as defined by the Act) or as when instructed by the Unclaimed Financial Assets Authority (UFAA).

- Every year Financial Services (FS) will run a drive to encourage customers to claim their funds before submission to UFAA.

- This drive will include a self-service or a manual channel to withdraw funds
- FS will use the customer’s ID and other attributes to confirm line ownership before the claim.

- Once funds are submitted the customers will be referred to the UFAA for required documents and instructions on how to claim the funds.

- NB; One of these requirements is the surrender letter.
- UFAA is currently encouraging customers to claim their funds online. A tutorial of the same is available on You Tube: [https://www.youtube.com/watch?reload=9&v=7FCN\_bX5cbQ](https://www.youtube.com/watch?reload=9&v=7FCN_bX5cbQ)

- Where the customer has been to UFAA and or is requesting for the UFAA surrender letter they will visit a Safaricom Shop for the same

- The retail CEE will vet the customer as per the current M-PESA vetting instructions.

For Customer Accounts the customer will present their ID for vetting

For LNM Accounts with individual names the person will present their ID for vetting

LNM Accounts with organization names will write/present a letter indicating the name and ID details of the person who will receive the letter on behalf of the organization.

- The CEE will confirm that the funds were submitted to UFAA via the intranet link [https://cxintranet.safaricom.net/cm2/E\_MshwariBlacklists\_query.php](https://cxintranet.safaricom.net/cm2/E_MshwariBlacklists_query.php)
- The CEE will duly fill and issue the customer with a stamped surrender letter indicating the customer details and the amount remitted.
- The CEE will advise the customer to take the surrender letter to UFAA

- UFAA will receive the surrender letter and will confirm that customer has all the other required documentation. Once done they will contact FS for the final claim of funds letter. FS will issue the final letter and the funds will be transferred as per the current UFAA processes.

# **UFAA Contacts**

**The following contacts will be issued to the customer to get in touch with the UFAA**: Phone: 020 4343440, 0706866984, 0736559152. Email: info@ufaa.go.ke , Website: [http://www.ufaa.go.ke/](http://www.ufaa.go.ke/) , P.O Box 28235-00200, Nairobi, Kenya.

# **Data Centre as a Service in Cloud Computing**

- Data Centre as a Service provides Enterprise-grade data center resources such as mail servers, web servers and application servers among others without the required capital outlay or associated lead times.
- It allows customers to outsource their Data Centre Infrastructure (servers and storage etc.) to Safaricom on-demand.
- This is delivered to you through the purchase of Virtual Machines or Virtual Servers accessed over the Internet. You can configure the virtual machines to your specifications (Operating Systems, RAM, Storage (size and type) and Processor etc.).
- You will receive a series of virtual machines, which you will have specified. The Safaricom team will configure these and the client can access these over the Internet.
- The client will have administrative rights and will manage and run these as their own. Similar to the dedicated servers you actually choose the size and capacity of the virtual machine you want from the available options; plus the same add-on services are available to our “virtual” clients as they are to our “dedicated” clients.

# **Benefits Data and Service Features**

**Benefits**

- Fixed monthly costs that combine raised floor space, power, cooling and bandwidth provisioning.
- Security: Facility provides a high-security environment, including fire detection, UPS power backup, access control, surveillance and backup power generators to ensure high availability.
- Geographical redundancy offering disaster prevention.
- Saves customer time and costs in ensuring business continuity.
- Redundant clean Power Feed options.
- Dedicated fixed bandwidth

# **Service Features**

- Commercially Flexible.
- Secure.
- Multi-tenant (Shared and Dedicated).
- Virtual compute blocks (single instance and resource pooling).
- X86 architecture.
- Rapid service provisioning.
- Automation.

articleTitle: Faulty Handset Issues at the Retail Center
markdownContent:
# **Faulty Handset Issues at the Retail Center**

# **Faulty Handsets**

A Customer can return the device to the nearest retail shop.

If within 3 days from purchase, customer can get a replacement unit (for manufacturer’s faults) from the retail outlet visited.

If it’s after the 3 days, the retail outlet books the phone for repair.

For handsets out of warranty period, customer will be referred to the attached authorized repair Center. Retail Center will not book the handset.

# **Out-of-box failure**

An "Out-Of-Box Failure" (OBF) is defined as a new handset / modem/Tablet that is found to be technically faulty within 3 (three) days of purchase.

Items must be returned within 3 (three) days from date of purchase on official sales receipt (proof of purchase)

All handsets must be assessed by receiving Safaricom Staff for any faults reported by the client before being exchanged.

Items that qualify as OBF will only be swapped for the same make and model.

# **Out-of-box criteria**

The device must be returned in the original, undamaged and complete sales package.

The sales pack must include the handset/device, original battery, original charger manuals, soft wares and any other accessories while returning to the retail shop.

There must be no visible signs of customer damage (without disassembly) or any physical damage on the product or its accessories or any signs of neglect due to physical abuse, liquid damage, screen scratches, dents or marks.

Devices with any physical damage including seemingly trivial surface scratches or marks should not be exchanged.

All kitted items that were issued with the device should be returned. Resources that may have been awarded with the device purchase should not be consume.

The IMEI number on the box must match the IMEI number on the device.

# **Repair** **Center**

Retail Agent does basic trouble shooting to rule out user problem.

If no solution is reached, device will be booked for repair and the RCSC raise an SR.

Faulty devices will be dispatched to the repair Center before the end of the next day, repaired and returned within 7 days (handsets within Nairobi and 14 days for up country shops)

Customer will be alerted once handset has been returned to the shop and SR closed.

If phone is irreparable, the vendor should issue swap stock. Replacement device serial will be indicated in the SR.

Find attached Phone Service Centres attachment.

# **Collecting on behalf of a third party**

You will be required to provide the booking form (filled and signed when booking the handset for repair),

An original copy of the person collecting identification document.

The owner will also be contacted for authorization by the retail agent.

If customer calls to inquire of a booked handset, confirm with the SR ticket.

If the SR ticket is within the SLA, advice of seven (7) working days.

If SR ticket is past SLA, send mail to CM Support Center Escalation folder for follow up. Capture the following:

Name of sub

#  **PAYBILL MERCHANT INTEROPERABILITY**

We are pleased to introduce Merchant interoperability for Paybill Transactions, a service that will enable Paybill Organizations to receive Lipa na M-PESA payments from Airtel and Telkom mobile money customers. Kindly continue to send us feedback on everything – opt-in, response time, limits…. via **customer feedback link** product name Merchant Interoperability.

**Paybill Interoperability FAQS**

 **Defination**

This is a joint project between Safaricom, Airtel, and Telkom to allow Lipa Na M-PESA paybill organizations to receive payments from Airtel money and Telkom T-kash customers.

 **Which customers will be enabled to use this service?**

The service shall be offered exclusively to Airtel and Telkom subscribers who have a valid SIM card and are registered for Airtel money and Telkom T-kash service.

**What is the maximum payable to a Lipa Na M-PESA paybill organization**

- Maximum amount payable to a Lipa Na M-PESA paybill organization is KSh. 150,000.

**What is the minimum payable to a Lipa Na M-PESA paybill organization?**

- Minimum amount payable to a Lipa Na M-PESA paybill organization is KSh 1.00

- System must auto reverse failed transactions.

**Which details are shared to the customer when making payment?**

**Which channel will the customers from other network providers use to contact us for assistance?**

- Customer shall contact their respective service providers directly for all support functions i.e., reversal requests.

**Which transactions will be reversed?**
